intro.heading: The school run is the real constraint in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Al Mamzar sits at the far north-eastern edge of Dubai, against the Sharjah border and the creek that runs behind Al Mamzar Beach Park. It is a settled residential district of villas and low-rise buildings with a large Arab and South Asian population, and the schools immediately around it predominantly teach CBSE or the UAE Ministry curriculum. Indian-curriculum schools account for 26 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, and this is one of the parts of the city where that share is concentrated.

The practical consequence for an IGCSE family is a commute. A student in Al Mamzar following a British curriculum is usually travelling towards Al Garhoud, Oud Metha, Al Qusais or further, because that is where the IGCSE provision sits. Drop-off runs across Al Ittihad Road and Abu Baker Al Siddique Road in the morning and back again in the afternoon, and the afternoon leg is the one that governs whether anything can happen before dinner.

That same geography is what makes the home-tutor question difficult. A visiting tutor serving Al Mamzar faces the same roads in the same direction at the same hour, and the travel time is inside the price. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the upper half of that band is largely the car. For a household in Al Mamzar, which sits further from the city's tutoring supply than Jumeirah or Al Barsha does, the premium is larger rather than smaller.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; sending a tutor to a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. This page makes that case on the specifics rather than in the abstract: which schools the neighbourhood actually feeds, what time those schools finish, how long the journey home takes at 3pm, and what hour a session can therefore start and still be attended by an alert fifteen-year-old.

The second argument is supply. The number of people in Dubai who teach Cambridge Chemistry 0620 or Pearson Further Pure 4PM1 well is modest, and they are not evenly spread across the city - most are closer to the schools that teach those syllabuses. A family in Al Mamzar hiring locally is choosing from a thinner pool than a family in Al Barsha. Video delivery removes that disadvantage entirely, which is the one argument on this page that is specific to this neighbourhood rather than general.

What follows is organised around that geography rather than around a list of benefits. The first section takes the home-tutor question at face value and works out what a visiting tutor would actually face getting here. The second maps where this neighbourhood's IGCSE students go to school, with finish times and journey times, because those two numbers decide everything else. The third works through which evening slot survives a term in a Deira household. The remainder covers the November resit route, what a parent can verify before paying, the coursework line a tutor does not cross, and the mandatory UAE subjects, which in this neighbourhood affect more families than the city average.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: An Al Mamzar family following a British curriculum is planning across a sequence that most of their neighbours are not. These are the stages that matter, and what each one requires here.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Three years with no external examination, during which the IGCSE tier and option recommendations are effectively formed. For a family who moved into a British-curriculum school from a CBSE one, this is also the period in which the differences in approach - coursework, extended writing, investigation - either get absorbed or do not.
programmes.countryNote: Curriculum transfers are common in this part of Dubai, in both directions, because school places and fee levels vary across Deira and Al Qusais. A student moving from CBSE into a British curriculum in Year 8 or 9 usually needs bridging work in extended writing and in investigative science rather than in content, which is the opposite of what families expect.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, assessed by terminal written papers with practical or coursework components in some subjects. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson's International GCSE tiers maths into Foundation and Higher. Those entries cap the attainable grade and are usually settled in the autumn of Year 11 at the latest.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student needs five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five. One competing tutoring site tells UAE parents six are required. Check the Ministry's own pages before building a subject list around either figure.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: The post-16 route most British-curriculum schools within reach of Al Mamzar offer, in three or four subjects. Entry depends on IGCSE grades in the same subjects, so a Year 11 result is not just a certificate line - it determines what Year 12 is permitted to look like, and in a commuting household it may also determine which school is practical.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, on top of the five IGCSE passes. That is a floor for attestation, not a university target. Families here often conflate the two, and the result is complacency about grades that a competitive course will examine closely.

programmes.name: The CBSE comparison, because it is the local default
programmes.description: Most schools around Al Mamzar teach CBSE, so families here are often weighing a British-curriculum commute against a CBSE place nearby. The honest difference for tutoring purposes is assessment style: CBSE rewards accurate recall against a defined syllabus, while IGCSE rewards command-term discipline and extended written reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector runs seventeen different curricula, with UK at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 and US at 14. In Deira and Al Qusais the Indian share is far above the city average, which is exactly why an IGCSE family here feels like an outlier among their neighbours and finds fewer local tutors who know the syllabus.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mamzar.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Mamzar families ask about most, with the component that usually decides the grade named rather than a general note on difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. The tier caps the grade at entry. Algebraic manipulation underpins everything else, and the multi-step questions at the back of the paper lose marks because method is done mentally and never written down.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity drains the most marks at Extended tier, followed by graph interpretation. The written practical component rewards precise method description, which is a writing skill rather than a physics one and is rarely taught as such.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the two reliable losses. Organic is taught last and revised least. A student who balances equations confidently but cannot convert between moles, mass and concentration loses marks across every paper.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty. Extended responses need the specification's own vocabulary, so a correct answer in everyday words frequently scores nothing because the mark scheme lists the term.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Common across this part of Dubai, where many households use Arabic, Malayalam, Urdu, Tagalog or Hindi at home. The listening component and the note-making exercise need timed practice more than they need vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 and 0990 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading summary carry the volatile marks. Students lose marks for not shaping a response to the stated audience and purpose, which is a mark-scheme habit rather than a comprehension gap.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. In this neighbourhood the first-language pathway is more common than the city average.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450) and Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Both reward answering the command term rather than the topic. An evaluate question answered as a description sits in the lower band however accurate it is, and that single habit is worth more marks than additional content.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Popular in this part of the city, where many parents work in trade, logistics and accountancy roles around Deira and Al Hamriya. Marks are lost to layout and presentation conventions as much as to the underlying bookkeeping.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables need deliberate practice; the practical ICT components need fluency against a specific software version. Both are commonly taken by students whose schools have strong computing provision.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460) and History (Cambridge 0470)
subjects.description: Source-skill subjects in content-subject clothing. Geography's data response and History's source evaluation are learnable techniques, and case-study specificity is what separates a grade 6 from a grade 8.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606) and Further Pure (Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Extension qualifications taken alongside the main maths syllabus by students heading for A Level maths. Frequently timetabled into an option block with fewer hours than the content requires, which is why strong mathematicians sometimes underperform here.

regions.name: Hor Al Anz and Hor Al Anz East
regions.note: Immediately inland from Al Mamzar, denser and closer to Abu Hail. Families here share the same school commute and the same afternoon congestion, and a visiting tutor would cross both neighbourhoods in one trip at the worst possible hour.

regions.name: Al Nahda and Al Qusais
regions.note: Towards the Sharjah boundary, with a large school cluster and the Green Line metro nearby. Several British-curriculum and Indian-curriculum schools sit here, which makes it the shortest IGCSE commute available to an Al Mamzar family.

regions.name: Deira and Al Muteena

regions.name: Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City

regions.name: Al Twar and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Further inland along the Sharjah corridor, with additional school provision. Families who moved from Al Mamzar to be closer to a school often land here, and the tutoring arithmetic does not change with the move.

sections.heading: What a home tutor would actually face getting to Al Mamzar
paragraphs: It is worth taking the home-tutor question seriously rather than deflecting it, because the search is sensible and the market does offer the service. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's in-home band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to 500. Advertised monthly packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. The travel is inside the price in every case.

For Al Mamzar specifically the travel is worse than the city average, and in a direction most rate comparisons ignore. The neighbourhood sits at the north-eastern edge of Dubai against the Sharjah border. The tutors who teach Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses tend to live nearer the schools that teach them, which in this city means Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Mirdif or the New Dubai belt. A trip to Al Mamzar at 4.30pm means Al Ittihad Road or Sheikh Rashid Road against the Sharjah-bound flow, and then the same journey back.

The consequences are predictable. The pool of tutors willing to make that trip is smaller than the pool teaching the subject, which means a family here is selecting from the intersection of two scarce sets rather than from one. The hourly price sits at the upper end of the band because the journey is longer. And the appointment is fragile - the sessions most often cancelled in this catchment are the ones that depend on somebody else's drive.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar, in Dubai, or anywhere in the UAE; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. That is not a limitation we are working around - it is why the delivery model is what it is. The table below compares the options honestly, including what in-home genuinely buys, because for some students a person in the room is worth the premium and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.

sections.heading: Where Al Mamzar's IGCSE students actually go to school
paragraphs: This is the part of the question that no generic page answers, and it is the part that decides the timetable. The schools immediately around Al Mamzar predominantly teach CBSE or the UAE Ministry curriculum. Indian-curriculum schools account for 26 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment overall, and in Deira and Al Qusais the local share runs well above that. So a British-curriculum family in Al Mamzar is almost always commuting.

There are two realistic directions. The shorter one is inland towards Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Al Twar, where a mixed cluster of schools sits close to the Green Line and where some British-curriculum provision is available. The longer one crosses towards Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Oud Metha, where the area's more established international-curriculum schools are, including schools offering IB programmes. The second direction is the one that involves the creek crossing.

Finish times across these clusters sit broadly between 2pm and 3.30pm, with Indian-curriculum schools often finishing earlier than British-curriculum ones. The journey home at that hour is the variable that matters. A metro commute from Al Qusais or Abu Hail gets a student home reliably. A car journey from Oud Metha across Al Garhoud Bridge at 3pm does not, and the arrival time can vary by twenty-five minutes week to week.

That variability is the strongest practical argument on this page. A session that depends on two uncertain arrivals - the student's and the tutor's - is a session that gets shortened or moved. An online session depends on one, and the student's own arrival is the one the family controls. The table sets out the clusters, the finish times and what each implies for a realistic start.

sections.heading: Fitting a session into an Al Mamzar evening
paragraphs: Once the commute is accounted for, the question becomes which hour a fifteen-year-old can actually think in. There are three candidate slots in a Deira household and each has a different failure mode, so it is worth choosing deliberately rather than taking whatever a tutor offers.

The straight-from-school slot, between 4pm and 5pm, works when the student arrives predictably - typically a metro commuter or a short Al Qusais route. Its advantage is momentum: the student is still in working mode and has not had to restart. Its failure mode is the creek crossing, where a twenty-five-minute variance in arrival turns a sixty-minute session into forty and makes the first ten of those forty useless.

The post-dinner slot at 7.30pm or 8pm is the most reliable in this catchment because it does not depend on traffic at all. It also fits working parents in Deira, many of whom finish after 6pm and want to be present rather than hearing about the session afterwards. Its failure mode is alertness, and it varies by age - workable for Years 10 and 11, poor for Years 7 and 8, who are better served earlier even at the cost of some reliability.

The weekend block is the one families in this area underuse. A longer Saturday or Sunday morning session is often the only time a full timed paper can be sat and then reviewed in the same sitting, which is what turns past papers into marks rather than exercises. Used alongside a shorter weekday session it gives a Year 11 student both consistency and genuine diagnostic work, and it depends on no road at all.

sections.heading: Why the local IGCSE tutor pool is thinner on this side of the city
paragraphs: Tutor supply follows school supply, and school supply in Dubai is uneven by curriculum and by district. The city runs seventeen different curricula across 227 private schools, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 and US at 14. Those shares are not distributed evenly: the UK-curriculum concentration sits towards Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and the New Dubai belt, while Deira, Al Qusais and Al Nahda carry a much higher Indian-curriculum share.

Tutors cluster where their market is. Someone who teaches Cambridge Chemistry 0620 builds a practice around the schools that teach it, and those schools are mostly not in Deira. The result is that an Al Mamzar family hiring locally for an IGCSE subject is drawing from a thinner pool than a family in Al Barsha, and thinner again for a specialist need - Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, or a less common option within a science syllabus.

This is where the online argument stops being general and becomes specific to this neighbourhood. For a family in the New Dubai school belt, moving a lesson online widens the pool from large to larger. For a family in Al Mamzar it widens it from small to the same large pool everyone else has. The relative gain is bigger here, and it is the clearest reason this page exists in the form it does.

There is a reverse advantage worth naming. Deira and Al Qusais have strong local provision in CBSE subjects and in Arabic as a first language, because that is where the demand is. A family needing Arabic first-language support, or help with a CBSE sibling, may well find the best option close to home. The honest position is that supply is uneven in both directions, and the right answer depends on which subject is being bought.

sections.heading: Counting back to the November series, not just the June one
paragraphs: Most revision advice counts down to the summer papers, which leaves out the half of the calendar that matters to a family deciding what to do after a disappointing result. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June series and the November series - the February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate planning around a February examination has been handed the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

The November route is worth planning before results arrive rather than after. Entries close well before the late-October start, and the gap between a June result and that deadline is short. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November resit produces a January result, which matters if a university or sixth-form offer depends on it.

The practical move is to decide in advance what grade would justify a resit in each subject, so that the decision takes minutes rather than weeks when the envelope opens. Then ask the school's exams officer for the paper-level breakdown of the summer grade. A near-miss caused by one paper is a far better resit case than a uniform shortfall across all of them, because one paper can be targeted in the ten weeks available and a general weakness cannot.

Two administrative details catch families out. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one - so get the timetable through the school. And Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so link to the live official document rather than trusting a restated date, including any on this page.

sections.heading: What a parent in Al Mamzar can actually check before paying
paragraphs: This market publishes credentials loosely and rates inconsistently, so it helps to separate the checkable from the unverifiable. The most checkable thing, and the one almost nobody asks about, is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any figure quoted to you as a penalty amount should be treated with suspicion - including figures circulating in parent groups. Anyone telling you private tutoring in Dubai is unregulated is simply wrong.

The second checkable item is the syllabus code. Ask which code the tutor teaches and which board's past papers they use. A tutor who answers 'maths' rather than '0580 Extended' or '4MA1 Higher' has told you how precisely they work. The third is what happens if the match fails: ask for the process before any payment, because a package with no exit is a package you will be arguing about later.

What is not checkable is most of what gets advertised. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners for individuals whose current status cannot be evidenced, and no examiner claim should be taken to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Self-published star ratings are weaker evidence still - competitor pages in this market show 4.92 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and figures that contradict each other on one screen are the signal.

sections.heading: Coursework, materials and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE maths has no coursework, but several subjects do have coursework or practical components, and those are where the honesty line gets tested. The boundary is simple to state. A tutor may teach content, explain what a mark scheme rewards, model a technique on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, finish or edit a piece of assessed work to completion.

The reason is where the consequence falls. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the sanction lands on the student. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. That transaction transfers the whole risk onto a teenager, and it is worth recognising it for what it is whenever a provider offers it - including providers who describe it as editing or polishing.

Materials work the same way. We reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, cite them, and link out to the boards. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, in the case of unreleased material, a malpractice exposure in themselves. A tutor who offers a folder of mark schemes has told you something about how they operate.

There is also a question about who teaches. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. Those are press-reported positions and should be verified against the current policy document, but the principle holds across the UAE: engaging your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what they mean in this neighbourhood
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The sector ran 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula. In Abu Dhabi the equivalent authority is ADEK, in Sharjah SPEA, in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education. That last point matters here, because Al Mamzar sits minutes from the Sharjah boundary and some families in this neighbourhood have children at schools under SPEA rather than KHDA.

The mandatory UAE subjects apply in Dubai regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and at least twenty-five minutes is advised for any mandatory subject lesson.

In this neighbourhood the first-language Arabic pathway is more common than the city average, and the rules around it are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students.

Two further constraints affect what any tutor can legitimately offer in those subjects. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach them. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited - which means support in Arabic or Islamic Education has to track the school's own material rather than introduce an alternative scheme.

process.title: Tell us the school and the finish time
process.description: Which school, in which cluster, and what time the day ends. That single piece of information decides whether an afternoon slot is realistic or whether the post-dinner slot is the one that will actually hold through a term in this part of the city.

process.title: Ask the school for the codes and tiers
process.description: The syllabus code for each subject and whether maths and the sciences are entered at Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. It takes one email and it prevents a term of practice on the wrong board's papers, which is a common waste here.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A marked paper tells us whether marks went to unknown content, unwritten method, misread command terms or the clock. A report grade tells us none of that, and the four need entirely different plans.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a live topic
process.description: The tutor teaches whatever is stuck this week, at the correct tier and board. It shows how explanations land, it costs nothing, and if the pairing is wrong there is no package to argue your way out of.

process.title: Pick the slot by reliability
process.description: We will usually recommend the slot least dependent on traffic rather than the one that looks neatest. For a creek crossing that means an evening session; for a metro commuter from Abu Hail an afternoon one works fine.

process.title: Use a weekend block for diagnosis
process.description: A longer weekend session is the only realistic time to sit a full timed paper and review it in the same sitting. We build those in at the start and end of a block so progress is measured rather than felt.

whyPoints.title: The school run is planned around, not ignored
whyPoints.description: We ask which cluster the student travels to and choose the slot accordingly, because in this neighbourhood arrival-time variance is the single biggest reason sessions get shortened or moved.

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no travel premium
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in this market run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the journey inside the price, and for Al Mamzar the journey is longer than average. Delivering online removes that cost rather than discounting it.

whyPoints.title: The same tutor pool as every other neighbourhood

faqs.question: Do you send a home tutor to Al Mamzar for IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Mamzar, in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE - a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and from Al Mamzar that journey is longer than average because tutors cluster nearer the schools that teach these syllabuses.

faqs.question: Which schools do IGCSE students from Al Mamzar usually attend?
faqs.answer: Almost always ones they commute to. The schools immediately around Al Mamzar predominantly teach CBSE or the UAE Ministry curriculum, and Indian-curriculum schools account for 26 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment with a much higher local share in Deira and Al Qusais. British-curriculum families here travel either inland to Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Al Twar, or south-west to Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Oud Metha. The second route involves a creek crossing, which is the main variable in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if the journey home crosses the creek?
faqs.answer: Realistically 7.30pm. A school finishing between 2.30pm and 3.15pm in Oud Metha or Al Mankhool means a journey of thirty to fifty minutes back to Al Mamzar at that hour, and the arrival time can vary by twenty-five minutes week to week. A 5pm session booked against that variance becomes a forty-minute session with ten unproductive minutes at the start. The post-dinner slot depends on no road at all, which is why it holds through a whole term.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely better for a family out here, or is that just what you offer?
faqs.answer: Both, and the second does not make the first untrue. The specific reason it is better here is supply: tutors cluster near the schools teaching their syllabus, and UK-curriculum schools cluster away from Deira. A family in Al Barsha moving online goes from a large pool to a larger one. A family in Al Mamzar goes from a small pool to the same large one, which is a bigger relative gain. For CBSE subjects or Arabic as a first language, local supply here is strong and the calculation reverses.

faqs.question: What should an Al Mamzar household expect to pay for weekly IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put online budget tutoring at roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, which generally means a university student, and a qualified online subject tutor from around AED 150 to 300. In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price, and advertised packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published rates. Our trial lesson and consultation are free, and a quote depends on subject, tier and frequency.

faqs.question: My child moved from a CBSE school into a British-curriculum one. What needs bridging?
faqs.answer: Usually not content, which surprises families. The gap is in assessment style: IGCSE rewards command-term discipline, extended written reasoning and investigative work, while CBSE rewards accurate recall against a defined syllabus. A student who knew the material well in Class 9 can lose marks in Year 10 for answering the topic rather than the question. A term of work on command terms, extended-answer structure and practical method writing closes most of it, and it is far cheaper in Year 10 than in Year 11.

faqs.question: Should we be planning for a November resit before the summer results arrive?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the window afterwards is short. Decide in advance what grade would justify a resit in each subject, so the decision takes minutes rather than weeks. November entries close well before the late-October start. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit produces a January result. Also ask the exams officer for the paper-level breakdown: a near-miss on one paper is a much better resit case than a uniform shortfall.

faqs.question: Can lessons run after Iftar during Ramadan for a Deira household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this neighbourhood most families move them. School days shorten, afternoons become unproductive, and a session at 9pm or 9.30pm after Iftar is frequently the most alert hour available. Because delivery is online there is nothing to rearrange beyond the calendar entry, and no one is driving anywhere at an awkward hour. Ramadan also falls close to the run-up to the May and June papers, which makes this a practical scheduling question for Year 11 rather than a courtesy.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally allowed to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Al Mamzar is so close to Sharjah?
faqs.answer: For some families it matters a great deal. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than by KHDA, and SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate. If your child attends a school across the boundary, the inspection framework and the regulator contact are different. Border traffic also makes an afternoon tutoring slot unrealistic, which is why online evening sessions are effectively the only workable option there.

faqs.question: We want help in four subjects. Is that affordable or sensible?
faqs.answer: Rarely either, and the arithmetic is the reason. Four weekly sessions at the qualified-tutor band is a commitment most households will not sustain for two years, and a student doing eight hours of tuition a week stops doing independent practice, which is what actually converts teaching into marks. The better structure is sequencing: take the subject where the marked papers show the cheapest marks available, finish a block, review, then decide whether the second is worth buying. It costs a quarter as much and usually produces more.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework in Al Mamzar without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, model a method on a different question, and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, finish or edit assessed work to completion. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the consequence falls on the student. A provider offering to produce coursework - including one describing it as editing - is transferring the whole risk onto your child.

faqs.question: Which is the best slot for a Year 8 student living here?
faqs.answer: The earlier one, even at some cost to reliability. Younger students concentrate poorly at 8pm, and a session they are present for but not awake in is money spent for nothing. If the commute makes a 4.30pm start unpredictable, a weekend morning block is usually better than a late weekday slot. The useful principle is to pick the hour the student can think in and then solve the logistics around it, rather than the reverse - which is what an in-person appointment forces you to do.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for the subject and tier we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Some combinations are genuinely thin - Pearson Further Pure 4PM1, a specific Cambridge syllabus version, or Arabic first-language support alongside an IGCSE subject list. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist can cover part of the need, and whether a local option or the school's own department is the better route. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit.

That decides which hour will survive a whole term in this part of Dubai, and the hour matters more than most families expect. Then send the syllabus codes and a marked paper, and the plan is straightforward. We do not visit homes in the UAE, and we would rather explain why that works in your favour here than pretend the question was not asked.

intro.heading: "Does anyone near me actually know this syllabus?"
paragraphs: It is the right question and almost nobody answers it. A parent in Al Manara searching for an IGCSE home tutor does not want a stranger's postcode; they want somebody who has taught the exact qualification their child is entered for. And IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a family of them, offered by Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel and OxfordAQA, each with its own syllabus codes, its own paper structures, its own tiering rules and its own way of handling practical science. A tutor who knows one well and the others not at all is common and perfectly respectable. A tutor who does not know which one your child is sitting is a problem.

Al Manara sits inland in the Jumeirah corridor, along Al Wasl Road and Umm Suqeim Street, between the coastal villa districts and the dense Al Barsha school cluster. It is largely residential villas, well served by road, and it feeds children into campuses in both directions - the coastal British-curriculum and IB schools towards Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah, and the inland cluster around Al Barsha and Al Quoz. Those schools use different boards. Two Al Manara children on the same street can be sitting Mathematics under Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 respectively, with different papers, different calculator rules and different grading behaviour.

So the honest answer to the question in the heading is: yes, there are capable tutors within a short drive of Al Manara, and no, proximity does not tell you whether any of them knows your child's board. What tells you is four or five questions, and this page gives them to you. It also gives you the syllabus codes side by side, because the fastest way to test a tutor is to ask them what changes between the two and listen to whether the answer is specific.

On the phrase in the URL: home tutoring is what parents search for, and this page treats it seriously rather than pretending the question away. Home tuition in Al Manara is a real market with real prices - in-home one-to-one visits across Dubai are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors - and for some families, particularly with younger children or where supervision is the point, it is the right purchase. IB Gram does not sell it. Home visits are a service we run only in India; UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and the comparison table later on sets out what that trade costs and buys.

The reason for that choice is the one this page opened with. A tutor who drives cannot specialise, because nobody fills a week with Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry students living within twenty minutes of their own villa. Travel time turns specialists into generalists. Removing the drive is what makes it possible to match an Al Manara family with somebody who knows their board, their code and the paper their child is entered for.
Read the syllabus code table first. It is the part of this page that will change how you interview a tutor, whoever you end up hiring.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara IGCSE enquiry can mean several different things depending on the board and the stage. These are the routes families in this part of Dubai are actually on, and what each one assesses.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely taught IGCSE in the UAE. Subjects carry four-digit codes - 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English - and many are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5 depending on the grading scale the school uses. Cambridge runs exams in a June series and a November series, with each centre allocated to one of six administrative zones.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an Al Manara family this is a one-line question to the school's exams officer, and it is worth asking in writing rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes begin with a digit and a subject prefix - 4MA1 Mathematics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; Mathematics B is a single harder tier. Pearson exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The practical difference for a tutor is the paper structure and the tiering decision. A student entered for Higher tier 4MA1 who would have been better on Foundation loses marks that are not recoverable by content work, and that entry decision belongs to the school - which makes it a conversation to have early rather than in March.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Where most IGCSE students in British-curriculum Dubai schools go next, as an alternative to the IB Diploma. Cambridge runs International A Levels in the same June and November series as IGCSE. The transition matters because A Level assumes algebraic fluency and practical skills that IGCSE only begins; a student who scraped an IGCSE grade through recall tends to find the first A Level term brutal.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE British-track equivalency, the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other common post-IGCSE route in Dubai, since many British-curriculum schools in the emirate run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with an internally assessed component in each subject.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE to Diploma jump is the one Al Manara families underestimate most, because the content overlap is reassuring and the assessment design is not. Internal assessment, command terms and extended response all arrive at once, and the students who cope are the ones whose IGCSE work was understood rather than memorised.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: IGCSE subjects come up by board and code in this part of Dubai, not by name alone. For each one, what the papers assess and where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two written papers per tier, with Extended reaching into functions, vectors, transformations and harder algebra. Marks go on unshown working, premature rounding and misread command words. Core is capped, so the tiering decision matters more than any amount of revision in the final term.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, calculator permitted throughout, which changes the balance of skills against some Cambridge routes. Higher tier assumes confident algebraic manipulation; the common loss is a correct method abandoned because the student cannot rearrange under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide grades in both routes. Marks are lost on state symbols, significant figures and explanations that describe rather than explain. Organic chemistry at Extended rewards mechanism understanding over memorised equations, and electrolysis questions punish vague electrode reasoning.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where most marks disappear. The failure is usually algebraic rather than conceptual: a correct formula, a correct substitution, then an arithmetic slip or a unit left unconverted. Graph questions reward careful gradient work that is quick to teach and rarely taught.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A volume subject that rewards exact terminology and penalises near-misses. "The cell takes it in" earns nothing where the mark scheme wants active transport against a concentration gradient. Data and graph interpretation questions on the longer papers need practice on material nobody has pre-digested.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Two or three sciences compressed into fewer qualifications, taken by many Dubai students who do not intend to carry all three forward. The content is shallower but the exam technique demands are identical, and students often arrive with weaker practical reasoning because fewer practicals were run.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing carry the paper. Students lose marks by summarising a passage rather than selecting and analysing from it, and by ignoring the specified audience and form in the writing task. Timing discipline is worth more here than vocabulary breadth.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Assessed on listening, reading and writing with a specified text type for each writing task. A capable speaker can plateau because register and text-type conventions were never taught explicitly - an email written as an essay loses marks before the content is read.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and case-study application carry the grade. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with the new equilibrium marked earns marks that prose cannot recover, and tool-based answers that never reference the named business are capped however fluent they read.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation in Computer Science; practical application skills in ICT. Students lose marks on trace tables by rushing rows, and on theory questions by giving an example where the command term asked for a definition or a comparison.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Dubai students frequently carry an IGCSE Arabic entry alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic lessons, which have their own content and expectations. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and sets the language of instruction for each, so treating the two as one subject leaves a student behind in both.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates heading for A Level Mathematics, and genuinely useful preparation for it. The jump in algebraic demand from the main IGCSE is steep, and students who found 0580 Extended comfortable through pattern recognition rather than understanding tend to stall here first.

sections.heading: What "knows the syllabus" actually means for IGCSE
paragraphs: It means naming the code. A tutor who knows your child's syllabus will ask, in the first two minutes, which board and which code - 0580 or 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1, 0625 or 4PH1 - and will tell you what changes between them. A tutor who says "IGCSE maths, yes, no problem" has not answered the question you asked. This is not pedantry. The codes carry different paper structures, different tiering rules, different calculator permissions and different practical arrangements, and a student prepared for the wrong one loses marks that have nothing to do with how well they understand mathematics.

The second part is tiering. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended and Core is capped, so a student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform. Pearson Mathematics A splits into Foundation and Higher on the same logic, while Mathematics B is a single harder tier. A tutor who does not know which tier your child is entered for cannot tell you whether the grade you are hoping for is arithmetically available, which is the most important thing a parent can be told in Year 10.

The third part is practical science, and it is the question most often missed in Dubai. Different routes handle it differently - some through a practical examination, some through an alternative-to-practical written paper assessing the same skills on paper. Which one your child faces changes what preparation is useful. Rehearsing laboratory technique for a student sitting a written alternative paper is wasted time; neglecting graph, table and method-evaluation work for that same student is lost marks.

So the honest version of the question in this page's title is answerable, and the answer is a test rather than a map. Ask the code. Ask the tier. Ask how practical science is assessed on that route. A tutor in Al Manara, Al Barsha or anywhere else who answers all three specifically is worth considering. One who answers none of them is a general tutor, which is a different and sometimes adequate product - but you should know which one you are buying.
bullets: Ask for the board and the four-character syllabus code before anything else
Ask which tier your child is entered for and what that tier caps at

sections.heading: The syllabus codes side by side
paragraphs: This table is the single most useful thing to have open when interviewing a tutor, and no competitor page in this search result publishes anything like it. Across the entire researched area cluster, exactly one syllabus code appears anywhere. Yet the code is the qualification: it determines the papers, the tiering and the assessment of practical work, and it is printed on your child's school entry confirmation.

Read it as a comparison rather than a list. The point is not that one board is harder - that argument is mostly folklore - but that they are different, and that a tutor's familiarity is board-specific in practice even when their subject knowledge is not. A teacher who has marked Cambridge Physics for a decade knows exactly which command words trigger which mark-scheme points in 0625. Dropped into 4PH1 they will teach the physics correctly and miss some of the technique, which is the part you were paying for.

Two practical notes on using it. First, confirm the code with your child's school rather than assuming from the textbook on the shelf - schools change boards, and a student who joined mid-course may have covered material from both. Second, where a school enters students for Combined or Coordinated Sciences rather than three separate sciences, the codes differ again and the depth expected is different, which matters for anyone planning A Level sciences afterwards.

Always check the live official syllabus document on the board's own site rather than relying on a summary, including this one. Cambridge publishes its syllabuses at cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson at qualifications.pearson.com, and both revise content between cycles.

sections.heading: Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher: the entry decision nobody explains
paragraphs: This is where Al Manara families lose grades without knowing it, and it happens months before the exam. Tiered IGCSE subjects cap the available grade at the lower tier. A student entered for Cambridge 0580 Core cannot reach the top grades however well they sit the paper, and a student entered for Extended who should have been on Core can lose marks across a paper that was never pitched at them. Neither outcome is a teaching failure. Both are entry decisions.

The decision belongs to the school, which is right - they have the data. But it is a decision a parent can and should interrogate, and the window for that conversation is Year 10 or early Year 11, not March. The useful question is not "which tier is better" but "what does my child's current performance predict on each tier, and what would have to change between now and entry to make the higher tier the better bet". A school with a view on that will say so.

Where a tutor is genuinely valuable here is in the arithmetic rather than the opinion. A specialist who knows the paper structure can look at a mock script and say which marks were lost to content gaps that are fixable in the time available and which were lost to the paper being pitched above the student's current fluency. That distinction is the whole decision, and it is not visible from a percentage.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Al Manara: what the market charges and what travel buys
paragraphs: Take the home-tutoring question on its own terms, because it is a legitimate purchase and the prices are knowable. In-home one-to-one tuition across Dubai is quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52. Named specialists run AED 200-450 and beyond, TutorChase at AED 270, with premium rates reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

The gap between the in-home and online bands is not a quality difference. It is the price of a car. A tutor coming to an Al Manara villa is driving in from Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or further, through late-afternoon traffic on Al Wasl Road or Umm Suqeim Street, and doing it again in reverse. One hour of teaching takes two and a half hours to deliver, and the rate reflects that honestly.

What the premium buys is worth naming fairly: a person in the room, physical supervision, and a working environment that does not compete with the laptop it runs on. For a younger student, or a household where screen discipline is genuinely the issue, that is worth paying for and plenty of Dubai providers deliver it well. What the premium does not buy is board specialism, because travel time forces generalism - nobody fills a week with 4CH1 Chemistry students living within twenty minutes of their own villa.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and for an Al Manara family delivery is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The table below makes the comparison concrete, including the cases where the in-home option genuinely wins.

sections.heading: How practical science is actually assessed on your child's route
paragraphs: This is the question that separates a tutor who knows the syllabus from one who knows the subject, and it is the one Dubai parents most often never think to ask. IGCSE science routes assess practical skills in different ways. Some use a practical examination; some use a written alternative-to-practical paper that tests the same skills - method evaluation, variable identification, table and graph construction, anomaly handling - entirely on paper. The content being examined is similar. The preparation that helps is not.

If your child sits a written alternative paper, the useful work is paper-based: reading a described method and identifying its flaw, constructing a results table with correct headings and units before any data arrives, plotting and interpreting a line of best fit, and explaining why an anomalous point is anomalous. That is a learnable, fast-moving skill set, and a term of rehearsing titration technique in a kitchen does nothing for it.

If your child sits a practical examination, the work is different again, and a tutor working over video can genuinely prepare the thinking even where the apparatus is not shared: the sequence, the readings to take, the precision expected, the common procedural errors. What an online tutor cannot do is stand beside a burette. Schools run the practical sessions and that is where the hands-on rehearsal belongs, which is worth knowing before paying anyone for it.

One honest caution for families considering private-candidate entry, which comes up in Dubai more than elsewhere because of mid-year moves. Practical arrangements for private candidates are set by the board and the centre, not by a tutor, and they constrain which subjects a private candidate can sit at all. Check with the examination centre first, in writing, before building a plan around it.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a student in Dubai - a point worth stating plainly, because a page quoting the wrong window to a UAE parent is a page that causes real harm.

The zone rule matters more than most families realise. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is one email to your child's exams officer, and it should be in writing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why every plan should link the live official timetable rather than lean on dates restated elsewhere, including here.

Counted backwards, the pattern is the same whichever board you are on: entries close months before the papers, mocks are the last honest diagnostic, the final weeks are for timed papers under real conditions, and results arrive on a known date with a resit series available. The table lays that out with the ownership column filled in, because knowing who sets a deadline is most of meeting it.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule, stated correctly
paragraphs: This matters for any Al Manara family whose child may apply to a UAE university, and one ranking competitor in this market publishes it wrong, which makes stating it correctly worth doing carefully. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that trips families up: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. That is not what the published requirement says, and a family planning option choices around a wrong number may drop a subject they needed or carry one they did not.

For completeness, because Dubai families often hold more than one curriculum between siblings: on the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the sourced material, so none is published here - if your child is on the Diploma, that figure must come from moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and no tutoring is required for it. And requirements change - verify every line against the authority's own current page before acting on it, however recently a page like this one was reviewed.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted, and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Two checks, both free, both worth making before money changes hands. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anyone.

The eligible categories are broad - teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. There is also a rule worth knowing: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Avoid paying your child's own classroom teacher privately, however kindly it is offered.

The second check is the coursework boundary. IGCSE coursework components, where a subject has them, must be the student's own work, and the same applies to anything a student submits for internal assessment. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the assessment criteria, mark practice work, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of a submission, supply data, or edit a draft to completion. One provider in the adjacent IB market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; the risk in buying anything of that kind falls on the student.

One more thing a parent should know how to check: no individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals. KHDA regulates and inspects Dubai private schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, but it does not rate or approve individual tutors. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE and claims no regulator approval of any kind. If a provider charges a premium for an approval that does not exist, that is the clearest overpayment available in this market.

sections.heading: What happens when the right board specialist is not free
paragraphs: Availability transparency is the gap nobody in this market fills, so here it is. Some board and subject combinations are taught by a small number of people, and in the weeks before the June series the right specialist for a narrow route may not have a slot at the hour an Al Manara family needs. Pretending otherwise is how a parent ends up with somebody who nodded at a code they have not taught.

The honest options get stated rather than hidden. A different time with the right specialist. A short wait with an actual date attached. Or a closely adjacent specialist - a Cambridge Chemistry teacher taking a Pearson 4CH1 student, say - who can cover the topic you need now, with the board differences named openly so you can judge. For a student with a mock in three weeks, that adjacent match is often the better answer than a perfect one in six.

Delivery being online also means the specialist may not be in the UAE, and that is stated rather than disguised. Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the Al Manara school run. Two competitors researched in this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers without saying so, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. A family choosing a board specialist over a nearby generalist is entitled to know exactly what they are choosing.

The free trial lesson is what makes all of this checkable rather than a promise. One lesson, with the student's own marked paper on screen, with the tutor naming the code and the paper. If the fit is wrong, nothing is owed and no block has been bought.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near Al Manara who knows my child's exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: There are capable tutors within a short drive, and proximity will not tell you whether any of them knows your child's board. IGCSE is offered by Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel and OxfordAQA with different codes, papers and tiering rules, and Al Manara children attend schools in two clusters that use different boards. The test is four questions: which board, which code, which tier, and how practical science is assessed on that route. A specialist answers all four immediately. Lessons with IB Gram are one-to-one over live video, which is how the pool stops being limited by driving distance.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a villa in Al Manara?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the student's marked paper, the specimen paper and the mark scheme are visible to both sides and the annotated script stays with the student. That is the mechanism rather than a limitation: removing the drive is what allows a household in a neighbourhood between two school clusters to work with a teacher who knows their specific board and code.

faqs.question: Where is the syllabus code written down, and who at the school has it?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, and ask in writing. The entry confirmation carries the board and the four-character syllabus code - 0580 or 4MA1 for mathematics, 0620 or 4CH1 for chemistry, 0625 or 4PH1 for physics. Do not infer it from the textbook, because schools change boards and a student who joined mid-course may have covered material from two. While you are asking, request the tier your child is entered for and, for Cambridge candidates, which of the six administrative zones your centre sits in, since the timetable differs by zone.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications assessing similar mathematics. Cambridge 0580 is tiered into Core and Extended with Core capped at a lower maximum grade, and the two written papers differ in calculator permissions depending on the component. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers and a calculator permitted throughout, while Mathematics B is a single harder tier. The consequence for preparation is technique rather than content: paper structure, timing and the command words that trigger mark-scheme points all differ, and that is what board-specific experience buys.

faqs.question: What does in-home IGCSE tuition cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures, not ours. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Online, a qualified subject tutor is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Budget online tutoring starts lower, EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52, and named specialists reach AED 200-450 and beyond. The gap between in-home and online is travel, not teaching quality: one hour delivered takes a tutor about two and a half.

faqs.question: Is Core or Extended the right entry for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends on the mock evidence, and the decision belongs to the school. What matters is understanding the arithmetic: Core and Foundation tiers cap the grade available however well the paper is sat, while the higher tier offers the full range but asks questions pitched above a student who is not yet fluent. The useful question to the school is not which tier is better but what your child's current performance predicts on each, and what would have to change by the entry deadline. A specialist reading a marked mock can separate fixable content gaps from fluency problems.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE practical science assessed if lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route, and that is the first thing to establish. Some IGCSE science routes use a practical examination; others use a written alternative-to-practical paper assessing the same skills on paper - identifying variables, evaluating a described method, building results tables, plotting and interpreting graphs, handling anomalies. If your child sits the written alternative, the useful preparation is entirely paper-based and works well over video. If they sit a practical examination, the apparatus work belongs at school, though the sequence, precision and common procedural errors can all be prepared remotely.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Dubai IGCSE candidates actually sit?
faqs.answer: The June series and the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Always work from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than any restated dates, including those on this page, because provisional timetables get revised.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Cambridge exam timetable differ from a cousin's abroad?
faqs.answer: Because of zones. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and it states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Two candidates sitting the same syllabus in different countries, or occasionally at different centres, can face different dates and times. It is a single question to your child's exams officer and worth having the answer in writing before any revision plan is built around a date.

faqs.question: Is it five or six IGCSE passes that the Ministry actually counts?
faqs.answer: Five, for the British track. The published guidance requires passing five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor in this market states six subjects, which does not match the sourced requirement. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process, not something a tutoring provider performs - verify every detail on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or must it be entirely my child's own work?
faqs.answer: It must be the student's own work, and a tutor can still help substantially within that. They can teach the skill the component assesses, explain the assessment criteria in plain language, mark practice attempts, and give written questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. They cannot write or rewrite any part of a submission, supply data or a conclusion, or edit a draft to completion. The honest test for a parent: could your child explain every decision in the work unprompted? If not, the line was crossed, and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with an Al Manara family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: A tutor delivering private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no amount should be quoted at you.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a reasonable alternative for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. A group class is cheaper per hour and works well for topic revision where every student needs the same content - stoichiometry, electricity, algebraic manipulation. It works badly where the problem is specific to your child's board, tier or command-term technique, because a mixed group cannot be taught to one syllabus code. Note too that a centre with premises in Dubai operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit, a different licence from an individual tutor's MoHRE permit, and it is reasonable to ask for the number.

faqs.question: My child is moving school and board mid-course. What actually needs doing?
faqs.answer: A syllabus-to-syllabus mapping, done quickly. Changing from Cambridge to Pearson or the reverse mid-course usually means some content has been covered that the new syllabus does not assess, and some has not been covered that it does. Paper structure, tiering and practical assessment may all change too. The practical job is a written gap list the student and the new school can both see, built by comparing the two live syllabus documents rather than from memory. Do it in the first fortnight, because the gaps compound quietly and surface in a mock.

faqs.question: What should an Al Manara parent send before the first IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take ten minutes to gather. The board and syllabus code from the school's entry confirmation. The tier your child is entered for. The most recent marked paper, with whatever annotations the teacher made. And the date of the next assessment that matters, whether that is a mock or a series. With those, a specialist can name the topics and command terms losing marks in the first session rather than the third, which is the difference between four useful hours and twelve.

intro.heading: The comparison families make, and the one that matters
paragraphs: There is a conversation that happens in every Bur Dubai building. A family in Al Mankhool hears that somebody in Karama found a good IGCSE tutor, or that the Oud Metha side has better options because the schools are closer, or that Bur Dubai proper has more tutors because it has been settled longer. The comparison feels sensible. Four neighbourhoods, four markets, pick the best one. The trouble is that the thing being compared is the wrong variable.

Take the real differences first, because they exist. Al Mankhool sits between Al Mankhool Road and Khalid Bin Al Waleed Road, with Al Fahidi and ADCB on the Green Line and the BurJuman interchange at its edge; school runs mostly stay inside Bur Dubai, so a 4.30pm session holds. Karama is tighter, with the shortest runs and the worst parking. Bur Dubai proper sits along the Creek with the oldest school stock. Oud Metha runs south towards Healthcare City and Al Jaddaf, with the Red Line and a slightly longer run for anyone crossing to Festival City. The spread across all four is perhaps twenty minutes.

Now take the published prices. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across Dubai as a whole, reviewed October 2026, and nobody publishes an Al Mankhool rate that differs from a Karama rate. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table, with independents to AED 500, and the variation inside that band is about the tutor rather than the street. The neighbourhood comparison, in other words, explains neither the cost nor the quality.

What does vary, sharply, is whether anybody within driving distance has taught your child's exact syllabus. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 are different specifications. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry carries a practical or alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson 4CH1 does not. KHDA's 2024-25 figures describe 227 private schools in Dubai offering seventeen curricula, and in a belt this mixed the local tutoring supply is spread across boards rather than concentrated in one. That is the binding constraint, and it is the same constraint in all four neighbourhoods.

Which is why the answer does not change with the postcode. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That turns the question from who lives near us into who has taught 0580 to examination and is free at 5pm, and the second question has a much better answer in every one of these four neighbourhoods. The rest of this page lays out the comparison in full, then the syllabus facts that make it moot.
