dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: The IGCSE years sit between a lower-secondary stage and a post-16 route, and the comparison between neighbourhoods is weakest at the ends and strongest in the middle. These are the stages and what each one changes locally.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No public examinations, so no board and no code to match on. Support at this stage is about study habits, written structure and arithmetic fluency, all of which any competent teacher can deliver. This is the one stage where a neighbour's recommendation is genuinely as good as a specialist search, and the only stage where proximity has a real advantage.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Mankhool and Karama this is where most of the informal tutoring market sits: a neighbour, a relative, a university student in the building, often at the AED 33 to 65 budget band that Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise. For a Year 8 student who needs company and routine rather than paper expertise, that is a sensible purchase and this page is not arguing against it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes, tiering into Core and Extended for most subjects, and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. The tier decision is made by the school in Year 10 and sets the grade ceiling. This is the stage where the specialist question bites and where the neighbourhood comparison stops being useful.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Schools in all four of these neighbourhoods know their zone.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Codes beginning with four, a single tier for most subjects, and practical knowledge examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. A student revising apparatus diagrams for a practical paper that does not exist on their specification has spent weeks on nothing, and that mistake is made in every one of these neighbourhoods.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma routes
programmes.description: Where the tier and board decisions show their consequences. Receiving schools apply entry expectations by subject, and a Core-tier or Combined Science student arrives with a content gap rather than a confidence one. The route also determines which neighbourhood a family will be driving to in Year 12, which is the only point at which geography genuinely re-enters the decision.
programmes.countryNote: British post-16 provision is available inside Bur Dubai; IB Diploma provision reachable from these four neighbourhoods sits mainly in Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City. Ask the receiving school in Year 10 which tier and board it expects, and make the Year 10 tier decision with that answer rather than after results day.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Subjects are where board differences become concrete. These are the IGCSE courses we teach across the Bur Dubai neighbourhoods, each described by what its specification actually demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended tier is what post-16 science routes expect. The marks go in algebraic manipulation and in multi-step problems where a student knows every individual step and cannot sequence them under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Higher tier is the equivalent expectation. The specification differs from Cambridge in emphasis and in paper structure, which is why a tutor fluent in 0580 is not automatically fluent here.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: The mole concept is the hinge and the hardest thing to repair late. Extended tier asks for calculation chains where Core asks for recall, so the tier changes the kind of practice rather than only the quantity.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves take the largest share of lost marks, and most of that loss is unit handling and rearrangement rather than concept. Right physics in the wrong unit scores nothing, every time.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Reads easily and marks hard. The credit sits in precision: diffusion against osmosis stated exactly, a genetics cross set out in full, an extended response that answers all three parts rather than the first.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers and no separate practical component, with practical knowledge examined inside the theory. Apparatus, method and expected observations therefore have to be revised as content.

subjects.name: English Language (Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Timed writing decides the grade more than reading comprehension does. Students who draft well and write slowly lose marks that look like skill gaps and are pace problems.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510/0511)
subjects.description: Common across this belt, and frequently the wrong entry: a student who should be on first-language English is capped, and a student placed too high loses marks for accuracy. Check the entry with the school before buying anything.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application and the command terms carry the marks. Students who learn definitions and cannot apply them to unseen material sit in the middle bands with full notes.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are the two technique fixes that move grades fastest, and both are learnable in a short block rather than across a year.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Covers all three sciences and counts as two qualifications. Papers switch between sciences without warning, so revising in silos costs time that students rarely budget for.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory paper plus a problem-solving paper. The algorithmic section is where marks are lost and where good teaching is scarcest locally, which is the clearest case on this list for looking beyond the neighbourhood.

sections.heading: Al Mankhool against the next neighbourhood over
paragraphs: Set the four side by side and the differences shrink. The school stock in Al Mankhool, Karama and Bur Dubai is broadly the same mixture of British and Indian curriculum provision, within ten to fifteen minutes of each other. Oud Metha adds IB exposure and a slightly longer run for anyone crossing to Festival City or Al Jaddaf. Across all four, the practical difference in when a weekday session can start is about half an hour, and nothing in the published pricing responds to it at all.

Where the four genuinely differ is in what a family is likely to be dealing with. Bur Dubai sees the most transfers in from Indian-curriculum schooling, which means a board change rather than a subject gap: the student is not behind, they are unfamiliar with how this specification asks questions. Karama is the most price-sensitive, so the budget tier is used more there and the mismatch between a budget tutor and an Extended-tier paper surfaces more often. Oud Metha families more often face an IGCSE-to-Diploma decision rather than an IGCSE-to-A-Level one.

None of that changes the answer, which is the point of the comparison. The table sets out what actually varies, and the pattern is visible in the final column: in every one of the four, local supply of a named syllabus specialist is thin, because the belt serves several curricula at once rather than concentrating on one. A family comparing neighbourhoods is comparing commute minutes while the real variable sits in a column they were not looking at.

sections.heading: What a home tutor costs in each of these areas, and why the figure barely moves
paragraphs: A parent can verify this without taking anybody's word for it. Search the published rate pages for Dubai tutoring and look for a figure that names a neighbourhood. There is not one. Rates are published by tier and by format, which is why the same bands apply in Al Mankhool, Karama, Bur Dubai and Oud Metha. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online tier. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE.

In-home one-to-one is where a neighbourhood effect might be expected, and it mostly is not there either. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts it at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and the variation inside that band tracks the tutor rather than the street. What does respond to geography is reliability: a tutor driving to Karama at 5pm and Al Qusais at 7pm is exposed to traffic twice, and the monthly package comparison shows what that exposure costs, with AED 799 a month advertised for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For context on the household budget rather than the hourly rate, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That makes tutoring the line a family can still size deliberately. None of the figures above is an IB Gram price; ours follows a free trial lesson and a look at the student's own marked work.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same in all four
paragraphs: If the commute varies by half an hour and the price does not vary at all, the neighbourhood comparison has nothing left to decide. What remains is the question families do not usually ask: has anybody within driving distance actually taught this specification to examination? In a belt serving British, Indian and IB provision simultaneously, with seventeen curricula licensed across Dubai's 227 private schools according to KHDA's 2024-25 figures, the honest answer in all four neighbourhoods is usually no, or not this year, or not at the hour you need.

That is a supply problem, not a postcode problem, and it does not improve by moving two streets. It improves by removing distance from the search entirely. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. The shortlist then becomes everybody who has taught 0580 or 4CH1 or 0625 and is free at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, which is a much larger and much more specific set than anybody's building can produce.

There is one case where the comparison does matter, and it should be said plainly. A young child who cannot stay at a desk without an adult beside them needs physical presence, and for that family the in-home market at AED 180 to 350 an hour is the right purchase and proximity is a genuine advantage. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student who needs somebody who knows where their paper's mark scheme refuses credit, the advantage runs the other way, and it runs the same way in Al Mankhool, Karama, Bur Dubai and Oud Metha alike.

sections.heading: Who runs Cambridge and who runs Pearson in this belt
paragraphs: Families assume the board follows the school's nationality or its name, and it does not. Both Cambridge and Pearson are used by British-curriculum schools across Bur Dubai, sometimes within the same school for different subjects, and the only reliable source is the exam entry statement. It lists each subject with its board and code. One email to the school office produces it, and until you have it, any tutoring decision is being made on a guess.

The difference matters most in the sciences and in mathematics. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended and carry either a practical test sat at the centre or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson sits in a single tier for most subjects and examines practical knowledge inside the written papers. In mathematics, Cambridge 0580 tiers into Core and Extended while Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher, with different paper structures behind each.

The practical consequence for a parent in any of these four neighbourhoods is a short checklist. Get the statement. Note the code for each subject. Ask prospective tutors which of those codes they have taught to examination. Where a tutor covers several subjects, ask separately for each, because fluency in 0620 does not imply fluency in 4CH1. One syllabus code appears across the entire seven-page area cluster researched for this project, which gives a sense of how rarely this is treated as the central question it is. The same statement also names the series your child is entered for, which for a UAE centre will be June or November, and that is the date every revision plan should be counted back from.

sections.heading: The grade ceiling: Core, Extended and single tier
paragraphs: For Cambridge subjects the school enters each student at Core or Extended tier, usually during Year 10. Core covers a reduced subset of the syllabus and reaches a lower maximum grade; Extended covers the full content and reaches the top of the scale. Many families in Al Mankhool and Karama discover the tier exists only when a mock result arrives with a cap on it that nobody explained, and by then the papers have diverged and a late change is difficult.

Pearson's single-tier structure removes that decision for most subjects, which genuinely suits a student who improves late, and it is one of the few places where the board a school chose has a direct effect on a family's options. In mathematics Pearson still tiers, into Foundation and Higher, so the question does not disappear entirely. Either way the decision should be made on evidence rather than on a predicted grade: three weeks of Extended or Higher tier past-paper questions, marked honestly, tells a family more than a term of predictions.

The consequences land post-16. Receiving schools in Bur Dubai and across the Creek apply entry expectations by subject, and an Extended-tier or Higher-tier pass is generally what they look for before timetabling a science or mathematics at A Level or Higher Level. A Core-tier student can still progress and arrives with a real content gap, typically four to six weeks of focused work, which is far cheaper closed in the summer before Year 12 than discovered in October of it.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are lost, in any postcode
paragraphs: The pattern of lost marks is remarkably stable across schools and across these four neighbourhoods, which is further evidence that the local comparison is the wrong one. The single largest cause is answer length. The mark allocation is a set of instructions and students read it as a suggestion, writing one sentence for three marks. This is the dominant loss in Biology, in Business Studies and in Economics, where the content reads easily and the credit sits in completeness.

The second is abandoned method. In mathematics and chemistry a student who shows two correct steps of a calculation and stops earns more than one who writes a bare wrong answer, and students routinely do the latter because they have been taught that the answer is the point. Teaching a student to leave their working visible is a technique session, costs almost nothing, and recovers marks on every quantitative paper they sit.

The third is question order. Students work front to back, spend eleven minutes on an early question they half know, and arrive at the final structured question with no time. Teaching a student to scan the paper, bank what they can finish and return to the rest is one session of work. All three of these are board-agnostic, subject-agnostic and postcode-agnostic, which makes them the cheapest marks available to any family in this belt, whichever neighbourhood they are comparing themselves against. They are also the three things a tutor can demonstrate inside a single hour, so they are a reasonable test of whether a first session was worth paying for.

sections.heading: The June and November series, and what to do in each window
paragraphs: Two series are available to UAE candidates and the planning value of knowing which one is next is considerable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not an option for a candidate at a school in Al Mankhool, Karama, Bur Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For results, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the November series one cycle ahead, so the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com is the document to plan from rather than any date restated elsewhere.

The zone detail is worth repeating because it has consequences. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable version per zone, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If anybody in your household is revising from a timetable found online rather than the one the school issued, check the zone before trusting a single date on it.

sections.heading: Regulators and permits, across the emirates and in your building
paragraphs: A family comparing neighbourhoods inside Dubai is comparing within a single regulator. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it publishes inspection reports for every private school in all four of these areas. Those reports are free, specific and more useful than any prospectus, and they are the document to read before a transfer between neighbourhoods.

Across the UAE the picture is different and nobody in this market explains it. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate regulator.

The tutor-level rule applies identically in every one of these neighbourhoods. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval and claims none.

process.title: Get the exam entry statement
process.description: One email to the school office produces the document naming each subject's board and syllabus code. Until you hold it, every tutoring decision is a guess, and the guess is the most expensive thing in this market. Do this before contacting any tutor, including us.

process.title: Send the code and the slot you can hold
process.description: A request that says Cambridge 0580 Extended, Thursday 5pm, is matched quickly. A request that says maths tutor in Al Mankhool takes several exchanges and often ends with the wrong specification taught competently, which is the failure this whole page is about.

process.title: Free trial lesson against your child's own paper
process.description: The tutor sets questions from the student's actual specification, watches where the method breaks, and reports what they found. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. One trial lesson per student, and it catches a board mismatch before it costs a term.

process.title: A short block with a target and an end date
process.description: You receive the number of sessions, the target, and the date it finishes. Blocks end rather than renew by default. An open-ended weekly arrangement across two IGCSE years is the most expensive purchase available here and the hardest to judge.

process.title: Review on marks, not on feeling
process.description: At the end you get the evidence and a recommendation that may be to stop. For many Year 10 students after a well-aimed block, the right answer is that the technique problem has closed and the next term's money belongs to a different subject.

whyPoints.title: We tell you the comparison does not matter
whyPoints.description: Four neighbourhoods, twenty minutes of commute difference and no published rate variation. The honest answer is that the postcode is not the variable, and a provider who tells you otherwise is selling local presence rather than subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different specifications with different practical arrangements. We match on the code from the exam entry statement, which removes the commonest expensive failure: a good tutor teaching the wrong paper very well.

whyPoints.title: Every rate carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and one asks the price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates here name their source, and the February and March series is identified as India-only because it is. A plan built on an exam window that does not apply to UAE candidates is worse than no plan, and that mistake has been published to UAE parents before.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not sell
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India. Where a family genuinely needs physical presence for a young child, we will say that in-home support is the better purchase even though we do not provide it.

whyPoints.title: No regulatory claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none of it. What this page does is name what each body governs and point you to its own pages so you can check things yourself.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IGCSE tutor in Al Mankhool or in Karama?
faqs.answer: Neither, in any way that matters. The two are about ten minutes apart, serve the same mixture of British and Indian curriculum schools, and no provider publishes a different rate for one than for the other. What is thin in both is local supply of somebody who has taught a specific syllabus code to examination, because the belt serves several curricula at once rather than concentrating on one. Karama families use the budget tier more, which means the mismatch between a generalist tutor and an Extended-tier paper surfaces there more often. The constraint is the specification, not the street.

faqs.question: Do tutors charge more in some Dubai neighbourhoods than others?
faqs.answer: Not in any published rate card we could find, and you can check this yourself. Dubai tutoring rates are published by tier and format rather than by area: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, qualified online tutors at AED 150 to 300 with Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table with independents to AED 500, and specialist support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Variation inside those bands tracks the individual tutor. The one thing geography changes is reliability, because traffic costs sessions.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our building in Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every lesson for a family in Al Mankhool, Karama, Bur Dubai or Oud Metha is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, at a slot chosen around the school run. The reason is not only the published price gap between formats. It is that removing distance from the search is the only way to reach somebody who has actually taught your child's syllabus code, which is the problem a local tutor usually cannot solve.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: From the exam entry statement the school issues, which lists each subject with its board and code. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson International GCSE codes begin with a four, such as 4MA1 or 4CH1. Do not infer the board from the school's name or nationality; both appear across British-curriculum schools in this belt, sometimes within the same school for different subjects. One email to the school office produces the statement, and until you have it any tutoring decision is being made on a guess.

faqs.question: Should we move schools to a neighbourhood with better tutoring?
faqs.answer: Tutoring supply is a poor reason to change schools, because it is the one input you can fix without moving anything. Choose a school on its KHDA inspection report, its subject offer, the post-16 route it leads to and the commute you can sustain for several years. All of those are published or observable. Tutoring, by contrast, stops being a local question the moment lessons are delivered over video, so a family that moves for tutor access has paid a large cost to solve a problem that a different delivery format solves for nothing.

faqs.question: Does Pearson's single tier make it an easier route than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Not easier, but it removes a decision that can go wrong. Cambridge separate sciences and mathematics are tiered, and a Core-tier entry made in Year 10 caps the grade available, which families often discover only when a mock result arrives. Pearson sits in a single tier for most subjects, so a student who improves late in Year 11 is not held down by a decision made a year earlier. Pearson still tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Confirm paper structures and weightings with the school, because both boards revise specifications between cycles.

faqs.question: My child is on Core tier. What does that cost us later?
faqs.answer: Roughly four to six weeks of focused work before Year 12, and considerably more if the gap is left until Year 12 itself. Core tier covers a reduced subset of the syllabus and caps the maximum grade; Extended covers the full content. Receiving schools in Bur Dubai and across the Creek generally expect Extended tier, or the Co-ordinated double award, before timetabling a science or mathematics post-16. The sensible move is to ask the receiving school in Year 10 what it expects, gather three weeks of Extended-tier evidence, and make the tier case to the school with the marked papers in hand.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE schools are near Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ambassador School sits in Al Mankhool itself, with New Academy School nearby, and Dubai Gem Private School, St Mary's Catholic High School, Dubai English Speaking School and The Indian High School all within a short run across Bur Dubai and Oud Metha. Across the Creek, Deira International School and Al Ittihad Private School in Al Mamzar also run IGCSE. Boards vary between them and sometimes within them, so never assume from the name. Read the current KHDA inspection report alongside the school's own subject list; both are published and free.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for UAE students?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates. Work from the timetable your school issued rather than one found online, and check it against cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: What is an administrative zone and why does our school have one?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones so that the same paper can be sat at different local times around the world, and it publishes a timetable version for each zone. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Your child's school in Al Mankhool or anywhere in Bur Dubai knows which zone it belongs to. Ask, and revise from the school-issued version only.

faqs.question: When will my child's results arrive?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes its own results schedule per series. Those dates matter for post-16 applications more than families expect, because a conditional place may need confirming within days. Plan the resit question before results day rather than after it, since the November window gives a real second attempt and the preparation for it has to start before the first result is known.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers schools in our area, and does it cover tutors?
faqs.answer: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, is responsible for the quality of private education across Dubai, including every school in Al Mankhool, Karama, Bur Dubai and Oud Metha, and it publishes an inspection report for each. It does not license individual private tutors. That sits with MoHRE, whose private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Elsewhere in the UAE the school regulator differs: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

faqs.question: Is a budget tutor enough for Year 10?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is the one place where a neighbour's recommendation competes properly with a specialist search. A Year 10 student who needs routine, homework discipline and company can be well served at the AED 33 to 65 budget online band that Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise. The calculation changes in Year 11 and changes completely eight weeks before a series, when a tutor who cannot say whether an alternative-to-practical paper applies to your child's entry is expensive at any rate, because those weeks cannot be bought back. Match the tier to the job.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for our subject and slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when somebody will be. Putting a generalist into the slot and hoping is the quiet failure in this market, and no competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all. If your window cannot be covered, the realistic options are to move the slot, to begin with the board-agnostic technique work that any strong teacher can deliver such as answer length and question order, or to wait for the right specialist. We will say which of the three we think fits your situation.

faqs.question: Can you give us past papers or mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge, Pearson and IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, and reproducing or distributing them is infringement. A tutor works from material the student legitimately holds through their school, cites the official source and links to it: cambridgeinternational.org for Cambridge qualifications and qualifications.pearson.com for Pearson Edexcel. The school is also the holder of the correct zone timetable, which matters more to a revision plan than any copy circulating in a group chat, and it is the only authoritative source for your child's entry details.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingHeading: Stop comparing buildings, start comparing codes
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mankhool.closingBody: The comparison worth making is not Al Mankhool against Karama. It is whether the person teaching your child has taught their exact specification to examination. Ask the school office for the exam entry statement, read the board and code against each subject, and send those with your enquiry. Take the free trial lesson and let the tutor set questions from that specification rather than from a general worksheet. Then agree a short block with a target and an end date. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around the Bur Dubai school run, with post-Iftar slots during Ramadan.

Tell us the syllabus code, the series your child is entered for and how many weeks are left, and the shortlist comes back built around the dates.

intro.heading: Count the weeks first, then decide what to buy
paragraphs: Nobody searches for an IGCSE tutor in the abstract. The search happens in a particular week of a particular term, usually after a report or a mock, and what should be bought depends almost entirely on how many weeks remain before the paper that matters. A family with eighteen months is making a different purchase from a family with eight weeks, and selling both of them the same weekly hour is the commonest failure in this market.

So start with the calendar. Find out which series your child is entered for, because that single fact sets everything else. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, and a revision plan built around a March window is a plan for a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Then count backwards from the paper, not forwards from today. Eight weeks is the shortest window that reliably moves a grade, and it only works if it is spent on the specific thing the marks are leaving from rather than on a general revision programme. Sixteen weeks allows content repair as well as technique. Three weeks allows nothing except examination technique and triage, and anybody promising more than that in three weeks is selling.

The home-tutoring question has a short answer. The local market does supply in-home tuition, at a published AED 180 to 500 an hour, and a meaningful part of that rate is the journey out past Mirdif through Algeria Street or Tripoli Street in the afternoon. IB Gram does not sell it anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Al Mizhar families are one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. On a calendar-driven purchase that matters practically as well as financially, because availability near a series is tight and a tutor who does not have to drive to Al Mizhar can start this week.

One warning about the arithmetic before you do it. The weeks you have are not the weeks on the calendar. Subtract Ramadan, subtract the school break, subtract the trip already booked, and subtract the week either side of any other subject's mock, because a student revising for one paper is not revising for yours. Families routinely believe they have twelve weeks and discover they have seven, which is how an eight-week plan ends up being attempted in five.

What follows is the detail: what each term of the year has to achieve, an eight-week plan that fits around a long bus route, the series and entry deadlines counted backwards, how to choose which subject gets the weeks when several are weak, and the honesty boundary on coursework.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mizhar.programmesIntro: Where a student sits in the IGCSE cycle changes what tutoring is for. These are the stages, described by how much time each has left.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the tier decision
programmes.description: The year before the examined course, and the cheapest point to act. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October give schools an external read, and many use Year 9 results to stream Year 10 into Core and Extended routes. Nothing here is examined for a certificate, which means a fluency gap costs a few sessions rather than a grade.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Mizhar from Mirdif and Al Warqa use this year to decide tiers. A Core placement quietly closes the route to A Level in that subject two years before anybody discusses university, so Year 9 is the term to ask which tier your child is heading for and on what evidence.

programmes.name: Year 10, the year with room
programmes.description: The only year of the examined course with genuine slack. Content gaps can be repaired properly, examination technique can be built as a habit rather than drilled in a panic, and the tier decision is still open. A weekly hour started here is worth considerably more than the same hour started in the spring of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Mizhar families this is also the year to settle the practical question of when a lesson can happen, because the bus routes from Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais run long. A slot that works through Year 10 will still work in Year 11; one improvised in Year 11 usually does not.

programmes.name: Year 11, counted in weeks
programmes.description: The examination year, where every decision is a calendar decision. Entry deadlines fall months before the papers and fix both the tier and the series. Mocks arrive in the term before the live series and are the best diagnostic a family will get. From the mock onwards the work is almost entirely past papers, marked against the published scheme.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Mizhar student in Year 11 is usually carrying eight or nine subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. That is why the choice of which subject gets the tutoring hours has to be made deliberately rather than by whichever test came back worst.

programmes.name: The November resit route
programmes.description: A second attempt in the November series for a student whose June result did not reach the grade a sixth form or a route required. The window is short and the work is entirely technique and targeted content, because the content was covered once already. Entry is made through a centre and the deadline sits well before the papers.
programmes.countryNote: The practical trap locally is assuming a resit can be arranged at short notice. It cannot: the entry runs through a centre on the board's own deadline, and the student needs the window from the June result to the November papers planned rather than improvised. Ask the school's exams officer about centre entry as soon as a resit is being considered.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: When several subjects look weak, the calendar decides which gets the hours. These are the subjects Al Mizhar families ask about, with how quickly each responds to targeted work.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Responds fastest of any subject to eight weeks of targeted work, because most losses are procedural: sign errors, method not shown, multi-step questions abandoned. Past-paper volume with the scheme open moves marks here more reliably than in any other subject on the timetable.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two distinct jobs. Circuits is a conceptual topic needing teaching, which takes weeks. The practical or alternative-to-practical component is a written skill learned from past questions, which takes days. With eight weeks, do the second first.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic is the whole game and it is pure repetition, so it fits an eight-week window well. Organic chemistry and the reactivity series reward memory, which also fits. Equilibrium reasoning does not compress neatly and is better addressed earlier in the course.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The volume tempts a thin pass over everything, which is exactly wrong late in the year. With eight weeks the productive work is extended-response technique on a smaller set of topics, using precise terminology, rather than another circuit of the textbook.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing responds well to a short window because the task types are finite and the marks go to answering the specific brief: the right form, the right audience, the right register. Reading comprehension technique also improves quickly with marked practice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language with its own structure and a speaking component. The speaking element is the one most often left unrehearsed, and it is the easiest part of the subject to improve in a fortnight of practice.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation marks at the end of structured questions are both finite, learnable and quick. A student who can draw a correctly labelled diagram with the shift in the right direction has secured marks no prose can replace.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case material rather than recall of theory is what the scheme rewards, and that is a habit rather than a body of content. Eight weeks of marked practice on applying every point to the stimulus is well spent.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: The theory paper's data-representation marks are mechanical and recoverable in days. The algorithm paper requires pseudocode in the board's own conventions, which students who code fluently in Python still lose marks on, and which is learnable quickly.

subjects.name: ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers on specific software tasks under timed conditions. The gap is procedural speed rather than understanding, which makes it one of the best fits for a short intensive block: a student who has done each task six times finishes in time.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school. Tutoring in them follows the school's own approved material, because KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.

subjects.name: Examination technique across all subjects
subjects.description: Reading the mark allocation, showing method so partial credit survives, answering the command term and abandoning a question rather than sinking ten minutes in it. The single best use of a short window, because it lifts marks in every subject at once.

sections.heading: Where you are in the year, and what that changes
paragraphs: The same request means different things in September and in March. A parent asking for help in the autumn of Year 10 can buy content repair, technique habits and a tier conversation that is still open. A parent asking in the spring of Year 11 can buy past-paper work and triage. Both are legitimate purchases; buying the first in the second window is the mistake.

The table sets out what each part of the year can realistically deliver. Read it with the actual date in mind rather than the vague sense of there being time, because the gap between those two is where families lose terms. By the mock window, support in the weakest paper should already be running, not being arranged.

One point applies at every stage. The subject to fund is the one the marked papers identify, not the one that feels hardest, and in a tight window it is usually the one closest to a grade boundary. An hour spent on a subject sitting a mark or two below a boundary buys more than the same hour spent on a subject that is comfortably failing and would need a term.

Get the entry details before any of this. The statement of entry names the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series for every subject, and most parents have never opened it. Your school's exams officer will send a copy, and it turns a vague plan into a dated one.

sections.heading: The eight-week plan, written backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the shortest window that reliably moves a grade, and it works only when it is planned backwards. Start from the paper date, mark the final week as consolidation rather than new work, and fill the remaining seven with specific question types rather than topics. A plan that lists topics is a revision timetable; a plan that lists question types is a tutoring brief.

The structure below is what we actually use. Weeks one and two diagnose and attack the single biggest loss. Weeks three to five work through the next two or three recurring errors, each tested immediately on a second question of the same type. Weeks six and seven run full timed papers. Week eight consolidates, rehearses the mechanics of the day, and does no new content at all.

Two things make or break it in Al Mizhar specifically. The first is the slot: three sessions a week during an examination term has to sit at an hour the student can actually use after an hour-long bus route, which usually means later than a parent would like or a weekend morning. The second is the practice between sessions, which should be short, named specifically in the written note, and placed on evenings that are genuinely free.

Be realistic about what eight weeks cannot do. It cannot cover two years of missing content, it cannot repair three subjects at once, and it cannot change a tier. What it does reliably is convert understanding the student already has into marks they were not collecting, which in most cases is where a disappointing mock grade actually came from.

sections.heading: June or November, and the deadline that sits months earlier
paragraphs: The date that catches families out is the entry rather than the exam. A school submits entries months ahead of the first paper, and the submission fixes both the tier and the series. A family discovering in February that their child is entered at the wrong tier has discovered it too late for that series.

UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, which is worth repeating because plans built around a March window have reached UAE parents elsewhere and a date a family acts on being wrong for their country is a real cost. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask which zone your centre sits in.

Pearson's published record gives the checkable shape. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is why they are safe to plan against as a pattern. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than relying on any restated date, this page included.

For a resit the practical point is lead time. Entry runs through a centre on the board's own deadline, so a November attempt decided in September may already be outside the window. If a resit is even possible, raise it with the exams officer in the week the June result arrives rather than in the month after.

sections.heading: A home tutor or an online one, with a deadline in the way
paragraphs: The home-tutoring comparison changes when the calendar is tight, and not in the direction most families expect. Availability is the first problem. In the weeks before a series every local tutor's evening slots are taken, and the subset of them willing to drive out past Mirdif for a single hour is smaller again. A family deciding in week eight does not have the luxury of waiting for the right person to have a free Tuesday.

Reliability is the second. An in-home arrangement during an examination term depends on a car crossing Algeria Street or the Garhoud interchange between four and six in the afternoon, three times a week in an intensive plan. Over eight weeks that is twenty-four journeys, and the sessions that are lost or shortened come out of a window that cannot be extended.

Cost is third rather than first. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Over twenty-four sessions that difference is substantial, and it buys travel rather than teaching.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the table compares market options with our own model named among them. There are genuine advantages to physical presence, particularly for a younger or very restless student, and a page that hid them would not be worth reading. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a paper, working through past questions with a mark scheme on a shared screen, they rarely decide it.

sections.heading: Which subject gets the weeks when three look weak
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in this corridor is carrying eight or nine subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for. When three subjects look weak and there is one hour a week, a choice has to be made, and made deliberately rather than by whichever test came back worst.

Three rules handle most cases. First, fund the subject closest to a grade boundary, because an hour buys the most marks a mark or two below a threshold. Second, fund the subject that blocks a post-16 route ahead of one that merely looks untidy, since the consequences of the two grades are not the same. Third, where the losses look identical across subjects, fund technique rather than a subject, because command-term discipline and showing method lift marks in every paper at once.

What not to do is split the hour. Thirty minutes each in two subjects achieves the arrival and departure and very little else, and over eight weeks produces no visible movement in either. If two subjects genuinely need the work and the budget allows one weekly hour, alternate full hours rather than halving them, and accept that it is a compromise.

Mathematics deserves a note because it responds faster than anything else to a short targeted window. Most losses there are procedural rather than conceptual, and procedural losses are exactly what eight weeks of past-paper work with the scheme open repairs. If maths is one of the three weak subjects and sits near a boundary, it is usually the right answer.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the weeks that are not full weeks
paragraphs: An eight-week plan that lands across Ramadan or a school break is not an eight-week plan unless it has been written that way. In a calendar-driven purchase this is the most common avoidable loss, and it is entirely predictable in advance.

During Ramadan school days are shortened and household routines move towards the evening. A 5.30pm slot that works in October is usually the wrong one then, and a post-iftar session is usually right. Because no tutor is travelling anywhere, moving the slot costs a message rather than a renegotiation. Families who agree the shift before Ramadan begins keep their continuity; families who improvise lose three or four weeks from a window that has none to spare.

School breaks cut the other way and can be an advantage. A holiday week with no homework competing is the best possible place for three or four concentrated sessions on a single paper, and it is worth planning deliberately rather than treating as dead time. For a Year 11 student eight weeks out, a break in the middle of the window can be the most productive part of it.

Travel is a standing feature in these villa communities. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone if the slot is adjusted, which no arrangement tied to an address can do. Send the dates in advance so the plan is redrawn rather than interrupted, and resist letting a trip become a four-week gap in a window that is only eight weeks long.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, especially under deadline pressure
paragraphs: Deadline pressure is exactly when the honesty line gets tested, which is why it belongs on a calendar-led page rather than in a footnote. A student three weeks from a deadline with an unfinished piece of coursework is the situation in which somebody offers to help in a way that is not help.

The boundary does not move with the calendar. A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question the student about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any piece of work the student submits. The practical test requires no subject knowledge: feedback as questions your child must go and answer is correct, feedback as sentences they could copy in is not.

It is worth knowing what is on sale nearby. One page in the researched competitor set advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an examination malpractice trigger, and the student carries the consequence through appeals, applications and sometimes a whole qualification while the seller carries none of it. Any offer of that kind should end a conversation rather than open a negotiation.

We also decline to reproduce or supply board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and reach you through them or through the school. In a tight window that matters practically as well as legally, because official material is current while a file circulating in a parent group may be from a superseded specification and will waste weeks you do not have.

sections.heading: Starting this week, and what we will say about availability
paragraphs: Send four things: the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, the series your child is entered for, a photograph of the marked mock, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. With those, a plan can be written backwards from the paper date in a single conversation.

The free trial lesson runs about forty minutes on a past question from your child's own code, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Afterwards you receive a written read on the biggest recurring loss and how many weeks it implies, which is also the honest answer to whether the window you have is long enough. Nothing is owed if you stop there.

Availability is tightest exactly when demand is highest, which is the weeks after mocks. Late-afternoon and early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots fill first, weekend mornings fill next, and a resit specialist in an unusual subject at a fortnight's notice may genuinely not exist. We give a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a generalist, because a tutor who does not know the code costs the fee and then the weeks, and in an eight-week window the weeks are all there is.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: board, code, tier, series, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

faqs.question: My child's mock came back badly and the paper is eight weeks away. Is that enough time?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the eight weeks are targeted. A mock two bands below target normally hides two or three repeating errors rather than a general absence of knowledge, and those convert into marks quickly. The plan is written backwards from the paper: diagnose in week one, attack the biggest loss in weeks one and two, work through the next errors in weeks three to five, run full timed papers in weeks six and seven, and consolidate in week eight with no new content. What eight weeks cannot do is cover two years of missing content.

faqs.question: We have three weeks. What is honestly possible?
faqs.answer: Technique and triage, and we would rather say that than take the money on a different promise. In three weeks a student can learn to read mark allocations, show method so partial credit survives a wrong answer, answer the command term that was used, and abandon a question rather than sinking ten minutes into it. They can also decide, explicitly, which topics to stop revising. Those gains are modest and real. Anybody offering substantial content coverage in three weeks is selling rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Which exam series is my child sitting, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry names it, along with the board, the syllabus code and the tier, and your school's exams officer will send a copy. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any plan built around a March window. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable, so ask which zone your centre is in.

faqs.question: Can we arrange a November resit after a disappointing June result?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is lead time rather than willingness. Entry runs through a centre on the board's own deadline, which sits well before the papers, so a resit decided in September may already be outside the window. Raise it with the school's exams officer in the week the result arrives, not the month after. Where a resit is viable, the work is almost entirely technique and targeted content, because the syllabus was covered once already and the gap is in converting it to marks.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor be quicker to start than an online one?
faqs.answer: Almost always slower, which surprises people. In the weeks after mocks every local tutor's evening slots are taken, and the subset willing to drive out past Mirdif for a single hour is smaller again, so a family deciding in week eight may be waiting until week eleven. An online specialist in the right syllabus code can usually start within days. Published rates are AED 180 to 500 an hour in-home against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an intensive plan need?
faqs.answer: Two or three, for eight weeks, with short named practice between them. Two is enough when the diagnosis is narrow, such as a single question type in mathematics. Three is justified when there are two or three distinct recurring errors to work through and full timed papers to fit in during weeks six and seven. More than three a week rarely helps, because the student also has eight other subjects, school homework and the mandatory UAE subjects on the same timetable.

faqs.question: Three subjects look weak and we can afford one. Which do we choose?
faqs.answer: The one nearest a grade boundary, because an hour buys the most marks a mark or two below a threshold. If one of the three blocks a post-16 route, that outranks a grade that is merely untidy, since the consequences differ. And if the loss pattern looks the same across all three, buy technique rather than a subject: command-term discipline and showing method lift marks in every paper at once. What not to do is split the hour, which achieves the arrival and departure and little else.

faqs.question: Which subject responds fastest to a short window?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, by a clear margin. Most losses there are procedural rather than conceptual, which is exactly what eight weeks of past-paper work with the mark scheme open repairs: sign errors, method not written down, multi-step questions abandoned too early. ICT is next, because its practical papers are a procedural speed problem and a student who has done each task six times finishes in time. Biology responds least well late, because its volume tempts a thin pass over everything, which is the wrong work in week six.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan if Ramadan falls inside our eight weeks?
faqs.answer: It gets written in from week one rather than discovered in week four. School days are shortened during Ramadan and household routines move towards the evening, so the usual slot shifts to after iftar; because no tutor is travelling anywhere, moving it costs a message. Families who plan the shift in advance keep their continuity through it. Families who improvise typically lose three or four weeks, which in an eight-week window is half of what they bought and cannot be recovered later.

faqs.question: Is a school holiday week wasted time in a revision window?
faqs.answer: The opposite, if it is used deliberately. A week with no homework competing is the best place in an eight-week window for three or four concentrated sessions on a single paper, and for Year 11 students it is frequently the most productive stretch of the whole plan. What wastes it is leaving a weekly slot limping along while the family is travelling. Decide before the break whether it is a block or a pause, and either is fine as long as it was chosen.

faqs.question: What should a weekly note from the tutor tell us during an intensive?
faqs.answer: The question type attempted, the specific error found, and whether the same error survived a second question of the same type. In an eight-week plan it should also say what has been removed from the revision list, because triage is part of the work. What it should not say is that progress is good, which tells a parent nothing checkable. If the notes are vague for two consecutive weeks, that is the signal to change the approach rather than to wait.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish my child's coursework if the deadline is this week?
faqs.answer: No, and the boundary does not relax because the date is close. A tutor may teach the method, work a comparable example, question your child about their own attempt and point out where the reasoning does not hold. A tutor may not write, complete, redo or edit to completion any work your child submits. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an examination malpractice trigger and the student carries it through appeals and applications while the seller carries nothing.

faqs.answer: From the board or through the school, not from us. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are not ours to reproduce or distribute. In a tight window this matters practically as well as legally: official material is current, while a folder circulating in a school parent group is frequently from a superseded specification and will send your child to question styles that no longer appear, which is a weekend you cannot get back.

faqs.question: What time can an intensive session run if our bus gets in at half past four?
faqs.answer: Realistically 6.30pm or later on a weekday, and weekend mornings for two of the three weekly sessions if you can get them. Al Mizhar students on Al Warqa and Al Qusais routes arrive home late and flat, and an intensive plan that assumes a 5pm start loses the first ten minutes of every session to the student arriving in the room rather than in the lesson. Over twenty-four sessions that is several hours of a window that cannot be extended.

faqs.answer: Four things. The syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry. The series your child is entered for, with the live official timetable open. A photograph of the marked mock, which is the diagnosis. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. From those, a plan written backwards from the paper date takes one conversation. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; the privacy link explains what is held.

intro.heading: Start with the specification, not with the subject
paragraphs: An IGCSE report card gives you a grade and almost no information about what to do next. The useful starting point is the statement of entry, which lists the syllabus code for every subject the student has been entered for. Those four characters determine the paper structure, the grading scale, whether the subject is tiered, what content is examinable and which past papers are worth the student's time. Everything a tutor does downstream depends on them, and almost nobody asks for them first.

Take Mathematics. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling of C, Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 is tiered differently into Foundation and Higher, graded 9 to 1, with two papers rather than two plus two. A student revising Higher 4MA1 material for an Extended 0580 paper is working largely useful content in slightly the wrong format, and the formula sheet conventions differ.

English does the same thing less visibly. Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 is assessed on reading and writing papers with a strict mark allocation for each; English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 are different qualifications with different expectations. A student placed in the wrong one has a ceiling problem rather than a skill problem, and families in the older Dubai districts, where many students are strong but not first-language English speakers, meet this more often than the city average.

The sciences add tiering and a practical paper. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610 each run a tiered theory pair plus Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, which most UAE school centres enter candidates for. Coordinated Sciences 0654 compresses all three into two grades and excludes content the single sciences require, so revising from a single-science textbook wastes hours.

That is the whole argument of this page. A tutoring plan built from a syllabus code tells a student which topics are off their paper, which marks are method marks, and which past papers to sit under a clock. A tutoring plan built from a subject name produces a student who understands more and scores the same, which is the outcome families in Al Muteena describe most often when a previous arrangement did not work.

One caveat before the detail. Codes change between series as boards revise specifications, and a revision guide bought two years ago for an older sibling may describe a syllabus that has since been updated. The authoritative version is the specification document on the board's own website for the series your child is entered for, which is free to read and takes a few minutes to check against the contents page of whatever book is on the desk. Where this page names a code, treat it as the starting point for that check rather than the end of it, and ask the school to confirm the entry in writing.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by the paper it is actually marked on and the specific place the mark scheme stops giving credit, which is the information a revision plan needs.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 is where grades are made. Method marks survive arithmetic slips, so a student who writes nothing but a final answer loses everything on a transcription error. Algebraic fractions, bounds, and the vectors and transformations cluster are the predictable weak points.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers rather than four, graded 9 to 1, with a formula sheet convention that differs from Cambridge. Higher tier questions run longer stems with more multi-step problem solving, and the commonest loss is abandoning a question rather than writing down the partial working that earns method marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection and own-words explanation; writing is marked on content and structure separately from style and accuracy. Students lose reading marks by quoting at length instead of explaining, and writing marks by producing one undifferentiated register across every task.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: A different qualification with a different ceiling from 0500, often the right placement for a strong student who is not a first-language speaker. Marks concentrate in summary writing and in the extended response, where the task's audience and purpose must be visibly addressed.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and balanced ionic equations carry the Extended grade. An unbalanced equation feeding a calculation destroys every mark downstream, which makes equation discipline the highest-yield fix available in the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Unit conversion in pressure and moments, ray diagrams drawn without a normal, and series-versus-parallel misreading account for most avoidable losses. Writing the relationship before substituting converts arithmetic slips into partial credit.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Looks like the memorisable science and is marked on command terms. Describe, explain and suggest carry different expectations, and the enzyme, transport and excretion cluster produces the most mismatches between what a student wrote and what the scheme credits.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455
subjects.description: Case-study papers where application to the given business or economy earns the marks and generic theory does not. Students who learn definitions thoroughly and never practise applying them to an unfamiliar scenario plateau in the middle grades.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics and further routes
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended in some Dubai schools as a bridge to A Level. Useful for a DP Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics candidate, and a poor use of hours for a student still insecure on Extended content.

sections.heading: What a syllabus code tells you that a report card cannot
paragraphs: A Dubai school report gives a grade, a predicted grade and a comment. None of those tell a parent what their child should do on Saturday morning. The statement of entry does, because it names the syllabus and therefore the paper structure. With 0580 Extended on the sheet, the student has Papers 2 and 4 to prepare, the grade ceiling is A*, and Paper 4 is the longer structured paper where method marks dominate. With 0580 Core, the papers are 1 and 3 and the ceiling is C, which changes what the next two years are for.

The same logic runs through every subject. A Chemistry 0620 Extended candidate must know mole calculations and ionic equations to a standard the Core subset never requires. A Coordinated Sciences 0654 candidate can safely ignore several single-science topics and should not be revising from a single-science revision guide. A First Language English 0500 candidate is marked on precise own-words explanation; an English as a Second Language 0510 candidate is marked on summary and task-appropriate register.

Finding the codes takes minutes. They appear on the statement of entry the exams officer issues, usually a term before the series, and schools will supply them earlier on request. Writing them down and giving them to a tutor at the first contact is the single highest-value piece of administration available to an Al Muteena parent, and it costs nothing.

The failure this prevents is specific and common. A student changes school mid-course, or a tutor assumes the board the previous student used, and a term of revision goes into material that is adjacent to the paper rather than on it. The student works hard, understands more, and scores the same, because the questions in the hall were never the questions being practised.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps: where credit stops even when the answer is right
paragraphs: Published mark schemes are specific, and the specificity is where students lose marks they have earned in their heads. In Mathematics the dominant trap is the unwritten method. Marks are allocated for the correct approach and the correct substitution as well as for the final answer, so a student who does the work mentally and writes one number down loses two marks for a slip that cost them nothing in understanding. Training the habit of writing the relationship, substituting, then stating the answer with units converts several zeros a paper into partial credit.

In English the trap is quotation without explanation. A reading question asking for an explanation in the student's own words gives no credit for a copied phrase, however apt. Students who have been praised for close reference to the text sometimes read that as permission to quote at length, and the scheme simply does not pay for it. The reverse trap in writing papers is register: one essay voice applied to a letter, a report and a narrative, where the task-specific audience carries marks.

In the sciences the trap is the command term. State wants a fact and credits nothing extra. Explain wants a causal chain and gives nothing for a description. Suggest expects applied reasoning in an unfamiliar context and accepts several answers, so a student who writes nothing because they have not memorised this exact case has given up marks that were available. Command-term sorting is a dull exercise that pays immediately.

In case-study subjects like Business Studies 0450 the trap is generic theory. The scheme credits application to the business in the stem, so an answer that correctly defines economies of scale without mentioning the firm in the case earns a fraction of the available marks. All four of these traps are diagnosable from a single marked past paper, which is why the first session works on a paper rather than on a conversation.

sections.heading: A week of past-paper work that actually produces marks
paragraphs: Past papers are the most abundant free resource in IGCSE and the most badly used. The standard pattern is to work through a paper with the answers nearby, feel reasonably good about it, and learn almost nothing, because no part of that process replicates what happens in the hall. A paper is only diagnostic if it is sat under a clock without help and then marked against the published scheme by somebody honest.

A workable weekly routine for a Year 11 student in Al Muteena looks like this. One full paper under timed conditions at the weekend, phone elsewhere, no notes. Self-marking against the scheme immediately, with every lost mark categorised as content, method, misread or time. Then the tutoring session spends its hour on the largest category rather than on the first question. Then a short targeted task for midweek on exactly that weakness, ten or fifteen minutes rather than an hour.

Categorising losses is the part families skip and it is the part that makes the routine work. A paper with twelve lost marks might break down as two content, seven method and three time, in which case more revision is the wrong response entirely and the student needs to write working and manage the clock. The same twelve marks all in content means the opposite. Two weeks of categorised papers tell you more about a student than a term of reports.

There is a volume question too. Sitting four papers a week produces fatigue and sloppy marking, and the marks stop improving. One properly sat, properly marked paper per subject per week, with midweek targeted work, is enough for most students and sustainable through a whole term, which matters more than intensity in the eight weeks before a series.
