sections.heading: Home tutoring in Al Muteena: what it costs, what it buys, and what IB Gram sells instead
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a genuine Dubai market and the published rates are higher than online for comparable qualifications. Bestimate's rate work puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel included in the figure. Comparable qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Monthly in-home packages circulating in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

What the premium buys is physical presence and the attention that comes with it, which genuinely helps some students, particularly younger ones or those who will not work unsupervised. What it also buys is a round trip through Dubai traffic at the hour the whole city is moving. In the older northern districts, where Salahuddin Road and the Ittihad corridor are at their worst between four and seven, that journey is long and the tutor is paid for it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Muteena or anywhere else in the Emirates. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. That is worth saying on the page rather than after a booking.

The argument for the online format on a syllabus-led page is narrow and strong. A family hiring in-home in Al Muteena is choosing from tutors willing to drive to Al Muteena on a Tuesday evening. A family hiring online is choosing from tutors who teach Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 every week, wherever they live. For a student whose problem is unwritten method marks on Paper 4, the second pool is the one that contains the answer.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the deadline nobody mentions
paragraphs: Tiering is the quietest high-stakes decision in IGCSE. In Cambridge Mathematics and the sciences a Core entry caps the grade at C; in Pearson Mathematics a Foundation entry caps it below the grades most A Level Mathematics courses require. The decision is usually made by the school on the strength of Year 10 performance, and it is frequently never discussed with the family at all.

There is a sound case for the lower tier. A student who would score across the bottom of an Extended paper can come away with a secure C from Core rather than an insecure E, and if science or mathematics is not a prerequisite for what comes next, that is a better outcome. The case against is that the ceiling closes IB Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and most A Level science and mathematics routes, and the student rarely understands that when the entry is made.

What makes this a tutoring matter is evidence. Schools move students between tiers on timed-paper performance, not on parental preference, and a head of department presented with six weeks of honestly marked Extended papers has something to act on. If the papers say the higher tier is viable, the conversation is short. If they say it is not, the family has chosen with their eyes open rather than hoped.

The timing is the part that catches people. Entries are submitted to the board months before the exam window, and the school's internal deadline for collating a whole cohort sits earlier still. A tier conversation opened in the spring term of Year 11 has usually missed the window for the next series. Opened in Year 10 or early Year 11, it is routine. Parents in Al Muteena with a child currently in Year 10 have the most room to act and the least urgency to do so, which is exactly why it gets left.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards, and why entries close so early
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a spring sitting belongs to another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Both boards publish provisional timetables well in advance and revise them, which is why the only timetable worth trusting is the current official one.

Cambridge also divides centres into six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. Its own guidance to exams officers states that using the correct version for your zone is essential and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a Dubai family this means the timetable the school issues is the authoritative one, not one found through a search engine.

Counting backwards from a June series produces the plan. The school's internal entry deadline comes first, weeks before the board's own final entry date. Mocks sit in the winter term. A specification coverage check about twelve weeks out turns every untaught topic into a named risk rather than a surprise. The final eight weeks are the timed-paper phase, which is where most measurable grade movement happens. Then the window, then results, then the resit decision.

Pearson's published dates show how long the tail runs. Its November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. For a student who misses a target grade in June, the November series is the resit route, and the entry for it closes long before the summer ends.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and board materials: the two boundaries that matter
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but the honesty boundary still applies and it becomes critical the moment a student moves into DP or A Level investigations. The working rule is that the student produces the work and the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on it. A tutor who hands back a rewritten version has replaced the student's thinking with their own and created a problem the student will carry.

That leaves plenty a tutor can legitimately do: explain why a method is uncontrolled, ask what the student thinks the next step is, mark a practice answer against the published scheme, and show a worked example of a comparable question. What a tutor should not do is write an answer for submission, edit assessed work to completion, or supply a model response to be handed in. Families are entitled to ask any provider directly where that line sits, and a vague answer is itself informative. Some operations serving this market advertise completed Internal Assessments for sale, which is a malpractice trigger carried by the student rather than the seller.

The second boundary is copyright. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should link them at source rather than distributing copies, and a provider advertising a downloadable library of board materials is telling you about its standards in a way its marketing copy does not.

Neither boundary makes tutoring less useful. Past papers are freely available on the boards' own sites and through the school, and a session spent working one properly under a tutor's eye is worth more than a folder of material nobody opens.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects and the real hours available in an Al Muteena week
paragraphs: A revision plan written for a Dubai student has to account for subjects that do not exist on a UK timetable. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with its requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. These occupy real hours in a Year 11 week.

KHDA also prescribes how they run. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

The practical effect on tutoring is arithmetic. A Year 11 student in Al Muteena carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus mandatory UAE subjects has fewer free evenings than a plan copied from a UK revision schedule assumes. Three fixed sessions a week looks decisive on paper and collapses by week four. One well-used weekly session per priority subject, plus the timed-paper routine, survives the term.

Ramadan compresses the school day and moves the household routine, and in this district that usually means sessions shift to after Iftar or to the weekend for the month. Online delivery makes that a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. Students sitting a June series should plan the Ramadan weeks deliberately, because it falls inside the window where the timed-paper phase does its work.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and one marked paper
process.description: The first message should name the school, the year group and the codes from the statement of entry, and attach a photograph of the most recent marked paper. That is enough to identify whether the problem is content, method, misreading or time, which decides everything else.

process.title: Free trial on a real past-paper question
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor marks the student's answer live against the published scheme, names the largest category of lost marks, and says roughly how many weeks that category takes to shift. No payment is taken before it.

process.title: Fix the weekly paper routine first
process.description: Before adding sessions, set the routine: one full timed paper per subject per week, self-marked the same day, with every lost mark categorised. Most families find this alone changes the next mock, and it makes the paid hour far more useful.

process.title: Weight the sessions by distance from target
process.description: Subjects are ranked by how far the timed-paper mark sits from the target grade, and hours go to the top of that list rather than spread evenly. Covering everything equally is the commonest way a term of tutoring produces no measurable change.

process.title: Recheck against the series, not the month
process.description: Every four weeks the plan is measured against how far the series is and what the papers show. Untaught topics become named risks. If a tier conversation with the school is needed, the paper evidence is already there to support it.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code comes first
whyPoints.description: A tutor who knows the entry is 0580 Extended rather than mathematics in general can tell a student what is off their paper. That is the difference between saving a student hours and spending them, and it is the first thing we ask for.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published scheme
whyPoints.description: Practice answers are marked live against the real scheme so the student sees where credit stopped. Feeling clearer and scoring higher are different outcomes, and only the second one shows up in a series.

faqs.question: Where do I find my child's IGCSE syllabus codes?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the school's exams officer issues, usually a term before the series, and schools will provide the codes earlier if asked. Each subject carries a four-character code, and that code decides the paper structure, the tier, the grading scale and which past papers are worth sitting. Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Chemistry 0620 and First Language English 0500 are examples; Pearson uses forms like 4MA1. Writing the codes down and handing them to a tutor at first contact is the highest-value five minutes of administration available to a parent.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 the same as Pearson 4MA1 for maths?
faqs.answer: They cover similar mathematics and are structured differently. Cambridge 0580 tiers into Core and Extended and sits four papers across the two tiers, grading A* to G. Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher, sits two papers and grades 9 to 1. The supplied formula conventions differ, and Pearson questions tend to run longer multi-step stems. A student revising one board's materials for the other board's paper will be working largely relevant content in the wrong format, which usually surfaces at a mock.

faqs.question: My son gets the right answer in maths and still drops marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Usually because the method is not written down. Mark schemes allocate credit for the correct relationship and the correct substitution separately from the final answer, so a student who calculates mentally and writes one number loses the method marks whenever there is an arithmetic slip. The habit worth training is mechanical: write the relationship, substitute the values, state the answer with its unit. On a Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 that converts several zeros into partial credit, and it is the fastest improvement available in the subject.

faqs.question: Should my child be on First Language English 0500 or Second Language 0510?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications with different ceilings and different mark expectations, and the placement is a school decision worth questioning rather than accepting. 0500 marks precise own-words explanation in reading and task-appropriate register in writing. 0510 concentrates marks in summary writing and extended response, with audience and purpose carrying weight. For a strong student who is not a first-language speaker, 0510 is often the better placement; for a student capable of 0500 who was placed in 0510 on arrival, the ceiling is doing the damage rather than the teaching.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student in Al Muteena use past papers?
faqs.answer: One full paper per subject per week, under a clock, with no notes and the phone elsewhere. Mark it against the published scheme the same day, then categorise every lost mark as content, method, misread or time. The paid session then spends its hour on the largest category rather than starting at question one. A short midweek task of ten or fifteen minutes targets that same weakness. Four papers a week produces fatigue and sloppy marking; one properly sat and properly marked beats three skimmed with the answers open.

faqs.question: What does in-home tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour from Bestimate's rate work and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, with travel included. Monthly in-home packages seen in the market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Comparable qualified tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and monthly online packages around AED 799 for eight sessions. The gap largely reflects the round trip rather than the teaching.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our apartment in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and mark scheme shared on screen. For syllabus-led work that format is an advantage rather than a compromise: the tutor you can reach online is the one who teaches your child's exact paper every week, instead of whoever is willing to drive into this district at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Can a Core tier entry still get my child into A Level sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the part that catches families late. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C and omits content the Extended syllabus examines, so a student arrives at A Level or IB Higher Level having never been taught several assumed topics. Most A Level science and mathematics courses, and IB Higher Level sciences, expect the Extended or Higher tier. If the post-16 plan needs those, the tier conversation has to happen in Year 10 or early Year 11, because entries close months before the exam window.

faqs.question: How do I get the school to move my child to Extended tier?
faqs.answer: With timed-paper evidence rather than a request. Schools make tier decisions on performance, and a head of department shown six weeks of honestly marked Extended past papers has something concrete to act on. Sit the papers under exam conditions, mark them against the published scheme without generosity, and bring the raw marks. If they support the move, the conversation is short. If they do not, the family has made an informed decision instead of a hopeful one, which is also a useful outcome.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually sat in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any schedule built around a spring sitting belongs to a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six administrative zones with a timetable per zone, and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so trust the timetable your school issues over anything found online.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses a grade in the June series?
faqs.answer: The November series is the resit route for both boards, and the entry for it closes much earlier than families expect, often while results are still being digested. Pearson's published pattern shows how long the tail runs: its November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. Decide quickly, confirm the entry with the exams officer, and check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or a science investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying content, question an experimental design, explain what the published criteria reward and mark practice work against them. A tutor cannot write the piece, edit it to completion or supply a model answer for submission; the work has to be the student's own. Ask any provider directly where it draws that line. Some operations serving this market advertise completed assessed work for sale, and the consequences of using one fall on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we get tutoring for at once?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Rank subjects by how far the latest timed-paper mark sits from the target grade and put the hours at the top of that list. Two subjects worked properly move more grades than five worked thinly, because thin coverage changes nothing measurable in any of them. If three subjects genuinely sit near a boundary, a short exam-term block across those three with full papers weekly is the shape that works, and it is also the point at which cost becomes the real constraint.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai school's KHDA rating tell me whether my child will get the grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, judging the whole school across many measures. It is a fair signal about the institution and a poor predictor for an individual subject set. The thing that predicts an IGCSE grade is a full past paper sat under exam conditions and marked against the published scheme. If you want to know where a student stands, that takes an afternoon and tells you more than any inspection report will.

faqs.question: Do mandatory UAE subjects reduce the time available for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: Yes, and plans copied from UK revision schedules routinely ignore it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. A Year 11 student here carries those on top of eight or nine IGCSE subjects. The realistic shape is one well-used weekly session per priority subject plus the timed-paper routine, not three fixed sessions that collapse by week four.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers our exact board and time slot?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. An unusual combination, a specific Pearson code at a specific hour on a specific evening, does occasionally come up empty. The honest options are a different time, a different tutor with a proper handover, or a wait with a date attached. A tutor working from the wrong specification is worse than no tutor, because the student spends a term practising questions that will not appear on their paper.

intro.heading: The school run in Al Nahda, and the two windows it leaves
paragraphs: Everything about tutoring in this neighbourhood follows from one fact: Al Nahda sits against the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, and Al Ittihad Road runs alongside it carrying one of the heaviest commuter flows in the country. Private schools across the catchment finish the academic day between roughly 14:30 and 15:15. Bus loops along Al Nahda Road and Damascus Street put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45, and students travelling to Al Garhoud, Festival City or across the boundary arrive later than that. By 16:30 the road is at its worst.

What that leaves is two usable windows on a term-time school night, not an open afternoon. The first runs from roughly 15:45 to 17:00, while the student is still in school mode and before the household's evening starts. The second runs from roughly 19:30 to 21:15, after the family has eaten. Between them sits the mandatory subject load that every Dubai private school carries - Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required regardless of the licensed international curriculum - which sets homework like anything else and takes up more of the evening than parents expect.

A tutor travelling to the house has to land inside one of those two windows having crossed the city. The early one collides with the worst of the outbound flow; the late one asks someone to drive in at 19:00 and home again after 21:00. The published Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour includes that travel, which is why in-home arrangements in Al Nahda drift towards Friday and Saturday within a month or two. That drift is the real cost, because it puts six days between a lesson and the homework it was meant to fix.

The second thing that shapes the week here is that not every child in the neighbourhood is on the same school calendar or under the same regulator. The Dubai side of Al Nahda sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority; across the boundary, Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Term dates, inspection frameworks and even the examination board a school uses can differ between two children on the same bus route, and a tutoring plan built on a neighbour's experience will not fit.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and we state it before anybody spends anything. What the online format gives an Al Nahda family is the ability to use the narrow 15:45 window and the long weekend block differently, with no travel at either end and nothing cancelled because Al Ittihad Road has stopped moving.

sections.heading: The Al Nahda week, timetabled: where each subject's session actually fits
paragraphs: This is the part of a tutoring decision that nobody writes down, and in this neighbourhood it determines whether a plan lasts past week three. Start from arrival: between roughly 15:00 and 15:45 for most students, pushing past 16:00 for those travelling to Al Garhoud, Festival City or across the Sharjah boundary. Then subtract the mandatory subject homework. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit and allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, which in practice means Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies occupy real evening time.

What remains is two windows, and they suit different subjects. The 15:45 to 17:00 window is short, the student is still in working mode, and it is ideal for drilling: twenty non-calculator maths questions marked as they go, a set of biology mark-scheme answers, twenty-five stoichiometry calculations. The 19:30 to 21:15 window is longer and better for anything that needs a single run - a physics problem set, an English reading response, a chemistry reasoning chain.

Then there is the weekend, which is the most under-used asset in this catchment. Saturday morning is the only time in the week with no competing homework and a student who is not tired, and it is where diagnosis belongs: a timed past paper, marked properly, turned into a written list. Families who use Saturday for a general catch-up session and Tuesday for a general catch-up session get two versions of the same hour. Families who use Saturday for diagnosis and Tuesday for correction get a loop that works.

An in-home tutor cannot flex across those three slots. One visit a week is the realistic ceiling at the published Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, and in this neighbourhood that visit migrates to the weekend because the weekday drive is punishing. Online delivery is what makes the short-slot-plus-long-slot shape affordable, and that shape is worth more than either slot alone.

sections.heading: Two regulators on one bus route: what differs across the Al Nahda boundary
paragraphs: Al Nahda is one of the few UAE neighbourhoods where schooling questions genuinely cross an emirate line, and it changes more than most families expect. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and which inspects on a published six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Across the boundary, Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education in that emirate.

The Sharjah authority's remit is broader than inspection. It and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum approval and fee approval sit with the emirate regulator, not only quality judgement. For a family weighing a Dubai-side school against a Sharjah-side one a few minutes away, that means two different approval regimes and inspection reports that cannot be read against each other as though they used the same scale.

The practical consequences for a tutoring plan are term dates, examination arrangements and the board a school uses. Two students on the same Al Nahda street can be sitting Cambridge and Pearson specifications respectively, in different term structures, with different internal assessment calendars. Any advice a parent receives from a neighbour should be checked against their own school's position rather than assumed to transfer, and that is the single most common source of confusion we hear from this neighbourhood.

For completeness, since families here move between emirates more than most: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Ras Al Khaimah sits with its Department of Knowledge; and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

sections.heading: Which board, which code: getting the right tutor for the paper your child sits
paragraphs: Because this catchment mixes schools from two emirates and several curriculum traditions, the examination board is not a safe assumption. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580, tiered Core and Extended, and now sets a non-calculator written paper on both tiers. Pearson's International GCSE in Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with two two-hour papers and a calculator permitted on both. Specification B is 4MB1, structured with a shorter first paper and a longer second.

In the sciences, Cambridge runs Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate sciences, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Pearson's equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 separately, or Science Double Award 4SD0. Cambridge separate sciences assess practical skills through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which applies is a centre-level arrangement rather than a student choice.

The reason this matters for choosing a tutor is that the same child, on the same content, needs different practice depending on the code. A student on Cambridge 0580 has to be drilled for a non-calculator paper; a student on Pearson 4MA1 does not. A student sitting the alternative-to-practical paper needs training in reading described methods and identifying real sources of error; a student sitting a practical test needs tabulating and planning discipline. A tutor matched by board name alone can spend a term preparing for the wrong paper.

On series: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so no Al Nahda family should be planning around a March examination. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the board's live official timetable rather than any restated date.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term dates and the parts of the year that change the plan
paragraphs: A tutoring schedule in this neighbourhood has to survive three predictable disruptions a year, and planning for them beats improvising. The first is Ramadan, when school days shorten across the UAE and the useful study window moves. The practical pattern is that late morning becomes available and the early afternoon does not, and that an evening session works better after Iftar than before it. Families who keep the same weekly slot through Ramadan usually lose several sessions; families who move the slot by agreement keep them.

The second is the examination period itself, when school internal assessments, mocks and external papers cluster. Counter-intuitively this is often the right time to reduce tutoring frequency rather than increase it, because what a student needs in an examination fortnight is sleep and timed practice rather than new content. A block that is scheduled to end with the examinations is better than one that runs through them out of habit.

The third is the long summer break, which is the most valuable and most wasted block in the IGCSE years. There is no competing homework, no commute and no mandatory-subject load. Eight to twelve hours across July and August closes the kind of gap - algebraic fluency, non-calculator arithmetic, graph work - that takes a whole term to close during the school year. The summer between Year 10 and Year 11 is the single best window available to an Al Nahda family.

The fourth item is not a disruption but a difference: term dates may not match across the boundary. A Sharjah-side school and a Dubai-side school can break at slightly different times, which matters for households with children in both. Confirm your own school's calendar with the school rather than from a general UAE calendar, and tell us the dates when we set the schedule so the plan is built around them rather than interrupted by them.

sections.heading: Home tutor or online: what the travel actually costs in teaching minutes
paragraphs: The usual comparison is made in dirhams, so try it in minutes instead. A tutor travelling from New Dubai into Al Nahda at 16:30 spends forty to seventy minutes each way. A one-hour lesson is therefore a two-and-a-half hour commitment, of which teaching is sixty minutes. At the published Dubai in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, the family is paying for the whole commitment whether or not the invoice itemises it, and the tutor is pricing it that way because the alternative is working for less than their rate.

That arithmetic produces three downstream effects a parent feels. The session migrates to the weekend, because nobody sustains the weekday drive. The frequency drops to one, because two visits a week is five hours of travel. And the tutor pool narrows to those who will make the journey, which is a selection on willingness to drive rather than on subject expertise. Those three effects do more damage to an IGCSE grade than the price does to a household budget.

Compare the published online band for a qualified subject tutor, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across the Dubai market, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. The same budget buys more sessions, and the sessions can sit in the narrow 15:45 weekday window as well as the long weekend one. The market's own packaged figures make the same point: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Where in-home genuinely wins is worth naming rather than arguing away. A younger child who will not engage with a screen, a household with unreliable broadband, or a student who needs someone physically present to stay on task - in those cases presence is the right purchase and the premium is justified. Every figure quoted here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026; none is an IB Gram price. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at any price, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted, and the arrangement to avoid
paragraphs: Anyone inviting a tutor into their home should ask the permit question first, and in the UAE the answer is public. Private tutoring is permit-regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fees listed and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor working regularly has no financial reason to be without one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published - Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties - so treat any figure circulating online as unverified.

The arrangement to avoid is paying your child's own classroom teacher privately. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document; the principle - that the person assessing your child should not also be paid by you - is sound anywhere in the Emirates.

A third category is different again. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. We describe what these bodies do; we claim nothing from them.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Nahda, and what the first month looks like
paragraphs: Send five things and the match becomes quick: the school and which emirate it sits in, the syllabus codes from the examination timetable, the tier where one applies, the two or three subjects that actually matter, and the nights of the week each subject's homework is set. The last of those is the item nobody includes and the one that decides whether a slot survives. Add your school's term dates if they differ from the Dubai norm.

The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, one tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards rather than agreed in advance. Its purpose is a fit decision rather than a sales conversation, and if the answer is no, you say so and we match again. A student who does not want to talk to their tutor will not learn from them, and that is cheaper to find out in week one than in month three.

The first paid session should be diagnostic rather than instructional: a past paper or a substantial section of one, sat under something close to timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, and turned into a written list of three to six named weaknesses with the marks lost beside each. You keep that document whether or not you continue with us. Everything after it is measured against the list rather than against the syllabus, which is what stops a weekly session becoming a habit with no output.

Then the shape: one short weekday slot pinned to the right night for drilling and correction, one longer weekend block for diagnosis and for subjects that need an unbroken run. Review against the school's next assessment rather than after an arbitrary number of sessions. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses, we operate no office or centre in the Emirates, and we would rather state both here than have a family discover them later.

process.title: Send the codes and the emirate
process.description: The syllabus codes from the examination timetable, the tier where one applies, and which emirate the school sits in. Al Nahda spans two regulators and two possible term calendars, so the school's own position matters more than the neighbourhood's.

process.title: Tell us which night each subject is set
process.description: Maths on Monday, physics mid-week, English at the weekend - every school differs. Pinning the short slot to the right night is the difference between a session that unblocks real work and one that handles something from last week.

process.title: Use the free trial to decide fit
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, fee discussed afterwards. Watch whether your child talks for a reasonable share of the hour and whether the explanations land. If the answer is no, say so and we match again rather than defending the first choice.

process.title: Diagnose on Saturday, correct midweek
process.description: Use the long weekend block for a timed paper marked properly and turned into a written list, then the short weekday slot to correct against it. Two general catch-up sessions a week are two versions of the same hour; this is a loop.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled against the bus, not the calendar
whyPoints.description: Buses reach Al Nahda between roughly 15:00 and 15:45 and later for cross-boundary routes, which leaves two usable windows rather than an open afternoon. We plan slots against those windows instead of offering whatever time was free.

whyPoints.title: Two short-and-long slots, not one long drive
whyPoints.description: Published Dubai in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour include a forty to seventy minute drive each way at peak, which is why in-home arrangements here become weekend-only. Online delivery makes the short-plus-long shape affordable.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, including the practical route
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 sets a non-calculator paper and Pearson 4MA1 does not; a centre sits either a practical test or the alternative paper. Matching by board name alone can mean a term of preparing for the wrong paper.

whyPoints.title: Both sides of the boundary explained
whyPoints.description: Dubai-side schools answer to KHDA; Sharjah-side schools to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. We publish the full emirate regulator map because families here need it and nobody else does.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here belongs to the provider that published it and carries the month it was read. We publish no success rate, star rating or student count, because none of those could be produced if you asked for the underlying data.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start for a student in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Two windows work. Schools across this catchment finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, and buses along Al Nahda Road and Damascus Street put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45 - later for those travelling to Al Garhoud, Festival City or across the Sharjah boundary. That makes a 15:45 or 16:00 start viable for a short drilling block, and 19:30 to 21:15 the second window after the family has eaten. The mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies homework usually fills the gap between them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our home in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. We state that before a family spends anything rather than afterwards, and it is written the same way on every UAE page on this site. The Dubai market does supply in-home tutors at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel; this page sets out what the travel costs in sessions and in tutor choice so you can judge the trade.

faqs.question: Why do in-home sessions in Al Nahda always end up on the weekend?
faqs.answer: Because the weekday drive is punishing. A tutor coming from New Dubai at 16:30 budgets forty to seventy minutes each way on Al Ittihad Road, which turns a one-hour lesson into a two-and-a-half hour commitment. Few tutors sustain that twice a week, so the arrangement migrates to Friday or Saturday within a month or two. The problem is not the day itself but the gap it creates: six days between a lesson and the homework it was meant to fix, which is where the benefit leaks away in cumulative subjects.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we actually buy tutoring for?
faqs.answer: Two or three, not the whole timetable. An IGCSE student typically sits eight to ten subjects and there are only two usable windows on a school night in this neighbourhood, so spreading hours thinly produces a plan nobody can keep. Diagnose the weakest subjects first with marked papers, then aim the hours at the ones where marks are genuinely recoverable. Biology and business studies often need a short drilling block rather than weekly teaching, which frees the long slot for physics or maths.

faqs.question: My child goes to a Sharjah-side school. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods as well as regulating quality, while the Dubai side answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Term dates, examination arrangements and the board a school uses can all differ. Advice from a neighbour on the other side of the boundary may not transfer, so confirm your own school's calendar and codes rather than assuming they match.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes should I send before booking an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Whatever appears on your child's examination timetable. Common ones in this catchment are Cambridge 0580 for mathematics, 0610, 0620 and 0625 for the separate sciences, 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences; and Pearson 4MA1 or 4MB1 for mathematics, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the sciences, or 4SD0 for Science Double Award. Add the tier and, for Cambridge sciences, whether the centre sits a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Those details change the practice regime entirely.

faqs.question: How should we use Saturday for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: For diagnosis, not for a general catch-up. Saturday morning is the only block in the Al Nahda week with no competing homework and a student who is not tired, which makes it the right time for a timed past paper marked properly against the published scheme and turned into a written list of named weaknesses. Then use the short weekday slot to correct against that list. Two general sessions a week are two versions of the same hour; diagnosis plus correction is a loop that actually closes gaps.

faqs.question: Should tutoring continue through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the slot moved rather than the frequency cut. School days shorten across the UAE, the early afternoon becomes less usable and late morning opens up, while an evening session generally works better after Iftar than before it. Families who keep the same weekly time through Ramadan tend to lose several sessions to clashes; families who agree a different time keep them. Tell us your household's preference in advance and we schedule against it rather than against a default.

faqs.question: When is the best time of year for an Al Nahda family to buy IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 10 and Year 11, which is the most under-used block in the whole two years. There is no commute, no competing homework and no mandatory-subject load, so eight to twelve hours in July and August closes the kind of gap - algebraic fluency, non-calculator arithmetic, graph work - that would take a full term to close during the school year. Most families here start in Year 11 after a mock, by which point the same money buys exam technique rather than foundations.

faqs.question: Is one long weekly session better than two short ones for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, which is why the best arrangement in this neighbourhood is one of each. Physics, English reading response and chemistry reasoning chains need an unbroken run, so they belong in a weekend or 19:45 block. Mathematics fluency, biology mark-scheme answers and stoichiometry respond far better to short frequent drilling with immediate marking, which fits the 15:45 window. A single long session a week - what in-home tutoring here usually becomes - serves the first group and underserves the second.

faqs.question: Do I need to ask an IGCSE tutor in Dubai about a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the answer is public so there is no reason for evasion. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount quoted online as unverified.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Al Nahda student sit for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November available as a resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a March examination in Dubai is built on incorrect information. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework where the specification includes it?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor may teach the published assessment criteria, question a plan before work starts, explain why a section does not meet a descriptor, mark a draft against the criteria and say plainly that it is below standard. A tutor may not write it, redraft it to completion or supply the content, because the work has to be the student's own. This market contains providers who offer otherwise, and the consequence of using one falls on the student rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: What does the first month of online IGCSE tutoring actually look like?
faqs.answer: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor first, to settle fit, with the fee discussed afterwards. Then a diagnostic session: a timed past paper or substantial section, marked against the published scheme, producing a written list of three to six named weaknesses with the marks beside each. Then the loop - a short weekday slot pinned to the right night for correction, a longer weekend block for diagnosis and for subjects needing an unbroken run - reviewed against the school's next assessment rather than after a set number of sessions.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingHeading: Tell us the bus time and the homework nights
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Nahda, the information that makes a plan work is unglamorous: what time your child actually gets home, which nights each subject sets homework, which emirate the school sits in and which syllabus codes are on the examination timetable. With those, the shape follows - a short weekday slot in the 15:45 window for drilling and correction, a longer weekend block for diagnosis and for the subjects that need an unbroken run. Send them over and the first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor: one lesson, fee discussed afterwards, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The term you are in decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Quoz is almost always a time-pressured search. A report has come home, or a mock has been marked, and there is a date at the end of the year that suddenly feels close. The useful question is not which tutor is strongest in the abstract. It is what this particular term can still achieve, given how many weeks remain and which paper the marks are going on.

Start with the calendar, because it is the only fixed thing. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate sitting in Dubai sits June, with November available as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Both boards publish provisional timetables ahead of a series and both revise them, which is why you should read the official timetable rather than a date written on a tutoring page.

Then count backwards. Internal deadlines come first and they are set by the school, not the board: coursework submission where a subject still carries it, the school's own mock window, the final entry deadline the exams officer works to, and the point at which changing tier between Core and Extended stops being possible. Two Al Quoz students at different schools can be in very different positions in the same week of the same term because of this.

Al Quoz itself shapes the practical side. The district is largely industrial by land area, with housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3, bordered by Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. Children travel outwards to school in several directions, so the realistic weekday start is between 5pm and 5.30pm depending on whether the run goes towards Al Barsha or across Al Khail. IB Gram delivers lessons into Al Quoz homes as live one-to-one video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are an India-only service.

One more thing shapes an Al Quoz plan: the cluster of schools the district feeds into is mixed. British and Indian curriculum schools sit within a few kilometres of each other, and their mock windows and internal deadlines can be six weeks apart. That is most of an eight-week block, so a plan copied from a neighbour's child at a different school is likely to be aimed at the wrong fortnight.

What follows is the plan rather than the pitch. The term-by-term table shows what each part of the year has to achieve. The board calendar table gives the series and the checkable results dates. The eight-week table shows what a realistic block of work looks like week by week. Then the cost table, the tier decision, the equivalency rules and the academic honesty boundary, so that by the end you know what to book and when to stop.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: Al Quoz children sit IGCSE through one of two boards, sometimes both in the same timetable, and arrive there from several different lower-secondary routes. Each programme below is described by what it means for planning the term rather than by its history.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subjects are identified by a four-digit code and that code decides everything: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Many subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with the Core tier capped at grade C or 5 depending on the grading scale the school uses. Papers are set per tier, so the tier decision changes which papers the student practises.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For an Al Quoz family that means the school's own timetable is the authority, not a timetable found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run differently: 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended. Assessment is wholly written in most subjects, with practical skills examined on paper, and some subjects are available in a modular structure where units can be sat across series rather than all at the end.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and revises them, so the entry and timetable position must be read from the live official document. Results timings are checkable: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. These tests are diagnostic rather than certificating, and their value to a family is that they identify weak strands in English, Mathematics and Science while there is still time to act without an examination deadline attached.
programmes.countryNote: In practice this is the cheapest point at which Al Quoz families can fix a problem, and the one most often skipped. A Year 9 student weak on algebraic manipulation becomes a Year 11 student weak on everything 0580 builds on top of it, at which point the same repair costs three times as many sessions.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into
programmes.description: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools run IGCSE at 16 and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. The subject and tier decisions made in Year 10 constrain that choice: a Core-tier Mathematics student is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, and discovering that in Year 11 is too late to do much about.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single best reason for an Al Quoz family to take Year 10 seriously rather than treating IGCSE as a staging post. The tier decision is a post-16 decision wearing a different hat, and it is usually taken by a school deadline in the middle of a term.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Quoz families ask about most, with the code and the component where marks actually go. The codes matter: a tutor who cannot tell you whether your child sits 0580 or 4MA1 cannot plan a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended and Higher carry the algebra, trigonometry and functions content that A Level and IB both assume. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they are method marks thrown away by unshown working, and premature rounding that breaks an otherwise correct multi-step answer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level IB. It introduces calculus and more formal function work. Students who find 0580 Extended comfortable but 0606 hard usually have a fluency gap rather than an understanding gap.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where Extended candidates lose most. Practical skills are examined on paper, so the student must be able to describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it, and that writing is a trainable skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, stoichiometry and organic chemistry account for the largest share of dropped marks. The usual failure is an answer that names the right substance without the equation or the units, which in most mark schemes scores nothing at all.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume makes Biology look like a memory subject, and students revise it as one. The marks are in command terms: describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different response shape, and a correct fact in the wrong shape earns nothing.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Two or one IGCSE grades covering all three sciences, sat by students who are not taking the separate subjects. The breadth is wide and the depth is shallower, so revision has to be scheduled rather than improvised; students routinely run out of time on the topic they met first.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection and close inference rather than retelling. Writing is marked on structure and control as much as content, and the most common lost marks come from answers that summarise the passage instead of analysing how it works.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and application to the stimulus material decide the grade. Evaluation has to reach a judgement rather than list both sides, and a generic answer that never touches the case study in front of the student loses the application marks entirely.

subjects.name: ICT (0417) and Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: ICT carries practical components with strict output requirements, where presentation errors cost marks that have nothing to do with understanding. Computer Science rewards pseudocode written in the board's own conventions rather than in whichever language the student happens to know.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. They sit on top of a full IGCSE load, which is why timetable pressure in Year 11 is a real cause of underperformance.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Quoz means in practice
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Quoz, as parents use the phrase, means one-to-one teaching that happens at home on a weekday evening without another car journey. IB Gram delivers exactly that as a live online session into Al Quoz homes, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

Separating the two halves of the phrase is worth doing. The home part is about where your child sits and when, and that is delivered as searched. The tutor-in-the-room part narrows your choice to whoever is qualified in the right subject, holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, is free in the slot and is willing to cross Al Khail Road at the busiest hour. Each of those is reasonable; together they produce a very short list.

For IGCSE the narrowing bites in a specific way. Boards matter. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0580 for years may not know the Edexcel 4MA1 Higher paper structure, and the student does not have time for them to learn it. Selecting on board and code rather than on driving distance is the whole gain, and it is only available once the lesson stops depending on a car.

So the plan on this page is built around the calendar rather than around geography. Where you live in Dubai sets the hour of the session. What series your child sits, which board, which tier and which paper is losing marks sets everything else, and that is what the tables below work through.

sections.heading: The academic year, and what each part of it has to achieve
paragraphs: Families often arrive with a vague sense of being behind and no sense of against what. The table below fixes that by setting out what each part of the year is for. Nothing in it is a board deadline; these are the school-side realities that decide whether tutoring is prevention, repair or triage.

The first term of Year 10 is the cheapest place in the whole two years to intervene, and almost nobody does. A student who is shaky on algebraic manipulation in October of Year 10 can be fixed in six sessions. The same student in February of Year 11 needs the same six sessions plus everything built on top of the gap in the meantime, which is where a reasonable hourly rate turns into an unreasonable total.

The second thing the table shows is where the decision points are. Tier changes between Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, have a school deadline. Entry decisions do too, and the school's exams officer works to the board's final entry deadline, not to the family's timetable. Once those have passed, the plan is fixed and tutoring is working inside it.

Read your own school's calendar alongside this. The Al Quoz cluster includes British and Indian curriculum schools with different mock windows, and the gap between two of them can be six weeks, which is most of an eight-week block.

There is one more use for the table, which is deciding not to book. If your child is in the first term of Year 10 and the only evidence is a single disappointing topic test, the proportionate response is to wait for the second data point rather than to start a standing weekly session in October. Tutoring works best against a pattern, and one test is not a pattern.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Edexcel sessions for a Dubai candidate
paragraphs: This is the part nobody else in this market publishes. Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IGCSE queries, the word November returned no hits at all: no session named, no entry deadline, no results date. So here is the position, stated carefully and with the limits marked.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting in Dubai. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so every plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date. The checkable results reference points are these: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The practical consequence for an Al Quoz family is simple. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and they are handled by your school's exams officer. If your child might need a tier change or a late entry, that conversation belongs with the school now rather than after the mock results arrive.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, counted out week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the useful planning unit, and it is roughly what a family has between a disappointing mock and the point where cramming takes over. Six to twelve focused sessions across that window will change one component. The same hours squeezed into the final fortnight mostly produce a tired student and no grade movement.

The structure below is what a sensible block actually looks like. Note what is in week one: diagnosis, not teaching. A specialist reading two marked scripts can usually say within forty minutes whether the problem is content, technique or timing, and those three problems need completely different work. Skipping that step is how families spend eight weeks fixing something that was never broken.

Note also what is in week eight: stopping. The plan has an end. Open-ended tutoring that nobody reviews is the most common way to overspend in this market, and it is far more expensive than paying a high hourly rate for a short block. If the component is fixed at week six, the right move is to finish early.

Between those two points the pattern repeats: a timed paper, marking against the mark scheme's own wording, an error log, and targeted teaching on what the log shows. It is unglamorous and it works, which is the usual relationship between those two things.

Two practical notes on running a block from Al Quoz. If the eight weeks include the school's own revision programme, do not duplicate it; find out what the school is covering and aim the sessions at what it is not. And if the family is travelling during the window, keep the sessions rather than pausing them, because the timed-paper rhythm is the part that carries the gain and it survives a change of time zone perfectly well.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: making the tier call honestly
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-leverage choice in the whole two years, and it is frequently made for the wrong reason. A Core entry caps the available grade. A Higher or Extended entry a student cannot cope with produces a worse grade than a Core or Foundation entry they could have handled comfortably. Both mistakes are common and they pull in opposite directions.

The honest test is not what the student can do with unlimited time and a textbook open. It is what they can do on a timed past paper from the harder tier, today, with no help. If that paper comes back at the bottom of the harder tier's range, there is a decision to make about whether eight weeks of work closes the gap or whether the capped tier is the better grade.

The decision also reaches forward. A Core-tier Mathematics student is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, so a tier chosen for comfort in Year 10 can close a post-16 door in Year 12. That is worth saying out loud at the point the decision is taken, because schools often present it as an administrative matter.
Whatever you decide, the deadline belongs to the school. Ask your child's subject teacher when the tier must be confirmed and work backwards from that date, not from the examination date.

One caution about how the question gets framed at parents' evenings. A teacher recommending the capped tier is usually protecting a student from a grade collapse, which is a legitimate aim, but it is not the same aim as keeping a post-16 route open. Both considerations are real and they conflict, so the useful thing a family can bring to that conversation is evidence: a recent timed paper from the harder tier, marked honestly.

sections.heading: What a term of IGCSE tutoring costs around Al Quoz
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work up, which is the opposite of how this is usually presented. Budget online tutoring in Dubai starts low: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 per hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that level you are typically buying a university student or a general tutor, which can be entirely appropriate for homework supervision and is not appropriate for diagnosing why an Extended Chemistry candidate keeps losing stoichiometry marks.

The middle band is where IGCSE work usually sits. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist rates run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. All of these are other providers' published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Now convert to the number that matters. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Where the money is wasted is not the hourly rate. It is buying a whole term of general revision when the student was losing marks on one component, and it is continuing after the problem is solved because nobody set a review point. For context on the wider household budget, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: five IGCSE subjects, not six
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that makes a foreign school certificate usable for UAE university admission and employment, and most pages in this market do not mention it at all. One that does tells parents their child needs six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and a wrong number on this topic changes what a family makes their child sit.

The published British-track rule is five. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises many families whose children are sitting them anyway as KHDA mandatory subjects.

The American track works on test scores instead: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, the source we read publishes no points threshold, so none appears here.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, submit or expedite equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it; it is a process the family completes through the official channel. And requirements change, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before you plan a subject list around it.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and where the line falls
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma does, but the honesty question arrives anyway, usually around practical write-ups, portfolio pieces and ICT practical components. The rule is the same in every case: the work submitted must be the student's own, and a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on it.

What that looks like in a session is a tutor reading the student's draft, saying which part does not meet the criterion it was written for, and teaching the student how to see that for themselves. What it never looks like is a tutor editing the document. A workable test: after the session, could the student explain and defend every change in their own words? If not, the line has been crossed, and the school's academic honesty policy decides the consequences.

There is a second boundary around materials. We do not publish, reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright. We reference it and link to the official source, and your child's school will have proper access to what the subject needs.

This matters more in this market than it should. One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an integrity breach with the risk sitting on the student, and the reason to state the boundary clearly is that the alternative is being quietly lumped in with it.

sections.heading: Starting mid-term from Al Quoz, and what we will not promise
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Tell us the board, the subject code, the tier and what the last two marked papers looked like, plus the school so that the plan can follow its calendar. We match a specialist in that board and component. The trial lesson is free, happens before any payment, and is diagnostic in purpose rather than promotional.

Then the parts most pages leave out. We will not promise a grade. Nobody can, and any provider who does is selling you a sentence rather than a service. We will not tell you tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or progression, because that is a false claim about a regulatory process. And when no specialist is free for a narrow request at the hour you want, which genuinely happens in the weeks before a series, we will say so and tell you when the slot is likely to open rather than substituting a generalist.

On the legal side, two facts worth having. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. Separately, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office or centre.
What is left is the thing you are actually buying: a specialist who knows your child's board and paper, a plan with an end date, and a review point where you decide whether to continue.
