sections.heading: The bus window, and the slot it leaves you
paragraphs: Begin with a document most parents have never asked for: the school transport office's route sheet for your child's bus. It shows which communities the route serves and in what order. That order, not the distance to the school, determines when your child walks through the door, and the spread between the first and last drop on a typical eastern-suburbs loop is around forty minutes.

The table below sets out the patterns we see from this area, with the realistic arrival window for each and the first tutoring slot that survives a full term rather than looking workable in September. Two notes on reading it. Year 11 students anywhere in this cluster lose the early evening from January, because school revision clinics take it. And the arrival window assumes the student then eats and changes, because a lesson that starts with food in one hand delivers perhaps forty useful minutes out of sixty.

The pattern across the table is consistent. Short routes from Garhoud and Festival City allow half past five. Longer loops through Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar push the first realistic slot to half past six or seven. Anything beginning in Al Khawaneej should be planned at half past seven. And Saturday morning outperforms every weekday option in reliability, which is the single most useful thing on this page for a household that has already tried and failed with a weekday slot.

This is also where the in-home comparison lands most sharply in Al Rashidiya. A tutor driving here for a six o'clock booking crosses the airport approaches at their worst, so the arrival risk the family just escaped is reintroduced at the other end of the hour. An online session begins on the hour regardless, which is not a sophisticated argument but is the one that decides how much teaching you receive across thirty weeks.

sections.heading: The Year 11 week: which subject can actually take the hour
paragraphs: A Dubai Year 11 student is carrying nine or ten IGCSE subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which KHDA requires in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and times on a 40-minute lesson unit. Add coursework, mocks and a school revision programme and the honest conclusion is that one tutored hour a week is what the diary holds. Two is possible for a very organised student with no co-curricular commitments. Three is a plan that fails in February.

So the question becomes which subject gets the hour, and the answer depends on two things rather than one: where the largest fixable gap is, and which subject can use a tired evening hour productively. Those are not the same consideration and families only ever apply the first. A student whose weakest subject is Additional Mathematics but whose only available hour is half past eight should not spend it there, because demanding new technique at half past eight produces errors to unpick next week.

The table sets out the main subjects against the homework load they generate, whether the hour tolerates being late in the evening, and what the hour is best spent on in each. Read the third column as the practical constraint. Biology, Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science all survive a late slot because the useful work is answer structure, evaluation technique and mechanical procedures. Mathematics, Physics and Additional Mathematics do not.

There is a third consideration worth naming: whether the subject's marks are being lost to content or to technique. Technique work, command terms, answer structure, timing, tabulation and graph presentation, tolerates a late hour and transfers across subjects. Content work needs an alert student. If the only hour available is a tired one, buy the technique work, in whichever subject, and let the school's teaching carry the content.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year: when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a year-round scheduling view, which is odd, because the Dubai calendar interrupts tutoring more than most. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises the evening entirely. Eid holidays land at different points each year. The summer break is long, hot and almost entirely unused for academic work. And the exam season itself removes the weeks most families expect to use for revision, because study leave is not the same thing as free time.

The table below sets out the windows across a typical academic year, what each is good for, and what reliably goes wrong in it. The headline for an Al Rashidiya family is that there are roughly three genuinely productive stretches in a school year, and the first of them, the autumn term, is the one almost nobody uses because the examination still feels distant.

Ramadan deserves its own paragraph because it is handled badly so often. School days shorten, Iftar reorganises the evening, and a six o'clock slot that worked in November no longer fits. Families who agree the arrangement before the month starts keep continuity through it; families who do not tend to lose the month entirely and restart in a worse position. Post-Iftar sessions work well for some households and not at all for others, and late morning on non-school days suits others again. The only wrong approach is improvising in week one.

The summer is the genuinely wasted resource. There is no competing homework, no fatigue from the bus, and no school revision programme to work around, which makes it the best available window for foundational work: algebraic fluency before Year 11, or the quantitative skills that underpin physics and chemistry at once. A short summer block is frequently worth more than a term of in-year sessions, and it costs the same per hour.

sections.heading: Two or three children, one quiet room
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya is a villa district and most households here have more than one school-age child. That changes the scheduling problem in a way no tutoring page addresses: two lessons cannot run simultaneously in a house with one room that has a door, and siblings arriving on different buses do not become available at the same time. Families discover this in week two and usually respond by cancelling one of the two engagements.

The workable patterns are straightforward once named. Consecutive hours on the same evening, younger child first while they still have attention and older child second, using the same room in turn. Or split across two evenings, which protects the household's dinner but means two evenings are committed instead of one. Which is better depends on whether the children fade at the same time, and the only way to know is to try it for a month.

Festival City's staggered pick-up times are the complication specific to this area. Where an older and a younger sibling attend the same school, the older one frequently arrives up to an hour later, which makes the obvious plan, both children at six, physically impossible. Build around the later arrival rather than the earlier, and accept that the younger child may be doing homework while the older one is in a lesson.

One more practical point. Where both children need support in the same subject area, it is tempting to put them in the session together. Resist it unless they are genuinely at the same point, which siblings rarely are. A shared session aimed at the midpoint between two students teaches neither of them, and it is the one economy in this area that reliably fails. If the budget only stretches to one engagement, buy one child a proper hour rather than two children half of one.

sections.heading: Four things that break when the slot is wrong
paragraphs: The failure modes are predictable and all four get blamed on the tutor. The first is arrival lateness: a student who walks in at twenty-five past four for a half past four session arrives hot, hungry and ten minutes behind, and the first third of the lesson becomes a recovery period. Across a term that is a third of the money spent on settling down.

The second is homework displacement. A slot placed too late means homework must happen after the session, which pushes bedtime back, which makes the following day worse. Parents then move the session earlier, into the arrival window, and reintroduce the first problem. The way out is to accept a later bedtime one night a week, or to move the session to Saturday, rather than oscillating between two unworkable options.

The third is cancellation drift. A slot that collides with anything, a school trip, a clinic, a sports fixture, gets cancelled rather than moved, and three cancellations in a term destroys the continuity that was most of what the hour was buying. This is where the delivery format matters more than it sounds: an online session can be moved to Thursday with a message, while an in-home visit requires somebody to re-plan a drive across the city and is usually written off instead.

The fourth is the quiet one: the student stops being honest. A fifteen-year-old who is exhausted at the session time will not say so, because the family is paying and they know it. They will attend, nod, and absorb very little, and the first evidence will be a report that has not moved. Ask your child directly, after three or four weeks, whether the hour is working and whether the time is right. In our experience of this area their answer is unusually accurate and almost nobody asks for it.

sections.heading: Delivering a lesson into an Al Rashidiya villa: what the setup needs
paragraphs: Since the lesson arrives over video rather than through the door, the household has to provide three things, and they are modest. A room with a door that closes, for the hour. A device the student can write on or in front of, so the tutor sees working as it is produced. And a connection that holds, which in this area is rarely the constraint people expect it to be.

The writing surface is the one that actually matters and the one families underestimate. A tablet with a stylus is ideal. A laptop with a phone propped on a stand pointing at a page works perfectly well and costs nothing extra. A shared document is excellent for tables, data and typed written work. What does not work is a student describing their working aloud while the tutor guesses, which is how a mathematics or physics session wastes half an hour.

The room matters more in a villa with several children than it does in an apartment, because the quiet room is contested. Decide in advance which room is the lesson room and whose turn it is, rather than negotiating it at six o'clock each week. Families who settle this in the first week notice the difference immediately, and families who do not generally report that the lessons feel scattered without identifying why.

For younger students a parent should be in the house, which is a safeguarding point rather than a technical one. For Year 10 and 11 students, independence in the session is appropriate and usually better. What a parent should receive instead is the work set, the marking and a short written note of what happened, so the household can see progress without sitting in the room.

sections.heading: Choosing the one subject the week can hold
paragraphs: If a household has one reliable hour, the choice of subject matters more than the choice of tutor. The framework we use with Al Rashidiya families has three questions. Where is the largest gap that can actually be closed in a term? Which subject can use the specific hour available, given how tired the student will be at that time? And is the loss in that subject content or technique, because technique transfers to other subjects and content does not.

That third question is the one that changes decisions. A student losing marks across three subjects on command terms, answer structure, timing and presentation does not have three subject problems. They have one technique problem showing up three times, and an hour spent on it in any one subject improves the other two. Families who identify this get three subjects' worth of improvement from one subject's worth of spending, which is the best available outcome from a constrained diary.

The evidence for all of this sits in the autumn mock scripts, which the school produces for free and which most families glance at and file. Those scripts show whether a paper was finished, whether answers matched the command terms, whether tables and graphs cost presentation marks, and whether the errors cluster in particular topics. That is a better diagnostic than any conversation, and reading it properly is the step we would urge before any booking.

Where the mocks say the problem is a specific content area in a specific subject, buy that subject and place the hour early in the evening. Where they say technique, buy whichever subject fits the hour available and ask the tutor explicitly to work on answer shape rather than content. Where they say pacing, buy timed sections and nothing else. The diary constraint stops being a limitation once the hour is aimed correctly.

sections.heading: Starting, with the timetable in hand
paragraphs: Send four things. The school's weekly timetable including which afternoons finish late. The bus route sheet or your child's typical arrival time. The syllabus codes from the exams officer, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers and a tutor must be matched to the right one. And the autumn mock scripts if they exist.

Then nominate the slot rather than asking us to suggest one. You know your household and we do not. We will tell you honestly whether we can staff that hour with a specialist in the subject you need, and if we cannot, we will say so rather than proposing a time we know will fail. In this area six o'clock, half past seven and Saturday mornings are the hours we can most reliably staff, which conveniently matches the hours that actually work.

The free trial runs in your nominated slot with the tutor who would teach your child. Use it to check two things the sales conversation cannot tell you: whether the tutor can describe your child's syllabus papers from memory, and whether your child was still thinking at the end of the hour. Then ask your child privately, a few weeks later, whether the time is right. Changing the slot is free and keeping a failing one is not.

Finally, the advice we would give regardless. If your child is in Year 10, establish the slot now while the evening is still available; a slot that exists before January survives January. If they are in Year 11 with mocks done, read the scripts before spending anything. And if the only hour you have is a tired one, buy technique rather than content, because technique is what a tired student can still absorb and what improves more than one subject at a time.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start in Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Six o'clock for most students, half past seven for Year 11 from January, and half past five only where the child attends a Garhoud or Festival City school on a short bus route. The decisive factor is not distance but where your child sits on their bus route: an eastern-suburbs loop can put forty minutes between the first and last drop. Ask the school transport office for the route sheet. Saturday mornings at half past nine are the most reliable hour of the week in this area and the one we suggest most often.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our villa in Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Other providers arrange that, at published Dubai rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. IB Gram does not: we do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. The practical objection specific to this area is that a tutor driving here for a six o'clock booking crosses the airport approaches at their worst, so the lateness you just escaped on the school bus reappears at the start of the lesson. An online session starts on the hour.

faqs.question: How many subjects can a Year 11 student really be tutored in?
faqs.answer: One, realistically, in most households here. A Dubai Year 11 carries nine or ten IGCSE subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which KHDA requires in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and times on a 40-minute lesson unit. Add coursework, mocks and a school revision programme and there is one reliable weekday hour. Two is possible for a very organised student with no co-curricular commitments. Three is a plan that collapses in February, having been paid for since September.

faqs.question: Our only free hour is half past eight. Is that worth using?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject and the type of work. A late hour is genuinely useful for command terms, answer structure, evaluation technique, pseudocode and trace tables, and reviewing marked work. It is close to useless for new mathematics, new physics or Additional Mathematics, because errors generated by a tired student have to be unpicked rather than simply repeated. If half past eight is the only hour, buy technique work in whichever subject fits, or move to a Saturday morning instead.

faqs.question: How should we handle tutoring during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Agree the arrangement before the month starts rather than improvising in week one. School days shorten and Iftar reorganises the evening, so a six o'clock slot that worked in November no longer fits. Post-Iftar sessions suit some households well; late morning on non-school days suits others; some families prefer to pause for the month and resume immediately after. All three are fine. What loses a term is cancelling week by week, because the slot is gone by the time the household wants it back.

faqs.question: We have two children who both need help. How do we schedule it?
faqs.answer: Either consecutive hours on one evening, younger child first while they still have attention, using the same quiet room in turn, or split across two evenings if both children fade at the same time. Build around the later arrival where school pick-ups are staggered, which in Festival City can mean an older sibling arriving an hour after a younger one. Do not put them in the same session unless they are genuinely at the same point: a lesson aimed at the midpoint between two siblings teaches neither.

faqs.question: What does a session need from our side if it runs online?
faqs.answer: Three things, all modest. A room with a door that closes, nominated in advance rather than negotiated each week. A way for the tutor to see written work as it is produced: a tablet with a stylus is ideal, and a phone propped over a page works perfectly well. And a parent in the house for younger students, though not in the room for a Year 11. What does not work is a student describing their working aloud while the tutor guesses at what is on the page.

faqs.question: Our tutoring slot keeps getting cancelled. What are we doing wrong?
faqs.answer: Probably nothing except choosing the wrong hour. Three cancellations in a term destroys the continuity that was most of what you were buying, and the usual cause is a slot that collides with school clinics, trips or fixtures. Two fixes. Ask the school for the term calendar and place the slot where nothing recurring lands. And move sessions rather than cancelling them, which an online slot allows with a message, while an in-home visit requires re-planning a drive and tends to be written off instead.

faqs.question: Is the summer break worth using for IGCSE work?
faqs.answer: It is the most under-rated window in the Dubai year. There is no competing homework, no fatigue from the bus, and no school revision programme to work around, which makes it the right time for foundational work: algebraic fluency before Year 11, or the quantitative skills that underpin physics and chemistry simultaneously. A short summer block is frequently worth more than a term of in-year sessions at the same hourly rate, and it leaves the student starting the year ahead rather than catching up.

faqs.question: Should sessions continue during study leave and the exam season?
faqs.answer: Taper rather than intensify. Study leave is not free time: students are sitting papers, recovering between them and revising to the school's own schedule. The useful work in that window is timed practice on a paper that has not been sat yet, and nothing new. Families who book extra sessions during study leave usually find them cancelled or unproductive. The work that should have happened intensively belongs in the eight to ten weeks before study leave, finishing as it begins.

faqs.question: Does the exam board matter when we are only choosing a time slot?
faqs.answer: It matters for who you book, not for when. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different structures and formula provision, and Dubai schools frequently mix boards by subject within one school. Get the syllabus codes from the exams officer in writing rather than from your child, then match a tutor to the code. Scheduling and matching are separate problems, and solving the diary with a tutor who teaches the wrong paper is not a solution to either.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the hour is being used well?
faqs.answer: Three checks. Is work set between sessions and marked before the next one, because most of the consolidation happens between lessons and a tutor who sets nothing is selling company. Does the session begin with a discussion of errors rather than a cold introduction. And can your child tell you, after a month and in private, that the hour is useful and the time is right. That third answer is unusually accurate in our experience and almost nobody asks for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects in the same hour?
faqs.answer: No, and offers to do so should be declined. An hour split between two subjects gives neither enough time to set work, review marked work and teach something, which is the cycle that makes a weekly slot work. The only sensible version of covering two subjects is alternating weeks, and even that halves the pace in each. If the household genuinely has one hour and the student has two weak subjects, pick the one where the hour can do most and accept the trade.

faqs.question: When is the best time of year to start a slot in this area?
faqs.answer: The autumn term, and it is the window almost nobody uses because the examination still feels distant. Three things are true in the autumn that are not true later: the school has not yet started taking the early evening for revision clinics, the content is still being taught for the first time, and the student is not yet tired. A slot established in Year 10 or in the autumn of Year 11 tends to survive the spring. A slot created in the spring usually does not.

Find it from the bus route sheet and the school calendar, nominate it rather than letting a provider offer you theirs, and then aim it at the work your child can still absorb at that time of the evening. Send us the timetable, the arrival time, the syllabus codes and the autumn mock scripts, and we will tell you honestly whether we can staff that hour with the right specialist and what the hour should contain. The trial lesson runs in your slot, and nothing is charged before it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-safa.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects by board and code, not by year group. Tell us the subject, the syllabus code on your child's entry and which paper is costing marks, then use the free trial to check the fit before anything is paid.

intro.heading: The code on the entry decides almost everything else
paragraphs: Two children in neighbouring villas in Al Safa can both be in Year 11 studying IGCSE Mathematics and be sitting genuinely different qualifications. One is entered for Cambridge 0580, tiered into Core and Extended, with a grade ceiling attached to the Core route. The other is entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, untiered, with Foundation and Higher papers that work on a different model and a formula sheet positioned differently. The textbook on the shelf may be right for one of them and wrong for the other.

This is the single most common correctable error we find in Al Safa households. A family buys revision guides on the strength of the subject name, the student works through hundreds of questions in the wrong style, and the mock result is read as weakness in the subject. It is not weakness in the subject; it is a year of practice calibrated to somebody else's examination. Checking the code with the school's exams officer takes one email and it is the first thing we ask for.

Beyond the code, the differences that matter are tiering, paper count, grading scale and where the formula information sits. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped below the top grades. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are generally untiered, which removes an entry decision and replaces it with a requirement to match past-paper practice to the right board. Grading also varies: some subjects report on 9 to 1 and others on A* to G, and the two scales are not interchangeable when a sixth form states an entry requirement.

The second theme of this page is where marks actually go, subject by subject. In Mathematics it is method marks lost to unwritten working and misread command words. In English Language it is answering the question the student would have preferred to a question that was asked. In the sciences it is the practical component, assessed in most UAE centres through a written alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards method writing rather than laboratory time. These are diagnosable in a single session from a marked script.

On delivery there is no ambiguity. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and the Dubai in-home market is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel by other providers if a family wants that. Our Al Safa tuition runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and the official mark scheme visible to both people at once.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-safa.programmesIntro: An Al Safa family usually meets IGCSE across three stages, and each one needs a different kind of help. Naming the stage is the quickest way to avoid buying the wrong thing.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the syllabus starts
programmes.description: Three years of general curriculum in which the habits that decide IGCSE grades are formed or not formed: showing working, converting units, writing a conclusion that refers to evidence, reading a question twice. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October where a school uses them. Content gaps at this stage are shallow and cheap to close.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Safa this is the stage families almost never book and the stage at which a weekly session pays for itself most clearly. The schools are close enough that a 4.30pm slot is easy, and a child of twelve concentrates better then than at seven in the evening.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal papers, with the entry decided partway through: board, subject set and, for Cambridge, tier. Most subjects are examined by two or three written papers, with science adding a practical or alternative-to-practical component. The entry deadline sits months before the exam, which is what makes a tier conversation in March too late to matter.
programmes.countryNote: The bulk of our Al Safa IGCSE work sits here, and the shape of the enquiry is consistent: a January mock that disappointed, four months of usable time, and a parent unsure whether the problem is the subject or the preparation. Reading the marked script usually answers that inside one session.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: Some schools in the Al Safa cluster run A Level after IGCSE and others run the IB Diploma, with a few offering both. The choice changes the next two years substantially: three or four subjects examined linearly, against six subjects plus an Internal Assessment in each and the Extended Essay. IGCSE grades are the main evidence a sixth form uses when setting entry conditions.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Safa family sometimes has to move a child at sixteen to reach the route they want, because the school that suited a British primary does not always run the post-16 programme they prefer. Knowing that in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is worth more than any amount of late tutoring.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside IGCSE
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson.
programmes.countryNote: The consequence for an Al Safa household is a fuller week than the IGCSE subject list implies, and fewer genuinely free evening hours. It is also why these subjects do not count towards the five required for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, which surprises families every year.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Safa families ask for most often, named by code where the code matters. Use this list to say something more specific than the subject name when you enquire; it changes which tutor we put forward.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Tiered, with Core capped below the top grades. Most lost marks are method marks that were never written down, plus algebraic manipulation that is accurate but slow. Extended candidates lose ground on functions, transformations of graphs and multi-step problems where the first step is not obvious.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers, with the formula provision and question style differing from Cambridge enough to matter. Students moving between resources find the Pearson questions longer in setup, which rewards reading carefully before calculating anything.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking, with the writing tasks marked for purpose and audience as much as accuracy. The commonest loss is a student writing a competent piece that does not do the task set, which is a planning failure rather than a language one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition plus reading response. Strong readers lose marks summarising a passage when the question asks how the writer achieves an effect, and the timing is tight enough that an unplanned composition rarely recovers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-dense rather than conceptually hard, which misleads students into thinking reading counts as revision. Genetics problems need a fixed layout, and extended responses need the command term answered rather than the topic described.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole and concentration calculations under time pressure are the reliable difficulty, alongside organic chemistry naming and reaction conditions. Qualitative analysis tests are predictable in form and therefore high-yield revision.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost Extended candidates most, usually because circuit reasoning was never secured. Graph work, units and the difference between a definition and a derivation account for a large share of avoidable marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Untiered, two papers each, with practical understanding examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. Question phrasing differs from Cambridge, so past-paper practice has to come from Pearson or the calibration is wrong.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with marks for application to the specific business in the stimulus. Students who learn definitions and apply them generically plateau, because the mark scheme rewards using the given numbers and the given context.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation decide the grade. A correct diagram drawn without labelled axes earns less than a student expects, and extended answers that explain without judging lose the evaluation marks entirely.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithm design and pseudocode. The practical difficulty is writing pseudocode that a marker can follow, and trace tables, which students treat as mechanical and then make arithmetic errors in under pressure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a first language and as a foreign language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language. Not counted among the five required subjects for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track.

sections.heading: What parents in Al Safa mean by an IGCSE home tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is about the home, but the need usually is not. What families want is somebody who knows the schools here, who can be held to something, and who will turn up. Those are fair expectations and they deserve a direct answer rather than a redirection into marketing.

The direct answer on format: IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Al Safa tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market in Dubai is genuine and is published at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel by Bestimate and by independent home tutors, so a family who specifically wants somebody in the room has somewhere to go, and this page will not pretend they do not.

The direct answer on what actually matters: whether the tutor teaches the right code. An Al Safa student entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 needs a tutor who works from Pearson papers and knows where the formula provision sits. A tutor living four streets away who works from Cambridge 0580 resources is a worse match than a specialist who happens to be elsewhere, and no amount of proximity changes that.

The direct answer on accountability: it comes from documents rather than presence. A written diagnosis after the first session, a named topic list by fortnight, a halfway review on comparable questions, and a session recording a parent can watch. That is more checkable than a tutor at a kitchen table, and it does not depend on who lives nearby.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: The two boards most Al Safa schools use are Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, and they differ in ways that change how a student should prepare. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with the Core route capped below the top grades. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are generally untiered. That single difference removes an entry decision on one board and creates a significant one on the other.

Exam series differ in their practical detail too. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached them on 22 January 2026.

Cambridge adds an administrative layer families often miss. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in and read paper times off that version only.

A caution on the February and March series, which has misled UAE families before. That series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. Any revision plan or deadline built around a February or March Cambridge window is wrong for a child sitting exams in Dubai, and the correction is worth making immediately if a household has been working to one.

sections.heading: Grading scales, and why a sixth-form requirement can be misread
paragraphs: IGCSE results do not all arrive on one scale. Depending on the subject and the board, a grade may be reported on 9 to 1 or on A* to G. Both are in current use, and the two are not directly interchangeable. A sixth form stating an entry requirement of grade 6 and a family holding a certificate showing a B have to do a translation, and getting it wrong in either direction causes avoidable distress.

The practical rule is to ask the receiving school to state the requirement in both scales, in writing, for the specific subject. Al Safa students regularly apply to schools that use a different convention from the one their own school reports in, particularly when moving between a Cambridge-heavy and a Pearson-heavy school. The admissions office will have an answer; it just is not usually on the website.

The second thing families misread is what a grade boundary means. Boundaries are set per series, after the papers have been sat, and they move. A student who scored a particular raw mark in one series cannot assume the same mark yields the same grade in the next. That is one reason we do not publish boundary tables: they belong to the boards, they change, and reproducing them would be both a copyright problem and a disservice.

What follows for a revision plan is modest and useful. Work from how many marks a student is losing and where, not from how close a grade looks. Marks are the currency the examiner deals in; grades are the output of an arithmetic a family does not control. A tutor who can point at four specific recoverable marks on a script is more useful than one who discusses a target grade.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing, by subject
paragraphs: Marked scripts are far more informative than reports, and the patterns repeat across subjects. In Mathematics the largest recoverable category is method marks that were never written down. A multi-step question awards marks for the relationship and the substitution as well as the answer, and a student who works mentally and writes one number collects nothing when that number is wrong. Making working visible is a habit, not knowledge, and it is worth several marks a paper.

In English the dominant loss is answering a different question. A student reads about a passage, recognises the topic, and writes what they know rather than what was asked. The directed writing tasks are marked for purpose and audience, so a competent piece aimed at the wrong reader scores poorly. Planning for two minutes before writing is the intervention, and students resist it until they see the mark difference on a timed comparison.

In the sciences it splits three ways. Content gaps are real but smaller than parents expect. Command-term failure is large: describe answers given to explain questions, and no comparative word in a comparison. And the practical component, assessed in most UAE centres through a written alternative-to-practical paper, is neglected because revising it does not feel like revising science, even though it tests clearly specified and coachable skills.

In the humanities and business subjects the losses concentrate in application and evaluation. Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455 both reward using the specific stimulus provided rather than reciting a framework, and both award evaluation marks that a student who only explains will never earn. That is a writing structure, and it can be taught in a handful of sessions once the pattern is visible on a script.
bullets: Maths: method marks lost to unwritten working, recoverable within weeks
English: tasks answered to the wrong purpose or audience, fixed by two minutes of planning

sections.heading: The practical science question when lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection and it deserves a straight answer. A tutor over live video cannot run an experiment alongside your child. What the tutor can do is prepare the component that is examined, which in most UAE centres for Cambridge science is a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory assessment. Confirm the component with the exams officer, because it varies by code and centre.

That paper tests a narrow and specific set of skills. Identifying independent, dependent and control variables. Describing a method in a sequence somebody else could follow. Reading an instrument to the correct precision. Plotting and interpreting a graph. Spotting an anomalous result and saying why it is anomalous. Suggesting an improvement that addresses the actual source of error rather than repeating a generic line about repeating the experiment. Every one of those is a writing and reasoning task.

For Pearson Edexcel sciences the practical understanding is examined inside the two written papers rather than in a separate component, which changes the preparation rather than removing it. Students still have to describe methods and interpret data, and they still lose marks for sequence and precision. The difference is that the questions arrive mixed in with theory rather than grouped.

The hands-on work belongs to the school and should. Where a tutored hour adds value is translation: a student who has done the experiment and still cannot describe it in the examiner's language is losing marks on something they already understand. Sitting with the official mark scheme and rewriting their own method until it earns the marks is the highest-return hour available in the month before a series.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys an Al Safa family
paragraphs: Set the comparison up as a price difference rather than a philosophy. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate's 2026 table and independent home-tutor listings. Published qualified online subject tutor rates run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The spread between those two bands is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and the honest description of what it purchases is a car journey.

For Al Safa the journey is short in distance and awkward in timing. The neighbourhood sits inside its own school catchment, so a tutor living in Al Safa or Al Wasl has a quick run, while anyone else is crossing Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Wasl Road at pick-up. That shrinks the in-home pool to whoever is both nearby and free at 4.30pm, and being nearby and free is not the same as teaching Pearson 4CH1 well.

Below both bands sits the budget end, which deserves a fair hearing rather than dismissal. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; the budget online band overall is AED 45 to 150. For a Year 8 student who needs structure and someone to check that homework has been attempted properly, that band can be enough. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series who needs mark-scheme-level diagnosis, it generally is not.

Above both sits the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate AED 200 to 450 plus, and the premium band at AED 500 to 650, where BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate estimates weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, against advertised packages of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Every figure here belongs to the named provider; none is ours.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, and the five subjects that count
paragraphs: Al Safa families planning a UAE university route meet equivalency eventually, and meeting it in Year 10 is better than meeting it in Year 13. For the British track the Ministry of Education requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that matters for subject selection is this: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student taking exactly five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not have five that count. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement for UAE candidates, which is not what the sourced clarification states, so it is worth reading the rule rather than a summary of it.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so no IB equivalency figure should be published or trusted without a moe.gov.ae page behind it.

Two boundaries. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry and the emirate authorities run; IB Gram does not perform them, speed them up or guarantee an outcome, and we point parents to the official channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. What IGCSE tutoring can do is affect the grades that feed the subject count, which is a narrower and more honest claim than the one some pages make.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator map and the mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually. For an Al Safa parent the useful habit is to read the current published band on KHDA's own listing rather than a rating quoted on a third-party page, which may be two inspection cycles old.

Elsewhere in the country the map differs, which matters on relocation. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by almost none of the competitor pages in this market.

On mandatory subjects, the federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for the two groups. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.

KHDA also sets the language of instruction for these subjects and requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them, which is a credential a parent can ask a school about directly. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any Arabic or Islamic Education tutoring material can be described.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit and a parent may reasonably ask about it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any figure circulating online is unverified until found on an official source.

An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is legally different from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and occupies no UAE premises, and no page of ours should suggest that a regulator or an examination board has approved or accredited us, because none has.

The academic-honesty boundary belongs in the same section because it is the same kind of promise. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, complete or dictate coursework or any assessed work. One seller in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an academic-integrity breach and the consequence falls on the student. We also reference syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes at their official source rather than reproducing them.

process.title: Get the syllabus code from the exams officer
process.description: One email to the school settles the most consequential question: which board and which code, per subject. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 need different past papers and different practice, and a family can be a year into the wrong one without anybody noticing.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a past-paper question
process.description: The trial runs on a real question from the correct board rather than as an introductory chat, so you can see whether the tutor's explanation lands with your child. No payment and no card are needed, and if the fit is wrong we will try a different tutor.

process.title: A diagnostic from the marked script
process.description: Send the most recent marked paper. The first session sorts lost marks by cause rather than by topic: method marks not written, command terms missed, content genuinely absent, or time run out. Those four need completely different work.

process.title: A written topic plan by fortnight
process.description: You get the block mapped out: which topics in which fortnight, when new teaching stops, and which papers your child sits between sessions. A visible plan makes a cancelled session's cost visible too, which tends to protect the slots.

process.title: Fixed slots on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked on GST around the Al Safa school run, usually from 4.30pm on weekdays with weekend mornings available. Ramadan slots shift later, including post-Iftar timings, and that is agreed in advance rather than improvised each week.

process.title: Halfway check on comparable questions
process.description: Midway through the block the same question types come back and the marks are compared. If they have not moved on the targeted cause, the plan changes or the tutor does, rather than the block continuing because it was already booked.

whyPoints.title: We ask for the code before the subject
whyPoints.description: Matching on Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 rather than on the word chemistry is the difference between useful practice and a year of wrongly calibrated questions. It is the first question we ask and it costs a parent one email to answer.

whyPoints.title: The February and March series warning, in writing
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only; UAE candidates sit June and November. Plans built around a February window are wrong for a child in Dubai, and we say so because that error has reached UAE parents before.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure carries the provider or table that published it so a parent can verify it. Three of the strongest pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote USD, a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; we publish the sourced rule and tell you to verify it on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board and code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the board and syllabus code for each subject. It is a one-line answer and it is the most useful information a parent in Al Safa can hold. Cambridge codes look like 0580, 0610, 0620 and 0625; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects in the same year group, so ask subject by subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything your child sits.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE the same qualification?
faqs.answer: They are comparable qualifications examined differently, and the differences matter for preparation. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped below the top grades; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are generally untiered. Question style and setup differ, the formula provision in maths and physics sits differently, and Cambridge science commonly uses a written alternative-to-practical component. Universities treat both as international GCSEs. The practical consequence for a family is simply that past-paper practice has to come from the board your child is actually entered for.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean for a student in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge tiered subjects they are two separate entries with different papers. Extended covers the core syllabus plus supplementary content and keeps the full grade range available; Core covers less and is capped below the top grades however well a student performs. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 11, and it closes at the entry deadline. The honest way to settle it is one timed Extended past paper marked strictly against the official mark scheme, which turns an impression into evidence in a single session.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our villa in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Safa lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and official mark scheme on a shared screen and a recording available afterwards. We target the home-tutor search because that is the phrase parents use, then answer it honestly rather than implying a service we do not sell. The Dubai in-home market exists and publishes AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor in Al Safa cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market bands, each attributed to its publisher: budget online and student tutors AED 45 to 150, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. IGCSE specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270. None of these is an IB Gram price. We quote against a plan after the free trial rather than publishing a rate card on a landing page.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and should be ignored entirely by a family in Dubai. Always read the live official timetable, and for Cambridge the correct zone version.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in maths when the answers are right?
faqs.answer: Usually because the method is not on the page. Multi-step questions award marks for the relationship written down and for the substitution as well as for the final answer, so a student who works mentally and writes one number collects nothing when that number is slightly wrong. This is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, which is why it is one of the fastest things to repair. Two or three sessions of writing every step on familiar questions, marked against the official scheme, usually changes the pattern permanently.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does an Al Safa student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The sourced Ministry of Education requirement for the British track is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That matters for subject selection, because a student taking five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not hold five that count. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before acting on it.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if my child studies online?
faqs.answer: In most UAE centres Cambridge science practical skills are examined through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory assessment, though the component varies by code and centre, so confirm with the exams officer. Pearson Edexcel examines practical understanding inside the two written papers. Either way the assessed skills are writing and reasoning: variables, method sequencing, instrument precision, graph interpretation, anomalies and genuine improvements. Those can be prepared properly with the question on a shared screen. The hands-on work belongs to the school, and that is where it should stay.

faqs.question: My child's mock was disappointing and there are four months left. What now?
faqs.answer: Start with the marked script rather than the grade, and sort the lost marks into four causes: method not written, command term not answered, content genuinely absent, and time run out. Those need entirely different work, and most students have one dominant cause rather than four. Then plan backwards from the first paper in fortnights, with content teaching finishing well before the end and the final fortnight reserved for timed papers and mark-scheme reading. Four months is a comfortable amount of runway if it is planned and very little if it is not.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students around Al Safa struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Across the Al Safa and Jumeirah cluster the recurring requests are Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, with English as a Second Language close behind for students who are academically strong but writing to the wrong purpose. In maths the difficulty is usually algebraic fluency rather than topic knowledge. In physics it is electricity and circuit reasoning. In chemistry it is mole calculations under time pressure. In the business and economics subjects it is application to the stimulus and the evaluation marks, which are a writing structure rather than content.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two or three IGCSE subjects for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the stage and the pattern. For Years 7 to 9, and for a student whose problem is technique rather than content, one tutor working across subjects is efficient and cheaper: method writing, command terms and timed practice are the same skills everywhere. For separate Extended entries in Year 11 where one subject is genuinely weak, a specialist in that subject is better value than a generalist covering three. The marked scripts usually make the right answer obvious.

faqs.question: Is a 9 to 1 grade the same as an A* to G grade?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not be mapped casually. Both scales are in current use depending on subject and board, and a sixth form stating a requirement in one while a certificate reports in the other creates a translation a family has to get right. Ask the receiving school to state the requirement for the specific subject in both scales, in writing. Separately, grade boundaries are set per series after the papers are sat and they move, so an old boundary cannot be used to predict what a raw mark will be worth.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework where a subject has it?
faqs.answer: Only within clear limits. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, question a student's plan, and read work the student has written and say where it falls short. A tutor may not write, rewrite to completion or dictate any part of work submitted for assessment. We also reference syllabus documents and mark schemes at their official source rather than reproducing them. Any provider offering to produce coursework is offering something whose consequences fall on your child, not on them.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session start for a family in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Al Safa sits inside its own school catchment, so arrival home is earlier than in most Dubai communities and a 4.30pm start is reliable on most weekdays, with 4pm workable for students at the nearest schools. From Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3 the first realistic slot is 5pm because of Beach Road congestion at pick-up. Saturday mornings are widely used where weekday evenings are full. Slots are booked on Gulf Standard Time and move later during Ramadan, including post-Iftar timings, agreed in advance.

faqs.question: Do I need to check that a private tutor in Dubai holds a permit?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question to ask. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-safa.closingBody: The highest-value thing you can do today costs one email. intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong filter for an IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: A parent in Al Satwa typing IGCSE home tutor into a search box is almost never looking for a particular pedagogy. They are looking for reassurance that somewhere within reach is a person who has taught this exact course before. That instinct is correct and the geographic version of it is self-defeating, because the IGCSE is not one qualification. It is two awarding bodies, dozens of syllabus codes, two tiers in most subjects, and two separate examination series, and a tutor who knows one combination well may know the next one barely at all.

Here is the specific trap. A family hires a competent maths graduate who lives fifteen minutes away. The child is entered for Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A, code 4MA1, where calculators are permitted in both papers and the tiering is Foundation and Higher. The tutor has taught Cambridge 0580, where the tiering is Core and Extended and the current syllabus includes a component sat without a calculator. Everything they teach is mathematically correct and a meaningful share of it is aimed at the wrong examination. The parent discovers this at the mock, not at the start.

So this page answers the question in the order that helps. First, how to establish which board and code your child is actually entered for, which is printed on the statement of entry and not always what the school says in conversation. Second, what the structural differences between the boards mean for revision. Third, the five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows a syllabus or merely knows the subject. Then the permit position, the coverage position, how practical science is assessed when lessons are online, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that one ranking competitor publishes incorrectly.

Al Satwa's own circumstances make the specialist question sharper than it would be in Jumeirah or Al Barsha. There is almost no international school inside the area, so children commute outward and the local pool of available tutors is not selected for anything except willingness to travel. Narrow that pool further by demanding a specific syllabus code and a specific tier and you are left with very few people, which is precisely why the honest answer to the search is to stop filtering by distance.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That service exists only in India, and it is stated the same way on every country page we publish. Al Satwa students are taught one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which is how a past paper gets annotated in front of both parties and how a mark scheme gets read line by line. The trade is a tutor you cannot shake hands with in exchange for a tutor who has taught your child's code.

sections.heading: The real question behind an IGCSE home tutor search in Al Satwa
paragraphs: Strip the search down and it asks something reasonable: is there anybody near me who actually knows this course? The problem is that the IGCSE is not one course. Two awarding bodies operate in Dubai, Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, each with its own syllabus codes, its own tier names, its own paper structures and its own rules on calculators and practical assessment. Knowing the subject is a lower bar than knowing the syllabus, and the gap between the two is where a term of tutoring gets wasted.

In Al Satwa the geographic version of the question is particularly unhelpful. The area holds almost no international schooling, so children travel outward each morning and the pool of tutors available locally is selected by willingness to drive rather than by what they have taught. Add a requirement for a specific code and a specific tier and that pool becomes very small. The families who get the best outcome here are the ones who abandon distance as the filter and use the syllabus code instead.

The honest reframing is this. Ask not who is nearby but who has taught 4MA1 Higher, or 0620 Extended, or 4ET1 with your child's set texts. Then ask how they will deliver it. IB Gram answers the first question by matching on board and code, and the second by teaching one-to-one over live video with a shared screen. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and that limit is published rather than discovered during a booking call.

sections.heading: First, establish which board and code your child is entered for
paragraphs: The document that settles this is the statement of entry, issued by the school ahead of the series. It lists the awarding body, the syllabus code and the components the candidate will sit. Ask for it, or ask the examinations officer directly, and do it before hiring anybody. Parents frequently rely on what a subject teacher said in a parents' evening, and subject teachers sometimes name the board the department used two years ago.

The table below pairs the codes for the subjects Al Satwa families ask about most, with the structural difference that actually changes revision. Mathematics is the clearest example: a current Cambridge 0580 syllabus includes a component sat without a calculator, while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. A student who has spent a year doing mental arithmetic drills for the wrong board has lost that year's marginal gain, and one who has never done them for the right board will feel it in the examination hall.

Science is the second place the boards diverge in a way that matters. Cambridge candidates sit a separate practical component, either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, which is a distinct examination with its own technique. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. Preparing for one and sitting the other is not fatal, but it costs marks on exactly the questions that separate the upper grades. Always read the current syllabus on the awarding body's own site rather than a summary, because components are revised.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Tiering is the decision with the longest reach and the least discussion. In most IGCSE subjects a candidate is entered for one of two tiers, and the tier caps the grade available. A student entered for the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and a student entered for the higher tier who is not ready risks a result well below what the lower tier would have delivered. The school decides, usually during Year 10, on evidence that is often a single internal assessment.

The practical point for an Al Satwa family is that the decision is cheap to revisit in Year 10 and expensive in Year 11. If a child is capable of the higher tier and has been placed lower because of one bad test, the window to change that is the first two terms of Year 10, and it requires evidence rather than argument. Equally, a child drowning on the higher tier late in Year 11 is usually better served by a confident lower-tier entry than by an ambitious one, and that is a conversation to have with the school in writing.

Tiering also interacts with what comes next. A lower-tier mathematics grade can close A Level Mathematics and some science routes, and it affects what a sixth form will accept even when the published grade requirement is nominally met. Ask the school directly what tier each subject is entered at, ask what the grade ceiling is for that tier in the current syllabus, and ask what evidence would change the decision. Those three questions take one email and settle most of the anxiety behind a tutoring search.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: A first conversation with a prospective tutor can be made genuinely diagnostic in about four minutes, and the questions below are the ones that work. Ask which code they have taught and which tier. A tutor who knows the course answers with a number, not with the subject name. Ask what the component structure is for that code, and listen for whether they name the papers and what each carries. Vagueness here is the single most reliable warning sign available to a parent.

Ask what the commonest mark loss is on a named topic in that syllabus. A tutor who has marked work will give a specific answer, such as state symbols omitted in ionic equations or a general rule stated without notation. Ask how practical skills are assessed on that code, because the answer differs between the boards and a tutor who has only taught the other one will get it wrong. And ask which series the student is entered for, which should prompt them to ask you for the statement of entry rather than guess.

Two things that are not diagnostic, despite being what the market advertises: a general degree classification, and a claim about examiner status. A first-class degree in physics says nothing about whether somebody has taught 4PH1. Examiner status should be treated carefully in this market, because current status is hard to verify and because it is often used to imply access to marking or boundaries, which no tutor has. What is verifiable is whether the person can describe your child's examination accurately, and that is the test worth applying.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in the market addresses, and the answer is public. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anybody quoting a permit fee is mistaken. The route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, available through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligible categories are broader than families expect and are set out in the table below. What matters alongside eligibility is the consequence of not holding one: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is not something an individual tutor holds.

One boundary is worth holding firmly. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the live policy, so verify it with ADEK before relying on it. The reason to know it is that families in Dubai sometimes ask for their child's own classroom teacher privately, and that is the one arrangement to steer away from.

Publishing the limits is more useful than concealing them, because a family that waits two weeks for the right specialist does better than one that starts next Tuesday with a generalist. The pattern is consistent. Mainstream mathematics and science at either tier is well covered and matches quickly. Narrower components take longer: Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science programming paper work, and English Literature where the set texts are unusual. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, our fallback is a specialist based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before booking rather than afterwards, and which is the real reason online delivery exists for a place like Al Satwa.

What we will not do is substitute. A general mathematics tutor placed into a 4PM1 Further Pure request produces a term of competent, irrelevant teaching, and the family discovers it at the mock. If the honest answer is a wait, or a different band in the week, or that we cannot cover it at all, that is what you will be told before a trial lesson is arranged. sections.heading: How science practicals are assessed when lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online science tutoring, and it deserves a direct answer. The practical skills in an IGCSE science are examined on paper, not in a laboratory. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper as a separate component, and the overwhelming majority of Dubai school candidates sit the alternative-to-practical version. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. In both cases the examination asks a student to read apparatus diagrams, identify variables, spot sources of error, process a results table and evaluate a method.

All of that is examinable work that happens on paper, with a mark scheme, and all of it is teachable over a shared screen. What cannot be taught online is the physical handling of equipment, and that is the school's job and happens in the school's laboratory. The honest division of labour is that the school supplies the hands and the tutor supplies the examination technique, and the component that carries the marks is the second one.

The practical technique that gains the most marks is reading a results table for what the examiner has planted in it: an anomalous value, an uncontrolled variable, a scale that invites a wrong gradient. Students are rarely taught to look for those deliberately. Working through the alternative-to-practical papers of past series, annotating what each question is testing and then marking the student's own answers against the published scheme, is the single highest-yield use of a tutoring hour in IGCSE science, and it needs a screen rather than a bench.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the rule a competitor publishes wrongly
paragraphs: Families in Dubai eventually meet equivalency, the process by which the Ministry of Education recognises a foreign secondary certificate for use in the UAE. For the British track the published requirement is specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches people out is what does not count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. One provider currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Getting this right matters because families make subject-dropping decisions in Year 10 on the strength of what they read, and a wrong subject count either wastes a year of study or leaves a shortfall discovered too late.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and the official channel is the authority's own page. And no IB points threshold for equivalency should be relied on from any source other than the Ministry's own publication, because the British-track figures are published and the IB figure is not. Tutoring is also not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression, and anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

You see that list before committing to a schedule, so the hours are spent on gaps rather than on a sweep of the whole course.
