process.description: Once content is in place, sessions move to timed past papers marked together against the official scheme. That is where command-term discipline, presentation and timing are built, and it is the part of the work that separates a solid grade from the one above it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child in Al Satwa is actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer for the statement of entry. It names the awarding body, the syllabus code and the components the candidate will sit, and it is the only reliable source. Parents often rely on what a subject teacher mentioned at a parents' evening, and departments change board between cohorts, so that information goes stale. Do this before hiring anybody. The difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 changes calculator rules, tier names and paper structure, and a tutor preparing for the wrong one will be teaching correct mathematics towards the wrong examination.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE qualifications the same thing?
faqs.answer: They are comparable qualifications from different awarding bodies, and they are not interchangeable in preparation. Tier names differ, with Cambridge using Core and Extended and Pearson using Foundation and Higher. Calculator rules differ in mathematics. Practical science assessment differs structurally, Cambridge using a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component while Pearson assesses practical skills within the written papers. Content lists overlap heavily but not entirely. Universities and the UAE Ministry of Education treat both as accredited, so the choice is the school's; the difference matters for revision rather than recognition.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean, and does it limit my child's grade?
faqs.answer: They are the two tiers of entry in most Cambridge IGCSE subjects, and yes, the tier sets a ceiling on the grade available before the examination is sat. Pearson's equivalent is Foundation and Higher. Schools usually decide during Year 10, sometimes on a single internal assessment. The decision is realistically revisable in the first two terms of Year 10 with evidence, and rarely revisable in Year 11. Ask the school which tier each subject is entered at, what the ceiling is under the current syllabus, and what evidence would change it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who has taught GCSE in the UK teach my child's IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it depends on the subject and how much they have read. The IGCSE and the English GCSE share a great deal of content but differ in paper structure, tiering, practical assessment and series timing. A tutor who has taught English GCSE Mathematics will know the mathematics; whether they know that current Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component, or how Pearson 4MA1 distributes marks across two papers, is a separate question. Ask them which international code they have taught, and treat a vague answer as a warning.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for a candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE family should be planning around it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November. Every centre is allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, and using the wrong zone timetable is a real risk, so work from the school's own confirmed timetable.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE subjects count for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One provider currently ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own page, since equivalency is a regulatory process no tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

faqs.question: Do you provide a tutor who comes to our building in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Local independent tutors and agencies do offer them, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. In Al Satwa the travel premium buys a tutor's unbillable hour in pick-up traffic and a candidate pool narrowed to whoever will make the trip, which is the opposite of what a specific syllabus code requires.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE practical science examined if my child never does experiments with the tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the practical marks are earned on paper. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and most Dubai school candidates sit the alternative. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Both ask students to read apparatus diagrams, identify variables, spot error sources, process results tables and evaluate methods, all of which is teachable on a shared screen with past papers and mark schemes. Physical apparatus handling happens in the school laboratory, which is where it belongs; the examined technique is what a tutor adds.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IGCSE tutor in the first phone call?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which syllabus code and tier have you taught? What are the components for that code and what does each carry? What is the commonest mark loss on a named topic in it? How are practical skills assessed on this syllabus? And which series is my child entered for, which should prompt them to ask for the statement of entry. A tutor who knows the course answers with numbers and paper names. Degree classification and claimed examiner status are not diagnostic, and the latter is difficult to verify in this market.

faqs.question: My child joined Year 10 IGCSE from a different curriculum. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a written gap list rather than a schedule. Two or three longer sessions checking the published syllabus content list topic by topic will establish what the course requires that your child has never been taught, which is almost never the whole course and is rarely what the family assumed. Students arriving from the Middle Years Programme typically have strong investigation habits and specific content holes. Students arriving from another country's system often have the content in a different order. Map it first, then commit hours.

faqs.question: Is the November series a realistic route if a June grade disappoints?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is used routinely in Dubai, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. The practical consideration is the entry deadline, which sits months before the examination, so the decision has to be made soon after results rather than at leisure. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results from the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives a sense of the turnaround. Work from the school's confirmed timetable and the awarding body's live timetable page rather than from any restated dates, because provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: We are behind in four IGCSE subjects. Should we book a tutor for all of them?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two at the outside. Families under pressure in Year 11 ask for four and then discover that four weekly hours plus school plus revision leaves no time to actually practise anything. The better pattern is to identify the subject where the grade is furthest from where it needs to be, work that one properly for a term, and reassess. Tutoring produces movement by changing how a student works, and that change has to be absorbed in the hours between sessions rather than during them.

faqs.question: If my two children sit different IGCSE boards, can the same tutor take both?
faqs.answer: Technically yes, and usually it is a false economy. A tutor matched to Cambridge 0620 Extended for one child and asked to cover Pearson 4MA1 Higher for the other is a specialist in one of those two things. Where both children need the same board, the same subject and a similar stage, a shared arrangement can work. Where they do not, two specialists each working one slot deliver more than one tutor working two, and the cost difference is smaller than families expect once wasted sessions are counted.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We say so before a trial lesson is booked. Mainstream mathematics and science at either tier match within a few days. Narrower components take longer: Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science programming work and English Literature with unusual set texts can take two weeks or more. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a specialist elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, disclosed in advance. What we will not do is put a general tutor into a specialist request and let you find out at the mock.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingBody: The most useful five minutes an Al Satwa family can spend is emailing the school's examinations officer for the statement of entry. Once you know the board, the code and the tier, the search stops being about who lives nearby and becomes a question with a clean answer. Send us the code and we will match a tutor who has taught that examination, tell you honestly what the wait is, and arrange a free trial lesson on work your child is doing this week. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If we cannot cover the code, we will say that instead.

intro.heading: Two years of tuition, priced properly
paragraphs: Nobody decides to spend forty thousand dirhams on IGCSE tuition. They decide to spend two hundred and fifty an hour, twice a week, for two subjects, and then the Year 11 panic adds a third subject in January. Priced by the hour, every individual decision looks modest. Priced across two years, the same decisions add up to a number most Al Sufouh families would have questioned if anybody had shown it to them at the start. This page shows it at the start.

The market figures are public, and they are the right place to begin. Published Dubai rates run from AED 33-52 an hour at the budget end, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel included, AED 200-450 and upwards for an IGCSE specialist, and AED 500-650 at the premium end. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are other providers' published numbers, read during the October 2026 research round, and you can open the same pages.

Multiply the mid-market monthly figure by two subjects, by ten months, by two years, and the arithmetic becomes the point of this page. The question is not whether the rate is reasonable - most of them are. It is whether the hours purchased are doing anything a cheaper or shorter intervention would not have done. In our experience of this market, a substantial share of IGCSE tuition spending in Dubai is defensible per hour and indefensible in total, and the gap between those two statements is where the five wasted-money patterns in this page live.

Context matters here too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are capped; tutoring is not. That makes tutoring the part of the education budget that can quietly double without anyone deciding it should, which is an argument for buying it against a diagnosis rather than against a worry.

On delivery, so it is clear before the cost discussion starts: IB Gram teaches Al Sufouh students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India. Al Sufouh is one of the few Dubai districts where the in-home option is genuinely practical, since the campuses and Knowledge Park are minutes away, so this page compares the models on published rates rather than pretending the choice is not real. It also means the cost comparison here is unusually honest in our favour and against it at the same time: the in-home premium costs an Al Sufouh family less than it costs a family in the far suburbs, because the driving is shorter, and the selection problem it creates is exactly the same. Both halves of that are on the page.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7-9
programmes.description: Broad content with internal assessment only and nothing that appears on a certificate. Because the stakes look low, gaps are tolerated here - and Year 8 algebra, Year 9 particle theory and Year 9 cell biology are the gaps that reappear in Year 11 as apparently sudden collapses.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest tuition available to an Al Sufouh family and almost nobody buys it. A term of Year 9 maths, bought at mid-market rates, typically costs a fraction of what the same gap costs to repair in Year 11, when it has to be fixed alongside new content and against a deadline.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, terminal examinations with practical or coursework components in some subjects. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel dominate in Dubai and differ in tiering, paper structure and grading. The tier a student is entered for sets a ceiling on the achievable grade.
programmes.countryNote: The years when tuition spending peaks locally, usually in the wrong pattern: nothing in Year 10, then three subjects from January of Year 11. Reversing that pattern costs less in total and produces better results, which is the single most useful cost observation on this page.

programmes.name: International A Level, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, with entry requirements set by the school and usually expressed as IGCSE grades in the corresponding subject. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement includes one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.

The cost-relevant point is that a subject dropped at IGCSE is rarely available at AS, so a weak Year 10 grade in a subject your child may want at 16 is a closing door rather than a disappointing number - and that is when spending is justified.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Rewards breadth, which means a student with one collapsed IGCSE subject is more exposed than one with a flat profile.

Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new International Baccalaureate schools, so a family in this area has more options at 16 than they did two years ago.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Al Sufouh families most often buy tuition for, with a note on where the money is well spent in each. Confirm the specification code with the school before buying anything at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The best value subject to tutor early and the worst to tutor late. Cambridge 0580 Extended includes a non-calculator paper and Pearson 4MA1 Higher does not, so the first money spent should be on confirming which. Tier boundary cases are where a term of work returns most.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most improvable science per hour because it is procedural: moles, electrolysis half-equations, rates gradients and organic conditions. A short block with mark-scheme marking moves marks quickly, which makes it good value even bought in Year 11.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Slower to move than Chemistry because the losses are in reasoning that must be written out rather than in facts. Worth buying earlier than families do. Prefix and unit errors under pressure are cheap to fix and rarely addressed.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Highest content volume, so the temptation is to buy more hours. The better purchase is command-word discipline, which costs a few sessions and lifts every answer rather than covering a few more topics at the end of a long list.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Reduced content across three sciences. A cheaper route in teaching hours and a more expensive one in options, since it can close A Level science doors. Check the target school's entry rule before accepting it as a neutral choice.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Where tuition is most often bought and least often needed in volume. The marks are in technique - inference questions have a mark-per-point structure - so three or four targeted sessions usually beat a weekly year-long arrangement.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with different implications for university applications and for the equivalency subject count. Confirm which one your child is entered for in writing before buying any resource or tuition.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation that is almost never self-taught: a judgement, two sides weighed, a stated reason for the preference. This is a cheap fix with a large return, and it is the thing to buy rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where the specified examples are the application marks. Students who revise concepts and improvise examples lose those marks every paper, and no amount of additional content teaching recovers them.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics and Computer Science
subjects.description: The subjects where Dubai families most often cannot find anyone locally, which is where an online pool genuinely changes what is available rather than just what it costs. Expect to pay in the specialist band for either.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition actually totals across two years
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Sufouh will quote you an hourly rate, and the hourly rate is not the number that matters. What matters is the total, and the total is a function of how many subjects, for how many months, at what rate - three variables that families decide separately and never multiply together. So here is the multiplication, using published market figures rather than invented ones.

Bestimate's Dubai guidance puts monthly cost for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Take the mid-market monthly band and run it across one subject for ten months: AED 6,000 to 12,000 for the year. Two subjects across both IGCSE years, at the same band, is four times that. Add a third subject from January of Year 11, which is the common local pattern, and the total moves again.

None of those individual decisions is unreasonable, and that is precisely the problem. A parent asked to approve the two-year total in advance would ask what it is buying. A parent approving AED 250 an hour in October and another AED 250 an hour in January never sees the total until it has been spent. The remedy is simple and nobody suggests it: write the number down before you start, decide what result would justify it, and review against that rather than against whether the lessons feel useful.

The comparison that puts this in perspective is school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year in Dubai, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The regulated part of the education budget is held flat by policy. The unregulated part grows by accumulation of small decisions. For a family in Al Sufouh where both parents may work in Media City or Internet City and the convenience of an in-home arrangement is real, the accumulation is easier still.

sections.heading: The five places IGCSE tuition money gets wasted in Dubai
paragraphs: These five patterns account for most of the wasted IGCSE tuition spending we see in this part of Dubai, and all five are avoidable before any money changes hands. The table sets them out with what to do instead. None of the alternatives involves buying more.

The first and largest is teaching aimed at the wrong specification. Cambridge and Pearson are both widely used in this corridor, a single school frequently mixes boards across subjects, and most tutors never ask. Two terms of competent teaching against the wrong paper structure costs the full price of two terms and returns a fraction of it. The fix is one email to the school requesting the syllabus code in writing, and it costs nothing.

The second is buying supervision at specialist rates. A student who understands the content and will not sit down to work needs somebody in the room, not a subject expert at AED 300 an hour. In Al Sufouh, where local in-home arrangements are genuinely practical and a parent may be home from Knowledge Park by 5:30pm, this is worth naming: the cheapest solution is often a parent in the next room or a lower-cost supervision arrangement, not a better tutor.

The third is the open-ended weekly arrangement that nobody ever ends. It starts in October for a reason, the reason resolves by February, and it runs to May because cancelling feels like giving up. The fourth is buying volume when the problem is technique: three subjects of weekly tuition when command-word discipline in one subject would have transferred to all three. The fifth is late panic buying, which costs the most per mark of anything on this list - eight weeks before a series, a student with real content gaps is better served by triage than by a full-syllabus sweep, and an honest provider will say so.

sections.heading: Comparing two offers: cost per mark rather than cost per hour
paragraphs: Two tutors quote AED 200 and AED 350. Nothing in those numbers tells you which is better value, because value depends on how many marks each can realistically move and how quickly. Cost per hour is the wrong unit. Cost per mark is unmeasurable precisely, but it can be reasoned about, and reasoning about it changes decisions.

Start from where the marks are. In Cambridge sciences the theory paper carries 50% of the grade, the multiple-choice paper 30% and the practical component 20%. A tutor who can mark an alternative-to-practical answer against the official scheme is working on a fifth of the grade that most revision never touches, and the marks there are rule-governed and quick to move. A tutor who re-teaches content the student largely knows is working on the part of the grade that is already secured. The second tutor may be cheaper per hour and is more expensive per mark, possibly infinitely so.

Then consider speed. Procedural subjects move fast: Chemistry calculations, electrolysis half-equations, mark-scheme phrasing, command words. Reasoning and writing move slowly. Content never learned moves slowest of all and does not move at all in eight weeks. A sensible way to compare two offers is to ask each tutor which of those three categories they think the problem is in and what they would expect to see change in six weeks. A tutor who answers specifically is quotable against; a tutor who answers warmly is not.

The table below lays out the published Dubai bands against what each realistically moves. It is a reasoning aid rather than a measurement, and the useful conclusion is consistent: the mid band buys the marks in most cases, the budget band buys routine, and the premium band buys scarcity. Paying premium rates for weekly delivery is the commonest overspend among families who can afford it, and paying budget rates for a technique problem is the commonest overspend among families who cannot.

sections.heading: Group, centre, in-home or online: a model comparison
paragraphs: Al Sufouh families have all four models genuinely available, which is not true everywhere in Dubai. The campuses and Knowledge Park make local in-home feasible; Al Barsha and Al Quoz hold tuition centres within a short drive; the villa communities inland run informal group arrangements; and online is available from anywhere. The table compares them on the terms that matter financially.

Group tuition at a centre is the cheapest per student and the pace is set by the group rather than by your child's diagnosis. That trade is acceptable for content coverage and poor for technique work, because a mark-scheme error is individual. It is also where families end up by default when an individual tutor is quoted above budget, which means the choice is often made on price and then rationalised.

In-home one-to-one is the most expensive and, in Al Sufouh specifically, less obviously inefficient than elsewhere, because the journey is genuinely short. What it buys is presence; what it costs is choice, because the tutor has to be qualified, free and nearby. Online one-to-one costs less than in-home for equivalent expertise and removes the travel variable entirely, at the price of no physical presence. Budget online sits below all of them and buys routine rather than marks.

The honest recommendation depends on the diagnosis rather than the budget. A student needing content coverage across several subjects and no individual technique work is reasonably served by a group arrangement. A student with one specific technique problem needs one-to-one and does not need it weekly for two years. A student who will not work without supervision needs presence, and in this district can get it locally. IB Gram sells only one of those four models - one-to-one online - and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison above is deliberately not weighted towards us.

sections.heading: Why Year 9 and Year 10 hours are the cheapest marks available
paragraphs: The strongest cost argument in IGCSE tutoring is also the least marketable, because it asks a family to spend money before anything is wrong. An hour of maths tuition in Year 9 does the same work as three hours in Year 11, for the simple reason that in Year 9 the content is being learned once rather than repaired while new material arrives and a deadline approaches.

The mechanism is worth understanding. A gap in Year 8 algebra does not announce itself; the student compensates, scores adequately on topic tests, and arrives at Year 10 quadratics with a foundation that cannot carry it. At that point the tutoring job is two jobs - teach quadratics, repair algebra - and both are happening while the school moves on. By Year 11 it is three jobs, because exam technique has joined the list. Same gap, three times the hours, at Year 11 rates.

Tier decisions make this sharper. Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation awards 5 to 1 and Higher awards 9 to 4. Entries are made by the school to the board's deadline, usually on Year 11 internal performance, which means the tier is effectively decided during Year 10. A student on the boundary who gets a term of focused work in Year 10 may be entered a tier higher, which changes the grade ceiling itself - a structural return no amount of Year 11 spending can replicate.

So the cheapest version of a two-year plan is counterintuitive: buy one subject weekly in Year 10, buy almost nothing in the autumn of Year 11, and buy a defined twelve-week past-paper block from February. That pattern costs less in total than the common local pattern of nothing in Year 10 and three subjects from January, and it produces better results because it puts the hours where the content is still being formed rather than where the panic is.

sections.heading: The extras to ask about before you agree a rate
paragraphs: A quoted hourly rate is not the price. Five things routinely change the real cost and all five should be settled in writing before a first lesson, local tutor or online provider alike. None of this is unusual to ask and a provider who resists any of it is telling you something.

First, the unit. A rate quoted per lesson is not a rate per hour, and a 45-minute lesson at AED 200 is AED 267 an hour. Ask for the rate per 60 minutes and the standard lesson length. Second, VAT. Ask whether the quoted figure includes it. This page deliberately does not state how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption - what you are entitled to is a clear answer about whether the number you were given is the number you pay.

Third, cancellation. Get the notice period and the charge for a late cancellation in writing. Over two years, cancellation terms can account for a meaningful share of total spend, particularly around mock weeks and family travel. Fourth, materials. Ask what is included and what is extra. No provider should be selling you board past papers or mark schemes - those are the boards' copyright material and should be referenced and linked rather than reproduced or supplied - so a material charge is worth questioning.

Fifth, the permit position. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you see quoted. Since the permit is free, a provider treating it as a cost to pass on has not read it.

sections.heading: What the spending is buying towards, and when to spend nothing
paragraphs: Two floors are worth knowing because they define what the money is for. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency, where the published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One competitor page currently states six IGCSE subjects are needed; the sourced rule is five. Verify on moe.gov.ae, and note that equivalency is run by the Ministry and the emirate authorities, not by any tutoring provider.

The second floor is progression, and it sits higher. A Level and sixth-form entry requirements are set by schools and are frequently above the equivalency threshold, sometimes well above for sciences and mathematics. Those two numbers are different, and a family planning only against the lower one can produce a student who is technically qualified and practically blocked. Knowing both numbers tells you which subjects are worth spending on and which are already comfortably clear.

Which brings us to when to spend nothing. If a subject is comfortably above both floors and your child is not aiming higher for a specific reason, tuition in it is a purchase without a target. If one mock grade dipped in a previously strong subject, wait for the next data point. If several subjects are weak at once, the cause is usually load, sleep or something outside academics, and three tutors makes the week worse rather than better. If the exam is four weeks away and the content was never learned, buy triage rather than rescue. And if a child needs supervision rather than teaching, buy the cheapest arrangement that puts an adult in the room.

The fixed limits apply here as elsewhere on this site. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, because IB Gram holds none. No reproduction or supply of specifications, past papers or mark schemes. No coursework written or completed. No grade promises and no statistics about our own outcomes, because we cannot publish the sample, date and method that would make such a figure meaningful.

faqs.question: What does two years of IGCSE tuition actually cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Work it out rather than accept an hourly rate. Bestimate's Dubai guidance puts a weekly one-hour session at AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with advertised packages at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Run the mid band across one subject for ten months and you are at AED 6,000-12,000 for the year. Two subjects across both IGCSE years is four times that, and the common local pattern adds a third subject from January of Year 11. Write the total down before you start.

faqs.question: Where does IGCSE tuition money most often get wasted here?
faqs.answer: Five places. Teaching aimed at the wrong specification, because nobody asked for the syllabus code - that can cost two full terms. Supervision bought at specialist rates when the problem is behavioural rather than academic. The weekly arrangement that runs to May because cancelling feels like giving up. Volume bought when technique was the issue, so three subjects are tutored when command-word work in one would have transferred. And late panic buying, which has the highest cost per mark of anything available. All five are avoidable before money changes hands.

faqs.question: How do I compare a tutor at AED 200 with one at AED 350?
faqs.answer: Not on the hourly rate, which tells you nothing about value. Ask each one which category the problem is in - content never learned, technique and command words, or procedural topics - and what they would expect to change in six weeks. Procedural work moves fast, technique moves at moderate speed, missing content moves slowly and does not move at all in eight weeks. A tutor who answers specifically can be held to it. In most cases the mid band of AED 150-300 buys the marks, the budget band buys routine, and the premium band of AED 500-650 buys scarcity rather than speed.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at a centre good value for an Al Sufouh family?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes; for technique, no. Group rates are the lowest per student and the pace is set by the group rather than by your child's diagnosis, which is fine when the need is to work through topics and poor when the need is to fix an individual mark-scheme error. A sensible hybrid many families here never consider is group tuition for breadth plus one individual diagnostic session per term on a marked paper. That costs a fraction of weekly one-to-one across several subjects and addresses the part a group cannot.

faqs.question: Why is Year 10 tuition cheaper than Year 11 tuition for the same problem?
faqs.answer: Because in Year 10 it is one job and in Year 11 it is three. A gap in Year 8 algebra does not announce itself; the student compensates until Year 10 quadratics, at which point a tutor has to teach the new content and repair the old while the school moves on. By Year 11 exam technique joins the list. Same gap, roughly three times the hours, at exam-year rates. Tier decisions sharpen this further, since entries are effectively determined by Year 10 performance and the tier sets a ceiling on the grade itself.

faqs.question: What should I ask about before agreeing an hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Five things, in writing. The rate per 60 minutes and the standard lesson length, because a 45-minute lesson at AED 200 is AED 267 an hour. Whether VAT is included in the figure you were quoted. The cancellation notice period and charge, which over two years can be a meaningful share of the total. What materials are included, noting that nobody should be selling you board past papers or mark schemes. And the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit position - the permit is granted free of charge for two years, so it is not a cost to pass on.

faqs.question: Is in-home tuition in Al Sufouh better value than elsewhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On cost, marginally yes; on selection, no. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, and in Al Sufouh the journey from a local campus or Knowledge Park is genuinely short, so less of the premium is mileage. What does not change is that the band overlaps the online specialist band of AED 200-450 almost entirely, so the money is not buying different teaching quality, and requiring the tutor to be nearby limits you to whoever is qualified, free and local. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE regardless.

faqs.question: My child is already getting grade 7s. Should we buy tuition to protect that?
faqs.answer: Probably not weekly. A student on track needs periodic marking against the mark scheme and a check that technique holds under timed conditions, not an additional weekly commitment that displaces independent practice. A single diagnostic session each half term on a recent paper, plus a short block of timed full papers in the final weeks, covers it at a fraction of the cost. Providers rarely suggest this because it is a smaller sale, and families rarely ask for it because the available products are shaped around weekly delivery rather than around what a secure student needs.

faqs.question: Four of my child's subjects are weak. Should we tutor all four?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, because four weak subjects is rarely four subject problems. The usual causes are timetable load, sleep, or something going on outside academics, and four weekly sessions makes a full week worse rather than better. There is also a transfer effect to use: command-word discipline and mark-scheme awareness learned properly in one subject improve answers in the others. Start with one subject and one diagnostic, and have the harder conversation with the school about load and support. Spending on volume here is the most expensive way to not solve the actual problem.

faqs.question: How much does the tier decision affect what we should spend?
faqs.answer: It determines whether spending has a structural return or a marginal one. Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation awards 5 to 1 and Higher awards 9 to 4. The school makes the entry to the board's deadline, usually on Year 11 internal performance, which means Year 10 is when the tier is effectively decided. A student on the boundary gets far more from a term of focused Year 10 work than a student comfortably inside either tier, because the ceiling itself moves. Ask the school which tier your child is heading for while it is still open.

faqs.question: Does the practical component justify separate spending?
faqs.answer: It is among the best-value purchases in Cambridge sciences. The practical test or alternative-to-practical paper carries 20% of the grade, and the marks go on written things: naming variables, justifying repeats by purpose, table headings carrying units, graph conventions, specific error sources and conclusions the data supports. Those are rule-governed and move quickly, and most revision never touches them because the component looks easy. Two or three focused sessions typically return more than the same hours spent on content. Pearson's sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers instead, so confirm the board first.

faqs.question: What are we spending towards - what grades actually matter?
faqs.answer: Two different floors, and most families only know one. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Progression requirements set by schools for A Level or sixth-form entry frequently sit well above that, particularly in sciences and mathematics. Knowing both numbers tells you which subjects need funding and which are already clear. Verify equivalency rules on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying premium rates of AED 500 or more an hour?
faqs.answer: For a short diagnostic in a genuinely scarce subject, sometimes. For weekly delivery over two years, rarely. Published premium rates reach AED 500-650 and upwards, with BartyED at AED 650, and what they buy is scarcity and reputation rather than a different speed of improvement. The work that recovers most IGCSE marks - mark-scheme marking, command-word discipline, practical write-up technique - is done just as well in the AED 150-300 band. Paying premium rates weekly is the commonest overspend among families who can afford to make it.

faqs.question: What would make you recommend we stop paying?
faqs.answer: Several things, and we would rather say them than keep invoicing. If the target category of lost marks has not shrunk on a fresh marked paper after a full six-to-eight-week block, something needs to change and sometimes that is stopping. If the original problem has resolved and the sessions continue out of habit, stop. If the subject is comfortably clear of both the equivalency floor and the school's progression requirement and nobody is aiming higher for a reason, there is no target to spend against. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and it should be on the table at every review.

faqs.question: Can we reduce cost by sharing a tutor with another family?
faqs.answer: You can reduce the cost per student, and you should know what you are trading. Two students in one session halves the rate each and halves the individual attention, which is acceptable for content coverage and poor for mark-scheme work, because a technique error is specific to one student's writing. It works best where the two students sit the same specification, the same tier and have genuinely similar gaps - which is less common than families assume. Where the gaps differ, the session drifts towards the weaker student and both pay for a compromise.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingHeading: Decide the total before you decide the tutor
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: The most useful thing an Al Sufouh family can do about IGCSE tuition cost takes ten minutes and happens before anybody is hired: multiply the monthly rate by subjects and months across two years, confirm the syllabus code by email, and find out which tier your child is heading for while it is still open. Then buy one diagnostic session on a marked paper and decide from the result. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, as fixed-length blocks with a review date, not as an arrangement that renews until May.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-twar.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE subjects for Year 10 and Year 11 students in Al Twar, Al Qusais and Mirdif, on both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications, in the evening and weekend slots this district can actually keep.

intro.heading: What time can an IGCSE tutor realistically start in Al Twar?
paragraphs: Al Twar is a villa district laid out on quiet internal roads behind Al Qusais, which makes it pleasant to live in and awkward to serve. Two facts follow from the geography. The first is that the school bus reaches Al Twar towards the end of its loop, so a 2.30pm finish often means a child through the front door closer to 3.15pm. The second is that a tutor driving in from anywhere central is committing forty to sixty minutes each way at the evening peak, which is why in-home rates in this part of Dubai sit where they do.

Put those together and the usable teaching window on a weekday is narrower than most families assume. By the time a Year 10 student has changed, eaten something and made a first attempt at the school's own homework, it is approaching 4.45pm. From there you have roughly ninety minutes of genuine concentration before the evening meal, and a shorter, blunter window after it that runs to about 9pm. Both are usable. They are not interchangeable, and treating them as if they were is the commonest reason tutoring quietly fails in this district.

The early window, from about 5pm to 6.30pm, is where new content belongs. A student who has to learn moles, or a new grammar structure, or how to structure a six-mark answer, needs attention that is not available at nine o'clock. The late window, from about 7.30pm, is where past papers, calculation layout and command-word drilling belong, because those tasks demand recall and discipline rather than fresh construction. Families who schedule new teaching into the late slot conclude their child cannot learn in the evening, when what failed was the ordering.

The third window is the one almost nobody books. In Al Twar households, Friday and Saturday afternoon carry most of the week's commitments, which leaves Saturday morning from nine until noon almost entirely free and the student at their best of the week. One ninety-minute Saturday session for new content, paired with a short weekday practice slot, is the shape we recommend most often for Year 10 and Year 11 in this area. It also survives a bad week, because school events rarely land on a Saturday morning.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked questions and marked past papers. For a problem that is fundamentally about forty minutes of driving at each end of a lesson, that is not a workaround. It is the fix: a 5pm slot begins at 5pm, a rescheduled session costs nobody any fuel, and the tutor is chosen for the board your child actually sits.

programmes.description: Mocks in the first half of the year, final entries confirmed, then the series itself. The useful tutoring here is paper technique and targeted repair rather than broad content coverage, because there is no longer time for broad anything.

programmes.name: AS and A Level after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, with AS content typically examined at the end of Year 12 depending on the school's modular choices. Subject-specific prerequisites mean the IGCSE tier a student sat can close a door two years before anyone notices.

Verify the current rule through the ministry's own channel.

programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Extended-tier IGCSE is reasonable preparation for Standard Level and thin preparation for Higher Level quantitative work.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Twar families ask for most, with the specification codes worth confirming and the point at which each one tends to go wrong.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this district. Marks go in algebraic manipulation done in the wrong order, in bearings and transformations, and in multi-step problems where each step is right and the sequence is not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Technique more than knowledge. Nearly every lost mark traces to unit conversion, to rearranging a formula after substituting, or to an answer given without the unit the question asked for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles are the wall. Reacting masses, concentration and gas volumes are where a student who has coasted on recall meets something that cannot be remembered, and electrolysis products end up at the wrong electrode.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and easy to revise inefficiently. The highest return comes from data and application questions, where students describe a trend instead of accounting for it.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response. Students lose marks by summarising a passage rather than analysing how its effects are produced, which is a trainable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Frequently requested in this cluster. Strong students lose marks on register and task fulfilment rather than on vocabulary, so practice has to be marked against the criteria to be useful.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to a given case rather than recall of definitions. The six and eight-mark questions reward evaluation, and students who list advantages without judging them cap themselves.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline carries the grade: axes labelled, curves named, the shift justified in words. A handful of sessions on diagrams usually outperforms a term of reading.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are where marks are lost, not theory. Both are drillable, and both are far easier to teach on a shared screen than on paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger sets as a bridge to A Level. For a student already secure on 0580 content this is better value than more hours on the main maths course.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. It occupies timetable space families should allow for when planning evening sessions.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: A separately examined skill set: variables, instrument precision, table headings, graph scales, anomalies and specific method improvements. Which paper your school enters for changes what to practise.

sections.heading: Why a 5pm home appointment in Al Twar is rarely a 5pm lesson
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in a villa district has a specific failure mode, and it is worth describing honestly because it is the thing this search is really about. The appointment is at five. The tutor leaves central Dubai at twenty past four, hits the Al Qusais approach at its worst, and arrives at twenty past five. The lesson now has forty minutes left in the slot the family planned, and the tutor has another appointment in Mirdif at half past six. Nobody has behaved badly; the geography did this.

Repeat that twice a week for a term and two things happen. The first is that the lesson gets shorter than the invoice. The second, and worse, is that the family stops relying on the slot, which means homework and revision stop being organised around it. A tutoring arrangement that cannot be depended on is worth considerably less than its hourly rate suggests, and this is the hidden cost nobody prices.

The published rates make the visible part of the cost clear. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors up to AED 500, against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 and Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap is travel time inside the hourly rate. In Al Twar, where the drive is long in both directions, that gap is being earned honestly by the tutor and paid reluctantly by the family.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For an Al Twar family the practical consequence is that a 5pm slot starts at 5pm, a session that has to move costs nobody a wasted journey, and the tutor can be chosen for teaching Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 specifically rather than for being prepared to drive to Al Twar 3 on a Tuesday.

sections.heading: Which schools Al Twar feeds, and when each year group gets out
paragraphs: There is no single Al Twar school day. The cluster around Al Twar, Al Qusais and Al Nahda spans Indian, British and IB continuum provision, and finishing times across it differ by as much as ninety minutes depending on the school and the year group. Secondary year groups generally finish later than primary, and some schools stagger release to manage the bus fleet, which adds another fifteen minutes for the stops at the end of a loop.

The practical consequence is that a parent should work from their own school's timetable rather than from a neighbourhood assumption. Two Year 10 students living on the same street in Al Twar 2 can have usable session windows an hour apart, because one attends a school in Al Qusais with a 2pm finish and the other a school in Mirdif with a 3.30pm finish and a longer bus route. We ask for the school by name in the first conversation for exactly this reason.

Cross-district school places are the biggest single disruptor. An Al Twar family with a child at a school in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City is adding a drive to the afternoon in both directions, and in most of those cases the early evening window disappears entirely. For those households the plan shifts to a Saturday morning teaching session plus one late-evening practice slot, which is a different schedule from the one a family in the local cluster should use.

The table gives the shape of this rather than published times, because timetables change and the school's own calendar is the authority. What it shows is the spread: the earliest usable slot in this cluster is around 4.30pm and the latest is after 6pm, which is wide enough that any service offering a standard district-wide time is not thinking about your child.

sections.heading: Year 10 or Year 11: when tutoring should actually start
paragraphs: Most families in this district start tutoring in Year 11, and most of them should have started in Year 10. The reason is not motivational. It is that Year 10 is the year in which content is introduced for the first time, at pace, and a gap created there is carried silently into a year where there is no spare time to repair it. A student who did not quite understand moles in February of Year 10 is a student who cannot do a third of the chemistry paper in Year 11, and nobody noticed in between because nothing was examined.

Year 10 tutoring is also cheaper per unit of effect. There is room in the week, the student is not simultaneously handling mock timetables and coursework deadlines, and one weekly hour can run through a term without competing with anything. Year 11 tutoring, by contrast, is bought under time pressure, often at a higher band, and spends a meaningful share of its hours on triage rather than teaching. The same AED spent a year earlier does more.

There is a specific Year 10 decision worth naming, because it is the one Al Twar families most often discover too late. Tier and specification entries are set well before the examination year, and they determine the grade ceiling. A student entered for a core tier or a combined route has a cap that no amount of Year 11 tutoring will lift. Ask the examinations officer for the entry codes and tiers in writing during Year 10, while a change is still possible.

If you are already in Year 11, the honest plan is different rather than hopeless. Pick one or two subjects rather than five, work paper by paper rather than topic by topic, and scope the block against the mock dates with a frank assessment of what is recoverable. A tutor who tells you everything is fixable in eight weeks is selling comfort. A tutor who tells you which two papers can realistically move and which cannot is giving you something you can act on.

sections.heading: Boards, tiers and the one email that makes the plan correct
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE in this part of Dubai, and they do not examine identically. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with Core and Extended tiering in several subjects and its own practical routes. Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSE with a different paper structure, untiered in many subjects though its Mathematics A is offered at Foundation and Higher tier. Both are respected, both are accepted by universities, and schools within a few kilometres of Al Twar have made opposite choices.

A tutor working on the wrong board gets the content broadly right and the specifics wrong, and the specifics are where the marks live. Question phrasing differs, mark-scheme expectations differ, and the way practical skills are assessed differs. A student drilled on one board's past papers for a term meets the other board's wording in the exam hall at the worst possible moment. This is not a subtle effect; it is the single most common avoidable waste in the local market.

So send one email to the examinations officer and ask for three things: the board, the specification code, and the tier for each subject. The answer takes a line and makes everything downstream correct. While you are asking, add a fourth question for science subjects: which practical route the centre uses, because the preparation differs between a hands-on paper and the written alternative. For Cambridge candidates there is a fifth: which of the six administrative zones your centre sits in, because Cambridge publishes a separate timetable version per zone and states that it is essential to use the correct one, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

The table lists the codes families in this cluster most often turn out to hold. Use it as a prompt for that email rather than as a claim about your child's school. Once the codes are confirmed, every past paper, mark scheme and revision list used in tutoring should match them exactly.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Nobody else in this market counts the year backwards, and it is the most practically useful thing a parent can hold. UAE candidates sit the June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a date from that series has no bearing on an Al Twar candidate and any page quoting it to you has given you something to act on that does not apply. Everything that matters in the year sits months ahead of the papers themselves.

The pattern can be stated from published facts. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those backward-looking dates tell you the real gap between the last paper and the result, which is what resit planning depends on. For live dates, read the official timetable from the board rather than any restatement.

Working backwards from the series gives an Al Twar family four decision points. Tier and specification entries, which set the ceiling and cannot be undone after the final entry deadline. The mock window, which is the best available predictor and the right trigger for a scoped block. The practical or alternative-to-practical preparation, which families notice last and which needs its own hours. And the resit route, which for a June candidate means the November series and a result in January.

Add your school's own internal dates to the milestones in the table and the year stops being a surprise. The one date worth putting on the fridge is the final entry deadline, because every other decision can be revisited and that one cannot.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the slots that still hold
paragraphs: The UAE year does not hand out study time evenly, and an Al Twar household running on Ramadan hours while a child sits a British-curriculum examination series feels that more than most. School days shorten. The useful study window moves from late afternoon to after Iftar. A revision plan built on a 5pm weekday slot does not survive contact with that, and the families who lose the most are the ones who try to defend the slot rather than move it.

The adjustment is simple once it is planned. Sessions shift to a post-Iftar start, typically from around 8.30pm, and they get shorter and sharper: forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new teaching. New content moves to weekend mornings, which stay workable throughout. Students who make that shift deliberately lose very little. Students who improvise lose most of a month at exactly the point in the year when a month matters.

Prayer times shape the ordinary week too, and they are worth saying out loud at the booking stage rather than working around awkwardly later. A session that reliably runs into Maghrib will be cut short or cancelled; one scheduled to finish before it, or to start after it, simply works. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to re-plan, so moving a slot by forty minutes for a term is an administrative change rather than a logistical one.

Travel is the third factor in this district. Many Al Twar households spend part of the long break and part of the winter holiday abroad. Over video a session can follow the family rather than pausing, which is impossible for any arrangement that depends on somebody arriving at a UAE address. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made and they get built in rather than breaking it.

sections.heading: What the school run costs when the tutor is the one driving
paragraphs: Start from what the market charges, because the timetable question and the money question are the same question in a district like this. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and online monthly packages of eight sessions appear at around AED 799.

Read those as a timetable decision rather than a pricing decision. For the same monthly spend you can have four long in-home sessions that must survive Dubai traffic twice a week, or eight shorter on-screen sessions that start when they say they will. For IGCSE, where the gain comes from frequent marked practice rather than from long teaching blocks, the eight-point pattern does more with the same money. That is the honest case for the format, and it is a case about effectiveness rather than about saving.

At the other bands, budget and university-student online tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52, while IB and IGCSE specialists sit at roughly AED 200 to 450 with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's survey agreeing on AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named tutors are advertised as high as AED 650 by BartyED. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider or survey that published it and was read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price; we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation instead.

One piece of household context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the school line flat, the sensible move is to name the monthly tutoring figure deliberately and then decide how many contact points it should buy, rather than letting hours accumulate by arrangement.

sections.heading: Three weekly schedules that survive an Al Twar term
paragraphs: The first is for a Year 10 student who is coping but drifting. One ninety-minute Saturday morning session for new content, aligned to the school's scheme of work, plus one forty-five-minute weekday slot in the late window for marked past-paper questions. Two contact points, under three hours a week, and the weekday slot can be moved without destroying the plan because the teaching already happened on Saturday. This is the schedule we propose most often in this district and the one families are most surprised by.

The second is for a Year 11 student with a specific weakness. A dated block of eight to ten sessions, twice weekly in the late window, aimed at one subject and one paper, scoped against the school's mock dates. The honest conversation happens at the start: here is what can move in eight weeks and here is what cannot. When the block ends, it ends, and the decision to continue is made deliberately rather than by drift.

The third is for a household with a cross-district school place, where the child is not home before six. Here the early window does not exist, so the whole plan sits on Saturday morning for teaching and one late weekday slot for practice, with the second weekday slot added only in the mock term. Trying to squeeze a 5pm session into this household is the mistake, and it is made constantly because 5pm is when tutoring is supposed to happen.

Two rules apply to all three. Protect the evening meal, because sessions scheduled across it get cancelled and cancelled sessions break the rhythm that makes tutoring work. And decide the Ramadan arrangement in advance, shifting to a shorter post-Iftar slot with new teaching moved to the weekend. A schedule built for the year it has to survive beats a schedule that is perfect in October.

faqs.question: What is the earliest an IGCSE session can start on a weekday in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: For most families, about 5pm, and for some not until after six. Schools in this cluster finish between roughly 2pm and 3.30pm, Al Twar sits late on most bus loops so add thirty to forty-five minutes, and then changing, eating and the school's own homework take until around 4.45pm. Households with a cross-district school place in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City should assume after 6pm. Send us the school name and the finish time and we will tell you which window is genuinely usable.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our house in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. IGCSE tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked questions and marked past papers. In a villa district behind Al Qusais that is the practical answer rather than a compromise: a 5pm slot starts at 5pm, a session that has to move costs nobody a wasted journey, and the tutor is chosen for the board your child actually sits.

faqs.question: Why do in-home lessons here often run short?
faqs.answer: Because of the drive. A tutor leaving central Dubai for a 5pm appointment in Al Twar faces forty to sixty minutes at the evening peak, arrives fifteen to twenty-five minutes late, and usually has a hard stop because of a later appointment elsewhere. The lesson shrinks while the invoice does not. Over a term the bigger loss is reliability: once a family stops depending on the slot, homework and revision stop being organised around it, and that is worth more than the minutes lost.

faqs.question: Is Saturday morning a sensible time for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the best slot of the week in this district and the least used. In Al Twar households Friday and Saturday afternoon carry most commitments, which leaves Saturday from nine until noon free with the student at their freshest. We normally propose a ninety-minute Saturday session for new content plus one short weekday slot for marked practice. It survives a bad week too, because school events and mock timetables rarely land on a Saturday morning.

faqs.question: Should my child start tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, in almost every case, and most families do the opposite. Year 10 is when content is introduced at pace, and a gap created there is carried into a year with no spare time to repair it. Year 10 hours are also cheaper per unit of effect: there is room in the week, no mock timetable competing, and no triage. Year 11 tutoring is bought under pressure and spends part of its hours assessing damage rather than teaching. The same money a year earlier does more.

faqs.question: Who at the school can tell me the specification codes my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the examinations officer and ask for the board, the specification code and the tier in each subject. Cambridge codes you may see include 0580 for Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics, 0610 for Biology and 0500 for English Language; the Pearson Edexcel equivalents include 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1. For sciences, also ask which practical route the centre uses. That single email makes every past paper and mark scheme used in tutoring correct for your child.

faqs.question: Does the tier my child is entered for limit their grade?
faqs.answer: At Cambridge, yes, in subjects with Core and Extended tiering: a Core entry carries a lower grade ceiling than an Extended entry, and no amount of Year 11 tutoring lifts it. That is why tier is a Year 10 question rather than a Year 11 one. Ask for the tiers in writing while a change is still possible, and if a tier looks wrong for your child's trajectory, raise it with the school early. Pearson Edexcel is untiered in many subjects, which removes this problem there, although its Mathematics A carries Foundation and Higher tiers of its own.

faqs.question: Which series will my child in Al Twar sit, and when do results come?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a UAE candidate. On published dates: Pearson Edexcel June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Read the live official timetable from the board rather than any restatement, including this one.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge have several versions of the same timetable?
faqs.answer: Because every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If you are checking dates yourself, ask the examinations officer which zone your centre sits in first, then read that version from Cambridge's own site. Getting this wrong is a genuinely consequential error rather than an administrative one.

faqs.question: How do we fit tutoring around mock season in Year 11?
faqs.answer: By inverting the usual plan. During mock season the school week fills with revision sessions and timed papers, which squeezes the early evening window to nothing. The workable arrangement is Saturday morning for teaching, one late weekday slot for marked practice, and a willingness to move sessions rather than defend them. Scope the block against the school's own mock dates and accept honestly that two subjects can move meaningfully in eight weeks while five cannot.

faqs.question: What happens to lessons during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. School days shorten and the useful study window shifts to after Iftar, typically from around 8.30pm, so sessions become shorter and more focused: forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new teaching. New content moves to weekend mornings, which stay workable. Decide the arrangement before Ramadan rather than in week one. Because lessons run over live video there is no travel to re-plan, so a slot change is an administrative matter.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around prayer times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth raising at the booking stage rather than working around awkwardly later. A session that reliably runs into Maghrib will be cut short or cancelled, while one scheduled to finish before it or start after it simply holds. Since nothing depends on a tutor's drive across the city, moving a slot by thirty or forty minutes for a whole term is a scheduling change rather than a logistical one. Tell us the constraint and the plan is built with it rather than against it.

faqs.question: Does the same monthly budget buy more online than in-home?
faqs.answer: It buys a different shape, and for IGCSE usually a better one. Advertised in-home packages of four two-hour sessions run AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month, while online packages of eight sessions appear at around AED 799. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors. Since IGCSE progress comes from frequent marked practice rather than long teaching blocks, eight shorter contact points generally do more than four long ones at the same spend.

faqs.question: Does a third weekly hour add anything for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: One to two, and more than two rarely helps. One weekly session suits a student who understands the content and loses marks on technique, because the learning happens in the practice between lessons. Two suit a real content gap or a Year 11 paper under deadline. Past two hours a week the limiting factor stops being teaching time and becomes the student's own independent practice, so additional hours displace the very thing that makes the earlier hours work.

faqs.question: We travel during the holidays. Do lessons have to pause?
faqs.answer: No, and that is one of the clearer advantages of the format. Because lessons are delivered over live video on Gulf Standard Time, a session can follow the family through a trip rather than stopping for three weeks and restarting cold. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made and they get built in, including a reduced frequency during the break if that suits. Any arrangement that depends on somebody arriving at a UAE address cannot do this at all.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IGCSE tutor in this area before booking?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Which board, specification and tier do you teach? Which practical route have you prepared students for? Can we trial the exact slot I intend to keep, rather than a convenient one? What will the first three sessions cover? Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and what are the cancellation terms both ways? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years? Hesitation on the permit or the cancellation terms is itself the answer.

intro.heading: Cheapest first: what IGCSE support in Al Warqa really costs
paragraphs: Work up from the floor rather than down from the premium. The lowest advertised online rates in Dubai sit around AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, which buys a university student or a recent graduate checking homework. That is a real product with a real use: a Year 9 who needs company while finishing set work is well served by it, and paying four times as much for the same service is the commonest avoidable expense in this market.

Above that sits the band most Al Warqa families actually need. A qualified subject tutor working online is roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. That tier can mark against a mark scheme, knows whether your child sits Paper 2 or Paper 3, and can tell the difference between a content gap and a technique problem. Above that again, specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and more make sense for one subject in the final run to a series, and almost never for all of them.

The expensive mistake in IGCSE is not the hourly rate. It is the tier. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is sat as Core, with Papers 1 and 3 and a grade ceiling at C, or as Extended, with Papers 2 and 4 and the full range to A star. The science syllabuses work the same way. A child entered for Core cannot be awarded an A regardless of how brilliantly they perform, and a child entered for Extended who is not ready can come out below where Core would have placed them. Correcting a tier decision costs a term. Nobody's hourly rate matters by comparison.

Delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Al Warqa lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For this part of Dubai that is more than a technicality. The local school supply around Al Warqa'a and Al Qusais is largely CBSE and British, and a tutor who lives within a short drive is far more likely to know a national curriculum than to know which paper a Cambridge Extended candidate sits.

What follows is written so a parent can check it. The codes are the ones printed on the examination entry. The grade ceilings are the published tiering rules. The series are June and November, the two Cambridge and Pearson sittings UAE candidates use. The rate bands name their sources. And where a figure could not be verified, it is left out rather than estimated, which is why you will not find a fine amount for unpermitted tutoring anywhere on this page.
