dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Al Warqa families reach IGCSE through British-curriculum schools in Al Qusais, Mirdif and Academic City, and increasingly through private candidacy. The notes below cover each route and what support costs inside it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by terminal written papers, with practical or alternative-to-practical components in the sciences. Most subjects are tiered: Core for grades C to G, Extended for the full A star to E range. Cambridge runs June and November series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, so the correct zone timetable matters more than parents realise.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge codes a parent in Al Warqa should be able to read off an entry form: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0654 Coordinated Sciences, 0500 English First Language. Knowing the code is the difference between a tutor teaching the right paper and a tutor teaching the subject.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's equivalent, available in May-June and November each year. Mathematics A is 4MA1, sat at Foundation or Higher tier rather than Core and Extended, with Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher running to grade 9. The sciences are 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with Double Award Science as 4SD0, and the assessment structure differs from Cambridge in ways that matter for revision.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from Al Warqa run Pearson in some subjects and Cambridge in others, which is why a tutor should be asked which board before anything else. The November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The usual continuation for a Dubai IGCSE student not moving to the IB Diploma. Subject choices at this point are constrained by IGCSE tier and grade, which is the practical reason the Year 10 tiering decision matters: a Core maths candidate has a narrower route into A Level Mathematics than an Extended one.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, alongside five IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB alternative to IGCSE at the same ages, assessed against four criteria per subject group rather than by terminal papers. Some Al Warqa families compare the two directly when choosing a school, and the honest answer is that they test different things rather than one being harder.
programmes.countryNote: Where a child moves from MYP into IGCSE mid-course, the gap to close is examination technique rather than content: criterion-marked tasks reward investigation and communication, while IGCSE papers reward precision against a mark scheme under time pressure.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: IGCSE support is bought by syllabus, not by subject. Each note below names the code, the tier structure and where Al Warqa candidates most often drop marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling at C; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A star. Extended marks are lost most often on algebraic manipulation under time pressure, on bearings and transformations, and on multi-step problems where the method is right and the working is unreadable.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Foundation reaches grade 5, Higher runs to grade 9 with grade 3 allowed. Two papers, both calculator-permitted, which changes revision priorities compared with Cambridge. Students moving between boards mid-course lose marks to unfamiliar question phrasing rather than to unfamiliar mathematics.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Core takes Papers 1 and 3, Extended takes Papers 2 and 4, and candidates sit either Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical. Marks go on electricity circuit analysis, on graph gradients without units, and on Paper 6 questions about variable control that reward method rather than recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic nomenclature account for most dropped Extended marks, together with the qualitative-analysis questions on the practical paper where students name a result without naming the observation that produced it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The volume of terminology hides the real issue, which is applying it to unfamiliar organisms and data. Extended candidates lose marks on osmosis and transport explanations where the direction of movement is stated without the gradient that drives it.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: One syllabus covering all three sciences, with Coordinated as a double award and Combined as a single. Students sit fewer papers than triple science but cover a wider spread per paper, so revision must be organised by paper rather than by subject.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response. Marks are lost where candidates summarise a passage instead of analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and in the writing paper where register is misjudged for the stated audience.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening with an optional spoken endorsement depending on the code entered. Al Warqa candidates frequently sit this rather than First Language, and the tier chosen affects both the grade ceiling and the vocabulary expectation.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455, 0450)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the top marks. Students lose heavily where they define a term correctly and never apply it to the case material in front of them, which is a technique fault rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 and 0544)
subjects.description: Entered as First Language or Foreign Language depending on the child's background, and this is separate from the Arabic that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to teach. Note that Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects counted for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency.

paragraphs: At the bottom of the Dubai market, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. It is a legitimate product and it is badly undervalued by parents who assume cheap means useless: a Year 9 who will not sit down without someone present is well served, and nobody should pay AED 300 an hour for that.

The middle tier is where IGCSE work actually belongs, and it runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Ask the code question before the rate question and the tier sorts itself out.

At the top, Bestimate's Dubai table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and BartyED sits at AED 650. Paying them across four subjects for two years is how a household ends up with a tutoring budget larger than a school fee instalment.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that costs more than any hourly rate
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers most of its IGCSE syllabuses, and the tier is chosen by the school when entries are made. Mathematics 0580 Core sits Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C. Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A star. The sciences follow the same pattern: Core takes Papers 1 and 3, Extended takes Papers 2 and 4, and candidates additionally sit either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers instead, with 4MA1 Foundation reaching grade 5 and Higher running to grade 9.

The money consequence is blunt. A child entered for Core who needs a B for a sixth-form place cannot get one, no matter how many hours you buy. A child entered for Extended who is not ready can finish below where Core would have placed them, because Extended papers assume content Core candidates never meet. Both are reversible before entries close and expensive afterwards, and the decision is usually made in a single conversation with a subject teacher that most parents do not realise is happening.

So the first useful thing an IGCSE tutor does in Al Warqa is pressure-test the tier against current work. That takes one or two sessions at ordinary rates, and it is worth more than a term of general revision. Where a child is borderline, the honest options are to buy targeted work on the specific Extended content they are missing, or to accept Core and plan the post-16 route around it. What nobody should do is enter Extended on optimism and buy specialist hours in Year 11 to rescue it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: ask the board before you ask the price
paragraphs: Several schools within reach of Al Warqa enter Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson Edexcel for others, and families routinely do not know which. The two are comparable qualifications and genuinely different papers. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is sat at Foundation or Higher with both papers calculator-permitted; Cambridge 0580 splits Core and Extended and has a non-calculator component. Revision built for one board wastes time on the other, and a tutor who has only ever taught one will not notice until the first mock.

The sciences diverge too. Cambridge 0625 Physics offers a choice between Paper 5, a practical test sat in a laboratory, and Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Pearson 4PH1 handles practical skills differently again. For a student taught online, the Paper 6 route is the one where remote support works best, because the paper rewards knowing how to describe variable control, identify sources of error and read a table, all of which are teachable on a screen with a mark scheme open.

The practical instruction for an Al Warqa parent is short. Find the entry form or ask the examinations officer for each subject's code. Write the codes down. Give them to any tutor you are considering and ask which papers that code requires. A tutor who cannot answer is not necessarily a poor teacher, but they are not yet teaching your child's qualification, and you are paying for the gap while they learn it. It is a two-minute test and it eliminates more unsuitable matches than any amount of reading about teaching philosophy.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects, and what the Ministry of Education actually requires
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai are told a number of different things about subject counts, and at least one competitor page ranking for these queries publishes the wrong one. The sourced position is this: for British-track equivalency, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that changes a timetable is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student taking Arabic and Islamic Education, which every Dubai private school teaches regardless of its licensed curriculum, still needs five other accredited subjects at the minimum grade. Families who assume the mandatory subjects count towards the five can find themselves one subject short at exactly the wrong moment.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency is a process the Ministry of Education runs, not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and the official channel is the authority's own page rather than any intermediary. And no IB points threshold for equivalency is published here, because the source available for the British and American tracks does not state one and nothing should be invented to fill the gap. Verify any figure on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on it.

sections.heading: Where Al Warqa IGCSE candidates lose marks, paper by paper
paragraphs: The pattern is consistent enough to plan around. In Extended Mathematics, students lose marks on algebraic manipulation under time pressure and on multi-step problems where the method is correct and the working cannot be followed. Examiners award method marks for working they can read; a correct answer with illegible working scores worse than a wrong answer with clear method. That is a thirty-minute conversation and a term of habit, not a content problem.

In the sciences, two specific failures dominate. The first is graphs: axes without units, gradients calculated from grid squares rather than axis values, and lines of best fit drawn through the first and last points. The second is command terms. State, describe, explain and compare each demand a different answer shape, and a student who explains when asked to state wastes time, while one who states when asked to explain loses the marks outright.

On the alternative-to-practical papers, 0620 Paper 6 and its siblings, the marks sit in method rather than recall: naming the controlled variables, identifying a source of error, describing an observation rather than an inference. These are the easiest IGCSE marks to recover with a tutor and the ones schools have least time to drill, because thirty students in a laboratory is a different exercise from one student and a mark scheme. The fourth recurring loss is unit conversion in the physical sciences, where a candidate computes correctly in grams and answers a question that wanted kilograms, and the fifth is significant figures, which a mark scheme penalises quietly and consistently across a whole paper rather than in one visible place.

sections.heading: The November series as a resit route, and what it costs
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February-March series exists but is offered to India only, which is worth saying plainly because incorrect advice about it circulates widely. For a Year 11 who misses a grade in June, November is the realistic second attempt, and planning for it is a budget decision as much as an academic one.

The published Pearson dates give a usable shape for how far ahead these things sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May-June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why the right habit is to open the live official timetable rather than trust a date restated on any page, including this one.

What that means for an Al Warqa family is a short, finite tutoring block rather than a new rolling commitment. A June result arriving in late August leaves roughly eight to ten weeks before a November sitting. Spending them on one subject's paper technique at specialist rates is defensible: it is six to ten sessions, with a known end date, aimed at the specific papers that went wrong. Spending them on general revision across four subjects is how the same money achieves nothing.

sections.heading: Online versus a tutor driving to Al Warqa, counted in subjects
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. The argument for online delivery here is therefore an argument about what the same money buys, and the clearest way to put it is in subjects rather than hours. At the in-home band a household supporting two subjects is paying for roughly ninety minutes of a tutor's driving per week on top of the teaching. At the online band, that same premium is a third subject.

There is a supply argument too, and in Al Warqa it is the stronger one. The schools immediately around this community are largely CBSE and British, so a resident tutor is more likely to know a national curriculum well than to know which papers a Cambridge 0620 Extended candidate sits. Widening the pool to everyone free at Gulf Standard Time changes who you are choosing between, and in a subject as code-specific as IGCSE Chemistry that matters more than proximity ever could.

The format also fits the paper that remote teaching suits best. Alternative-to-practical work is reading tables, describing method and identifying error, done with a mark scheme on screen and annotated live. For Core and Extended written papers, screen-shared past papers marked line by line is not a substitute for sitting beside a tutor; it is the same activity with a better view of the mark scheme. Where a child genuinely needs physical supervision to work at all, the honest answer is that a different arrangement suits them better.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and what a tuition centre actually is
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted rather than unregulated. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so no figure appears here; a number circulating online could not be verified against any official source and is left out deliberately. What matters for a parent is that the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, which removes every excuse for not holding one.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. It needs an educational services permit for a training institute from KHDA, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Anybody in this market claiming otherwise should be asked for the number.

process.title: Find the syllabus codes
process.description: Ask the school's examinations officer for the code and tier of each subject, or read them off the entry form. Cambridge 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610; Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1. Those few characters tell a tutor which papers to teach and let you test whether they know the qualification.

process.title: Send a marked past paper
process.description: One recently marked paper in the weak subject, with the teacher's annotations, is worth more than a report card. It shows whether marks are going on content, on technique, or on working nobody could read, and those are three different purchases.

process.title: Pressure-test the tier before entries close
process.description: One or two sessions at ordinary rates will show whether Extended or Higher is realistic. Doing that before the school finalises entries is the single highest-value hour in the whole IGCSE course, and it is far cheaper than rescuing an optimistic entry in Year 11.

process.title: Take the free trial, then fix the slot
process.description: The trial should end with a named weakness and a rough number of weeks. Then set the time against the real Al Warqa school run: 16:30 at the Al Qusais end, 17:15 towards Al Khawaneej Road, later again for Academic City families.

process.title: Review at six weeks, then decide
process.description: Compare the school's own assessment data rather than the tutor's impression, then extend, change subject, or stop. Where a child is heading into a pre-series block, agree the end date in advance so the block stays a block.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Al Warqa charge?
faqs.answer: Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. IB Gram publishes no fixed UAE price list and quotes after a free trial, because what you need depends on the tier, the subject and how many weeks remain before the series.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE syllabus code is my child in Al Warqa actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer or read the entry form; it is the most useful question a parent can ask. Cambridge codes include 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0654 Coordinated Sciences and 0500 English First Language. Pearson Edexcel uses 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences and 4SD0 for Double Award Science. Several schools near Al Warqa enter different boards for different subjects, so one answer does not cover the whole timetable.

faqs.question: What is the grade ceiling if my child sits IGCSE Core instead of Extended?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A star. Pearson uses tiers instead: Mathematics A 4MA1 Foundation reaches grade 5 while Higher runs to grade 9. The practical consequence is that no amount of tutoring lifts a Core candidate above the ceiling, so if a sixth-form place requires a B the tier has to change before entries close, not afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor change my child's IGCSE tier before entries are finalised?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change the entry; only the school can, and the decision usually happens in a conversation with a subject teacher that parents do not realise is taking place. What a tutor can do, in one or two ordinary-rate sessions, is test current work against the upper-tier papers and give you an evidenced view. That evidence is what a reasonable head of department will discuss. Doing this before entries close is far cheaper than buying specialist hours in Year 11 to rescue an optimistic entry.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my Al Warqa school enters Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: They are comparable qualifications rather than one being harder, but they are genuinely different papers. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits Core and Extended and includes a non-calculator component; Pearson 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers with both papers calculator-permitted. The sciences differ in how practical skills are assessed. Revision built for one board wastes time on the other, which is why a tutor should be asked which board they are teaching to before anything else is agreed.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does an Al Warqa student need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. Students on the British track must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking Dubai page states that six subjects are required, which does not match the published clarification. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel rather than through any provider.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams happen for students in Al Warqa?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, so the correct zone timetable matters: Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE also runs in May-June and November. The February-March series exists but is offered to India only, so it does not apply here.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth paying for after a disappointing June result?
faqs.answer: Often, and the timing works. For the June 2026 series, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, which leaves roughly eight to ten weeks before a November sitting; the November 2026 final Pearson timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. That window suits a short, finite block of six to ten sessions on one subject's paper technique, with a known end date. It does not suit general revision across four subjects, which is how the same money achieves nothing.

faqs.question: My Al Warqa child is taught online, so what happens with the science practical paper?
faqs.answer: Cambridge science candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school decides which. Paper 6 is assessed on method rather than manual skill: naming controlled variables, identifying sources of error, describing an observation rather than an inference, reading tables and plotting correctly. All of that is teachable over live video with a mark scheme on screen. Where a school enters Paper 5, laboratory practice happens at school and tutoring covers the theory and technique around it.

faqs.question: Does anybody travel to Al Warqa to teach IGCSE in person?
faqs.answer: Providers in the Dubai market do, at AED 180 to 500 an hour with the commute inside the rate, but IB Gram does not. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In this community the trade is usually favourable: the schools immediately around Al Warqa are largely CBSE and British, so a nearby tutor is more likely to know a national curriculum than to know which papers a Cambridge Extended candidate sits.

faqs.question: Where do Al Warqa IGCSE candidates lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Three places, consistently. Working that an examiner cannot read, which forfeits method marks that were genuinely earned. Graphs with unlabelled axes and gradients measured in grid squares instead of axis values. And command terms treated as interchangeable, when state, describe, explain and compare each demand a different answer shape. On alternative-to-practical papers the marks sit in method rather than recall, which makes them the easiest IGCSE marks to recover and the ones a class of thirty has least time to drill.

faqs.question: Should we buy tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if there is a known weakness, because starting early is what makes the middle market tier sufficient. A content gap addressed in Year 10 at AED 150 to 300 an hour becomes, in the final term of Year 11, a specialist-rate problem under deadline pressure. The exception is paper technique, which is genuinely a Year 11 purchase: a short block of timed papers marked against the scheme in the eight to ten weeks before a series is one of the few places specialist rates earn themselves.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards my child's five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count on the British equivalency track. Those subjects are still mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so a student takes them and needs five other accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Families who assume the mandatory subjects count can discover they are a subject short at an awkward moment.

faqs.question: Does my IGCSE tutor need a licence to teach in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Because it is free and fast, asking is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. Cambridge, Pearson and IB materials are copyright, and reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is infringement. What a tutor can legitimately do is point you to the official source, work with material the school has already issued, and teach the technique that a mark scheme rewards. The teaching is the product; the papers belong to the board that wrote them.

The free trial lesson should finish with three things: which papers your child sits, where the marks are going, and whether the tier they are entered for is realistic. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nothing is promised about a grade, there is no fixed term, and if we cannot cover a syllabus properly we will say so rather than take the booking.

intro.heading: The villa, the dining table and the arithmetic underneath
paragraphs: Al Wasl is a villa and compound district running along Al Wasl Road, close to the Al Safa school cluster and a few minutes from Jumeirah and City Walk. Households here are often larger than in the apartment districts nearby, with two or three school-age children at different stages, and the mental image behind this search reflects that: a tutor who comes to the house, works at the dining table, sees one child and then the next, and solves the week in a single visit. It is an appealing picture and it is worth examining on the numbers before anybody commits to it.

The published rates in this market are the place to start, because the per-child figure is what actually decides a household budget. In-home one-to-one work in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to 300. For one child, the in-home premium is a single journey. For two children in different subjects it is two journeys by two different specialists, or one generalist covering both, which is the compromise families make without noticing they have made it.

That compromise is the real cost. An IGCSE candidate is entered for eight to ten subjects across one or two examination boards, and the subjects that genuinely need paid teaching are rarely the same for two siblings. A single visiting tutor who can cover Year 8 mathematics and Year 11 chemistry to specification level is an unusual person; what families more often get is somebody competent in one and approximate in the other. The approximate half is the half that was paid for at a premium, and it is the half that does not move a grade.

IB Gram's position, stated at the top. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. An Al Wasl household therefore gets a different specialist per child per subject, each matched on the specification rather than on willingness to drive, and two children can be taught back to back on the same evening by two different people without anyone arranging a route. The comparison is laid out below with the published figures attached so a family can disagree with the conclusion if they want to.

What follows is the detail an Al Wasl parent can use today: how this district genuinely compares with the three next to it, the practicalities of in-home tutoring that nobody writes about, the per-child cost arithmetic for one, two and three children, how to triage eight to ten subjects down to a fundable list, how tuition centres and school clinics fit in, what to ask any tutor before the first session including the permit question, and the limits of what we will claim.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: An Al Wasl household with several children is usually spanning three or four stages at once. These are the stages, with what each one genuinely needs bought and what it does not.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course
programmes.description: Content-led teaching with internal assessment, and no external examinations. Almost nothing here is irreversible, which makes it the cheapest stage at which to fix anything and the stage most often over-tutored. A younger sibling receiving weekly sessions because an older one needs them is a common and avoidable line in a household budget.
programmes.countryNote: In this corridor the one genuinely consequential thing in these years is the evidence that feeds the Year 9 or Year 10 tier decision in mathematics and the sciences. A single diagnostic session in Year 9 is worth more than a term of weekly ones, because it addresses the decision rather than the term, and the decision has a shadow that reaches sixth form.

programmes.name: Year 10, the first IGCSE year
programmes.description: The two-year course starts, tier placements are decided and the evidence for them accumulates. Cambridge syllabuses in mathematics and the sciences run Core and Extended routes; Pearson Mathematics A runs Foundation and Higher tiers. The route determines which papers are sat and which grades can be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Al Wasl families consistently start support in Year 11 and consistently wish they had started in Year 10, and the reason is tiering rather than content. A ceiling set on an entry form cannot be lifted by a tutor later. Ask the school which tier each science and mathematics entry sits in, what evidence it rests on, and when the window to revisit it closes.

programmes.name: Year 11, the examination year
programmes.description: Mocks in winter and often again in spring, entry deadlines settled, practical components to prepare, then the series itself. Eight to ten subjects, six or more science papers for a separate-science candidate, and a revision calendar that cannot be completed, which makes subject triage the central decision of the year.
programmes.countryNote: This is the year the search for a home tutor usually happens, and it is the year in which the one-visit model fails hardest. A Year 11 candidate needs specification-specific help in two subjects and a written timetable in the rest; a generalist covering four subjects at a premium rate is the most expensive way to buy the least useful version of that.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: The federal process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate. For the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which matters in Dubai where both are mandatory in every private school. One competitor ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. IB Gram neither performs equivalency nor guarantees any outcome in it, and no tutoring is required for it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects an Al Wasl household is most often juggling, with a straight answer on whether each one usually justifies a paid hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Almost always worth funding where there is a weakness, because algebraic fluency underpins the sciences as well, and because tier placement rests on it. The specific gain is speed: a student who rearranges an equation slowly loses marks across four subjects, not one. Establish which of the three specifications applies before the first session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The science most worth funding if only one can be. The quantitative chain from moles through concentration to titration arithmetic breaks at a link the student cannot locate alone, and a revision guide will not find it. One diagnostic session usually does, which makes this a short intervention rather than an open-ended one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Responds to short frequent practice on formula handling, units and graph reading rather than to long sessions, which is a scheduling fact worth knowing. Electricity and the wave vocabulary account for most losses. Often addressable with one block of work plus a written practice schedule rather than weekly hours all year.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest recall volume and the subject least likely to need a tutor. A structured retrieval timetable moves biology more reliably than weekly sessions do. What does need teaching is command-term discipline and the data-interpretation questions, which surprise students who treated the subject as memorisation.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Frequently requested and frequently the wrong purchase. Marks move on structure, on answering the question asked and on timing rather than on vocabulary or reading more widely. Two or three sessions on essay structure plus marked timed practice usually achieves what a term of weekly conversation does not.

subjects.name: Combined and double-award science
subjects.description: The route for students taking science as one or two subjects. Content is reduced rather than easier and the revision calendar is genuinely lighter, which is sometimes the right answer for a candidate carrying ten subjects. Past-paper practice must come from the combined specification, not from the separate-science papers.

subjects.name: Business, Economics and ICT
subjects.description: Case-study subjects where the technique is applying terminology to the specific scenario rather than reciting it. That is teachable in a small number of sessions and then practised alone, which makes these poor candidates for weekly year-long support and good candidates for a short block.

subjects.name: Modern languages
subjects.levels: French, Spanish, Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: The one area where regular short sessions genuinely beat blocks, because speaking and listening need frequency. Availability varies by language and level, and Arabic at a high level is better served in Dubai than in most markets. Oral components need a tutor who will conduct them rather than discuss them.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: KHDA requirement · all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and prescribed languages of instruction. They occupy real homework time in an examination year and are excluded from the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency count.

paragraphs: The search phrase describes a specific arrangement, and it is worth saying out loud because nobody in this market examines it. A tutor arrives at the villa on a weekday evening, works with the Year 11 for an hour at the dining table, then spends thirty minutes with the Year 8, answers a question from the Year 6 on the way out, and leaves. One journey, one invoice, one relationship, and a parent who can be in the kitchen rather than in a car. In a villa district with several children per household, that is a genuinely attractive proposition and it is why this search exists.

Three things about it do not hold up. The first is specification depth: the person who can teach Pearson 4CH1 chemistry to a Year 11 at grade-9 level is unlikely to be the same person who should be handling Year 8 mathematics, and a tutor who claims both across four curricula is describing availability rather than expertise. The second is pricing: published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, and the premium is a car. The third is attention: a half-hour tacked onto the end of another child's session is supervision, not teaching, and it gets billed as the latter.

The alternative is less tidy and works better. Each child is matched to a specialist on the specification their school actually entered, the sessions sit back to back on the same evening if that suits the household, and nobody travels. The Year 11 gets somebody who knows the board; the Year 8 gets forty minutes aimed at one thing; the Year 6 probably needs nothing at all, which is the part of the conversation most providers will not have. The rest of this page sets out the comparison with the figures so the trade can be judged rather than taken on faith.

sections.heading: Al Wasl against Al Safa, Jumeirah 1 and City Walk
paragraphs: Four districts, all within about fifteen minutes of each other, and four separate searches that return four different pages. The table below sets out what genuinely differs for an IGCSE family, and the honest finding is that only two of the columns vary meaningfully: housing, which changes whether in-home tutoring is even practical, and the length of the school run. The supply of tutors who know a specific syllabus code at Year 11 level does not vary, because the four districts share Al Wasl Road, Jumeirah Beach Road and the same cluster of schools in Al Safa.

Al Wasl's distinctive feature in this group is household size and housing type. A villa has a room that can be used, which makes in-home tutoring physically possible in a way it often is not in a City Walk apartment with three children and one study. That is a real difference and it is the reason this district produces more of these searches than its neighbours do. It is also the reason the per-child arithmetic matters more here: the model being considered is usually a multi-child one.

What does not differ, and is worth checking rather than assuming, is the specialist pool. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen different curricula. Filter for somebody who has taught a specific Cambridge or Pearson specification at Year 11 level, is free on a particular weekday evening, and will drive to this corridor, and the list is short in every one of these four districts. The practical test for any provider, including this one, is to ask how many of their tutors have taught your child's exact syllabus code in the last two academic years.

sections.heading: The practicalities nobody writes about: who is in the room
paragraphs: In-home tutoring carries a set of domestic questions that no page in this market addresses, and they are worth thinking through whichever delivery model a family chooses. The first is supervision. A tutor working with a fifteen-year-old in a villa should not be alone with them behind a closed door, and the sensible arrangement is a room with a door open and an adult in the house. Families who have not considered this in advance tend to improvise, which is how a session ends up at the kitchen table with two siblings and a television nearby.

The second is attention. Siblings are the main reason a dining-table session underperforms: a Year 11 working on titration arithmetic with a Year 8 asking questions across the table is not having an hour of teaching. Where in-home tutoring works well, the household has set up a specific space, a closed hour and an understanding that the hour is not interruptible. That is achievable and it takes deliberate effort, and it is more effort in a house with three children than most families anticipate when they book.

Online delivery changes the shape of both problems rather than removing them. The session happens in a room the family chooses, with the door as open or closed as they prefer and a parent able to hear it from the next room, and the whole lesson is on a screen rather than in a private conversation. Siblings still interrupt, but a headset and a defined hour handle it better than a shared table does. The practical advice applies either way: name the room, name the hour, and tell the other children that it is not available. A family that does that gets more from a cheaper arrangement than one that does not gets from an expensive one.

sections.heading: The per-child arithmetic for one, two and three children
paragraphs: Household cost is the figure that decides this, and it is not the hourly rate. The table below works it through for one, two and three children using published Dubai market bands, because that is the calculation an Al Wasl family is doing in their head without the numbers in front of them. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's 2026 rate table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300.

The arithmetic produces one counterintuitive result and one obvious one. The obvious one is that in-home costs more per hour. The counterintuitive one is that the in-home premium per child falls as the number of children rises only if a single tutor covers all of them, which is precisely the arrangement that compromises specification depth. If each child needs their own specialist, in-home means several journeys and the premium multiplies rather than dividing. Families usually solve this by accepting a generalist, and the saving is then paid for in the Year 11's chemistry grade rather than in cash.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the other useful frame: AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. A household funding one subject per child for two children is therefore looking at a mid-market figure in the low thousands per month, and funding four subjects across three children is looking at a figure that will not survive the term. That is the arithmetic behind the triage section below, and it is why the honest recommendation is almost always fewer subjects than a family came prepared to buy.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one budget: the triage that has to happen first
paragraphs: An IGCSE candidate is entered for eight to ten subjects, and funding a weekly hour in each at the published band of AED 150 to 300 produces a figure no household should pay. More importantly, no Year 11 student can absorb it: a child with eight hours of tutoring a week on top of a full school timetable and mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework is not learning, they are attending. The first decision is therefore which subjects to fund, and it has to be made from marked work rather than from which subjects the student says they dislike.

The triage sorts subjects into three categories. Needs teaching: the student does not have the content or has a structural gap they cannot locate, which in this corridor is most often chemistry and mathematics. Needs timed practice: the student knows the content and loses marks to timing, command terms or carelessness, which is biology and the case-study subjects more often than not. Needs nothing: the student is secure and the anxiety belongs to the household rather than to the subject. Most Year 11 candidates end up with two in the first category, three in the second and the rest in the third.

The table below sets out how to tell which is which, using evidence a parent already has. The test is always the marked script rather than the predicted grade, because a predicted grade is a summary and a script is data. Where a student has not sat anything under timed conditions, that is itself the finding: the first purchase is a past paper and a mark scheme rather than a tutor. A provider who recommends weekly sessions in four subjects before seeing any marked work is not diagnosing anything.

sections.heading: Tuition centres, group classes and the provision you already pay for
paragraphs: Before buying one-to-one hours, two cheaper options deserve proper consideration. The first is the school. Dubai private schools are fee-paying, well resourced and inspected annually by KHDA, and most run subject clinics, lunchtime help, after-school revision and past-paper libraries. Parents in this district frequently do not know what exists because it was announced once in September. One email to the head of year, asking what is available in each subject and whether the child is on any intervention list, routinely changes the budget more than any rate negotiation.

The second is a tuition centre or group class, of which several operate within reach of this corridor. The per-hour cost is lower, the parent drives instead of the tutor, and the delivery is genuinely useful for one specific thing: content a student has not been taught, which happens after a staff absence or a mid-year move. What a group cannot do is read one student's own written answers each week and name the habit costing them marks, because those habits differ between students. Ask how many students will be in the room before comparing any rate.

The honest sequencing, then, is school provision first, group classes for content gaps second, and one-to-one for individual diagnosis third. A family that works through that order spends less and gets more than one that starts at the expensive end. It also means the paid hour, when it is finally bought, is aimed at the thing only a paid hour can do. A provider whose first recommendation is weekly one-to-one across several subjects has skipped two cheaper steps that would have worked, and the family will not discover that until February.

sections.heading: Verifying the person who will teach your child
paragraphs: Only one competitor page in the researched corpus touches licensing, in a single subheading, and it is the most useful check available to an Al Wasl parent. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation introduced the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service is called 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time listed. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, a figure circulating online could not be verified, and so none is quoted here. There is a second point on the same theme. Do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school: the permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tuition of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. That rule is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK document, but the principle is sound across the UAE and we do not make such arrangements.

Beyond the permit, four questions separate a specialist from a generalist and take two minutes. Which board and syllabus code have you taught this subject under, and in which of the last two academic years. Which tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. For a science, has the school entered a practical test, an alternative-to-practical paper, or a specification that examines practical skills inside the written papers. And what will you ask to see before the first session. A tutor who wants the marked script and the school's topic list is diagnosing. A tutor who asks only for the subject and the year group is not.

sections.heading: Online delivery from an Al Wasl address, and the limits
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script, the correct board's past paper and the published mark scheme on screen together. Nobody is sent to an Al Wasl address: IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a multi-child household the specific advantage is scheduling. Two or three children can each have a different specialist on the same evening, half an hour apart, and a cancellation or a mock timetable change moves one session rather than unpicking a route.

Availability is finite and we publish where. Mathematics and the sciences at Extended or Higher tier in a narrow weekday window may take several days to fill; less commonly taught languages and ab initio levels take longer. Standard subjects, the case-study options and English Language are usually matched in two or three days. When the first choice is not available we say so and name the alternative: a different hour with the right specialist, a tutor whose specialism is adjacent with the limitation stated, or a short wait. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit at all, which is why this one is written down and can be held against us.

The claims this page declines to make. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB organisation; a KHDA educational services permit belongs to training institutes with premises and we hold none. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link the official source. We do not perform or guarantee Ministry of Education equivalency and do not suggest tutoring is required for it. And no tutor can guarantee a grade, because the board marks the papers and sets the boundaries after the examination.

faqs.question: We have a villa with space for a tutor. Does IB Gram still only teach online?
faqs.answer: Yes. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. The space is genuinely an advantage for an Al Wasl household and it is the reason this search is more common here than in the apartment districts nearby, but it does not change the two things that decide outcomes: whether the tutor knows the exact specification, and whether each child gets their own specialist. Published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour sit above the AED 150 to 300 online band, and the difference is a journey rather than a better lesson.

faqs.question: Is an in-home IGCSE tutor better value for two children than for one?
faqs.answer: Only if one tutor can genuinely teach both, and that is the catch. Spreading a single journey across two children does reduce the premium per child, but two siblings rarely need the same subjects at the same stage, and a tutor who covers Year 8 mathematics and Year 11 chemistry to specification level is an unusual person. What families more often get is depth in one and approximation in the other, and the approximate half was the expensive half. If each child needs their own specialist, in-home means two journeys and the premium multiplies instead of dividing.

faqs.question: Who should be in the room when a tutor works with a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the house and the door should not be closed, whichever delivery model you choose. That is a straightforward safeguarding position and worth deciding in advance rather than improvising, because improvising is how a session ends up at the kitchen table with two siblings nearby. With online delivery the lesson happens in a room the family picks, audible from the next room, and the whole session is on a screen. Either way the practical advice is the same: name the room, name the hour, and tell the other children that the hour is not available.

faqs.question: Does an Al Wasl address get us a wider choice of IGCSE tutors than City Walk would?
faqs.answer: No. The two districts sit on the same road network, feed the same school cluster in Al Safa and therefore draw on the same group of teachers. What an Al Wasl villa does change is whether an in-home visit is practical at all, which is a real difference and the reason this question comes up here more than next door. The pool of people who have taught a specific Cambridge or Pearson syllabus at Year 11 level and are free on a particular evening is short in both districts. Ask any provider how many of their tutors have taught your child's exact code recently.

faqs.question: How many of our child's nine IGCSE subjects actually need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually two. Triage from marked scripts, not predicted grades, sorts subjects into three categories: needs teaching, where content is missing or a structural step is broken and the student cannot locate it; needs timed practice, where the content is known and marks go to timing, command terms or carelessness; and needs nothing. In this corridor a typical Year 11 candidate ends up with two subjects in the first category, three in the second and the rest in the third. Funding four or more weekly is almost always a sign that the triage has not been done.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in this corridor cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and the parent drives instead of the tutor. A group is genuinely useful for content a student has not been taught, which happens after a staff absence or a mid-year move. What it cannot do is read one student's own written answers each week and name the specific habit costing them marks, because those habits are individual: state symbols for one student, command-term discipline for another. Ask how many students will be in the room before comparing rates, and use groups for content gaps rather than for examination technique in Year 11.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor before the first session?
faqs.answer: Five things, and they take two minutes. Which board and syllabus code have you taught this subject under, and in which of the last two academic years. Which tier. For a science, has the school entered a practical test, the alternative-to-practical paper, or a specification that examines practical skills inside the written papers. Can you show your MoHRE private tuition work permit. And what do you want to see before we start. A tutor who asks for the marked script and the school's topic list is diagnosing; one who asks only for the subject and the year group is not.

faqs.question: Can our child's own class teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Do not arrange it. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school. That particular rule is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document, but the principle holds across the UAE and the conflict of interest is obvious regardless of emirate. A teacher at your child's school can, of course, help your child during school hours through the clinics and intervention the school already provides, and that is free.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is unwell, or we travel over a school break?
faqs.answer: A session moves rather than cancelling, which is a practical advantage of online delivery rather than a claim about teaching. A family travelling for a school break takes the slot with them as a time-zone adjustment, and a tutor unavailable one week is covered by moving the session within the week rather than losing it. Over a thirty-week year that difference is typically several sessions kept, which is worth more in cash terms than most hourly-rate negotiations achieve and considerably more in continuity, which is where most of the value in a two-year course sits.

faqs.question: Do tutors charge more for Year 11 than for Year 10?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai bands do not generally separate the two: qualified subject tutors online are quoted at AED 150 to 300 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above across IGCSE work. What changes is the number of hours a plan needs and the scarcity of good slots. In February and March the early-evening hours fill and the tutors with current specification experience are already committed, so a Year 11 family booking late pays the ordinary rate for a worse hour. Starting in Year 10 is also cheaper in total, because tier decisions can still be influenced then.

faqs.question: How can we tell whether a tutor actually knows the specification?
faqs.answer: Ask them something only somebody who has taught it would know. For a Cambridge science, which paper the school has entered for the practical component and what the difference means for preparation. For mathematics, whether the student is on 0580, 0607 or 4MA1 and what changes between them. For any subject, which topics the specification places in which paper. A tutor who answers those without looking anything up has taught the course. One who says the subject is the subject regardless of board is describing general competence, which is not what a Year 11 candidate needs.

faqs.question: Can siblings in Year 8 and Year 11 share one tutor?
faqs.answer: They can share a provider and should not share a session or, usually, a tutor. The content, the pace and the target are different, and a shared hour becomes supervision of one child while the other is taught. The arrangement that works in a multi-child household is different specialists scheduled back to back on the same evening, which online delivery makes trivial because nobody is travelling between them. One adult then covers the whole household's tutoring from one room, which is the practical benefit families were hoping a single visiting tutor would deliver.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for English Language tutoring at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Often not in the form families imagine. Marks in English Language move on structure, on answering the question that was asked, and on timing, rather than on vocabulary or reading more widely. Two or three sessions on essay and response structure, followed by timed practice marked against the specification's own criteria, typically achieves what a term of weekly discussion does not. Where a student is working in English as an additional language and is entered for a first-language specification, that is a different situation and regular sessions are justified; establish which specification applies before deciding.

faqs.question: What does a trial lesson actually prove?
faqs.answer: Less than families hope and more than nothing. It shows whether the tutor and the student can work together, whether the tutor watches the working rather than marking answers, and whether they can name the problem precisely by the end of the hour. It cannot show whether marks will move, because that takes four or five sessions and at least one marked paper. The useful output of a trial is the written note afterwards: if it classifies the problem specifically and says what would change in a term, the tutor is diagnosing. If it is encouraging and vague, it is not.

faqs.question: If we can only fund one subject, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Mathematics or chemistry, in most cases in this corridor, and for different reasons. Mathematics because algebraic fluency carries into the sciences, so one subject's worth of work raises marks in three or four papers, and because tier placement rests on it. Chemistry because the quantitative chain breaks at a link the student cannot find alone and a single diagnostic session locates it, which makes it a short intervention with a large effect. The wrong answer is to fund the subject the student complains about most, which is usually the one they are avoiding rather than the one costing the most marks.

intro.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve
paragraphs: Most pages about IGCSE tutoring are written as though the year had no shape. It has a very precise shape, and in November it sits at one of its few genuinely decisive points. Candidates are sitting the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November series, whose final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge, which enters most candidates in the schools serving this belt, examines IGCSE in a June and a November series in the UAE, and its entry deadlines fall a full term or more before each of them rather than weeks before. And for the great majority of Year 11 students living in Arabian Ranches, the papers that count are the June ones, which means mocks in January and a finite number of teaching weeks in between.

That runway is not evenly useful, and treating it as though it were is the commonest planning error in this market. The eight weeks between now and the winter break are the last stretch in which content can still be learned properly rather than crammed, because January belongs to mocks and February onwards belongs to the consequences of them. Anything a student does not understand by the break will be revised rather than taught, and revising something you never understood in the first place is the most expensive way to spend a Saturday morning.

Written backwards from the June series, the plan for a Year 11 student in this community has four stages. By the end of this term: every topic met once, two full past papers sat under timed conditions in each weak subject, and the specification printed and marked up against what has actually been covered in class. In January: mocks sat properly and marked against the real mark scheme rather than against hope. February to April: targeted work on the components the mocks exposed. May and June: the papers, on the timetable for the zone Cambridge has allocated your child's centre.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; that is a service we operate only in India. The UAE side is one-to-one teaching over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers, working and mark schemes. On a page driven by a deadline that matters for a practical reason. A plan with a date attached cannot afford a session lost to traffic on Al Qudra Road, and a slot at half past seven survives a late bus, a changed fixture and a parent still on Sheikh Zayed Road in a way that a drive out to the community does not.

The rest of this page is the calendar in detail: the eight-week table, the awarding bodies' published session and entry dates with their sources, what a mock result actually tells you, what tiering does to a grade ceiling before revision even begins, what a block of eight weeks costs in this market, and the retake routes through November. Read the entry-deadline table first if your child is a private candidate or might be entered for the November series, because entry deadlines are the dates nobody mentions until after they have gone.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: An IGCSE plan depends on two facts most families cannot state immediately: which awarding body enters your child, and what comes after Year 11. Both change what the next eight weeks should do. The routes below are set out with the detail a Year 11 parent in Arabian Ranches actually needs rather than a general description of each qualification.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a June and a November series, with results released through Cambridge's Direct portal and certificates following later. Most subjects offer Core and Extended routes, and the syllabus code on the entry, 0580 for Mathematics or 0625 for Physics, fixes exactly which papers a candidate sits. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant IGCSE route in the British-curriculum schools serving Arabian Ranches and the Dubailand communities. Entries are made by the school acting as the centre, so the exams officer is the person who knows your child's zone, tier and entry codes. Ask for all three in writing before planning anything, because each one changes which papers a tutor should be working on.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in May or June and again in November each year, with a modular structure in some subjects that Cambridge does not offer. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the clearest illustration of how long a retake takes to confirm.
programmes.countryNote: Used by a meaningful minority of Dubai schools, and sometimes alongside Cambridge inside one school for different subjects. A student can sit different subjects with different awarding bodies, which is exactly why the syllabus code rather than the subject name has to drive the tutoring plan in the weeks before a mock.

programmes.name: A Level, the usual next step
programmes.description: Two years, three or four subjects, assessed by external examination with no criterion grids anywhere in it. The IGCSE grade in the same subject is the main entry signal, which is why a 6 rather than a 7 in Mathematics this June can close a Further Mathematics door eighteen months later. Entry conditions are set by each school and published, usually subject by subject rather than as a single threshold.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools serving the Dubailand communities run A Level after IGCSE, with entry conditions attached to specific subject grades. Those conditions are the real reason a June grade matters, and they are worth reading before the January mocks rather than after the August results, because only one of those two moments leaves time to act.

programmes.name: IB Diploma, the alternative at sixteen
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. It is broader than A Level and keeps both a second language and a mathematics course compulsory. The IGCSE route still governs entry: Higher Level places usually assume a strong IGCSE grade in the same subject, so the condition sits inside this term rather than outside it.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places near Arabian Ranches sit mostly in Dubai Hills, Nad Al Sheba and Al Barsha, and most of them set IGCSE grade conditions for Higher Level entry. A student aiming at Higher Level Chemistry in September needs that grade in June, which puts the requirement firmly inside the eight-week window this page is about.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Give the syllabus code rather than the subject name when you enquire, because 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers and an eight-week plan built on the wrong one wastes the whole block. The subjects below are listed with their codes and with the component that most reliably moves marks inside a short, dated plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers in each specification, and the calculator rules differ between the boards and have been revised recently, so confirm on the awarding body's own page which of your child's papers allows one. Extended and Higher carry the top grades; Core and Foundation cap them. Algebraic manipulation and multi-step problem solving are where most marks move inside an eight-week block, because both are technique rather than content.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. Calculus, trigonometric identities and vectors arrive earlier than in the main course, so a student performing well in 0580 can still be in trouble here. Worth planning separately rather than treating as more of the same maths.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism carry the most lost marks, and the practical component differs between the two specifications. Numerical answers lose marks for units and significant figures rather than for method, which makes them the cheapest category of marks to recover in eight weeks and the first thing worth drilling.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the distance between a middling grade and a strong one. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards precise experimental writing that is teachable in a handful of sessions, which makes it the highest-yield single target available this term.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Command terms do the real work: describe, explain and suggest want different things, and a student who writes everything they know scores below one who answers precisely. Diagram and data questions are quick, reliable wins late in the year.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Double-award routes covering all three sciences across two IGCSEs. The content is narrower than three separate sciences, but the papers still test all three, so one weak science shows up across the whole award. Check which route is on the entry before any plan is written, because the papers are not interchangeable.

subjects.name: English Language and English Literature
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response in Language; set texts and extract analysis in Literature. Marks sit in structure and in answering the actual question, and both move quickly with marked feedback. Literature needs the specific texts your child's school chose, which is another reason the entry details matter more than the subject name.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, precise definitions and applied evaluation carry the grade. Students lose marks describing a concept where the question asks them to apply it to the case material. Eight weeks is usually enough to rebuild examination technique in these two subjects even when content knowledge is still thin.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.levels: Mandatory alongside the IGCSE timetable in Dubai
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. They occupy real space in a Year 11 week, which is the practical reason an eight-week plan has to be honest about how many hours exist.

sections.heading: Where the IGCSE year actually stands in November
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in Arabian Ranches is at the point in the year where the calendar stops being background and starts being the constraint. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November series has been running, with its final timetable set from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge, which enters most candidates in the British-curriculum schools near this community, examines IGCSE in a June and a November series in the UAE, and its final entry deadlines land a full term or more ahead of each sitting rather than weeks ahead. And the June series, which is what most students here are actually sitting, is close enough that the weeks between now and the winter break are the last genuinely teachable ones.

That last point is the one worth sitting with. There is a difference between learning something and revising it, and it is a difference of weeks. A topic taught in November can be practised in December, tested in a January mock, repaired in February and consolidated in April. The same topic taught in March gets one pass and a prayer. So a parent deciding in November whether to start is not choosing between tutoring now and tutoring later at the same price and the same effect. They are choosing between teaching and triage.

This is also the point in the year when the questions parents ask stop being useful. Is my child behind, how many hours do they need, which tutor is best: none of those can be answered without the specification, the entry details and a marked piece of recent work. The questions that can be answered are specific and dated. Which topics have not been taught yet? Which components lost marks in the last school assessment? What is the entry code and the tier? Those three answers produce a plan. The others produce a quotation.

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, week by week
paragraphs: Here is the plan, written as a calendar rather than as advice. It assumes a Year 11 student sitting in June, one or two weak subjects, and roughly two usable evenings a week once the bus has arrived in the community and dinner has happened. It does not assume a cooperative teenager, which is why each week has an output rather than an intention attached to it.

The single most important item in the table is the first one, and it costs nothing. Print the specification for each weak subject from the awarding body's own site and go through it with your child, marking every topic as taught, half-taught or never seen. Parents are consistently surprised by how much of a syllabus is still unmarked in November, and the exercise converts a vague anxiety into a list. A list can be worked through. An anxiety cannot, and it is what most families are actually paying a tutor to absorb.

The second most important item is the two timed papers. Not practice questions, not a worksheet, not a revision guide: a full paper, in one sitting, at the right time of day, marked against the real mark scheme. Most students have never done this before a mock, which is why mocks come as a shock. Doing it twice in the next eight weeks removes the shock and produces something genuinely diagnostic, and it is the cheapest form of exam preparation that exists because it needs nobody's time but the student's.
