sections.heading: Entry deadlines sit months before the paper
paragraphs: The gap between an entry deadline and the examination it governs is the piece of the system families discover late and expensively. Entries are made by the school acting as the examination centre, normally a full term or more before the papers, and once a series has closed the entry code and the tier are fixed for that sitting. Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June and a November series in the UAE, allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable, and publishes its deadlines for each series well ahead of it. None of those dates is set by the family and none of them is negotiable afterwards.

Pearson's published dates make the same point from the other end, which is the end families feel. The June 2026 series sent results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, more than two months after the last paper was sat. The November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. A family planning a retake needs to know that a November paper does not produce a usable grade until well into January, which is after most post-16 applications have been decided. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including one for the November series beyond this one, so the live official timetable is the only thing worth planning against.

What to do with that is practical. Ask the school's exams officer, in writing, for your child's entry codes, tier and administrative zone, and ask when each entry closes. Then diary the dates. If a private candidate entry is being considered, the lead time is longer again, because the centre has to accept the candidate before any entry can be made. None of this requires a tutor. All of it decides what a tutor can usefully do, which is why it sits near the top of this page rather than in a footnote.

sections.heading: Zones, timetables and the error that costs a whole paper
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge's own guidance to exams officers is unambiguous about the consequence: it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is a sentence worth reading twice before a family downloads a timetable from a search result.

In practice this means the only timetable that matters is the one your child's school issues, cross-checked against the awarding body's live page for the right zone. A timetable circulated in a parent group, or found on a revision site, may belong to a different zone and differ by a day or a session. For a student sitting eight or nine subjects across four weeks, a one-day error in one subject is enough to lose a paper entirely, and there is no appeal route built on having read the wrong document.

The same discipline applies to everything else a tutor works from. Syllabus codes change editions, specifications are revised, and a 2019 past paper may test content that has since moved. The awarding bodies publish all of it on their own sites, and that is where it should come from. A tutor may point a family to the official page and should not be circulating copies: reproducing syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice matter as well.

sections.heading: Reading a January mock instead of mourning it
paragraphs: Mocks arrive in January and are almost universally misused. A grade comes home, the house reacts to the grade, and the script, which is the only part with information in it, goes into a bag. The grade tells you roughly where a student stands. The script tells you why, and the difference between those two pieces of information is the difference between buying twenty hours of general revision and buying four hours that fix something.

The reading is mechanical. Go through the script with the published mark scheme beside it and sort every lost mark into one of a small number of categories: never taught, taught but not understood, understood but mis-executed, understood but ran out of time, and answered the wrong question. Those five categories need completely different responses, and the proportions tell you what the next eight weeks should look like. A student losing marks to timing does not need more content. A student with one blank topic does not need hours spread evenly across the subject.

One more thing is worth saying about mocks in Dubai specifically. They are set by the school, not the awarding body, and schools vary in how closely their mocks mirror the real papers. Ask whether the mock used a real past paper and, if so, which series. A mock built from a genuine past paper under genuine conditions is a diagnostic. A mock assembled from topic questions is a progress check wearing a diagnostic's clothes, and reacting to it as though it predicted a June grade produces a term of panic for no reason.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of IGCSE tuition costs in this market
paragraphs: Every figure in this section can be checked by a parent in about ten minutes, which is the only honest reason to publish any of it. Open the pricing page of three Dubai providers and read the numbers. EdFlik lists online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour. Tutopiya starts at AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED's examiner-led rate is AED 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives bands rather than one rate: AED 180 to 350 for an in-home visit and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist.

Now cost the block rather than the hour, because an eight-week plan is a block purchase whether or not anybody calls it that. Eight weekly sixty-minute sessions at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 comes to AED 1,200 to 2,400 in one subject. At the specialist band it is AED 1,600 to 3,600. Two subjects doubles it, and most Year 11 families are looking at two. Bestimate's monthly estimates line up with the same arithmetic: AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more where an exam-year specialist is involved.

Three things are worth knowing before any of it is spent. Rates rise as a series approaches, so the same specialist is dearer in April than in November, and the eight weeks this page is about are the cheap ones as well as the useful ones. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and market packages run AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions, which makes the travel premium close to a doubling. And nothing here is an IB Gram price list: these are other providers' published figures on the dates their own pages carried them, and the first lesson with us is free precisely so that the teaching can be judged before any money moves.

sections.heading: Tiering: the grade ceiling that is set before revision begins
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects are entered at one of two routes, and the route caps what can be awarded. Cambridge calls them Core and Extended; Pearson calls them Foundation and Higher. The decision is made by the school when it enters the candidate, usually on the strength of work done in Year 10, and it is made well before the revision that might have changed the judgement. A capable student entered on the lower route can work extremely hard and still be awarded the ceiling of that route and nothing above it.

This is the single most consequential thing on a Year 11 entry slip and the one families are least likely to have seen. Ask the exams officer which route each subject is entered on, and ask by when it can still be changed. The honest answer is usually the entry deadline for the series, which is exactly why this section sits next to the deadline table. After that point the ceiling is fixed for that sitting, and the only remaining route to a higher grade is a different series.

Where a tier looks wrong, the useful move is evidence rather than argument. A full past paper from the higher route, sat under timed conditions and marked against the mark scheme, gives the school something concrete to consider. It also settles the question honestly in the other direction: a student who scores poorly on the higher-route paper is probably entered correctly, and knowing that early redirects eight weeks of effort towards securing the top of the route they are actually on, which is a far better outcome than a term spent resenting the entry.

sections.heading: The November series and the retake routes nobody explains
paragraphs: A grade that does not do what a student needed is not the end of the matter, and the routes onwards are published rather than mysterious. Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June and a November series in the UAE; Pearson examines International GCSE in May or June and again in November. A subject can therefore be re-sat within months rather than a year, provided the entry is made in time and a centre will enter the candidate for it.

The timing is the part that catches families. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which means a November retake confirms a grade in January rather than in the autumn. If that grade is needed for a sixth-form place starting in September, the retake has to be planned against the receiving school's deadline rather than against the awarding body's. Cambridge releases its November results on its own published schedule, also well after the autumn, so the same constraint applies whichever board the subject sits with.

Private candidate arrangements are worth asking about early, because they are the slowest part of the process. A student not entered through their own school needs a centre willing to accept them, and that acceptance has to happen before any entry can be made. Some tuition centres in Dubai act as examination centres for private candidates; a centre operating with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a reasonable thing to ask to see. IB Gram is not an examination centre and does not enter candidates, so for the entry itself the school or the centre is the only route.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the three-term year, and the hours that actually exist
paragraphs: Dubai private schools on the September start run three terms, with the long break across July and August, a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in March or April. For a Year 11 student that produces a specific shape: content through term one, mocks at the start of term two, a spring break that falls awkwardly close to the June papers, and a final run of weeks in which almost nothing new can be learned. Any plan that ignores that shape is a plan for a student in a different country.

Ramadan now falls in the early part of the calendar year, which in practice places it between the mocks and the final revision run, and in Dubai it shortens the school day too. Families across the Dubailand communities move an afternoon slot to after Iftar, and a lesson delivered online absorbs that change without renegotiating anybody's drive. The same flexibility matters in the exam weeks themselves, when a paper in the morning makes an evening session either ideal or impossible depending on the subject sat that day.

Count the hours honestly before buying any. A Year 11 student in Arabian Ranches with a bus arriving after four, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons in the timetable, school assessments through term one and a weekend partly spoken for has perhaps two usable weekday evenings and one weekend morning. That is the budget. Filling it with four tutoring sessions produces a student who does no independent practice, and independent practice is where the marks actually move. Two well-aimed sessions and a protected hour of past-paper work beats four sessions and no homework every time.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the tier and the series
process.description: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry code, the tier and the administrative zone, then send all three with the subject. That is what decides which papers a teacher works on. A subject name alone frequently produces a plan built on the wrong specification, and eight weeks is not long enough to absorb that error.

process.title: Diagnose against the specification first
process.description: The first session goes through the published specification marking every topic as taught, half-taught or never seen, using your child's own exercise book as evidence. The output is a list. Families are routinely surprised by how much of the syllabus is still unmarked in November, and the list is what makes the following weeks spendable.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: One lesson at no charge, booked before any payment and with no card details taken first. It runs as a working session on a real topic, with written feedback afterwards. Judge it on whether your child can now do something they could not do an hour earlier, which is the only test that matters this late in the year.

process.title: Put two timed papers inside the block
process.description: A full past paper, in one sitting, marked against the published mark scheme, twice before the winter break. It costs nothing but the student's time and it is the most diagnostic thing available. Most students have never done it before a mock, which is exactly why mocks come as such a shock in January.

process.title: End the block with a written plan, then decide
process.description: The block closes with a plan for the break and for January that the student can follow alone. At that point you continue through to the June series, change teacher, or stop. If no specialist is free for the subject and slot you need, we say so rather than filling the hour with somebody approximate.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is cited, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every session and entry date on this page comes from Cambridge or Pearson's own published pages, with the milestone named. Across the competitor pages researched for this project, the words November and May returned almost nothing: no session, no entry deadline, no results date anywhere on the page.

whyPoints.title: Plans have an end date
whyPoints.description: Blocks are sold as eight weeks to the winter break or two sessions after the mocks, with a stated output. Open-ended weekly hours are easy to sell and hard to evaluate, and in a dated year they let a term pass without anyone having to say what the hours were for.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers, and a tutor is matched to the one on your child's entry. This also decides tiering, the practical component and the command-term style, which is why the code is the first thing we ask for and the last thing most providers mention.

whyPoints.title: No syllabus documents or papers supplied
whyPoints.description: Specifications, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites, and that is where a family should get them. We will point you to the right page for the right zone and edition. Circulating copies is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, worse.

whyPoints.title: Honest about hours and about availability
whyPoints.description: A Year 11 week in this community holds about two usable evenings, and a plan that pretends otherwise fails in week three. If the specialist you need is not free for your slot, you are told, with the options stated. No grade is promised by anyone here, in any subject, at any price.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE home tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending tutors to houses is a service we operate in India only. Teaching for Year 11 families in Arabian Ranches is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers, working and mark schemes. On a plan with a deadline attached that turns out to matter: a session cannot be lost to traffic on Al Qudra Road, and a slot at half past seven survives a late bus and a changed school fixture in a way that a drive out to the community does not.

faqs.question: It is November. Is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring for the June series?
faqs.answer: No, and in fact this is the best remaining point in the year to start. The weeks before the winter break are the last stretch in which content can be taught properly rather than crammed, because January belongs to mocks and the months after them belong to repairing what the mocks expose. A topic taught now gets practised in December, tested in January, repaired in February and consolidated in April. The same topic started in March gets one pass. Starting now is also cheaper, because specialist rates in this market rise as a series approaches.

faqs.question: How far before the papers do IGCSE entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Entries are made by the school acting as the examination centre, and in practice they close a full term or more before the papers are sat. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which means entries for that series were settled while the autumn term was only beginning. Cambridge publishes its deadlines ahead of each June and November series in the same way. Once a series closes, the entry code and the tier are fixed for that sitting, and the only route to a different entry is a later series. Ask the exams officer for the code, the tier and the zone in writing, then diary the deadlines.

faqs.question: What should a Year 11 student have finished by the end of this term?
faqs.answer: Four things. Every topic in each weak subject met at least once, with the published specification printed and marked up as taught, half-taught or never seen. Two full past papers sat under timed conditions in each weak subject and marked against the real mark scheme. The entry code, tier and administrative zone confirmed in writing by the school's exams officer. And a written plan for the winter break and for January that the student can follow without an adult beside them. Those four produce a usable January. Nothing else on the list matters as much.

faqs.question: My child's mock result came back two grades below target. What now?
faqs.answer: Read the script, not the grade. Go through it with the published mark scheme and sort every lost mark into categories: never taught, taught but not understood, understood but mis-executed, ran out of time, or answered a different question from the one asked. Those five need completely different responses, and the proportions tell you what to buy. A student losing marks to timing needs practice under the clock, not more content. Ask too whether the mock used a genuine past paper, because a mock assembled from topic questions predicts far less than families assume.

faqs.question: What are Cambridge administrative zones, and why does the timetable matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge's guidance to exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. So the only timetable worth planning against is the one your child's school issues, cross-checked on the awarding body's live page. A timetable shared in a parent group may belong to a different zone and differ by a day.

faqs.question: How long after the last paper does a Pearson International GCSE grade land?
faqs.answer: Pearson publishes the dates, and they are further out than most families expect. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November retake confirms a grade in January, not in the autumn, which matters if the grade is needed for a place starting the following September. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable rather than a restated date is the thing to plan around.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE paper in the November series instead of June?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a legitimate route rather than a last resort. Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June and a November series, and Pearson examines International GCSE in May or June and again in November. The practical constraints are the entry deadline and the centre: entries are made by the school, and a candidate not entered through their own school needs a centre willing to accept them first. The other constraint is results timing, since a November grade is confirmed in January. Confirm both with the exams officer before building a plan around the idea.

faqs.question: What are forecast grades, and who decides them?
faqs.answer: A forecast grade is the centre's prediction of the grade a candidate is expected to achieve, submitted to the awarding body by a deadline the board publishes ahead of each series. The school decides it, based on the evidence it holds, which in practice means mocks and classwork. For a family the useful implication is that mock performance is not only diagnostic, it is evidence feeding a formal submission. A student who sits a mock casually in January has supplied the evidence for a forecast they may later want to argue with. Ask the school when forecasts are submitted and what evidence it uses.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tuition does one weak IGCSE subject need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is content or technique, and a diagnostic hour answers that faster than a term of weekly lessons. A single untaught topic is often two or three sessions. Weak examination technique across a paper is six to eight, because it needs marked practice and the marking is the slow part. A subject where most of the syllabus is unmarked in November is a two-term project, not an eight-week one, and anyone who tells you otherwise before seeing a marked script is guessing.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week block of IGCSE tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At the qualified subject tutor band, which Unitors publishes from AED 150 an hour, eight weekly sixty-minute sessions in one subject comes to roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400. At the specialist band, which Bestimate puts at AED 200 to 450 and above and TutorChase quotes at AED 270, the same block is AED 1,600 to 3,600. In-home delivery is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, so the same block costs considerably more. Those are the providers' own published figures rather than an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan interfere with the final IGCSE revision run?
faqs.answer: It changes when the work happens rather than whether it happens. Ramadan now falls in the early part of the calendar year, placing it between the January mocks and the final revision weeks, and in Dubai it also shortens the school day. Families across the Dubailand communities move an afternoon slot to after Iftar, and an online lesson absorbs that without renegotiating a drive. The sensible move is to plan for it rather than around it: decide in December which weeks will be lighter, and bring forward the content that has to be taught rather than revised.

faqs.question: We think the tier on my child's entry is wrong. Can it still be changed?
faqs.answer: Usually only up to the entry deadline for the series, and with the school's agreement, because the school enters the candidate and holds the judgement. After entries close the route is fixed for that sitting and the grade ceiling with it. If you think a tier is wrong, bring evidence rather than an argument: a full past paper from the higher route, sat under timed conditions and marked against the mark scheme, gives the school something concrete. It also settles the question honestly if the result is poor.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code is on my child's entry, and does it change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the plan completely, and the exams officer at your child's school is the person who can tell you. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Mathematics 4MA1 are different specifications with different papers, and Pearson includes a non-calculator paper that Cambridge structures differently. Codes also determine the practical arrangements in the sciences and the command-term style across the papers. Ask for the code, the tier and the zone together, in writing, and send all three when you enquire about tutoring so the first session is not spent discovering them.

faqs.question: Who is allowed to tutor privately in Dubai, and is it checked?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page. School teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see the permit in the tutor's own name, and ask separately whether they teach at your child's school, which the permit's code of conduct prohibits.

faqs.question: What happens if no IGCSE Maths specialist is free before the mocks?
faqs.answer: You are told, and given the real options: a different evening, a short wait for a slot, or a teacher whose subject depth we describe honestly before you commit. November and December are the busiest booking weeks of the Dubai year for exactly the reasons set out on this page, so evening slots in Mathematics and the sciences go first. What we will not do is fill the hour with a generalist and let the gap appear in a mock script in January. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.closingHeading: Eight weeks, two papers and one written plan
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.closingBody: If your child is in Year 11 in Arabian Ranches and sitting in June, the next eight weeks decide whether February is teaching or triage. Ask the exams officer for the entry code, the tier and the administrative zone. Print the specification and mark it up. Put two timed past papers in the diary before the winter break. Then send us the subject, the code and the evening that works once the bus has arrived, and we will say who is free and what the block can realistically achieve. The trial lesson is free on a stated condition: one session, before any payment, with written feedback afterwards. Lessons run live online on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The twentyfold price spread, and what explains it
paragraphs: A parent in Arabian Ranches 2 who spends an evening collecting IGCSE tuition quotes ends up with numbers that cannot all be describing the same thing. Tutopiya advertises online sessions from AED 33 to 52 an hour. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED's examiner-led tier is AED 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 research puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Every one of those figures was published by the company that charges it.

Four things explain the spread, and only two of them are about teaching. The first is who the tutor is: a university student and a subject teacher with a decade of mark-scheme experience are different purchases. The second is whether the person knows the specific syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, which is the difference between useful past-paper work and a term of near misses. The third is whether a car is involved. The fourth is simply what the provider thinks the market will bear.

That third factor is the one worth measuring, because it is the largest single variable and it buys nothing academic at all. Compare the two monthly packages advertised in this market: AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Per hour of teaching the in-home package is roughly twice the online one. The extra is fuel, driving time and the fact that a tutor crossing Dubai in the evening can fit fewer students into a week. None of it reaches your child.

Arabian Ranches 2 makes that arithmetic sharper than most addresses. The community sits off Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street past the original Ranches, with Palma, Rosa, Lila, Yasmin, Camelia, Casa and Reem spread across it and Ranches Primary School inside for the early years. Secondary students travel out. A tutor driving in from Al Barsha or Mirdif at five o'clock is paying for that journey twice, once in time and once in the price they have to quote to make the evening worthwhile.

IB Gram is direct about where it stands in that comparison. We do not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India, and it is stated on all forty-eight of our country pages. For UAE families every lesson is delivered live over video, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time. The honest case for that is not that it is better in every way. It is that it removes the largest cost that buys nothing, and it widens the pool from people who can reach Arabian Ranches 2 by five o'clock to everyone who teaches the syllabus.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: The stage a child is at changes the cost as much as the rate does, because it changes how many hours are needed. These are the three stages where Arabian Ranches 2 families most often buy IGCSE support, with the honest cost implication of each.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years to terminal written examinations in the May/June or November series. Cambridge syllabuses are tiered into Core and Extended with separate theory papers and a practical or alternative-to-practical component; Pearson Edexcel runs untiered papers with experimental skills examined inside them. The number of subjects a student carries, usually eight to ten, is what makes the tuition arithmetic difficult.
programmes.countryNote: Arabian Ranches 2 secondary students travel out to campuses across the Dubailand belt and towards Al Barsha South, so an evening session realistically starts after five. The cost consequence is that a tutor making a visit to Palma or Camelia can serve fewer families per week, which is reflected in every in-home quote a parent will receive.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: The three years when tuition is cheapest and most effective per dirham spent. The skills that decide IGCSE outcomes, rearranging formulae, standard form, scale reading, graph plotting, planning a long written answer, can be made automatic here in a handful of sessions rather than repaired under pressure two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Ranches Primary School covers the early years inside Arabian Ranches 2 before children move on. Families who buy a short block in Year 8 or Year 9 typically spend a fraction of what the same household spends in Year 11, and they spend it without the deadline pressure that pushes parents towards the premium tier.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after IGCSE
programmes.description: The two post-16 routes available around the belt. A Level is linear with practical endorsement; the IB Diploma assesses papers plus an internal assessment and adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Both assume Extended-tier IGCSE content, which is where tier decisions made in Year 10 come back with a price attached.
programmes.countryNote: Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City take the A Level route; JESS Arabian Ranches and the IB campuses around Dubai Hills Estate and The Sustainable City take the Diploma. A Core-tier candidate heading for either route usually needs a summer catch-up block, which is a cost worth forecasting in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 12.

programmes.name: November series and resit entries
programmes.description: Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. A November entry is a normal route rather than a penalty, and for a single weak subject it is often cheaper than a year of general support. Entry is made through a centre, and entry fees vary by centre, so the figure must be requested from the centre directly.
programmes.countryNote: For a family in Arabian Ranches 2 the practical question is which centre the school uses and whether it accepts the entry, since not every school enters candidates in every series. Ask the examinations officer, and ask for the centre's own fee schedule in writing rather than relying on any figure found online.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Cost varies by subject more than most families expect, because the market for a tutor varies by subject. These notes describe each IGCSE subject by how easy it is to find someone competent and what that does to the price.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580
subjects.description: The deepest tutor market in Dubai and therefore the most competitively priced. Plenty of people can teach IGCSE mathematics well, which pushes rates towards the middle of the published range. The quality variable to test is whether the tutor marks against the scheme rather than only checking answers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics, Cambridge
subjects.description: A much thinner market than 0580 and priced accordingly. Taken by a minority of Year 11 students, it introduces calculus early and is the best possible preparation for post-16 science or mathematics. Expect to pay towards the specialist band because fewer tutors cover it.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Harder to staff than mathematics, especially at Extended tier, which moves the price up. Graph interpretation and formula rearrangement cause most of the lost marks, and both are cheaper to fix than the content, which is worth knowing before buying a long content-led block.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Extended-tier quantitative chemistry, mole calculations and electrolysis, is where a specialist earns the premium. A generalist science tutor can handle Core-tier work adequately; the same person will struggle with a two-step mole calculation under the time pressure of Paper 4.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: Widely taught and reasonably priced. Biology marks are lost to vocabulary precision rather than reasoning, so the useful work is specific and quick: distinguishing diffusion, osmosis and active transport in the exact terms the scheme uses, and answering the command word that was actually asked.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: A single tutor can usually cover the whole double award, which makes it cheaper per grade than three separate sciences. The hidden cost arrives later: the content gap into A Level or Diploma science is wider from a double award, and closing it is a separate purchase in Year 11 or the summer after.

subjects.name: English Language, Cambridge 0500 or 0990
subjects.description: Priced in the middle of the market. The marks move through structure and timing rather than through reading more, so a short block on planning a response and managing the clock is usually better value than a standing weekly commitment across two years.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: A thinner market than English Language and priced slightly higher. The work that counts is essay construction against the assessment criteria and precise textual reference, which means a tutor needs to have taught the set texts rather than read them.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Well supplied in Dubai and reasonably priced. Case-study technique and command-word discipline carry most of the available marks, and both transfer between the two subjects, so a student taking both gets more from one block of technique work than from two subject blocks.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: A thin tutor market relative to demand, which pushes rates up. Pseudocode, trace tables and the practical component need someone who has taught the specific syllabus, because the notation conventions differ between boards and losing marks on notation is common.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, and that all teachers of Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach it in school. Tuition demand is high and the market is specialised.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Also mandatory alongside the international curriculum, with KHDA setting the language of instruction and the class organisation rules. For the mandatory subjects, additional or different content may not be used without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, which constrains how any tuition material can be described.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor actually costs around Arabian Ranches 2
paragraphs: Think in months, not hours, because that is how a household budget works. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 research estimates the monthly cost of a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Against those estimates sit two advertised packages: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Put the two packages on the same footing. Eight online sessions is eight hours for AED 799, roughly AED 100 an hour. Four two-hour in-home sessions is eight hours for AED 1,599 to 1,799, roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. Same teaching time, double the price, and the difference is a car. For a family in Palma or Camelia running one subject through Year 11, that difference is AED 800 to 1,000 a month, or the cost of a second subject.

The hourly table below sets out every published band with the name of whoever published it. Read it as a market map rather than as a price list, because none of these are IB Gram rates and several are the cheapest end of a provider's range rather than the price a family would actually be quoted. The one figure in the table that is genuinely fixed is the last one: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge, so any tutor claiming a permit cost is passing on something that does not exist.

What the table cannot show is fit, which is the variable that decides whether the money works at all. A Year 11 Extended chemistry candidate needs someone who knows Cambridge 0620 Paper 4 and marks against its scheme. That person sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, not at AED 650 and not at AED 45. Paying above the band buys reputation; paying below it buys someone learning the specification alongside your child. Both are expensive in different ways.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: The in-home option deserves a fair hearing rather than a dismissal, because for some families it genuinely is the right purchase. A tutor in the room removes the need to supervise a screen, works with the student's own books and notes spread on a table, reads hesitation that a video call flattens, and keeps a distractible fourteen-year-old on task through physical presence alone. For a younger child, or for a student who will not engage with a screen, those are real and they are worth money.

For a Year 11 IGCSE student the same advantages weigh much less. The material is written, the working is shared on screen in either case, the past paper and mark scheme are documents rather than objects, and the student is old enough to run their own session. Set against that, the travel premium is substantial and it also narrows the choice: the tutor pool shrinks to people who can reach Arabian Ranches 2 by early evening and still make the trip worth their while.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai. That is a limit on what we sell rather than a claim about what families should want, and it is stated here because a page that quotes in-home rates without saying so would be misleading. Visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. For every UAE household the delivery is live video, one-to-one, and the argument for it is the one the table makes: the same teaching time at roughly half the published in-home rate, drawn from a wider pool.

The table also includes the two options families forget to price. A small group at a tuition centre is cheaper per student and requires two trips a week from the parent, which is a cost that never appears on the invoice. School after-school support is usually included in fees already, and it is the first thing to use before paying anyone, because it is free, it is staffed by people who know the student, and it is the only option on the list where the teacher also sets the classwork.

sections.heading: The five places IGCSE tuition money gets wasted
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is buying content when the problem is technique. A student losing marks to command words, units, significant figures and graph conventions does not need the biology re-explained, and a term of content lessons will not move the grade. The diagnosis takes one session with two marked papers in front of a tutor, and skipping it is how families spend four months on the wrong thing. This is the single most common expensive mistake in this market.

The second is practising the wrong papers. Cambridge Extended papers are not useful for a Core candidate, and Cambridge papers are poor timing practice for a Pearson Edexcel candidate even where the content overlaps. Families who have not confirmed the board, the syllabus code and the tier are frequently buying tuition against the wrong specification, which produces real improvement in material that will not be examined. One email to the school examinations officer prevents it.

The third is spreading hours too thinly. Three subjects at one session a fortnight each produces very little in any of them; one subject at one session a week usually produces a visible change. The fourth is buying the premium tier for a problem it does not solve. An examiner-led tutor at AED 650 an hour is not twice as useful as a subject specialist at AED 250 for a Core-tier candidate who needs graph marks, and the difference compounds over a year.

The fifth is starting too late. A block bought in March of Year 11 can only do paper technique, because there is no time to rebuild content, and it is bought at the point in the year when every good tutor is already full and rates are at their most confident. The same money spent in Year 9 or early Year 10 buys the mathematics-for-science skills that make the whole course easier. Nothing in tutoring is as cheap as acting early, and nothing is as expensive as acting in the last term.

sections.heading: Hours rather than rate: how much tuition a Year 11 student needs
paragraphs: Rate is the number families negotiate and hours is the number that decides the bill. Doubling the rate from AED 150 to AED 300 adds AED 600 a month at one session a week. Going from one session a week to three adds AED 1,200 at the lower rate. Frequency is the expensive variable, which means the most useful question is not what a tutor charges but how many hours the problem actually requires.

The honest answer depends on what is wrong. A technique problem across several subjects is four to six sessions, once, and then it is done. A single weak topic in one subject is three or four sessions. A whole subject that has drifted for a year is a term at one session a week. A Core-tier candidate who needs to be ready for Extended-tier content, or for a post-16 science, is a summer block. Only the last of those is genuinely expensive, and it is predictable a year in advance.

What does not work is an open-ended weekly commitment with no stated objective. It is comfortable for everyone, it produces slow improvement, and it costs more over two years than any of the targeted options above. A family in Arabian Ranches 2 paying AED 250 an hour weekly through Years 10 and 11 will spend somewhere around AED 20,000 across the two years. The same money buys a great deal of targeted work, and targeted work is what moves grades.

The table gives indicative hours by scenario. These come from the pattern of enquiries rather than from a study, so they are planning figures and not findings, and no tutor can promise a grade outcome from any number of hours. They are useful as a sanity check: if a provider proposes thirty sessions for a problem that appears in this table as four to six, that is a conversation worth having before the first payment.

sections.heading: The questions to ask before paying for a block
paragraphs: Most tuition disappointment in this market is a specification problem rather than a teaching problem, and it is preventable with six questions asked before any money moves. Which syllabus code and tier will you teach to? What will the first session diagnose, and how will you tell me what you found? Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? Does the quoted figure include value added tax? What happens if we stop after one session? And do you hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit?

The first question matters most because it is the one a weak provider cannot answer. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE chemistry has told you nothing; a tutor who asks whether your child is on Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 has told you a great deal. The second question protects against a block that never produces a diagnosis, which is how families end up four months in without knowing whether anything is working.

On the money questions, be specific. Some providers quote per lesson where the lesson is forty-five minutes, which is not the same as an hourly rate. On value added tax, the honest position is that a parent should ask whether the quoted figure is inclusive and get the answer in writing; we do not state the tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact here, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption. Ask, and keep the reply.

On the permit, the correct answer is yes, and the correct follow-up is that it cost nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor adding a permit cost to a quote is charging for something that is free. Do not accept a quoted fine amount either: no schedule of penalties has been published, so any figure is invented. These two facts alone are worth more than most of what is written about tutoring prices in Dubai.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context: school fees, entries and the fee freeze
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest line in a Dubai education budget and it is often the only one still moving. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family in Arabian Ranches 2 that means the school line is fixed for a year while the tuition line is entirely discretionary.

The scale of the sector is worth knowing too. Dubai's private schools held 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the British curriculum the largest at around 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, American at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

A larger, more competitive school sector is good news for a parent comparing options and neutral for tuition prices, which are set by the availability of tutors rather than by the number of schools. What a bigger sector does change is the tier question: more British-curriculum places means more IGCSE candidates, which keeps mathematics and biology tuition competitively priced and does nothing for the thin markets like Additional Mathematics and Computer Science.

On examination entry costs, this page publishes no figure. Entry fees are set by the centre and vary, and a private candidate entry is priced differently from a school entry, so the only reliable number is the one the centre gives in writing. Ask the school examinations officer for the fee schedule for the series your child will sit. Any figure found on a tutoring page, including this one, should be treated as a prompt to check rather than as a price.

sections.heading: When nobody is available, and what we say then
paragraphs: No tutoring provider covers every subject at every level in every time slot, and the honest ones say so before taking money rather than afterwards. Thin markets are predictable: Additional Mathematics, Computer Science, English Literature on specific set texts, Arabic as a first language, and Extended-tier physics or chemistry in the weeks immediately before a series. If a provider claims instant availability across all of those, that claim is the thing to question.

What IB Gram does when a specialist is not free is state it and offer the realistic alternative: a different time slot, a later start date, or a tutor who covers the adjacent area with the limitation named. What we do not do is place a general tutor in front of an Extended-tier candidate and let the first month establish that it was not working. That month is expensive in money and more expensive in confidence, especially for a student already behind.

The second honest limit concerns delivery. Every lesson for a UAE family is online. We do not send anyone to an address in Arabian Ranches 2, Palma, Camelia or anywhere else in the Emirates, and no amount of asking changes that, because the service does not exist here. A family that specifically wants a tutor physically present is better served by telling us so, because then at least nobody spends a trial lesson discovering it.

The availability table sets out the pattern as it actually is. Match times are typical rather than guaranteed, and they lengthen in the two months before a series when demand across Dubai peaks at once. The useful planning conclusion for an Arabian Ranches 2 family is that a subject with a thin tutor market should be arranged weeks earlier than a subject with a deep one, and that waiting until the mock results arrive is what turns a mid-band purchase into a premium-band one.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify for nothing
paragraphs: Three of the most useful checks in this whole process are free, and almost nobody makes them. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time.

The second free check is the school. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it publishes an inspection report for every private school in the emirate on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The reports are free to read and they are specific about teaching quality by subject and phase, which makes them far more useful than any summary. Abu Dhabi families have the equivalent through ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there.

The third free check is the syllabus. Cambridge and Pearson publish their specifications, timetables and key dates openly, and the school examinations officer will confirm which code and tier your child is entered for. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. That is a free, two-minute check with real consequences.

Two things should be said about what IB Gram is not, because competitors in this market blur them. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we hold no partnership with any school or school group. We have no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and no overseas telephone number is used as the route for UAE families. A tutoring business with premises here would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific authorisation we do not hold and do not imply.

process.title: Confirm the code, the tier and the series
process.description: One email to the school examinations officer establishes the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child is entered for. Those four facts decide which past papers are useful and which are a waste, and no sensible quote can be given without them. This step costs nothing and prevents the most expensive mistake in the list.

process.title: Send two marked papers
process.description: A diagnosis from marked work beats a description of the problem. Two scripts with the marks on them let a tutor classify the losses as content, technique or presentation, which determines whether you are buying four sessions or a term. It also tells you quickly if the real problem is mathematics rather than science.

process.title: Get the plan and the number of sessions in writing
process.description: Before any payment, you should have the objective, the number of sessions, what will be reviewed at the halfway point and when the block ends. An open-ended weekly commitment with no stated objective is the most expensive way to buy tuition, and a provider who will not define the block is telling you something.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session before anything is paid, worked on a real problem from a real paper, with no card details required. The tutor reports what they found in your child's technique. If the match is wrong, say so and we try another tutor; nothing is owed either way and the diagnosis is yours to keep.

process.title: Review at the halfway point and decide honestly
process.description: A short written note on what has moved, what has not, and whether the block should continue, change or finish. Finishing because the problem is solved is a legitimate outcome, and we will say so when we think it has been reached rather than letting a weekly slot become a habit.

whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run to AED 500 an hour because the drive is inside the price, and the advertised monthly in-home package costs roughly double the online one for the same eight hours of teaching. Our delivery removes that cost rather than marking it up.

whyPoints.title: The permit fact stated plainly

Both facts protect a parent from being charged for a permit or frightened by an invented penalty figure, and both are checkable on mohre.gov.ae and u.ae.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with an end, not open commitments
whyPoints.description: Most IGCSE problems are four to six sessions, one term, or one summer. Pricing and planning the work as a finite block with a stated objective is the main defence against a weekly slot that runs for two years out of habit and costs more than everything else combined.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor actually charge in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Published figures put in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai at AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's 2026 research, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Advertised monthly in-home packages run at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Arabian Ranches 2 sits further from the city's tutor supply than Motor City or Dubai Hills Estate, so quotes here tend towards the upper end of those bands. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; these figures are the market's, quoted for comparison.

faqs.question: How much of a home tutor's hourly rate is paying for the drive to Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Compare the two advertised monthly packages. Eight hours of online teaching is listed at AED 799 a month, roughly AED 100 an hour. Eight hours in-home, as four two-hour sessions, is listed at AED 1,599 to 1,799, roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. The difference is travel time, fuel and the fact that a tutor crossing Dubai in the evening serves fewer families in a week. On those published numbers, somewhere around half the in-home rate is paying for the journey rather than the teaching.

faqs.question: Is a monthly IGCSE package better value than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Usually yes on price and sometimes no on fit. An advertised AED 799 monthly package for eight online sessions works out well below the AED 150 to 300 hourly band for qualified subject tutors, which is the commitment discount. The risk is that a package commits you to a number of hours before anyone has diagnosed what is wrong, and most IGCSE problems turn out to need four to six sessions rather than a standing monthly arrangement. Diagnose first, then buy the shape that matches the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Where do Arabian Ranches 2 families most often waste money on tuition?
faqs.answer: Five places, in order of cost. Buying content lessons when the lost marks are technique, which a single session with two marked papers would have revealed. Practising past papers from the wrong board or tier because the syllabus code was never confirmed. Spreading too few hours across too many subjects. Paying the premium tier for a problem the mid band solves. And starting in the final term, when nothing but paper technique is still possible and every good tutor is already full.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor cost more for Extended tier than Core tier?
faqs.answer: Often, and for a supply reason rather than a greed reason. Extended-tier chemistry and physics need someone comfortable with quantitative work under time pressure, and fewer tutors are, so the market is thinner and the rate sits higher in the published band. Core-tier work can usually be handled competently in the AED 150 to 300 range. The useful consequence is that the tier your child is entered for should be settled before you start comparing quotes, because it changes which band you are shopping in.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE tuition does a Year 11 student actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong, and the range is wide. A technique problem across several subjects is four to six sessions, once. A single weak topic is three or four. A subject that has drifted for a year is a term at one session a week. Exam pacing alone is three or four timed papers reviewed. Only the whole-subject case is genuinely expensive. Frequency, not rate, is what drives a tuition bill, so the question to answer first is how many hours rather than how much per hour.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tuition rates rise as the May series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens across Dubai in the two months before a series, and tight availability pushes quotes towards the upper end of a provider's published range. That is not a formal price rise so much as the cheaper slots disappearing first. The practical consequence for an Arabian Ranches 2 family is that a block arranged in November is bought from a wider market than the same block arranged in March, and the March version can usually only do paper technique because there is no time left for content.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at a Dubai centre cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and centres publish their own group rates. The costs that do not appear on the invoice are the two round trips a week a parent makes, and the loss of diagnosis: a group session cannot work on the specific criterion or command word your child is losing marks to. Group provision suits broad revision across a syllabus. It does not suit the tier-specific or technique-specific repair that most Year 11 students actually need, which is where one-to-one earns its premium.

faqs.question: Does the quoted IGCSE tuition rate include VAT in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask each provider directly and get the answer in writing, because quotes differ. This page does not state the tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, since that would require a citation from the Federal Tax Authority rather than an assumption, and getting it wrong in either direction misleads a parent. What a family can reasonably insist on is clarity: whether the figure quoted is the figure payable, and whether a tax registration number appears on the invoice if one is charged.

faqs.question: What should an Arabian Ranches 2 parent ask before paying for a block of lessons?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Which syllabus code and tier will you teach to? What will the first session diagnose and how will you report it? Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? Is the quoted figure inclusive of value added tax? What happens if we stop after one session? Do you hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit? The first is the one a weak provider cannot answer, and the last should be answered yes, with the note that the permit is free.

faqs.question: How does the cost of IGCSE tuition compare with Dubai private school fees?
faqs.answer: Tuition is smaller and more discretionary, and it is the line still moving. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package, so the school line is fixed for the year. A weekly session at the mid-market band, AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's estimates, is a material addition to a household budget but a fraction of a secondary school fee. The decision is about what the money is buying, not whether it is affordable.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Arabian Ranches 2 villa share one session?
faqs.answer: Only where they genuinely need the same thing, which is rarer than it sounds. A Year 9 and a Year 11 student, or an Extended and a Core candidate, are working on different material and sharing a session halves the value for both. Where two siblings are in the same year, on the same board and tier, with the same weakness, a shared session can work and costs less per child. Otherwise the better arrangement is separate sessions with the scheduling handled together so no evening carries two.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the first IGCSE tutor is not the right match?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson exists precisely so this is answered before any payment. It is one full session, run on a real problem, with no card details required. If the match is wrong you say so and we try a different tutor, and nothing is owed. After a block has started, the halfway review is the point at which a family can change tutor, change frequency or stop. Any provider who cannot explain what happens when a match fails is worth more questions before a deposit.

faqs.question: Is paying extra for an examiner-experienced IGCSE tutor worth it?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level, usually not. BartyED's examiner-led tier is published at AED 650 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the marks a Year 11 student is losing are generally command words, units, graph conventions and tier-appropriate content rather than anything requiring examiner insight. There is also a caution worth applying: examiner status should only be claimed where it can be evidenced, and it does not give anyone access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram quote in-home rates it does not offer?
faqs.answer: Because a page about what tuition costs in Arabian Ranches 2 would be dishonest without them. In-home visits are a large part of this market, they are published at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and comparing them is the clearest way to show what travel costs a family. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered live over video. Quoting the market and naming our own limit is better than quietly omitting either.

intro.heading: Why an IGCSE plan has to be built backwards
paragraphs: Almost every IGCSE tutoring request from Arabian Ranches 3 arrives at the wrong point in the year. The call comes after a mock result, which is roughly four months after the moment the result was decided and a few weeks before the window in which it can still be changed cheaply. The work is not harder in February than it was in October; there is simply less of the year left to spend, and some of the decisions that matter have already been submitted to a board by somebody else.

The sessions are public and almost nobody writes them down. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; UAE centres sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and again in November. In both cases the centre's final entries close months ahead of the first paper, which means the most consequential decision of the year, which tier your child sits, goes to a board long before anyone has seen a spring mock. Your school's exams officer holds that date for your series, and asking for it is one email.

Pearson runs on its own rhythm. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November each year; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including a provisional grid for the November series a year out, which is exactly why a page like this should point at the live official timetable rather than reprint a date that can be revised.

So the honest delivery note, early and plainly. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and does not send anyone to an address in Arabian Ranches 3; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the family keeps. On a calendar-driven subject that turns out to be an advantage rather than a concession: a session the week before a mock does not get cancelled because of traffic on the Dubailand roads, and a tutor can be matched to the exact specification your child sits instead of to whoever is free to drive.

What follows is the year counted backwards: the entry and results milestones with their sources, what the eight weeks before a series can realistically achieve, how Ramadan and study leave move the usable hours, where the Core and Extended decision sits and when it stops being reversible, and what a term of support costs in dirhams as a monthly figure rather than an hourly one. Every date is attributed to the board that published it, and where a date is not verifiable it is marked as such instead of being guessed at.
