dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: An IGCSE page needs to be precise about what your child is actually entered for, because the word IGCSE covers two boards, several tiering systems and at least three different mathematics routes. These are the four decisions that shape a Year 10 or Year 11 plan in a Dubai school, with what each one means for the calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the shared content of a Cambridge syllabus and caps the available grades at C. It suits a student who would be swamped by the Extended content and who needs a secure pass rather than a competitive one. The papers are shorter and the questions sit within a narrower range of demand. The decision is made by the school on the subject teacher's recommendation and is submitted with the centre's final entries.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Core and Extended decision often gets made quietly in Year 10 and surfaces for parents only when a report mentions a grade ceiling. For an Arabian Ranches 3 family that usually means a conversation with the school in the autumn term of Year 11, before the November entry deadline, rather than after a spring mock when the tier is already locked with the board.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: The Extended tier adds content on top of the core and opens the full A* to E range. It is the route almost every Dubai British-curriculum school uses as its default for students heading toward A Level or the IB Diploma, because a C ceiling closes post-16 doors. The extra content is the reason Extended students need topic-level support earlier: the additional material is taught later in the course and met first in a mock.
programmes.countryNote: Extended entries are the norm across the Dubailand British schools, which is why most tutoring requests from this community are about depth rather than rescue. The practical consequence is that a Year 11 here is usually working on the last third of the syllabus and paper technique at the same time, in an evening that also has to absorb the mandatory UAE subjects.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs Foundation and Higher tiers rather than Core and Extended, sits two written papers in mathematics rather than four, and has its own series pattern in May or June and November. The content overlaps heavily with Cambridge and the question style does not. A student who has revised from Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry has practised the wrong house style, which is a real and avoidable loss of marks.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools are split between the two boards, sometimes within one school across different subjects, so the first question any Dubailand tutoring conversation should answer is which code appears on the entry. Pearson publishes its timetables and provisional timetables openly, and those are the documents to check rather than a summary on a tutoring site.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide which post-16 route is available, and the two routes make different demands. A Level narrows to three or four subjects in depth; the IB Diploma keeps six with a core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Entry requirements are set by the school, and a grade that is comfortable for one route can be short for the other, particularly in mathematics and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Arabian Ranches 3 families face this choice with both routes available nearby but at different campuses, so the decision carries a commute as well as a curriculum. Schools in the inner Dubailand ring mostly run A Level after IGCSE, while the Diploma campuses sit further out toward Al Barsha South and The Sustainable City.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Arabian Ranches 3 families book most often, written with the syllabus code because the code is what decides the papers. Where Cambridge and Pearson both offer the subject, both are named: a tutor who has taught one and not the other will coach the wrong question style.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in Dubai and the one with the clearest calendar. Cambridge 0580 sits four papers across the tiers; Pearson 4MA1 sits two. Marks leave through unshown method, rounding at the wrong stage and multi-step questions abandoned halfway. All three are technique problems and all three move inside eight weeks.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580, not a variant of it, with a graphics-calculator component and an investigation-style demand. Students moved onto it mid-course often arrive without calculator fluency, which costs marks that have nothing to do with the mathematics. Preparation has to include the device, not just the content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical paper account for most of the losses. Cambridge separates the alternative-to-practical and practical routes, which changes what a Year 11 should be practising in the final weeks. Pearson 4PH1 assesses practical skills within the written papers, so the revision looks different for the same content.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Moles and organic chemistry are where the grade is decided, and both are taught late. A student who meets them first in a February mock is behind by design rather than by fault. Qualitative analysis questions reward memorised observations, which is the cheapest revision on the syllabus and the most often skipped.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, which makes it a scheduling problem as much as a teaching one. Marks leave on imprecise terminology and on data questions answered by describing the graph. Short frequent sessions beat long ones here, particularly in the weeks when three subjects are revising at once.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Two award routes that cover all three sciences in less time than three separate entries. The syllabus is narrower, not easier, and the papers sample across all three disciplines in a single sitting. A student here needs breadth-first revision, which is a different plan from the depth-first approach three separate sciences require.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response, assessed on technique that transfers between texts. This is the subject where eight weeks of focused work moves the most, because nothing has to be memorised. The commonest loss is writing a good answer to a slightly different question from the one set.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: A separate qualification from English Language, with its own papers and its own grade meaning for post-16 entry. Families sometimes discover late that the two are not interchangeable for a sixth-form offer. Worth checking against the school's own entry requirements before the final entries go in.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Both reward application to the named case rather than textbook recall, and both have command terms that set the depth of the answer. Analyse and evaluate carry more marks than explain and are answered at the same depth by most students, which is a correctable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the mandatory Arabic provision every Dubai private school must run, and often in a different stream from it. The exam skills are specific and the marks are concentrated in writing. Support here means practice inside the school's own scheme of work, because the mandatory-subject content cannot be substituted.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.regionsTitle: Arabian Ranches 3 phases and the hour the calendar leaves free
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.regionsIntro: In exam term the question is not where a family lives but which hour survives the school run, the mandatory subjects and whatever the school set that day. These are the phases we schedule from, with the slot that holds up through a mock window rather than a description of the streets.

regions.name: Sun
regions.note: Settled routines in the earlier handover phases, which makes a standing slot easy to protect through mocks. Families here tend to book the autumn diagnostic and keep the same hour through to study leave rather than restarting in February.

regions.name: Joy
regions.note: Townhouse layouts where two children often revise in the same space. Staggering sessions on consecutive hours works better than parallel ones, and it keeps the quiet room occupied once rather than twice in an evening.

regions.name: Ruba
regions.note: A ground-floor study in most layouts, so a 16:30 slot is workable when the bus runs on time. In exam term the more useful request from here is a second weekend session rather than a longer weekday one.

regions.name: Spring
regions.note: Later handovers, and a number of households still finalising a campus. Short bookings built around a single mock series are common, with the plan rewritten once the school and the board are both confirmed.

regions.name: Bliss
regions.note: Households split between the inner Dubailand British schools and the Al Barsha South campuses, which produces two pick-up times. In the eight weeks before a series the later 18:00 slot is the one that survives.

regions.name: Caya
regions.note: Journeys run toward Dubai Hills and Al Barsha rather than Motor City, so afternoon traffic peaks differently. During Ramadan the post-Iftar slot is requested more from this side of the community than from any other.

regions.name: June
regions.note: Newer handovers where the study is often still being furnished. A laptop, a headset and a closing door is the entire requirement, and the shared whiteboard replaces the paper a desk would otherwise need.

regions.name: Anya and Raya
regions.note: The outer phases, where every car journey costs extra minutes. Weekend morning sessions are booked more often here, which in exam term is useful: a Saturday timed paper is easier to run than a Tuesday one.

regions.name: Mudon and Town Square
regions.note: Neighbouring communities on the same school runs, often entered for the same boards at the same campuses. Families here ask the same calendar questions and frequently share a tutor across consecutive slots.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Closer to GEMS Metropole and Victory Heights, so the school day finishes earlier for some students and the 16:30 slot is more often viable. The mock calendar, though, is the campus's rather than the community's.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.modesIntro: IGCSE support divides naturally by where you are in the year rather than by budget. These three arrangements are what Arabian Ranches 3 families actually book, and each has a point in the calendar at which it stops being the right purchase.

modes.title: The autumn diagnostic and a standing slot
modes.description: Booked in September or October, before the first mock and before the entry deadline. One marked paper establishes where the marks are going, then a fixed weekly hour works through the named topics. This is the cheapest version of IGCSE tutoring because it has the whole year to spend and the tier decision is still open.

modes.title: The eight-week block before a series
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week across the final eight weeks, built on timed papers and the two or three topics the data says cost most. It has an end date written into it. Eight weeks changes timing, command-term depth and two topics; it does not reteach a two-year syllabus, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hours rather than outcomes.

Pearson runs a November window and Cambridge runs June and November, so a retake decision has a real deadline attached.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Arabian Ranches 3 is actually being hired for
paragraphs: The phrase gets typed in two different moods. In September it means somebody who will keep a Year 10 honest about homework. In February it means somebody who can rescue three subjects in six weeks. Those are not the same purchase, and treating them as the same is why a lot of tutoring money in Dubai produces no visible change: the February version is bought at the price of the September version and expected to do four times the work.

The literal part of the request deserves a straight answer too. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches 3 and does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; that service exists only in India. The market does offer it, at AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the provider, and a family who specifically wants somebody in the room should hire locally and ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. What we provide is one-to-one teaching over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the exact specification code the child is entered for.

That permit question is worth asking whichever route you take. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page for it, Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any figure you see quoted is somebody's guess.

The rest of this page assumes the September version of the question and then shows what each later starting point can still achieve, because most families arrive later than they meant to and deserve a straight answer about what that costs rather than reassurance.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar. The word November returned no hits across every fetchable competitor page in the research for this project, which is remarkable for a qualification that runs a November series. So here is the year counted backwards, using Pearson's own published dates as the worked example because Pearson states them openly, and describing the Cambridge deadlines structurally because they are held by the centre rather than printed on a marketing page.

The headline is the gap between the entry deadline and the first paper. Entries are submitted by the centre months ahead of the exam window in both boards' June and November series, and everything that depends on the entry, above all the tier, is settled at that point rather than afterwards. A family having the Core-or-Extended conversation in the spring term of a June series is having it after the board has already been told the answer. The exams officer can give you the date in a sentence, and that date is the one a tutoring plan should be anchored to.

There is a second trap specific to international centres. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A revision plan built from a timetable downloaded from the internet rather than from the school is a plan built on somebody else's zone. The school's exams officer knows the zone; it takes one email to confirm.

The IB's dates are a different matter and this page will not pretend otherwise. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and none is published here. For IGCSE, Cambridge and Pearson both publish openly, which is why their dates appear above with the document they came from.

sections.heading: Pearson's series, and why the results date matters more than the exam date
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and again in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. That second window is the one Dubai families underuse: it allows a single-subject retake or an early entry without waiting a full year, and it turns a disappointing August result into a January one rather than a next-summer one.

The results dates are what make that planning possible. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read those two facts together and the retake calendar becomes concrete: a June result arrives in late August, a November entry closes in the autumn, and the replacement grade is in hand by late January, in time for most post-16 and university conversations rather than after them.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the November sitting that is still a year away. Provisional means revisable, which is the reason this page links the board's live timetable rather than restating a date that may move. A tutoring site that prints a provisional date as fact and never updates it is the commonest small error in this market, and it is the kind that costs a family a sitting.

For an Arabian Ranches 3 household the practical use of all this is simple. If the result you need is for a sixth-form or university offer with a deadline, work from the results date backwards, not from the exam date. The exam date tells you when the revision has to be finished. The results date tells you whether the plan is any use to you at all.

sections.heading: The eight weeks before a series, and what tells you it is working
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the commonest booking length and the one most often oversold. What it can do is specific: it can change how a student uses the time in the exam, it can lift answers to the depth the command term asks for, it can clean up the mechanical losses, and it can properly teach two or three topics. What it cannot do is cover a two-year syllabus that was never learned the first time. A tutor who tells you that at the first lesson is giving you information; one who agrees to everything is selling hours.

The structure that works runs diagnosis, depth, then timing. The first session is a full past paper, worked rather than revised, with the errors sorted afterwards into three piles: content the student does not know, method they know but cannot execute, and marks lost purely to the clock. Those three piles have different remedies and mixing them is why generic revision feels busy and changes nothing. Three named topics come out of that paper, and nothing outside those three gets taught.

The middle weeks are the only ones where new learning happens. A topic is taught from the beginning, not revised from notes, and the test of it is whether the student can answer a past-paper question on that topic unaided a week later. The final fortnight is deliberately dull: timed sections, paper-order strategy, and a one-page checklist in the student's own handwriting for the mechanical marks. No new content after that point, because anything learned in the last ten days displaces something already secure.

The checks in the table below matter more than the plan. A plan that has never been tested against a marked paper is a hope. Any arrangement that cannot show you a rising mark on a mixed paper, rather than on a topic paper the student has already practised, has not yet proved anything.

sections.heading: Term dates, Ramadan and the hours the UAE year actually leaves
paragraphs: A revision plan drawn up in a UK textbook assumes a year that does not exist here. The UAE academic year has its own shape, and two features of it reliably break imported plans: the autumn term carries most of the coursework and the first mock, and Ramadan moves the usable study hours into the evening at a point in the spring that varies year to year. Neither is a problem if the plan was built around them. Both are a problem if the plan arrived from somewhere else.

Ramadan is the one families ask about most. School hours shorten, the household rhythm moves after Iftar, and a 16:30 session that worked all autumn stops working. The practical answer is shorter and more frequent rather than longer and heavier: three forty-minute sessions do more in that month than two ninety-minute ones, and a post-Iftar slot is easier to protect than an afternoon one. Because the lesson is online there is no journey to negotiate around the timing, which is the single clearest operational advantage of the format during that month.

Study leave is the other inflection point and the one most underestimated. The school stops setting work, the timetable disappears, and a student who has been carried by structure for five years suddenly has none. The right move is to keep the tutoring slot at exactly the same hour and day it has always been, because at that point the structure is most of the value. Families who pause tutoring during study leave to save money frequently lose more in drift than they save in fees.

The mandatory UAE subjects sit across all of this. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA requires its current arrangements to have been in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those are real timetable minutes that are not available for IGCSE content, which is why the evening hour carries more weight in a Dubai school year than it would elsewhere.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the tier decision that has a deadline
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-stakes thing in an IGCSE year and the one parents are least often consulted on. Cambridge Core caps the grade at C; Cambridge Extended opens A* to E. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers for the same purpose. A C ceiling is sufficient for some post-16 routes and closes others, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and the student usually finds this out from a sixth-form entry requirement rather than from a report.

The decision belongs to the school, on the subject teacher's recommendation, and it is submitted with the centre's final entries. That submission is the deadline that matters, and it falls months ahead of the first paper in both boards' June and November series. Before that date a conversation with the subject teacher, supported by a marked paper showing what the student can actually do at Extended demand, is a conversation that can change something. After it, the tier is what the board has been told, and the work shifts to getting the best available grade at the tier entered.

There is a quieter version of the same trap in mathematics. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a separate syllabus from 0580, with its own tiering and a graphics-calculator component. A student moved between them mid-course can be strong on content and weak on the device, which costs marks that look like mathematical errors and are not. If the entry says 0607, the calculator is part of the preparation and not an afterthought.

The honest framing for a parent is this: before the entry deadline, ask whether the tier matches where the student is heading. After it, stop asking and spend the hour on marks instead. Both are reasonable positions; mixing them up wastes a term.

sections.heading: What a term of IGCSE support costs in Dubai, as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring look cheap and monthly figures make it look real, so this section uses the monthly ones. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged pricing in the market shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A term is roughly three of those months, which is the number worth having in mind before the first call rather than after the third invoice.

Translating back to hours, the market bands are published as follows. Budget online tuition, often delivered by a university student, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Online work with a qualified subject tutor is published between AED 150 and AED 300, and Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel included is quoted at AED 180 to 500, Bestimate putting it at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Specialists in IB, IGCSE or A Level are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270, and a premium tier exists above that, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Read against school fees those numbers land differently. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A fee freeze does not make tutoring cheaper, but it does mean the tutoring line in a family budget is the one that moved this year, which is a reason to buy it with a plan and an end date rather than as a standing arrangement.

None of the figures above is an IB Gram price. They are other providers' published rates and a published rate survey, cited so you can check them. Our own number depends on the subject, the tier and how many weeks are left; the free first lesson exists so it arrives attached to a named tutor rather than as a band in a table.

sections.heading: Coursework and the honesty line when a deadline is close
paragraphs: Pressure is where academic honesty actually gets tested. A coursework deadline a week away, a student who has not started, and a tutor who is being paid by the hour is the exact situation in which a line gets crossed quietly. So the line is written here rather than implied. No tutor may write, redraft to completion or supply any part of an assessed piece. A tutor may teach the skills it requires, explain the criteria, read what the student has written and say where it falls short of them, and help plan the time that remains.

This is not a theoretical concern in this market. One operator found during the research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright. For the student, submitted work that is not their own is a malpractice finding, and a malpractice finding costs considerably more than a poor grade. For a family paying for help, the useful question to ask a prospective tutor is simple: what exactly will you do with my child's draft? An answer that includes the word rewrite is the wrong answer.

Board materials fall under the same discipline. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright, and IB Gram does not host, email or hand them over. They should come from the school's own subscription or the board's official channels. A provider offering a drive full of papers is offering you a copyright problem, and where any material is unreleased it becomes a malpractice exposure for the student as well.

The constructive version of all this is that a student who has done the work themselves can defend it, and defending it is part of several assessments. A draft improved through feedback reads as the student's own voice sharpened. A draft written by somebody else reads as what it is, to the teacher who has marked that student all year.

sections.heading: Starting mid-term from Arabian Ranches 3, and what each start date can still achieve
paragraphs: Most families reading this are not at the start of the year, so the useful thing is an honest map of what remains possible from where they are. The map is below and it gets narrower as it goes down. That narrowing is not a sales device; it is the structure of a qualification whose entries close in November and whose papers are sat in a fixed window.

Booking itself is short. You tell us the subject, the syllabus code if you have it, and the hour the bus gets back to your phase; we propose one tutor with their specification and level stated; the first lesson runs free with no card details taken, and you decide afterwards. If the subject is one where UAE-hours coverage is thin, you are told at the match stage rather than after a fortnight of silence. A tutor based in India rather than the UAE is disclosed as such before anything is paid, and the hour does not move off Gulf Standard Time.

The disclosure is deliberate. No competitor page in the research for this project publishes a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE numbers without mentioning where the teaching happens. Knowing in advance which requests are hard to fill is worth more to a family than a promise that everything is available, followed by two weeks of silence. If nobody suitable is free, the answer is no with a reason attached.

On data, briefly. A tutoring enquiry collects a child's name, school, year group, subjects and tier, because the matching does not work without them. We use it to propose a tutor and run the lessons; we do not need a photograph or a report card for that, and a deletion request is honoured. What is held, why, and how to have it removed is set out in the privacy policy linked from this page, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

process.title: Name the series, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us which series your child is entered for and which board, because a June Cambridge entry and a November Pearson entry are different plans with different deadlines. If you do not know, the school's exams officer does, along with the administrative zone that decides which timetable version applies.

process.title: One marked paper before any plan
process.description: The first session is a full past paper, worked with the tutor rather than revised beforehand, then marked against the published scheme. The output is not a score. It is the errors sorted into content, method and timing, which is what decides whether the next eight weeks are teaching or technique.

process.title: A free first lesson, with the conditions stated
process.description: One lesson, one proposed tutor, at the slot you asked for, with no card details taken before it runs. That is the whole condition. You receive the written notes afterwards whether you continue or not, and if the match is wrong, saying so is the expected outcome rather than an awkward one.

process.title: Three named topics and a dated finish
process.description: The plan names the topics it will cover and the date it ends, usually the first paper of the series. A plan without an end date drifts into a subscription. The topics come from the marked paper, not from a syllabus checklist, and anything outside them is explicitly not being taught.

process.title: A halfway check against evidence, not feeling
process.description: Midway through, the arrangement is checked against a mixed paper rather than a topic paper, because improvement on something already practised proves nothing. If the marks have not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does. If the work is finished, we say so and the booking ends.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from the board's own calendar
whyPoints.description: Cambridge publishes its key dates and administrative zones; Pearson publishes its timetables, provisional timetables and results dates. Both are linked rather than summarised here, because a provisional date can be revised and a stale date on a tutoring page can cost a family a sitting.

whyPoints.title: The specification code drives the match
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different mathematics qualifications with different papers and different calculator demands. A tutor matched on the word maths is a coin toss. A tutor matched on the code has taught the papers your child will sit.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is somebody's published number
whyPoints.description: The monthly and hourly bands on this page are attributed to the provider or the rate survey that published them, so you can check them yourself. Three of the six main competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in.

whyPoints.title: The end date is part of the offer
whyPoints.description: An exam-year block is supposed to finish when the series does. We write the finish date into the plan and review at the halfway point against a mixed paper. A provider that never finds a reason to stop is selling a standing order rather than a result.

whyPoints.title: Nothing is claimed about regulators or boards
whyPoints.description: KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai, MoHRE issues the private tuition work permit, and Cambridge and Pearson set the qualifications. None of them endorses IB Gram, and this page does not suggest otherwise. Any provider advertising board-approved tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should IGCSE support start for a Year 11 here?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the mock results, which is when most Arabian Ranches 3 families call. The useful marker is the entry deadline rather than the exam window. Both Cambridge and Pearson take the centre's final entries months ahead of the first paper, so the autumn is the last point at which the tier is still a conversation rather than a decision already submitted. After the entry closes, eight weeks of technique work is a genuine purchase and reteaching a year is not. Your exams officer can give you the exact entry date for the series your child is sitting.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge want the entry months before the exam?
faqs.answer: Because an entry is an administrative commitment, not a booking. The centre declares the subject, the syllabus and the tier, and the board then builds timetables, scripts and zone allocations around those declarations before shipping papers to every centre in the world. That is why final entries close months ahead of the first paper in both the June and the November series. The practical effect for a family is that the single highest-stakes decision of the year, which tier your child sits, is taken well before anyone has seen a spring mock, and it is taken by the school rather than by the parent.

faqs.question: What are Cambridge's administrative zones and does our school's zone matter?
faqs.answer: It matters enough that Cambridge says so in its own guidance. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A revision plan built from a timetable found online is built on somebody else's zone. The school's exams officer knows which zone the centre sits in, and confirming it takes a single email.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results actually reach students?
faqs.answer: Pearson publishes this clearly. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those two dates are what make retake planning concrete: a summer result arrives in late August, a November entry closes in the autumn, and a replacement grade is in hand by late January. If the grade is needed for an offer with a deadline, work backwards from the results date rather than from the exam date.

faqs.question: Can my daughter sit her IGCSE in November instead of waiting for June?
faqs.answer: Yes, both boards run a second window. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The entry goes through the school as the centre, so the first conversation is with the exams officer rather than with a tutor. Pearson's provisional timetables are published in advance for planning.

faqs.question: Is it too late to move from Core to Extended in the spring term?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the tier goes to the board with the centre's final entries, and those close months ahead of the first paper. Before the deadline, a marked paper showing what your child can do at Extended demand is the thing that makes the conversation with the subject teacher productive rather than awkward. After it, the tier is settled and the hour is better spent on marks at the tier entered. The decision itself belongs to the school on the subject teacher's recommendation, and the exams officer holds the date it was submitted.

faqs.question: What does a realistic eight-week IGCSE plan actually contain?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, depth, then timing. Weeks eight and seven are one full past paper per subject, worked rather than revised, with the errors sorted into content, method and clock. Weeks six to three teach two or three named topics from the beginning and work command-term depth. Week two is timed sections with the clock visible. The final week is paper strategy and the mechanical marks, with no new content, because anything learned in the last ten days displaces something already secure. The test throughout is a rising mark on a mixed paper, not a practised one.

faqs.question: How should Ramadan change when IGCSE revision happens in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Shorter and more frequent, and later in the day. School hours shorten, the household rhythm moves after Iftar, and an afternoon slot that worked all autumn stops working. Three forty-minute sessions in that month generally achieve more than two ninety-minute ones, and a post-Iftar slot is easier to protect than a 16:30 one. Because the lesson runs over live video there is no journey to schedule around, which is the clearest operational advantage of the format during that month. Plan the month before it starts rather than improvising through it.

faqs.question: What does a full term of weekly IGCSE tutoring cost in dirhams?
faqs.answer: As monthly figures: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged pricing in the market shows about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A term is roughly three of those months. Those are other providers' published figures, cited so you can check them, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Does an in-home IGCSE tutor visit villas in this part of Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Local providers offer it; IB Gram does not. We do not send anyone to a UAE address, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The published market rate for an in-home visit including travel is AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. A family set on somebody in the room should hire locally and ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Our lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: My son has mocks in three weeks. What can genuinely change in that time?
faqs.answer: Paper strategy and the mechanical marks, and that is roughly it. Three weeks is enough to teach a student to answer the verb in the question rather than the topic, to finish a paper inside the time allowed, and to stop losing marks on units, rounding, unshown method and unlabelled axes. It is not enough to teach a topic that was never learned. The honest version of a three-week booking names those limits at the first lesson, and a provider that promises more in that window is describing something that does not happen.

faqs.question: Who decides which exam board my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The school, as the examination centre. Dubai schools are split between Cambridge and Pearson, sometimes within one school across different subjects, and the entry is submitted by the centre rather than chosen by the family. It matters for tutoring because the question styles differ even where the content overlaps: a student revising from Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry has practised the wrong house style. The syllabus code on the entry, 0580 or 4MA1 or 0607, is the thing to ask the exams officer for before any plan is written.

faqs.question: What should be finished before the winter break in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Three things. All coursework and controlled assessment drafts should be complete, because an internal deadline in January leaves no room if a draft turns out to need rebuilding. The entry should be settled, because for a June series the centre's final entries close well before the spring term begins. And at least one full past paper per subject should have been run against the clock and marked, so the spring plan starts from evidence rather than from impressions. A break spent on none of those is a break; a break spent on all three is a month of the spring term recovered.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover three IGCSE subjects in the run-up to a series?
faqs.answer: Sometimes for two, rarely well for three. The three sciences can work with one tutor when they are being sat as a Co-ordinated or Combined award, because the demand is breadth rather than depth. Mathematics plus a science is a common and workable pair. Three separate sciences at Extended, each with its own papers and practical component, is three jobs, and a tutor who agrees to all of them in the final eight weeks is agreeing to spread an hour too thin. The honest answer is usually two tutors or two subjects.

faqs.question: What happens to the tutoring schedule once study leave starts?
faqs.answer: It should stay exactly where it is, same hour and same day. Study leave removes the school timetable, which for most students removes the only structure they have ever worked inside, and that is the point at which a fixed external slot earns the most. The content of the session changes rather than the slot: timed papers, paper-order strategy and the mechanical checklist rather than new teaching. Families who pause during study leave to save fees generally lose more to drift in those weeks than the fees would have cost.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.closingHeading: Tell us the series and we will work backwards from it
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.closingBody: An IGCSE plan is only as good as the date it is pointed at. Tell us the board, the syllabus code and the series your child is entered for, plus the hour the bus gets back to your phase of Arabian Ranches 3, and we will propose one tutor who has taught those papers. The first lesson is free, with no card details taken, and it is spent on a real past paper rather than on an introduction. You get the marked script and the written notes afterwards whether you continue or not, along with a plan that names three topics and the date it finishes.

intro.heading: Nothing about tutoring here works until the slot works
paragraphs: Bluewaters Island is a small, dense residential community built on reclaimed land off JBR, joined to the mainland by one road bridge and a pedestrian link across to The Walk. It has retail, a hotel and a famous wheel. It has no school. Every child living here commutes, most of them inland to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim, The Greens, Jumeirah Park or Emirates Hills, and the journey is short in distance and unpredictable in time.

That single fact shapes every tutoring arrangement on the island, and it is the reason most of them fail. A family books a Tuesday at five, discovers the bus does not reach the bridge until twenty past four on a bad day, adds the walk from the drop-off and a meal, and finds the session has become a negotiation. After three weeks of starting late and twice rescheduling, the arrangement quietly stops. The teaching was never the problem.

So this page is written from the school run. Where Bluewaters children actually go, roughly when the day ends at each ring of campuses, what the bridge does to the five-to-seven window, how households with two children on different timetables manage, and what Ramadan does to all of it. Then the slot that follows from those facts, which for most secondary students here is half past five or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings available for anything demanding.

The IGCSE content matters too and it is on this page: boards, tiers, syllabus codes, the series available to a UAE candidate and what to ask the exams officer. But a family that gets the timetable right and the board slightly wrong will do better than one that gets the board right and never holds a consistent session, which is why the order here is deliberate.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. On a school-run page that is the operative advantage: the session begins at the booked minute because nobody has to cross the bridge to reach it, and a late bus moves the start by five minutes rather than cancelling the hour.

Everything here was reviewed in October 2026. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. Where a timetable is involved, read the board's own live PDF rather than any restatement, including this one.

One more thing worth settling early, because it interacts with the timetable. Mock season lengthens the school day with revision sessions, which pushes arrival later in precisely the term a family most wants to add hours. The right response is to protect the slot that already works and narrow what it contains, rather than stacking more sessions onto a week that has just lost thirty minutes at the front of every evening. We plan for that shift when the schedule is first set.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-isl.programmesIntro: Three routes appear in Bluewaters households, and which one applies changes both the revision material and what grade is reachable. Get the answer from the exams officer in writing before any plan is built.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Mostly tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Syllabus codes identify the course precisely: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Assessment is linear at the end of the course, with practical or alternative-to-practical routes in the sciences chosen by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your school which zone it sits in, because that determines which timetable governs your child's study leave.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Uses 4-prefix codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4EA1 English Language, graded 9-1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the International GCSE sciences are untiered. Practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and revises them, so plan study leave against the live official PDF. The results calendar drives the local resit conversation twice a year: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools near Bluewaters move students into AS and A Level at sixteen, with subject-specific IGCSE grade requirements for entry. Mathematics and the sciences typically need a grade 6 or B, and the step in abstraction from Extended to AS is steeper than anything a student has met previously.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-isl.subjectsIntro: Eight subjects, with a note on how much session time each realistically needs and whether it tolerates a tired evening slot. That second column is the one nobody publishes and the one that decides whether a plan survives.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1. Tolerates a tired slot better than most subjects because the work can be broken into short problems. Method marks for visible working are the largest avoidable loss, and that is a habit rather than a concept.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 or 0510, or Pearson 4EA1. Directed writing and the summary task are governed by a learnable structure, which makes this the fastest-moving subject late in the year. Needs alertness, so better earlier in the evening or at weekends.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Electricity and moments carry the paper. Explanation structure is the main loss: naming the quantity that changed rather than describing the outcome. Breaks into short questions well, so it survives a 6pm start.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. Moles and electrolysis are the gates. Mole drill is ideal for a short tired slot because it is repetitive by design, and making it automatic pays across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1. The highest content volume of the three sciences and the least tolerant of a late slot, because the work is memory-intensive. Weekend mornings suit this subject better than weekday evenings.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0455 or Pearson 4EC1. Diagram accuracy decides the grade and diagrams can be drilled in short bursts. Data response needs figures quoted from the extract rather than paraphrased, which is a precision habit.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Cambridge 0450 or Pearson 4BS1. Students reach the analysis band and stop short of evaluation, where the top marks sit. Teaching a justified judgement takes a handful of sessions and transfers to every extended answer in the subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 or Pearson 4CP0. Theory covers data representation, hardware, networks and security; the programming component rewards pseudocode discipline. Trace tables and binary conversion are high-frequency and suit short sessions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0606. A separate qualification taken by a small strong cohort as a bridge to AS, covering early calculus, identities and series. Demands a fresh slot rather than a late one, and local specialist supply is genuinely thin.

regions.note: One road bridge, one pedestrian link to JBR, no school. Everything about session timing follows from the drop-off time at the island end, which is later than the mainland journey time suggests.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A dense campus ring including Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Raffles World Academy. Twenty to thirty-five minutes, and the bus routes serving the island add stops at both ends.

regions.note: Regent International School sits in The Greens. A shorter run than the Al Barsha ring, so students from Bluewaters attending here are often home by four, which opens an earlier slot.

regions.note: Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. Twenty-five to forty minutes, the longest commute most island families run.

regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, well served by metro and tram, and where a larger share of tutors actually live. Relevant to in-home arrangements and irrelevant to online ones, which is the point.

schoolClusters.note: The nearest ring of campuses and where most Bluewaters secondary students study. Predominantly British curriculum with sixth-form routes, which is why both Cambridge and Pearson appear and why we ask for the syllabus code before planning anything.

schoolClusters.note: The inland ring, twenty to forty minutes from the island depending on the hour. Students attending here have the longest bus day of any Bluewaters family and the latest realistic weekday session slot.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-isl.modesIntro: Three ways to fit IGCSE support around a Bluewaters week. Which one works depends less on the subject than on what time the student is genuinely usable.

modes.title: Fixed weekday evening slot
modes.description: One or two sessions a week at the same time, set after the student's actual arrival and meal rather than at a round hour that sounds convenient. For most island secondary students that is half past five or six. The fixed slot is what makes the arrangement last, because a session with a standing time survives a bad week while an ad hoc one does not.
bullets: Start time set from the real arrival time, not a nominal one
Session begins at the booked minute because nobody is travelling to it
Short written note after each session on what was covered and set
Slot held through half-terms, exam leave and travel weeks

modes.title: Weekend morning block
modes.description: A longer session on a weekend morning for the work that cannot be done tired: full timed papers, biology content, Additional Mathematics, anything needing sustained concentration. Many Bluewaters families run one weekday slot for maintenance and one weekend morning for the demanding work, which is a better split than two tired evenings.
bullets: Full timed papers sat properly, then marked in the same session
Memory-heavy subjects scheduled when the student is fresh
Longer format suits Additional Mathematics and extended answers
Keeps the weekday slot short enough to be sustainable

modes.title: Split-sibling scheduling
modes.description: For households with children on different campuses and different arrival times, which is common on the island. Back-to-back slots are set so one child works while the other eats, and both tutors use the same fixed times each week. It sounds administrative and it is the difference between two arrangements lasting and both lapsing by October.

Same times every week so the household routine is predictable

sections.heading: Where Bluewaters children actually go to school
paragraphs: There is no school on Bluewaters Island, so the first question in any tutoring conversation here is which campus and how. The answer falls into three rings, and each ring produces a different arrival time and therefore a different workable slot.

The nearest ring is Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, holding campuses including Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Raffles World Academy. Private car at ten in the morning is fifteen minutes; at the end of the school day it is twenty-five or more, and a bus with stops is longer again.

The second ring is The Greens and The Views, where Regent International School sits. This is the shortest run available to an island family, and students attending here are frequently home by four, which makes a five o'clock session genuinely possible rather than theoretically possible.

The third ring is inland: Jumeirah Park, The Meadows and Emirates Hills, holding Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. Twenty-five to forty minutes each way depending on the hour, which is the longest commute most Bluewaters households run and the one that pushes a weekday slot to six o'clock. Figures below are indicative rather than guaranteed, and they move with roadworks on the Marina approach. A school bus adds stops at both ends of the journey, which in practice means fifteen to thirty minutes on top of the private-car figure, and that is the number a family should plan the slot from rather than the drive time they remember from a weekend.

sections.heading: The bridge, and the two hours that decide everything
paragraphs: Bluewaters is reached by one road bridge from the Marina side. For a resident that is unremarkable for most of the day. Between roughly five and seven in the evening it becomes the single most relevant fact about tutoring logistics on the island, because that window contains the end of the working day, the Marina exit, The Walk traffic at JBR and the bridge itself.

For an in-home tutor the consequence is arithmetic. A tutor leaving a campus in Al Barsha at four has a journey that is twenty minutes at noon and thirty-five to forty-five in that window, then needs visitor parking in a residential tower, then needs to reach a specific apartment. The last kilometre is often the slowest part, and none of it is teaching time. The published Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour, visible in the gap between online and in-home bands, is that journey expressed as money.

For an online session the bridge is irrelevant to the tutor and relevant only to the student, which halves the problem. The student still has to get home, but once they are home the session starts at the booked minute. A bus running twenty minutes late moves the start by twenty minutes rather than cancelling an hour that somebody has already travelled for.

This is why we do not offer UAE home visits, and it is not a hedge. Across a twelve-week term, the number of sessions that actually happen is the variable that determines whether tutoring works, and on an island with one access route in the evening, an arrangement requiring somebody to arrive is an arrangement with a cancellation built into every bad traffic day.

sections.heading: When a session realistically fits, by age and by subject
paragraphs: The slot that works is not the slot that sounds convenient. Three things set it: the arrival time, whether the student has eaten, and whether the subject tolerates a tired brain. Families routinely get the first two right and ignore the third, then conclude the tutoring is not working.

For a Year 10 or Year 11 student from the Al Barsha ring, arrival is around half past four after a bus with stops, and a usable start is half past five. From the Emirates Hills ring it is closer to six. For a primary-age child, arrival is earlier but attention fades faster, and two thirty-minute sessions a week work better than one hour.

Subject tolerance is the part worth planning deliberately. Mathematics breaks into short problems and survives a tired slot reasonably well. Chemistry mole drill is repetitive by design and is arguably better late than early, because it needs persistence rather than insight. Biology, with its content volume, is the least tolerant, and English Language analysis needs alertness. Additional Mathematics needs a fresh student, full stop.

The practical pattern most Bluewaters families settle on is one weekday evening slot for maintenance work and one weekend morning for the demanding material. That is a better split than two weekday evenings, and it means the timed papers actually get sat properly rather than abandoned halfway through at seven o'clock on a Wednesday.

Session length matters alongside timing. Forty minutes of genuine attention beats a nominal hour in which the last twenty minutes are spent watching a tired student reread a question, and for a younger child two short sessions a week are consistently better than one long one. We would rather shorten a session and keep it than hold the hour and lose the arrangement.

sections.heading: Two children, two campuses, one evening
paragraphs: A large share of Bluewaters households have children at two different schools, because provision for different ages and curricula sits in different places and nothing is walkable. That produces two arrival times, two homework loads and one kitchen, and it is the most common reason a tutoring arrangement that suited one child becomes impossible once the second starts.

The workable approach is consecutive slots rather than parallel ones. One child works while the other eats, then they swap. It requires both slots to be at the same times every week, with different subject specialists working to a shared written schedule, and it is more administrative than anybody wants. It is also the difference between two arrangements lasting a year and both lapsing by October.

Where the children are on different systems, which happens often here with one on IGCSE and one on the MYP or an American curriculum, the schedules also need to respect two different reporting calendars and two different holiday patterns. Those do not always align even between schools in the same emirate, and a plan written against one child's term dates will collide with the other's.

The practical request to make of any provider is simple: fixed times, named tutors, one shared written schedule, and both slots moved together when travel or Ramadan requires it. If a provider cannot do that, the arrangement will survive the easy weeks and fail in the busy ones, which are the weeks it was bought for.
bullets: Consecutive slots rather than parallel ones, so one child eats while the other works
Same times every week, so the household routine is predictable

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened day and the slot that moves
paragraphs: During Ramadan, school hours in Dubai are shortened and household routines move substantially later. For a Bluewaters family that changes the tutoring slot rather than ending it: study happens after Iftar for many households, and a session at nine in the evening with the family awake is often more productive than one at five while fasting.

The planning complication is that Ramadan moves. It shifts earlier by roughly eleven days each Gregorian year, which means the school weeks it overlaps with change annually. A schedule copied from a previous year will be wrong about which term is affected, and that matters when it lands on a mock window or on study leave.

The other predictable disruptions are easier and still frequently mishandled. The long winter break tempts families into booking an intensive, which usually produces a tired January in a term where mocks are often close. The spring break often sits near the series, and the right use of it is timed paper work rather than new content. Both decisions are better made in advance than in the week itself.

The practical step is to put the dates on the table at the first conversation: school term dates, travel plans, and the Ramadan window for the year ahead. A plan built around those is a plan that still exists in week nine. Because the sessions are online they also follow the laptop, so a fortnight in another time zone becomes a different clock time rather than a gap.
bullets: Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, changing which weeks it affects
Post-Iftar sessions are a normal request and the slot is held rather than dropped

sections.heading: Board, tier and the email that should precede any plan
paragraphs: Once the slot works, the content question matters a great deal, and it starts with one email. Ask the exams officer for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series for each subject, in writing. In a school entering candidates with both boards, the answer genuinely differs by subject, which is why a report card can carry 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades with nothing wrong.

The differences are substantive. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is tiered Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C; Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher on a 9-1 scale. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical route and the school chooses; Pearson International GCSE sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers. Some Pearson subjects are modular, which changes the shape of a revision term.

The tier question deserves its own attention because of the ceiling. A Cambridge 0580 Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform, and if a sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has already settled the outcome. That decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11.

Ask also which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, which makes it a question with a real consequence rather than an administrative curiosity.
bullets: Ask for board, syllabus code, tier and series per subject, in writing

sections.heading: The mock term, when the slot is hardest to hold
paragraphs: Mock season is when the timetable argument stops being theoretical. School days get longer with revision sessions, early evening tutoring slots across the city fill up, and a student who was managing a Tuesday at half past five is suddenly arriving at half past five. This is also the point at which families most want to add hours, which is exactly the wrong move if the existing slot is already failing.

The better response is to protect what works and change what it contains. Keep the fixed slot, shorten it if necessary, and narrow the content to whatever the mock script shows. Ask the school for component marks rather than the grade: blank questions mean content gaps, attempted questions marked low mean command-term misreads, and a script that thins towards the end means pacing. Those three need different work and different amounts of it.

If hours genuinely need adding, add them at the weekend rather than in the evening. A full timed paper on a Saturday morning, marked in the same session against the published mark scheme, is worth more than two tired weekday hours and is the one thing a weekday slot cannot accommodate.

And if the slot has become impossible, say so rather than letting the arrangement decay. Moving a session permanently to a different day is a five-minute conversation. Three weeks of late starts followed by a quiet stop is how most families' tutoring ends, and it ends in the term they needed it most.
bullets: Protect the existing slot before adding any hours
Ask for component marks, not the mock grade, before changing the plan
Add weekend hours rather than weekday ones during mock season

sections.heading: Cost, permits and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: Dubai market rates, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified IGCSE subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, rising to AED 500. A twelve-week term at one weekly session is therefore AED 1,800-3,600 at the qualified band.

Context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices; we publish no price list on these pages and start with a free trial lesson.

On permits: individual tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

On academic honesty: a tutor teaches the skills an assessment examines, explains what the criteria reward, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote, never writing, rewriting or completing assessed work. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit and has no UAE office.
