faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a Bluewaters Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Half past five on a weekday for most, and six o'clock for students commuting to the Emirates Hills or Jumeirah Park ring. There is no school on the island, so every child travels, and the honest figure is the arrival time at the apartment rather than the school's finish time. Add a meal and a short break to that and you have the usable start. Families who set the slot from the school bell instead end up thirty minutes optimistic, and three weeks of late starts is how most weekly arrangements quietly end.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living on Bluewaters Island attend?
faqs.answer: No school sits on the island, so children commute into three rings. The Greens is the shortest run, with Regent International School, and students there are often home by four. Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim form the main ring, with campuses including Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Raffles World Academy. The inland ring covers Jumeirah Park, The Meadows and Emirates Hills. We name these as context for scheduling and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Why does the bridge matter so much for tutoring logistics?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only vehicle route on and off the island, and the two hours it is worst are the two hours a secondary student is free. A tutor leaving an Al Barsha campus at four faces Sheikh Zayed Road, the Marina exit, The Walk traffic and then the bridge, followed by visitor parking in a residential tower. The last kilometre is frequently the slowest. None of that is teaching, and the published Dubai travel premium of AED 50-150 an hour is that journey priced into the lesson.

faqs.question: Should the demanding subjects go in the weekday or weekend slot?
faqs.answer: The weekend, and planning that split is what keeps a schedule working. Mathematics breaks into short problems and survives a tired evening; chemistry mole drill is repetitive by design and arguably better late. Biology has the highest content volume and fails when a student is tired, English Language analysis needs alertness, Additional Mathematics needs a genuinely fresh student, and a full timed paper needs an uninterrupted block. Most Bluewaters families settle on one weekday evening for maintenance and one weekend morning for the hard material.

faqs.question: We have two children at two different schools. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Consecutive slots rather than parallel ones, so one child works while the other eats, then they swap. Both slots at the same times every week, with different subject specialists working to one shared written schedule, and both moved together when travel or Ramadan requires it. Where the children are on different systems, which is common on the island, the plan also has to respect two reporting calendars and two holiday patterns, since those do not always align even between schools in the same emirate.

faqs.question: Will the weekly slot survive Ramadan, or do we pause for a month?
faqs.answer: Move them after Iftar and agree it in advance. School hours shorten and household routines move later, so a nine o'clock session with the family awake is usually more productive than a five o'clock one while fasting. The planning catch is that Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so the school weeks it overlaps with change and a schedule copied from last year will be wrong about which term is affected. We hold the slot and the tutor rather than dropping either.

faqs.question: Is a winter-break intensive a good use of the holiday?
faqs.answer: Rarely as a full programme. Families book ten to twenty hours across the long break and produce a tired January, in a term where mocks are often close. One or two targeted sessions on a single identified weakness, with real rest around them, achieves more. The spring break is different: by then content teaching has limited returns and timed paper work has high ones, so a short burst of papers over that break is usually sound. Decide either in advance rather than in the week itself.

faqs.question: Our Tuesday slot keeps slipping. Should we add more hours?
faqs.answer: No, fix the slot first. Adding hours to a schedule that is already failing produces more late starts, not more learning. Either move the session permanently to a day and time that works, or shorten it so it fits the window that actually exists. Mock season makes this acute: school days lengthen with revision sessions and a student who was managing half past five starts arriving at half past five. A five-minute conversation about the time is worth more than a month of extra sessions nobody attends properly.

faqs.question: What should we ask the exams officer before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things per subject, in writing: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child is entered for. Also ask which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in, because Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. In a school entering with both boards the answers differ by subject, which is why a report card can carry 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without any error.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier really limit what grade our daughter can get?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, yes: Core is capped at grade C, so a student performing at the very top of that tier cannot be awarded a B. If a sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has effectively decided the outcome before revision begins. The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11, because Extended content never taught would have to be learned alongside revising everything else.

faqs.question: What does one term of weekly IGCSE tuition cost from Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: A Dubai term is roughly twelve weeks, so one weekly session is twelve hours. At the market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, that is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600. Specialists sit higher at AED 200-450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home runs AED 180-350 and up to AED 500 because travel is in the rate. Those figures were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table, and they describe the market rather than our price list.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our apartment on Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. On this island that is the operative advantage rather than a limitation: with one bridge and the worst traffic falling in the only hours a student is free, an arrangement requiring somebody to arrive has a cancellation built into every bad traffic day. Independent home tutors do work here, and for a younger child who needs somebody physically present they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings apply to a Bluewaters IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and revises them, so plan study leave against the live official PDF rather than any restatement. Your school's exams officer can confirm which series and which board each subject is entered under.

faqs.question: Can sessions move when we travel during half-term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and because they are online they follow the laptop rather than being cancelled. A fortnight in another time zone usually means a different clock time rather than a gap, which matters because a missed session in a twelve-week plan does not cost one lesson; it breaks the sequence that each lesson builds on. Tell us the travel dates when the schedule is set and they go into the plan from the start, along with term dates, exam leave and the Ramadan window for the year ahead.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence to teach our child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals offering private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-isl.closingHeading: Get the slot right and the rest becomes possible
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bluewaters-isl.closingBody: On an island with no school and one bridge, the timetable decides whether tutoring happens at all. Work out when your child genuinely walks through the door, add a meal, and set the weekly slot from there rather than from the school bell. Put the demanding subjects at the weekend and the drill in the weekday evening. Then get the board, the syllabus code and the tier from the exams officer, put the term dates and the Ramadan window in the calendar, and take a free trial lesson in the slot you actually intend to use.

intro.heading: The same shortlist on both sides of the creek
paragraphs: Parents in Old Dubai research tutoring geographically. A family in Al Mankhool asks whether rates are better in Karama; a family in Deira wonders whether crossing to Bur Dubai widens the choice; a family that has just moved from Al Qusais assumes the options there were thinner. The comparison is natural and the finding is consistently dull: for IGCSE at Years 10 and 11, the shortlist of people who can actually teach Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 to the mark scheme is small, it is not organised by neighbourhood, and nobody in it lives within walking distance of everybody.

What does differ by district is the cost of getting a tutor to your door and the time it takes. Old Dubai is dense and the afternoon exit is slow. A tutor crossing from Business Bay to a flat in Al Raffa at 5pm has lost two hours of their evening before teaching anything, and prices it accordingly, which is why in-home tutoring in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for comparable qualifications working online. The travel premium is real, it is geographic, and it buys proximity rather than subject depth.

So this page compares the districts honestly and then explains why the conclusion collapses into one answer. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tuition at the door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, with the student's own past papers on a shared screen. The point is not that travel is inconvenient — it is that removing travel is what lets a child in Karama work with the same Chemistry specialist as a child in Jumeirah.

There is a second comparison that matters more than geography and that almost no local page covers: which exam board your child's school actually uses. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award an International GCSE, both are accepted by UAE universities, and they set different papers with different codes, different tiering and different practical arrangements. A tutor working from Cambridge 0625 material with a student entered for Pearson 4PH1 will be approximately right and specifically wrong, and the marks lost sit in exactly the places parents cannot see.

The remainder of this page sets out the district-by-district comparison with schools and realistic session times, the board comparison by subject with syllabus codes, the Core and Extended tier decision, what the Dubai market charges from the bottom of the range upwards, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rules that apply identically whichever side of the creek you live on.

One practical note before the detail. Everything on this page about rates is what the Dubai market charges, attributed to whoever published the figure, rather than an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement opens with a free trial lesson and a conversation about which series your child is working towards, because the answer for a Year 10 student in October is a different purchase from the answer for a Year 11 student eight weeks out from the June papers.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: Old Dubai schools run IGCSE as the Year 10 and 11 stage of a British pathway, and most then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. These are the stages a Bur Dubai family meets, and what help is worth buying at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE begins, with no external examination and school-set assessment throughout. Gaps opened here are cheap to close and expensive to ignore: algebraic manipulation, scientific notation, and the written explanation that IGCSE mark schemes reward. Most Year 10 crises are Year 8 gaps that nobody measured at the time.
programmes.countryNote: Across Old Dubai this stage is where families transferring from an Indian or American curriculum arrive, and the mismatch is rarely in content coverage. It is in question style: a CBSE-trained student will often know more topics and score less, because IGCSE questions ask for applied reasoning in a fixed number of marks.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally by Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel. Tiering matters: Cambridge offers Core and Extended in several subjects with different grade ceilings, while Pearson uses a Foundation and Higher structure in some. Entry decisions are usually made in Year 10 and shape what A Level or Diploma choices remain open.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Confirm every date against the board's live timetable, since provisional versions are revised.

programmes.name: International A Level, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, assessed by examination with some practical components. Cambridge and Pearson both offer modular and linear routes depending on the subject, and the step up from IGCSE Extended is substantial in mathematics and the sciences. Students who got a grade 7 at IGCSE by memorising often meet a wall in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects. That is published guidance; verify current detail with the attestation authority in your emirate.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, taken by a minority of Dubai students but offered by several schools within a short drive of Bur Dubai. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. An IGCSE Extended background in mathematics and a science is close to a prerequisite for Higher Level in those subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Garhoud and Al Jaddaf schools run the Diploma, so an Old Dubai family choosing between A Level and IB is making a real choice rather than a theoretical one. The decision is usually better made on which assessment style suits the student than on which looks more impressive on an application.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: IGCSE requests from Old Dubai concentrate in mathematics and the sciences, with English Language and Business Studies close behind. Each entry names the common syllabus codes and where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most requested subject in this district. Extended adds functions, transformations of graphs, vectors and harder trigonometry. Marks go on unshown method, on premature rounding, and on reading a multi-step question as a single-step one. Past-paper volume beats revision guides here by a wide margin.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Calculus arrives early and unsupported, and students who relied on calculator work in 0580 struggle with algebraic differentiation. A term of steady weekly work in Year 11 is usually enough to make the A Level transition survivable.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and moments cause most of the damage, followed by anything requiring a graph to be interpreted rather than drawn. Cambridge assesses practical skills through a separate paper, and students lose marks there for method and variable control rather than for physics. Definitions must be reproduced precisely to earn the mark.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are the reliable failure points. Students who can balance an equation still lose marks on state symbols and on explaining a trend using the structure of the substance. Multi-mark explanation questions need a taught structure, not more revision time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A long syllabus where command terms decide the band. Describe, explain and suggest are not interchangeable, and a student who writes the same content for all three caps in the middle grades. Diagram labelling and data interpretation are both trainable and both routinely untrained.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Two-award and single-award routes that compress three sciences, taken by students who need science without three separate entries. Content is narrower than the separate sciences but the question style is identical, so technique work transfers directly. Check which route the school has entered your child for before buying anything.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response, where fluent speakers lose marks on structure rather than vocabulary. The reading questions reward close selection of evidence and nothing else; summary tasks punish paraphrase that drifts. Timed practice with a marked script is the only reliable intervention.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from English Language, with its own mark scheme and a speaking component. Many Old Dubai students are entered for this rather than first-language English, and the two need different teaching. Check the entry code before assuming your child's tutor is working on the right paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study application under time pressure. Students who learn definitions score in the lower bands because the marks sit in applying a concept to the stimulus material. Calculation questions in both subjects are reliable, quick marks and are the first thing worth drilling.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, logic gates and data representation on the Computer Science side; practical application files on the ICT side. The two are regularly confused by parents and by tutors. ICT loses marks on file management and version discipline, which sounds trivial and is worth whole grade boundaries.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab students to be taught in separate classes with different expectations. First-language and foreign-language entries are entirely different papers, which is the most common mismatch in this district.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.description: Highly procedural and therefore highly tutorable: a student who cannot produce a balance sheet in week one can usually produce one in week four. Marks go on presentation conventions and on narrative questions asking why an adjustment is made, which rote learners skip.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsIntro: These are the Old Dubai districts families compare against Bur Dubai, with the schools in each and what the afternoon actually does to a session plan. The practical difference between them is smaller than the map suggests.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Immediately south-east of Bur Dubai, with compact flats and large households. Tutors quote similar travel to here as to Al Mankhool, but shared study space makes session length the real variable rather than price.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Several British and Indian schools inside walking distance, which is unusual in Dubai. Short school runs make a 4pm start realistic, and that single hour is worth more than any rate difference between districts.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Large schools and sports clubs in one place, so dismissal and evening activities overlap. Families here usually land on 5.30pm or later, and three evenings a week are often already committed to clubs.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: Across the creek, with heavy afternoon congestion and a wide spread of curricula. The crossing is the only material difference from Bur Dubai, and online delivery removes it entirely.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Where much of the district's IB and premium British provision sits. Rates quoted to Al Garhoud addresses tend to sit at the upper end, which reflects the neighbourhood rather than the teaching.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: A long school corridor towards Sharjah with substantial Indian-curriculum and British provision. Students commuting from here lose the most time to traffic and gain the most from a session with no travel attached.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Newer towers with an IB continuum school nearby. Many families here are new to the emirate and comparing districts before a lease renewal, which is exactly the comparison this page answers.

regions.name: Al Mamzar
regions.note: Northern edge of Old Dubai, close to the Sharjah border. Tutors travelling from New Dubai rarely quote competitively for this address, and the gap between in-home and online rates is widest here.

schoolClusters.city: Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Oud Metha
schoolClusters.note: The district's core, mixing large Indian-curriculum schools with long-established British schools entering students for Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE. Boards vary by subject within a single school, which is why the entry code question matters more than the school's name.

schoolClusters.city: Karama, Al Jaddaf and Al Garhoud
schoolClusters.note: A short drive from Bur Dubai and the nearest concentration of IB Diploma provision, alongside British schools running IGCSE. Families regularly cross between these districts daily, which is the practical reason district-by-district rate shopping rarely pays off.

modes.description: One subject, sixty minutes, the same evening each week across the year content is actually taught. This is the cheapest useful version of IGCSE support and the least often bought, because Year 10 rarely feels urgent. Families who do it arrive in Year 11 needing technique work rather than content rescue, which is a far shorter and cheaper engagement.

modes.description: Two sessions a week for six to eight weeks, aimed at the June or November series. sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Bur Dubai costs, and what the same tutor costs in Karama
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Bur Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour in the Dubai market, including travel, and the figure barely moves if the address is in Karama, Al Mankhool or Oud Metha instead. Qualified online subject tutors in the same market run roughly AED 150 to 300. IB Gram works in the second group and sends nobody to a UAE address: lessons are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time.

The reason district comparison disappoints is supply-side. There are only so many people in this emirate who have taught Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 to the mark scheme, and they are not distributed evenly across neighbourhoods because nobody chose where to live based on tutoring demand. A family ringing round Karama agencies and then Bur Dubai agencies is often being offered the same handful of tutors through two intermediaries, at two different margins.

Where neighbourhood genuinely changes the number is at the extremes of the map. A tutor quoting for Al Mamzar or Al Qusais from a New Dubai base prices in a longer drive than one quoting for Al Mankhool, and the gap between in-home and online widens accordingly. The honest summary for an Old Dubai parent is that geography sets the travel premium and nothing else, and that the decision worth spending time on is the board and tier question in the next two sections.

One more point on agencies specifically. Several of the Old Dubai operators advertising a neighbourhood presence are intermediaries rather than employers, which is not a criticism but does explain the pricing. They hold a list, they take a margin, and the tutor who arrives is drawn from the same pool a competitor three streets away is drawing from. Asking directly who will teach the lesson, what they have taught before, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit cuts through most of the district-level marketing. Those three questions are answerable in one message, and the answers vary far more than the advertised rates do.

sections.heading: Bur Dubai against the districts next door, school by school
paragraphs: The table below is the comparison parents actually want and nobody local publishes: what each district holds, what the afternoon does to it, and when a weekday session can realistically start. The last column is the one with money in it, because a session booked at a time the child cannot use is a session paid for twice.

Two patterns are worth drawing out. First, walking-distance districts buy an extra usable hour. Al Mankhool families can hold a 4pm slot because the child is home and fed by 3.30pm; Deira and Al Qusais families cannot, whatever they pay. Second, the districts with the heaviest school-run load are also the ones where an in-home tutor's travel premium is highest, so the two costs compound rather than offset.

The conclusion is the same in every row, which is the point of the exercise. Whichever of these addresses you are at, the constraint on a good IGCSE tutor is subject supply rather than distance, and the constraint on a good session time is the school run rather than the tutor's availability. Removing travel fixes the second and widens the first at the same time.

A word on how to use the table if you are mid-move. Families comparing districts before a lease renewal usually want to know whether a shorter school run is worth a higher rent, and the tutoring line in that calculation is small. The hour you gain from walking distance is real and it is worth having, but it is an hour you can also recover by removing a tutor's commute from the arrangement entirely. Rent the flat that fits the school and the commute; do not let the tutoring market influence a four-figure monthly decision when the variable it controls is measured in minutes.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same IGCSE subject
paragraphs: This is the comparison that changes grades, and almost no local tutoring page attempts it. Both boards award an International GCSE accepted by UAE universities and by the Ministry of Education equivalency route. They set different papers, number them differently, tier them differently and assess practical science differently. A student entered for Pearson 4PH1 revising from Cambridge 0625 past papers is practising the wrong paper structure and the wrong mark-scheme language.

Ask the school for the board and the syllabus code per subject, in writing, and expect them to differ within one school — it is common for a Dubai school to enter mathematics with one board and the sciences with another. Once you have the codes, every official specimen paper, specification and grade-description document is free on the board's own site, and a tutor should be working from those rather than from a commercial revision guide.

The practical-science difference deserves a line of its own because it catches families out in Year 11. Cambridge assesses practical skills through a dedicated paper, and students lose marks there on experimental method, variable control and graph work rather than on recall. A tutor cannot run the practical, but the skills the paper tests are taught at a desk, which is why the paper is a reliable target for a short block.

There is also a timing consequence worth planning around. Because the two boards run their series on different timetables and publish results at different points, a household with children entered with different boards can face two separate revision peaks in one academic year. That is manageable if it is known in September and difficult if it is discovered in April. Ask for the codes once, write them down, and check the live timetable on the board's own site each autumn rather than relying on a figure quoted in a tutoring advert or repeated from a previous year.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision with a grade ceiling attached
paragraphs: Cambridge offers Core and Extended routes in several IGCSE subjects, and the two have different grade ceilings. A Core entry cannot reach the top grades at all, which means the decision quietly closes doors to A Level and to Higher Level Diploma study in that subject. Schools make this decision in Year 10, sometimes without a conversation, and parents frequently discover it from a report rather than from a letter.

The decision itself is defensible. A student placed on Extended who cannot handle the content will underperform across a whole paper rather than securing solid middle grades on the Core one, and a confident Core grade is worth more than a collapsed Extended attempt. What is not defensible is making the decision from a single term's results early in Year 10, before any technique teaching has happened, and then treating it as settled.

So the practical advice for an Old Dubai family is to raise it early and in writing. Ask which tier each subject is entered for, what evidence the decision rested on, what the deadline for changing it is, and what performance would justify a move. A term of focused weekly work in Year 10 is often exactly what converts a borderline Core recommendation into a viable Extended entry, and that window closes long before Year 11 revision starts.

Two further details catch Old Dubai families out. Tiering is subject by subject, so a student can sit Extended mathematics and Core science in the same year, and parents who ask about one entry sometimes assume they have the answer for all of them. And the tier affects what revision material is appropriate: working through Extended past papers for a Core entry wastes weeks on content that will not appear, while the reverse leaves a student unprepared for the harder half of the paper. Confirm the tier before buying any tutoring, because it determines what the sessions should contain.

sections.heading: The cheapest useful IGCSE tutoring in Old Dubai, counted from the bottom up
paragraphs: Most rate tables start at the premium end, which flatters the seller. Counting upwards is more useful for a family with a budget. The floor of this market is about AED 33 to 52 an hour, which is Tutopiya's published starting rate, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65. At that level you are buying supervised homework time, usually from a university student. For a Year 8 who will not sit down without an adult present, that is a reasonable purchase and the right one.

The next band up is where IGCSE work properly starts. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, and qualified online subject tutors in this market sit broadly in the AED 150 to 300 range. This is the band where the tutor has taught the syllabus, has marked against the scheme, and can tell you which three topics are costing marks rather than asking your child what they find difficult. Above it, TutorChase publishes AED 270, Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, and the highest published figure found in this market is AED 650 at a premium named-tutor agency.

Monthly, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates, a weekly one-hour session runs AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these are IB Gram prices — they are what the market charges, each attributed to the source that published it, and our own arrangement opens with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in a Bur Dubai flat against the same tutor online
paragraphs: Comparing formats within a district is more revealing than comparing districts. Take a single Year 11 student in a Bur Dubai apartment preparing Cambridge 0620 Chemistry for the June series. The in-home option delivers a tutor at the table, which suits a student who needs supervision to start work at all, and it costs the travel premium. The online option delivers whoever in the matched pool actually knows 0620 electrolysis questions, and produces a file trail.

The trade is clearer once the week is laid out. An in-home session in Old Dubai usually cannot begin before 6pm because of the tutor's own commute, which in a Year 11 household competing with Arabic homework and a sibling's bedtime is the worst slot available. An online session can run at 4.30pm. Over an eight-week block that difference is not cosmetic: it is the gap between a student working while alert and a student working while tired.

Against that, three honest caveats. A student who will not engage with a screen needs a different plan, not a better platform. A shared study space in a Karama or Bur Dubai flat needs headphones and a negotiated hour, which is a household logistics problem rather than a teaching one. And a parent who wants to watch the lesson happening can do that online too, which several families in this district prefer for the first fortnight. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the table sets out why we think that is the right side of the trade for an Old Dubai IGCSE family.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same in Deira as in Al Mankhool
paragraphs: Pull the comparisons together and the district variable collapses. Rates differ by travel time. School-run timing differs by walking distance. Inspection bands differ school by school rather than neighbourhood by neighbourhood. None of those three changes which tutor can teach Pearson 4MA1 Higher to a student who is losing marks on functions and transformations, and that is the only variable that determines the grade.

This is not an argument that place does not matter. Place determines the school, and the school determines the board, the tier, the internal deadlines and the quality of the subject department your child sits in every day. Those are enormous. What place does not determine, once travel is removed from the equation, is the pool of people available to teach a specific syllabus at a specific level on a Tuesday evening.

For a parent comparing districts before a lease renewal, the useful conclusion is to stop costing tutoring by neighbourhood and start costing it by subject and year group. A Year 10 student needing one subject weekly is a different budget from a Year 11 student needing two subjects twice weekly before the June series, and that difference dwarfs anything geography contributes. The schools and the commute should decide where you live; they should not decide who teaches your child chemistry.

There is one genuine exception to all of this, and it is worth naming so the argument stays honest. A student who needs an adult physically present to begin work at all is better served by somebody in the room, and for that family geography does decide the shortlist, because only tutors who can reach the address are candidates. That is a minority of IGCSE students and it is usually a younger one. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student who will sit down and work, the district question has no grade attached to it.
bullets: Travel time, not teaching quality, explains inter-district rate differences
Inspection bands vary school by school, not district by district

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory UAE subjects and equivalency, identical on both sides of the creek
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports. That publication is the single most useful free resource an Old Dubai parent has, and it is subject-specific enough to tell you whether the mathematics department at your child's school is the problem.

KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with its requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies — combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Content for those subjects cannot be substituted without prior Ministry of Education permission, so tutoring works within the school's stream rather than around it.

The equivalency rules are federal and therefore identical in Karama and Al Garhoud. On the British track, students must pass five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at no less than grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees; verify current requirements with the ministry or the attestation authority in your emirate.
bullets: Read the published KHDA inspection report for your child's school before buying tutoring

process.title: Send the syllabus codes, not just the subjects
process.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 need different preparation, and the codes are the fastest way to get the match right. If you do not have them, ask the school for the board and code per subject in writing — it is a reasonable request and schools answer it.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnosis
process.description: The first session costs nothing and is spent finding where the marks are going, working from the student's own recent school work or a past paper rather than a generic placement test. A written summary follows whether you continue or not.

process.title: A plan with a tier decision in it
process.description: For Year 10 students the plan says explicitly what Core or Extended entry looks like and what performance would support a change. That conversation belongs at the start rather than after the school has made the decision for you.

process.title: Weekly sessions on an Old Dubai timetable
process.description: The slot is fixed for the term around your actual school run, club commitments and Ramadan hours. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with the whiteboard saved and the session recorded for the student to revisit.

process.title: Checkpoint, then continue or stop
process.description: At the agreed point you compare a marked paper against the diagnostic one. If nothing has moved we change the tutor or the approach, and if the work is done we say so rather than letting the arrangement roll on by default.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific, not board-agnostic
whyPoints.description: Teaching is planned from the actual syllabus code and the board's own specimen papers and specifications. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers is approximately right in a way that costs marks nobody can see until results day.

whyPoints.title: The same specialist pool for every Old Dubai address
whyPoints.description: A student in Al Qusais is matched to the same people as a student in Al Mankhool. That is the practical consequence of removing travel, and it is the only part of the district comparison that changes outcomes.

whyPoints.title: Rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page names who published it and what band it describes. Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain mark schemes and give feedback on the student's own writing. We do not produce coursework or any assessed piece, and we say so on the page rather than in the small print.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can check
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, saved whiteboards, recordings and a written note after each session. At the checkpoint you are comparing two marked papers rather than two impressions.

whyPoints.title: Straight answers on availability
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in a particular syllabus is free in the window you need, we say so at the start. In the weeks before the June series that answer matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE tutoring rates in Karama cheaper than in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Barely, and not for a reason that helps you. Quotes to Karama, Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai addresses sit in much the same range because the travel time is similar. The in-home band across Dubai runs roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour, and the gap between districts only widens at the edges of the map, where a tutor driving to Al Mamzar or Al Qusais prices in a longer journey. What does not change by district is the number of people who have actually taught your child's syllabus, which is the variable that moves a grade.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our flat in Bur Dubai or Karama?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are something we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In Old Dubai that is usually the better trade rather than a limitation: a travelling tutor cannot start before about 6pm after their own commute, and the pool narrows to whoever can reach your street. Online, your child works with somebody who has taught that exact syllabus code, at 4.30pm rather than 6pm, with the whiteboard and marked scripts saved for you to look at.

faqs.question: Which exam board has my child's Bur Dubai school entered them with, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the board and the syllabus code for each subject, in writing, and expect the answer to vary by subject within one school. Dubai schools commonly enter mathematics with one board and the sciences with another. Once you have the codes, the specification, specimen papers and grade descriptions are free on the board's own website, and any tutor worth paying will be working from those. A tutor using the wrong board's past papers will look competent and will be drilling the wrong paper structure.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series do UAE students actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. The February and March series that circulates online is offered to India only, and planning a UAE child's revision around it is a real error rather than a technicality. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026. Always check the board's live timetable, because provisional versions are revised.

faqs.question: Can we move my child from a Core entry to Extended in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the window is narrower than most parents realise. Ask the school which tier each subject is entered for, what evidence the decision rested on, and the deadline for changing it. A borderline recommendation made early in Year 10, before any technique teaching has happened, is frequently movable with a term of focused weekly work. What is not sensible is pushing a student onto Extended who will collapse across the whole paper; a secure Core grade beats a failed Extended attempt, so treat it as a real decision.

faqs.question: What is the least we can spend and still get something useful for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Below about AED 100 an hour you are buying supervision rather than teaching. Tutopiya publishes rates from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which suits a Year 8 who needs an adult present to start work. Proper IGCSE syllabus teaching starts around AED 150, where Unitors pitches its IGCSE tuition, and qualified online subject tutors in this market sit between AED 150 and 300. If the budget is tight, buy fewer hours in that band rather than more hours in the band below it.

faqs.question: Is it worth crossing the creek for a better tutoring agency?
faqs.answer: No. The agencies on either side of the creek draw from the same small pool of people who can teach a given syllabus code, and you are often offered the same tutor through two intermediaries at two margins. What crossing the creek does cost you is time: a 3.15pm collection from Al Garhoud puts a Bur Dubai child at a desk around 5.30pm at best. The decision worth researching is the board and tier your school has entered your child for, not which district an agency advertises from.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One properly, or two if they share a skill base, such as mathematics with a science. A family that buys an eight-week block and asks for four subjects inside it ends up with twenty minutes of practice per topic and no measurable change anywhere. Each weekly session also generates two or three hours of work between sessions, so four subjects is a workload a Year 11 student with Arabic homework and club commitments will not service. Pick the subject where the most marks are recoverable and work it until it stops costing them.

faqs.question: My child is at an Indian-curriculum school in Karama and moving to IGCSE. What changes?
faqs.answer: Usually not the content, which is often broader on the national board, but the question style. IGCSE papers ask for applied reasoning inside a fixed mark allocation, so a student who knows more can score less. The fixable gaps are command-term discipline, showing method, and reading a multi-step question properly. Expect six to ten weeks of weekly work to rebuild that, ideally in Year 10 rather than Year 11, and expect the first marked past paper to look worse than the school reports suggested it would.

faqs.question: How is the Cambridge practical science paper handled if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The practical paper tests experimental method, variable control, measurement and graph work rather than manual skill, and all of that is taught at a desk. A tutor works through the board's own past practical papers, the mark schemes and the recurring question types: identifying the dependent variable, spotting an uncontrolled factor, choosing axes, drawing a line of best fit, and explaining an anomaly. The school runs the laboratory work; the marks on that paper are won in interpretation and in precise written method, which is exactly what online sessions can target.

faqs.question: Does an Al Qusais address limit which tutors we can get?
faqs.answer: For an in-home tutor, yes, noticeably — it is one of the longest drives from the New Dubai tutoring base and quotes reflect it. For online lessons it makes no difference at all, which is the single clearest argument for the format in this part of the emirate. Al Qusais students also lose the most time to the daily commute, so the hour saved by not waiting for a tutor to arrive is worth more here than almost anywhere else in Old Dubai. Session timing is the constraint, not tutor supply.

faqs.question: Which subjects do Old Dubai families most often ask us to teach at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first by a wide margin, then Chemistry and Physics, then English Language, with Business Studies and Accounting behind them. Additional Mathematics appears in Year 11 from students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Arabic requests rise through the year, which reflects the fact that every Dubai private school timetables it whatever the licensed curriculum, and that first-language and foreign-language entries are different papers needing different teaching.

faqs.question: Is the KHDA inspection report worth reading before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports, which comment at department level. If the report says attainment in mathematics is weaker than in other subjects, you have learned something specific about where your child's problem originates. Bands also vary sharply between schools two streets apart, so a neighbour's experience of one school tells you very little about another in the same district.

faqs.question: What can an IGCSE tutor legitimately do with my child's coursework draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying skills, explain what the published criteria reward, discuss approach and structure, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite passages into better prose, or supply material for the student to transcribe. We hold that line explicitly because the alternative is sold openly in this market, and the consequence of buying finished work falls on the student rather than on the seller. Feedback from our tutors comes back as comments and questions on the student's own document.

faqs.question: What should I send before the first IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them takes long. The board and syllabus code for the subject, so the tutor prepares the right paper. The most recent school report or assessment, including the tier your child is entered for. And a photograph of a recent marked piece of work, because the specific errors on it tell a tutor more in two minutes than a description of the problem does in twenty. If you have none of that, the free trial lesson starts with a short diagnostic instead.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingHeading: Compare the districts, then stop comparing them
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingBody: If you have been pricing tutors by neighbourhood across Old Dubai, the finding on this page is that the travel premium is the only thing that moves. What changes a grade is whether the person teaching your child has taught that exact syllabus code and can name the three topics costing marks. Send us the board and code, tell us which year group and which series you are working towards, and the first lesson is free and spent on diagnosis. Every session is one-to-one over live video, timed around the Old Dubai school run, with a written summary afterwards whether you continue or not.

intro.heading: Answering the home-tutor question straight, then comparing it properly
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE home tutor in Business Bay is asking for something specific: a qualified person who comes to the apartment at an agreed hour and teaches their child at the dining table. That is a real service, it exists in Dubai, and plenty of families use it. The honest thing to do on this page is tell you what it costs, what the hour actually contains once travel is accounted for, how families choose between providers, and then say plainly what IB Gram does instead and why. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India.

Start with the money, because that is where the home-tuition decision is usually made. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table records in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. Advertised monthly packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Per contact hour that is close to double, and the difference is not buying more teaching. It is buying a car journey, a tower basement and a security desk.

The Business Bay geography makes that journey expensive in a way villa communities do not. This is a district of towers along the Dubai Canal and Marasi Drive, with limited and often paid visitor parking in building basements, security sign-in at reception, and lift waits in buildings with several hundred apartments. A tutor who leaves Al Barsha at 5.15pm for a 6pm appointment in a canal-side tower is budgeting forty-five minutes of driving and ten of access. Across a thirty-week school year, the access time alone eats several hours of teaching, and all of it is inside the rate whether it appears on the invoice or not.

Here is the comparison this page is built around. A family in Business Bay, a family in Downtown Dubai, a family in DIFC and a family out in Al Quoz are all looking at the same thing from slightly different positions. Business Bay and Downtown are tower districts with nearly identical school runs and almost no schools inside their own boundaries. DIFC is the same again with longer parental working hours. Al Quoz has schools on its doorstep and slower roads out. The travel premium, the tutor pool and the access friction differ in degree between them and point the same direction in every case, which is the useful finding rather than a convenient one.

What changes the answer is not the postcode. It is the age of the child and the subject. A Year 4 pupil who will not stay seated genuinely benefits from an adult in the room, and no amount of argument about tutor pools alters that. A Year 11 student working Cambridge 0580 past papers on a shared screen does not, and for that student the binding constraint is whether the tutor knows the paper structure for their syllabus code. The rest of this page sets out the comparison with figures, names the provider models, explains the permit position, and shows what we do when we cannot match a request.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: IGCSE in Dubai is sat at 16 and sits inside several different structures depending on the school. These are the routes Business Bay families are on, and what each means for the kind of tutor who is useful.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: The largest board in Dubai by candidate volume. Subjects carry four-digit codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0500 English as a First Language, 0620 Chemistry, 0450 Business Studies — and most are tiered, with Core candidates assessed on reduced content and a grade ceiling, and Extended candidates assessed on the full content. UAE candidates sit the June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Business Bay family that means working only from the timetable the school issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Used by a substantial minority of Dubai schools, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4EA1 English Language. The separate sciences are untiered and graded 9 to 1, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. Examinations are available in May/June and November each year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes its timetables openly, which makes planning easier than for some other qualifications. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Double award and combined science routes
programmes.description: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 give two IGCSE grades from one course covering all three disciplines. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 gives one. Content is reduced relative to three separate sciences, but the breadth is not, and tutors who have taught the double award specifically are scarcer than tutors who have taught the separate subjects.
programmes.countryNote: A large number of Dubai schools use the double award for students carrying nine or ten subjects, because it frees a timetable slot. Business Bay parents frequently do not know which route their child is on until they check the statement of entry, and the distinction changes what should be revised.

programmes.name: What follows IGCSE in Dubai
programmes.description: Students split between A Levels and the IB Diploma, and a smaller number move to an American diploma route. The Diploma adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS on top of six subjects, while A Level narrows to three or four. Both are accepted by UAE universities, and the Ministry's equivalency requirements differ by track rather than by preference.
programmes.countryNote: The decision is made in Year 11, usually in the same term as mock examinations, which is why IGCSE tuition requests from this district often arrive bundled with a question about which post-16 route suits. Those are separate conversations and both deserve a proper answer.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: Business Bay enquiries concentrate in a handful of IGCSE subjects, and the pattern is consistent enough to publish. These are the ones requested most often, with the part of each that usually needs the work.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The single most requested IGCSE subject in this corridor. Cambridge 0580 now splits into a non-calculator and a calculator paper at each tier, which caught out a whole cohort of students who had learned to reach for a device by reflex. Pearson 4MA1 permits calculators in both papers.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Marks turn on directed writing and the summary task rather than on reading ability. Students who read widely and still underperform are almost always losing marks to structure and to a failure to use the question's own terms in the response.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, bonding, the periodic table and organic chemistry. The avoidable loss is in quantitative questions set out so untidily that method marks are not awarded, which is a presentation habit rather than a chemistry gap.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the topic Business Bay students flag most, and it is almost always a circuit-reading problem rather than an equation problem. Pearson 4PH1 adds astrophysics content that is taught late in the course and revised least.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rewards precise syllabus vocabulary over general understanding. A student who explains a process correctly in everyday words will lose marks a tutor can recover in a few sessions by drilling the terms the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Popular in this district, partly because the parents work in the industries the case studies describe. Marks are lost on application: students explain a concept accurately and never tie it back to the specific business in the question stem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students expect, and a mislabelled axis costs more than a weak paragraph. The evaluation questions at the end of each section are where the grade is actually decided.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory questions on data representation and architecture tend to score worse than the programming elements, because students revise the practical work they enjoy. Pseudocode conventions are worth drilling explicitly.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger mathematicians alongside 0580, often as preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. The jump in algebraic demand is steep, and students who coasted through 0580 Extended feel it immediately.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Taken as an IGCSE subject and separately required by KHDA of all Dubai private schools. Note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-business-bay.regionsIntro: Business Bay sits in a line of central districts that share schools, roads and the same tower-access problem. This page compares them deliberately, because the comparison is what tells you whether the postcode changes the answer.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Several hundred towers along the Dubai Canal and Marasi Drive, with its own Red Line metro station. No private school inside the district, so every child commutes, and visitor parking is limited and often paid.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately north across the canal. Nearly identical school runs and the same absence of schools inside the boundary. Bus returns run slightly earlier here, which shifts the workable session start forward by about half an hour.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: The same tower pattern with longer parental working hours, since many residents work in the buildings above. A financial free zone with its own courts, though schools remain regulated by KHDA throughout Dubai.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: The genuine contrast case: several long-established schools sit inside the district, so some children walk or take a short ride. The roads out are slower, which makes an in-home tutor's journey here worse than to Business Bay.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Culture Village
regions.note: Creek-side communities with a school within ten minutes and a lower-rise housing mix. Access for a visiting tutor is easier here than in a canal-side tower, which is the one place the comparison genuinely shifts.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: A school destination rather than a commuter origin, with British and IB campuses on the same development. Many Business Bay buses end their morning run here.

regions.name: Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Villa districts where in-home tuition is more practical than in a tower, with parking at the door and no security desk. The tutor pool is still limited by the drive, which is the constraint that does not change.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Newer villa developments between Meydan and Al Quoz, with schools opening into the area. Session timings here track Business Bay closely despite the different housing type.

schoolClusters.city: Schools Business Bay children commute to
schoolClusters.note: The campuses named most often in IGCSE enquiries from Business Bay and the canal-side towers. They do not all use the same examination board, and several have changed board between cohorts, so this year's statement of entry is the only reliable source.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Oud Metha and Al Garhoud
schoolClusters.note: The older school belt either side of the centre, holding both Indian-curriculum schools with IGCSE streams and British schools running Cambridge subjects. Roughly twenty minutes from Marasi Drive outside peak hours, considerably longer at 3.30pm.

schoolClusters.city: Creek-side and continuum campuses
schoolClusters.note: Schools in Al Jaddaf, Hartland and Meydan running the IB continuum or offering IGCSE alongside it. Families here sometimes request IGCSE support when their child is on MYP, which is a different assessment model altogether.

sections.heading: What an in-home tutor's hour actually contains in a canal-side tower
paragraphs: Take a sixty-minute in-home session in a Business Bay tower and account for the whole transaction rather than the advertised hour. The tutor leaves their own home with a buffer for Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road, which at 5.15pm on a weekday means forty to fifty minutes for a journey that takes twenty at 11am. They arrive at the building and look for visitor parking, which in most Business Bay towers is limited, sometimes paid and occasionally full. They sign in at reception, wait for a lift in a building with several hundred apartments, and reach the door some minutes after the appointed time.

None of that is the tutor's fault and none of it is avoidable. It is also not free. A tutor making one visit per evening has to price in roughly ninety minutes of unpaid time around a sixty-minute lesson, and that is precisely why the published in-home band — Bestimate records AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500 — sits above the online specialist band for comparable expertise. You are paying the same person more money for the same teaching because the journey exists.

The second cost is less visible and larger. A tutor who will only take appointments within a twenty-minute radius of their home is a tutor whose client list is geographically constrained, and so is yours. Filter for someone who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended with the new non-calculator paper, is free at 6pm, and lives close enough to Marasi Drive to make the trip worthwhile, and the set of candidates collapses. Families feel this as a sequence of near misses rather than as an economic constraint, but that is what it is.

sections.heading: Business Bay against Downtown, DIFC and Al Quoz: does the postcode change the answer?
paragraphs: This is worth testing rather than asserting, because a tutoring page claiming that four different districts have the same needs is usually a page that has not looked. So compare them on the four things that actually vary: whether schools sit inside the district, how long a visiting tutor's journey takes, how hard the building is to enter, and what hour the child is realistically free.

Business Bay and Downtown are near twins. Both are tower districts with no private school inside the boundary, both feed the same four school clusters, both have constrained visitor parking and security desks. The only meaningful difference is timing: Downtown buses tend to collect and return slightly earlier, which moves the workable session start forward by around thirty minutes. DIFC adds a third variable, which is parental working hours — residents who work in the towers above frequently want a slot after 7pm, and that is a scheduling preference rather than a geographic difference.

Al Quoz is the genuine contrast and the reason this comparison is worth making. It has long-established schools inside the district, so some children have a short journey or none. On the face of it that should favour in-home tuition. In practice it does the opposite: the roads around Al Quoz are slower than those around the canal, so a tutor driving in from anywhere else loses more time, and the local tutor pool is no larger. The district where children travel least is the district where tutors travel worst.

The finding is that the travel premium, the pool constraint and the access friction vary in degree across these four districts and point the same way in all of them. What does change the answer is the child's age and the subject, which is a different axis entirely. The table sets out the comparison with the figures each district actually produces.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition compared on IGCSE terms
paragraphs: Three formats are genuinely available to a Business Bay family and each suits something. Group tuition at a centre is the cheapest per student and works for a cohort at the same tier covering the same topic on the same timetable. Its weakness for IGCSE is tiering: a Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same room are being taught material one of them will not be examined on, and a student with a specific gap gets the group's average pace rather than their own.

In-home one-to-one buys presence. An adult in the room can see the page, notice disengagement early and keep a younger child seated. For Year 7 to Year 9 that is a real benefit. For Year 11, where the work is past papers and mark schemes, presence matters much less than whether the tutor can tell your child, within thirty seconds, which of three standard traps they just fell into on a 0580 Extended question.

Live online one-to-one buys match quality and reliability. The tutor is selected on syllabus knowledge and availability rather than on where they live, the session opens on the minute, past papers are annotated on a shared screen and saved rather than left in a bedroom, and a session can be moved in mock season without anyone writing off a journey. The cost of it is that the student needs a quiet room and the self-containment to sit through an hour without an adult beside them, which most Year 10 and Year 11 students have and most Year 4 pupils do not.

Being explicit about the trade-off matters more than winning the argument. If your child is eight, a visiting tutor is probably the better purchase and IB Gram is not the right provider, because we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. If your child is fifteen and sitting nine IGCSEs next June, the match is the thing that moves the grade and the format should be chosen to maximise it.

sections.heading: Provider models in the Dubai market, compared without naming favourites
paragraphs: Every tutoring site in Dubai compares itself to an unnamed category of inferior competitor, which tells a parent nothing. A more useful comparison is between the business models, because the model determines what you can and cannot expect. There are broadly six, and each one has a predictable strength and a predictable failure.

A specialist agency vets tutors, charges a margin and usually replaces a poor match. An international marketplace offers volume and price competition with much weaker vetting, and often prices in a currency UAE parents do not transact in. A freelance independent tutor is the cheapest per hour and carries the most variance, with no replacement if the fit is wrong and no cover if they are unavailable. A tuition centre with premises offers group classes and a physical location, and in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a real regulatory step. School-run support is the best aligned to your child's actual scheme of work and the least individually diagnosed. An online platform like IB Gram trades presence for match quality and scheduling reliability.

What a parent should extract from this is a short set of questions that work on any of the six. Does the quoted rate cover sixty minutes or a session of unspecified length? Is travel inside or outside it? What happens if the tutor is unavailable for three weeks? What happens if the match is wrong after two lessons? Does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Is there a free trial, and if so what condition is attached to the word free?

Those six questions sort the market faster than any comparison table a provider writes about itself, this one included. Ask them of us too; the answers are on this page and we would rather you checked.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted rather than unregulated, and the rules are more specific than most parents realise. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. A figure sometimes circulated in news coverage could not be verified, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so any number quoted to you should be treated as unverified rather than as a fact.

There is a separate and much larger requirement for anyone running a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai. That needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and runs no office, centre or branch in the UAE, which is why no address appears on this page. Describing a tutoring business as having regulatory endorsement when it holds no permit is the single most common misrepresentation in this market.

One further rule is worth knowing because it affects a request parents sometimes make. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the practical point stands: do not ask for your child's own class teacher privately.

sections.heading: Hidden extras, cancellations and what happens if you stop after one lesson
paragraphs: The published hourly rate is rarely the whole price, and in this market the gap between the two is where most complaints originate. Five things commonly sit outside the headline figure. Travel, which is inside the in-home band but sometimes charged separately for distant areas. Materials, where some providers bill for printed packs. Assessment or diagnostic fees charged before teaching starts. Minimum commitments, where a rate is only available if you book ten sessions. And cancellation terms, which vary from forgiving to punitive and are almost never on the pricing page.

Ask the five directly. Does the quoted figure cover sixty minutes or a session of unspecified length? Is travel inside it? Are materials included? Is there a minimum booking to access that rate? What notice cancels a session without charge, and what happens when the tutor cancels rather than you? A provider that answers all five in one message is a provider worth dealing with regardless of which model they run.

The word free deserves its own paragraph, because it is used loosely here. A free trial with a condition attached — a card on file, a minimum follow-on booking, or an eligibility rule — is not free in the way a parent reads it, and the condition should appear on the same screen as the offer. Our trial is one real lesson at no charge with no obligation to continue and no card required, and if you stop after it you owe nothing. That is a simple commitment to make and it is worth asking any provider to match it in writing.

On continuity: if you stop after one lesson because the match was wrong, the right response from a provider is to offer a different tutor rather than to treat the enquiry as closed. A mismatch in the first hour is information, not failure, and in a market where parents commonly go through three tutors before finding the right one, a provider who rematches without friction saves you a term.

sections.heading: Planning a term around the June and November series
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two IGCSE series a year, and the choice between them is a real decision rather than an administrative detail. Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series that appears in some revision forums is offered to India only and does not apply to a child in Dubai, so any February or March date quoted to you is for a different country.

Pearson publishes its pattern openly. Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is exactly why a plan should be built from the live official timetable rather than from dates restated anywhere else, including here.

Working backwards from a June series, the useful checkpoints are these. In September, confirm the board, the codes and the tier for every subject and fix the weekly tuition slot. By the winter break, complete one full past paper per subject under timed conditions to produce a real baseline rather than a teacher's impression. By February, have the mock results and choose the two subjects that will take the remaining tuition budget. From March, run timed papers weekly and stop learning new content in the weakest subject. In the final fortnight, revise only what has been practised.

A November entry runs on a compressed version of the same logic, decided in the week August results arrive. Eight weeks is enough to move one subject meaningfully and not enough to move three, so the decision is which single grade matters most, and the exams officer is the person to have that conversation with immediately rather than a month later.
