sections.heading: Coverage, matching and what we do when the answer is no
paragraphs: No provider in this market publishes where its coverage runs thin, and that silence is why families go through a sequence of near misses. Ours, stated plainly: Cambridge and Pearson mathematics and separate sciences are well covered at both tiers, because they are the highest-volume codes in Dubai. English as a First Language, Business Studies and Economics are well covered. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is covered but thinner, because fewer tutors have taught the double award specifically. Cambridge 0653, Additional Mathematics 0606 and Oxford AQA subjects are narrower, and we will say so before you book rather than afterwards.

When a request cannot be matched well, the options are a named wait, a different hour where a better-matched tutor is free, or a subject specialist with the code-specific gap described openly so you can judge it yourself. What we will not do is take a 0654 booking and put a biology graduate on it in the hope that the discipline knowledge covers the double-award structure, because with tiering and reduced content it frequently does not.

Two further disclosures belong here. Some of our tutors are UAE residents and others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, working with Dubai students over live video scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not route UAE families to a non-UAE number while implying a local presence, and we claim no UAE office because there is none. Both of those facts are checkable in the free trial lesson, which is the point of offering one.

On data: we ask for the school, the year group, the syllabus code and tier, and the hour your child is realistically home. Those four facts determine the match. We do not ask for grades, report cards or photographs. Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection you can ask what is held about your child and ask for it to be deleted, and a provider who cannot answer that quickly is telling you something useful.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE home tutor who comes to my apartment in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Providers in Dubai do offer in-home tuition, and the published rates are AED 180 to AED 350 an hour per Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. If a tutor in the room is what your child needs, usually because of age, that is a legitimate choice and we would rather tell you plainly than take a booking we cannot honour as described.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition in a Business Bay tower more expensive than online?
faqs.answer: Because roughly ninety minutes of unpaid time surrounds every sixty-minute visit, and it is priced into the rate. A tutor driving from most parts of Dubai to a canal-side tower at 5.15pm budgets forty to fifty minutes, then looks for limited and often paid visitor parking, signs in at a security desk and waits for a lift in a building with several hundred apartments. Advertised monthly packages show the gap: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

faqs.question: Does the right answer change if we live in Downtown or DIFC instead of Business Bay?
faqs.answer: Not materially. Business Bay and Downtown are near twins: tower districts with no school inside the boundary, feeding the same school clusters, with the same parking and security friction. Downtown buses return slightly earlier, which moves the workable session start forward by about half an hour. DIFC adds longer parental working hours, so slots after 7pm are more commonly requested. The travel premium, the tutor-pool constraint and the access friction point the same way in all three. What changes the answer is the child's age, not the postcode.

faqs.question: Is Al Quoz different, given that it has schools inside the district?
faqs.answer: It is different in a way that makes the case stronger rather than weaker. Al Quoz does have long-established schools inside the district, so some children travel very little to school. But the roads around Al Quoz are slower than those around the canal, so a tutor driving in from elsewhere loses more time than they would reaching Business Bay, and the local tutor pool is no larger. The district where children travel least turns out to be the district where visiting tutors travel worst, which is the opposite of what parents expect.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at a centre a reasonable alternative for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. It is the cheapest option per student and works well where a group is at the same tier covering the same topic on the same timetable. Its weakness for IGCSE is tiering: a Cambridge Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same room are being taught material one of them will not be examined on. A student with a specific diagnosed gap also gets the group's average pace rather than their own, which is why centres work better for general revision than for fixing a particular weakness.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Dubai tutoring provider about price before booking?
faqs.answer: Five questions sort the market quickly. Does the quoted rate cover sixty minutes or a session of unspecified length? Is travel inside or outside it? Are materials included or billed separately? Is there a minimum booking required to access that rate? And what notice cancels a session without charge, in both directions, including when the tutor cancels rather than you? A provider who answers all five in one message is worth dealing with whatever model they run. Ask us the same five.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a permit, and what is it actually called?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can I hire my child's own class teacher as a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It should be avoided and in Abu Dhabi it is explicitly barred. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That position is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document. For a Dubai family the sensible reading is that the arrangement creates a conflict for the teacher, so do not ask for it.

faqs.question: What does a tuition centre in Dubai need that an individual tutor does not?
faqs.answer: A KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a substantially larger requirement than an individual permit. The process begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE, which is why no address appears anywhere on this page. If a provider implies regulatory endorsement, ask for the permit number.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Business Bay families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics by a wide margin, then the separate sciences, then English as a First Language. Business Studies and Economics also appear more often here than in other Dubai districts, which is unsurprising given what the parents in these towers do for a living. Within mathematics the most common issue since the 0580 syllabus change is the non-calculator paper, which caught out a cohort of students who had learned to reach for a device by reflex. Pearson 4MA1 permits calculators in both papers, so the problem is board-specific.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board and tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry the school issues for the examination series carries the board name and the syllabus code for every subject, and the exams officer holds the entry data and can confirm it in a short email. The science department or curriculum overview page on the school's website usually names the board too. The one source not to rely on is the textbook on your child's shelf, which is frequently from a different board than the one they are entered for. You want the board, the code and the tier.

faqs.question: When should we decide between a November resit and waiting for June?
faqs.answer: In the week the original result arrives, with the exams officer. A November entry gives roughly eight weeks of preparation and a result in January; Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and its November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026. A June entry gives a far longer runway and an August result. Eight weeks is enough to move one subject meaningfully and not enough to move three, so the real question is which single grade matters most for the next step.

Ask any provider to confirm their trial terms in writing.

We do not need grades, report cards or photographs and do not ask for them. A marked past paper is useful if you choose to send one and is used only for diagnosis. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach to a named syllabus code rather than to a general subject. Each one will ask which board, which tier and which optional papers your child's school has entered before planning anything, because the answer changes the content, the practical arrangement and the achievable grade range.

intro.heading: Before you hire anyone, find out which syllabus your child is on
paragraphs: City Walk families mostly use schools in Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, and those schools do not all enter students with the same examination board. One campus runs Cambridge IGCSE, the next runs Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a third enters mathematics with one board and the sciences with another. The subjects have the same names and the same reputations, and almost nothing else in common at the level a tutor works at: different syllabus codes, different paper structures, different tiering rules, different grade ranges and, in the sciences, a completely different approach to assessing practical work.

That single piece of information is worth more than any amount of neighbourhood searching. A tutor hired without it will teach the subject competently and will prepare the wrong paper. A Cambridge physics candidate sits either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper on top of the theory papers; a Pearson International GCSE physics candidate sits neither, because practical skills are assessed inside the written papers. A tutor who does not know which of those applies cannot prioritise correctly, and the family discovers the mismatch in a mock.

The second thing to establish is the tier. Cambridge syllabuses in mathematics and the sciences run Core and Extended routes, and the route determines the grade range a candidate can be awarded; Pearson mathematics runs Foundation and Higher tiers with the same consequence. A student sitting a Core or Foundation paper cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and a student wrongly placed on Extended or Higher loses marks on content they were never going to secure. Tier placement is a school decision made on evidence, it can sometimes be revisited, and a parent who does not know which tier their child is on is not in a position to discuss it.

Delivery, stated at the top rather than discovered later. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. A City Walk family is therefore matched to a tutor who has taught the exact syllabus code their child is entered with, instead of to whichever tutor is prepared to drive to Al Wasl Road at five o'clock. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online, and that gap is a journey rather than a better lesson.

What follows is the detail a parent can act on today: the board comparison with the actual syllabus codes, the tier rules and the grade ranges attached to them, how to read a Dubai IGCSE report across two different grading scales, how practical science is handled when tuition is online, the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency rule including the thing a ranking competitor gets wrong, how many subjects it is sensible to fund at once, and the limits of what we will claim.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.programmesIntro: An IGCSE family in this corridor is making decisions at four points, and at each one the board and tier question returns. These are the four, with what the local school pattern means for each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Syllabus codes a parent can look up: 0580 Mathematics, 0607 International Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language. Mathematics and the separate sciences run Core and Extended routes with different grade ranges. Sciences add either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A City Walk parent should get the zone-correct timetable from the school rather than from any website, including this one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes include 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4MB1 Mathematics B, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4SD0 Science Double Award, 4EA1 English Language A, 4ET1 English Literature. Mathematics A runs Foundation and Higher tiers. Practical skills in the sciences are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into locally
programmes.description: Most schools in this corridor split at sixteen into A Levels or the IB Diploma. Extended or Higher tier content is what both routes assume: the algebra, the graph work and the quantitative science all reappear immediately and are not retaught. A Core or Foundation background is workable for some routes and a genuine obstacle for others, which makes tier placement a decision with a two-year shadow.
programmes.countryNote: One IB continuum school sits in Al Safa within a short drive of City Walk, with others in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, and the British-curriculum campuses nearby run A Levels. Families here therefore have both routes inside the same commute, which makes the Year 11 decision real rather than nominal and makes mathematics tier the single most consequential IGCSE choice.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: The federal process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate for use in the UAE. For the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Equivalency is a process families complete through the official channel; IB Gram neither performs it nor guarantees any outcome in it, and no tutoring is required for it.

subjects.description: The subject where tier matters most. Cambridge Core candidates sit papers 1 and 3 and are eligible for a restricted grade range; Extended candidates sit papers 2 and 4 for the full range. Pearson Mathematics A splits Foundation and Higher with the same effect. Algebraic fluency is the single best predictor of what comes next at sixteen.

subjects.name: International Mathematics
subjects.description: A separate Cambridge syllabus, often used by IB continuum schools because it includes a graphing-calculator paper and an investigation. Confusing it with 0580 is a common and expensive error: the papers, the calculator policy and the assessment style differ, and a tutor prepared for one is not prepared for the other.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit theory papers plus either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson candidates sit two written papers with practical skills examined inside them. Electricity and the wave vocabulary are where marks go in both. The practical arrangement is the first thing a tutor needs to know.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, bonding, rates and organic nomenclature, with the same practical distinction between the boards. The quantitative chain, moles into concentration into titration into yield, is where a student cannot locate their own weak link, and it is the clearest case for paid one-to-one time in either syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy recall, precise terminology and a surprising amount of data interpretation. The highest-yield work is command-term discipline: a student who answers 'describe' when the paper asks 'explain' loses marks on every paper regardless of how much content they have learned. Diagram labelling conventions differ slightly between boards.

subjects.name: Combined and double-award science
subjects.description: The route for students taking science as one or two subjects rather than three. Content is reduced rather than easier, and the decision matters for sixth-form entry: some A Level and Diploma science courses expect separate sciences. Worth checking against the school's own published entry requirements before accepting the default.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: First Language English and English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different expectations, and schools in this corridor enter students for both depending on background. Literature is a separate entry at Pearson. The marks move fastest on structure and on answering the question asked, not on vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business, Economics and ICT
subjects.description: Popular option choices in this corridor. All three reward case-study discipline and application of terminology to the specific scenario, which is a teachable technique rather than a content problem. ICT and computer science are distinct syllabuses and students sometimes do not realise which they are entered for.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: KHDA requirement · all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum is licensed, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. They sit alongside the IGCSE programme, occupy real timetable time, and are explicitly excluded from the five subjects the Ministry of Education counts for equivalency, which surprises a great many families.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.regionsTitle: City Walk and the districts whose schools set the board
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.regionsIntro: For an IGCSE family the relevant difference between neighbouring districts is not the tutor supply, it is which schools are in them and therefore which boards and tiers your child will meet. These are the areas and what each one tends to mean.

regions.name: City Walk
regions.note: No secondary campus inside the district, so the board depends entirely on which school the family chose. Every IGCSE student here commutes, most often west into Al Safa and Jumeirah. The short internal distances make a 17:00 session feasible once the return journey is accounted for.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Villas along Al Wasl Road with the shortest run to the Al Safa school cluster. Families here and in City Walk frequently attend the same schools and therefore sit the same syllabus codes, which is why the two districts behave identically for tutoring purposes.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The densest school cluster in this corridor, with British-curriculum campuses and one IB continuum school side by side. Both major boards are represented across these schools, so two neighbours in Al Safa can have children on different syllabus codes in the same subject.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Long-established British-curriculum provision close to the coast. Several of these schools have run the same board for many years, which makes the syllabus codes easy to establish and the tier conventions well understood by parents already in the community.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Mostly residential with primary provision nearby and secondary a slightly longer run. Families here are typically travelling into the Al Safa or Umm Suqeim clusters, so the board question is settled by the destination rather than by the home address.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Two substantial campuses including an IB continuum school, which is where Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 most often appears rather than 0580. A City Walk student travelling here daily faces the longest afternoon return in this group, pushing weekday sessions to 17:30.

regions.name: La Mer and Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Coastal and residential with no secondary schools of their own. The pattern matches City Walk exactly: commute out, board determined by the school, and evening session slots contested with three neighbouring districts at once.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: North across Al Wasl Road, dense and without secondary provision. Included because City Walk families search it alongside their own district; for IGCSE purposes it adds no schools and therefore no new board or tier combinations.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa and Al Wasl campuses, the shortest commute from City Walk
schoolClusters.note: Both major examination boards appear across this cluster, and some schools split boards by subject. Establish the syllabus code and the tier from the school's own option documentation before hiring anybody, and confirm the examination zone for the timetable.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Al Safa

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha campuses
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, where IB continuum schools sit alongside British-curriculum ones. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is more likely here than in the British-only campuses, and the distinction between 0607 and 0580 matters a great deal to a tutor.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home-tutor search in City Walk is really deciding
paragraphs: Parents in this corridor type this phrase for an understandable reason: in most places they have lived, tutoring arrives at the door. The question underneath it is narrower and more answerable, which is whether anybody can prepare their child for the specific papers their school has entered them for. Those are different questions, and separating them changes what a family should spend money on. The second question has a precise answer and it starts with four pieces of information the school holds.

Those four are the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the optional papers. A Year 10 chemistry student might be a Cambridge 0620 Extended candidate sitting the alternative-to-practical paper, or a Pearson 4CH1 candidate with practical skills assessed inside the written papers. Both are called IGCSE chemistry. Almost nothing else about them is the same from a tutor's point of view: the papers differ, the mark schemes differ, the practical arrangements differ, and the past-paper library a tutor should be working from differs entirely. A family that hires on proximity and discovers this in February has paid for the wrong preparation.

The third thing worth separating out is how many subjects to fund. An IGCSE candidate typically takes eight to ten, which makes blanket tutoring unaffordable and unnecessary. The useful approach is triage: establish from marked work which two or three subjects are genuinely at risk, which are safe, and which need timed practice rather than teaching. That decision saves more money than any rate negotiation, and it is the subject of its own section further down. Everything on this page is written to make those three decisions concrete rather than to persuade anyone of anything.
bullets: Four facts first: board, syllabus code, tier, optional papers
The school's option documentation holds all four

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, with the codes attached
paragraphs: Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the entire seven-page area cluster researched for this project, which is a remarkable omission given that the code is the first thing a tutor needs. The table below sets out the pairs a City Walk family is most likely to meet, with what differs for tutoring purposes. Read the last column first: that is where the money and the preparation time actually go.

Two differences matter more than the rest. The first is the practical arrangement in the sciences. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper in addition to the theory papers, and that component has its own skills: apparatus diagrams, tabulation conventions, reading scales to the right precision, plotting, and the specific language the mark scheme rewards for a conclusion. Pearson International GCSE candidates do not sit a separate practical component; those skills are examined inside the written papers, which changes how they should be practised but not whether they should be.

The second is mathematics. Cambridge runs two separate mathematics syllabuses, 0580 Mathematics and 0607 International Mathematics, and they are not interchangeable. International Mathematics includes a graphing-calculator paper and an investigation, and it appears most often at IB continuum schools, several of which are within a short drive of City Walk. Pearson runs Mathematics A, code 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers, and Mathematics B as a separate specification. A family that tells a tutor 'IGCSE maths' and nothing more has given them a one-in-three chance of preparing the right papers.

sections.heading: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher: what the tier actually decides
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential thing on a Year 10 option form and the least explained. In Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences, candidates follow either the Core route or the Extended route, and the route determines which papers they sit and which grades they are eligible to be awarded. Core candidates cannot reach the top grades however well they perform; Extended candidates can, and will meet content that a Core candidate never sees. Pearson Mathematics A works the same way through Foundation and Higher tiers.

The practical consequence for a family is twofold. A student placed on the lower route who is capable of the higher one has a ceiling imposed on them that will matter at sixteen, because both A Level and IB Diploma science and mathematics courses assume higher-tier content and do not reteach it. A student placed on the higher route who is not ready loses marks across papers designed to stretch the top of the cohort, and often ends with a lower grade than the lower route would have produced. Neither error is the school acting carelessly; both come from evidence that was thin at the time the decision was made.

What a parent can do is specific. Find out which tier your child is on, ask what evidence the placement was based on, and ask when and whether it can be revisited, because entry deadlines sit well before the examinations and the window is finite. Then make sure any tutoring is aimed at the right route: an Extended candidate drilled on Core content is wasting the hour, and a Core candidate taught Extended material is being demoralised for no mark. The table sets out the comparison in the terms that matter for planning.

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai IGCSE report across two grading scales
paragraphs: Parents in this corridor compare notes constantly and the comparison breaks down because the scales differ. Pearson International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 numeric scale. Cambridge reports on an A* to G scale for many syllabuses and on a 9 to 1 scale for others depending on the syllabus and the region of entry. Two children at neighbouring schools can come home with a 7 and a B and nobody can say which is stronger without knowing the board and the syllabus. The first question for any Dubai IGCSE report is therefore which scale it is on.

The second question is what the number or letter is actually reporting. A school report in Year 10 is usually a working-at or predicted grade generated from internal assessments, not an examination grade, and the two are produced in different conditions. Internal assessments are often open-book, sat in a classroom, and marked by the class teacher against a mark scheme they also taught from. A terminal examination is none of those. A student who holds a comfortable internal grade and drops two grades in a mock has usually met the terminal conditions for the first time rather than declined.

The third question is the one worth asking at the next parents' evening, and it is more useful than asking how the child is doing. Ask the subject teacher which paper the child would currently lose most marks on and what the specific loss is: content not covered, technique, timing, or precision of language. Teachers can answer that because they mark the scripts. The answer converts a grade into a target a weekly session can be built around, and it also reveals when the answer is that nothing needs buying because the student simply needs to sit more papers under time.
bullets: Establish the scale before comparing anything with a neighbour

sections.heading: How science practicals are handled when tuition is online
paragraphs: This is the question every science family asks and it has a precise answer that depends on the board. The practical work itself happens at school, in the school laboratory, with the school's apparatus and under the school's supervision. No tutoring arrangement, in-home or online, changes that or should attempt to. What tutoring prepares is the assessment of practical skills, and that assessment is a written exercise in both boards even where it is called a practical test.

For Cambridge candidates, the school enters either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, and the family should find out which. Both reward a tightly defined set of skills: drawing apparatus conventionally, tabulating results with consistent precision and correct headings, reading scales to the appropriate number of figures, plotting points accurately and drawing a line of best fit that respects the data, identifying the dependent and control variables correctly, and writing a conclusion in the language the mark scheme rewards. Every one of those is taught better on a shared screen with the student's own attempt visible than it is standing next to them, because the annotation is permanent and can be revisited.

For Pearson International GCSE candidates there is no separate practical component. Practical skills are assessed within the written papers, which means the same tabulation, plotting and evaluation work is required and arrives embedded in theory questions. Students frequently miss these marks because nobody told them this part of the paper existed as a distinct skill. The preparation is identical in substance and differs only in where it lands, which is a good illustration of why the board question has to be settled before any teaching is planned.
bullets: Practical work happens at school; tutoring prepares the assessment of it
Cambridge: either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper
Pearson International GCSE: practical skills examined inside the written papers

sections.heading: The five-subject equivalency rule, and the error a ranking page makes
paragraphs: Equivalency is the federal process by which a foreign secondary certificate is recognised for use in the UAE, and it is absent from four of the ten query clusters researched for this project. For the British track the published requirement is specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Two details matter and both are commonly got wrong. First, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count, which surprises families whose children take both as KHDA requires. Second, one competitor ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. That is not what the published rule says, and inheriting the error would be worse than saying nothing. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is no figure published here, deliberately. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on the Ministry of Education's own site or on an emirate attestation authority's page, so none appears on this page. Families on an IB route should verify directly rather than trusting a number from any tutoring website. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, does not guarantee any outcome in it, and does not suggest that tutoring is required for it; it is a regulatory process and implying otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about something a family handles through the official channel.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects to fund, and what a parent can check themselves
paragraphs: Here is a figure a City Walk parent can verify without trusting anybody: open the school's option booklet and count the subjects. Eight to ten is normal in this corridor. Now take the published Dubai market band for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 150 to 300 an hour, and multiply by one weekly hour in each subject across a thirty-six week year. The result is a number no household should be paying, and the arithmetic is the point. Any provider recommending support across more than three subjects simultaneously is selling hours rather than solving a problem.

The alternative is triage, and it is cheap. One diagnostic session per candidate subject, using the student's own marked work, establishes three categories: subjects genuinely at risk where teaching is needed, subjects where the student knows the content and needs timed papers and a mark scheme, and subjects that are fine and should be left alone. Most IGCSE students in this corridor turn out to need teaching in two subjects, timed practice in three, and nothing at all in the rest. A family that funds two weekly sessions instead of eight is spending within the AED 600 to 1,200 monthly mid-market band rather than several multiples of it.

The rest of the published market is worth knowing so that the triage decision is made with the numbers in view. Budget online provision, generally university students, is advertised from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist tutors occupy AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Those are other companies' published prices, named and dated; IB Gram quotes its own rate in writing before anything is booked.

sections.heading: Online delivery, and the claims this page will not make
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own script, the correct board's past paper and the published mark scheme on screen together. Nobody is sent to a City Walk address: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service that exists only in India. The practical argument has already been made with the published numbers, and there is one more worth adding for an IGCSE family specifically. A student taking eight subjects across two boards may need three different specialists in a single term, and assembling three people who will each drive to Al Wasl Road on a different evening is a logistical problem that online delivery simply does not have.

On regulation the position is short and factual. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts has been published, none is quoted here. Ask any tutor to show the permit. Separately, do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school; the permit carries a code of conduct and ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar it in Abu Dhabi.

What this page declines to claim: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB organisation, and nothing here should be read as implying any of it. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not supply, reproduce or host syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and no statistic appears here without its source and date. The examination timetable your child works from should come from the school and the board's official PDF for the correct administrative zone, never from a tutoring site.

process.title: Send the four facts from the school
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and any optional papers, for each subject you are considering. They are in the school's option documentation or available from the head of year in a single email. Without them a tutor is guessing, and a tutor guessing about which board will prepare the wrong paper very competently.

process.title: Triage before you fund anything
process.description: One diagnostic session per candidate subject, using the student's own marked work rather than predicted grades. The output is a ranked list in three categories: teaching needed, timed practice needed, leave alone. Most Year 11 candidates in this corridor need teaching in two subjects and nothing in the rest.

process.title: A free 55-minute lesson in the subject that ranked first
process.description: No charge, no card details taken. The tutor works from a past paper from the correct board and series and watches the working rather than the answers, then writes a short note classifying the problem and saying what a term of weekly sessions would realistically change.

process.title: A written rate and a session plan tied to the specification
process.description: The rate per session in writing before anything is booked, with the plan referenced to the specification's own content list so you can see what is being covered and what is not. No bundles bought in advance and no discount conditional on committing to a term.

process.title: Re-triage after the mock, and stop subjects that are done
process.description: The mock is the honest checkpoint. Each funded subject is reassessed: continue, move to timed practice only, or stop. A plan where one subject drops out in February because it no longer needs paying for is the intended outcome, not a lost customer.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the seven-page area cluster researched for this project. A tutor working on 0580 when the school entered 0607, or on Cambridge practical papers when the board is Pearson, is preparing the wrong examination. We establish the code and the tier before the first session rather than after the first mock.

whyPoints.title: Advice about how little to buy
whyPoints.description: This page does the arithmetic on funding eight subjects and tells you not to. Triage from marked work usually produces two subjects that need teaching, three that need timed papers and a mark scheme, and the rest left alone. That recommendation makes a smaller sale, which is why most pages in this market do not make it.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation parents are not having
whyPoints.description: Core against Extended and Foundation against Higher decides the grade range available and casts a shadow over sixth-form options. We set out what to ask the school, what evidence the placement rests on and when the window to revisit it closes, because a tutor cannot fix a ceiling that was set on the option form.

whyPoints.title: Practical assessment handled board by board
whyPoints.description: Cambridge candidates sit a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson International GCSE candidates have those skills examined inside the written papers. Tabulation, plotting, precision and conclusion language are taught explicitly either way, on a shared screen where the annotation on the student's own attempt stays visible.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated correctly, with the source
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A ranking competitor publishes six subjects. We publish the sourced rule, say where to verify it, and make clear that no tutoring is required for a regulatory process.

whyPoints.title: Timetables from the board, never from us
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version of the timetable. We will tell you that the zone matters and point you to the school and the official PDF rather than restating dates that can be revised.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board does my child's school in this corridor actually use?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it varies between campuses a few minutes apart and some schools split boards by subject. The answer sits in the Year 9 or Year 10 option documentation and the head of year can confirm it in one email. You want four things: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and any optional papers. A Cambridge 0620 Extended chemistry candidate sitting the alternative-to-practical paper and a Pearson 4CH1 candidate are both doing 'IGCSE chemistry' and need materially different preparation, so this is the first question rather than a detail.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE treated as equivalent in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Both are internationally recognised qualifications and both appear across Dubai's private schools, so for school progression and for the Ministry of Education's five-subject count the distinction is not usually the issue. Where the difference bites is in preparation. The syllabus codes, paper structures, tiering arrangements and, in the sciences, the practical assessment are different. A tutor needs to know which one; a university or a school admissions office generally does not. Check any specific entry requirement against the institution's own published list rather than assuming interchangeability.

faqs.question: Core or Extended: which route is my child on, and can it still change?
faqs.answer: They are two routes through the same syllabus. Core candidates sit the core pair of written papers and cover a reduced content list; Extended candidates sit the extended pair, meet the stretch topics and are eligible for a wider grade range, including the top grades that Core candidates cannot be awarded. The choice is a school decision made on evidence before the entry deadline, and it can sometimes be revisited within that window. It matters beyond sixteen, because A Level and IB Diploma courses in mathematics and the sciences assume the extended content.

faqs.question: If my child is on Foundation tier mathematics, what grade can they be awarded?
faqs.answer: A restricted range: Foundation tier in Pearson Mathematics A does not give access to the top grades, and the same principle applies to the Cambridge Core route. That is the point of tiering, and it is not a judgement about the child so much as a prediction made from the evidence available when the entry was decided. If the prediction now looks wrong, the conversation to have with the school is about evidence and about the entry deadline, which sits well before the examinations. A tutor cannot lift a ceiling that was set on an entry form.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if our tuition is online?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens at school with the school's apparatus, and no tutoring arrangement changes that. What is assessed, and what tutoring prepares, is written: Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and Pearson International GCSE candidates have practical skills examined inside their written papers. The skills are the same either way: conventional apparatus diagrams, consistent tabulation, reading scales to the right precision, accurate plotting, correct variable identification and conclusions phrased as the mark scheme rewards. All of that teaches well on a shared screen with the student's own attempt annotated.

faqs.question: For equivalency, how many IGCSE passes does a City Walk student need?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submits proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor ranking for these searches states six, which does not match the published rule. Verify against the Ministry's own guidance and the emirate attestation authority before acting, because this is a regulatory process rather than an academic one.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education included in the five required subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published guidance states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. This surprises many families, because both are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and occupy real timetable time. The practical implication is that a student needs five qualifying subjects outside those two, which is worth checking against the option choices in Year 9 rather than discovering at the end of Year 11. Confirm the current position through the official channel, since requirements are set by the Ministry and can be updated.

faqs.question: When do students in Dubai actually sit their IGCSE examinations?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable, so take the dates from the school and the official board PDF.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE in November without repeating the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, both boards run a November series alongside the June one, which is the normal route for a targeted resit. The decisions that matter are made with the school: whether the school will enter the candidate for that series, which subjects are worth resitting, and what the entry deadline is, because it sits well before the examination window. Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 with results in January. A resit works best as a short focused block on the specific papers rather than as a repeat of the whole course.

faqs.question: Is the 9 to 1 scale or the A* to G scale used for IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Both appear, which is why comparing grades with a neighbour so often produces confusion. Pearson International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 numeric scale. Cambridge reports on an A* to G scale for many syllabuses and on a 9 to 1 scale for others, depending on the syllabus and the region of entry. Establish which scale your child's certificate will use before interpreting anything, and bear in mind that a Year 10 school report is usually a working-at grade produced under classroom conditions rather than an examination grade produced under terminal ones.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects is it sensible to fund tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: Two, in most cases. An IGCSE candidate takes eight to ten subjects, and funding a weekly hour in each at the published Dubai band of AED 150 to 300 produces a figure no household should be paying. Triage from the student's own marked work usually yields two subjects that genuinely need teaching, three that need timed papers and a mark scheme, and the rest that should be left alone. Three funded subjects is defensible for a short block in an exam year. Four or more almost always means the triage has not been done.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do families in this corridor most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a long way, and specifically the algebraic fluency that both tiers assume and that nothing in the curriculum explicitly drills. Then chemistry, where the quantitative chain from moles to concentration to titration arithmetic breaks in a place students cannot locate themselves. Physics follows, usually on electricity and the wave vocabulary. English Language is requested often and benefits least from content teaching and most from structure and answering the question asked. Biology is a recall-volume problem that responds to a timetable rather than to a tutor in many cases.

faqs.question: Can my child take different IGCSE subjects with different examination boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this corridor it is common: a school may enter mathematics with one board and the sciences with another, and a student moving schools mid-course can end up with a genuinely mixed set. It creates no problem for the certificate or for the Ministry of Education's five-subject count, but it creates work for a family hiring help, because each subject needs its own board, code, tier and practical arrangement established. Keep a single list of all four facts per subject; it is the document that makes every subsequent tutoring conversation efficient.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures, named and dated: Unitors advertises IGCSE from AED 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to 300, specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650, and budget online provision from university students is advertised at AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. IB Gram does not sell UAE home visits and quotes its own rate in writing before anything is booked.

faqs.question: Should we start IGCSE support in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if there is a known weakness, and the reason is tiering rather than content. Tier placement decisions and entry deadlines sit before the examinations, and the evidence a school uses comes largely from Year 10 work. A student who closes an algebra gap in Year 10 may be placed on the higher route; the same student discovered in Year 11 may not be, and that ceiling then follows them into sixth form. Where there is no known weakness, waiting is reasonable: start with one diagnostic session rather than a term of lessons bought on anxiety.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.closingHeading: Start with the four facts, then the triage
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-city-walk.closingBody: Send the board, syllabus code, tier and optional papers for each subject you are worried about, along with the school, the year group and two evening windows that survive the return journey from Al Safa, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim. We will run one diagnostic session per candidate subject from the student's own marked work and give you a ranked list in three categories: teaching needed, timed practice needed, leave alone. The first 55-minute lesson carries no charge and takes no card details. If the honest result is that one subject needs a tutor and the rest need a timer and the right mark scheme, that is what the written note will say.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-culture-villag.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE for families in Culture Village: matched to the specification and tier, working from the school's own exam timetable, and available in the early evening window a Creek-side commute allows.

intro.heading: The calendar does more work than the hours do
paragraphs: An IGCSE course is two years long and the useful decisions in it are nearly all about timing. The content is fixed. The papers happen when the board says. What a family in Culture Village controls is when work happens relative to those dates, and that turns out to matter more than how many hours are bought, because the same hour has very different value in October of Year 10 and in April of Year 11.

Start with the fact most families discover late: entry deadlines sit months in front of the papers. The school's exam office makes the entries, within the board's window, and once they are made the board, the tier and the subject list are settled. A conversation about tier in the autumn term can change an outcome. The same conversation in the spring cannot, because the entry has gone. That single piece of sequencing is worth more than a term of tuition and costs an email to the exam office.

The second is mock season, which is widely misread. Families treat a mock as a rehearsal, and schools use it as evidence: for tier decisions, for setting, for predicted grades where those apply, and for identifying who needs intervention. A student who treats a December mock as practice has misunderstood what the school is doing with the result. The useful move is to prepare for the mock as though it counted, because in several practical respects it does.

The third is the eight to twelve weeks before a series, which has a specific weekly shape that almost nobody plans. It is not a syllabus review. It is a diagnostic cycle: sit a timed paper, mark it against the published scheme, work only on what the marking exposed, repeat. A topic list produced that way gets shorter each week. A list copied from the syllabus contents page stays the same length until the exam, and the student can feel the difference.

On the home-tutoring question, stated plainly. Home tuition exists in Dubai at published in-home rates of AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India.

One correction to make early, because it is a date a family would act on. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Several pages written for Gulf parents quote a February or March window with an Indian entry deadline, and a Culture Village family planning revision towards it would lose a term to an exam their school cannot enter them for.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-culture-villag.programmesIntro: Culture Village families need IGCSE support at three points in the two-year calendar, and the right work differs completely at each. These are the routes we cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course assessed by written papers at the end, entered at Core or Extended in many subjects, with Core capped below the top grades. Codes identify the content: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500 or 0990, Additional Mathematics 0606.
programmes.countryNote: The calendar detail that catches Culture Village families out is zoning. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two pupils from the same tower at different schools can therefore sit the same paper at different local times. Use the timetable the school issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher in mathematics, with Specification A coded 4MA1 and sciences coded 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Science practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published dates make the calendar concrete. International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so we plan from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: The options year
programmes.description: The year before IGCSE begins, when subjects and sometimes tiers are chosen. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October where a school uses them. The work that pays off is algebraic fluency, the habit of writing method, and enough subject vocabulary to read a question stem once.
programmes.countryNote: For a Culture Village family this is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to intervene, and the one most often skipped. A fluency gap addressed in Year 9 is a few weeks of work. The same gap in Year 11, competing with eight or nine subjects and a series approaching, is a different and more expensive problem, and it arrives at the point when specialist availability across Dubai is thinnest.

programmes.name: The November series
programmes.description: Both boards offer a November series available to UAE candidates, functioning as the standard retake route. The entry is made through the school's exam office shortly after June results and the results arrive in the new year.
programmes.countryNote: The calendar consequence is specific and often missed: a November entry means the autumn term carries both resit preparation and, for a student who has moved into a post-16 course, the opening weeks of A Level or the IB Diploma. Those compete for the same evenings. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the decision that follows also arrives mid-year rather than in August.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-culture-villag.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Culture Village families ask for, each with a note on where in the two-year calendar support makes the most difference.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject and the one where early support pays best, because algebraic fluency compounds. A gap in Year 10 widens through Year 11; the same gap addressed in the autumn of Year 10 is a few weeks of work rather than a term of it.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics, electricity, waves and atomic physics. Benefits most from the final eight-week diagnostic cycle, because the losses are unit conversion and command-term errors that a marked timed paper exposes immediately.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, electrochemistry and organic chemistry. Moles arithmetic needs to be secure before the final term, so this is a subject where mid-Year-11 work beats pre-series work.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Wide content, precise marking on named structures and processes. The subject that responds best to the last eight weeks, because recall discipline improves quickly under a repeated timed-paper cycle.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Two or three sciences in a smaller award. Revision must rotate across the sciences rather than block, which makes the weekly structure of the final term unusually important for this award.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and composition. Improvements here are slow and steady rather than sudden, so support belongs across Year 10 and the first half of Year 11 rather than in the final eight weeks.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0993)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an optional speaking endorsement. Vocabulary range is scored and builds over months, so this is another subject where early and steady beats intensive and late.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Data response and case-study application. Both respond quickly to technique work, so the final eight weeks are genuinely productive here: anchoring an answer to the named firm in the stem is a fast, teachable shift.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, binomial expansion and advanced trigonometry alongside 0580. Needs support from the start of the course rather than at the end, because it has no lower tier and schools frequently teach it in less time than the content warrants.

sections.heading: The two IGCSE years, term by term
paragraphs: Here is the course written as a calendar rather than a syllabus, because the calendar is what decides whether an hour is well spent. The structure is stable across schools even where the dates differ, and the terms have genuinely different characters: Year 10 is about building, the first half of Year 11 is about consolidating, and the final stretch is about claiming marks that are already within reach.

The pattern most Culture Village families follow is the reverse of the useful one. Nothing is bought in Year 10 because nothing seems wrong. Something is bought in the spring of Year 11 because a mock came back badly. The expensive intervention happens at the point of least available time and highest market demand. The cheap intervention, in Year 10, was available when nobody was looking for it.

Two specific sequencing points. The entry deadline sits months in front of the papers, so any conversation about tier or subject list has to happen before it. And the mock, which in most schools falls in the term before the live series, is treated by the school as evidence for tier decisions, setting and intervention. Preparing for the mock therefore changes decisions, while treating it as a rehearsal lets those decisions be made on a worse sample of the student's ability.

Where a date is given it is a published, backward-looking one that can be checked; where the date is school-set it says so, because the school's exam office is the only authority on it and a page guessing at it would be worse than useless.

sections.heading: The eight-week block, week by week
paragraphs: The final stretch is where most tutoring money in this market is spent and where it is most often spent badly, because it gets bought as a revision course. A revision course works through the syllabus. That is the wrong instrument eight weeks out, because the student has already met the syllabus and what they have not done is find out which parts of it they cannot yet do under timed conditions.

The right instrument is a cycle. Week one: sit a full timed paper on the exact board, code and tier, and mark it question by question against the published scheme. The marking produces a topic list, ranked by marks lost. Weeks two and three: work only on the top of that list, with the student writing full method. Week four: sit another paper. The list should now be shorter. Repeat the cycle. If the list is not shortening, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than the hours increasing.

The weekly shape matters for a Culture Village household because of the commute. A full timed paper needs an uninterrupted stretch, which a weekday evening after a Nad Al Sheba run does not provide. So the paper goes to a weekend morning and the weekday sessions carry the targeted work and the technique drill. Families that try to fit papers into weekday evenings end up with papers sat under conditions that teach nothing about timing.

The table below sets out the cycle. It is deliberately a cycle rather than a linear plan, because the number of iterations depends on how much the list shortens and the whole point is that the plan responds to evidence rather than running to completion regardless.

sections.heading: Entries, tiers and the conversation that has to happen first
paragraphs: Entries are made by the school's exam office, within the board's window, months before the papers. They fix the board, the subject list and, where a subject is tiered, the tier. After that point, the questions a parent might want to raise have no practical effect, which makes the autumn term of Year 11 a genuine deadline rather than a soft one.

Tier is the consequential part. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation both carry a grade ceiling that performance cannot exceed. Extended and Higher carry the full range with harder content. Schools decide on Year 10 evidence, and a family who does not ask will usually learn the decision afterwards. If post-16 plans involve A Level Mathematics, Physics or Economics, or an IB Higher Level science, the ceiling matters, because those courses assume the higher-tier content.

The window where support genuinely changes a tier decision is narrow and specific: between the provisional decision and the final entry. A borderline student who gets focused work on the exact topics the department doubts can move the decision. A student who gets generalised extra maths or extra science usually does not, because the department is watching particular evidence rather than general effort. So the useful question to the department is not whether they will reconsider but what evidence would change their mind.

One more entry-related point worth making on a Culture Village page. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable each, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two pupils in the same building at different schools can sit the same paper at different local times. Print the timetable the school issues and give the tutor the same copy.

sections.heading: Mock season, and what schools actually do with it
paragraphs: Mock examinations are widely described to students as practice, and that description is incomplete enough to be misleading. Schools use mock results for several real decisions: tier confirmation where an entry has not closed, setting and grouping, identifying who needs intervention, and in some schools informing predicted or reference grades for post-16 applications. A student who approaches the mock casually is handing the school a worse sample of their ability than they need to.

The practical consequence for a Culture Village family is that the four to six weeks before the mock are a better time to buy support than the four to six weeks after it. Buying afterwards is reactive and treats the mock as a diagnostic. Buying before uses the mock as both diagnostic and decision point, which is two outcomes from the same hours. The difference is purely sequencing and it costs nothing to get right.

Preparing for a mock well is also a rehearsal of the pre-series cycle in miniature. Sit one timed paper, mark it against the published scheme, work on what the marking exposed, and drill the timing. If that process produces a better mock result, the family has also learned that the process works, which makes the final eight weeks easier to commit to. If it does not, there is still a term in hand to change the approach.

The reverse case is worth naming. A mock result that is better than expected is also information, and it should reduce spending rather than maintain it. A student who has demonstrated they can do the paper under timed conditions needs maintenance rather than intervention, and continuing an intensive arrangement at that point is buying reassurance. We will say so, which is less revenue and the only honest reading of the evidence.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Culture Village, and the calendar case against it
paragraphs: The price case is straightforward and published. In-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, with monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 799 a month for eight online sessions appears in the market. All of those belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026.

The calendar case is less often made and matters more here. IGCSE cohorts across Dubai move through the year together, so mock season arrives everywhere at once and the final eight weeks arrive everywhere at once. In those windows, demand for subject specialists peaks simultaneously and a tutor bounded by driving distance from Jaddaf Waterfront is both least likely to have a free slot and hardest to replace. Replacement inside the same week requires a pool that is not geographic.

There is a second calendar problem specific to visiting arrangements. A full timed paper needs an uninterrupted stretch, and a visiting tutor charging by the hour with a next appointment to reach cannot easily supervise one. In practice the papers get sat at home unsupervised, which is fine for content and useless for timing discipline, which is the thing the paper was supposed to test. A weekend online session can run the paper properly because nobody is travelling.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village or anywhere else in the UAE; tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. There are cases where a visiting tutor is the right purchase, mostly younger or easily distracted students needing an adult present. A Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a series is not one of them.

sections.heading: Results day, and the decision made before it
paragraphs: Results arrive on a known date and the decision that follows should be made before it, not on the morning. Pearson's published dates make the shape clear: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November route is therefore a mid-year decision rather than an August one, which matters where a sixth-form or university conversation depends on it.

The rule to set in advance is simple to state and rarely written down. For each subject, what result would trigger a resit, and what result would not. Agreeing that in the spring means August produces an action rather than a week of uncertainty, and it lets the autumn block be booked while slots still exist. It also prevents the opposite error, which is resitting a grade that was already sufficient for where the student is actually going.

The November entry carries a calendar collision worth planning for. The autumn term after a June series contains both resit preparation and, for a student who has moved on, the opening weeks of A Level or the IB Diploma. Those compete for the same evenings and the post-16 course has the longer consequences. A resit plan that ignores this buys hours into a week with no room for them, and the usual outcome is that both suffer.

One last piece of the calendar: enquiries about results and remarks have their own deadlines, set by the board and administered through the school's exam office. If a grade looks inconsistent with the student's own evidence, that is the route, and it is time-limited. It is worth knowing the deadline exists before results day rather than discovering it afterwards, because the window is short and the school handles the submission.

paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff that we do not hold, because we have no UAE premises.

Tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

A boundary that matters during mock and pre-series season specifically. A Culture Village parent may be offered their child's own subject teacher privately, and the pressure to accept rises as a series approaches. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person setting and marking the mock should not be separately paid by one family in the class.

On materials, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. We reference and link them from the boards' own sites rather than reproducing or supplying them as downloads, and in sessions we show a student where to find the current document themselves. That also means they can check a claim a tutor has made, including one of ours.

sections.heading: Getting started, with dates rather than hours
paragraphs: Three emails do most of the work and none of them costs anything. Ask the exam office for the board, the specification code and the tier your child is entered for, plus the school's own issued exam timetable. Ask the subject department when the mock falls and what evidence would change a tier decision. Ask the school for the term calendar so the crowded weeks are visible before they arrive.

Then send us the board, the code, the tier, the series and two evening windows that genuinely work from Culture Village after the school run. If a weekend morning is available, say so, because full timed papers belong there and the pre-series cycle depends on them. We match a specification specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, with one trial per student, nothing charged beforehand and no card details needed.

If no specialist is free we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing a general tutor against a specification. Scarcity concentrates in Additional Mathematics 0606, in Pearson Specification B, and in mock season and the final eight weeks when every Dubai cohort reaches the same point at once. Booking before the cluster costs exactly the same and secures a better match.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; on the British track the sourced rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Verify your own case with the Ministry.
