faqs.question: When should a Culture Village family start IGCSE tutoring in the two-year course?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if there is a genuine gap, and that is the window families skip because nothing yet looks wrong. A fluency gap addressed in the autumn of Year 10 is a few weeks of work; the same gap in the spring of Year 11 competes with eight or nine subjects and a series approaching, and arrives when specialist availability across Dubai is thinnest. The pattern most families follow buys nothing early and everything late, which is the reverse of the useful order.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the papers are IGCSE entries actually made?
faqs.answer: Months ahead, by the school's exam office within the board's window, and once made they fix the board, the subject list and the tier. That makes the autumn term of Year 11 a real deadline for any conversation about tier or subject choice rather than a soft one. Ask the exam office for the board, the specification code and the tier your child is entered for, and ask before the window closes rather than after a mock result prompts the question.

faqs.question: What do schools actually do with IGCSE mock results?
faqs.answer: More than students are usually told. Mock results feed tier confirmation where an entry has not closed, setting and grouping decisions, identification of who needs intervention, and in some schools reference or predicted grades for post-16 applications. A student treating the mock as a rehearsal hands the school a worse sample of their ability than necessary. The practical consequence is that the four to six weeks before a mock are better value than the four to six weeks after it.

faqs.question: What should the final eight weeks before the series actually look like?
faqs.answer: A cycle rather than a revision course. Week one, a full timed paper on the exact board, code and tier, marked question by question against the published scheme, producing a topic list ranked by marks lost. Weeks two and three, work only on the top of that list with full written method. Week four, another paper, and the list should be shorter. Repeat. If the list is not shortening, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than the hours increasing.

faqs.question: Where in the week should a full timed paper be sat?
faqs.answer: A weekend morning, because it needs an uninterrupted stretch and real exam conditions. A weekday evening after a commute from Nad Al Sheba or Sobha Hartland cannot provide either, and a paper sat badly teaches nothing about timing, which is the thing it was meant to test. Keep weekday sessions for the targeted work and technique drill the marking produced. Culture Village's short runs to nearer schools make a 16:30 weekday slot realistic for that.

faqs.question: Can tutoring still change which tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Within a narrow window, yes. Between the department's provisional decision and the final entry, focused work on the exact Extended or Higher topics they doubt can move it. Generalised extra lessons usually cannot, because the department is watching particular evidence: algebraic fluency, confidence with harder geometry, and performance on the longer structured paper under timed conditions. So the useful question is what evidence would change their mind, rather than whether they will reconsider.

faqs.question: Should we be planning around a February or March exam series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Several pages written for Gulf parents quote a February or March window with an Indian entry deadline, and a Culture Village family planning a term of revision towards it would be preparing for an exam their school cannot enter them for. Treat that as a reason to check the provider's other claims.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results arrive, and does the November route change that?
faqs.answer: It changes it substantially. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. The November route lands much later: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a resit decision taken in August produces an outcome mid-year rather than before the new academic year begins, which matters where a sixth-form or university conversation depends on the grade. Plan the resit knowing when the answer actually arrives.

faqs.question: How do I decide in advance whether a resit is worth it?
faqs.answer: Set a rule per subject in the spring, before results. What grade would trigger a November entry and what grade would not, measured against the destination the student is actually heading to rather than against a general wish for a better number. That converts results day into an action, lets the autumn block be booked while slots exist, and prevents the common error of resitting a grade that was already sufficient for the course the student has accepted.

faqs.question: Does a November resit clash with starting A Level or the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Directly. The autumn term after a June series contains both resit preparation and the opening weeks of the post-16 course, and they compete for the same evenings. The post-16 course carries the longer consequences, so a resit plan that ignores the overlap buys hours into a week with no room for them and both tend to suffer. If both are unavoidable, fewer and better-placed sessions beat more of them, with the weekend used for the resit paper work.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our apartment in Culture Village during the final term?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not visit UAE addresses; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Agencies that do visit publish rates of AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home providers. In the final term there is also a practical issue: a visiting tutor with a next appointment cannot easily supervise a full timed paper.

faqs.question: Why does my child's exam timetable differ from a friend's at another school?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and it states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two pupils living in the same Culture Village tower at different schools can therefore sit the same paper at different local times. Print the timetable the school issues, give the tutor the same copy, and do not work from a general download.

faqs.question: Is a good mock result a reason to keep the tutoring going?
faqs.answer: Usually not at the same intensity, and we will say so. A student who has demonstrated they can complete the paper under timed conditions needs maintenance rather than intervention, and continuing an intensive arrangement at that point is buying reassurance. The honest read of good evidence is to reduce the commitment and keep a short check-in before the series. Spending that ignores good news is as wasteful as spending that ignores bad news, and it is far more common.

faqs.question: What can I ask for if a grade looks wrong after results?
faqs.answer: Enquiries about results and remarks have their own board-set deadlines, administered through the school's exam office rather than directly by a family. The window is short, so it is worth knowing it exists before results day rather than discovering it afterwards. If a grade looks inconsistent with the student's own marked papers and school evidence, that is the route to raise it. A tutoring provider cannot submit one and should not offer to.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and an inspection rating judges a school rather than any tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff, and we have no UAE premises, office or branch.

intro.heading: Three documents decide the grade
paragraphs: Almost every IGCSE family in DAMAC Hills owns a textbook and has never seen the three documents that actually determine the grade. The specification states what is on the course and how it is assessed. The mark scheme states what earns a mark. The examiner report states what candidates got wrong last time. All three are published by the board, all three are free, and between them they answer the question a textbook cannot: not what the subject contains, but what the paper pays for.

A tutor who works from those documents behaves differently from one who works through chapters. The session starts from a marked script and a mark scheme side by side, and the question is always the same — why was this mark withheld. Over a block that question produces a list of specific, repeated reasons, and the list is almost always shorter and more mechanical than a parent expects.

The difference between subjects is in what the paper rewards. English Language pays for form, audience and register as separate things from content, so a well-written text in the wrong form loses marks no amount of quality rescues. The humanities pay for named, dated, located examples, so a generally accurate answer about urbanisation scores a fraction of a specific one. The sciences pay for layout, terminology and causal chains in three different proportions. Mathematics pays for visible method.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In a community where secondary students travel out to school and return after five, a session that adds no journey for anybody and starts on the minute is the practical format rather than the compromise.

Matching by code matters more at IGCSE than families expect, because two schools a few minutes apart can enter the same subject with different boards. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 cover similar mathematics and ask for it differently. Cambridge 0500 and Pearson 4EA1 set different text types in directed writing. A tutor matched to the subject rather than the code teaches correct material against an unfamiliar paper.

The tier is the second administrative fact. Several Cambridge syllabuses split into Core and Extended, with different papers and a different range of grades available, and the school makes that entry. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however the revision goes, so the entry has to be known before any plan is made.

What follows is the subject detail: where to find the three documents and what each answers, then English, humanities, languages, sciences and mathematics in turn, then grade scales, rates and the resit question.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-damac-hills.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the code and the specific thing that paper rewards. The code sits on the school's subject information sheet and at the top of every past paper, and it is the first fact worth establishing.

subjects.name: English Language — Cambridge 0500 and 0990, Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: Reading response, summary and directed writing. Form, audience and register carry marks separately from content, so a strong article where a letter was specified loses marks that quality cannot recover. Summary is lost mainly to writing too much rather than too little.

subjects.name: English Literature — Cambridge 0475 and 0992
subjects.description: Set texts, passage-based questions and extended essays. Narrating the plot accurately scores a fraction of what analysing one quoted phrase for its effect does. The trade between coverage and depth is the whole technique and it is counter-intuitive to most students.

subjects.name: Geography — Cambridge 0460
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with a skills paper. Case studies must be named, dated and located to earn credit; a generally accurate answer about migration without a specific example scores poorly. Map and graph skills are reliable marks and routinely under-practised.

subjects.name: History — Cambridge 0470
subjects.description: Depth studies and source questions. Source work is a technique rather than a knowledge test: provenance, purpose and reliability discussed against the source's own content. Students who revise only content and never practise source questions lose a predictable block of marks.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics — Cambridge 0450 and 0455
subjects.description: Case-study papers requiring application to the stimulus. Definitions earn little; applied analysis and a supported judgement earn most. Economics diagrams lose marks for unlabelled axes and for being drawn and then never referred to in the written answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics — Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded separately from answers, so unwritten working forfeits them even when the final value is right. Premature rounding loses the accuracy mark. Both are mechanical and both repeat across every paper in the series.

subjects.name: Sciences — Cambridge 0610, 0620, 0625
subjects.description: Three subjects with three different causes of lost marks: biology to rejected near-synonyms, chemistry to calculation layout, physics to explanations written as formulae. A single science tutor across all three will be strong in one and adequate in two.

subjects.name: Arabic — Cambridge 0508 and 0544
subjects.description: Distinct syllabuses for first-language and foreign-language candidates, and students are sometimes entered for the one that does not match their background. Writing tasks are marked on register and text type as much as on vocabulary accuracy.

subjects.name: French and Spanish — Cambridge 0520 and 0530
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing. Writing tasks specify a form and a register, and a grammatically clean answer in the wrong register loses more than a slightly flawed one in the right one. Speaking preparation is the most neglected component.

subjects.name: Computer Science — Cambridge 0478
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, security, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode is marked on logic rather than on the syntax of any one language, and trace tables are a two-session technique that appears in every series.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in DAMAC Hills actually is here
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in DAMAC Hills means private one-to-one tuition in a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel subject, arranged outside school, for a student living in the community. IB Gram supplies that teaching live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is stated here rather than discovered after a deposit has been taken.

The word 'home' survives in the search because for twenty years private tuition in Dubai meant someone arriving with a folder. That market still exists in Dubailand and has a published rate. What has changed is that the constraint it was designed around — the tutor must be nearby — has gone, while the time cost of driving has not. In a community where the student has already made two journeys and arrives home after five, adding two more journeys is a poor trade.

What the online format buys is matching by code. A student entered for Cambridge 0470 History needs someone who has taught 0470 and marked its source questions, not a history graduate who last met a Dubai school syllabus some years ago. The content overlap between boards is substantial; the question styles, tiering rules and text-type requirements are not, and a mismatch there produces good teaching and an unchanged mark.

The arrangement itself is plain. A fixed weekly slot at a realistic hour, one named tutor per syllabus, past-paper work set and marked against the published scheme, a content checklist shared with parents, and a written note after each session. Where no specialist is free for a code, the answer is a stated wait or a referral, because a general tutor placed into a Year 11 block costs a term that cannot be recovered.

sections.heading: The three documents, and what each one answers
paragraphs: Before any teaching, three documents are worth finding, and all three are published free by the board. The specification sets out the content list, the assessment objectives, the paper structure and what is provided on the paper. The mark scheme for any past paper states exactly what earns a mark. The examiner report for a series states what candidates actually got wrong, in the board's own words.

Most families have never opened any of them, and most revision is therefore guesswork about what the paper wants. That is not a criticism of parents; the documents are not advertised and the textbook arrives in a bag on day one. But a student working from the content list knows what is examinable, and a student working from a mark scheme knows what a mark looks like, and those two pieces of information change behaviour more than another chapter does.

The examiner report is the most neglected and often the most useful. It names the question numbers candidates handled badly and explains why — a term misunderstood, a command word ignored, a calculation attempted in the wrong order. Practising precisely those things is about as targeted as revision gets, and it costs nothing but the time to read a document.

The table below says where each document sits and what question it answers. A DAMAC Hills parent can assemble all three for one subject in about twenty minutes, and doing it before contacting any tutor makes the first conversation substantially more useful.

sections.heading: English Language and Literature: form before fluency
paragraphs: English is the subject where strong students most often under-perform, and the reason is structural rather than linguistic. In English Language, directed writing specifies a form — a letter, a report, an article, a speech — and marks are available for handling that form, its audience and its register. A fluent, well-argued article written where a letter was asked for loses those marks regardless of how good the prose is.

The summary question is the second predictable loss, and it fails in the opposite direction to what students expect. Marks are for selection and compression, so a longer answer that includes everything relevant usually scores below a shorter one that selects. Students who write generously are penalised for it, which feels unjust until they read the mark scheme and see what is being rewarded.

In English Literature the dominant failure is narration. A student who retells the plot accurately and at length scores a fraction of one who quotes a single phrase and explains what it does to a reader. The required move — from what happens to how it is written — is a habit, and it can be installed in four or five sessions of deliberate practice against passage-based questions.

Both subjects respond quickly, which makes them good value in a short block. Form identification takes one session: read the task, name the form, note the audience, then plan. Analytical writing takes four or five. Neither requires new content, which is why a Year 11 student with limited time often gains more from an English block than from a science one.

sections.heading: Humanities: the named, dated, located discipline
paragraphs: Geography, History, Business Studies and Economics share one requirement that decides most of their marks: specificity. A case study has to be named, dated and located to earn credit. A business answer has to be about the business in the stimulus. An economics answer has to reference the diagram it just drew. General accuracy about a topic scores a fraction of specific accuracy about an example.

That gives these subjects an unusually clear revision method. Build a small bank of case studies — fewer than students imagine, usually six to eight per paper — and learn each with its name, its date, its place and three or four figures or details. Then practise deploying them against past questions. A student with eight well-known case studies outperforms one with vague knowledge of twenty.

History adds source work, which is a technique rather than a body of knowledge. Provenance, purpose, and reliability judged against the source's own content and the student's contextual knowledge. Students who revise only the depth-study content and never practise source questions lose a predictable block of marks every series, and the examiner reports say so explicitly.

Economics adds diagrams, where the losses are mechanical: axes unlabelled, curves shifted without annotation, and a correct diagram that the written answer never refers to. Business Studies adds tool application, where naming a tool without applying it to the stimulus earns almost nothing. Each of those is a three-week fix and each recurs across every paper in the subject.

sections.heading: Languages, including Arabic at two different syllabuses
paragraphs: Language subjects at IGCSE are assessed across listening, reading, speaking and writing, and the writing component is where the most recoverable marks sit. Tasks specify a form and a register, and a grammatically clean answer in the wrong register scores below a slightly flawed one in the right one. That is a scheme decision rather than a judgement about language ability, and it is learnable.

Arabic is the case that catches families in Dubai, because Cambridge runs separate syllabuses for first-language and foreign-language candidates. Students are occasionally entered for the one that does not match their background, which produces either an artificially low ceiling or an unreachable demand. Establishing which code a student sits is the first step, and it is on the school's subject sheet.

There is a further point specific to Dubai. KHDA requires Arabic in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, and combined classes for both groups prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Schools must also ensure teachers of Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for the subject. The mandatory Arabic requirement and an IGCSE Arabic entry are not the same thing, and families frequently conflate them.

For French and Spanish, the neglected component is speaking. It has a fixed school date, it is prepared last, and it is the one part of a language qualification that rewards rehearsal most directly. Three sessions of structured speaking practice against the task types, done a month out rather than a week out, is among the better-value purchases in any language subject.

sections.heading: Sciences and mathematics: three fixes and one
paragraphs: The sciences and mathematics are covered briefly here because each has its own page, but the structural point belongs on any subject-led page. The three sciences fail for three different reasons and need three different first interventions, and a single tutor covering all of them will be strong in one and adequate in two.

Biology loses marks to terminology the scheme rejects: a near-synonym for a required term scores nothing, so the fix is a vocabulary list built from past mark schemes rather than from a glossary. Chemistry loses marks to calculation layout, because method marks are awarded for the structure of the working, and three calculation families carry most of the numerical credit. Physics loses marks to explanations written as formulae where a causal chain in words was wanted.

Mathematics has a single dominant fix: visible method. Method marks exist separately from answer marks, so working held in a calculator forfeits them, and a rounded intermediate value carried forward loses the accuracy mark. Underneath that sits algebraic fluency, and a student who stalls at the same rearrangement in mathematics, physics and chemistry has one problem rather than three.

The planning consequence for a DAMAC Hills family carrying several of these subjects is to look for the shared cause before buying three blocks. Twenty minutes of non-calculator manipulation and unit conversion will show whether the losses across subjects have a single quantitative root. If they do, one block pays in four subjects, and that is both cheaper and faster than three subject blocks in sequence.

sections.heading: Grade scales, boundaries and what a grade actually means
paragraphs: Two grade scales are in use at IGCSE, which confuses almost every family that meets both. Some Cambridge syllabuses report A* to G and others report 9 to 1; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses 9 to 1. A school can therefore send home a report containing both scales in the same term, and the two are not simply interchangeable labels for the same thing.

Grade thresholds are set per series after the papers are marked, and the board publishes them afterwards. That has two consequences worth understanding. The first is that the number of marks needed for a grade varies between series, so a threshold from a past series is a rough guide and not a target to bank on. The second is that no tutor, teacher or provider can tell you in advance how many marks a grade will require, and anyone who does is inventing it.

What that means practically is that revision should aim at marks rather than at grades. 'Recover fifteen marks across Paper 2' is a target a student can act on and measure. 'Get a 7' is not, because it depends on a threshold nobody knows yet and on performance across components. Framing a block in marks is also what makes the four-session review possible, since marks on a comparable timed paper are directly comparable and grades are not.

The tier interacts with all of this. On a Core or Foundation entry the top grades are not available, so a mark target has to be set inside the range the tier permits. That is a reason to establish the tier before setting any target, and a reason to have the tiering conversation with the school before entries close rather than after results arrive.

sections.heading: What the rates buy, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: The published bands in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year. Packages advertised locally include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. All of those figures are published by the providers named and were read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's price list.

More useful than the numbers is what a parent can actually verify before paying. Three things are checkable in a first conversation. Can the tutor name the syllabus code and tier without being told? Can they say, from a marked script, which specific reasons the marks were withheld? And will they state what the block will not attempt? A provider who cannot do the first two is not matched to the paper, whatever the rate.

The fourth check is a permit. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and asking whether a tutor holds one is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one. The permit is free and valid for two years, so there is no cost reason for an eligible tutor not to have applied for it.

sections.heading: Entries, the two series and the resit decision
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate therefore plans around June, with November available as a resit route, and any schedule referencing a February window is for a different country.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. The timetable a parent finds through a search is not necessarily the one the school's centre is working to, and that is worth checking rather than assuming.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. In the most recently completed cycles, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning from.

The resit question comes up in August. A November resit in one subject is a reasonable move where a grade blocks a post-16 intention and where the loss was specific and identifiable. It is a poor move where the student is about to start a demanding new programme and the subject is not required, because the resit competes with the first term of the next course. The decision should be made against a named requirement rather than against disappointment.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and the claims not made
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Private tuition is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

IB Gram holds no Cambridge, Pearson, International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content.

Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports are referenced and linked at their official sources rather than reproduced or supplied here. They belong to the boards, they are free to access, and a provider offering a private library of them is doing something to be cautious about rather than impressed by. No success statistic appears on this page, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method cannot be checked by a reader.

process.title: Find the code and the tier first
process.description: The school's subject information sheet and the header of any past paper carry both. 'Cambridge 0470 History' or 'Pearson 4EA1, Higher' is enough to decide whether a genuine specialist is free, and it takes a parent two minutes to establish before contacting anyone.

process.title: Bring a marked script, not a report
process.description: The trial session is spent with the script and the official mark scheme side by side, with the student explaining why each mark was awarded or withheld. That produces a list of specific, repeated reasons, which is the diagnosis a report cannot give.

process.title: Agree the target in marks
process.description: Targets are set in marks on a comparable timed paper rather than in grades, because grade thresholds are set per series after marking and nobody knows them in advance. A mark target is measurable at the four-session review; a grade target is not.

process.title: Weekly work against the specification
process.description: Questions are set from the five most recent years and marked by the student against the official scheme. The content checklist comes from the specification rather than from a textbook, and the examiner report for the last series supplies deliberately targeted practice.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The mark target is measured in writing. If the same categories keep recurring in the error log, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes at no cost. Catching that at the halfway point rather than at the end is the difference between one lost month and two.

whyPoints.title: Specification first, textbook second
whyPoints.description: The content list says what is examinable, the mark scheme says what earns a mark, and the examiner report says what candidates got wrong last series. All three are free and published, and almost no family has opened any of them before a first tutoring conversation.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code and the tier
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0500 and Pearson 4EA1 set different text types; 0580 and 4MA1 differ in formula provision and scaffolding; Core entries cap the grade. A tutor matched to the subject rather than the code teaches correct material against an unfamiliar paper.

whyPoints.title: Targets stated in marks
whyPoints.description: Grade thresholds are set per series after marking, so nobody can say in advance how many marks a grade needs. 'Recover fifteen marks on Paper 2' is actionable and measurable; 'get a 7' is a hope that cannot be reviewed at session four.

whyPoints.title: The examiner reports actually used
whyPoints.description: The board publishes, for every series, what candidates handled badly and why. Practising precisely those question types is about as targeted as revision gets, costs nothing, and is almost entirely absent from how IGCSE revision is normally conducted.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around a long commute
whyPoints.description: DAMAC Hills secondary students are usually home after five, so sessions run from 5.30pm or on a weekend morning, and two shorter sessions beat one long one. Online delivery is what makes that pattern choosable rather than dictated by a tutor's driving route.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor from IB Gram come to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community it is also the more practical format: the student has already made two journeys and is home after five, and a visiting tutor would add two more through the busiest corridors. Published in-home market rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching.

faqs.question: Which free board documents should I download before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Three, for each subject that concerns you. The syllabus specification, which lists the content and the paper structure. A recent mark scheme, which states exactly what earns a mark. And the examiner report for the last series, which says what candidates got wrong and why. All are published free by Cambridge or Pearson. Assembling them for one subject takes about twenty minutes and makes the first tutoring conversation substantially more useful.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in English Language despite writing well?
faqs.answer: Because form, audience and register carry marks separately from the quality of the prose. Directed writing specifies a letter, report, article or speech, and a fluent piece in the wrong form loses those marks whatever its quality. The summary question compounds it: marks are for selection and compression, so a longer answer that includes everything relevant usually scores below a shorter one that selects. Both are technique, and both move within a few weeks of deliberate practice.

faqs.question: How many case studies does a Geography or History student need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students assume, and known far better. Six to eight per paper, each learned with its name, its date, its location and three or four specific details or figures, outperforms vague familiarity with twenty. The marks are for specificity: an accurate general answer about migration or industrialisation without a named example scores a fraction of a specific one. Then practise deploying them against past questions rather than re-reading them.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Arabic first language the same syllabus as Arabic foreign language?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge runs separate syllabuses for first-language and foreign-language candidates, and students are occasionally entered for the one that does not match their background, producing either an artificially low ceiling or an unreachable demand. Check the code on the school's subject information sheet. Separately, KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs; that requirement and an IGCSE Arabic entry are different things.

faqs.question: Should revision targets be set in grades or in marks?
faqs.answer: In marks. Grade thresholds are set per series after the papers are marked and published afterwards, so the number of marks a grade needs varies and nobody knows it in advance. 'Recover fifteen marks on Paper 2' is something a student can act on and something that can be measured on a comparable timed paper at the four-session review. 'Get a 7' cannot be reviewed, and anyone promising a specific grade is inventing the threshold.

faqs.question: What is the examiner report and why does nobody use it?
faqs.answer: It is a document the board publishes after each series setting out which questions candidates handled badly and why, in the board's own words: a term misunderstood, a command word ignored, a calculation attempted in the wrong order. Practising exactly those things is about as targeted as revision gets. It goes unused mostly because it is not advertised and does not arrive in a school bag, unlike the textbook, which is the least useful of the available documents.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth taking after June results?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether a named requirement is blocked. Where a specific grade is needed for a post-16 course and the loss was identifiable — a component missed, a tier ceiling, a specific topic — a November resit in one subject is reasonable. Where the subject is not required for the next programme, the resit competes with the first term of a demanding new course, which usually costs more than it recovers. Decide against a requirement, not against disappointment.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover English, a humanity and a science?
faqs.answer: Competently, perhaps, but each of those subjects pays for something different and a tutor strong in one is usually average in the others. English pays for form and register, humanities for named and dated specificity, sciences for layout, terminology or causal chains depending which science. The arrangement used here is a specialist per syllabus, scheduled on separate evenings so the homework load is spread rather than landing on one night.

faqs.question: Which four checks separate a code-matched IGCSE tutor from a general one?
faqs.answer: Four things. Can they name the syllabus code and tier without being told? Can they look at a marked script and state specific reasons marks were withheld? Will they say what the block will not attempt? And do they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years so there is no cost reason not to. A provider who cannot answer the first two is not matched to the paper, whatever their rate.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report show both 9-1 and A*-G grades?
faqs.answer: Because two scales are still in use at IGCSE. Some Cambridge syllabuses report A* to G and others report 9 to 1, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses 9 to 1 throughout. A school entering a mix of codes can therefore send home a report containing both. They are not interchangeable labels for the same thing, so comparing a 7 in one subject with a B in another is not a like-for-like comparison.

faqs.question: How long does an English or humanities block usually need?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions for form identification, summary technique or case-study deployment, because none of those requires new content and all are habits. Longer if the underlying problem is reading comprehension or writing fluency, which is slower work. For a Year 11 student with limited weeks, an English or humanities block often returns more marks than a science block, because the fixes are technique rather than content and technique moves faster.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is most neglected in revision?
faqs.answer: Speaking components in the modern languages, followed by source questions in History. Both have fixed demands, both are predictable in format, and both are prepared last or not at all. Three structured speaking sessions a month before the school date, or four sessions of source practice, each return marks that content revision cannot reach. The examiner reports for both subjects say as much, which is a reason to read them.

faqs.question: Do tutors teaching DAMAC Hills students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

intro.heading: Does anyone near DAMAC Hills 2 actually know your child's IGCSE syllabus?
paragraphs: Here is the question under the question. A parent in DAMAC Hills 2 searching for an IGCSE home tutor is rarely worried that nobody can teach Year 10 maths. They are worried that the person who turns up will teach Year 10 maths in general, miss the fact that the school enters Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 rather than Cambridge 0580, and spend six months drilling the wrong paper structure. That worry is well founded, and it is the thing this page is about.

IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge International runs its own IGCSE syllabuses, numbered in that familiar four-digit way — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Pearson runs International GCSE with its own codes and its own structure, 4MA1 for maths and 4PH1 for physics among them. The content overlaps heavily. The papers do not. Tiering works differently, the number of papers differs, and the way a grade is arrived at differs. A tutor fluent in one and unfamiliar with the other will teach competently and still cost your child marks.

The second part of the honest answer is about geography. DAMAC Hills 2 sits well out along the Al Qudra corridor, in a belt of newer villa communities where the professional tutoring supply has not caught up with the residential build-out. Dubai's tutors cluster near the older school districts. A tutor prepared to drive out to DAMAC Hills 2 on a Tuesday evening is a smaller group than a tutor prepared to work in Al Barsha, and once you narrow that group to the correct board and the correct subject, it can empty out entirely.

IB Gram does not solve this by finding somebody closer. We solve it by removing distance from the problem. Lessons for DAMAC Hills 2 families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is a service we run in India only. That means the pool you choose from is defined by which specification a tutor teaches, which is the variable that actually decides the grade.

KHDA reported 387,441 pupils across Dubai's 227 private schools in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment — the largest single bloc. That is a very large IGCSE cohort, which is exactly why the market is full of general tutors advertising to it and short of tutors who will tell you which specification they teach. Ask the question. A specialist answers it in one sentence.

There is a timing point too, and it is the one DAMAC Hills 2 parents most often wish they had heard a year earlier. Tier decisions in Cambridge and Pearson subjects are taken during Year 10, and they set the grade ceiling for the rest of school. A child placed on Core or Foundation cannot reach the top grades however well they are taught, and moving tier means covering content the reduced route never included. So the first question we ask a Year 10 family is not about grades at all. It is which tier each subject is entered for, and whether that is compatible with what the child wants to do after sixteen. The answer decides whether the next twelve months are urgent or ordinary, and both of those are useful things to know.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: DAMAC Hills 2 families meet IGCSE as one stage in a longer route, and what comes after it changes what good support looks like now. These are the stages we cover and what each actually demands.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, the years before IGCSE
programmes.description: The two years before option choices are where IGCSE grades are quietly decided. Algebraic manipulation, scientific explanation and extended writing all have to be secure before a specification is layered on top. Schools assess internally and report in levels or percentages, which tells a parent very little about readiness for a Cambridge Extended tier paper.
programmes.countryNote: In DAMAC Hills 2 this is the most common point of arrival from another system. A child moving in from CBSE, an American school or a different UK school meets a new topic order mid-stream. We use a diagnostic on Year 9 material rather than a report grade, because the report is measuring a syllabus the child may only have met in March.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally at the end. Cambridge offers many subjects in Core and Extended tiers with different grade ranges; Pearson structures its International GCSE differently and offers modular assessment in some subjects. Grades are 9-1 or A*-G depending on subject and board, and both scales appear on UAE school reports.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools do not all use the same board, and some use both across different departments — maths with Pearson, sciences with Cambridge, for instance. That is normal and it is why we ask for the code per subject rather than per school. It also means a single household can need two differently specialised tutors.

programmes.name: What IGCSE feeds into
programmes.description: Most UAE British-curriculum schools split after Year 11 into A Levels or the IB Diploma. The IGCSE grades a student holds decide which subjects are open to them: a maths-heavy A Level or Higher Level Diploma course usually expects a strong Extended-tier or higher-grade maths result, and sciences expect the equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 families frequently have both routes available within a reachable commute, with British-curriculum schools nearby and IB Diploma provision towards Motor City and the wider city. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects DAMAC Hills 2 families request most, with the specification detail that matters and the place marks actually go. Board coverage is confirmed at the trial lesson, not promised in advance.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The two boards diverge most here. Cambridge Extended caps higher than Core and the paper count differs; Pearson Higher tier covers content Cambridge Core never touches. Marks are lost on non-calculator fluency, on unstructured multi-step problems, and on failing to show method where method carries the marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions must be precise and formulae must be applied with units carried through. Electricity, waves and energy transfer are the recurring weak areas. Where a school cannot run every practical, the Alternative to Practical paper becomes the assessed route and needs its own preparation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall. Students who can balance an equation still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume under time pressure. Qualitative analysis and the required ionic tests are heavily examined and easy to drill once identified as the gap.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of recall plus precision of command term. Describe, explain and suggest want different answers, and a student who writes a description where an explanation is asked loses the mark regardless of knowledge. Experimental design and data interpretation questions reward structured practice.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and both are won on structure and register rather than vocabulary. Reading questions test selection and inference against a mark scheme that rewards precise textual reference, not retelling.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A common entry for students newer to English in Dubai schools. Assessment is split across reading, writing, listening and, in some variants, speaking. Progress is fast with targeted work because the skills are discrete and measurable rather than diffuse.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn and then used. Data-response questions reward applying a concept to the stimulus and reaching a judgement; definitions alone score low. Students who revise by memorising terms plateau quickly and need case-based practice instead.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The theory paper tests data representation, logic and networks as much as programming, and the practical component needs documented evidence rather than working code alone. Students comfortable at a keyboard often lose marks on hand-traced algorithms and pseudocode conventions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level Diploma maths. Calculus and trigonometric identities appear earlier than in standard IGCSE, and students carrying small algebraic weaknesses find them exposed immediately. This is the single most common bridging request we see.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge first and additional language routes
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs with different curriculum expectations. Support must match which stream the student sits, because the two are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel? Find out before you hire anyone
paragraphs: This is the first question to ask your school office, and it takes one email. Which board, and which syllabus code, for each subject. Schools in Dubai are not obliged to use one board across the curriculum, and plenty do not — a maths department on Pearson and a science department on Cambridge is an ordinary arrangement, and the school report will not usually tell you.

Why it matters comes down to paper structure. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with Core capped at a lower grade and a different paper pairing from Extended. Pearson International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher tiers with its own paper structure. Both assess broadly similar mathematics. Neither prepares a student for the other's paper. A tutor drilling Cambridge Extended past papers at a child entered for Pearson Higher is teaching useful mathematics in an unhelpful shape.

The sciences repeat the pattern. Cambridge numbers them 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology; Pearson uses 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Practical assessment differs, the balance between recall and application differs, and the command-term vocabulary each board favours differs. Pearson also offers modular assessment in some subjects, which changes when a student can bank a result — a genuinely different planning picture from a single terminal series.

So the single most valuable thing on this page is not a rate or a testimonial. It is the instruction to get the codes first, bring them to the conversation, and refuse to hire anyone who cannot immediately say which specification they teach.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the grade ceiling parents are not told about
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential thing on a Dubai IGCSE report that nobody explains at parents' evening. Cambridge offers many subjects in Core and Extended versions. They are different papers with different content coverage, and the Core route cannot reach the top grades at all. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work on the same principle. A child sitting Core who needs a high grade for a Higher Level Diploma course is not going to get there, no matter how well they are tutored.

Tier decisions are usually made by the department during Year 10, based on class performance, and they are often reversible for a while. That window is the point at which tutoring has the most leverage it will ever have. A student moved from Core to Extended in Year 10 has a different ceiling for the rest of their school career. A student moved in February of Year 11 is being set up to sit a harder paper with no time to cover the extra content.

So the first conversation we have with a DAMAC Hills 2 family in Year 10 is not about grades. It is about tier, and whether the current tier is compatible with what the child says they want to do at sixteen. If it is not, there is a window and it is closing. If it is, the work is ordinary and steady and does not need urgency manufactured around it.

The table below sets out what the tier decision actually governs. The point of it is the last column: the tutoring implication is different in each row, and treating a tier question as a grades question wastes the window.

sections.heading: What IGCSE help costs around DAMAC Hills 2, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start and it is where the most money is wasted. Budget online tutoring in Dubai advertises from AED 33-65 an hour — Tutopiya from AED 33-52, EdFlik from AED 45-65. At that price you are buying homework supervision from somebody capable and generalist. For a Year 9 student who needs company and structure, that can be genuinely good value. For a Year 11 student sitting Pearson Higher tier in eight weeks, it is money spent on the wrong thing.

The next band up is where IGCSE work properly belongs. Unitors publishes qualified online IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai research putting the specialist band at AED 200-450 plus. Premium named tutors go further, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

In-home visiting sits apart from that ladder rather than above it. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and home-tutor listings go to AED 500, travel included. Monthly in-home packages advertised in the Dubai market run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. From DAMAC Hills 2 that premium is paying for a drive down the Al Qudra corridor, and the thing to ask is whether the tutor who makes that drive is the one who knows your syllabus code.

sections.heading: The November series as a resit route, and the deadlines nobody mentions
paragraphs: One correction first, because it circulates widely among UAE parents and it is wrong. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. If anyone has told you your child can resit in March, they are describing a different country's provision, and planning around it costs a term.

Cambridge runs its International GCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone — and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Check your school's zone, not a timetable found by search.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a sense of how the November route actually times out: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results for a November series reach students in January — the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF rather than any date restated on a tutoring site, including this one.

The practical consequence for a DAMAC Hills 2 family is that a disappointing June result does not mean a whole year lost. It means a November entry, a defined block of work across the summer and first term, and a result in January. That is a real plan, and it is a better one than the panic that usually follows results day.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: the equivalency rule most parents get wrong
paragraphs: If there is any chance of a UAE university, or of needing a UAE-attested certificate, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements change which subjects matter. The published British-track rule is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They are mandatory school subjects — KHDA requires them in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum — and they still do not count towards the equivalency five. So a student with five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic education does not have five for this purpose. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects; that is not what the published rule says.

For the American track, for comparison, English proficiency is a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified from an official Ministry source, so we publish none — anyone who quotes you an IB equivalency figure should be asked where they read it.

IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a Ministry process and the Ministry is the only authority on it. What we can do is make sure that the five subjects your child is relying on are the five they are actually going to pass, which is a tutoring question with a clear answer.

sections.heading: How science practicals work if the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the sensible objection to online IGCSE science tuition and it deserves a real answer rather than a reassurance. Practical skills are assessed, and a tutor on a screen is not standing next to a burette.

What matters is how the boards actually assess practical work. For many Cambridge science entries the assessed route is a written Alternative to Practical paper, which tests the understanding behind experimental work: reading a measuring instrument, spotting a flawed method, identifying a control variable, drawing and using a results table, plotting and interpreting a graph. Every one of those is a paper skill, and paper skills are exactly what one-to-one screen work improves. Students routinely lose more marks on that paper than on any content topic, because schools under practical-timetable pressure teach it last.

Where a school does run assessed laboratory work, the hands-on part happens at school and cannot be replaced by any tutor, in person or online. What a tutor contributes is the preparation and the analysis around it: predicting what the experiment should show, handling anomalous results, propagating uncertainty into a conclusion, and writing up to the mark scheme's expectations. That is where the marks sit even for a student whose technique at the bench is fine.

So the honest position: online tuition cannot teach bench technique, and bench technique is a small share of the assessed marks. It can teach the Alternative to Practical paper and the analysis, which together are a large share. If your child's school enters a practical-assessed route, ask them which, and we will match a tutor who has prepared students for that specific component.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you hire permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is a permitted activity rather than an unregulated one, and most parents have never been told. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is wider than most families expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. A university student tutoring your Year 10 child can hold a valid permit. The question is only whether they have one. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts, so disregard any figure circulating informally.

There is also a boundary worth knowing. The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi describes the same restriction for school staff there. If a provider offers you your child's own classroom teacher privately, that is a fact about the provider.

For completeness: an individual needs the MoHRE permit, while an organisation operating tutoring from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership and does not claim one.

sections.heading: Why we deliver online to DAMAC Hills 2 and what you give up
paragraphs: A page arguing only one side of this is not worth reading, so here is the trade honestly. An in-home tutor can take a phone off the table, notice a child disengaging before the parent does, and exert a physical presence that a screen cannot. For a younger or less self-managing student, that is worth paying for and no amount of online convenience replaces it.

What you give up for it, from DAMAC Hills 2 specifically, is the pool and the hour. The pool, because the people willing to drive out along Al Qudra Road on a school night are a fraction of the market and a smaller fraction once filtered to the correct board. The hour, because the same traffic that pushes your school run to a 4:30pm arrival also pushes the tutor's arrival, and a session that starts at six and finishes at half seven is being taught to a tired child.

Online delivery inverts both. The tutor is chosen on whether they teach Pearson 4MA1 or Cambridge 0580, and the lesson can start the moment your child is home and fed. Screen sharing makes past-paper marking visible and annotatable, and notes persist for revision months later. Against that, a poor connection ruins a lesson, and a student who will not engage with a screen will not engage with ours.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. There is no UAE visiting service, no office and no centre here; in-home tutoring is something we offer in India only. That is a limit, we publish it on every page, and the free trial lesson is how you find out whether it is a limit that matters for your child before you spend anything.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our home in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 online, over live video, and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is an India-only service for us. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor that rate carries a long drive inside it. Our argument is that the scarce thing is a tutor who teaches your child's actual specification, and distance is what was stopping you getting one.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Email the school office and ask for the exam board and syllabus code for each subject. You are looking for either a Cambridge four-digit number such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry or 0610 Biology, or a Pearson code such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 or 4BI1. Schools can and do mix boards across departments, so ask per subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything. Bring those codes to any tutoring conversation. A specialist will tell you immediately which they teach; a generalist will change the subject.

faqs.question: How much does the Cambridge or Edexcel distinction change the tutoring itself?
faqs.answer: It matters at the paper, which is where the grade is decided. The underlying content overlaps heavily, so a capable tutor will teach your child real and correct subject material either way. What differs is tiering, paper pairing, formula provision, practical assessment route and the command-term vocabulary each board favours. A term of past-paper practice from the wrong board trains the wrong instincts about what a question is asking for. Pearson also offers modular assessment in some subjects, which changes the planning picture entirely compared with a single terminal series.

faqs.question: Is my child on Core or Extended, and can that change?
faqs.answer: Ask the department, because it is rarely stated clearly on a report. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation tiers cover a reduced syllabus and cap below the top grades; Extended and Higher cover the full syllabus with the full grade range. The decision is usually made during Year 10 on class performance and is often reversible for a while. That window is where tutoring has the most leverage, because moving up requires covering extra content, not merely practising harder. By February of Year 11 the window has effectively closed.

Monthly in-home packages advertised run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Those are the publishing providers' figures, not ours. We quote after the free trial, because the honest number depends on subject, board and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE in February or March?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. This is worth stating plainly because the belief circulates widely and planning a resit around a March sitting costs a term. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A disappointing June result therefore means a November entry, a focused single-subject block over the summer and first term, and a result in January — the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: When do November IGCSE results arrive and what can we do with them?
faqs.answer: In January. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results for a November series reach students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. For context, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. A January grade is still useful for post-16 applications, and schools are used to receiving updated grades at that point. Always work from the awarding body's live official timetable rather than dates restated on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a DAMAC Hills 2 student need for MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which catches families out because both are mandatory in Dubai schools. One competitor page currently states six subjects are required; that is not the published rule. Verify on moe.gov.ae — we do not process equivalency.

faqs.question: If our lessons are online, how does the practical side of IGCSE science get covered?
faqs.answer: Depends on the entry. For many Cambridge science entries the assessed route is a written Alternative to Practical paper, which tests reading instruments, spotting flawed method, identifying control variables, tabulating results and interpreting graphs — all paper skills that one-to-one screen work improves directly, and often where students lose the most marks because schools teach it last. Where a school runs assessed laboratory work, the bench technique happens at school and no tutor replaces it. The tutor's contribution there is prediction, anomaly handling, uncertainty and writing up to the mark scheme.

faqs.question: Does a private IGCSE tutor in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes, a permit. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor for the permit and verify it with MoHRE. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

faqs.question: Which schools near DAMAC Hills 2 run IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The UK-curriculum schools along the Al Qudra corridor and into Dubailand: Jebel Ali School in neighbouring DAMAC Hills, South View School, The Aquila School, Ranches Primary School and JESS Arabian Ranches on the nearer side, and GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary, Safa Community School and Dubai Heights Academy further in. UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of Dubai private enrolment, the largest bloc. These are named as local context; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. The school matters because it sets the board and the topic order.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with mocks done badly. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the mock actually showed, which is why we diagnose before quoting. If the content has been taught and the output is poor — timing, command terms, method marks not shown, wrong-board instincts — a focused block through the final term moves a grade realistically. If a year of foundations is missing in a subject, a term will not replace it, and we will say so rather than sell you sessions. The second case is usually better served by narrowing to fewer subjects and entering the November series for the rest.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and a science for the same child?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it has a real advantage: a single tutor who sees the whole workload can balance a maths mock against a Chemistry topic test instead of each tutor optimising for their own subject. Maths and Physics pair particularly well because the algebraic and graphical demands overlap. Chemistry and Biology pair less naturally. What we will not do is stretch one tutor across subjects they do not genuinely teach in order to save you a second match — two correct specialists beat one willing generalist in every case we have seen.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still have to be taken alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects sit alongside IGCSE and do not count towards the equivalency five.

faqs.question: Can lessons shift during Ramadan or while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most DAMAC Hills 2 families change the pattern at least twice a year. During Ramadan school days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so sessions commonly move to late morning, early afternoon or post-Iftar slots, and some families pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. While travelling, sessions continue, because the tutor's location is already part of the arrangement rather than an obstacle to it. Tell us the new pattern and we reset the fixed slot rather than letting sessions lapse.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the series, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Deira is the oldest part of Dubai and one of the most densely populated, a grid of apartment blocks and souqs north of the Creek where families live close together and children travel to schools spread across Al Qusais, Al Mamzar, Bur Dubai and Al Garhoud. It is also a neighbourhood where IGCSE results carry real weight, because they are the qualification that decides post-16 options and because Ministry of Education equivalency rests on them. So when a parent here searches for a tutor, there is usually a date behind the search.

The problem is that almost nobody sells tutoring against that date. Enquire with an agency and you will be asked which subject and how many sessions, not which series your child is entered for and whether the tier can still be changed. Those two questions determine what tutoring can achieve far more than the number of sessions does, because several of the decisions that control an IGCSE outcome close months before the papers are sat and cannot be reopened by paying more.

Here is the ordering that matters. Tier and subject entries are decided by the school on the basis of earlier attainment, then submitted to the board well before the series. Mocks follow, and the marked scripts from them are the only honest diagnostic a family gets. Then the examination window. Then results in August for the summer series, with the November series as the resit route and its results reaching students in January. Tutoring bought before the entry deadline can change which papers a child sits. Tutoring bought after it can only change how well they sit them.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. In Deira that format solves a specific local problem as well as a scheduling one: apartment living means a quiet room is not always available at 5pm, and an online session can be moved to a morning in the holidays or to a time when a shared room is free, which a visiting tutor's weekly slot cannot.

What follows is the year in order. There is a backwards-counted calendar with the official sources named. There is a table showing what eight weeks can achieve depending on how many weeks remain. There is the mock-script method that sorts lost marks into three bins, which is the single most useful hour a Year 11 family will spend. There is the June and November comparison for resit decisions. There are the dirham market rates with sources. And there is a short section on the paperwork waiting at the end, because equivalency catches families out after the grades are in.
