dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: Ordered here by how much the calendar matters in each. Some subjects reward support across a whole year; others respond better to a focused block in the final term, and buying the wrong pattern wastes money even when the teaching is good.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cumulative, so support is worth more early than late. The skill that moves grades is method-mark discipline: showing working a marker can follow and not abandoning a multi-step question halfway. Needs a term to become automatic, which is why a six-week push before the series rarely changes a boundary.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and forces carry most of the marks and most of the confusion. Written explanation quality is the gap: students calculate correctly and then describe a cause and effect in the wrong order. Benefits from steady work from the start of Year 11 rather than a late block.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry sit between a 6 and an 8. The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards precise language about apparatus and error, and because question types repeat across series it is unusually learnable in a short block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, which makes it the subject most improvable in the final term. Command-term discipline and a condensed definition list do more in six weeks than re-reading the textbook does in six months.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: All three sciences in one or two awards, common for students taking nine or ten subjects. The syllabus is narrower than the separate sciences, so the single most valuable calendar action is confirming the entry code before any revision material is bought.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Improves through frequent short marked pieces rather than long sessions, so the pattern that works is fortnightly across the year rather than intensively at the end. The reading paper's analysis questions are where the marks concentrate.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification with its own mark scheme and a speaking component in some variants. The entry decision is a Year 10 conversation, not a Year 11 one, because moving between First Language and Second Language after entries is not usually possible.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: The clearest case for a late focused block. Marks sit in diagram accuracy and justified judgement rather than content volume, both of which respond to six concentrated weeks far better than to a year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: ICT carries substantial practical coursework that occupies specific weeks of the year, so support has to be timed to those weeks and is wasted outside them. Computer Science is theory and pseudocode with a steadier rhythm and benefits from consistent work.

subjects.name: Arabic and modern languages
subjects.description: Speaking components are often assessed earlier than the written papers, which catches families by surprise every year. Ask the school when the oral is scheduled; it is frequently weeks or months before the main window and needs preparation on its own timetable.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody competing for these searches publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what a parent is actually holding. The table below runs the year in reverse from the series, with who sets each milestone and what should already be complete by then. Every date in it should be confirmed against the official timetable for your child's board and, for Cambridge, for your centre's administrative zone.

Two sources anchor the dates that can be stated. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, examinations are available in May/June and November; the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is the reason to link the live official document rather than restate a date that may be revised.

For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June series with November available as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. One further warning that matters specifically here: the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. A Dubai revision plan built around a February sitting is using the wrong country's calendar.

The practical use of the table is to find out which decisions are still open. Before the entry deadline, tier is negotiable and tutoring can change which papers a student sits. After it, tutoring can only change performance. Knowing which side of that line you are standing on is the difference between a sensible plan and an expensive one.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can do, depending on how many are left
paragraphs: Parents ask whether it is too late, and the answer depends on arithmetic rather than optimism. Eight weeks of weekly sessions is roughly one term and is enough to make one examination skill automatic in one subject. It is not enough to cover a year of missing content in three subjects, and any provider who says otherwise is selling hours rather than outcomes.

With thirty weeks left, the right purchase is a cumulative subject taught weekly — Mathematics or a science — because habits built over that period hold under examination pressure. With fifteen weeks, the right purchase is one subject plus a mock-script repair block, because there is still time for a habit to form but not for two. With eight weeks, the honest purchase is the subject where content volume is the only obstacle, usually Biology or Business, plus timing and paper-order work. With three weeks, no amount of money changes a grade boundary, and the useful spend is one session on paper triage and then leaving the student alone to revise.

A warning about the opposite error. Families who start early frequently over-buy, booking three subjects weekly from September and discovering in November that the student's week never had room for it. Starting early is an argument for buying one thing properly for a long time, not for buying everything at once. The protected single slot plus a fortnightly weekend paper is the shape that survives thirty weeks.

sections.heading: Mock scripts and the three bins
paragraphs: This is the most valuable hour in an IGCSE year and most families skip it. Mock papers come home marked against real mark schemes, get glanced at, and go into a drawer. The grade is noted and the information inside the script — which is far more useful than the grade — is thrown away.

The method is simple enough to do without a tutor, and worth doing even if you never buy a session. Go through every lost mark on the script and put it in one of three bins. Bin one: the content was not known. Bin two: the content was known but the method or working was not shown in a way the mark scheme could credit. Bin three: the question was misread, mistimed or left blank. Count the bins.

What families find is usually counter-intuitive and encouraging. For most students the largest bin is the second or third, not the first. That matters because bins two and three are far faster to fix than missing content: showing working properly is a habit that can be trained in a few weeks, and running out of time on the last question is a paper-order problem rather than a knowledge problem. A student who revises harder when their largest bin is bin three is working hard at the wrong thing.

Once the bins are counted, the tutoring brief writes itself. Largest bin content: teach the topics, weekly, for as long as there is time. Largest bin method: a short block on working, layout and mark-scheme language, then timed practice. Largest bin question-reading: timing drills, question triage and a fixed order for attempting the paper. Three different purchases, and buying the wrong one is how families spend a term with nothing to show.

sections.heading: June or November: making the resit decision properly
paragraphs: The November series exists and is used, and a Deira family should understand it before results day rather than in the week after. For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit June as the main series with November available as the resit route. Pearson offers May/June and November. The November window and the January results date are both published, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The decision to resit is made quickly after August results, under pressure, and it is better made against criteria agreed in advance. The questions worth settling early: which subjects actually need a higher grade for the post-16 plan, as opposed to which grades were disappointing; whether the student will be carrying a full A Level or Diploma workload at the same time as resit revision; and whether the gap was close to a boundary or a long way from it. A grade that missed by two marks and a grade that missed by twenty are different problems and only one of them is a resit candidate.

The timing is the hard part. A November resit means revision running through the summer and into the first term of a new post-16 course, which is the heaviest transition in a student's school career. Families who do this successfully usually resit one subject, not three, and start the preparation in the summer rather than in October.

For Ministry of Education equivalency the arithmetic also matters: the published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A family needs to know which five they are relying on before deciding what to resit, and that is a conversation to have with the school rather than with a tutoring provider.

sections.heading: What a term of IGCSE support costs in Deira
paragraphs: The travel premium is the line a Deira family should look at first, because this is a district where a visiting tutor's journey is genuinely slow and genuinely priced in. Published Dubai in-home one-to-one rates run AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's rate work, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. The difference between those bands is not teaching; it is a car in Deira traffic and the parking that follows it.

Below that band, Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both online and generally generalist. Above it, specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists in the same range, while BartyED publishes AED 650 at the named or examiner-level end.

For a term, which is how this page thinks about everything, the arithmetic is straightforward. Twelve weekly sessions at the qualified band is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600; at the specialist band, AED 2,400 to 5,400. Bestimate's monthly estimates are AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. Advertised packages show about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All read in October 2026, each attributed to its publisher.

Those are market figures, not ours. We quote after a free trial lesson, one per subject before any payment, against a written plan with a term total on it, because a post-mock repair block and a thirty-week Mathematics plan are different purchases and a single hourly rate would misprice both.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the second half of the year
paragraphs: Ramadan falls in the half of the Dubai school year when IGCSE revision should be building, and it moves earlier each year, so a plan written in September should already name what happens during it. Schools shorten the day and reduce after-school activities, and households reorganise the evening around Iftar.

Handled deliberately, this is an opportunity rather than a loss. A shortened school day frees the early afternoon, which is the only time in a normal Dubai term when a student is both awake and unburdened by homework. An early-afternoon session in that period is often the most productive hour of the whole year. The alternative, suited to older students who have adjusted their sleep, is a post-Iftar slot later than a family would normally accept.

Both are straightforward online and difficult with a visiting tutor, whose own travel and schedule are compressed in the same way. More importantly, both need agreeing in advance. The failure we see every year is a session that quietly stops for a month and is never rebuilt, costing six weeks of momentum in the term the whole year was pointing at. Agreeing a reduced but real pattern — one session a week instead of two, at a different hour — keeps the thread intact.

Prayer times matter outside Ramadan too. Fixing a session relative to Maghrib rather than to a clock hour, and adjusting it every few weeks as the time moves, is normal practice for a UAE family and a tutor who treats it as an inconvenience is the wrong tutor.

sections.heading: Where a Deira student actually sits down to work
paragraphs: This is a practical section rather than an academic one, and it applies to Deira more than to most Dubai districts. Housing here is overwhelmingly apartments, often with more people than bedrooms, and a Year 11 student frequently does not have a quiet desk available at 5pm. That is a real constraint on both tutoring and revision, and pretending otherwise produces plans that fail for reasons nobody names.

What works, in order of how often families report it working. A morning slot at the weekend or in a holiday, when the flat is quieter and the student is fresher. A session timed to when a shared room is genuinely free, which an online booking can accommodate precisely. Headphones and a corner rather than a dedicated study, which is adequate for a one-to-one session in a way it is not for group revision. And, for revision rather than sessions, a public library, a school study room or a quiet café, all of which are easier to reach in Deira than in most of Dubai because the Metro runs through it.

What does not work is a visiting tutor arriving at a fixed hour into a full flat. The session needs a table and relative quiet for sixty minutes, and in a dense household that window moves day to day. This is the one argument for online delivery that is specific to this neighbourhood rather than general, and it is the reason online uptake in the Deira belt has been faster than in Dubai's villa communities.

One further point worth raising with the school: most Dubai secondaries run supervised study or revision rooms after hours, free of charge, and they are under-used. For a student without a quiet space at home, that provision is worth more than an extra paid session.

sections.heading: The paperwork waiting after results day
paragraphs: Families plan for the examinations and then meet the administration, which is a poor order to discover it in. Ministry of Education equivalency is the step that converts an international qualification into something UAE institutions can act on, and it has published requirements that are worth reading in Year 11 rather than in September after results.

On the British track the published requirement is passes in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and inheriting that error would cost a family a decision. On the American track, English proficiency can be shown with a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB there is no points threshold in that source, so none is published here. Confirm the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning around it. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; it is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or can accelerate, and no tutoring is required for it.

The schools context behind all of this: private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of them, and any provider claiming such status should be asked to produce the permit number.

process.title: Tell us the series and the weeks remaining
process.description: The first question is not which subject but which series your child is entered for and how many weeks are left. That number determines what is achievable, and we would rather tell you that three weeks out the honest answer is one session than sell you six.

process.title: Confirm the tier and the board
process.description: Ask the school in writing which tier or paper your child is entered for in each subject, the exact syllabus code, and whether a change is still possible. Before the entry deadline that information changes the whole plan; after it, it changes which past papers we use.

process.title: Bring the mock scripts
process.description: If mocks have happened, the scripts are the brief. We sort every lost mark into content, method or question-reading and the largest bin decides what the block targets. Without the scripts the first session is spent guessing at something the papers already answered.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one per subject
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject before any payment, taken at the proposed slot time. For a Deira family it is worth taking it at the hour you intend to use, so you can check the room is quiet and the student is actually available.

process.title: Reviewed at the next timed paper
process.description: The review point is a paper sat to time, not a number of weeks. If the score moved, we pick the next target. If it did not, we change the tutor or the method and say which we think it was. Every review is a clean exit point.

whyPoints.title: The calendar published, counted backwards
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, mocks, oral components, the series, results and the resit route, in reverse order with the official sources named. No competitor page in this market publishes a session, a deadline or a results date, and those are the facts a Year 11 parent needs most.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is no longer possible
whyPoints.description: The weeks-remaining table says plainly what tutoring cannot change from each position in the year, including that in the last three weeks you should not buy sessions at all. That costs us revenue and is the correct thing to tell a parent.

whyPoints.title: Dates cited, not restated
whyPoints.description: Where a date can be stated it is attributed: the Pearson November final timetable to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026, November 2025 results to students on 22 January 2026. Everything else points at the live official timetable, including the correct Cambridge zone version.

whyPoints.title: Built for apartment living
whyPoints.description: Slots are set to when a quiet room is genuinely free, with weekend mornings and holiday blocks offered as the better option where evenings do not work. In a district of dense housing that is a real constraint, and a visiting tutor's fixed hour cannot accommodate it.

whyPoints.title: Market rates with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its publisher and is dated October 2026, given hourly, monthly and per term. We quote our own figure after the free trial against a plan with a term total, so it is comparable to anything else you are considering.

whyPoints.title: Claims we do not make
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no board partnership, no promise about a grade, no self-published ratings and no statistics without a source. Equivalency is described and attributed, never offered as something we perform. Several pages in this search fail at least one of those tests.

faqs.question: My child's exams are in eight weeks. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only for the right things. Eight weeks can make one examination skill automatic in one subject, and it is enough to recover marks in subjects where content volume is the only obstacle — Biology, Business Studies, Economics. It cannot build method discipline in Mathematics, which needs a term, and it cannot change the tier your child is entered for. The highest-value use of eight weeks is timed papers plus whichever subject the mock scripts show is closest to a boundary.

faqs.question: How do I use my child's mock scripts properly?
faqs.answer: Go through every lost mark and sort it into three bins: content not known, method not shown in a way the mark scheme could credit, or question misread, mistimed or left blank. Count them. Most students find the largest bin is the second or third, which is good news because both are faster to fix than missing content. The largest bin then writes the tutoring brief, and buying the wrong one of the three is how families spend a term with nothing to show for it.

faqs.question: How long before the June papers does my child's entry get locked in?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, because the school submits a candidate list and paper allocation to the board as an entry centre. The practical consequence is that tier and subject decisions close long before the examination date suggests, and tutoring bought after that point can change performance but not which papers your child sits. Ask the school in writing for the entry deadline and for the tier your child is on, and treat that date as the real deadline rather than the examination itself.

faqs.question: Is the November series a sensible resit route for a Deira student?
faqs.answer: For one subject, often yes. For three, almost never, because November revision runs through the summer and into the first term of a new post-16 course, which is the heaviest transition in a student's school career. Decide against criteria set in advance: which grade the post-16 plan actually requires, how close the result was to the boundary, and whether the student will be carrying a new course at the same time. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit grade may arrive after enrolment.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable should we be working from?
faqs.answer: The one for your centre's administrative zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in and get that document rather than a general listing. One further point: the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai plan built around a February sitting is using the wrong calendar.

faqs.question: When are the oral and practical components assessed?
faqs.answer: Frequently weeks or months before the main written window, which catches families by surprise every year. Speaking components in language subjects and practical or alternative-to-practical arrangements in the sciences are scheduled by the school, not by the parent, and they need their own preparation timetable. Email the school early in Year 11 and ask for every non-written assessment date in one list. It is a two-minute question that prevents the most avoidable disappointment in the IGCSE year.

faqs.question: What does a term of IGCSE tutoring cost in Deira?
faqs.answer: Using published Dubai figures read in October 2026: twelve weekly sessions at the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour comes to roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600, and at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, roughly AED 2,400 to 5,400. Budget online generalists at AED 33 to 65 would be about AED 400 to 780 for the same term. In-home visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel work out considerably higher. Those are market rates; we quote after a free trial with a term total.

faqs.question: Our flat is crowded. Where should my child take a lesson?
faqs.answer: Wherever is genuinely quiet at that hour, and the honest answer in much of Deira is a weekend morning or a holiday block rather than a weekday evening. Headphones and a corner are adequate for a one-to-one session in a way they are not for group revision. Also ask the school about supervised study or revision rooms after hours, which most Dubai secondaries run free of charge and which are badly under-used. For a student without a desk at home, that is worth more than an extra paid session.

faqs.question: What should a Deira revision plan do about the Ramadan weeks?
faqs.answer: Agree the change before the period starts rather than improvising. Schools shorten the day and reduce activities, which frees the early afternoon — often the most productive academic hour of the entire year, because the student is awake and not yet carrying homework. The alternative is a post-Iftar slot for older students who have adjusted their sleep. The failure to avoid is a session that quietly stops for a month and is never rebuilt, in the term the whole year has been building towards.

faqs.question: Can tutoring still change which papers my child sits?
faqs.answer: Only before the entry deadline. Schools decide tier on earlier attainment, and until entries are submitted a well-evidenced case for moving a student from Core to Extended, or Foundation to Higher, is sometimes accepted — which is the single largest lever available, because tier sets the grade ceiling. After entries close, tutoring changes performance within the papers already chosen. That is why the first question we ask is which series and how many weeks remain, rather than which subject.

faqs.question: Should we buy sessions in the last fortnight before the papers?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and we will say so. In the final two or three weeks a student needs sleep, a sensible paper plan and uninterrupted time to revise what they already know. One session on paper order and question triage can recover marks that are currently being thrown away. Beyond that, additional sessions compete with revision rather than supporting it, and they tend to be bought to relieve parental anxiety rather than because they will change a grade.

faqs.question: Which five subjects should we be protecting for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Decide with the school, early. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One currently ranking competitor page says six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Knowing which five you are relying on changes what is worth tutoring and what is worth resitting.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our apartment in Deira?
faqs.answer: Not from us. Every UAE lesson is online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. In this district the online format solves a specific problem: a visiting tutor needs a quiet table at a fixed hour, and in dense housing that window moves day to day. In-home tutoring is available in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel for families who need it.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we realistically tutor at once in Year 11?
faqs.answer: One weekly, plus a fortnightly weekend paper session across subjects. A Dubai Year 11 week contains eight to ten subject entries, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons, two or three afternoons of clinics or fixtures, and clustered homework. Three weekly sessions into that week produces three half-attended hours and an arrangement that collapses by half term. One protected slot that survives to the series is worth more than three that do not reach February.

faqs.question: Does starting in Year 10 actually save money?
faqs.answer: Usually, because it changes what is possible rather than just adding hours. In Year 10 a tier change is still negotiable, content gaps are small enough to close in a term, and the week has room for a session. The expensive pattern is doing nothing for two years and then buying intensively for the final two months, which is also the pattern least likely to work, since examination technique needs repeated practice across a term before it holds under pressure.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to prove they know the board?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the syllabus code, the number of papers at that tier, and how the practical or oral component is assessed for your child's specification. Then ask them to mark one page of a mock script aloud, saying what each annotation is worth. A specialist uses mark-scheme language and finishes by naming one behaviour to change. A generalist corrects spelling and suggests more practice. You do not need subject knowledge to hear which one you are listening to.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-deira.closingHeading: Start with the date, then work backwards
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-deira.closingBody: Tell us which series your child is entered for, how many weeks remain, which board and tier, and whether mocks have happened. With those four facts we will say what is achievable from where you are standing, including when the honest answer is fewer sessions than you expected or none at all. The first lesson is free, one per subject, before any payment, and best taken at the hour and in the room you intend to use. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and every date we work from comes off the official timetable rather than a website.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE one-to-one over live video. Each works to a single syllabus code and tier, which is the thing a rate should be buying and the thing most quotes in this market do not specify.

intro.heading: Comparing prices when nobody tells you what is inside them
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in DIFC is one of the better-paid tutoring jobs in Dubai, and a parent trying to buy one is working with almost no information. Three of the six largest providers in this market publish no price at all. One quotes in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. One publishes an hourly rate in its page copy that contradicts the price range in its own structured data. The result is that a DIFC parent is asked to choose between quotes that are not comparable, on a service whose contents nobody has defined.

So this page is written from cost, in both directions. It publishes the Dubai market bands with the provider or publication that stated each one and the month the figure was read. It sets out what a quoted hourly rate typically does and does not include, because the gaps between quotes are usually in the inclusions rather than in the number. And it names, plainly, the five places where IGCSE tutoring money in this district gets spent without buying anything: the wrong board's papers, the wrong tier, the untargeted retainer, the four-subject plan that collapses in week five, and the travel premium on a service that does not need travel.

DIFC adds a specific wrinkle. The district has no school inside it, so every IGCSE candidate here commutes out, most often towards Al Safa, Al Quoz, Sobha Hartland or Al Jaddaf. That means the in-home premium a DIFC family pays is being charged for a tutor's drive across central Dubai in the evening peak, into a district with structured parking and tower access. It is the most expensive logistics in the emirate and it buys nothing a parent can point to on a marked paper.

One statement before the numbers, because it affects how you should read all of them. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and we have no office, branch or centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's title is the phrase DIFC parents search, and answering it honestly means telling you what the in-home market charges and then telling you what we actually do.

Every AED figure below belongs to the provider or publication named beside it. None of them is an IB Gram price, and we do not publish a UAE rate card on these pages. We also publish no satisfaction percentage, no average-score claim and no statistic we cannot support with a number, a date and a method, which is why there are none here. The free trial lesson exists so that a DIFC family can see the teaching before any money is discussed.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: Three purchase decisions sit behind most IGCSE spending in this district, and each has a different honest price. These are the programmes in play for a DIFC family, framed by what each one actually costs to support.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, examined at the end. The spending pattern is predictable: almost nothing in Year 10, then a large uncoordinated purchase in the spring of Year 11 across three or four subjects at once. The reverse order is cheaper and more effective. One subject supported weekly from Year 10 typically costs less across two years than four subjects supported in panic for one term, and produces a better result.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the IGCSE year sits under KHDA inspection alongside the mandatory UAE subjects. For a DIFC family the practical cost variable is the commute: a child arriving home at 4pm has more usable hours than one arriving at 4.45pm, and usable hours are what tuition is actually buying.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the tier decision
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention point in the whole sequence and the one nobody buys. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests give an external datapoint before the school's tier decision. A Year 9 who is heading for Core tier in mathematics has a year to change that, and a year of weekly support costs less than a term of Year 11 crisis tutoring across multiple subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The October window produces evidence before the tier decision rather than after it, which for a DIFC family is the difference between a conversation with the school and an argument with it.

programmes.name: Resit and post-results spending
programmes.description: The most emotionally driven spending in this market and the easiest to waste. The right decision is made from component marks rather than from the overall grade, because a paper that fell four marks short is a narrow piece of work and one that fell twenty is a different problem entirely. A resit block bought without reading the component marks is money spent on the wrong paper.
programmes.countryNote: Looking at a published pattern: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. A November entry produces a grade in January, which is in time for many sixth-form confirmations and not all. Ask the receiving school in writing before paying for a block.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in every Dubai private school. They occupy timetabled hours and appear on the report, and families sometimes buy tutoring for them under the impression that they count towards Ministry of Education equivalency. They do not count among the five IGCSE subjects required on the British track, so the spending rationale should be the school report rather than the equivalency file.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: What each subject typically costs to support is a function of how recoverable its marks are. The list below is ordered roughly by value for money: the subjects at the top move fastest per session, which is where a constrained budget should go first.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The best value subject in this market because so many of its lost marks are procedural. Reverse percentages, frequency density, circle-theorem naming and rounding discipline are each worth marks on nearly every paper and each takes two or three sittings. A budget that can only cover one subject usually belongs here.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Good value if the losses are in the practical or alternative-to-practical component, where marks come from precise description of method, variables and sources of error. That is a writing skill and it responds quickly. Poor value if electricity and electromagnetism are genuinely not understood, which is a term rather than a block.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and electrolysis are arithmetic-confidence problems dressed as conceptual ones, and they are cheap to fix. Organic chemistry left until the final term is the single most expensive thing to repair in any science, because it is cumulative and there is no shortcut through it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: High content volume, so a content gap here is expensive. But a large share of lost marks come from command terms rather than knowledge: explain, suggest and compare each want a different answer shape, and a student writing descriptions where explanations were asked for scores nothing for correct biology. That part is three sessions.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Frequently the best-value purchase in the whole set, because the issue is almost always structure rather than vocabulary, and structure is teachable against the mark scheme in a handful of sessions. Buying open-ended essay practice without reading the criteria first is the classic way to waste money here.

subjects.name: English Literature (Edexcel 4ET1 / Cambridge 0475)
subjects.description: Moves on textual reference density rather than on insight. Strong students sit mid-band because they quote too little. For a closed-book paper, memorised quotation is a timetable problem rather than a tutoring one, which means fewer paid hours and more structured homework.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation marks are the recoverable ones. The Dubai pattern is strong theory and weak evaluation, because evaluation requires committing to a judgement rather than listing both sides. That is a specific, teachable move and it is worth paying for; more content revision usually is not.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are mechanical marks that fluent Python coders routinely drop, because the board has conventions and a student's own style is not one of them. Cheap to fix. The theory paper on data representation and networks is usually under-revised and needs homework rather than hours.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study and source papers. Geography rewards named places and specific figures; History rewards source evaluation on provenance and purpose. Both lose marks to vagueness, which responds to structured practice. A tutor should be marking against the criteria here, not delivering content a textbook already contains.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Worth paying for only where the main specification is already secure, because it assumes complete fluency. A student still consolidating 0580 Extended who takes on Additional Mathematics support is buying two problems instead of solving one, and this is a genuine and common waste in strong-school cohorts.

subjects.name: Accounting and Information Technology
subjects.description: Precision subjects where method and format marks dominate. Accounting rewards correctly structured statements even with a wrong figure; ICT rewards following the task specification exactly. Both improve quickly because the losses are to convention rather than to understanding, which makes them unusually good value per session.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and taught in separate classes under KHDA rules. Buy support for it because of the school report, not because of equivalency: it does not count among the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires on the British track.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.regionsTitle: DIFC and the commute the premium is paying for
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: The in-home rate in this district is priced against a specific journey. These are the areas a DIFC IGCSE family travels between, and what each one does to the cost and the usable evening.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: A financial district with residential towers and no school inside it. Structured parking, tower access procedures and the shortest school run in the central corridor, which means a 4pm session start is genuinely achievable here.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: The closest established British-curriculum cluster and where a large share of DIFC's IGCSE candidates study. Fifteen to twenty-five minutes depending on the hour, with the return slower than the outbound run.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and operationally identical for school-run purposes. A tutor driving from Downtown to DIFC in the evening peak is charging a travel premium for a journey that is short in distance and long in minutes.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: One canal crossing away, also with no school inside the district. DIFC and Business Bay families face the same market and the same thin local specialist pool for any single syllabus code.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Several campuses inside a large district that is slow to cross in the evening. Students schooling here arrive home fifteen to twenty minutes later than the Al Safa cohort, which shortens the usable evening and raises the effective cost per usable hour.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Creek-side campuses including Hartland International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. Quick from DIFC outside peak, mixed curricula in the catchment.

regions.name: Al Barsha and the western corridor
regions.note: A longer run along Sheikh Zayed Road to several established campuses. The highest travel premium a DIFC in-home arrangement would attract, and the one where the cost is most visibly logistics rather than teaching.

regions.name: Jumeirah and the coast
regions.note: Established schools fifteen to thirty minutes west. Weekend sessions work well on this side of the city, and weekend hours are often cheaper to secure simply because fewer families compete for them.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: The nearest and largest UK-curriculum cluster to DIFC, and where most of the district's IGCSE candidates sit. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications are in use across these schools, which is why a quote should always name the board.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and the Creek side
schoolClusters.note: Quick from DIFC outside the evening peak, with mixed curricula across the catchment. Confirming the specification code matters more here than anywhere else in the corridor before any money is spent on past papers.
schools: GEMS Our Own Indian School, Al Quoz

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Al Barsha and the western corridor
schoolClusters.note: The longest journeys from DIFC and therefore the highest travel component in any in-home quote. Also the widest spread of boards and tiers, which makes a generic rate quote least meaningful here.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.modesIntro: Three ways to spend an IGCSE tutoring budget, with what each actually delivers per dirham, plus a plain statement of what we do not provide in the UAE.

modes.title: A short targeted block on one subject
modes.description: Eight to twelve sessions on the subject with the widest grade gap, starting with a diagnosis from marked papers and ending at a defined point. This is the highest-value purchase available in this market because the budget is concentrated where the recoverable marks are, and because the commitment has a visible end rather than renewing by default.
bullets: Diagnosis from marked papers before any package is agreed
One subject, chosen by marks lost rather than by anxiety
A defined endpoint, so renewal is a decision and not a default
Free trial lesson first, with no card required

modes.title: Weekly support from Year 10, on one or two subjects
modes.description: Lower intensity, longer horizon, and across two years usually cheaper than a Year 11 crisis purchase across four subjects. The work is consolidation in real time, so gaps never accumulate into a project. It also keeps the tier conversation open while it can still be won, which is the single largest financial variable in the whole IGCSE course.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, premium end first
paragraphs: Starting at the top is more informative than starting at the bottom, because the premium end tells you what the ceiling is and therefore how to read everything beneath it. BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour at the premium named-tutor end of this market. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist tutoring at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in.

Below that, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200 for a qualified subject tutor online. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Every figure in this paragraph and the last belongs to the provider or publication named with it and was read in October 2026.

Read top-down, the structure of the market becomes legible. There is roughly a twentyfold spread between the cheapest and the most expensive published hour in Dubai, and the thing that varies across it is not primarily the tutor's knowledge of a syllabus. It is credential claims, brand positioning, and whether somebody is driving. A DIFC parent paying at the premium end should be able to say what the extra is buying in terms a marked paper would show, and if nobody can answer that question, the premium is positioning.

IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card on these pages and does not present any of these figures as ours. We also decline to describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, because examiner claims are a large part of what justifies the premium end of this market and the status is rarely verifiable. For wider context on a Dubai education budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: The five places IGCSE money disappears in this district
paragraphs: Waste in tutoring is rarely a bad tutor. It is almost always a correctly delivered service aimed at the wrong thing, and the five patterns below account for most of it in central Dubai. Each is avoidable with information a parent can obtain free, which is why they are worth naming explicitly rather than hinting at.

First, the wrong board's papers. A student entered for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher who spends a block working Cambridge 0580 Extended papers is practising a related subject with different phrasing and a different distribution of question types. Second, the wrong tier. Paying for intensive support towards a grade the tier cannot award is the most complete waste available in this market, and it happens because nobody told the family the ceiling. Third, the untargeted retainer: an open-ended weekly session with no diagnosis behind it and no review date, which renews quietly for a year.

Fourth, the four-subject spring plan. A Year 11 carrying nine courses and a commute can absorb one or two tutored subjects; four produces attendance that collapses around week five, after which the family has paid for sessions nobody attended and concluded that tutoring does not work. Fifth, the travel premium. In DIFC this is charged for a drive across central Dubai in the evening peak, into a district with structured parking and tower access, and it buys logistics rather than teaching.

The counter to all five is the same and it is free. Email the school for the specification code and the tier in writing. Ask for the two most recent marked papers rather than the grades. Set a review date before the first session rather than after the tenth. Pick one subject. And ask any in-home quote what the premium over the online rate is buying in terms you could see on a marked script. Four emails and one question remove most of the financial risk in this purchase.

sections.heading: What a quoted hourly rate does not include
paragraphs: The reason two Dubai quotes at the same hourly rate are not the same price is that the inclusions differ and almost nobody states them. A DIFC parent comparing AED 200 against AED 200 may be comparing a session with marked timed papers, written session notes and a free cancellation window against a bare hour with none of those things. The number is identical and the service is not.

The items that vary most are marking of full timed papers, written feedback after each session, access to the same tutor rather than a rotating pool, the cancellation and rescheduling window, whether the first session is chargeable, whether the rate is per hour or per session of unstated length, and whether the quote is per child in a sibling arrangement. Each of those is worth real money across a block and each is answerable in one message before you commit.

Two further questions are specific to this market. Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, because a rate quoted excluding it is a different number on the invoice; this page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so would require a Federal Tax Authority citation we do not have, so the correct question is simply whether the figure you have been given is the figure you will pay. And ask whether the provider uses a UAE contact number, because two ranking competitors route UAE parents to numbers outside the country, which matters when something needs resolving quickly.

The table below is a checklist rather than an argument. Sending it as a list of questions to two or three providers produces comparable quotes in about a day, which is faster than most families spend deciding and considerably cheaper than discovering the gaps in month two.

sections.heading: Three plans, priced out properly
paragraphs: Abstract hourly rates are hard to decide between, so here are three realistic DIFC plans with their session counts and what each is actually for. The costs below apply published market rates to the session count; they are arithmetic on other providers' figures and not IB Gram prices.

Plan one is the targeted block: ten sessions on the single subject with the widest grade gap, diagnosed from marked papers, ending at a defined point. Plan two is the two-year drip: one session a week on mathematics from the start of Year 10, roughly sixty sessions across two years, which keeps the tier conversation open and prevents gaps compounding. Plan three is what most families actually buy: four subjects at one session a week for the final twelve weeks of Year 11, forty-eight sessions bought in a hurry.

At the qualified-tutor online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, plan one is roughly AED 1,500 to 3,000, plan two is AED 9,000 to 18,000 spread over twenty-four months, and plan three is AED 7,200 to 14,400 concentrated into one term. Plan three therefore costs nearly as much as two full years of plan two, delivers it at the point of maximum stress, and is the plan most likely to lose sessions to collapsed attendance. That comparison is the single most useful thing on this page.

The right plan depends on where in the calendar you are standing, which is why the first question in any consultation should be the date rather than the budget. If there is a year or more, plan two is cheaper per unit of effect. If there are twelve weeks, plan one on one subject beats plan three on four, every time, and the money saved is better spent on nothing at all than on sessions a tired Year 11 will not attend.

sections.heading: The tier decision is the biggest number on this page
paragraphs: No cost comparison in this market matters as much as the tier a child is entered for, and almost no tutoring page mentions it. Cambridge IGCSE subjects are often tiered into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics into Foundation and Higher. The tier caps the grade that can be awarded. Spending at the specialist end of the market towards a grade the tier cannot produce is the most complete waste of money available to a DIFC family, and it happens routinely.

The mechanics are worth stating. A Core-tier candidate sits different papers covering a reduced syllabus and cannot be awarded the top grades. If a sixth-form course requires grade 6 and the Core ceiling sits below that, the route closes regardless of how many hours are bought. The school makes the entry decision in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the basis of internal assessment, and once entries are submitted the window narrows sharply.

So the first expenditure a DIFC family should make is an email, not a session. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for in each tiered subject, and what evidence that decision rests on. If the answer is Core in a subject your child needs, you have a conversation to have and possibly a year in which to have it. If entries are already in and the ceiling is fixed, then the honest financial advice is to spend less rather than more: secure the grade available within the tier and stop.

This also reframes the Year 9 and Year 10 spending question. A year of weekly mathematics support in Year 10, at roughly thirty sessions, frequently costs less than one term of multi-subject Year 11 tutoring, and it is bought at the point where it can still change the tier. Families who understand that tend to spend less in total and get more for it, which is the opposite of how this market is usually sold.
bullets: Tier caps the awarded grade; hours cannot raise the ceiling

sections.heading: What the DIFC travel premium is actually buying
paragraphs: The in-home band sits above the online band in every published figure in this market, and the difference is the journey. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. Across a twelve-session block the gap is several hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams.

In DIFC the journey being purchased is unusually expensive in minutes. The district sits at the junction of Sheikh Zayed Road and the Financial Centre corridor, has structured parking rather than street parking, and most towers have reception and access procedures. A tutor arriving for a 5pm session is leaving somewhere else at 4.15pm and will not be free again until after 7pm for a single taught hour. That cost is real, it is legitimate for an in-home provider to charge it, and it is being charged to you.

What it does not buy is a better match. The in-home pool for any single syllabus code and tier in central Dubai is thin, because the district has no school inside it and the candidate population is split across two boards, two tiers and nine or ten subjects each. A family paying the travel premium is frequently paying more for a less exact match, which is the inversion at the centre of this market and the reason this page exists.

There is also a quieter cost to in-home sessions that nobody quotes. A session that depends on somebody's drive cannot be moved at short notice, which in exam term is precisely when sessions need moving, around a mock, an unexpected school commitment or a sick day. Online sessions reschedule in a message. Across a twelve-week block that flexibility is worth more than it sounds, because a cancelled session is a session paid for and not received.

sections.heading: The permit is free, and other facts about cost in UAE tutoring
paragraphs: A surprising amount of pricing conversation in this market rests on misunderstandings about regulation, so here are the sourced facts. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit is free, no part of any quoted rate is a permit fee, and a provider presenting one is misinforming you. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, but no fine schedule has been published, so no figure appears on this page; an amount circulating online could not be verified against an official source.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal arrangement from an individual tutor. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a real cost base for a tuition centre and part of why centre group rates are structured as they are. IB Gram does not hold that permit and does not operate premises in the UAE, and we would never describe ourselves as authorised by KHDA.

On claims generally: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, licence, approval or partnership. We publish no self-asserted star rating or review count, because review markup that is not backed by real countable reviews is a structured-data violation and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. One competitor in this market publishes two different aggregate ratings on the same page; that is the standard this page is written against.

sections.heading: Honesty, coursework and the most expensive purchase in this market
paragraphs: The single most expensive thing a DIFC family can buy in this market costs a child their entry. There is a provider operating in this space that sells completed Internal Assessments. Any offer to write, complete or produce assessed work is an academic-integrity breach, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

The legitimate boundary is clear and it is worth knowing before you pay anybody. A tutor may teach content, explain the assessment criteria, model a technique on a different example, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write the text, supply sentences to be copied, or edit a piece to completion. IB Gram will not do any of the second list, and will not accept assessed work if a family offers it.

We also do not publish or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to all of it, free, which is where a revision plan should start and where a paid block should take its material from.

A practical test at the trial lesson, which costs nothing to apply. Ask what the tutor would do with a half-finished piece of coursework. The right answer involves reading it, naming which criterion is underserved, and setting the student a task. The wrong answer involves the tutor taking the document away. You can hear the difference in one minute and it is the most valuable minute in the whole purchase.

sections.heading: Starting from DIFC without overbuying
paragraphs: The cheapest effective first step costs nothing. Email the school for the specification code and the tier in each subject you are considering, and ask for the two most recent marked papers rather than the grades. Those documents turn a guess into a diagnosis, and a diagnosis is what decides whether to buy one subject, two, or none.

Then take a free trial lesson. It is a taught session rather than a sales call, no card is required, and it should end with a written note naming which marks are being lost and what the first four weeks would address. That note is useful to you whether or not you book anything, and it is the only way to compare two providers on something other than their rate card.

Coverage for IGCSE is reliable across the core subjects at both boards and both tiers, so a match is normally available within a few working days. What fills first is the hour. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested across the whole emirate; a DIFC student arriving home around 4pm has an advantage here and should use it, because 4pm and 4.30pm slots are the easiest in the corridor to secure. If no specialist is free at the hour you need, you will be told at the enquiry rather than matched to whoever is available.

Finally, set the review date before the first session rather than after the tenth. Six weeks, measured against marked papers rather than impressions, with stopping as a legitimate outcome. The untargeted retainer that renews quietly for a year is the most common way money leaves a family in this market, and a review date in the diary is the entire defence against it.

process.description: Compare marked papers against the baseline from the trial, then continue, narrow or finish. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we will recommend it when the marks say the work is done. A block that ends on purpose costs less than one that renews by default.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or publication that stated it and the month it was read. Three of the six largest providers in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, so a sourced band in dirhams is useful on its own, whoever you end up buying from.

whyPoints.description: Blocks have a defined length and a review date agreed before the first session. The open-ended retainer that renews quietly is how most tutoring money is wasted in Dubai, and the defence against it is a date in a diary rather than a promise.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video to DIFC. There is no drive across central Dubai in the evening peak inside the price, no parking, and no tower access time. Sessions also move at short notice in a message, which matters most in exam term.

whyPoints.description: The free trial reads marked papers and produces a written note of marks lost by type. Procedural losses are weeks of work; structural losses are terms. Knowing which one you have is what decides whether a budget should be ten sessions or sixty, and it is free to find out.

whyPoints.description: Where the tier caps the grade, where the losses are already small, or where the subject will be covered by the school anyway, the honest advice is fewer sessions or none. faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in DIFC cost per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is published at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and budget providers from AED 33 to 65. Those are each provider's own published figures read in October 2026. IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutoring quotes at the same rate cost different amounts?
faqs.answer: Because the inclusions differ and almost nobody states them. At the same headline figure, one quote may include marking of full timed papers, written session notes, the same tutor every week and a free cancellation window, while another includes none of those. Ask whether the rate is per clock hour or per session of unstated length, whether marking is inside it, whether the first session is chargeable, what the cancellation window is, and whether the figure quoted is the figure that appears on the invoice. Those answers make two quotes comparable in about a day.

faqs.question: Where do DIFC families most often waste money on IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Five places, in order of cost. Working the wrong board's past papers, because nobody confirmed the specification code. Paying towards a grade the tier cannot award. An untargeted weekly retainer with no diagnosis and no review date. Four subjects bought in the spring of Year 11, which produces attendance that collapses around week five. And the in-home travel premium, which buys a drive across central Dubai rather than a better match to the syllabus. All five are prevented by information the school will give you free, in one email.

faqs.question: Is a targeted block cheaper than a year of weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: Per unit of effect it usually is, when the losses are procedural. Ten sessions on one subject at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is roughly AED 1,500 to 3,000, against AED 9,000 to 18,000 for sixty weekly sessions across two years. But the comparison depends on the calendar. With a year or more, weekly support prevents gaps forming and protects the tier decision, which is the single largest financial variable in the course. With twelve weeks, a block on one subject beats a thin plan across four, every time.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour get my child a better IGCSE tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Published Dubai rates span roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, and what varies across that range is largely credential claims, brand positioning and whether somebody is driving. The variable that actually predicts whether marks move is whether the tutor has taught your child's exact specification and tier. Ask that question first and let the rate follow. A premium you cannot explain in terms a marked script would show is positioning rather than teaching, and a DIFC parent is entitled to ask what it buys.

faqs.question: Does a quoted IGCSE tutoring rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so responsibly would require a Federal Tax Authority citation that we do not have, and a tax statement on a tutoring page is not a thing a parent should rely on. The question to put to any provider is simpler and entirely answerable: is the figure you have quoted the figure that will appear on the invoice? A provider who cannot answer that clearly is one to be cautious with on other matters too.

faqs.question: Is part of a Dubai tutor's rate a licence or permit fee?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. So no part of a legitimate rate is a permit cost, and a provider presenting one is misinforming you. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, which is why no amount appears anywhere on this page.

faqs.question: Why is paying for the wrong tier the most expensive mistake available?
faqs.answer: Because the tier caps the grade that can be awarded, so hours bought towards a grade above the ceiling buy nothing at all. Cambridge subjects are often tiered into Core and Extended, Pearson Edexcel Mathematics into Foundation and Higher, and the entry decision is made by the school in Year 10 or early Year 11. If a sixth-form course requires grade 6 and the Core ceiling sits below it, the route closes however much is spent. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for before buying anything.

faqs.question: Our DIFC tower has restricted access. Does that affect in-home tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: It does, and it is rarely itemised. A tutor arriving for a 5pm session in DIFC leaves somewhere else around 4.15pm, parks in a structure, passes reception, teaches for an hour and is not free again until after 7pm. That is close to three hours of a working evening consumed for one billed hour, which is why in-home rates sit above online ones across every published figure in this market. The charge is legitimate for an in-home provider. It is simply not buying anything that would show on a marked paper.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we buy before deciding whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Set the review at six weeks and measure it against marked papers rather than impressions. Six weeks is long enough for procedural repairs to show in a timed paper and short enough that a wrong match has not cost much. Agree the review date before the first session, not after the tenth, because the quiet renewal of an unreviewed weekly retainer is how most tutoring money leaves a family in this market. Stopping at the review is a legitimate outcome and a good provider will sometimes recommend it.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Dubai tuition centre better value for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and the comparison is not only about price. A group class cannot diagnose from your child's marked papers, cannot work to their specification and tier if the group spans both boards, and cannot change pace for one student. It suits a child who is close to a grade and needs structured practice, and suits poorly a child with a specific diagnosable gap. Note also that a centre with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is part of its cost base.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if we stop after two sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask before you start, in writing, and treat the answer as part of the price. Providers in this market differ substantially: some bill per session, some sell packages that are not refundable, and some fall between the two without saying so. Our own position is that the trial lesson is free and requires no card, and that blocks are agreed as a session count with a six-week review built in, so the decision to continue is made deliberately rather than by default. Whoever you buy from, get the cancellation terms in writing first.

faqs.question: Should we buy tutoring for Arabic or Islamic Education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Decide it on the school report rather than on equivalency. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of them. But they are not counted among the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education requires on the British track. Note also that for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited, which limits what any tutor can legitimately provide.

faqs.question: Can we pay for help finishing a piece of IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: No, and the most expensive purchase available in this market is exactly that. A tutor may teach content, explain the assessment criteria, model a technique on a different example and give feedback on your child's own draft. A tutor may not write text, supply sentences or edit a piece to completion. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost an entry. There is a provider in this space selling completed assessed work; that offer is a reason to walk away, whatever else they appear to do competently.

faqs.question: Does tutoring get more expensive closer to the exam series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than rates rising, which has the same practical effect on a family. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested across the whole emirate in exam term, and specialists for a given specification and tier fill first. A DIFC family has an advantage here because the short school run makes 4pm and 4.30pm slots genuinely usable, and those are the easiest hours in the central corridor to secure. Booking a less convenient slot immediately is usually better value than waiting three weeks for a preferred one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our apartment in DIFC if we pay the in-home rate?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch or tuition centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Other providers in this market do offer in-home visits, and the published rates for that are on this page so you can compare honestly. What we would say is that the premium pays for the journey and not for a closer match to your child's syllabus code.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.closingHeading: Spend the free hour before you spend the first dirham
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-difc.closingBody: The four most valuable things in this purchase cost nothing: the specification code, the tier of entry, the two most recent marked papers, and a review date in the diary before session one. With those, a DIFC family can tell in a single session whether the losses are procedural, in which case ten sessions on one subject is the honest answer, or structural, in which case the plan is different and longer. Bring them to a short consultation on Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson is free, no card is required, and it ends with a written note of the marks being lost. If the right advice is to buy fewer sessions, or none, that is the advice you will get.
