intro.heading: Two communities, one answer
paragraphs: Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan sit either side of the same stretch of road, share bus routes and metro stations, and feed many of the same schools. They look like different markets to a parent. Discovery Gardens is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings arranged in themed districts, next to Ibn Battuta. Al Furjan is villas and townhouses across four districts. The conversations in each community's parent groups sound different as a result.

The practical differences are real. An Al Furjan family worries about bus loops spreading arrival across fifty minutes. A Discovery Gardens family worries about where in a two-bedroom flat a Year 11 student can work for an hour undisturbed. Visiting tutors quote the two communities at similar rates but find the villa side easier to serve, because there is usually a room to put them in.

What is identical is the question that decides an IGCSE grade: which exam board and syllabus code your child is entered for, and whether the tutor teaches it. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel equivalent is 4MA1; the tiers are named differently, the papers are structured differently and the mark schemes credit method differently. That is true on both sides of the road and it is the thing almost nobody checks.

It matters more in this corridor than most parents realise, because the schools these two communities feed do not all use one board, and several enter different boards in different departments. A Discovery Gardens student and an Al Furjan student at the same school can need different past papers for different subjects. The school's exams officer holds the entry list that settles it, and it is free.

IB Gram matches on that code and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we run only in India. That removes the one genuine difference between the two communities from the equation entirely, because nobody needs a spare room and nobody is driving anywhere.

The rest of this page runs the comparison properly: what differs between the two communities, what is identical, how the study setup differs in an apartment and why that is manageable, and which of the two communities' typical worries are worth acting on. The short version is that the housing changes the logistics and nothing about the syllabus, and the syllabus is what the exam marks. One more point before the detail, and it applies in both communities: the useful tutoring year for an IGCSE student starts in Year 10 rather than the spring of Year 11, because that is when a tiering problem or an algebra fluency gap can still be fixed cheaply and when the entry has not yet closed.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-discovery-gard.programmesIntro: The stages are the same in both communities and the timings differ slightly. These are the four phases either side of the Year 11 papers.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE begins, with no external assessment and therefore no signal. Algebraic fluency, formula rearrangement, and writing a paragraph that answers the question asked are the three things that later decide whether the upper tier is viable. Gaps formed here are cheap to close and become expensive once Year 10 requires all three at once.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, terminal written papers, and tiers fixed at entry. Most lost marks are method marks and command-term errors rather than content gaps, which is why topic revision so often produces no grade movement. Cambridge grades 9 to 1, as does Pearson Edexcel International GCSE.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Discovery Gardens enquiries sit. Students travel out of the community for school, so they are home from about 15:50 on the nearest routes and 16:30 or later from the Al Barsha corridor. programmes.name: Advanced Level or IB Diploma afterwards
programmes.description: The Year 11 grade profile determines which routes remain open, with most schools wanting grade 6 or 7 before accepting a subject at Advanced Level and IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asking the same. A capped tier entry closes routes in subjects the student is otherwise capable of, which is the real consequence of a Year 10 decision.

That makes a summer bridging block valuable on either side of the road, particularly in mathematics where the gap into Diploma study is widest.

programmes.name: The November series
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-discovery-gard.subjectsIntro: The subject picture is identical across the two communities, because the schools are shared. Each note names the codes to check on the entry list.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Core and Extended at Cambridge, Foundation and Higher at Pearson, with the tier capping the grade available. The dominant loss is method marks: working is credited independently of the answer, so a calculator result written bare forfeits most of a multi-step question.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Sat alongside the main entry by students heading for post-16 mathematics. Brings calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities a year early and is the hardest subject in this corridor to staff locally, which is exactly where online matching earns its keep.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity, with either a laboratory paper or a written alternative depending on the entry. Gradients, unit prefixes and methods without control variables named are the reliable losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, moles, organic chemistry and chemical tests. Mole arithmetic underpins everything quantitative, and the chemical tests must be answered as an observation plus a conclusion rather than recalled as a list.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics, ecology and human physiology. Imprecise language is the main loss: naming the mechanism and the direction is required, and an answer stating that a value increases earns nothing on its own.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award covering all three disciplines in reduced content. A weakness in one discipline appears in every paper rather than in one grade, so support should concentrate there rather than spreading across three.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Reading marks reward selective quotation and precise explanation of effect; students write everything they noticed, which is the commonest way marks go in this paper.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts, unseen poetry and extract-based questions. The grade depends on argument structure and embedded quotation rather than plot recall, and only repeated timed writing with marked feedback moves it.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram-led analysis and case-study application. Explain, analyse and evaluate each require a different answer shape, and students who write one paragraph type for all three cap out around grade 6 regardless of knowledge.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithms, pseudocode and data representation, with a practical element in ICT. Confident coders lose marks writing pseudocode outside the board's conventions, which is narrow and quickly fixed once someone points it out.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source analysis, case-study recall and extended writing under timing. Content learned without mark-scheme awareness is the standard failure, and structured essay drilling with marked feedback is what changes it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic to all pupils under KHDA rules, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. First language and additional language are separate qualifications, so the entry needs confirming before anything is planned.

sections.heading: Discovery Gardens against Al Furjan, measured honestly
paragraphs: A fair comparison needs to be specific rather than flattering to either side. Discovery Gardens is apartments: 291 buildings in themed districts, mostly studios and one or two bedroom flats, with a Route 2020 metro station and Ibn Battuta next door. Al Furjan is villas and townhouses across four districts with two metro stations. Both are served by the same cluster of schools and the same bus operators.

On travel, Discovery Gardens is marginally better placed. The community is compact, so bus pickup and drop-off is quicker than the long loops that spread Al Furjan arrival times across fifty minutes. A Discovery Gardens student on a Dubai Investments Park route can be home by 15:50; the equivalent Al Furjan student in the Murooj district may not be home until 16:10 from the same school.

On study space, the position reverses and the gap is larger. A villa generally offers a room where a Year 11 student can close a door. A two-bedroom apartment with two children and two working parents generally does not, and the realistic setup is a desk in a shared living space. That is workable with headphones and a household agreement, and it is genuinely harder than the villa alternative.

On tutor supply the two communities are identical, and this is the point of the comparison. Both are residential, neither has a concentration of subject specialists living in it, and both are reached on the same drive from the Al Barsha and Jumeirah tutor clusters. Visiting tutors quote them in the same band. So whatever advantage the villa side has, it is not a better choice of tutor.

sections.heading: The thing that is the same, and that decides the grade
paragraphs: Whatever the housing, an IGCSE grade turns on whether the tutor teaches the paper the student sits. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalent is 4MA1. Cambridge Physics is 0625, Pearson is 4PH1. In each pairing the tier names differ, the paper structure differs, the formula support in the exam room differs and the mark schemes credit method differently.

The mistake this produces is the same on both sides of the road and it is invisible for months. A competent tutor works through good lessons using the other board's past papers. The topics are right, the command terms and mark-scheme conventions are not. Nothing looks wrong until the mock, and by then a term of revision has been aimed slightly off target.

Several schools in this shared cluster enter different boards in different departments, so the assumption that one school means one board is unsafe. A Discovery Gardens student may sit Cambridge mathematics and Pearson physics in the same year and need two sets of past papers. The entry list from the exams officer names the board, the code and the tier for every subject, and it costs nothing to request.

The second shared constant is the tier. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, and post-16 study usually needs grade 6 or 7, so a tier chosen in Year 10 can close a route in a subject the student is capable of. That is identical in an apartment and in a villa, and it is a Year 10 conversation in both, because the entry window closes months before the papers.

sections.heading: Working in an apartment, and what actually solves it
paragraphs: The study-space problem is the one genuine disadvantage Discovery Gardens carries, and it has a practical answer rather than a resigned one. The equipment half is easy: over-ear headphones with a microphone turn a shared living space into a usable session space, and most families here already own a pair. A laptop on a desk with the marked work beside it is the whole hardware requirement.

The harder half is interruption, and no equipment addresses it. What works is treating the session as a timetabled lesson rather than as homework, which is a household agreement reached once at the start rather than negotiated each week. Where that agreement exists, apartment sessions run exactly as well as villa sessions. Where it does not, the tutor spends ten minutes of every hour waiting.

This is also where hosting a visiting tutor becomes impractical for reasons that have nothing to do with money. Inviting an adult into a shared living space for an hour in the evening, with other family members present and nowhere else to be, is a real imposition in a one or two bedroom flat. Families in this community mention that more often than price when explaining why they stopped looking.

IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE, so the question does not arise: every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The side effect is that the villa-versus-apartment comparison stops mattering, because the arrangement requires a desk rather than a room.

sections.heading: What each community's families actually ask about
paragraphs: The enquiries from these two communities differ in a way that is worth naming, because it shows how logistics shape what parents think the problem is. Al Furjan families lead with time: when can a session start, will it survive a late bus, can it move if there is a fixture. Discovery Gardens families lead with space and with siblings: where can this happen, can two children be covered, does it work with family in the room.

Both sets of questions are reasonable and neither is about the syllabus. That is the pattern worth noticing. When a parent's first three questions are logistical, the subject conversation often never happens, and the tutor is selected on availability. Asking a tutor which board and code they teach, and what the paper structure is, takes two minutes and belongs before any scheduling discussion.

There is one request specific to this community that deserves a direct answer. Families in apartments frequently ask whether two children can share a session to save both money and space. The honest answer is only when they are in the same subject at the same level with the same gaps, which siblings rarely are. Consecutive slots with different tutors keeps the quality and still uses one desk and one hour of household quiet.

The other recurring Discovery Gardens question is whether online tuition is a second-best option forced by the housing. For Year 10 and Year 11 work it is not. A session is largely a marked paper, a mark scheme and shared annotation, which works at least as well on a screen as across a table. The exception is children under eight, who are genuinely easier to hold in a room.

sections.heading: The two-year shape, identical on both sides of the road
paragraphs: The IGCSE course runs the same way wherever a student lives, and the shape is worth knowing because most families meet it a year late. Entries close months before the papers and fix both the board and the tier. Practical and coursework components complete before the written papers. Mocks sit in the winter. Study leave frees the afternoon. Then the series itself, results, and a narrow window to consider a November entry.

UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February exam window is working from another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable for the zone.

That zone warning is worth taking seriously: Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version of the timetable. The document to plan from is therefore your school's own zone timetable rather than a generic one, and the exams officer holds it. For a student sitting eight or nine subjects, it also shows where the gaps between papers fall.

Published Pearson dates give a sense of how far ahead the calendar runs. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations; forward planning should use the live official timetable, since provisional versions are revised.

sections.heading: What proximity-based hiring does, in either community
paragraphs: Hiring on distance has the same effect in an apartment community as in a villa community, because the limiting factor is the same: neither Discovery Gardens nor Al Furjan has a resident population of IGCSE subject specialists. Both are reached on the same drive from where Dubai's tutors actually live and work. So a proximity search in either place returns a small pool, and a small pool means accepting the available tutor.

The cost side is published and consistent. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate's Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. The difference is the drive. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and not an IB Gram price list.

Where the travel premium genuinely buys something is with young children, who are easier to hold in a room than on a call, and for a tutor who wants to see the folder and the state of the notes. Online recovers the second by having the student share their actual work on screen and by writing a session note the parent reads. The first is real and applies mostly below about age eight.

Against that sits the subject question. For Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science or a scarce humanities entry, the local pool in this corridor may be one person or none. Paying a premium to choose from that pool is paying to narrow the choice. This is the same conclusion the Al Furjan version of this page reaches, from the opposite housing stock, which is rather the point.

sections.heading: Tier, practical papers and the answers that do not change
paragraphs: Three decisions dominate an IGCSE outcome and none of them is affected by which side of this corridor a family lives on. The first is tier. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade, Extended and Higher reach the full range, and the evidence for the right choice is three marked papers across a year rather than one strong assessment. If the losses are method and reading, the student is stronger than the mark suggests; if algebraic fluency is absent, the lower tier protects the grade.

The second is the practical component. Depending on board and entry, a science candidate sits either a laboratory examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper testing the same skills: instrument reading, tabulating with units in the heading, scaling a graph, drawing a line of best fit, naming a control variable and how it was controlled, explaining an anomaly. All of it is trainable without a laboratory, which makes it the cheapest grade available in science.

The third is what revision actually is. Unmarked past-paper practice builds recognition of question types and very little else, which is why students who have done a great many papers still plateau. Timed, marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by cause rather than by topic, is the version that moves marks. Two causes usually explain nine lost marks.

None of those three is a local question. They are the same for a student in a Discovery Gardens apartment, an Al Furjan townhouse, a Jebel Ali villa or a Dubai South flat. The logistics differ and the decisions do not, which is why comparing neighbourhoods is a less useful exercise than comparing a marked paper with the mark scheme beside it.

process.title: Ask the school for the entry list
process.description: It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and it is free. Several schools in this shared cluster enter different boards in different departments, so one document can change what past papers your child should be working from in two subjects at once.

process.title: Send the codes and your quiet hour
process.description: Not just the subject but the code and tier, plus the hour in the evening your household can realistically protect. In an apartment that second detail matters as much as the first, and it is better settled at the start than renegotiated every week.

process.title: We name the tutor and their board
process.description: Before any lesson you are told who will teach, which board they work to, and which components they have taught or marked. If the exact code cannot be matched we say so rather than offering a near equivalent, because wrong-board practice wastes a term invisibly.

process.title: Free trial around a marked paper
process.description: Bring the most recent marked work and ask what pattern connects the lost marks. A specialist names behaviours: method not shown, command-term errors, accuracy demands unread. No payment is taken for the trial and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

process.title: Set up the space once, then keep the slot
process.description: Over-ear headphones, a desk, the marked work to hand, and a household agreement that the hour is a lesson rather than homework. Then keep the slot for the term. Families who renegotiate weekly lose two sessions a month, in an apartment or a villa.

process.title: Build the exam term from the zone timetable
process.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and warns that the wrong timetable can cost a candidate an exam. Plan the final term from your school's own zone document, and book study-leave sessions months ahead because that fortnight fills first across the whole city.

whyPoints.title: The same tutor pool as the villa side
whyPoints.description: Delivering online means the pool is everyone available in UAE evening hours rather than everyone willing to drive into this corridor. Whatever advantage a villa community has, a better choice of subject specialist is not one of them.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams, and several schools here enter different boards in different departments. We confirm the code from the entry list before the trial, because wrong-board teaching is invisible until the mock.

whyPoints.title: Built for an apartment setup
whyPoints.description: A desk, headphones and the marked work is the whole requirement. No room needs clearing and no adult needs hosting in a shared living space, which is the practical objection Discovery Gardens families raise most often.

whyPoints.title: Two shorter sessions where that helps
whyPoints.description: A quiet forty-five minutes is easier to arrange twice than ninety minutes once in a busy flat, and two shorter sessions retain more anyway because work set in one gets checked in the next.

whyPoints.title: Papers marked, not just attempted
whyPoints.description: Timed, marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by cause. Nine lost marks usually come from two causes rather than nine topics, and students cannot do that categorisation alone because they see the question rather than the behaviour.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no UAE office, no written coursework, no reproduced mark schemes, no accreditation claims and no grade guarantees. If no specialist is free for your board and slot, we say so instead of substituting one.

faqs.question: Do Al Furjan families get better tutors than Discovery Gardens families?
faqs.answer: No. Both communities are residential, neither has a resident population of IGCSE subject specialists, and both are reached on the same drive from where Dubai's tutors actually live and work. Visiting tutors quote them in the same band, in-home at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online. What the villa side has is more study space, which is a real advantage for hosting a visitor and irrelevant once lessons are delivered online.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our flat in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video; home visiting is a service we run only in India. In a community of mostly one and two bedroom apartments, hosting an adult for an hour in a shared living space in the evening is a genuine imposition, and families here mention that more often than price as the reason they stopped looking for a visiting tutor. The online setup needs a desk, headphones and the marked work to hand.

faqs.question: How does a Year 11 student study properly in a two-bedroom apartment?
faqs.answer: With over-ear headphones and a household agreement. The headphones solve noise and most families here already own a pair. The agreement solves interruption, which no equipment addresses: a session treated as a timetabled lesson by everyone in the flat runs exactly as well as one in a villa with a door, and a session treated as homework does not. Two shorter sessions a week also place more easily than one long one, and retain more in any case.

faqs.question: Which board does my child's school in this corridor actually use?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the entry list, because several schools in this shared cluster enter different boards in different departments. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson Edexcel equivalent is 4MA1; Cambridge Physics is 0625, Pearson is 4PH1. In each pairing the tier names, paper structure, formula support and mark-scheme conventions differ. A student can need two different sets of past papers in the same year, which is why the document matters.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one session to save space and money?
faqs.answer: Only if they are in the same subject at the same level with the same gaps, which siblings rarely are. Otherwise one child spends the hour watching the other get taught. What works in an apartment is consecutive slots with different tutors matched to each child's subject and level: one desk, one device, one protected block of household quiet, and a separate written session note for each. That is the arrangement most families in this community end up with.

faqs.question: Is online tuition second-best for Year 10 and Year 11, or just cheaper?
faqs.answer: For this age group it is not a compromise. A session is largely a marked paper, a mark scheme and shared annotation, which works at least as well on a screen as across a kitchen table and often better, because both people see the same annotation. It also removes the travel constraint that keeps the local in-home pool small, which matters most for scarce entries like Additional Mathematics. The honest exception is children under about eight.

faqs.question: What does the tier on the entry list mean for my child's options at 16?
faqs.answer: A great deal. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available, and most British-curriculum schools want grade 6 or 7 in a subject before accepting it at Advanced Level, with IB Diploma Higher Level entry usually asking the same. So a tier chosen in Year 10 can close a route in a subject your child is capable of. The evidence for the right choice is three marked papers across a year, and the entry window closes months before the exams.

faqs.question: Why do students who do lots of past papers still plateau?
faqs.answer: Because the papers are not being marked. Working through a paper with the answers beside it builds recognition of question types and little else. The version that moves marks is timed, in one sitting, without notes, then marked strictly against the real scheme, with errors grouped by cause: command term, method not shown, misreading, accuracy, timing. Nine lost marks usually come from two causes, not nine topics, and students cannot categorise that alone.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams in February in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: What should a science student practise if there is no laboratory at home?
faqs.answer: Everything the practical component actually assesses, because it is all written. Reading an instrument to the right precision, tabulating with units in the column heading, scaling a graph so the data fills the grid, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, naming a control variable and how it was controlled, explaining an anomaly instead of circling it, and writing a conclusion that answers the hypothesis. None of that needs equipment and it is the cheapest grade available in science.

faqs.question: When is the easiest time of year to get a specialist in this corridor?
faqs.answer: The UAE summer and early autumn, when November-series candidates are the only demand and Dubai's tutoring market is quiet. The hardest is the four weeks of study leave before the June series, when every Year 11 family in the city is looking at once and the common subjects fill first. The same request produces a different answer depending on the month it is made, which is a better reason to book early than any argument about price.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory KHDA subjects fit around eight or nine IGCSE entries?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and states combined classes are strictly prohibited. Ask which Arabic entry your child sits, because first language and additional language are separate qualifications.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to cover from this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, Computer Science and the smaller humanities entries. Mathematics, the three sciences and English are usually matched within a few days. This is identical in Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan, because the constraint is the citywide supply of those specialists rather than anything local. For a scarce entry, paying a travel premium narrows the pool you choose from rather than widening it.

faqs.question: Should we wait until Year 11 before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper and more effective. A weekly session through Year 10 lets a tutor see marked class work as it happens, which is how a tiering problem or an algebra fluency gap gets found while there is still a year to fix it. Families who start in Year 10 rarely need an intensive Year 11 block, and the two-year total is usually lower than a single crisis term. The tutor is also already matched when study leave arrives and the whole city is looking.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do with assessed school work?
faqs.answer: Teach the technique it requires, explain what each assessment strand rewards, question a weak plan until it works, show how a published piece is structured, and give written feedback on your child's own draft. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite, dictate or supply content that appears in the submission. IB Gram tutors state that at the first session of any coursework block and give feedback in writing, so a school asking what help was received gets a defensible answer.

faqs.question: So is there any real disadvantage to living in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: One, and it is manageable: a quiet hour is harder to arrange in an apartment than in a villa with a door. Travel is actually slightly better here, because the community is compact and bus pickup is quicker than the long loops that spread Al Furjan arrivals across fifty minutes. The schools are shared, the local supply of subject specialists is equally thin in both, and in-home rates are quoted in the same band. The housing changes the logistics and nothing about the syllabus.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-discovery-gard.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IGCSE home tutor in Discovery Gardens against what neighbours in Al Furjan are doing, the comparison matters less than one free document. Ask the school's exams officer for your child's entry list, which names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, then send it with the hour your household can realistically protect. We will name a tutor matched to that board and run a free trial around a marked paper. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, 15:30 to 21:30, and need a desk and headphones rather than a spare room.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE subjects for students in Years 10 and 11. Each profile names the syllabus codes that tutor teaches and the papers they mark practice against, so you can judge the fit before you pay for a single hour.

intro.heading: The price of IGCSE tuition in Downtown Dubai, stated plainly
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number rather than the hourly one, because that is the figure that decides whether tutoring lasts a term or a fortnight. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market run from about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions up to AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A Downtown household comparing those two lines is mostly comparing travel, not teaching.

The hourly bands behind those monthly totals are easy to find once you look. EdFlik lists tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52, both online and both staffed in large part by university-student tutors. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for its premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits across Dubai are quoted between AED 180 and 500 depending on distance and subject. Those are market rates from other providers, not an IB Gram price list.

Downtown Dubai makes the travel line unusually expensive. The district is dense, vertical and surrounded by the busiest road network in the emirate. A tutor living in Al Barsha who agrees to a 5pm session in a Burj Khalifa district tower is committing to perhaps ninety minutes of driving and parking for sixty minutes of teaching, and no honest pricing model absorbs that for free. It is recovered either in the rate, in a minimum two-hour booking, or in a quietly narrower pool of people willing to take the job at all.

That last cost is the one parents notice too late. Hiring on proximity shrinks the candidate list to whoever happens to live within a short drive and happens to be free at the hour your child is home. For a general IGCSE need that may be fine. For Extended-tier Physics 0625, for Pearson Edexcel's modular structure, or for a student who has to lift two grades in Chemistry 0620 before a November entry closes, proximity is the wrong filter. The subject match matters more than the postcode, and once lessons are online the postcode stops mattering at all.

So this page does three things. It publishes the AED bands with their sources, because three of the six pages currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries quote no price whatsoever and the two that do quote US dollars. It compares formats on the things that actually differ: contact minutes, travel, tutor pool, cancellation risk. And it is explicit about delivery. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. IGCSE tuition in Downtown Dubai reaches your child as live, one-to-one online lessons.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.programmesIntro: Downtown and the central corridor hold a mix of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel centres, so a tutoring plan has to name a board before it names a topic. These are the stages an IGCSE student here passes through, and what each one costs in tutoring hours rather than in adjectives.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before option choices are made. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and the results are the first external signal a parent gets about whether Extended-tier IGCSE is realistic in two years' time. Support at this stage is cheap in hours and expensive to skip: algebraic fluency and written explanation are both built here.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Downtown corridor often move school at the end of Year 9, from a through-school in Al Quoz or Sobha Hartland to a different curriculum entirely. A Checkpoint report travels with the student and is the cheapest diagnostic available, because it costs nothing extra and already exists.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, tiered entry in several subjects, and an exam series in June with November as the resit route for UAE candidates. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended; the sciences 0625, 0620 and 0610 follow the same pattern. Grade 9 to 1 reporting now sits alongside A* to G depending on the subject and the centre.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. A Downtown family with children at two different schools may be reading two different zone timetables.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other half of the British-curriculum market in Dubai. Mathematics A carries the code 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, and the structure differs from Cambridge in paper count, tiering and the availability of a January-adjacent results route. Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, with provisional timetables published ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from a November series reach students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. For a Downtown student retaking one subject, that is a usable second chance inside the same academic year.

programmes.name: Post-16: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the gate to both routes, and the two cost different amounts to support. A Level narrows to three or four subjects with deep content; the IB Diploma keeps six plus the core, which spreads tutoring thinner across more subjects. Deciding in Year 11 rather than Year 12 keeps the bill predictable.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Several sit within reach of the central corridor, which changes the post-16 shortlist for families currently assuming their through-school is the only option.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Downtown and central-corridor families ask about most, with the syllabus code that decides which past papers are worth buying. A tutor who cannot name the code is guessing at the paper structure, and you are paying for the guess.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Edexcel Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most requested subject in this corridor. Marks are lost in the same four places every series: algebraic manipulation under time pressure, unstructured multi-step problems, trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, and method marks thrown away by unshown working. Extended tier assumes fluency the Core tier never tests.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Maths AA at Higher Level. Calculus arrives here first, and students who have only ever met procedural algebra find the differentiation and integration questions a genuine step up. Useful as a bridge, punishing as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, followed by anything requiring a rearranged equation with units carried through. The practical paper rewards students who can describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it, which is a writing skill as much as a physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and reacting-mass calculations separate grades more than any other topic, and organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition over memorisation. Qualitative analysis questions ask for observation plus inference, and students routinely give one and lose the mark for the other.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. The marks sit in command-term discipline: describe, explain and suggest ask for different things, and a correct biological fact written in answer to the wrong command term scores nothing. Data and graph interpretation questions are the fastest place to gain.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Taken by students who need science breadth without three separate IGCSEs. The syllabus trims each discipline, which makes revision selection critical: using triple-science past papers wastes hours on content that is not assessed. IGCSE Combined Science needs its own paper diet, not a borrowed one.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading paper marks hinge on selecting evidence and explaining effect rather than summarising plot. Directed writing tasks are lost on register and audience. Students who read widely often still underperform because nobody has shown them how the mark scheme rewards analysis of language choices.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A common choice in a city where most students speak more than one language at home. Listening and speaking components carry real weight, and the written paper rewards controlled accuracy over ambition. Timed practice with feedback on error patterns moves grades faster than vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definitional precision carry the paper. Students lose marks drawing an unlabelled axis or shifting the wrong curve, then lose more by describing a policy without evaluating it. The UAE context questions reward students who read local business coverage.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole subject. Generic textbook answers score low; answers anchored in the stimulus material score well. Calculation questions on break-even, cash flow and ratios are reliable marks that students skip because they assume the subject is essay-only.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring actually costs in Dubai, with sources
paragraphs: A direct answer first. IGCSE tuition in Dubai is advertised between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour as of October 2026, and where a particular tutor sits in that range is decided by qualification, format and travel rather than by subject. The cheapest end is online and largely staffed by university students. The most expensive end is a named premium tutor. In-home one-to-one sits in the middle and carries the travel cost inside the rate.

The individual figures are published by the providers themselves. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour. Tutopiya lists from about AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors as high as AED 500, with subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. None of these are IB Gram prices and none should be read as such.

What makes this worth publishing is that most of the cluster does not. Three of the six competitor pages measured in this market quote no price at all, and one of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. The two that do quote figures use US dollars, a currency a Dubai family does not transact in. A table of AED bands with named sources is the most useful thing a page in this market can carry, and it is uncontested.

Read the table below as a market map rather than a quotation. Then ask any provider two questions: is the rate per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT. Those two answers move the real monthly figure more than any discount negotiation will.
bullets: Ask whether the quoted figure is per hour or per lesson before comparing anything
Ask whether the rate includes VAT, and get the answer in writing
Ask what a cancelled session costs and how much notice is required
Ask whether the first session is charged, and on what condition any trial is free

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what it buys in a tower district
paragraphs: The gap between an online qualified tutor at AED 150 to 300 and an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 is not a teaching-quality gap. It is a logistics gap, and in Downtown Dubai it is wider than in a villa community. A tutor driving to a Burj Khalifa district tower at 5pm faces Sheikh Zayed Road, then visitor parking that often requires a resident to meet them at a barrier, then a lift queue in a building with several hundred apartments. Fifteen minutes of that is normal and forty is not unusual.

Somebody pays for those minutes. Usually the family does, through a higher hourly rate, a two-hour minimum, or a package priced at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Sometimes the tutor pays, by accepting less per productive hour, and the predictable consequence is that the tutor leaves for easier work and the family starts again with somebody new in the middle of a term. Neither outcome improves a Chemistry grade.

The honest case for in-home tutoring is not cost. It is that a young child concentrates better with an adult physically present, or that a household has no quiet space a laptop can occupy, or that a parent wants to overhear the lesson. Those are real reasons and a Downtown family that holds one of them should hire locally and pay the premium knowingly. What they should not do is pay the premium by accident while believing it buys better teaching.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody from IB Gram will arrive at a Downtown address. Home visiting is a service offered only in India. What a Dubai family gets instead is the whole of a subject-specialist pool rather than the slice of it that lives within a twenty-minute drive, at a rate with no driving inside it.

sections.heading: Three ways Downtown families lose money on IGCSE tutoring
paragraphs: The first is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A parent sees a 5 in Physics, books twenty hours, and discovers in week six that the student understood the content and was losing marks on command terms and unshown working. Twenty hours of content revision cannot fix a technique problem. One marked paper read properly by a subject specialist would have found it in an hour, and the correction would have taken four sessions rather than twenty.

The second is the wrong past papers. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are both heavily used in this corridor, and so are Core and Extended tiers within Cambridge. A student sitting Coordinated Science 0654 who revises from triple-science papers is working on assessed-elsewhere content. A Foundation-tier Edexcel candidate drilling Higher questions is losing confidence on material that will not appear. Both mistakes are invisible to a family and obvious to anyone who has taught the syllabus, and both are pure waste.

The third is paying for a generalist in a subject that needs a specialist. A capable all-rounder can lift a Year 10 student in several subjects at once, and for most families that is good value. In Extended Physics 0625, in Additional Mathematics 0606 and in the moles and organic topics of Chemistry 0620, the gap between a generalist and a specialist is visible in the first session. Paying generalist rates for specialist work is cheap per hour and expensive per grade.

The avoidable version of all three is the same: one diagnostic hour, a named syllabus code, and a tutor chosen for the paper rather than the postcode. That sequence costs less than a week of the wrong tutoring.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and why the board changes the bill
paragraphs: Parents in the central corridor frequently do not know which board their child sits, because schools talk about subjects and not codes. It matters financially. The two boards set different numbers of papers, tier differently, and sit in different series windows, so the number of hours needed before an exam is genuinely different. A tutor who asks for the code in the first message is saving you money; one who does not is about to guess.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For UAE candidates the live series are June and November.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, so the only sensible instruction is to work from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page.

The practical effect for a Downtown household with two children at two schools is that they may be running two different calendars, two different tiering decisions and two different past-paper libraries. Treating that as one tutoring plan is how a term of effort produces one improved grade instead of two.

sections.heading: What a term of online IGCSE support actually contains
paragraphs: A term is roughly twelve teaching weeks. Bought as one weekly hour, that is twelve hours, and twelve hours is enough to move one subject meaningfully if they are spent in the right order. Spent badly, twelve hours is a tour of the syllabus that ends where it started. The order that works is diagnosis, then the two or three topics carrying the most lost marks, then timed technique, then a full paper under exam conditions with the marking read aloud.

Weeks one and two go on the student's own last paper. Not a new test, the real one, because the errors in it are the errors under the conditions that matter. Weeks three to seven take the topics that paper exposed and teach them properly, with work set between sessions and marked before the next lesson starts. Weeks eight and nine move to question technique: command terms, working shown, units carried, and the discipline of answering what was asked. Weeks ten to twelve are timed papers and their post-mortems.

What that buys at the published mid-market rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour is twelve to thirty-six hundred dirhams for one subject for a term, which sits inside Bestimate's AED 600 to 1,200 monthly band. A family running two subjects doubles it. A family running an exam-term intensive block in the eight weeks before a June series will sit in the higher band simply because the hours are higher, not because the rate is.

Set against the rest of a Dubai education budget, that is a small line. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A flat fee year is the easiest year in which to fund a term of targeted tutoring without adding to total household spend.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: This question has a clear answer and almost nobody in this market publishes it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is broad. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you a specific amount is quoting something it cannot source.

Two further points a parent can use. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carrying a similar bar.

So the useful question to ask a prospective tutor is simply whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and the useful thing to know is that it costs them nothing to hold. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform; it does not hold and does not claim KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge accreditation of any kind, and no page here should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and what you must never buy
paragraphs: This matters on a cost page because the most expensive thing available in this market is cheap. One provider in the researched corpus sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. What that buys is an academic-honesty breach, and in the IB system the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. The same logic applies to IGCSE coursework components and to any assessed piece submitted under the student's name.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a mark scheme rewards, help a student narrow a research question, ask the questions that expose a weak argument, comment on a draft the student has written, and teach referencing. A tutor must never write the IA, draft the Extended Essay, produce the coursework or edit a piece to the point where the thinking is no longer the student's. No tutor at IB Gram will do any of that, and a tutor who offers it should be refused.

There is a related rule about materials. Published syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference and link them from the official site, not hand over copies. A page that offers a downloadable mark scheme is telling you something about how it treats rules in general.

Said plainly: you are paying for teaching hours and feedback, and the written work stays the student's own. That is a differentiator in a market where at least one ranking site sells the opposite, and it is the only version of the service that leaves a student's qualification intact.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency, and the money you do not need to spend on it
paragraphs: Families budgeting for IGCSE tutoring often fold in a vague fear about UAE certificate equivalency, and the fear is usually more expensive than the facts. For the British track, the Ministry of Education's published requirements are that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and submits proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details save money. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count, so a family paying for extra tutoring in them on equivalency grounds is paying for something the count does not use. And the threshold is a pass at E or grade 3, not a high grade, which means equivalency and university entry are different problems with different budgets. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the same page sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no published points threshold that can be responsibly restated here, so the only honest instruction is to verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and cannot influence its outcome. The process belongs to the Ministry of Education and the emirate authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of it. Describing it as one would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, which is precisely the kind of pressure a parent should price at zero.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Every British-curriculum school in Dubai runs mandatory UAE subjects next to its licensed curriculum, and families regularly discover this only when a report card arrives with an unfamiliar grade on it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific enough to be worth knowing. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is counted in forty-minute lesson units. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential rather than a marketing line. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited.

For a tutoring budget the consequence is simple. Support in these subjects follows the school's own scheme of work and nothing else, and a tutor who proposes alternative material for them has misunderstood the rule. It is also worth remembering that these grades sit outside the five IGCSE subjects the MoE counts for British-track equivalency, so their place in the plan is school progression rather than attestation.

process.description: Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier and the year group. For a Downtown family that usually means reading it off the last report or asking the school office once. This single step removes the most common cause of wasted hours, which is a tutor preparing for the wrong paper.

process.description: The first session works from the most recent school assessment rather than a new test. A subject specialist marks it, names the topics costing marks, and separates content gaps from technique losses. You get that in writing, and it is useful whether or not you continue.

process.description: Before the second session you receive a plan: which topics, in what order, how many hours, and what the student does between lessons. If the plan needs twelve hours rather than thirty, it says twelve. A plan without an hour count is not a plan, it is an open invoice.

process.description: Sessions are scheduled around the school day and the household's evening, not around a tutor's drive. Lessons run over live video, one-to-one. Because nobody is travelling, a 7.30pm slot is as available as a 4pm one, and a slot missed for a school event moves without renegotiating the rate.

process.title: Review after the next school assessment
process.description: The plan is re-cut when the next real mark arrives, not at the end of a package. If the named topics have recovered and new ones have not appeared, hours come down. If the student has stalled, the tutor match is reconsidered rather than defended.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Downtown Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tutoring across Dubai is advertised between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors going as high as AED 500. In a tower district the figure sits higher in that range because travel, visitor parking and lift time are inside the rate. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300 for the same teaching minutes. IB Gram delivers IGCSE support online rather than in homes in the UAE, so there is no travel component in the hour you pay for.

faqs.question: What does a month of IGCSE tuition cost for a Downtown Dubai family?
faqs.answer: For one weekly hour, Bestimate's Dubai estimates run about AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Two subjects roughly doubles the figure. These are market rates published by other providers and reviewed in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire online or in-home tuition in a Burj Khalifa district tower?
faqs.answer: Online is cheaper on published rates and cheaper again on productive minutes. A qualified online subject tutor is listed at AED 150 to 300 an hour against AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit, and the online hour starts on the minute while the in-home hour absorbs parking, a resident escort to the lift and the building's evening lift traffic. The honest reasons to prefer in-home are a young child who concentrates better with an adult present, or a home with no quiet space for a laptop. Cost is not one of them.

faqs.question: Which syllabus code should I give you when I ask for an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Whichever one is on your child's report or in the school's curriculum letter. The common ones in this corridor are Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology and 0654 Coordinated Science, plus Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A and 4PH1 Physics. Add the tier, Core or Extended for Cambridge and Foundation or Higher for Edexcel. Those two pieces of information decide which past papers are worth the student's time, and getting them wrong is the single most common way a term of revision is wasted.

faqs.question: Why would a nearby tutor be the wrong choice for my child?
faqs.answer: Because proximity filters for the wrong thing. Searching within a short drive of Downtown narrows the list to people who live close and happen to be free when your child is home, and that list may contain nobody who has taught Extended Physics 0625 or the moles and organic sections of Chemistry 0620. For broad Year 10 support a strong generalist nearby is good value. For a specific grade gap in a specific paper, the subject match decides the outcome and the postcode decides nothing, because lessons run over video either way.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service provided only in India. IGCSE support for a Downtown Dubai family is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The page uses the phrase home tutor because it is what parents search for, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a quiet redirect. What you gain in exchange is access to the whole subject-specialist pool instead of the part of it within driving distance of your building.

faqs.question: How many hours of tutoring does one IGCSE grade usually take?
faqs.answer: There is no guaranteed conversion and anyone offering one should be treated with scepticism. What can be said is that a term of twelve weekly hours, spent in the right order, is enough to move a single subject for a student who is one or two grades below target. The order matters more than the total: two hours on the student's own marked paper, five on the topics it exposed, two on question technique, three on timed full papers. The same twelve hours spread randomly across a syllabus usually ends where it began.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a government permit, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit and no to the cost. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any page quoting a figure.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on IGCSE coursework help we are paying for?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before the first session. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, help the student narrow a question, challenge a weak argument and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never produce the piece, redraft it to completion, or supply text the student submits as their own. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying that risks the student's qualification, not the seller's. The work stays the student's own.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE exams my child will actually sit?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates use the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in June and November, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones; Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026. Always work from the live official timetable.

faqs.question: How quickly do November IGCSE results come back if we need a retake?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel, November results reach students in January: November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June results come far faster, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. That timing is what makes November useful for a Downtown student who missed a target in June, because the improved grade exists inside the same academic year. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so confirm the exact dates on the official timetable page before planning around them.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry of Education requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry and the emirate authority, not by a tutoring service, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

faqs.question: Can we pay for one session to find out whether tutoring is even needed?
faqs.answer: That is the sensible way to start. A single diagnostic hour works from the student's most recent school paper rather than a new test, and produces a written list of the topics costing the most marks and a judgement on whether the problem is content, technique or timing. Families who start here usually buy fewer total hours and spend them better, and a fair number discover the weak subject was not the one they suspected. There is no obligation to continue, with the same tutor or at all.

faqs.question: Does a Downtown Dubai family need tutoring in Arabic and Islamic Education too?
faqs.answer: Those subjects are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is built from forty-minute units, with at least twenty-five minutes advised per lesson. Support in them has to follow the school's own scheme, because using different or additional content without prior MoE permission is prohibited. They also sit outside the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency, so budget for them as school progression rather than as an attestation requirement.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutoring provider before I pay anything?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Is the rate per hour or per lesson. Does it include VAT. What does a cancelled session cost and how much notice is needed. Is the first session charged, and if a trial is free, on what condition. Which syllabus code and tier will the tutor prepare for. And does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which costs them nothing and lasts two years. Any provider that cannot answer those in writing is asking you to price a service you cannot see.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Academic City is actually being asked to fix
paragraphs: Start with the syllabus code, because that is where most of the wasted money in this market goes. 'IGCSE Maths' is not one qualification. Cambridge runs Mathematics 0580, and the 9-1 graded version 0980, with Core and Extended tiers that sit different papers. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers, and Specification B, 4MB1, which is a different beast again. A tutor who knows one and not the other will teach content your child does not sit and skip content they do.

The same applies across the sciences. Cambridge Physics is 0625 with an alternative-to-practical option; Chemistry 0620; Biology 0610; Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award. Pearson's equivalents are 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1. The content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not. Pearson Physics has no practical examination and assesses experimental skills within the written papers; Cambridge offers a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical, and which one your child sits is the school's decision, not yours.

So the first thing to establish, before any tutoring is booked, is which specification your child's school entered them for. Dubai English Speaking College sits inside Academic City and runs the British route; across the road in Silicon Oasis, GEMS Wellington Academy and other schools in this cluster make their own board choices subject by subject. It is common for a single student to sit Cambridge in one subject and Edexcel in another. Ask the examinations officer for the syllabus codes in writing and bring that list to the first session.

IB Gram delivers this tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - that is an India-only service - and the phrase in this page's title is the phrase parents search rather than a promise to drive to Al Ruwayyah. The practical gain is that the tutor can be the person who teaches 4MA1 Higher routinely, rather than whoever lives near Dragon Mart and remembers GCSE maths.

There is a second reason the code matters in this specific district. Academic City sits behind the university campuses off Al Ain Road, and the pool of adults within a twenty-minute drive who teach a named international specification routinely is small. A tutor who lives near Dragon Mart and once taught GCSE in the United Kingdom is not a tutor who knows what the Pearson 4CH1 mark scheme rewards on an electrolysis question. Proximity is a weak filter on exactly the quality that decides the grade, which is why removing travel from the matching decision widens rather than narrows the choice.

The rest of this page is syllabus-first. Paper structures with weightings. Core against Extended, with what the tier ceiling actually means for a university application later. Cambridge against Edexcel in the same subject. The specific places marks go missing, subject by subject. The June and November series counted backwards. And the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides how many of these subjects your child actually needs to pass.
