dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic.programmesIntro: IGCSE is the middle of a longer route, and the tutoring question changes depending on which part of it your child is in. These are the three stages Academic City families book help for.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 into IGCSE
programmes.description: The two years before the IGCSE course starts are where the algebra and written-English foundations are either built or left incomplete. Nothing is externally examined, so weakness is invisible until Year 10. The specific gaps that cause trouble later are negative-number manipulation, fraction arithmetic without a calculator, rearranging formulae, and writing a paragraph that answers the question asked.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the Year 9 option choices matter more than parents expect, because they determine whether a child enters Core or Extended tier in mathematics and whether they take three separate sciences or a co-ordinated double award. Those choices cap the achievable grade. Ask the school at the Year 9 parents' evening which tier they intend to enter your child for, and what would change their mind.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: A two-year course per subject, externally examined at the end, usually across two or three papers. Cambridge grades on A*-G or 9-1 depending on the syllabus variant; Pearson grades 9-1. Tiering decides the grade ceiling: Cambridge Core caps at C or grade 5, Extended runs the full range; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5, Higher runs to 9.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is the cheaper year to buy tutoring in and the one families skip. By the February of Year 11 the content is nearly complete and the work becomes past-paper technique under time pressure, which is useful but cannot rebuild a missing topic. Academic City families who start in the first term of Year 10 typically buy fewer total hours than those who start after the Year 11 mocks.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The step up is steeper in mathematics and the sciences than in anything else. A Level Mathematics assumes the Extended tier content as automatic, and the IB Diploma's Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches assumes it too. Students who scraped a 6 by relying on calculator methods find the first term of Year 12 brutal, because the new content arrives faster than the old content can be repaired.
programmes.countryNote: In Academic City the route splits visibly: Dubai English Speaking College continues to A Level on site, while families wanting the IB Diploma move towards Silicon Oasis, Mirdif or Nad Al Sheba. Either way, a short bridging block of tutoring in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the highest-value tuition most of these families ever buy.

programmes.name: November resit route
programmes.description: A subject taken again in the November series, either because a grade was below a sixth-form entry requirement or because a paper went wrong. Cambridge and Pearson both run November sessions, so the gap is roughly five months rather than a full year. Entry is through a school or an approved centre, and the registration deadline sits months before the exam itself.
programmes.countryNote: For a resit, the first job is a forensic one: get the component-level breakdown from the school rather than only the overall grade. A grade 5 built on a strong Paper 1 and a collapsed Paper 2 needs completely different work from a grade 5 that was uniformly weak. That breakdown decides the entire plan, and most families have never asked for it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the syllabus code, what the papers actually demand, and the specific place marks go missing. That is the level at which an IGCSE tutor earns their fee.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Two papers, non-calculator and calculator depending on variant. Extended adds functions, calculus-adjacent gradient work, vectors, matrices and harder trigonometry. Marks go missing on method: answers given without working score a fraction of the available marks, and rounding too early in multi-step problems loses accuracy marks throughout.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, both calculator permitted. Higher tier ceiling is grade 9, Foundation caps at 5. The style is more procedural than Cambridge and rewards fluent algebraic manipulation. The common loss is in the extended multi-mark problems at the end of each paper, which students routinely leave blank rather than attempting partially.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry the heaviest mark load and produce the most confusion. Cambridge offers a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical; Pearson assesses experimental skills inside the written papers. Marks go on equation selection and unit handling rather than arithmetic, and on explanations that describe instead of explaining.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry are the three reliable mark-losers. Students who can recite the reactivity series still cannot write a balanced ionic equation under time pressure. Practical questions on separation techniques and gas tests reward specific vocabulary, and vague answers earn nothing even when the chemistry is understood.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem, not the difficulty. Marks are lost on command terms: 'describe' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and students answer both the same way. Data and graph questions reward reading the axes first, and genetics questions reward drawing the cross out rather than attempting it mentally.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into the equivalent of two subjects, assessed across combined papers. The trap is assuming it is easier: the content is reduced but the examination still moves between biology, chemistry and physics within a single paper, and students lose time re-orienting. Tutoring works best organised by paper section rather than by subject.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Marks are lost on form: a student who writes a good essay when a letter was asked for forfeits the whole form mark band. Reading questions reward selecting and using quotation economically, and the most common error is copying long stretches of the passage instead of analysing a phrase.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in 0511, a speaking component. The paper rewards accuracy over ambition: controlled, correct sentences score better than complex attempts with errors. Note-taking and summary tasks are the most teachable components and the ones where the fastest grade movement happens.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward application to the case material in front of the student and both punish generic answers. In Economics, diagrams must be labelled, titled and referred to in the prose to earn marks. In Business Studies, the higher mark bands require a judgement with justification, not a list of advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Both are source-and-structure subjects. Geography marks go missing on case-study specificity - a named place, a figure, a date - and on skills questions involving graphs and maps. History marks go on source evaluation that comments on provenance rather than content, which is a technique rather than knowledge and can be taught quickly.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Computer Science combines theory with a pseudocode and programming component where students lose marks on trace tables and on writing algorithms that do not handle edge cases. ICT is practical-assessment heavy and the loss is almost always procedural: steps omitted, evidence not captured, file naming conventions ignored.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and the A Level bridge
subjects.description: A short bridging programme rather than an examined subject for most students here: indices and surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, basic differentiation and the trigonometric identities A Level and IB Diploma mathematics assume from day one. Six to eight sessions in the summer after Year 11 removes most of the first-term shock.

sections.heading: Paper structures and weightings for the subjects this cluster actually sits
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is the sum of two or three components with fixed weightings, and a student who does not know those weightings cannot allocate revision sensibly. A paper worth half the subject deserves half the preparation, and in several subjects students spend most of their time on the component they are already comfortable with. Getting the structure on paper, for each subject, is a twenty-minute exercise that changes how a whole term is spent.

The structures also differ between boards in ways that matter operationally. Cambridge Physics offers either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school chooses; Pearson Physics has no practical component and places experimental skills inside the written papers. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator paper in some variants; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both. A student who has drilled mental arithmetic for a paper that allows a calculator has wasted the hours.

The table below sets out the shape of the components for the subjects most often requested in this cluster. Treat it as orientation and confirm the exact variant and option with your child's examinations officer, because syllabuses are revised and schools make per-cohort choices. Never work from a printed summary that nobody has dated.

One point of technique that applies across every subject here: the mark allocation printed beside each question is instruction, not decoration. A four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, and a student who writes one point beautifully has lost three marks by misreading a number printed in bold on the page.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, Foundation against Higher: the tier decision and its ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in the IGCSE course and it is usually made by the school at the end of Year 9 or during Year 10, sometimes without a conversation. Cambridge Core and Extended sit different papers covering different amounts of the syllabus, and Core caps the achievable grade. Pearson Foundation and Higher work the same way, with Foundation capping at grade 5 and Higher running to grade 9.

The temptation with a struggling student is the lower tier, because a secure grade looks better than a risky one. Sometimes that is right. But the cap has consequences two years out: a sixth form requiring grade 6 in mathematics for A Level Mathematics or for the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches has excluded a Core candidate before they sat the paper, and for Ministry of Education equivalency the requirement is only a grade no lower than E or 3, which Core comfortably reaches. So the question is not 'can they pass' but 'what does this close'.

The honest version of the conversation needs two pieces of information the school holds and you probably do not: the student's current performance on Extended-tier past-paper questions specifically, and the sixth-form entry requirements for the courses they are likely to want. A tutor is useful here mainly as a diagnostician - two timed Extended papers marked properly will tell you more than a term of impressions.

Where a tier change is worth fighting for, the work is specific rather than general. Extended tier in mathematics adds a defined set of topics on top of Core, and most of the gap is in those topics rather than across the whole subject. A targeted block through the first term of Year 10 is often enough to move a borderline student up, and it is far cheaper than discovering the ceiling in Year 12.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel in the same subject
paragraphs: Schools in this cluster mix boards, and a single Year 11 student may sit Cambridge in three subjects and Pearson in two. Parents are rarely told why, and the answer is usually departmental preference built up over years rather than anything about the child. The two boards cover similar content to similar standards; what differs is assessment architecture, and that difference changes how a student should revise.

The clearest case is physics. Cambridge 0625 carries a practical or alternative-to-practical component, which means laboratory technique and apparatus knowledge are directly examined. Pearson 4PH1 has no practical paper and tests experimental skills inside the written papers, usually as method-design and data-analysis questions. A student moving schools mid-course between these two specifications is not covering the same ground, and the gap needs mapping deliberately rather than assumed away.

Mathematics differs too. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; Pearson 4MA1 permits calculators throughout. Cambridge Specification style leans towards structured multi-part questions; Pearson 4MA1's longer problems at the end of each paper reward persistence. These are small differences that compound across a hundred hours of revision, which is why matching a tutor to the code rather than the subject name is not pedantry.

Practically, the only thing you need to do is get the codes. Ask the examinations officer for the full entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option. Bring it to the first session. A tutor who asks for that list before quoting is working the right way round; one who does not will teach a generic course and you will pay for content your child never sits.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Most IGCSE mark loss in this cluster is not caused by not knowing the content. It is caused by a small set of repeatable technique failures, and the reason tutoring moves grades quickly in Year 11 is that these are faster to fix than content is to learn. A tutor who starts by marking two timed papers properly will usually find three or four recurring errors that account for the bulk of the missing marks.

In mathematics the recurring failures are working not shown, rounding applied too early, and the last long question left blank. In the sciences they are command-term confusion, units omitted, and explanations that describe a phenomenon without giving a cause. In English it is form: a student writes a competent essay when a letter or an article was specified and loses the entire form band regardless of quality. In the humanities it is specificity: no named example, no figure, no date.

The method that works is an error log, kept by the student rather than the tutor. Every marked question that lost a mark goes in with the reason in the student's own words. After three or four sessions the log shows a pattern, and the pattern becomes the lesson plan. It is unglamorous and it is the single most effective thing a sixteen-year-old can do with a returned paper.

On materials: we cite and link official syllabuses, specimen papers and mark schemes on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than supplying copies of them. Reproducing board material is a copyright matter, and the official source is also the only one guaranteed to be the current version.

sections.heading: The June and November series counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. UAE candidates sit June and November. The February/March series is offered to India only, and a page telling a Dubai parent to prepare for a February exam is giving them a date they cannot use.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. For a sense of how far ahead the machinery sits: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

One Cambridge detail that catches families out and appears on almost no tutoring page: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If you are checking a timetable yourself, check which zone your child's centre sits in first.

The planning consequence is simple. Work backwards from the written papers to the school's internal coursework and mock deadlines, and from those to the point at which tutoring has to start to be useful rather than consoling. For a June series candidate, the decision point is the first term of Year 11, not March.

sections.heading: Practical science when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the fair objection to online science tutoring and it deserves a direct answer. If your child's school has entered them for a Cambridge practical examination, the apparatus work has to happen in the school laboratory, and no tutor on a video call can substitute for standing at a bench. What a tutor can do is everything around it, and that turns out to be where the marks are.

Practical examinations and alternative-to-practical papers do not mainly test manual dexterity. They test whether a student can identify the independent and dependent variables, choose a sensible range and interval, state controls, read a scale to the right precision, record to consistent significant figures, plot a graph with sensible axes and scale, draw a line of best fit rather than joining points, and write an evaluation that names a specific limitation and a specific improvement. Every one of those is teachable on a screen with a dataset.

For Pearson candidates the position is simpler still, because 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 have no practical examination and assess experimental skills inside the written papers as method-design and data-analysis questions. That is written-paper technique, and it is exactly what a weekly online session is good at. Students who have never thought about why a question asks for 'two further readings' pick up marks quickly once somebody explains what the examiner wants.

What we do not do is supply board practical papers or mark schemes, or coach a student through work the school is assessing as their own. Where a school sets internally assessed practical work, the tutor's role is to teach the underlying skills and to question the student's own write-up, not to contribute to it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on IGCSE coursework and the line we will not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or internally assessed components - English in certain variants, ICT, art, and internally assessed practical work in the sciences. Wherever a mark is awarded for work the student submits as their own, the same rule applies as at Diploma level: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback, and the student produces every word and every number.

The distinction is operational rather than philosophical. A tutor may explain what the assessment criteria reward, show what a strong response looks like in general terms, teach the skill the task depends on, and read a draft and comment on it. A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submission, rewrite a paragraph into better English, choose the topic, or generate or process the data. If the student cannot explain why a sentence says what it says, it should not be there.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the search results your child's subject sits in include operators selling completed coursework. One competitor in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. The exposure is not theirs. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, and at sixteen the consequence can be a subject grade withheld in a series they cannot easily retake before a sixth-form offer lapses.

So we say the boundary out loud rather than leaving it in a terms page. It makes some sessions slower - a draft comes back with questions rather than corrections - and it is the only version of coursework support that is safe for the student to accept.
bullets: Allowed: teaching the underlying skill, explaining criteria, questioning a draft, written feedback the student acts on
Not allowed: supplied text, rewritten paragraphs, chosen topics, generated or processed data

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: what MoE equivalency actually requires
paragraphs: Families in this cluster planning on a UAE university need to know what the Ministry of Education equivalency route asks of an IGCSE candidate, and the published rule is narrower than the version circulating in this market. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two further points follow from the same source and both save money. First, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. Second, the grade threshold is low - E or grade 3 - which means equivalency is almost never the reason to buy tutoring. A ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published requirement is five, excluding those two. Accuracy here is worth more than volume.

For the American track, for comparison, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. We publish no IB points threshold anywhere on this site, because no IB equivalency figure in this project has been read on a Ministry of Education source.

Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, and no tutoring is required for it. Describe it, check it on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority, and plan the subject list in Year 10 rather than discovering a gap in Year 13. The real tutoring question is not equivalency but the sixth-form and university entry grades, which sit far above the equivalency floor.

sections.heading: Finding a tutor who knows your child's actual specification
paragraphs: The matching question for IGCSE is narrower than for most subjects, and that narrowness is why distance is the wrong filter. You are not looking for a maths tutor. You are looking for somebody who teaches Pearson 4MA1 Higher, or Cambridge 0580 Extended, routinely enough to know which question types appear where and what the mark scheme rewards. In the eastern suburbs of Dubai, the number of such people within a twenty-minute drive of Academic City is not large.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see the permit.

There is one arrangement to decline rather than pursue. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. If somebody offers your child's own subject teacher privately, that is a problem for the teacher and potentially for your child.

Where a specification is genuinely hard to staff - and 4MB1, some second-language options and a few of the less common humanities are - we say so at the consultation and give a realistic wait rather than substituting a generalist. That disclosure is uncomfortable and it is better than the alternative, which is finding out in lesson three.

process.title: Send the entry list, not the subject names
process.description: Subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option for each examination your child is entered for. The examinations officer at the school can produce this in a few minutes. It is the single most useful thing you can give a tutor, and it prevents an entire term of teaching the wrong specification.

process.title: Two marked timed papers as a diagnosis
process.description: Before planning anything, the tutor has the student sit questions at the intended tier under timed conditions and marks them against the published mark scheme. That produces a list of recurring errors rather than an impression, and the list becomes the plan for the first six sessions.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a written summary
process.description: A real lesson on real content. Afterwards you get a plain note of what the tutor found, which components are weakest, and what they would do over the next eight weeks. If it is not right, say so and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Weekly rhythm, error log, periodic review
process.description: One session a week per subject in term time, with the student keeping an error log of every mark lost and why. Every few weeks a short written note on what has moved. If the tutor is not the right fit, we reassign rather than defend the match.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are not the same qualification and should not be taught by the same lesson plan. We ask for the entry list before matching, which sounds procedural and is the difference between useful tutoring and expensive company.

whyPoints.title: Technique first, because that is where the marks are
whyPoints.description: Most IGCSE mark loss in Year 11 is command terms, missing working, early rounding and wrong task form. These are faster to fix than content is to learn, which is why a marked timed paper is the first thing a tutor should ask for rather than the last.

whyPoints.title: The calendar UAE candidates actually use
whyPoints.description: June and November for Cambridge; May/June and November for Pearson Edexcel. The February/March series is offered to India only. Pages that tell Dubai parents to prepare for a February exam are giving them a date for the wrong country.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that cannot cost your child a grade
whyPoints.description: On any assessed work the student writes and we question. No supplied sentences, no rewritten paragraphs, no chosen topics. One operator in these search results sells completed coursework outright; the malpractice consequence of that falls on the sixteen-year-old.

whyPoints.title: We state what we are not
whyPoints.description: No UAE office or centre. No KHDA permit, because that is issued to training institutes with premises and we have none. No published star rating we cannot evidence. Every AED figure on this page is attributed to whoever published it and dated October 2026.

whyPoints.title: Online removes geography from the matching decision
whyPoints.description: From Academic City, International City or Al Khawaneej, the pool of tutors who routinely teach your child's exact specification is the same, because none of them is driving. That is a larger pool than a twenty-minute radius produces anywhere in eastern Dubai.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE home tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: You can get one-to-one IGCSE tutoring for a child living in Dubai International Academic City. With IB Gram it is delivered live online rather than by a tutor coming to your address, because home visits are a service we run in India only. The Dubai market does include tutors who travel, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel according to rates published in 2026. For IGCSE the trade-off is particularly sharp, because what decides the grade is whether the tutor knows your child's exact specification rather than how close they live.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board does my child's school in this cluster use?
faqs.answer: It varies by school and often by subject within the same school, so the only reliable answer comes from the examinations officer. Ask for the full entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option. It is common in this part of Dubai for a Year 11 student to sit Cambridge in three subjects and Pearson Edexcel in two. The codes matter because Cambridge 0625 Physics carries a practical or alternative-to-practical component while Pearson 4PH1 has no practical examination at all, which changes how a student should revise.

faqs.question: Core or Extended tier: which should an Academic City Year 10 be entered for?
faqs.answer: They are different tiers covering different amounts of the syllabus and sitting different papers. Core covers a reduced content set and caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5; Extended covers the full content and runs to A star or grade 9. The equivalent in Pearson Edexcel is Foundation, capped at grade 5, and Higher running to 9. The decision matters two years out rather than immediately: a sixth form asking for grade 6 in mathematics has excluded a Core candidate before they sat the paper.

faqs.question: Is there a practical paper for the sciences at the schools near Academic City?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and on the school's choice. Cambridge sciences offer either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school decides which; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences such as 4PH1 and 4CH1 have no practical examination and assess experimental skills inside the written papers. Ask the school which option they have entered your child for, because revision differs. For Cambridge, apparatus and technique knowledge is examined; for Pearson, the same skills appear as method-design and data-analysis questions in a written paper.

faqs.question: How can online tutoring help with practical science skills?
faqs.answer: Apparatus work has to happen in the school laboratory, and no video call substitutes for a bench. But practical and alternative-to-practical papers mainly test things that are taught perfectly well on a screen: identifying variables, choosing a sensible range and interval, stating controls, reading scales to the right precision, recording to consistent significant figures, plotting a graph with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit, and writing an evaluation naming a specific limitation and improvement. Those skills, worked through on real datasets, are where most practical-paper marks are won and lost.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in eastern Dubai struggle with most?
faqs.answer: By volume of enquiries from this cluster: Mathematics at Extended or Higher tier, Physics - particularly electricity and electromagnetism - and Chemistry, where moles calculations and electrolysis account for a large share of lost marks. English Language causes a different kind of trouble: strong students lose whole mark bands by writing in the wrong form for the task. Biology struggles are usually volume and command terms rather than difficulty. The pattern is consistent enough that a tutor can predict the weak areas before seeing a single piece of work.

faqs.question: When in the two-year IGCSE course should an Academic City family book help?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and it is usually cheaper overall. In Year 10 there is time to rebuild a missing topic properly and to argue for a tier change if the evidence supports one. By the February of Year 11 the content is nearly complete and the useful work becomes timed past-paper technique, which recovers marks quickly but cannot replace a topic that was never learned. Families in this cluster who start in the first term of Year 10 typically buy fewer total hours than those who start after the Year 11 mocks.

faqs.question: My son got a grade 5 in June. Should he resit in November?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the component-level breakdown before deciding, because the grade alone cannot answer it. A 5 built on a solid Paper 1 and a collapsed Paper 2 is a very different proposition from a 5 that was uniformly weak: the first is a repairable, specific problem with roughly five months to work on it, the second usually is not. Cambridge and Pearson both run November series, and entry is arranged through the school or an approved centre with the registration deadline sitting months before the exam window.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost around Academic City?
faqs.answer: Taking the cheapest band first: budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one, travel included, runs AED 180 to 500 per Bestimate and advertised home-tutor rates. Those are market figures from the providers named, read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. Start with the free trial lesson for ours.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, which means no tutor can price it into their rate. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the published rule is five. Note that the equivalency floor is far below any realistic university entry requirement, so plan around the course requirements, not the equivalency minimum.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the skill the task depends on, explain what the assessment criteria reward, show what a strong response looks like in general terms, and read her own draft and comment on it. A tutor cannot supply sentences that end up in the submission, rewrite a paragraph into better English, choose her topic, or generate or process her data. The test is whether she could explain, without notes, why each sentence says what it says. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, not on the tutor.

faqs.question: What are Cambridge timetable zones and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a different version of the timetable for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If you are checking dates yourself rather than relying on the school, find out which zone your child's centre sits in before you read anything off a timetable. It is a detail almost no tutoring page mentions and it has caused missed papers.

faqs.question: Could one tutor take both IGCSE maths and physics for my Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor with a physics or engineering background often teaches both to IGCSE level credibly, and the overlap in algebraic technique makes the combination efficient. Where we would not combine is when the two subjects sit on different boards with different assessment architectures and the tutor only knows one well. The entry list answers this: if it is Cambridge 0580 and Cambridge 0625, one tutor is plausible; if it is 4MA1 and 0625, check the depth in each.

faqs.question: Can sessions be scheduled around school timings and prayer times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and because no tutor is travelling it is a scheduling question rather than a logistics one. From Silicon Oasis or Mirdif, where the school sits inside the district, a 4.45pm start is realistic. From Academic City to a Silicon Oasis school, 5pm. From International City, where children travel out to Al Warqa or Mirdif, 6pm is the honest answer. Weekend mornings suit Year 11 past-paper work better than any weekday slot. Tell us the pattern you want and we fix the slot rather than rearranging week to week.

faqs.question: Will the tutor send us Cambridge past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own that material, and reproducing or distributing it is a copyright matter; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. What we do is cite and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, which has the added benefit of being the only place guaranteed to hold the current version rather than a syllabus two revisions out of date. Schools also hold past papers and will usually release them to students on request.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic.closingHeading: Send the entry list and we will tell you what we find
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-academic.closingBody: If your child is sitting IGCSEs and you live in Dubai International Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa or International City, the useful first step is the examination entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option. With that in hand we can say honestly whether we have a tutor who teaches that exact specification routinely, and what a realistic plan looks like between now and the June series. The trial lesson is free, it is a real lesson rather than a sales call, and you get a written summary of what the tutor found. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IGCSE subjects across Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel and Oxford AQA specifications for families in Dubai Creek Harbour. Each one establishes what a transferred student has and has not covered before teaching, and works from the student's own marked papers rather than a generic scheme.

intro.heading: In a new district, the syllabus question is usually a transfer question
paragraphs: Dubai Creek Harbour is a new district, which means its population is largely new arrivals, and a large share of the IGCSE students living here started the course somewhere else. Some moved from another country mid-course. Some moved from a different curriculum entirely, arriving from CBSE, an American system or a national curriculum. Some stayed in Dubai and changed schools, which sounds harmless and can mean a change of awarding body halfway through a two-year examination course.

That reframes the question behind the search. A parent asking whether anyone nearby knows this syllabus often has a student who is not weak at the subject but is missing a specific set of topics that their previous school had not reached yet, or had covered in a different order, or had covered under a different specification that tests them differently. Those are mappable gaps, and the mapping is the valuable work. Without it, tutoring becomes a re-teaching of a whole year, which is slow, expensive and unnecessary.

The second thing a new district lacks is a local teacher pool. There is little school provision inside Creek Harbour itself, so almost every student commutes out, and no body of teachers lives here because no school here employs them. A near-me search therefore returns people willing to drive across the creek rather than people who have taught your child's specification, and in a transfer case specification knowledge is exactly what is needed.

There is a third complication specific to transfers, and it is administrative rather than academic. A student who changes schools mid-course may have entries, tier decisions and coursework already in train at the old school, or may need new ones at the new school. Which awarding body, which tier, which specification code, whether any non-written component has already been completed: these have to be established in writing, and a surprising number of families discover an error in Year 11.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Dubai Creek Harbour as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the specification rather than to the postcode, which in a district with no local teacher pool is the only sensible way to match at all. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below map the board differences, the curriculum differences, and what a tutor must establish first.

Nothing here promises a grade. It gives a newly arrived family the questions that turn a vague worry about a struggling child into a list of named topics, which is the work that makes the tutoring hours afterwards worth paying for.

One further reason to begin with the mapping rather than the booking. A transferred student who is told they are behind tends to believe it, and a term spent re-covering material they already knew confirms the belief without improving anything. A written list of four named topics does the opposite: it is finite, it is achievable, and a fifteen-year-old can see the end of it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.programmesIntro: A transfer lands differently depending on when it happens. These three cases cover most of what we see from this district, and each needs a different first lesson.

programmes.name: Transferring in Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The easiest transfer to handle, because no awarding body is involved yet and there is time. What matters is identifying the specific gaps the previous system left: often algebraic manipulation taught later, or scientific vocabulary not yet introduced, or extended writing never required. A short diagnostic block followed by targeted work closes these before the examination course assumes them.
programmes.countryNote: New districts fill with families arriving at all points in the year, and schools in and around this part of Dubai take mid-year entrants routinely. A student who arrives in Year 8 and is quietly placed in a lower set on arrival should be reassessed once they have settled, because the initial placement reflects the gaps rather than the ability.

programmes.name: Transferring during Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: The hardest and most common case here. The student is midway through a two-year examination course and may now be sitting a different specification from the one they started, with different tier names, different calculator rules and a different model for assessing practical skills. The first job is a written map of what has been covered, under which specification, and what the new school assumes was covered.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the new school's examinations officer for the awarding body, specification code and tier for every subject, in writing, and ask whether any non-written component has already been completed or needs completing. For a mid-course transfer that email is more valuable than any amount of tutoring bought before it.

programmes.name: Arriving in time for results and post-16 entry
programmes.description: Students who transfer late in Year 11 or just after results face a different problem: grades earned under one system being read by a school setting its own thresholds for A Level or IB Diploma entry. A bridging block in the summer, aimed at the specific post-16 subject, is both a readiness check and the most useful preparation available.
programmes.countryNote: This is also when Ministry of Education equivalency becomes relevant for a newly arrived family. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, and the British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus Advanced Level requirements.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.subjectsIntro: Transfer gaps fall differently in each subject, because curricula differ in what they teach first. These are the subjects we cover for this district, with the gap a transferred student most often arrives with.
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same subjects by awarding body, because a transfer between Dubai schools can mean a transfer between boards. Ask the new school's examinations officer for the code in writing.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The commonest transfer gap is sequencing: topics taught in a different order, so a student may be strong in trigonometry and have never met cumulative frequency. The second is calculator habits, because specifications differ on whether arithmetic is tested without one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Transferred students frequently arrive with the content and without the practical assessment model, because boards differ on whether experimental skills are tested through a separate paper or inside the written papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations are taught at different points in different systems, so a transferred student may be a term behind on the single most load-bearing topic in the subject and fluent in everything after it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content overlaps heavily across systems; what differs is the required terminology and the command-term expectations. A transferred student often knows the biology and writes it in the wrong register for the mark scheme.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The highest-stakes transfer question in this subject is which qualification the new school has entered the student for, since First Language and Second Language are different courses with different criteria and sometimes a spoken component.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts differ by school and by year, so a transferred student has often studied texts they will not be examined on. This is the clearest case where a tutor must teach the new school's actual texts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram conventions and the expected structure of evaluation differ between systems, so a transferred student may lose marks for presentation rather than for understanding the economics.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the mark-bearing skill and not every system teaches it. Students arriving from content-recall systems write generically correct answers and lose the application marks consistently.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions differ between specifications, so a transferred student can write correct logic in a notation the mark scheme does not reward. A quick and specific thing to fix.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Sometimes taken at the new school and not the old, which means a transferred student may be starting a whole qualification late. Worth asking whether it is required or optional before committing to it.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Under the syllabus in use from 2025, each tier pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper. A student transferring in from a board that permits calculators throughout has never rehearsed half of this.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers of two hours at 50% each with a calculator permitted throughout. A student arriving from Cambridge will have drilled mental arithmetic that this specification does not test.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences 0620, 0625, 0610
igcseSubjects.description: Tiered papers with an alternative-to-practical route available for experimental skills. A transferred student needs to know which practical option their new centre uses.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Practical understanding is assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, which changes how experimental method should be revised.

igcseSubjects.name: Oxford AQA International GCSE
igcseSubjects.description: In use at some Dubai centres and the body most often assumed away. For a transferred student the code must be confirmed rather than inferred, because the paper structures differ.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English 0500 and 0510
igcseSubjects.description: Different components and in some routes a speaking element. A transfer is exactly when a student can end up entered for the route that suits the new timetable rather than their ability.

schoolClusters.note: The schools Creek Harbour families travel further for, including the mixed-curriculum provision in the eastern suburbs. This mix is why transfers between curricula as well as between boards are common in this district.

sections.heading: Changing awarding body mid-course: what actually differs
paragraphs: A family moving between Dubai schools rarely asks whether the awarding body changes, and schools do not always volunteer it. Yet a student who spent Year 10 on one specification and sits Year 11 examinations on another has a specific, bounded problem that nobody has described to them, and it is nothing like being behind.

Take mathematics. Under the Cambridge syllabus in use from 2025, each tier pairs a paper taken without a calculator with one taken with it. Pearson Edexcel Specification A permits a calculator in both papers. A student moving from Pearson to Cambridge has never rehearsed an entire paper format, and a student moving the other way has drilled mental arithmetic that their new specification does not test. Neither is a knowledge gap and both cost marks.

The sciences differ on practical assessment: Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route for experimental skills, while Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Tier vocabulary changes, with Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. The formulae provided in the examination differ. In Computer Science the pseudocode conventions differ, so correct logic can be written in a notation the mark scheme does not credit. In English, which qualification a student is entered for may change entirely.

The table sets out what to check. Treat it as a reason to ask the new school's examinations officer rather than as a description of your child's case, because specifications are revised and schools change boards. The point is that four to six sessions aimed at these differences usually resolves a board change completely, and that is a much smaller purchase than the weekly arrangement a worried family would otherwise buy.

sections.heading: Changing curriculum: arriving into IGCSE from elsewhere
paragraphs: A larger transfer is a change of curriculum, and in a district of recent arrivals it is common. A student coming into IGCSE from CBSE, from an American system, from a national curriculum or from a British school in another country is not simply behind or ahead. They have a different profile, with strengths the new course will reward and habits it will penalise, and the profile is predictable enough to plan for.

Students arriving from CBSE typically have strong procedural mathematics and less experience of extended written answers in the sciences and humanities. Students arriving from American systems usually have broader coverage, more coursework experience and less practice with terminal written examinations. Students from national curricula may have limited experience of English-medium assessment in their subjects even where their English is strong. Students from a British school elsewhere often have the closest fit and the clearest sequencing gaps.

In every case the useful first step is the same and it is not teaching. It is a written map of what has been covered and how the student has been assessed, built from their own work rather than from a syllabus comparison. A diagnostic session with a marked script from the old school and a task sheet from the new one produces that map in an hour, and it typically shows that three or four named topics need teaching rather than a year.

The table sets out the common patterns. It is a starting point for a conversation, not a judgement about any individual: students vary far more than systems do, and a confident mathematician from any system is a confident mathematician. What the table is good for is telling a family what to look for first, which in a district where many households are managing a move as well as a course is worth having before the first tutoring hour is bought.

sections.heading: What a tutor must establish before teaching a transferred student
paragraphs: A tutor who begins teaching a transferred student in the first session has skipped the work that makes the rest of the sessions worth anything. The list below is what should happen instead, and it takes one hour rather than a term. A parent can also use it as a test: a tutor who does not ask these things is about to re-teach a year of material your child may already have.

First, which awarding body, specification code and tier the new school has entered them for, in writing. Second, what the old school had covered, established from the student's own exercise books and marked work rather than from a claim about a syllabus. Third, how the old school assessed them, because a student who has never sat a timed terminal paper has a technique gap rather than a content gap.

Fourth, whether any non-written component has been completed or is outstanding, which is the administrative detail most often missed in a mid-course move. Fifth, whether the tier looks right now, because an arriving student is often placed on the basis of a first assessment taken while jet-lagged and unsettled. Sixth, what the new school assumes has been covered by this point in the course, which the class teacher can state in a sentence.

From those six answers a written gap map follows, and the map is the deliverable from the first session. It should name topics rather than describing a general level, and it should distinguish a sequencing gap, which closes in a session or two, from a genuine content deficit, which takes longer. Ask for it in writing. A tutor who can produce it has understood the case; one who offers general reassurance has not, whatever their subject knowledge.

sections.heading: Online against nearby, in a district with no local teacher pool
paragraphs: Every district in Dubai has a thin supply of specification-literate tutors. This one has an unusual version of the problem, because it has little school provision inside it and therefore no body of teachers living here at all. A near-me search returns people prepared to cross the creek, which is a filter on willingness to travel rather than on having taught the specification your child has just transferred onto.

For a transfer case that mismatch matters more than usual. The work required is specification-specific by definition: knowing what differs between two boards, what a given paper format demands, what the new school's practical option is. A generalist who knows the subject will teach the subject, which is the thing the student may least need, and the mapping work will simply not happen.

Online delivery changes the match in three ways. It draws the shortlist from the whole market rather than from those within driving distance, so a tutor who has taught both the old and the new specification becomes findable. It removes a journey across the Ras Al Khor crossings at four in the afternoon, which in a commuting household matters. And it produces written artefacts, including the gap map and marked practice, which a newly arrived family can take to the new school as evidence.

The variable where a local tutor has a genuine claim is presence, particularly for a younger or unsettled student in the first weeks of a move. That is real and we will not argue it away. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the choice here is between our online delivery and a local arrangement you would make yourself, with the market bands below to judge it against.

sections.heading: Entries, tiers and the administrative chain for a mid-course arrival
paragraphs: The academic gap is the visible half of a mid-course transfer. The administrative half is less visible and can be more expensive, because entry deadlines belong to the awarding body and are administered by the school, and a newly arrived family does not know what the school has or has not done.

Start with entries. Confirm, in writing, which subjects your child is entered for, with which awarding body, under which specification code and at which tier. Ask whether any non-written component, such as a spoken element or a coursework piece, has been completed at the old school and whether it transfers, or whether it needs doing again. Ask when the entry deadline falls and whether anything is still changeable.

Then the tier. An arriving student is frequently placed from a first assessment taken in their first fortnight, while unsettled and sometimes jet-lagged, and that placement sets a grade ceiling for the rest of the course. It is worth asking for a review once the student has been in school a term, with a marked script as evidence, and it is worth asking in Year 10 rather than Year 11 when it becomes a resit conversation instead.

Finally the timetable, which has a detail almost nobody passes on. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A family who has moved countries may be holding a timetable from the old centre's zone. Use only the one the new school issues.

sections.heading: KHDA, equivalency and attestation for a newly arrived family
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a family that has just arrived and may move school again, those published reports are the most useful free document available, and the departmental commentary matters more than the band.

The scale of the market is why transfers are so varied here. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year. Seventeen curricula in one emirate is the reason a Dubai-to-Dubai move can still be a change of system.

For a newly arrived family, equivalency is the question that arrives next. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires a student to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is incorrect.

Two cautions on that. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own circumstances through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring service, including this one, and do not treat tutoring as a requirement for it. And on credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be, since a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: Practical science, coursework and what we will not do
paragraphs: A transferred student in the sciences has a particular exposure, because practical programmes do not transfer. Whatever experiments the old school ran, the new school's own practical scheme of work is what underpins the assessment, and a student arriving in Year 11 may have missed experiments their new classmates did a year ago. A tutor cannot substitute for that, and one claiming to supervise practical work remotely is overselling.

What can be taught remotely is the examined written element: experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, reliability, uncertainty, graph work and the written conventions the mark scheme rewards. Whether that is assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers depends on the specification, which is one more reason to confirm the code. The missing hands-on experience is a conversation for the new school's department, and it is worth having rather than hoping.

Where a coursework, portfolio or spoken component exists, the rule is unchanged by a transfer: the work must be the student's own. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a chosen focus until it is workable, teach the skills required, rehearse a spoken component in the specification's format, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the focus, supply content, write or rewrite text, or hand over an example close enough to copy.

We state those boundaries to the student in the first session rather than burying them, and they matter more for a transferred student because the pressure is higher: a new school, an unfamiliar specification and a deadline inherited mid-course. At least one operator ranking for UAE curriculum queries sells completed assessed work at a published price, and the consequence falls on the student. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the awarding body's own page.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the first hour we would spend
paragraphs: Send three things from the new school and two from the old. From the new school: the awarding body, specification code and tier for each subject in writing, the English entry route, and the most recent task or assessment with its marking. From the old school: the student's exercise books or a photograph of a few pages, and any report that says what had been covered.

With those, the first session is a diagnosis rather than a lesson. The tutor works through the student's own material, establishes what has been covered and under which assessment model, and produces a written gap map naming topics rather than describing a level. That map is the deliverable, and it should distinguish sequencing gaps that close in one or two sessions from genuine content deficits that take longer.

The trial lesson is free, and for a transfer case it is the most useful free hour available in this market, because the mapping is the part that determines whether everything afterwards is targeted or wasted. Afterwards, ask for the map in writing and ask how many sessions the named gaps will take. A tutor who answers with a term-long arrangement before the map exists has not done the diagnosis.

And the honest part. We will say when the answer is that your child has no significant gap and was simply placed in a low set on arrival, which happens often enough to mention and which is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase from us. We will also say when a subject is thinly covered: English Literature with unusual set texts, Computer Science, Oxford AQA specifications and the less commonly entered languages. When nobody suitable is free we offer another slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE who has taught that specification, disclosed as such.

faqs.question: My child transferred schools mid-IGCSE. Where do we even start?
faqs.answer: With two emails rather than a tutor. Ask the new school's examinations officer for the awarding body, specification code, tier and English entry route for every subject in writing, and whether any non-written component is outstanding. Then gather the old school's exercise books or a few photographed pages. From those, one diagnostic session produces a written map of named topics, which usually shows that three or four specific gaps need closing rather than a whole year needing re-teaching.

faqs.question: Can a school change in Dubai mean a change of exam board?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families rarely think to ask. Dubai schools use Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and Oxford AQA International GCSE, sometimes different bodies for different subjects within one school. A student who spent Year 10 on one specification and sits Year 11 papers on another has never rehearsed some paper formats: Cambridge's current maths structure includes a non-calculator paper, while Pearson's Specification A permits a calculator throughout. That is a bounded problem, usually four to six sessions, and not a knowledge gap.

faqs.question: Is there anyone living in Dubai Creek Harbour who teaches IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Very few, and the reason is structural rather than discouraging. The district has little school provision inside it, so no body of teachers lives here because no local school employs one. A near-me search therefore returns people willing to cross the creek rather than people who have taught your child's specification. For a transferred student, specification knowledge is exactly what is needed, which is why we match from the whole market and deliver one-to-one over live video instead.

faqs.question: Will someone come to our apartment, or is it all remote?
faqs.answer: Remote, delivered one-to-one over live video throughout the UAE. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and we say so plainly because home tutor is the phrase parents search. For a household here it also removes a journey across the Ras Al Khor crossings at four in the afternoon. Local in-home arrangements exist, and the Dubai market band is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against about AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor.

faqs.question: What gaps does a student arriving from CBSE usually have?
faqs.answer: Typically strong procedural mathematics and recall, and less practice with extended written answers and with application marks in the sciences and humanities. The content is often not the problem; the answer structure is, because IGCSE command terms expect a particular kind of response that a recall-oriented system does not drill. Command-term work and answer structure usually move those grades quickly. Students vary far more than systems do, so this is a place to look first rather than a prediction about any individual.

faqs.question: My child came from an American school. What will they find hardest?
faqs.answer: Terminal written examinations and the pacing they demand. American systems typically give broader coverage, more coursework and more continuous assessment, so a student may know the material and have little experience of producing it under timed conditions in a single paper carrying half the grade. That is a technique gap rather than a content gap, which means it responds faster than families expect: whole timed papers, marked against the published criteria, with the pacing benchmarked across several attempts.

faqs.question: Should we buy a weekly session or a short block for a transferred student?
faqs.answer: A short block first, almost always. Three to five sessions, with the first producing a written gap map and the rest closing the named topics, is what most transferred students need and nothing further. A weekly arrangement is the second purchase, justified only if the map shows a genuine content deficit rather than a sequencing gap. Buying weekly support before the map exists means paying to re-cover material your child may already have, which is the commonest waste in a transfer case.

faqs.question: My child was put in a low set when they arrived. Is that permanent?
faqs.answer: It should not be, and it is worth challenging politely. Arriving students are often placed from a first assessment taken within a fortnight of a move, while unsettled and sometimes jet-lagged, and that placement can set a tier and a grade ceiling for the rest of the course. Ask for a review once your child has been in school a term, with a marked script as evidence, and ask in Year 10 rather than Year 11, when the same conversation becomes one about a resit.

faqs.question: Does practical science work transfer between schools?
faqs.answer: The written understanding does; the hands-on experience does not. Each school runs its own practical scheme of work, so a student arriving in Year 11 may have missed experiments their classmates did a year earlier, and no tutor can substitute for that. What can be taught remotely is the examined written element: method, variables, controls, reliability, uncertainty and graph work. The missing laboratory experience is a conversation for the new school's science department, and it is worth having rather than hoping it does not matter.

faqs.question: What should I ask the new school's examinations officer?
faqs.answer: Six things, in one email. Which subjects my child is entered for, with which awarding body and specification code. Which tier, where tiering applies. Which English qualification. Whether any spoken or coursework component is complete, transferable or outstanding. Which practical option the centre uses in the sciences. And which administrative zone the centre is in, with a copy of the timetable the school issues. Those answers prevent every common administrative failure in a mid-course transfer.

faqs.question: Which exam timetable should we use after moving countries?
faqs.answer: Only the one the new school issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A family that has moved may still hold the old centre's version, which could belong to a different zone entirely. Ask the new school which zone applies and work only from their document.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects will my child need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, alongside one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own case through its attestation channel.

faqs.question: Is my child behind, or just differently prepared?
faqs.answer: Usually the second, and the distinction is worth the diagnostic hour. A transferred student commonly knows everything their old school taught and is missing topics the new school covered in a different order, which is a sequencing gap closing in one or two sessions rather than a deficit. The test is specific: a written map of named topics built from their own marked work. A general impression that they are behind is not a finding, and it is what leads families to buy a year of unnecessary support.

faqs.question: When are the exams, and could my child resit if the transfer cost them a grade?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and November functions as a resit route inside the same academic year for both main awarding bodies. The February and March series that appears in some online material is offered to India only. The published pattern: Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry goes through the school shortly after summer results, so the decision window is short.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to cover for a transferred student?
faqs.answer: English Literature where the new school's set texts are unusual, because a transferred student has often studied texts they will not be examined on. Then Computer Science, where pseudocode conventions differ, Additional Mathematics if the new school requires it and the old one did not, any subject entered through Oxford AQA, and the less commonly taught languages. Mathematics, Biology and Business Studies are well covered. We tell you which category each subject falls into before you book rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: What will the first session actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written gap map, which is the deliverable rather than a lesson. The tutor works through your child's own material from both schools, establishes what was covered and under which assessment model, and lists named topics, separating sequencing gaps that close in a session or two from genuine content deficits that take longer. Ask for it in writing and ask how many sessions the named gaps will need. A tutor proposing a term-long arrangement before that map exists has not done the diagnosis.

intro.heading: The Dubai Festival City school run is the real constraint on IGCSE tuition
paragraphs: Work out the available hours before you work out the budget, because in this corner of Dubai the hours are the scarcer resource. Secondary dismissal at the schools Dubai Festival City families use lands between about 2.15pm and 3.30pm. A bus route serving Al Badia, Festival Boulevard and Nad Al Hamar adds thirty to fifty minutes. A child who is driven home is often collected later than one on the bus, because the pick-up queue at a large campus is slower than the route. So the realistic earliest a Year 10 student is sitting down, fed and willing, is around four o'clock, and more often half past.

That leaves two usable windows on a weekday. The first runs from roughly 4pm to 6pm and is the good one: the student is tired but not finished, and homework has not yet eaten the evening. The second runs from about 7pm after dinner, and it works for a focused hour on a single topic but not for new content. Anything after 8.30pm on a school night is money spent on a student who is no longer learning, however willing they look.

Now put a car into that picture. An in-home tutor has to arrive inside one of those two windows, which means travelling across Dubai in the worst part of the afternoon. Garhoud Bridge and the Dubai-Al Ain Road interchange are the two choke points for anyone reaching Festival City from the west or the south, and a 4.30pm appointment booked from Jumeirah or Business Bay is a 4.45pm arrival on an ordinary Tuesday. The fifteen minutes come out of the lesson, not out of the invoice. Repeat that weekly across a term and the loss is substantial.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Dubai Festival City, tuition is delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, which means a 4.15pm lesson starts at 4.15pm because nobody has to be anywhere. It also means the first window becomes genuinely usable: you can book the good hour instead of the hour a tutor can physically reach, and the student is working at the point in the day when they are still capable of it.

The rest of this page is built around that clock. Which schools near Dubai Festival City finish when, which board each one enters, how two subjects fit into five evenings, what Ramadan does to the pattern, and when in the year the hours have to be bought to be worth anything. The money matters and it appears here with its sources, but the timing is what determines whether the money does anything at all.
