dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.programmesIntro: Dubai Festival City households run more than one curriculum between them more often than the market assumes, so a page about IGCSE has to say what sits either side of it. These are the stages that matter for timetable planning, because each one changes what an evening session can usefully achieve.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, the years before IGCSE
programmes.description: Three years with no external examinations, which is why they are the cheapest years in which to fix anything structural. Algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and written extended answers are all built here. A Year 9 student who cannot rearrange a formula will meet that same weakness in every IGCSE science paper two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For a Dubai Festival City family this is the stage where the school run is kindest: dismissal is often earlier for lower secondary and homework load is lighter, so a 4pm slot is comfortably achievable. Using that window well in Year 9 reduces how many Year 11 evenings have to be bought at a higher rate.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years leading to externally marked papers, with Cambridge grading 9 to 1 on most syllabuses and Pearson grading International GCSE on a 9 to 1 scale as well. Subjects are tiered or set in Cambridge as Core and Extended, and the tier decision made in Year 10 caps the grade available in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: This is the band where evening time becomes contested, because coursework, mocks and six to nine subjects all compete for the same 4pm to 6pm window. Families around Al Badia and Mirdif who plan the week on paper rather than by feel consistently buy fewer hours and get more out of them.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after Year 11
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai split at 16 into A Level or the IB Diploma, and a few offer both. The IGCSE tier and grade profile determines which doors stay open, particularly in mathematics and the sciences where entry requirements are specific rather than general.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School runs the IB continuum through to Diploma, so a Dubai Festival City student may move from IGCSE into Diploma within the same campus. That transition changes the shape of evening work sharply: Diploma internal assessments have school deadlines that do not care what else is happening that week.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the British curriculum
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA required these arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April, and calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit.
programmes.countryNote: These lessons occupy timetable space that parents often forget when they look at a school day and assume it is all IGCSE content. For a non-Arab student in Dubai Festival City, the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies, while Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education for Arab students are taught in Standard Arabic.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects Dubai Festival City families ask for most, with the syllabus code where it matters and the part of each course that evening sessions are genuinely good for. Check the code on your child's school report before booking anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Both boards run two papers, both allow a calculator throughout, and both punish untidy algebra. The Extended and Higher tiers add algebraic fractions, functions, vectors and more demanding trigonometry. The tier decision is the single highest-stakes choice in the subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, forces and motion, waves, energy and nuclear physics. Marks are lost in two predictable places: multi-step calculations where units are dropped, and six-mark written answers where a student describes an effect without naming the mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: States of matter, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, organic chemistry. Moles calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the two areas where a weekly hour pays back fastest, because both are learnable procedures rather than vague skills.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, inheritance and ecology. Biology rewards precise sentences more than long ones; an answer that names the structure, the process and the consequence scores where a paragraph of general sense does not.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: One or two grades covering all three sciences, chosen by schools that want breadth without three separate subject blocks. Content is narrower than the single sciences, which makes it an easier timetable fit and a harder one to catch up in if a term is missed.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and composition. The commonest cause of lost marks is answering the question the student expected rather than the one printed, particularly in directed writing where audience and form are specified.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts, poetry and unseen extracts. Quotation selection is the technical skill that separates grades: a short embedded quotation analysed closely beats a long one left to speak for itself.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Demand and supply, market structures, business objectives, finance and marketing. Data-response questions reward reading the table before the question, and the extended evaluation marks require a judgement that is actually stated rather than implied.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithms, data representation, networks and practical skills. The theory paper is where grades are usually lost, because students who can code well often cannot explain why their code works in the terms the mark scheme wants.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and a prohibition on combining the two groups. Support works from the school's approved material, since using different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.regionsTitle: The school run, community by community
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.regionsIntro: Each community around Dubai Festival City has a different relationship with the afternoon. These notes are about time rather than postcode prestige, because time is what decides whether a tuition slot is real.

regions.name: Al Badia
regions.note: Closest to Deira International School, so the walk or short drive home is the quickest in the area. A 3.45pm start is genuinely possible here, which makes Al Badia the one community where the early window is reliably available on a school day.

regions.name: Festival Boulevard and Marsa Al Khaimah
regions.note: Apartments beside the mall. The obstacle is retail rather than commuter traffic: late-afternoon mall access slows the final approach, so a car-based appointment is less predictable than the short distance suggests. A video link ignores all of it.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Villas between Festival City and Mirdif with little walkable school provision, so most students are bussed or driven a real distance. Parents here consistently report a 4.30pm to 5pm arrival home, which pushes a visiting tutor into the evening window by default.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Older housing across the Dubai-Al Ain Road, feeding a mix of British and Indian curriculum schools with staggered dismissal times. Households with children at two schools often have two different arrival times, which is the hardest case of all for a single visiting tutor.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: The large neighbouring family district, with its own IB continuum school and several British-curriculum options. Internal Mirdif journeys are short, but a Mirdif student at a Festival City or Garhoud school has a long one, often forty minutes on the bus.

regions.name: Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Lower-density villa areas further east. School buses run longer routes here than anywhere else in the cluster, and a 5pm arrival home is normal rather than exceptional. The early window effectively does not exist on a weekday.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: Dense established housing with heavy local school traffic at dismissal. The practical effect is that the roads around Al Warqa are slowest at precisely the hour a tutor would need to be arriving, which is why evening slots dominate here.

regions.name: International City and Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: South of Festival City along the Dubai-Al Ain corridor. Journeys to Garhoud-area schools are twenty-five to forty minutes depending on the hour, and families here are often the first to give up on finding a local subject specialist.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City, Al Badia and Garhoud
schoolClusters.note: The immediate cluster, and the one that sets the afternoon clock for most families reading this. Dubai Festival City School runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE, Deira International School runs IGCSE before the IB Diploma, and Universal American School sits on an American spine with the Diploma at the top. Three dismissal times, three homework cultures, one neighbourhood.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Mizhar and the eastern suburbs
schoolClusters.note: The wider catchment, reached by bus routes that are long enough to matter. Uptown International School runs the IB continuum in Mirdif, Star International School Mirdif and Al Mizhar American Academy serve the villa communities, and Dubai English Speaking College draws from across the east. Bus arrival times here are the single biggest determinant of whether a 4pm slot is usable.

schoolClusters.city: Silicon Oasis and the southern corridor
schoolClusters.note: Twenty-five to forty minutes from Festival City depending on the hour. GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis is one of the larger British-curriculum secondary providers in eastern Dubai, and Repton School Dubai at Nad Al Sheba draws from the same corridor. A tutor who knows one school's scheme of work usually recognises the next one's.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.schoolDisclaimer: These schools are named to describe the Dubai Festival City education market; IB Gram has no affiliation with, endorsement from or relationship to any of them.
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.modesIntro: Three session shapes cover the realistic Dubai Festival City week. All are delivered as live one-to-one or small-group video lessons on Gulf Standard Time, so the start time is the time you booked rather than the time a car arrived.

modes.title: The early window, 4pm to 6pm
modes.description: The slot worth fighting for. New content, worked examples and anything that needs the student to think rather than recall belongs here. It is also the slot a visiting tutor can least reliably reach in this part of Dubai, which is why it is usually the first thing a family gives up without realising they have given it up.
bullets: Best for new teaching and for topics the student currently cannot do
Achievable from Al Badia and inner Festival City without a rush
Fills first across the week, so book before term starts
Thirty minutes of food and decompression first, not straight off the bus

modes.title: The post-dinner focused hour
modes.description: From about 7pm, suited to consolidation rather than instruction: a past-paper section under time, a set of moles calculations, a redraft of one written answer. It works well for students bussed from Al Mizhar or Al Khawaneej who are simply not home earlier, and it is the realistic default for most of the eastern suburbs.
bullets: One topic, one hour, one measurable output
Timed paper sections rather than new content
Works for households with two different school finish times
Stop by 8.30pm on a school night; later hours do not teach

modes.title: Weekend blocks and holiday intensives
modes.description: Saturday and Sunday mornings carry no school-run constraint at all, which makes them the right place for anything long: a full past paper, a tier decision review, or catching up a missed unit. Half-terms and the long summer break serve the same purpose at larger scale, and they are when the biggest gaps actually close.
bullets: Full papers under exam timing, then marked and reworked
Two subjects in one morning without competing with homework
Useful before the mock window rather than after it
Pausable during family travel without losing the regular slot

sections.heading: Dismissal times, bus routes and the hour you actually have
paragraphs: A tuition slot that does not exist cannot be used, so start with the clock. Secondary dismissal across the schools Dubai Festival City families attend lands roughly between 2.15pm and 3.30pm, with primary usually earlier. The variation matters more than the absolute time, because a household with a Year 7 and a Year 11 at different campuses has two arrival times and one evening. Confirm your own school's time from its own calendar; what follows is the shape, not a published timetable.

Add the journey. A bus serving Al Badia from a Garhoud campus is short. A bus serving Al Khawaneej or Al Warqa from the same campus is long, and routes that drop multiple communities put some children home almost an hour after dismissal. Private collection is often slower than the bus at large schools because the pick-up queue is the bottleneck. Then add the non-negotiable thirty minutes for food and decompression, which every experienced tutor builds in because a session that starts on an empty stomach achieves nothing.

The result is the table below. Read the final column as the honest answer to the question parents actually ask, which is not when school ends but when work can start. For most of the eastern suburbs the answer is between 4.15pm and 5pm, and for the outer villa communities it is later. A visiting tutor has to travel into that same window across the city. A video lesson does not have to travel at all, which is the entire operational argument for it in this neighbourhood.

columns: Typical journey from a Garhoud or Festival City campus
rows: Festival Boulevard and Marsa Al Khaimah
10 to 20 minutes, slower near the mall
25 to 40 minutes on a multi-stop route
35 to 50 minutes on a long route

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out before you book anything
paragraphs: Two different boards run International GCSE in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge International syllabuses carry four-digit codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English Language. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look different: 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong one wastes the term politely.

The differences are structural, not cosmetic. Cambridge sets Core and Extended routes on many syllabuses with different papers and different grade ceilings. Pearson sets Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics and runs a modular structure on some qualifications, which changes when a paper can be sat and how a resit works. Practical science is handled differently too: Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper on several syllabuses, which is the route most students sitting from a UAE centre meet.

Finding out takes one message. Your child's report, the school's curriculum page or the exams officer will name the board and the code, and the code is the thing to quote when you ask for a tutor. The table below lays the two side by side so you can read your own child's situation off it. If the school enters some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson, which is common in Dubai, then you need that detail subject by subject rather than once.

It is worth knowing why this goes wrong so often. A tutor advertising IGCSE Chemistry is not lying when the student turns out to be on a different board; the subject label is the same and most of the chemistry is the same. What differs is the command-term phrasing, the paper structure, the way practical skills are assessed and the shape of the mark scheme, and those are precisely the things a final term of preparation is supposed to drill. Getting the code right at the start costs one message and protects every hour after it.

A Cambridge combined entry needs a tutor comfortable across all three

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: On many Cambridge syllabuses a student is entered for either Core or Extended, and the choice is usually made during Year 10 by the school. It is not a comment on a student's worth, it is a prediction about which papers they will perform best on, and it has a hard consequence: the Core route does not reach the top grades. A student aiming for a sixth-form science place needs to know whether their current entry can get them there.

Extended covers additional content and sets harder papers. In mathematics that means algebraic fractions, functions, vectors and more demanding trigonometry. In the sciences it means additional topics and supplementary material flagged in the syllabus, plus questions that expect multi-step reasoning rather than recall. A student who is coping with Core content but has been placed there because of one weak term is a candidate for review, and the review has to happen while there is time to move.

This is the clearest case for buying tuition early rather than late. The window in which a tier decision can be influenced is Year 10 and the first part of Year 11, not the spring before the papers. A diagnostic block that establishes whether the ceiling is being set by ability or by a gap from Key Stage 3 is cheap relative to a capped grade, and in the eastern suburbs it is also easier to schedule, because Year 10 evenings are less crowded than Year 11 ones.

rows: Extended needs more weeks, so start earlier in Year 10
Full range to the top grade

sections.heading: Fitting two subjects into five school evenings
paragraphs: Families rarely need one subject. The common Dubai Festival City request is mathematics and one science, or a science and English, in Year 10 or Year 11. Two weekly hours sounds modest until you place them in a week that already contains homework for eight or nine subjects, a sport, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that occupy school timetable space rather than evening space but still generate work.

The pattern that holds up is two tuition evenings, spaced, with the heavier subject in the earlier window and nothing on the evening before a long school day. Monday and Wednesday works for most households. Tuesday and Thursday works where a sport sits on Monday. What fails reliably is consecutive evenings, because the student has no gap in which to attempt the work set, so the second session is spent re-teaching rather than progressing.

The single most useful thing a parent can do is write the week down. Not a schedule in anyone's head, an actual grid: arrival time, dinner, homework blocks, tuition, sleep. The exercise usually reveals that one evening is already overloaded and another is empty, and it almost always shows that the useful early window on one particular day has been going unused because nobody noticed it was free. The table below is the version most eastern-suburbs families end up with.

Households with two children at different schools need one further adjustment. Two dismissal times mean two arrival times, and a single visiting tutor cannot serve both without one child waiting. Online slots can simply be booked at different hours with different tutors, which sounds obvious until you price the alternative: a visiting tutor charging a travel-inclusive rate for a session that half the household is sitting out. Stagger the two bookings and the week stops competing with itself.

A gap day is what makes the Monday session count

sections.heading: Ramadan, half-terms and the Dubai academic year
paragraphs: The Dubai school year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a half-term break in autumn, a winter break around the turn of the year, a spring break and a long summer. Those breaks are where the real catching up happens, because they are the only periods with no school-run constraint and no homework competing for the evening. A family that uses one week of the spring break well can often reduce its term-time booking afterwards.

Ramadan changes the day rather than cancelling it. School hours shorten, which paradoxically makes the afternoon easier for tuition, and many families move sessions to a post-Iftar time when the household is awake and settled. For fasting students, the late afternoon is the worst hour of the day for concentration and the hour after Iftar is among the best. Keeping the same tutor and simply moving the slot is routine and worth arranging in advance rather than week by week.

The practical rule is to plan the year in four blocks rather than as a continuous weekly subscription. Autumn term for diagnosis and building method. Winter break for closing one named gap. Spring term for timed papers and technique. The run-up to the series for past papers under exam conditions. A visiting tutor cannot easily flex around travel, Ramadan timings or a sudden mock week; an online slot can be moved in a message, and the student keeps the same person throughout.
bullets: Breaks are where structural gaps close; term time is for maintenance and technique
Ramadan sessions commonly move to post-Iftar; arrange it before the month starts
Shortened Ramadan school hours make the afternoon window easier, not harder
Plan in four blocks across the year instead of one open-ended weekly booking

sections.heading: Exam series and entry deadlines for a UAE candidate
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai Festival City school will sit it. Any page that hands a UAE parent a February entry deadline is quoting another country's calendar.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series and revises them, which is why no page should be the source of truth for a date. Use the board's live timetable or your school's exams officer. What this page can tell you reliably is the shape: entries close months before the paper, mocks sit a term earlier, and the November series is the resit route for a June candidate, with results arriving in January rather than August.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: A parent choosing a visiting tutor from a community noticeboard is making a compliance decision without being told so. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae records that it is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are broad: registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

Tutoring without that permit exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published anywhere official, so this page quotes none, and you should be sceptical of any site that does. The application goes through MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time via the smart app, website and e-services system.

Two boundaries are worth holding onto. An individual permit is not the same thing as permission to run a centre: premises and staff in Dubai require a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE code of conduct carrying a comparable restriction, so nobody should be offering you your child's own teacher privately.
bullets: Ask the direct question: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
The permit is free and lasts two years, so there is no cost excuse for not holding it
Premises and staff need a KHDA institute permit, which is a different authorisation
No official fine schedule is published; distrust any specific penalty figure you read

sections.heading: What tuition costs around here, and what it should not pay for
paragraphs: Timing decided, the money is simpler than it looks. Published market rates in Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE tuition from AED 150. The budget online band sits lower, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour by Bestimate and by independent home tutors, because a car and a driver's unpaid hour are inside that figure. All of these were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers named, not to us.

What the in-home premium buys, in this neighbourhood specifically, is a later start. The tutor arrives when the traffic allows, which in practice means the good 4pm to 6pm window is partly spent waiting and the lesson runs into homework time. Paying more for a worse slot is the specific inefficiency this page exists to point out. It is not an argument that in-home tutoring is bad; it is an argument that in eastern Dubai the geography takes most of the value out of it.

Our own commercial terms are set after a free trial lesson and a diagnostic conversation, because quoting one hourly figure across Year 7 English and Extended Chemistry would mislead you in both directions. What the market table above is for is checking a quote you already hold. If it sits above the specialist band without a reason you can name, ask what the reason is.
bullets: Market bands, October 2026: budget online AED 45-150; qualified online AED 150-300; in-home AED 180-500
Monthly packages seen: about AED 799 for eight online sessions; AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions
Confirm whether a quote is per hour or per lesson, and whether VAT treatment is stated in writing
The hidden cost in this area is not the rate; it is the minutes lost to arrival time

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Festival City, and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the subject, the board code and the tier, plus the hour your household can realistically manage on a school night. We match a tutor to that code and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video. Afterwards you receive a written note of where the marks are going, by topic, and a recommended number of hours and slots. If the recommendation is smaller than you expected, that is the diagnosis working.

Two honest limits. The 4pm to 6pm window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest in the week, so popular subject and tier combinations fill there first; if the slot you want is taken we will say so and give you the wait rather than moving you quietly to a generalist. And all delivery is online: IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, has no UAE office, centre or branch, and does not claim one.

A final boundary that matters more in this market than it should. We do not describe any tutor as a current Cambridge or Pearson examiner unless that status can be evidenced, and we do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do. We reference them and link to the official source. Ask us for evidence on any claim on this page, and ask the same of everyone else you are considering.

What you should expect from the first month is modest and specific: the student knowing which paper they are being prepared for, a written list of the topics that are costing marks, and one visible improvement in how an answer is structured. Grade movement takes longer than a month and nobody can promise it. A provider that opens with a predicted grade rather than a diagnosis has told you something useful about how it operates.
bullets: Send the syllabus code, not just the subject name; it determines the match
Tell us the realistic arrival time rather than the official dismissal time
Free trial lesson first, then a written gap note, then a booking

process.title: Send the code and the clock
process.description: Two pieces of information do most of the work: the syllabus code your child is entered for, such as 0580 or 4CH1, and the hour the student is genuinely at a desk on a school night. The first decides the tutor, the second decides whether the booking survives past week three.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson in your real slot
process.description: Run the trial at the time you intend to book, not at a convenient weekend hour. A 5pm Tuesday session tells you something a Saturday morning session cannot, which is whether your child can work at 5pm on a Tuesday after a bus from Al Mizhar.

process.title: Read the written gap note
process.description: You get a short account of where marks are being lost, by topic and by paper, with a recommended number of hours and a suggested pattern for the week. It is written to be challenged. A note that recommends the maximum in every case is a sales document rather than a diagnosis.

process.title: Protect the gap day
process.description: Book two spaced evenings rather than two consecutive ones, so there is time to attempt the work set between them. This single change does more for progress than adding a third hour, and it costs nothing. Weekend mornings take the long tasks that will not fit a school night.

process.title: Rebuild the plan at each break
process.description: Half-term, winter and spring breaks are the only windows with no school-run constraint, so that is where structural catching up belongs. Reset the plan at each one: cut a subject that is now stable, add intensity where mocks have exposed something, and keep the tutor constant.

whyPoints.title: Built around the hour you actually have
whyPoints.description: Dismissal times, bus routes and arrival times across Al Badia, Nad Al Hamar, Mirdif and Al Khawaneej are the real constraint on IGCSE tuition in eastern Dubai. A live video lesson starts when it is booked, which makes the better afternoon window usable instead of theoretical.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different courses with different structures, and Core and Extended are different again. We ask for the code before matching because a tutor prepared for the wrong one will teach a perfectly good term of the wrong material.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision gets raised early
whyPoints.description: A Core entry caps the grade, and the window to review it is Year 10 and early Year 11. Most providers never mention this because it is easier to sell revision in the final term. We would rather tell you while it can still be changed.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources, not vague reassurance
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all and two quote US dollars to families who pay in dirhams. Every band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to when it was read.

whyPoints.title: Regulation explained, never claimed
whyPoints.description: We set out what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education each govern, and claim accreditation from none of them, because IB Gram holds none. A provider calling its tutors KHDA approved is describing a permit that is issued to institutes with premises.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the busy window
whyPoints.description: The late-afternoon slot on Gulf Standard Time is the most contested part of the week, and Extended sciences fill first inside it. When your preferred hour is unavailable we tell you the wait instead of substituting someone who does not know your child's board.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start for a Dubai Festival City family?
faqs.answer: Between about 3.45pm and 4pm if you live in Al Badia and your child is at a nearby campus, 4.15pm to 4.30pm from Festival Boulevard or Nad Al Hamar, and 5pm or later from Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej where bus routes are long. Add thirty minutes after arrival for food and decompression, because a session that starts straight off the bus achieves very little. Confirm your own school's dismissal time from its calendar and work forward from there rather than from a generic figure.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to homes in Dubai Festival City or Nad Al Hamar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Tuition for Dubai Festival City families is delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. In this part of Dubai that is the practical advantage rather than the compromise: a visiting tutor has to cross Garhoud Bridge or the Dubai-Al Ain interchange in the worst hour of the afternoon, and the minutes lost to arrival come out of the lesson rather than out of the fee.

faqs.question: Which board does a Dubai Festival City school enter, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Look at the school report, the school's curriculum page, or ask the exams officer directly. The answer comes as a code: Cambridge uses four digits such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics or 0620 Chemistry, while Pearson Edexcel uses forms like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Many Dubai schools enter some subjects with one board and some with the other, so ask subject by subject rather than once. Quote the code when you request a tutor, because it is what determines whether the match is right.

faqs.question: Can a Core entry be changed to Extended, and when?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window is Year 10 and the early part of Year 11. The school makes the entry decision, so the conversation is with them rather than with a tutor, but a diagnostic assessment that shows the ceiling is being set by a Key Stage 3 gap rather than by ability is useful evidence to bring. What cannot be fixed is a Core entry discovered in the spring before the papers, because the grade range available is already capped at that point.

faqs.question: Is two tuition evenings a week too much for a Year 10 student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two is usually the sensible maximum during term, and the spacing matters more than the number. Two consecutive evenings means the student has no gap in which to attempt the work set, so the second session is spent re-teaching the first. Monday and Wednesday, or Tuesday and Thursday where a sport sits on Monday, works for most eastern-suburbs households. Long tasks such as a full past paper belong on a weekend morning, where no school-run constraint applies at all.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan for a fasting Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten during Ramadan, which makes the afternoon easier rather than harder, but late afternoon is the worst part of the day for a fasting student's concentration. Most families move the slot to a post-Iftar time and keep the same tutor, which is straightforward with an online booking and difficult with a visiting one. Arrange the change before the month starts rather than week by week, because the evening slots fill quickly once everybody is trying to move at once.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai Festival City families ask for most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then Chemistry and Physics, then English Language. The pattern follows sixth-form entry requirements: a student aiming at A Level or IB Diploma sciences needs specific IGCSE grades, so the pressure concentrates there. Combined and Coordinated Science entries generate a different request, because catching up a missed unit across three sciences at once needs a tutor comfortable in all three rather than a specialist in one. Say which it is when you ask.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually take place for a student in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's own risk, so take dates from your school's exams officer rather than from any tutoring site.

faqs.question: When do November series results arrive, and can we still act on them?
faqs.answer: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. That January timing is the reason the November series works as a resit route for a June candidate: the grade arrives in time for most sixth-form and university conversations. Hold a small reserve in the budget for a remark or a resit entry, because both have deadlines that follow results closely.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost around Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours, all read in October 2026: budget online tuition from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya; a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside that figure. IB Gram's own terms follow a free trial lesson and a diagnostic conversation, since one hourly number across Year 7 English and Extended Chemistry would be misleading in both directions.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Ask the question directly; the permit costs nothing, so there is no excuse for not holding it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover mathematics and a science for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor comfortable with Cambridge 0580 Extended mathematics and 0625 Physics is a realistic match because the two courses share algebraic and graphical demands. Mathematics and Chemistry is a weaker pairing, and mathematics with English is rarely the same person. Where one tutor can genuinely cover both, you gain continuity and lose a handover; where they cannot, two specialists in spaced slots beat one generalist trying to hold both.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education timetable affect IGCSE revision time?
faqs.answer: It affects the school day rather than the evening, but it is real timetable space. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and a prohibition on combining the groups. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Where a student needs support in these subjects, it works from the school's approved material, because using different or additional content requires prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: What happens if the 4.30pm slot we need is already taken?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you how long the wait is likely to be. The late-afternoon window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest part of the week across the whole UAE, and Extended science combinations fill inside it first. You will be offered the nearest alternative hour, a weekend block, or an honest timeline, rather than a quiet substitution with someone who does not know your child's board. None of the competitors researched in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere on their pages.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework and school assignments?
faqs.answer: With teaching, feedback and process, yes; with producing the work, never. A tutor can explain what a task is assessing, work through a comparable example on a different topic, read what your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write, complete or edit the piece to a finished state. That boundary protects your child, because assessed work submitted as their own that is not theirs is a malpractice matter with consequences that land on the student.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.closingHeading: Fix the hour first, then the subject
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-festival.closingBody: If the tuition slot does not fit the week, nothing else on this page matters. So start by writing down when your child is actually at a desk on a school night, allowing for the bus from Al Mizhar or the queue out of Festival City, and book around that rather than around an official dismissal time. Then send us the syllabus code and the tier. A free trial lesson runs at your real hour, on live one-to-one video, at no cost, and you get a written note of where the marks are going before you commit to anything. That order round saves more money than any discount.

intro.heading: Comparing providers, not just tutors
paragraphs: A parent in a Dubai Harbour tower looking for IGCSE support will usually encounter five different kinds of seller within a week. An agency that matches you to a tutor and takes a margin. An international marketplace listing tutors by price and rating. A freelancer recommended in a community group, often a working teacher. A tuition centre with premises, usually running small groups. And an online platform. Those are not five versions of the same service. They differ in who employs the tutor, who is accountable when a session is missed, what verification exists, and how the rate is constructed.

The comparison that matters is therefore about model rather than about charm. A freelancer at AED 200 an hour who is excellent and unavailable for six weeks in the spring is worse value than a slightly dearer arrangement that holds. A centre group class at a lower rate per student is good value for a student who needs content coverage and poor value for one who needs a specific habit corrected. A marketplace listing a tutor at the lowest rate is usually listing a university student, which is adequate for Year 9 homework and thin for an Extended-tier paper.

The second comparison families here should make is about what the qualification is for. IGCSE is a gate rather than a destination, and for families in the UAE one of the gates it opens is Ministry of Education equivalency. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects as the requirement. The sourced figure is five, and the difference matters when subject choices are being made.

Dubai Harbour itself shapes the delivery question. The district is new, built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through a single corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street shared with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. There is no school and no tuition centre inside it. Tower basements need a resident to clear visitor access. Children travel out to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah before 07:00 and return after 15:30. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows compares the five provider models on rate and accountability, sets out the Ministry equivalency rules with their source, compares one-to-one against small-group and in-home formats for a student in this district, publishes the market rates with each figure attributed, explains what licensing each kind of provider actually needs, and compares the IGCSE route with the MYP route for the many families here whose school offers both. Verify the equivalency rules on the Ministry's own channel before acting on them, because this page describes rather than performs that process.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubai Harbour families most often ask about, with the code where it matters and a note on which provider model usually serves each well.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tiered, with different paper pairs and grade ceilings. Needs one-to-one at Extended tier because the losses are individual habits: unshown method, ignored rounding instructions, unit conversion. A group class cannot see which of those applies to your child.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620 or Edexcel 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations and qualitative analysis carry disproportionate marks. Group teaching works for content coverage in Year 10 and poorly for Year 11 diagnosis, because the reasoning gaps differ student by student.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits dominate the losses, usually from a circuit redrawn incorrectly before any analysis. This is visible only when someone watches the student draw, which is an argument for one-to-one over any group format.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610 or Edexcel 4BI1
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. The breadth suits group coverage; the command-term repair does not, because it requires reading the student's own answers against mark schemes repeatedly.

subjects.name: English First Language, 0500 or 0990
subjects.description: Reading response plus directed writing and composition. Composition improves fastest with individual feedback on the student's own writing, which no group format delivers at useful frequency.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language, 0510 or 0511
subjects.description: A different examination from First Language English with its own components and speaking arrangements. Students moved between the two syllabuses need their practice material changed with them, which providers frequently miss.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram-led, with data response rewarding the figures being read before the theory is written. Group classes handle the theory well; the diagram discipline that actually carries marks needs individual correction.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Application marks dominate, so a definition applied to no named context collects the first mark and stops. Case-study technique is teachable in a handful of individual sessions and is where most of the available improvement sits.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: A separate qualification taken alongside 0580, assuming complete fluency in its algebra. Worth checking against the post-16 route before adding it, because for a student not yet fluent it produces two mediocre grades rather than one strong one.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and Arab and non-Arab streams are taught separately. Support must match the stream the school has placed the child in, and note that Arabic is excluded from the five subjects Ministry equivalency counts.

sections.heading: The five provider models, compared on what you can check
paragraphs: Every one of these models can deliver a good outcome and they fail in different ways, which is why comparing them on rate alone is misleading. An agency carries a margin and in exchange should carry accountability: a replacement when a tutor leaves, a record of what has been covered, a single point of contact. A marketplace is cheaper because it carries neither, and its ratings are generated by its own users rather than independently verified. A freelancer may be the best teacher available and is a single point of failure.

A tuition centre with premises is the only model that can offer group classes, and it is also the only model that requires a specific Dubai permit to exist: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and then permit and licence steps, renewed annually with the request made at least thirty days before expiry. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead, which is granted free of charge for two years. Those are different instruments and neither one makes anybody KHDA-approved in the sense the phrase is usually marketed.

The questions worth asking any provider are the same across models, and the answers are checkable. Which syllabus code and tier will you teach? Who is the named tutor, and what have they taught at that tier? What happens if they become unavailable in week eight? Is there a written record of what has been covered? And, for an individual, do you hold a current MoHRE permit? A provider who answers all five specifically is a different proposition from one who answers with reassurance.

sections.heading: Ministry equivalency: what five IGCSE passes actually means
paragraphs: For families intending to use a UAE qualification pathway, Ministry of Education equivalency is the gate that follows the certificate, and it is barely mentioned anywhere in this market. On the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details matter when subjects are being chosen. First, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a basket that relies on them to reach five does not reach five. Second, the figure is five: one ranking competitor in this market publishes six as the requirement, which is wrong and would lead a family to enter an unnecessary subject. Publishing the correct rule is one of the few places where a tutoring page can straightforwardly beat a ranking page on accuracy.

For other curricula the rules differ. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold is published here, because none could be read on the Ministry's own site for this project, and an unsourced figure on a page like this would be a liability rather than a help. Verify every rule on the Ministry's own channel; equivalency is a process the authority performs and no tutoring provider can guarantee or carry out.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small group or a visit: which for which year
paragraphs: The format question has a clean answer that providers rarely give because it sometimes points away from the sale. In Year 9 and much of Year 10, where the need is content exposure and consolidation, a small group at a centre is good value and the shared pace is not a disadvantage. The student hears the material, works problems alongside others, and the cost per hour is lower. For a family in this district the trade is a second journey after the school run, which is the real price rather than the fee.

In Year 11, the calculation inverts. The marks a particular student is losing are individual: unshown method, a misread command term, a unit conversion, a circuit redrawn wrongly, an unattempted final question. A group format cannot see any of those, because the teaching is pitched at the group and the diagnosis would require reading one student's script closely. That is the point at which one-to-one becomes necessary rather than preferable, and it is also the point at which families most often economise.

The in-home option sits across both and is mostly a question about the student rather than the year. For a younger child who cannot hold attention on a screen, a person in the room is a genuine advantage and we say so. For a Year 10 or Year 11 candidate working through written papers, diagrams and mark schemes, the shared screen is not a compromise, and removing travel widens the shortlist to anyone who teaches the right code at the right tier. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison is between our online sessions and the local in-home market.

sections.heading: What you can actually verify about a rate
paragraphs: Start with what is published, because most of this market publishes nothing. Three of the seven competitor pages researched for this project quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in. One publishes a schema price range that contradicts the figure on the visible page. Against that background, the useful question to ask a provider is not what they charge but what their rate is constructed from and whether anything about it can be checked.

The figures that can be checked, read in October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the budget end and typically university-student provision. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist cover. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500.

Those are market rates, not IB Gram's price list, and they are published here because a parent who can see the bands negotiates better with everybody including us. Two structural points follow from them. The in-home premium over the equivalent online rate is a travel charge rather than a quality difference. And a rate at the bottom of the range is almost always a university student, which is a sensible purchase for Year 9 homework support and a poor one for an Extended-tier paper in the spring of Year 11.

sections.heading: What licensing each kind of provider needs
paragraphs: This is where a lot of marketing goes wrong, so it is worth stating precisely. An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so none appears here. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service through its app, website and e-services system.

An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval followed by permit and licence steps within a defined window, and renewed annually with the request submitted at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is issued to the institute, not to its teachers, and it does not make an individual tutor approved by anybody.

The practical consequence for a parent comparing providers is a question rather than a conclusion. Ask an individual whether they hold a current MoHRE permit. Ask a centre which KHDA permit the institute holds. And treat the phrase describing a tutor as regulator-approved as a signal to look more closely, because that credential is not issued in that form. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation and claims none; we teach online, one-to-one, and the only verification we can offer is about the tutor's experience with your child's code and tier.

sections.heading: IGCSE or MYP at 16, for the schools in this cluster
paragraphs: Several schools serving Dubai Harbour run the IB Middle Years Programme to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, while others continue the programme to Year 11. Families here therefore compare the two routes more actively than most, often across the same tower. The comparison is usually framed as rigour, which is the least useful axis. The real difference is what each route assesses and therefore what it builds.

IGCSE assesses through tiered external written papers in named subjects with published syllabus codes. It builds procedural speed, mark-scheme literacy and examination stamina, and it produces grades that travel legibly between school systems and countries, which matters for a family who may relocate. MYP assesses through four criteria per subject marked by the school, with extended tasks and a Personal Project. It builds investigation, extended writing and reflection, which are exactly the skills the Diploma core later demands.

Neither route disadvantages a student and each leaves a predictable gap. An IGCSE student entering the Diploma usually needs help with the core's writing and reflection demands. An MYP student entering the Diploma usually needs timed procedural work. Where the choice is genuinely open, the questions are about the child: do they produce better work across three weeks or in ninety minutes, and does the family need an externally marked, portable result at 16? For Ministry equivalency purposes, note that it is the external certificate that is counted.

One thing the comparison does not decide is the tutoring. Whichever route a school takes, the support needed is diagnosed from the student's own marked work rather than from the programme they are on, and the first session should produce the same kind of document either way.

sections.heading: What to ask before you pay anybody
paragraphs: Five questions, in this order, and the specificity of the answers tells you more than any amount of marketing. First: which syllabus code and tier will you teach, and have you taught that combination before? A provider who cannot answer this has not asked you for the information and is not working from the examination your child sits. Second: who is the named tutor and what is their experience at that tier, as opposed to in the subject generally?

Third: what happens if that tutor becomes unavailable in week eight? This is the question the freelance and marketplace models answer worst and the one that matters most in a Year 11 spring, where a twenty-session block has no spare weeks. Fourth: will there be a written record of what has been covered and what was diagnosed, available to me? Fifth, for an individual: do you hold a current MoHRE private tuition permit?

Then one more that applies to everybody, including us. What will you not be able to cover in the weeks available? A provider who answers that honestly is doing the arithmetic. A provider who implies that everything can be covered has either not looked at the calendar or is selling hours. We put our own coverage limits in writing because the alternative is a family discovering them in week eight, by which point the weeks are gone and so is the opportunity to have chosen differently.

Write the five answers down and compare them across providers rather than relying on an impression formed during a phone call. Marketing is designed to be memorable and specifics are not, which is why the provider who gave the vaguest answers is often the one a family remembers most warmly.

sections.heading: Booking from a Dubai Harbour address
paragraphs: Send the board, syllabus code and tier for each subject, the marked mock script if the school will release it, the series your child is entered for, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. On the hours, be honest rather than optimistic: families nominate 16:30 and lose a third of the sessions, and the conclusion afterwards is that tutoring failed rather than that the slot never existed.

We match one tutor per subject to the code and tier and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a written breakdown of lost marks by type with an honest session estimate. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week two, we change the tutor, which is the accountability difference between a platform and a freelance arrangement and the main thing the margin pays for.

The limits, stated before you pay rather than after. Extended-tier specialists at popular spring evening hours are sometimes unavailable for a given week, and we will say so and offer a weekend slot or a defined short block instead of substituting someone who teaches the other board. We cannot promise a grade. And one hour a week can direct the student's other six hours without replacing them, which is true of every provider model on this page.

We would rather lose an enquiry at this stage than take one on a plan that cannot hold. A family who is told in week one that two subjects are realistic and three are not has a decision to make; a family told that all three are fine has a disappointment scheduled for the spring.

process.title: Ask the five provider questions first

process.title: Check the subject basket against equivalency
process.description: On the British track, Ministry equivalency counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Worth confirming in Year 10 while subject choices are still open, and verifying on the Ministry's own channel rather than here.

process.title: Send the code, tier and mock script
process.description: The code decides which tutor and which question style; the script decides how many sessions and what kind of work. With both, the trial lesson produces a plan. With neither, it produces a conversation that reaches the same place a fortnight later and a fee further on.

process.title: Choose the format by school year
process.description: A group is good value for Year 9 and Year 10 content coverage and poor value for Year 11 diagnosis, because the losses are individual. We will say that even when it points away from the sale, because a family who buys the wrong format concludes that tutoring does not work.

process.title: Fix an hour that genuinely exists
process.description: 17:30 from this district on a weekday, with weekend mornings for longer work. Mark the school's trips, breaks and mock window before committing, and agree the Ramadan pattern in advance. A plan built on an hour that does not exist collapses in week three.

whyPoints.title: Models compared, not straw men
whyPoints.description: Every competitor page researched for this market compares itself against an unnamed alternative. This page compares agency, marketplace, freelance, centre, school and platform on rate, accountability and what a parent can actually verify.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS-Levels. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects; the sourced figure is five.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure is attributed to the provider or market source that published it, read in October 2026. Three of seven researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency Dubai families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The licensing distinction made properly
whyPoints.description: An individual tutor holds a MoHRE permit; a centre with premises holds a KHDA Educational Services Permit. Neither makes a tutor regulator-approved, and IB Gram claims no accreditation from any authority or examination board.

whyPoints.title: Format advice that sometimes costs us the sale
whyPoints.description: A group class is better value than we are for Year 9 content coverage. We say so, because a family who buys one-to-one when a group would have done concludes the money was wasted and does not come back when it is needed.

whyPoints.title: Accountability when a match fails
whyPoints.description: If the tutor is wrong after the trial or in week two, we change them. That is the difference a platform margin buys over a freelance arrangement, and it matters most in a Year 11 spring with no spare weeks in it.

faqs.question: Should we use an agency, a freelancer or an online platform for IGCSE in Dubai Harbour?
faqs.answer: It depends on which failure you can least afford. A freelancer may be the best teacher available and is a single point of failure, with nobody accountable if they become unavailable in week eight. A marketplace is cheaper and carries neither accountability nor independent verification. An agency or platform carries a margin and should carry a replacement policy and a written record. In a Year 11 spring with twenty-odd appointments that all have to happen, that accountability is usually worth more than the rate difference.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, so a basket relying on them does not reach the count. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before acting on it.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre good value?
faqs.answer: For Year 9 and much of Year 10, yes. The need at that stage is content exposure and consolidation, the shared pace is not a disadvantage, and the cost per hour is lower. In Year 11 it stops being good value, because the marks your child is losing are individual: unshown method, a misread command term, a unit conversion. A group format cannot see those. For a family in this district there is also a second journey after the school run, which is the real price.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Travel, not qualification. Market sources quote in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The same teacher online costs less because the hour is no longer costing them two. In this district the premium also carries the risk of a single approach corridor and a cruise terminal, which is why the sessions that go missing tend to go missing in the weeks you can least spare.

faqs.question: Do independent tutors in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private tuition need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts has been published. Asking whether a tutor holds a current permit is reasonable and easy to answer. A centre with premises needs a different instrument, a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

faqs.question: What does "KHDA approved tutor" mean?
faqs.answer: In practice it usually means nothing verifiable. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to a training institute with premises, and that permit belongs to the institute rather than to any individual teacher. There is no KHDA approval issued to a private tutor in the way that phrase implies. Treat it as a prompt to ask which permit is held and by whom. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation and does not claim any.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that are AED 150 apart?
faqs.answer: By asking what each rate is constructed from. Ask which syllabus code and tier the tutor has taught, who the named person is, what happens if they stop in week eight, and whether you get a written record of what was covered and diagnosed. A rate at the bottom of the published range is usually a university student, which is a reasonable purchase for Year 9 homework and thin for an Extended-tier paper. The cheaper quote is sometimes the better one, and never for the reason stated.

faqs.question: Our school switched from MYP to IGCSE after Year 9. What changes?
faqs.answer: The assessment model entirely. Criterion marking stops and tiered external written papers begin, with published syllabus codes and an externally marked result at 16. Your child moves from being assessed on investigation and reflection over weeks to being assessed on correct answers produced quickly under timing. That is a real transition and the first term is where it shows. Six to eight sessions on paper technique and mark-scheme reading in that term prevents a disappointing first set of mock results.

faqs.question: Which format suits a Year 11 who is strong in class and weak on paper?
faqs.answer: One-to-one, and quickly. That specific pattern is almost always answer construction rather than knowledge: command terms misread, method invisible, rounding instructions ignored, the final question unattempted because of timing. None of it is addressable in a group, because the diagnosis requires someone reading this student's own script closely. Four sessions on technique plus two paper audits usually move this student more than a term of content revision, and cost considerably less.

faqs.question: What record should a provider give us?
faqs.answer: A written note of what was covered, what was diagnosed and what was set between sessions, available to you rather than held internally. This is the single easiest thing to ask for and the question that separates models fastest: a platform or agency can produce it, a marketplace generally cannot, and a freelancer may or may not. It also matters later, because a new tutor handed that record starts where the last one finished rather than beginning again.

faqs.question: Is it better to begin with a single subject in a Year 11 spring?
faqs.answer: That is usually the right order, and we will suggest it. Starting three subjects at once in a Year 11 spring crowds out the independent work that makes sessions productive, and a student in this district already loses ninety minutes a day to the school run. Begin with the weakest subject or the one with the nearest fixed deadline, let the pattern become clear over three or four weeks, then add. A provider proposing three appointments in week one is selling hours.

faqs.question: How honest are published tutoring rates in this market?
faqs.answer: Patchy. Three of the seven competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams, and one publishes a structured-data price range that contradicts the figure on its own visible page. Against that, the published figures on this page are attributed to the source that stated them and dated to October 2026. Ask any provider what their rate is constructed from; the answer is more informative than the number.

faqs.question: Do you teach the Arabic our school requires alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition. Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires Arab and non-Arab streams to be taught separately because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Support has to match the stream your child sits in and must work with the school's own material, since using different or additional content for these mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. Note too that Arabic does not count towards the five equivalency subjects.

faqs.question: What will you not be able to cover before the series?
faqs.answer: We will tell you specifically in the trial lesson, which is the question we would ask any provider first. A mid-year start has a finite number of usable weeks once trips, breaks and the mock window are marked out, and a plan that implies everything will be covered has not done that arithmetic. Naming the items to abandon is what lets the remaining weeks go to the highest-value work, and it is a more useful answer than an encouraging one.

intro.heading: Same subject, two boards, and the question nobody asks first
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai Hills Estate who decides their Year 10 child needs IGCSE help usually begins by searching for the subject. Maths tutor. Physics tutor. Science tutor. That is one level too coarse, because the two dominant boards in Dubai assess the same subjects through different papers with different tiering rules and different practical arrangements. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into a Core route sitting Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling, and an Extended route sitting Papers 2 and 4. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, is tiered differently and papered differently again.

The consequence is practical rather than pedantic. A student revising Cambridge Extended past papers for an Edexcel entry is practising question styles they will not meet, and a tutor who has only taught one board will hand them exactly that. Before anything else happens, the board and the tier have to be confirmed from the school, in writing, for each subject separately, because a single student can be entered with two different boards across their nine subjects. Schools in this corridor do mix them.

This page is built as a comparison because that is what actually helps at this stage. Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel on the papers that matter. Core against Extended on the grade a tier can actually reach. Dubai Hills Estate against Motor City and Town Square on what each community's school mix does to a tutoring plan. The in-home market against online delivery on cost, logistics and subject match. Each comparison is a table, because five of the six competitor pages in this market carry no table at all and the one that does carries eleven data rows.

The home-tutoring part of the question deserves a straight answer. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is real and widely sold, published at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Monthly in-home arrangements of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate here. IB Gram does not sell that: we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we deliver to Dubai Hills Estate is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

The last thing to say before the tables start is what the two IGCSE years are actually for. Nine or ten subjects, two years, one external examination series, and a set of grades that will decide both the sixth-form route and, eventually, the Ministry of Education equivalency file. That equivalency rule is the single most commonly misreported fact in this market, and one page ranking for these searches publishes the wrong subject count. It is set out correctly, with its source, further down.
