process.title: Settle the board, code and tier
process.description: One email to the school's examinations officer, or the front page of a past paper. Cambridge codes are four digits; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1. This is the filtering that proximity cannot do, and it makes the rest of the search faster as well as better.

process.title: Tell us what time the bus gets in
process.description: Which school, which route, what time your child is actually through the door. On this strip that is usually between four and five, which puts the workable slot at six or later. From Barsha Heights it can be earlier, and from the Marina or the Palm it is usually later.

process.title: Matched on specification, with limits stated
process.description: Matching is by board, syllabus code and tier, not by district. If nobody suitable is free in the hour you need, you are told so with the earliest realistic alternative, including when the match would be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching in Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: One lesson at no cost, worked on a question from the actual specification your child sits, followed by a written note naming the largest single loss and what the first four sessions would target. Nothing is paid until you have read that and agreed.

process.title: One held hour, one timed paper, one error log
process.description: The weekly shape is a tutored hour, a paper attempted alone during the week, and a running error log that becomes the revision document for the series. Progress is measured by whether logged errors stop recurring, which you can check without taking anyone's word for it.

whyPoints.title: The comparison answered rather than dodged
whyPoints.description: Internet City, Media City and Knowledge Park produce the same tutoring answer because none of the things that matter is geographic. Barsha Heights changes the slot and the Marina changes the in-home premium, and that is the whole of the difference. Saying so is more useful than pretending each district needs its own strategy.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific matching
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different tiers, and the sciences handle practical assessment differently. Matching on the syllabus code keeps a tutor working from the right mark scheme in the part of the paper where marks are tightest.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered with a source
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is free for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own channels. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a business permit for a centre, not a tutor credential.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium in a district built for traffic
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online, and the arrival hour on this strip is the hour everyone is leaving. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India.

whyPoints.title: Useful where tower networks are thin
whyPoints.description: Free-zone towers lack the informal recommendation networks that villa communities have, which is the real disadvantage of living here. Matching on specification rather than on word of mouth is what closes that gap, and it is why this page spends its length on how to specify rather than on who to trust.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what IB Gram is
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE office and no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. It claims no relationship with any school named here, and offers a re-match rather than a grade promise.

faqs.question: Would my child have better tutoring options in Media City than in Internet City?
faqs.answer: No. The two free zones sit next to each other in Al Sufouh, share a Metro station and a set of school destinations, and neither has a school inside it. A proximity search run from either address returns almost the same results, which tells you distance is ranking very little. What differentiates a useful tutor is the board, the syllabus code and the tier your child was entered for, and none of those appear in a map listing or vary by free zone.

faqs.question: Does moving inland to Barsha Heights change what we should buy?
faqs.answer: Only the hour. Barsha Heights is the closest residential district to the main Al Barsha school cluster, so a child who was home at half past four is home at half past three, which makes a 5pm slot viable and lets homework follow the session rather than precede it. That is a real gain. The board, the tier, the mark scheme, the series and the specialist who can teach it are all unaffected, so the match itself should stay as it is.

faqs.question: Why are there no schools in these free zones?
faqs.answer: Because they were planned as commercial districts with residential towers attached rather than as family communities. Internet City, Media City and Knowledge Park hold offices, studios and campuses, and the schools sit inland in Al Barsha, along the coast in Al Sufouh, or in the villa belt behind Sheikh Zayed Road. The practical consequence for tutoring is that there is no local teacher pool attached to the district, which is why a search by distance surfaces advertising rather than expertise.

faqs.question: Why is it harder to get a tutor recommendation in a tower than in a villa community?
faqs.answer: Because the networks are thinner. Villa communities like Emirates Hills or Al Safa have long-settled populations where three names circulate at the school gate. Free-zone towers have a more transient population, often arriving through an employer, so a parent typically starts from a search engine rather than from a neighbour. The useful substitute is narrower than a district: other families in your own building with children at the same school share your bus route, bell time and scheme of work.

faqs.question: How many tutors are actually available for a specific IGCSE paper and slot?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the supply suggests. The UK curriculum holds 37 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, so many adults have taught this material. Then subtract everyone teaching the other board, everyone whose experience is the other tier, everyone who has not marked against the official scheme, and everyone unavailable on a spring weekday evening. What remains is small, and it is the same small number from any address on this strip, because only the last subtraction is geographic.

faqs.question: Do tutors actually come to apartments in these free zones?
faqs.answer: Some providers offer it, at published rates of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included. In practice it works awkwardly here: controlled access, limited visitor parking, and an arrival hour that coincides with the whole strip leaving work. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha at five spends about an hour travelling for a one-hour lesson. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and lessons here run over live video.

faqs.question: Is private tuition in these free zones permitted work or an informal arrangement?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is there a fine for tutoring without a permit, and how much?
faqs.answer: The federal portal states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, but no schedule of amounts has been published. Figures circulating online could not be verified against a government source, which is why no number appears on this page. If a provider or an article quotes you a specific amount, ask for the official source, because a confident figure without one is a sign about the rest of their information too.

faqs.question: What does KHDA-approved mean when a tutoring company says it?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing that applies to a tutor. A training institute with premises and staff can hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a business permit for a centre. There is no KHDA approval for an individual private tutor. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation and has no UAE office.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own teacher privately?
faqs.answer: It is best avoided and in some cases prohibited. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify against current guidance, but the sensible answer is to look outside your child's own school.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for on this strip?
faqs.answer: Computer Science and ICT, because the pseudocode conventions and practical components narrow the pool sharply, and Arabic as a first language for a student schooled in English since nursery, which is the hardest match in the UAE market generally. Beyond subject, the hardest booking of all is any popular subject in a weekday evening slot between 6pm and 8pm in the spring, when demand across the whole emirate peaks at once and every specialist already has a full evening.

faqs.question: We are arriving mid-year from another country. Where should we start?
faqs.answer: With the new school's scheme of work rather than with the previous school's reports. The mobile populations in these free zones mean mid-year arrivals are common, and the problem is almost always sequence rather than ability: the new school has covered topics in a different order, and the gaps are invisible until a test. A six to eight session block that maps the gaps and closes them in dependency order is the right purchase, finishing with a written handover rather than drifting on.

faqs.question: Should we book a tutor now for a slot we will need next term?
faqs.answer: On this strip, yes. Weekday evenings between 6pm and 8pm in a popular subject are the most contested hours in the Dubai market, because every family here faces the same school run and reaches the same conclusion. Families who ask in September get the hour they want; families who start looking in March take whatever is left, which is often an awkward time or a weekend block. Booking early is not keenness, it is how the supply behaves.

faqs.question: If we move within Dubai, do we need to find a new tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost never. A move inland or seaward within this part of Dubai changes the school run and therefore the sensible session time, and it changes what an in-home arrangement would cost. It does not change the board, the syllabus code, the tier, the mark scheme or the series your child sits. The correct response is to adjust the hour and keep the arrangement. Families who restart the search after a move usually arrive back at the same answer two months later.

faqs.question: What should the first four sessions produce?
faqs.answer: Something readable without taking anyone's word for it. Session one diagnoses from your child's own marked paper, session two targets the largest single loss, session three tests whether it transferred to an unseen question, and session four is a timed paper marked against the official scheme. If nothing has moved in marked work, the honest conclusion is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong rather than that more hours are needed, and a re-match follows at no extra cost.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet.closingHeading: Same strip, same answer, different hour
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-internet.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Dubai Internet City, the comparison with Media City, Knowledge Park and Barsha Heights is worth running once and then setting aside. The school gates differ, the drive differs, the in-home premium differs, and the thing you are buying is identical: a tutor matched to your child's board, syllabus code and tier, available in an hour the household can protect. Get those three facts from the school, take a free trial lesson on a real question from that specification, and judge the arrangement at session four on a timed paper marked against the official scheme.

intro.heading: Knowing IGCSE is not the same as knowing your child's IGCSE
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2 and mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj. It has its own Metro station on the line towards Expo City, a British-curriculum school and two IB schools inside the district, and a wider cluster of schools in Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and Dubai South that its children travel to.

When a parent here searches for an IGCSE home tutor, the anxiety underneath is almost never about distance. It is about competence: will this person actually know the syllabus my child is sitting? That is a fair worry, and in the IGCSE market it has a precise answer, because IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, with different codes, different tier vocabulary and different mark allocation conventions, and a tutor who has taught one may not know the other.

That is where most disappointment in this market comes from. Not from tutors who cannot teach, but from tutors working diligently from the wrong board's past papers. The student recognises most of the content, the sessions feel productive, and nobody discovers the mismatch until a mock paper looks unfamiliar. The fix costs nothing: confirm the code before the first session.

The second thing worth knowing out here is that general tutoring supply is reasonable and specific supply is not. A tutor who covers lower-secondary mathematics and science is relatively easy to find in any district. A tutor who has taught Edexcel 4PH1 Physics to Year 11 for several cohorts, and can read a marked paper and name the component losing marks, is a narrower proposition, and in a southern district with low residential density relative to its footprint, finding one locally and free at five o'clock is harder again.

The southern corridor adds one more wrinkle. Several schools around Dubai South and Expo City are recent, and families here move between schools more often than in older districts, which means a Year 10 decision such as a tier entry can turn out to constrain a post-16 choice at a different school entirely. That makes the boring administrative questions unusually worth asking out here.

So this page is practical rather than reassuring. It sets out the three questions that test a tutor's board knowledge, what to send with an enquiry so a useful answer comes back, which subjects we can and cannot reliably cover, the tier trap that catches families in newer schools, and what the market charges with every figure attributed. One premise first: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, and sends no tutors to UAE addresses, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit codes identify every subject and determine the paper structure. Many subjects are tiered Core and Extended, with the Core tier capped below the top grades and papers set per tier, so practice has to match the entered tier exactly rather than approximately.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The timetable that counts for a DIP child is the one the school's exams officer holds, not one found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Different codes and structure: 4MA1 Mathematics tiered Foundation and Higher, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Assessment is wholly written in most subjects with practical skills examined on paper, and some subjects are available modularly so units can be sat across series.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so plans belong against the live official document. Checkable reference points: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Mixed-board timetables
programmes.description: Many UAE schools enter candidates with Cambridge for some subjects and Edexcel for others, because departments choose independently. A student can therefore sit 0580 Mathematics and 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year, with two sets of paper conventions and two timetables to manage.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common reason a DIP family ends up with a tutor using the wrong practice set. Check the code per subject on the school's assessment paperwork rather than assuming one board applies across the school, and tell any prospective tutor which codes they will be working from.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into locally
programmes.description: The southern corridor mixes British-curriculum schools offering A Level with IB schools offering the Diploma, and some schools offer both. Year 10 tier decisions constrain that choice: a capped mathematics or science entry removes a prerequisite regardless of the grade achieved within the cap.
programmes.countryNote: Because families here frequently move between schools in a growing corridor, post-16 provision can change between the tier decision and the year it matters. That is an argument for keeping the fuller tier open where the student can genuinely cope with it, and for asking the question explicitly.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-investme.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects DIP families ask about, with both boards' codes where they exist and the component where marks are actually lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Similar ground, different papers and tier language. Most lost marks are procedural: unshown working forfeits method marks, and premature rounding breaks a multi-step answer that was otherwise correct throughout.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves cost the most at the higher tiers. Practical skills are examined on paper in both boards, so the student must describe a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat it, which is a trainable writing skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, stoichiometry and organic chemistry account for most dropped marks. Naming a correct product without the balanced equation or the units scores nothing in most schemes, however well the chemistry was understood.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Revised as a memory subject and marked on command terms. Describe, explain and suggest demand different response shapes, and a correct fact in the wrong shape earns no marks, which is a short fix once named.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: One or two awards covering all three sciences for students not taking separates. Breadth is wide and depth shallower, so revision needs a written rotation; the predictable gap lands on whichever science was taught first.

subjects.name: English
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection and close inference rather than retelling. Writing is marked on structure and control as much as content, and summarising the passage instead of analysing it is the dominant error.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and application to the stimulus material decide the grade. Evaluation must reach a judgement, and a generic answer that never engages the case study loses the application marks outright.

subjects.name: ICT and Computer Science
subjects.description: ICT practical components carry strict output requirements where presentation errors cost marks unrelated to understanding. Computer Science rewards pseudocode in the board's own conventions rather than in a language the student happens to know.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A bridge to A Level or Higher Level IB taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts, introducing calculus and formal function work. Students fluent in 0580 Extended who struggle here usually have a speed gap rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. They sit on top of a full IGCSE load, which is a real cause of Year 11 timetable pressure.

sections.heading: Three questions that test whether a tutor knows your syllabus
paragraphs: This is the most useful thing on the page, and it costs one phone call. The anxiety behind an IGCSE home tutor search in Dubai Investments Park is about competence, and competence in this market is testable rather than a matter of trust.

Question one: which board and code have you taught this subject at, and for how many cohorts? A specialist answers immediately with a code, such as 0620 or 4CH1, and a number. A generalist answers with the subject name and an adjective. Neither answer is dishonest; they describe different services, and only one of them is what a Year 11 student needs.

Question two: what is the tier structure in this subject, and which papers does my child's tier sit? Cambridge sets Core and Extended in many subjects; Edexcel Mathematics is Foundation and Higher. A tutor who blurs these terms, or who cannot say which papers correspond to each tier, is going to build the wrong practice set, and the student will not be able to tell.

Question three, and the decisive one: if I send you two marked papers, can you tell me which component is losing marks before the first session? A specialist says yes and then does it, naming something specific such as method marks forfeited by unshown working, or frequency density omitted in histogram questions. A general tutor offers to assess the student in the first session, which is a reasonable offer and a different one. Ask all three, in that order, of every provider including us.

sections.heading: What to send with an enquiry so the answer is useful
paragraphs: Most tutoring enquiries contain a subject and a year group, and that is not enough information to answer usefully. A provider receiving it can only respond with generalities, which is why so many first conversations in this market feel like sales calls: there was nothing specific to discuss.

Send six things instead and the reply changes character entirely. The board and code for each subject of concern. The tier the student is entered for. The school, so the plan can follow its calendar. The last two marked papers, photographed. The next deadline the school has set, such as a mock window. And the slot pattern your household can actually sustain, which in this corridor is usually a 5pm to 6pm weekday plus a weekend morning.

The marked papers do most of the work. A grade reports that something is wrong; a marked script shows where. With two scripts a specialist can usually distinguish four problems that produce identical grades: weak content, method marks lost to unshown working, a single catastrophic topic, and running out of time. Three of those are short fixes and one is a term, and nobody can tell which from a report card.

sections.heading: Why the board matters more than the district
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages researched for this market, exactly one syllabus code appeared in an entire seven-page cluster. That silence is why the board mismatch is so common: nobody tells families the distinction exists, and the content overlap between Cambridge and Edexcel is large enough that the error is invisible from inside a session.

What differs is the examination rather than the chemistry or the mathematics. Paper structure, the number and length of papers, mark allocation conventions, how heavily particular topics are weighted and how practical skills are framed all vary between the boards. Tier vocabulary differs too, which creates a specific and avoidable hazard: a parent translating between Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher in a phone call can agree to the wrong entry without anyone noticing.

Departments choose independently, which is the part families most often miss. A student at a school in DIP or Jebel Ali can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year. So the check is per subject, not per school, and it takes one email to the subject teacher.

The practical consequence for a household in this corridor is simple. Your postcode decides what time a session can start. The board decides whether the session is useful at all. Of those two variables only one is worth spending time on, and it is not the postcode.

There is a related check worth making on the practice material itself. Ask to see, or be told, which series the papers in a session came from and which tier they were set for. A tutor who can answer that immediately is working from an organised set; one who cannot is improvising, and improvised practice in Year 11 is how a term disappears without any identifiable mistake having been made.

paragraphs: No competitor page in the research behind these pages states a coverage limit. Every service has one, so the omission is simply a decision not to mention it, and it is a large part of why families distrust the category. Here is ours.

Core IGCSE subjects at both boards are reliably covered, and a match can usually be arranged within a few days. Constraints appear in two places. The first is timing: early-evening slots in the weeks before a series are genuinely contested, because much of Dubai's Year 11 cohort wants the same hour. The second is narrow subjects, where a particular board and code combination may not be covered immediately, and where the honest answer is sometimes a date rather than a tutor.

When a request cannot be met you will be told, offered the nearest workable alternative, and given a realistic view of when the slot or the specialism opens. A generalist will not be presented as the board specialist you asked for. That is the standard failure in this market and the reason many families conclude, reasonably, that tutoring does not work for them.

One further disclosure. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a subject and board, the match may be a teacher working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time. That is stated rather than hidden, which is the difference between a disclosed delivery model and a non-UAE phone number in a footer. sections.heading: The tier trap, and why it bites harder in a growing corridor
paragraphs: The tier decision caps or opens the grade available, and it is confirmed by the school to a school deadline. In this corridor it carries an extra complication, because families move between schools more often here than in older districts, and post-16 provision varies between the established schools in Jebel Ali and the newer ones towards Dubai South and Expo City.

The consequence is specific. A capped mathematics or science entry removes a prerequisite regardless of the grade achieved within the cap: a Core or Foundation mathematics candidate is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. If a family then moves to a school with a different post-16 offer, the Year 10 decision constrains a choice nobody was thinking about when it was made.

The honest test is a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now, with no notes, marked properly. Mid-range or above and the conversation is over. Near the bottom of the range and there is a genuine decision about whether a block of work closes the gap in the time available. What should not decide it is which tier feels more comfortable in class, because comfort and capability diverge sharply under examination timing.

Ask the subject teacher when the tier must be confirmed and work backwards from that date rather than from the examination. And ask explicitly what the entry means for post-16 options, because it is frequently presented as an administrative form rather than as the pathway decision it actually is.

sections.heading: What you can verify before paying anything
paragraphs: Price comparisons in this market are hard because most providers do not publish one. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, two quote in US dollars, and one publishes a star rating it awarded itself. So the useful approach is to compare on what can be verified, and to judge any quote against the market.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 per hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

The verifiable items are these. Whether a rate is published at all, and in a currency you transact in. Whether the provider states a position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit that individuals offering private lessons need under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Whether a free trial exists and what condition is attached. Whether the tutor can name the board and code. And whether any approval is claimed from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, which an independent tutoring platform does not hold and we do not hold either.

For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, which is the argument for a defined block with a review date.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: the equivalency rule
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency decides what a UAE university or employer will accept, and it is absent from most pages in this market. Where it does appear it is sometimes wrong, which matters more than an omission because a family can act on a wrong number by making a child sit a subject they did not need.

The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises families whose children sit them anyway as KHDA mandatory subjects.

One competitor page currently ranking in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required. That is wrong on the published rule. Note too how the science route interacts with the count: a Combined Science award is one subject, while separate sciences are three, which can matter for a student whose option choices are otherwise thin.

The American track runs on test scores instead: at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying, with English proficiency satisfied by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section. For the IB no points threshold appears in the source we read, so none is published here. Two cautions as always: IB Gram does not perform, submit or expedite equivalency and tutoring is not required for it, and requirements change, so verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send the six items from the enquiry table: board and code per subject, tier, school, two marked papers, the next school deadline and the slot pattern you can sustain. The free trial lesson comes before any payment and exists to produce a diagnosis rather than a sales conversation.

Expect an honest coverage answer in the same reply. In this corridor that matters more than the rate, because a plan built around a specialism that is not actually available at your hour is worse than no plan. If the answer is a date rather than a tutor, you will get the date.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because nobody can make one honestly. No suggestion that tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch. No satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

On data, one practical note. Enquiry forms collect information about a child, so we ask only for what the plan needs, state why, and keep a privacy link on every page. We do not ask for a child's photograph, and you can ask for the enquiry record to be deleted. Finally, we do not publish or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright; we cite it and link to it instead.

faqs.question: How can I be sure a tutor really knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Test it rather than trust it. Ask which board and code they have taught and for how many cohorts, expecting an answer like 0620 for four cohorts rather than a subject name and an adjective. Ask about the tier structure and which papers each tier sits. Then ask whether they can name the component losing marks from two marked papers before the first session. A specialist answers all three without hesitation, and hesitation on the second question tells you what you need to know.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our house in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach IGCSE one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we send no tutors to any UAE address; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. Other Dubai providers do visit homes, at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included per Bestimate's 2026 rate table, although arranging one this far south at a peak hour is harder in practice than the published rates suggest.

faqs.question: What should I include when I contact a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Six things, and the reply will change character completely. The board and code for each subject of concern, the tier your child is entered for, the school so the plan follows its calendar, photographs of the last two marked papers, the next deadline the school has set, and the slot pattern your household can genuinely sustain. The marked papers matter most: they distinguish weak content, lost method marks, one catastrophic topic and poor timing, which produce identical grades and need different plans.

faqs.question: Is local tutor supply really thinner out here?
faqs.answer: For specific board and code combinations at a specific early-evening hour, yes, and we would rather say it than imply otherwise. Dubai Investments Park is largely industrial and commercial land with residential enclaves, so resident numbers are low relative to the district's size, and it sits far enough south that in-home tutors ration their evening slots by drive time. Online delivery removes the constraint entirely, which is the practical case for it here rather than a general preference.

faqs.question: Our school uses Cambridge for some subjects and Edexcel for others. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Entirely normal, and the single most common reason a tutor ends up with the wrong practice set. Departments choose independently, so a student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics alongside Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year, with two sets of paper conventions and two timetables. Check the code per subject rather than per school, and tell any prospective tutor which codes they will be working from, in writing, before the first session is booked.

faqs.question: What if you cannot cover the subject and board we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the nearest workable alternative and a realistic date for when the specialism or the slot opens. Core subjects at both boards are reliably covered within a few days; narrower combinations and peak early-evening hours before a series are where constraints appear. What will not happen is a general tutor being presented as the board specialist you asked for, which is the standard failure in this market and the reason many families give up on tutoring.

faqs.question: Could the tutor be outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and if so it is stated rather than hidden. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a board and code combination, the match may be a teacher working from outside the country on Gulf Standard Time. Several providers conceal this behind a non-UAE phone number, which is a trust failure rather than a delivery one. The question that matters stays the same: has this person taught this board and code, and can they diagnose a component from a marked paper?

faqs.question: Does the tier entry really affect what our child can do at 16?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this corridor it can bind in an unexpected way. A capped mathematics or science entry removes a prerequisite regardless of the grade achieved inside it, so a Core or Foundation mathematics candidate is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Families here move schools more often than in older districts, and post-16 provision varies between established Jebel Ali schools and newer ones near Dubai South, so the constraint can surface later.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended honestly?
faqs.answer: With a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now, with no notes, and marked properly. Mid-range or above and the decision is made. Near the bottom of the range and there is a genuine question about whether a block of work closes the gap in the weeks available. What should not decide it is which tier feels more comfortable in class, because comfort and capability separate sharply under examination timing. The confirmation deadline belongs to the school.

faqs.question: Why will nobody in this market publish a price?
faqs.answer: We cannot speak for others, but the research behind these pages found three of six competitor pages publishing no price at all and two quoting in US dollars, which is not a currency Dubai families transact in. Our approach is to publish the market instead, attributed and dated October 2026, so any quote can be judged: budget online AED 33 to 65, qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, specialists AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a tutor holds a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the question is reasonable rather than intrusive. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a better option for a family this far south?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong and how far the centre is. A group class teaching a fixed syllabus is reasonable value for broad coverage and poor value for repairing one component, because it cannot stop for your child's specific error. From DIP, add two car journeys per session on top, which is a real cost in time whether or not it appears on an invoice. If the marked papers point at one topic or one component, one-to-one gets there in fewer hours.

faqs.question: Three subjects are weak. Should we book help for all of them now?
faqs.answer: Two comfortably, three only with care and a written plan. Each subject needs a session plus independent practice between sessions, and a Year 11 timetable already carries the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside everything else. A household trying to support four subjects usually ends up with four shallow plans. Start with the subject where the marked paper shows the clearest recoverable component, verify the fix on a timed paper, then move to the next.

faqs.question: When is it too late to start before a series?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is the planning unit that works, with six to twelve focused sessions inside it, and the first week should be diagnosis rather than teaching. Four weeks can still fix one component if the diagnosis is precise. Two weeks mostly produces a tired student. If the remaining time is short, the honest plan targets the component carrying the most marks rather than attempting coverage, and the November series exists as a resit route for both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects to students in the Marina, JBR and the wider New Dubai cluster. Each teaches a full trial lesson before any payment, and every rate conversation happens after you have seen the teaching rather than before.

intro.heading: Price the whole thing, not the hour
paragraphs: Almost every conversation about tutoring cost in this neighbourhood starts in the wrong place. A parent asks what the hourly rate is, compares two or three numbers, and picks. Six months later the household is spending considerably more than anyone intended, and nobody can point to the decision that caused it. The reason is that the hourly rate is the least important variable in the equation. The bill is set by how many subjects are supported and for how many weeks, and those two numbers are chosen almost by accident.

Look at the arithmetic a Dubai IGCSE family is actually facing. A Year 10 student at a British-curriculum school here is typically entered for eight or nine subjects. In a bad term, three or four of them will be causing concern at the same time, because a student who is struggling with workload struggles across the timetable rather than in one place. If the instinct is to buy a tutor for each weak subject, the household has just committed to three or four weekly hours for the remaining eighteen months of the course. Multiply any rate in this market by that and the figure is uncomfortable.

The alternative is not to spend less per hour. It is to buy fewer subject-weeks and choose them deliberately. Two subjects supported properly for two terms, sequenced rather than simultaneous, costs a fraction of four subjects supported indefinitely and usually produces better grades, because a student with two extra hours a week still has evenings and a student with four does not. The expensive mistake in this market is not paying AED 250 instead of AED 180. It is paying anything at all for the fourth subject.

There are local factors that push the Marina bill up specifically, and they are worth naming. Household incomes in this cluster support higher rates, so the quotes that arrive here sit towards the upper end of the market. The school run already consumes the early afternoon, because no secondary campus sits inside the Marina and the ones families use are out along Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and towards Emirates Hills. A visiting tutor adds their own journey into the worst hour on Sheikh Zayed Road, and prices it. And the subjects most often needed here are the ones with the thinnest local specialist cover, which is where rates climb fastest.

This page prices all of that honestly. Every AED figure below is a rate that another provider has published for this market in 2026, named so you can check it, and none of them is an IB Gram price: we do not print a rate card on these pages because the honest number depends on subjects, weeks and level. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India, and this page compares the two models on cost rather than skirting the comparison.

Support at this stage is short, cheap and preventive, and almost nobody buys it, because there is no assessment pressure to force the decision.
programmes.countryNote: In the Marina cluster this is where the money is not spent and arguably should be. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced figure is five excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae, because equivalency is the Ministry's process and not something any tutoring platform performs.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Marina families most often pay for, with the syllabus codes and the specific thing that makes each one expensive or cheap to support. Read this as a shortlist for deciding which two subjects to buy rather than which four.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The most commonly supported subject in this cluster and one of the cheapest to move, because the failures are diagnosable and the practice material is endless. Extended is the tier that keeps A Level and Diploma mathematics open. Marks leak on method communication, on algebraic fraction work and on unjustified steps in multi-mark questions.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent, with its own tier names and paper structure. Worth naming separately because a tutor quoting for IGCSE maths should ask which board before quoting at all, and one who does not ask is not reading the entry. Confirm the code on the statement of entry rather than assuming from the textbook.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits decide most grades, and precision with units, prefixes and significant figures decides most of the rest. Expensive to support late and inexpensive to support early, because the conceptual gaps compound: a student who never understood potential difference will not be rescued in April.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the gateway, and a student who cannot do mole calculations loses marks across every topic rather than in one. That concentration makes it one of the better-value subjects to support, because a handful of sessions on one skill lifts answers throughout the paper.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Volume of content plus precise use of command terms. The cheapest subject to self-support with discipline and the easiest to waste money on, because a weekly hour spent re-reading content with an adult present is comfortable, feels productive and changes very little.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: Where a student takes sciences as a double or single award rather than three separate entries. This changes the tutoring arithmetic substantially, because one tutor can often cover the whole award, where three separate sciences realistically need two or three specialists.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Half the qualification is reading unseen texts, which is a habit rather than a body of knowledge. That makes it the subject where paid hours are least able to substitute for reading volume, and where an honest tutor will sometimes tell a family the problem is not purchasable.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Includes a listening component with a trainable technique, which is the fastest available improvement anywhere in the English family. A small number of focused sessions on listening is one of the highest-return purchases in this market.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent and a structured paper worth seventy. Marks are lost on the mark ladder inside a structured question rather than on content, so technique work of six to eight sessions often moves the grade without teaching any new economics.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study assessment where command words control every mark ceiling. Cheap to improve and often over-bought, because the fix is usually five marked answers with the command words circled rather than a term of content teaching.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Two papers, one on computer systems and one on algorithms, programming and logic. Paper 1 responds to weeks of work and Paper 2 to months, so the honest cost depends entirely on which half is weak. Worth asking a tutor to split the mock before agreeing anything.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge 0470)
subjects.description: Source evaluation and essay argument, where a student who cannot infer loses marks in English as well. That overlap is useful for a budget: supporting the underlying skill once sometimes lifts two subjects, which is the only genuine two-for-one available.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsTitle: What families pay across the Marina cluster, and why it varies
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsIntro: Quoted rates differ measurably between these communities, and not because the teaching differs. What drives the variation is the journey, the school attachment and what a provider assumes about the household.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: Quotes here match the Marina almost exactly, because the access, parking and traffic constraints are identical. Families in JBR report the same pattern: an in-home quote that sits well above the online band, with the gap unexplained.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Marginally lower in-home quotes than the Marina, because the approach from Sheikh Zayed Road is simpler and tower access is easier. The difference is real and small, which rather proves that the premium is about the journey rather than the teaching.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: The highest in-home quotes in the cluster, for a single reason: one bridge. A tutor pricing a journey that can be blocked at half past five prices the risk as well as the distance, and should.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where several of the campuses this cluster uses actually sit. Shorter runs mean an earlier session is possible, which matters more to the outcome than the rate does: analytical work at five is worth more than the same hour at seven.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Lower-rise and closer to Al Khail Road. The enquiry mix here is weighted towards two subjects rather than four, which is also the cheapest pattern, and the households reporting the least wasted spend are disproportionately from here.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities where two or three children often need different subjects. The sibling arithmetic matters: two children in consecutive online slots costs two hours, where two visiting tutors in one evening is rarely even arrangeable.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Longer runs in both directions and quotes at the top of the market. This is where the travel premium is largest in absolute terms and where the gap between an in-home quote and an online specialist rate is widest.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: A single access road and long internal distances, so a visiting arrangement costs more in time than the map suggests. Term-time travel is also more common here, which wastes prepaid blocks unless the schedule can follow a laptop.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Further inland with a different school mix and visibly lower quoted rates. Worth listing because Marina families comparing notes with friends here are comparing a different market, not a better negotiation.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum campuses Marina and JBR households use
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend these schools; they are named as ecosystem context, not as any relationship. The budget-relevant detail is which board each campus enters and whether sciences run as three separate subjects or as a co-ordinated award, because that single fact changes how many tutors a family needs.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses inland along Al Khail Road and Hessa Street
schoolClusters.note: The second ring a Marina household commutes to. Later pick-up times and longer co-curricular programmes push the first workable session later, which is the main reason evening slots here are both scarcer and more expensive.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-marina.modesIntro: Three ways to buy IGCSE support, priced honestly. Everything is one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India, and the comparison below quotes the in-home market rather than pretending it does not exist.

modes.title: One subject, one term, reviewed
modes.description: The cheapest purchase that reliably works. A single subject, a weekly hour, a fixed review point at six weeks against marked work, and an explicit decision to continue or stop. Most families who tell us they wasted money were paying for three subjects with no review point in any of them.
bullets: One subject at a time, chosen on where marks are actually missing
A six-week review using a marked piece compared with an earlier one
An explicit stopping rule agreed before the first session
No commitment past the term

modes.title: A sequenced pair across two terms
modes.description: For the household with two genuinely weak subjects. Rather than two concurrent weekly hours for eighteen months, the subjects are taken in sequence: the first until it stabilises, then the second. Same total hours, half the weekly load on the student, and a natural exit point between them.
bullets: Subjects sequenced rather than stacked, so evenings survive
The second subject reassessed before it starts, because it may have improved
Total spend bounded at the outset
Lower risk of the student disengaging from the whole arrangement

modes.title: A short pre-series block
modes.description: Six to ten sessions aimed at technique before a May or June series: timing, command words, question selection and the two or three specific mark leaks a mock script reveals. This is the highest-return purchase per dirham in the whole market, and it is the one families most often skip in favour of a long slow weekly slot.
bullets: Full papers sat to time and marked within 48 hours
Work driven by the mock script rather than by the syllabus order
A written list of the student's three recurring mark-losing habits
A stated endpoint, so the block does not quietly become a subscription

sections.heading: Subjects times weeks: the only arithmetic that matters
paragraphs: Take a Year 10 student in a Marina tower carrying nine subjects, four of which are causing concern in the same term. The instinct is to find four tutors. Price that properly before doing it. Four weekly hours, held from the middle of Year 10 through to a June series in Year 11, is roughly sixty working weeks after mock seasons, half-terms and family travel are deducted. At any rate published in this market, that total is a number most households would not have agreed to in advance if anyone had written it down.

Now price the alternative. Two subjects, chosen on where marks are genuinely missing rather than where the student feels worst, supported in sequence rather than together: the first for two terms until it stabilises, then the second for two terms. That is a similar number of total hours spread over a longer period with only one weekly commitment at any time, and the student keeps three evenings a week. In our experience the sequenced version produces better grades as well as a smaller bill, because the binding constraint on a struggling IGCSE student is almost never instruction. It is time and energy.

The third option nobody prices is the short block. Six to ten sessions in the ten weeks before the series, aimed entirely at technique that a mock script has identified: timing, command words, question selection, the specific leaks. For a student who knows the content and is underperforming, this is the highest-return spend available anywhere in this market, and it is bounded. Families skip it because it feels insufficient next to a year-long arrangement, which is exactly backwards.

The table below prices four realistic patterns using published market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online, so the comparison is between purchase shapes rather than between providers. Read the right-hand column, which is the one that should decide the choice.

sections.heading: What each tier of the Dubai market charges, and what the money buys
paragraphs: With the shape of the purchase settled, the rate becomes a secondary decision, but it is still worth understanding what separates the bands. The lowest tier in this market is budget online tutoring, typically delivered by university students or generalist teachers. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, and the band as a whole runs from roughly AED 45 to 150. For supervising homework in a Year 8 subject that is good value. For diagnosing why a Year 11 chemistry student cannot do mole calculations it is not, because diagnosis is a learned skill and a generalist has not learned it.

The second tier is a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where most sensible IGCSE purchases sit. The third is the IGCSE, IB or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. The fourth is premium named or examiner-led tuition, where BartyED advertises AED 650. Monthly packages circulate as well: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Bestimate also publishes monthly estimates for a single weekly one-hour session, which is the most useful framing for a household budget: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a specialist in an examination year. Those three numbers tell a Marina family more than any hourly rate, because they are what appears on a bank statement.

Two honesty points. Every figure in this section is a rate another provider has published for this market in 2026, named so that you can verify it; three of the six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in a currency UAE parents do not transact in. And none of these is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card on these pages, because an honest figure depends on how many subjects and how many weeks, and a number printed here would be stale before your child's series.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that changes the bill
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, with Core and Extended entries that cover different amounts of content and carry different grade ceilings. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in the equivalent subjects. This is a budget decision as much as an academic one, and it is usually taken by the school on prior attainment, which means a family who wants to influence it has a window in Year 9 and not afterwards.

The cost consequences run in both directions. A Core entry caps the grade, and in mathematics and the sciences that cap can remove a post-16 route: an A Level or Diploma course that expects a specific tier will not accept a Core grade however high it is within the tier. A family that discovers this after results day faces a far larger bill than any tutoring, because the options are a resit year, a change of post-16 plan, or private entries in the Extended tier.

Running in the other direction, an Extended entry for a student who cannot cope with it produces two years of pressure and a grade no better than a confident Core result. We have seen Marina households buy weekly support in three subjects for eighteen months essentially to hold an Extended entry that was never the right fit, which is the most expensive form of this mistake. The honest conversation is about the destination: what does the student want to study after sixteen, and which tier does that route actually require?

The table sets the decision out on the terms that matter to a budget. The one row families overlook is the last: in some subjects a mid-course tier change is possible before the entry deadline and in others it is not, and the entry deadline falls months before the paper. The gap is wide in both directions: Cambridge June entries close in the spring, months ahead of the papers, and Pearson's November 2026 window ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with its own entry deadline long since passed.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the same subject, two different purchases
paragraphs: A parent asking for an IGCSE maths tutor has not yet specified what they are buying. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run separate qualifications with separate codes, separate paper structures and separate past-paper banks. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. Cambridge Physics is 0625; Pearson's is 4PH1. A tutor who quotes before asking which board is on the statement of entry is not reading the entry at all.

The differences are practical rather than philosophical. Paper structures differ, so timing practice does not transfer cleanly. Pearson offers some subjects in patterns where units may be sat across different series, while Cambridge entries within a series are taken together, and the arrangements vary by subject; the exams officer is the only reliable source on which applies to your child. Past papers, which are the main revision currency in these years, are board-specific, and practising the wrong board's papers is worse than practising none, because it builds confidence in the wrong shapes.

The series calendars also differ and that affects when money should be spent. Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones; Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results timing follows from that, and it matters to families planning a resit budget. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge publishes its own results date for each series on Cambridge International Direct, so take the June or November date for your series from the school as the centre rather than from a figure restated elsewhere. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, the live official timetable rather than any third-party page is the thing to plan against.

sections.heading: Six places IGCSE money is wasted in a Marina household
paragraphs: The first is buying every weak subject at once. A student struggling with workload struggles across the timetable, so three or four subjects look equally urgent in the same week. Supporting all of them converts a workload problem into a workload problem with less free time and a large invoice. Choosing two, on evidence from marked work rather than on the student's sense of dread, is both cheaper and more effective.

The second is paying a specialist rate for supervision. A student who will not start work without an adult present needs an adult present, and that is a legitimate need, but it does not need somebody at AED 300 an hour. Separating the two purchases, supervision and teaching, is the single clearest saving available and almost nobody makes it, because both arrive bundled as a tutor.

The third is group classes that re-teach rather than diagnose. A group session moving through the syllabus at a shared pace is cheaper per hour and frequently worth less than nothing to a student whose problem is specific, because it occupies the time in which the specific problem could have been addressed. Cheaper per hour is not cheaper per mark. The fourth is starting too late: Year 10 is the inexpensive window and the second term of Year 11 is the expensive one, and the rates in this market move with urgency.

The fifth is the travel premium, which we price in the next section. The sixth, and the one that costs the most over two years, is the absence of a stopping rule. A weekly slot that was correct in November is frequently unnecessary by March, and nobody cancels it because the grade is now fine and nobody wants to disturb what is working. A review every six weeks against marked work, with an agreed stopping condition, is the difference between buying a term and buying two years.

sections.heading: The travel premium in the Marina, priced honestly
paragraphs: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one tutoring in this country at AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate in this market, against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Set those two package figures side by side: eight online hours against eight in-home hours, and the in-home version costs roughly twice as much.

What the premium buys in this specific neighbourhood is a journey into high-rise towers with visitor parking constraints, during the hour when Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road are at their worst, for sixty minutes of teaching. A tutor pricing that honestly must charge for it. A tutor who does not charge for it will quietly prefer households closer to home, which produces cancellations rather than savings. Bluewaters Island families see the sharpest version, because a single bridge means the tutor is pricing risk as well as distance.

There is a second cost that never appears in a quote. Restricting the search to people willing to make that journey restricts it to people who live nearby, and in a subject with thin local cover that materially reduces the quality of the choice. The parent is paying more to choose from less. For a tiered subject where the tutor's judgement about Core or Extended may be the most valuable thing they contribute, that trade is a poor one.

Cases where a person in the room is genuinely worth the premium exist and should be named: a younger child who will not engage with a screen, a student who cannot start work without an adult physically present, or a subject needing shared physical equipment. An IGCSE student at fifteen or sixteen working through past papers is none of these; the materials are a question paper, a mark scheme and a script, all of which work better on a shared screen that saves the annotation. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India.
