sections.heading: Examination entries, private candidates and the costs nobody quotes
paragraphs: Tuition is not the only line in an IGCSE budget, and the other lines are poorly advertised. If a student is entered through their school, entry fees are usually folded into the school's charges and the family never sees them separately. If a student is sitting a subject their school does not offer, or resitting after leaving, they become a private candidate and the arrangement changes completely.

A private candidate must find a centre that accepts external entries, meet that centre's own deadlines, and pay that centre's fees. Those fees are set by the centre rather than by the board and they vary, which is why we will not print a figure here: an amount quoted on a page like this would be a guess dressed as information, and this market already has too much of that. Ask two or three centres directly and compare, well before the entry deadline.

The deadline is the part that costs families real money. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series illustrates how early entries close: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, the entry deadline for them had gone months before, and the results for the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's June series closes entries in the spring on the same logic. A family deciding in January that a private entry would be sensible has already missed the window and will wait for the next series, which may mean a lost year rather than a lost term.

Two further cautions on costs. Past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards on their own sites, and a provider charging for a pack of them is charging for something the board publishes itself; a tutor should reference and link the official material rather than redistribute it. And on tax, the sensible question to ask any provider is simply whether the quoted price includes VAT and whether they hold a tax registration number. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because doing so without a Federal Tax Authority citation would be exactly the kind of confident unsourced claim that this market is full of.

sections.heading: Where to stop paying: the signals that the job is done
paragraphs: This is the section that costs us money to publish and it is the most useful one on the page. A tutoring arrangement should have an end, and almost none of them do. The default is that a weekly slot continues until the course finishes, long after it stopped changing anything, because the grade is now fine and nobody wants to disturb what is working. Over eighteen months that default is the largest single item of wasted spend in this market.

Three signals say the subject is done. The first is that marked work has been stable at or above the target for two consecutive assessments, with the student producing it unaided. The second is that the student starts the session by telling the tutor what the problem is, accurately, which means the diagnostic skill has transferred and the external pair of eyes is now redundant. The third, and the clearest, is that the tutor is spending the hour on general revision because there is nothing specific left to fix.

When any of those appear, the right move is to stop the weekly slot and keep a thin connection: a session before each mock, a session on a returned paper, nothing in between. That typically costs a tenth of the weekly arrangement and holds the gain. If the grade slips, resume. A subject that needed support in November and does not need it in March has not become easy; the support worked, which is the outcome everyone wanted.

We agree this rule before the first session rather than after the twentieth, and we raise it ourselves at the six-week reviews. A provider whose incentive is a long weekly subscription will not do that, which is why a parent should set the stopping condition themselves at the outset and write it down. The question to ask any tutor at the trial is simply: what would make you tell me to stop paying? The answer, and the comfort with which it is given, is informative.

sections.heading: What school fees do to the tutoring budget here
paragraphs: Tutoring spend is decided inside a household budget that is already dominated by school fees, and that context has moved recently in a way that matters. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a Marina family, that freeze is the single most relevant financial fact of the year.

The supply side is moving too. Dubai's private sector added six schools during 2025-26 with enrolment rising six per cent, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following the UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Across the emirate there were 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, US at fourteen and the International Baccalaureate at seven.

Why any of this belongs on a tutoring page: a frozen fee and widening supply mean the marginal spending decision in a Marina household this year is more likely to be about tuition than about a school move, and more families will be making it. That makes it worth making well. The honest framing is that tutoring is a bounded intervention with an endpoint, not a permanent line item alongside the fees.

One final caution against false urgency. Tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission, or for school progression, and anyone implying otherwise is selling with a claim about a regulatory process rather than about teaching. The five accredited subjects at grade E or 3 that the British track requires, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, are a floor set by the Ministry; a student clearing them comfortably does not need to buy anything, whatever a tutoring page suggests.

process.title: List the subjects and rank them by evidence
process.description: Send the marked work, not the worry. We rank the subjects by where marks are actually missing rather than by where the student feels worst, and those two orders differ more often than parents expect. The ranking decides which one or two subjects are worth buying, which is the decision that sets the bill.

process.title: Agree the shape and the total before the rate
process.description: Sequenced pair, single subject with a review, or a short pre-series block. We write down the working weeks and the implied total so the figure is visible at the start. Families who tell us they overspent were almost always never shown a total, only an hourly rate.

process.title: Set the stopping rule at the outset
process.description: Two consecutive stable assessments at or above target with unaided work, or a tutor with nothing specific left to fix. Write it down before the first session. Then the six-week review is a decision rather than a progress report, and the default becomes stopping rather than continuing.

process.title: Take the free trial, then talk about money
process.description: A full lesson with the tutor your child would keep, before any payment. Watch whether they work from your child's own marked script and name the specific leak. Rates are discussed after you have seen the teaching, which is the only order in which the number means anything.

process.title: Review against marked work every six weeks
process.description: A marked piece compared with an earlier one against the same criteria. If it is not moving we change the approach or tell you to stop. If no specialist is free in your preferred hour we say so rather than substituting a generalist, and nothing is charged while you decide.

whyPoints.title: The total is shown, not just the rate
whyPoints.description: Working weeks multiplied by subjects, written down before anything starts. Every household that has told us it overspent on tutoring was shown an hourly rate and never a total. Showing the total sometimes loses the sale, which is the point: a family that would not agree to the figure should not be quietly spending it.

whyPoints.title: Rates are attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a named provider's published rate for this market in 2026. Three of the six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two of the three that do quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. We publish no IB Gram rate card, because an honest number depends on subjects and weeks.

whyPoints.title: The stopping rule is agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: Two stable unaided assessments at target, or a tutor with nothing specific left to fix, and the weekly slot ends. We raise it at every six-week review rather than waiting to be asked. The absence of a stopping rule is the largest item of wasted spend in this market over a two-year course.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier are established before any quote
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different qualifications with different papers and different past-paper banks, and Core against Extended changes both the teaching weeks and the post-16 options. A tutor who quotes without asking which is on the statement of entry has not read the entry.

whyPoints.title: We separate supervision from teaching
whyPoints.description: A student who cannot start work without an adult present has a real need that does not require a specialist rate. Naming the two purchases separately is the clearest saving available in this market, and almost nobody offers it because both arrive bundled as a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The in-home market rate is quoted above with its source so the comparison can be made on figures rather than on assertion.

faqs.question: What should we budget for IGCSE tuition in a Marina household?
faqs.answer: Budget the shape before the rate. Published market estimates for one weekly one-hour session put monthly outlay at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a specialist in an examination year, per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. The number that actually decides the bill is how many subjects you support and for how many weeks: four subjects from mid Year 10 to a June series is about sixty working weeks of four hours, and most households would not agree to that total if it were written down first.

faqs.question: My son is weak in four subjects. Can we afford tutors for all of them?
faqs.answer: You probably can and you almost certainly should not. A student struggling with workload struggles across the timetable, so four subjects look equally urgent in the same week. Buying all four converts a workload problem into a workload problem with less free time and a large invoice. Pick two on evidence from marked work rather than on where the student feels worst, support them in sequence rather than together, and reassess the other two in a term. Many families find the second pair improved on their own once the weekly load came down.

faqs.question: Is a Core entry cheaper to support than an Extended one?
faqs.answer: Per week, yes, because there is less syllabus to cover. Over a lifetime, often not. A Core entry caps the grade, and in mathematics and the sciences that cap can remove an A Level or Diploma route that expects a specific tier, which means a resit year or a change of post-16 plan. That costs far more than any tutoring. The expensive version of this mistake runs the other way too: holding an Extended entry that was never the right fit, with paid support in three subjects for eighteen months simply to sustain it.

faqs.question: Does supporting Pearson Edexcel cost more than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Rates do not differ by board, but the purchase does. Cambridge and Pearson run separate qualifications with separate codes, paper structures and past-paper banks: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended, Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. Practising the wrong board's papers is worse than practising none, because it builds confidence in the wrong question shapes. Any tutor who quotes before asking which code is on the statement of entry has not read the entry, and that is the signal worth acting on rather than the price.

faqs.question: Is a group class better value than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and frequently worth less per mark. A group moving through the syllabus at a shared pace re-teaches the lesson the student already sat, which helps a student whose problem is coverage and does almost nothing for one whose problem is specific: a mole calculation they cannot do, a command word they misread, a timing collapse in the last twenty minutes. Worse, it occupies the hour in which the specific problem could have been fixed. Diagnose first with one session, then decide whether the answer is group teaching.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and the honest version is earlier still. Rates in this market move with urgency, and a family arriving in the second term of Year 11 is negotiating from the weakest possible position for the scarcest slots. More importantly, the problems are cheaper to fix early: a conceptual gap in physics or a missing method in algebra compounds across two years, and the same gap costs a handful of sessions in Year 10 and a term in Year 11. The least expensive intervention of all is a term in Year 8 that nobody buys because there is no exam pressure.

faqs.question: How much extra does a tutor who travels to the Marina charge?
faqs.answer: Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour per Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent home tutors from AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The package comparison is starker: around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions, so eight in-home hours cost about twice eight online ones. The premium buys a journey into towers at the worst hour and a pool restricted to whoever lives nearby. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: What does a private candidate pay to sit an IGCSE paper in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Fees are set by the examination centre rather than by the board and they vary between centres, so any figure printed on a page like this would be a guess dressed as information. Ask two or three centres directly and compare. What matters more than the fee is the deadline: a Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, months ahead of the papers, and the Pearson November entry closed well before a window that ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A family deciding in January that a private entry makes sense has already missed the window and may lose a year rather than a term.

faqs.question: Does paying for a block of hours up front actually save anything?
faqs.answer: Sometimes a little, and it reliably costs something else: flexibility. A prepaid block creates pressure to use hours that may no longer be needed, which works directly against the stopping rule that saves real money. It also carries risk in this cluster specifically, because term-time travel is common on the Palm and in the Marina and unused hours in a block are pure waste. If a discount is offered, compare it with the cost of two sessions you will not need. Usually the arithmetic favours paying as you go with a review every six weeks.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for a subject?
faqs.answer: When any of three signals appears. Marked work has been stable at or above target for two consecutive assessments with the student producing it unaided. The student opens the session by accurately naming the problem themselves, which means the diagnostic skill has transferred. Or the tutor is filling the hour with general revision because nothing specific is left to fix. At that point drop the weekly slot and keep a thin connection: one session before each mock, one on a returned paper. That costs a fraction and holds the gain.

faqs.question: Why do some providers quote more in February than in October?
faqs.answer: Because demand concentrates before the May and June series and the specialist slots are finite. A family arriving ten weeks before the papers is competing for the same evenings as everyone else in the cluster and has no time to wait, which is the weakest negotiating position available. The practical answer is to buy the pre-series technique block in October for February, or to accept a weekend morning, which matches faster and is better for timed-paper work anyway. The underlying lesson is that urgency is the most expensive thing a tutoring budget can contain.

faqs.question: We have children in Year 10 and Year 11. Does that halve anything?
faqs.answer: Not the rate, and that is the wrong thing to chase. What it does change is scheduling: two children in consecutive online slots on the same evening is straightforward, where two visiting tutors in one evening is rarely even arrangeable and two journeys are certainly priced. Shared sessions across two year groups are a false economy, because the syllabus positions differ and one child ends up watching. The real saving for a two-child household is the same as for a one-child household: fewer subjects, chosen on evidence, with a stopping rule.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in the rates quoted in this market?
faqs.answer: Ask each provider directly, because practice varies and a quoted figure that turns out to exclude tax changes a monthly budget meaningfully. The two useful questions are whether the quoted price includes VAT and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because asserting it without a Federal Tax Authority citation would be precisely the kind of confident unsourced claim this market already has too much of. Get the answer in writing alongside the rate, before the first invoice rather than after it.

faqs.question: How many subjects can one tutor realistically cover?
faqs.answer: Two well, in adjacent disciplines, if they genuinely hold both: maths and physics, or economics and business studies. Three is where the willingness exceeds the depth, and a single convenient tutor stretched across three subjects is the most common way a family pays specialist money for generalist work. One exception runs the other way: where sciences are taken as a co-ordinated or combined award rather than three separate entries, one tutor can often cover the whole thing, which genuinely reduces the bill. Check which arrangement your child's school uses before deciding how many tutors you need.

faqs.question: Should we be paying for past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. The boards publish past papers and mark schemes on their own sites, and a provider charging for a pack of them is charging for material the board makes available itself. A tutor should reference and link the official sources rather than redistribute them; reproducing syllabus documents, papers or mark schemes is a copyright matter rather than a grey area. What is worth paying for is the marking and the diagnosis: a script annotated against the scheme by someone who knows where the marks go, which is a different purchase from the paper itself.

faqs.question: Do school fees in Dubai change what we should spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: They set the context, and the context moved this year. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Supply is widening too, with seven new private schools for 2026-27 creating 16,846 places. The practical consequence is that more households will be making a tuition decision rather than a school decision, so making it with a total and a stopping rule in front of you matters more.

We will also agree the stopping rule in advance. The trial lesson is free and happens before any payment, with the tutor your child would keep, and lessons are delivered one to one over live video.

intro.heading: The question hidden inside an IGCSE tutor search from this district
paragraphs: Dubai Media City is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh, between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with Dubai Internet City on one side and Dubai Knowledge Park on the other. It has residential towers but no school. Its school-age population lives in those towers and in the surrounding communities: The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Al Sufouh, Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers. Almost every child here travels out to a school gate in Al Barsha, Emirates Hills or along the coast.

The British curriculum is the largest in this city. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools running 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37 per cent of enrolment against 26 per cent Indian, 14 per cent American and 7 per cent International Baccalaureate. So unlike the IB, there is no shortage of adults around Media City who have taught GCSE-level content. The scarcity is finer than that: it is finding someone who knows which board and which syllabus your child was entered for, and what that specific paper rewards.

That distinction is not pedantry. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and splits into Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1 and splits into Foundation and Higher papers. The content overlaps heavily, the papers do not. Cambridge IGCSE sciences handle the practical requirement differently from Pearson. A tutor who has spent three years on Cambridge 0625 Physics past papers and is handed a Pearson candidate will teach competently and miss things, and in Year 11 missing things is expensive.

So the honest version of this page is about identification before instruction. Find the board. Find the syllabus code. Find the tier. Then find someone who has taught that combination. A parent can establish the first three in one email to the school and one look at the front page of a past paper, and this page shows you how. The fourth is what matching is for.

On delivery, we are explicit. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Media City families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, typically between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights. The reason is not cost-cutting. It is that matching on syllabus code only works if the pool is everyone teaching in this time zone, not everyone willing to drive through Al Sufouh at five.

One practical note before the detail. Year 10 is the cheap year and Year 11 is the expensive one, and the difference is larger than most families expect. A student who starts weekly work in Year 10 can still influence a tier decision, still rebuild algebra that was shaky in Year 9, and still treat past papers as practice rather than as evidence of a problem. A student who starts in the spring of Year 11 has eight or nine usable weeks, which is enough to transform paper technique and command-word response and not enough to rebuild two years of content. Both are worth doing. They are not the same purchase, and a provider who pretends otherwise in March is selling optimism rather than teaching.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-media-ci.programmesIntro: Around Media City, the 14-to-16 age group splits across two examination boards and two non-examined alternatives. Knowing which one your child is on changes what tutoring should look like.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5. Grading appears as A*-G or 9-1 depending on the subject version the school entered. Preparation is past papers, mark schemes and command terms, in that order.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes look like 4MA1 Mathematics Specification A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Mathematics Specification A tiers into Foundation and Higher papers. Science practical skills are assessed in the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, which changes how a tutor should prepare a student working online.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · MYP 4 and MYP 5 at this age
programmes.description: The non-examined alternative taken at IB continuum schools: eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria out of eight, with the grade accumulated from coursework across the year rather than from papers. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project. A student here needs criterion literacy, not past-paper technique, which is a completely different tutoring job.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai IB schools run the MYP only to 14 and then enter students for IGCSE anyway, so a child in an IB school may still be sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers. This causes real confusion in the Media City towers, where neighbours at the same school can be on different tracks. The school's examinations officer is the person who can confirm which.

programmes.name: What follows at 16: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide sixth-form options. A Level entry usually requires a grade 6 or B in the subject, and IB Diploma Higher Level choices depend on the same evidence. Mathematics is the pinch point: a student who took Core or Foundation has a visible gap to close before Higher Level mathematics in either system, and closing it in Year 11 is cheaper than in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: In this corridor both routes are available within a short bus ride, with GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh offering British and IB Diploma pathways and Dubai College running the British route. Families often decide at the end of Year 11, which means the Year 10 tier decision has already quietly constrained the choice.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-media-ci.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most requested from the Media City, Marina and Greens communities, with the syllabus codes and the specific places marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended and Higher carry algebraic manipulation, trigonometry beyond right angles, functions and transformations that Core and Foundation do not. Most dropped marks are method marks lost to unshown working, and misread command words on multi-step problems. Past papers under timed conditions fix more of this than reteaching topics does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are the standing complaints from this corridor. The real failure mode is unit handling and rearranging equations under time pressure, not conceptual confusion. Graph questions reward gradient calculation with units stated, which students routinely leave implicit and lose the mark for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables. Students memorise reactions and then cannot handle a substance they have not seen. The fix is pattern work from the periodic table plus deliberate practice on multi-step mole questions where the limiting reagent is not obvious.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High content load, assessed with precise command terms. A student who writes everything they know about osmosis scores below one who answers the question asked. Data and experiment-description questions are the cheapest marks in the paper and the ones least often practised deliberately.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Two IGCSEs' worth of content compressed, or a single award covering all three sciences. Students arrive believing it is easier; the content per mark is denser. Tutoring works best as a triage exercise across the three sciences, targeting whichever discipline is dragging the overall grade rather than spreading effort evenly.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Able writers lose marks by not answering the specific directed task, and by writing beyond the time allowance for the first question. The work is reading the question's audience and purpose instructions properly, then planning to a fixed structure.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Exercise-by-exercise technique: skimming for specific information, note-taking, summary writing with a word limit. Students with strong spoken English often underperform here because the paper tests reading precision rather than fluency. Progress is usually quick with structured practice.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definitions and applied case-study response. The most common loss is answering with general knowledge rather than the case material in front of them. Marks are won by naming the concept, applying it to the stimulus, and finishing with a judgement where the command word asks for one.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithm and pseudocode work for Computer Science; practical application skills for ICT. Students who code confidently in Python still lose marks on the required pseudocode conventions and on trace tables, which are mechanical skills that respond to short, repeated practice.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 and 0544 streams, plus school-set MoE requirements
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. For additional-language students the gap is usually script fluency and vocabulary, which responds to short frequent sessions rather than long ones.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study recall. History candidates lose marks by describing sources rather than using them as evidence for a claim; Geography candidates lose them by omitting named examples. Both are structural problems with a short fix once the student knows what each command word is asking for.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor search from Dubai Media City is really asking
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Dubai Media City means, in practice, one-to-one teaching for a Year 10 or Year 11 student on a named board and syllabus, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time. There is no school inside the free zone, so there is no local teacher pool attached to the district. The filter that matters is the syllabus code on the front of the paper, not the distance to the tutor's flat.

This is a different problem from the one IB families face. The British curriculum is the biggest in Dubai, so plenty of nearby adults have taught this material. The question is whether they have taught the version your child is entered for. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, tier differently, and handle practical science differently. A tutor fluent in Cambridge 0620 Chemistry will prepare a Pearson 4CH1 candidate reasonably well and will still be working from the wrong mark scheme, which shows up in the final third of the paper where marks are tightest.

There is a quick way to settle it. Ask the school's examinations officer for the board and syllabus code for each subject, or look at the top of any past paper your child has been given: the code is printed there. Then ask a prospective tutor which board they teach that subject on, and which tier. A specialist will answer with the code. A generalist will say that the content is much the same, which is true and is also not an answer.

Having identified the specification, the location of the tutor stops being relevant. Lessons run over live video, the slot starts on time, and the pool of available specialists is everyone teaching in Gulf Standard Time rather than everyone willing to cross Al Sufouh in the evening. That is the whole argument for the delivery model, and it is stronger for IGCSE than for almost anything else, because the board-specific match is so easy to get wrong.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: how to tell, and why it changes the teaching
paragraphs: Both boards are widely used in Dubai, sometimes within the same school for different subjects. The table below sets out the pairs most often requested from this corridor, with the codes, the tier structure and the practical-science arrangement. Print it, then check it against your child's papers.

The differences that matter to a tutor are structural. Cambridge tiers mathematics into Core and Extended with separate papers and a grade cap on Core; Pearson Specification A tiers into Foundation and Higher. Cambridge sciences are offered with alternative arrangements for the practical requirement depending on what the centre runs, while Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers. For a student working with an online tutor, that second difference changes the preparation: where there is no separate practical paper, experiment description and data interpretation have to be drilled inside written-paper practice.

The other live difference is modular entry. Pearson's International GCSE structure allows some subjects to be sat across sessions, which gives a student a second chance at one paper without repeating the whole qualification, while Cambridge is generally a single-series linear entry with November as the resit route. If your child's school has entered them in a way that allows a staged approach, that is worth knowing before you plan a tutoring block, because it changes what the next eight weeks should aim at.

None of this makes one board better. It makes the match board-specific. The practical consequence for a Media City parent is that the first question to a tutor is not how experienced they are. It is which board, which code, which tier, and when did they last teach it.

sections.heading: The tier decision: Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher
paragraphs: The tier is the most consequential decision in a British-curriculum Year 10, and in Dubai it is often made quietly on the basis of a Year 9 assessment. Core and Foundation papers cover less content and cap the achievable grade. Extended and Higher cover more and leave the top grades available. Schools make the call to protect students from a paper they cannot access, which is a legitimate reason, and sometimes to protect a results profile, which is a different reason.

What a parent needs is evidence rather than an opinion. The useful evidence is a Core or Foundation paper and an Extended or Higher paper from the same series, both sat under time. If the student scores comfortably on the lower tier and collapses in the second half of the higher one, the school is probably right. If they score moderately on both, the gap is specific topics, and specific topics are what a term of weekly tutoring is for.

The downstream consequence is what families miss. A student who sits Core or Foundation mathematics and then wants A Level Mathematics or Higher Level mathematics in the IB Diploma has a visible algebraic gap to close, and closing it during Year 12 while the course moves on is painful. Closing it during Year 11, when the content is familiar and the pressure is lower, is a fraction of the work. That is the single best argument for starting tutoring in Year 10 rather than the spring of Year 11.

The table sets out what each tier changes. Exact content and grade arrangements vary by syllabus version and by what the centre enters, so treat it as the shape of the decision and confirm the detail with the school.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs here, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start and it is where the money is most often wasted. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. At that price the tutor is typically a university student or recent graduate. For supervised homework in Year 9 that can be fine. For Year 11 past-paper marking against an official scheme it usually is not, because the person marking has never seen the scheme.

The next tier up is where most IGCSE work should sit. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. For a single IGCSE subject in Year 11, the specialist tier is usually justified only if the grade sits on a university or sixth-form threshold.

In-home visits in Dubai are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's band for in-home work is AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The second number is roughly double the money for half the number of contacts, which for a Year 11 student working through one past paper a week is the wrong shape as well as the wrong price.

All of those are figures other providers have published, not IB Gram prices. The things a parent can actually verify before paying are narrower than they look, and worth insisting on: the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms, and what happens if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is the real reason this section exists.

sections.heading: The five-subject rule: Ministry of Education equivalency for British-curriculum students
paragraphs: This is the part of the British route that Dubai families discover late and that almost no tutoring page mentions. A UAE secondary certificate equivalency is what lets a qualification be used for local university admission and for official purposes, and the Ministry of Education publishes clear requirements for the British track.

As reported in July 2026, students on the British curriculum must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause matters, because a family counting Arabic towards the five will come up short.

One competitor page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five accredited subjects excluding Arabic and Islamic education, so check any count you are given against the Ministry's own published requirements rather than against a tutoring website. The American-track rules are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math.

Two cautions. No IB points threshold for equivalency appears in the source we could read, so any IB figure you are quoted should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before you rely on it. And equivalency is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates: it is a process you complete with the authority, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. sections.heading: June, November and the resit route, counted backwards
paragraphs: A parent in Media City planning tutoring needs two dates: when the papers are, and when entries close. The second is the one that surprises people, because it sits months before the first and is handled by the school without much announcement.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a UAE candidate, whatever a search result tells you. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination as a result of using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is precisely why a tutoring page should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

The planning consequence is simple. If a grade matters for a sixth-form place, the June series is the one to aim at and the November series is the recovery route, with results arriving in January. Counting backwards from June, the work has to start in the autumn: a Year 11 student beginning in March has eight or nine weeks of real preparation available, which is enough to fix technique and not enough to fix two years of missed algebra.

sections.heading: Practical science, and whether online lessons can prepare for it
paragraphs: This is the honest objection to online IGCSE science tutoring, and it deserves a straight answer. A tutor over video cannot stand beside a student at a bench while they set up a titration. What they can do is prepare the student for how practical skill is actually assessed, which in an examination is on paper.

Both boards test practical understanding in writing. Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers for International GCSE sciences. Cambridge centres run either a practical arrangement or an alternative-to-practical arrangement depending on what the centre offers, and in either case the written requirement is the same shape: describe a method precisely enough to be repeated, identify variables, read a measuring instrument correctly, process data, plot it, and evaluate the method's limitations. Every one of those is a paper skill and every one responds to screen-shared practice on real past questions.

Where online delivery genuinely helps is in the marking. A student who draws a graph and has it annotated live, mark by mark, against the official scheme learns faster than one who does the same practical twice. The commonest lost marks in science data questions are mechanical: axes without units, a gradient calculated without showing the triangle, a conclusion that restates the trend instead of evaluating it. Those are fixed by repeated marked practice, not by laboratory time.

The school remains responsible for the laboratory work, and should be. If your child's centre runs a separate practical examination, ask the science department what equipment the paper assumes familiarity with, and treat that as school business. Tutoring covers the written assessment of practical skill, which is where the marks are, and it should say so plainly rather than implying a laboratory it does not have.

sections.heading: When the match is hard, and what we say instead of improvising
paragraphs: Mathematics and the three separate sciences are straightforward to match in this corridor. The awkward requests are Cambridge ICT with its practical components, Computer Science pseudocode conventions, Arabic as a first language for a student schooled in English, Business Studies coursework where the centre runs it, and any subject in the final six weeks before a series when every specialist is already booked.

We publish the limit rather than improvising around it. If no suitable tutor is free in the slot you want, you are told that with the earliest realistic alternative. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before you book rather than disguised behind a local-sounding contact number. No provider in the researched set discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why this paragraph is unusual rather than modest.

The second honest limit is about what tutoring can do inside a short window. A Year 11 student arriving in March can reliably improve paper technique, time management and command-word response, and can close one or two specific topic gaps. They cannot rebuild Year 10 algebra while also revising everything else. A provider who tells you otherwise in March is selling you hope. The useful conversation at that point is about which subjects to prioritise and which to leave alone.

If a match turns out wrong after the first paid session, you are matched again. That is a testable promise, which is more than can be said for claims about quality. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in a market where one provider sells completed coursework outright, the absence of a guarantee is a feature rather than a gap.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child's school entered them for?
faqs.answer: Two ways, both quick. Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the board and syllabus code for each subject, or look at the top of any past paper your child has been given: the code is printed on the front. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 Mathematics or 0625 Physics. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. Once you have the codes you can match a tutor to the specification instead of to a subject name, which is the difference that shows up in the final third of a paper.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether a tutor has taught Cambridge rather than Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, in Year 11. The content overlaps heavily, so a good teacher will cover the material either way. What differs is the paper structure, the tier arrangements and the mark scheme's preferred wording, and those decide marks in the tightest part of the paper. Cambridge tiers mathematics into Core and Extended; Pearson Specification A uses Foundation and Higher. Science practical skill is assessed differently between them. Ask a prospective tutor which board and code they teach, and when they last taught it.

faqs.question: My child has been put on Core maths. Can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the way to argue it is with evidence rather than opinion. Have them sit one Core or Foundation paper and one Extended or Higher paper from the same series, both to time. If they handle the lower tier comfortably and collapse in the second half of the higher one, the school is probably right. If they score moderately on both, the gap is specific topics, which is what a term of weekly work addresses. Raise it early in Year 10, because entries are submitted months before the series.

faqs.question: What does Core or Foundation tier cost my child later?
faqs.answer: A visible gap before A Level Mathematics or Higher Level mathematics in the IB Diploma. The lower tiers omit the harder algebra, trigonometry and functions that both sixth-form routes assume from day one, so a student arriving in Year 12 from Core spends the first term catching up while new content keeps coming. Closing that gap in Year 11, when the material is familiar and the pressure is lower, costs a fraction of the effort. That is the strongest practical argument for starting support in Year 10.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do families around Media City ask for most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first by a wide margin, then Physics and Chemistry as separate sciences, then First Language English and English as a Second Language exercise technique. Combined and Coordinated Sciences come next, usually from families who expected them to be easier and found the content per mark denser. Economics and Business Studies appear mostly in the spring, when case-study response technique becomes the limiting factor. Computer Science and ICT are the hardest to cover at short notice in this corridor.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for IGCSE sciences without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: For the assessed part, yes. Practical understanding in International GCSE sciences is tested in writing: describing a method precisely, identifying variables, reading instruments, processing and plotting data, and evaluating limitations. Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers, and Cambridge centres run either a practical or an alternative-to-practical arrangement. All of that is screen-shareable and improves fastest with live marking against the official scheme. The laboratory work itself stays with the school, which is where it belongs.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education actually require?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competitor page ranking for these searches says six subjects, which does not match the published requirement. Verify any count on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority rather than from a tutoring website.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for a candidate sitting in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates centres to six administrative zones with different timetables, so your school must use the correct zone version.

faqs.question: How does a resit work if the June grade is not enough?
faqs.answer: November is the recovery series for both boards, with Pearson results reaching students in January and Cambridge following its own schedule. Entry administration sits with the school or the examination centre, not with a tutoring provider, and private candidates need a centre willing to enter them. The preparation is shorter and more surgical than a first attempt, because the previous result usually points at two or three topics. Decide early: a November entry planned in August is calm, and the same decision in October is not.

faqs.question: What should a Year 11 weekly session actually consist of?
faqs.answer: A timed paper or section, marked line by line against the official scheme with the student present, and an error log that accumulates into a revision document. Reteaching happens only where the papers show a real gap. This matters because the most common Year 11 problem is not ignorance but answering a question other than the one that was set, and that is only visible when real papers are marked against the real scheme rather than discussed in general terms.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a premium tutor at AED 500 or more an hour?
faqs.answer: Rarely for a single IGCSE subject. The published premium band reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650, while qualified subject tutors online are published from AED 150 to AED 300 and specialists from AED 200 to AED 450. For an IGCSE year, continuity matters more than prestige: a mid-tier tutor held weekly for two terms usually does more than a short premium block. The case for the top band is narrow, mostly where a grade sits on a hard threshold.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor who lives nearby so they can come to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Other providers offer that, at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is not only price: it removes about an hour of a tutor's driving from each lesson, makes the slot survive a bad evening on Sheikh Zayed Road, and widens the pool to specialists on your child's exact syllabus.

faqs.question: Should we use one tutor for maths and the sciences, or separate specialists?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but be careful what you are buying. A tutor genuinely strong in Physics and Chemistry is common; one equally strong in Extended mathematics, Biology and First Language English is unusual. Where a single tutor covers several subjects, ask which they teach most often and how recently. For two subjects on the same board it is often a good arrangement because the student keeps one relationship. For three or more, the depth usually thins somewhere.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 now. Is it too early to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and most effective moment available. Year 10 support prevents the Year 11 scramble instead of repairing it, allows a tier decision to be made on evidence, and leaves time to fix algebra rather than triage it. One hour a week in the subject that is actually weak, across Year 10, usually costs less than an intensive block in the spring of Year 11 and does considerably more. Families who start in March of Year 11 can improve technique reliably, and little else.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education tutored the same way as other subjects?
faqs.answer: Not quite, because the rules are different. Arabic is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students since the expectations and language of instruction differ. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. Honest support therefore reinforces the school's own material and builds language fluency rather than importing a parallel syllabus, and short frequent sessions work better than long ones.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the series, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Dubai Production City, which residents still call IMPZ, holds a large British-curriculum cohort and no secondary campus inside its own boundary. Students bus out to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and Jebel Ali, and they come back late. That shapes when tutoring can happen. But the thing that shapes what tutoring should cover is not the community at all. It is the exam series, and the deadlines sitting months in front of it.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Production City candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Those are the two calendars almost every Dubai British-curriculum student lives inside, and the entry deadlines that govern them sit with the school's exams officer, not with the parent.

The practical consequence is that the useful question is never "should we get a tutor". It is "what do the next eight weeks have to achieve, and is that achievable". Eight weeks before a mock is a different brief from eight weeks before a terminal paper, which is different again from eight weeks after disappointing results when a November resit is on the table. Each one calls for different work: content repair, technique repair, or a narrow push on two specific papers.

This page lays out that calendar counted backwards, the AED cost of buying those weeks in Dubai, and the honest position on home visits. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one live video. We say so early because the alternative is a family booking on a false expectation, and because for exam-block work the online format is the one that actually protects the hours. A session that starts at the booked minute, twice a week, for eight weeks, is fifteen hours. The same arrangement with a thirty-minute drive at each end loses several of those hours to Al Khail Road before anybody opens a paper.

One more calendar fact shapes revision in this community specifically. The Dubai academic year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, and Ramadan moves earlier by roughly eleven days each year, which means the weeks it overlaps with mock season shift from one year to the next. Families here plan around shortened school days and post-Iftar study, and a tutoring block written without reference to that is a block that will lose sessions. We build the schedule around it rather than discovering it in week three, and we hold the slot rather than quietly dropping it.

Figures and timetable references on this page were reviewed in October 2026. Where a date can be revised, link and read the official timetable rather than trusting any restatement of it, including ours. Pearson in particular publishes provisional timetables for sessions a year ahead and then revises them, so the live PDF on the Pearson support site is the only version worth planning against.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.programmesIntro: Three qualification routes cover nearly every Production City enquiry at this stage, and the distinction between them changes the paper structure a student will actually sit. Ask the school's exams officer which board each subject is entered under before buying any tutoring.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE subjects are mostly tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Syllabus codes matter: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Assessment is linear, sat at the end of the course, with practical or alternative-to-practical papers in the sciences. Grading in the UAE is generally reported on the A*-G scale.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every UAE centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Your child's exams officer knows the zone. Ask for it in writing before planning revision around any published date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE uses 4-prefix codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry, graded 9-1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the sciences are untiered. Pearson offers some subjects in a modular pattern where units can be sat across sessions, which changes revision planning entirely compared with a single terminal run.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, including International GCSE sessions a year out, and revises them. For a Production City family this means the timetable to plan against is the live PDF on the Pearson support site, and the resit decision in January is informed by results that reached November 2025 students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools move students from IGCSE into AS and A Level at 16, usually requiring specific IGCSE grades for entry to each subject. Mathematics and the sciences typically need grade 6 or B as a minimum, and the step up in abstraction between IGCSE Extended and AS is the steepest most students will have met.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

programmes.name: IB Diploma progression
programmes.description: A proportion of Production City IGCSE students move into the IB Diploma rather than A Levels, usually at a different campus. The Diploma asks for six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Breadth replaces the narrowing most IGCSE students expect at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: The transition subjects that cause the most trouble locally are Mathematics and the sciences, because IGCSE Extended does not cover the calculus or the uncertainty treatment a Higher Level course assumes from week one. Families here often book a short summer block between Year 11 and DP1 specifically to close that gap.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Production City and Jebel Ali families most often ask about near an exam series, with the component where the marks are usually lost. Each is board-specific in practice, so the tutor is matched to the board as well as the subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher both reward method marks for visible working. Algebraic manipulation, bounds and vectors cause most of the damage. Students who answer mentally and write only the answer lose marks they had already earned in their heads.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1. Electricity, moments and the equations of motion are where grades are decided. The common failure is describing an outcome without naming the principle, which scores nothing on an explain question however correct the description is.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1. Moles and stoichiometry, electrolysis and organic chemistry carry the paper. Students lose marks on state symbols, on unbalanced equations, and on failing to show the calculation steps the mark scheme awards separately from the answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1. The content volume is the problem rather than its difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and genetics generate the most lost marks, and command-term discipline matters: describe, explain and suggest each buy different things.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 and 0510, Pearson 4EA1. Directed writing and the summary question are the most teachable components in the whole qualification, because both are governed by a structure that can be learned in a handful of sessions once a student sees the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0455 and Pearson 4EC1. Diagram accuracy decides the grade: a correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram with analysis attached scores where prose alone does not. Data response questions need figures quoted from the extract, not paraphrased.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Cambridge 0450 and Pearson 4BS1. Evaluation marks are the bottleneck. Students describe advantages and disadvantages competently and then do not reach a justified judgement, which is where the top band sits in every extended-answer rubric.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 and Pearson 4CP0. Paper 1 theory covers data representation, hardware, networks and security; the programming component rewards pseudocode discipline. Trace tables and binary conversion are high-frequency, high-return topics close to an exam.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Cambridge 0508 first language and 0544 foreign language. For Dubai students this sits alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement, and the two are not the same syllabus. Families frequently need support on the school's mandatory stream as well as the examined IGCSE.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0606. Taken by stronger mathematicians as a bridge to AS, covering early calculus, trigonometric identities and series. It is the single most useful preparation for A Level Mathematics available at sixteen, and the cohort taking it is small enough that specialist tutors are scarce locally.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.regionsTitle: Where Production City students come home from, and when
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.regionsIntro: Session timing in this cluster is set by the bus, so these notes are about the school run rather than the architecture. Each is a community a Production City family is routinely grouped with when a tutor plans an evening.

regions.name: Dubai Production City (IMPZ)
regions.note: No secondary campus inside the community. Year 11 students are typically home between four and half past four, which puts a workable session at 5:30pm or later on a weekday.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Holds Greenfield International School on site, so some DIP students are home by four. Shorter run, earlier session, and the one nearby community where a 4:45pm start is realistic.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Arbor School sits inside the community and metro access is good. Families here often run a split timetable, with a primary child home early and a Year 11 sibling home an hour later.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Dense clusters with contested visitor parking, which is why an in-home tutor's last three minutes often take as long as the previous fifteen. Online sessions remove that variable entirely.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: The Winchester School Jebel Ali and Delhi Private School Dubai serve this area, both large and both on long bus routes. Evening availability here is tight and books out early in the exam term.

regions.name: Dubai South and Emaar South
regions.note: Long distances between residential pockets and limited campus provision inside them. Students here have the longest bus day in the cluster, and a 6pm start is often the first honest slot.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-density enclave within Dubai Investments Park with a single main access route. Pleasant to live in, awkward to reach between five and seven on a weekday.

regions.name: Motor City and Sports City
regions.note: Directly north of Production City across Al Khail Road, and where several Production City families' children actually attend school. Ten minutes on a Sunday morning, thirty on a Tuesday evening.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Investments Park, Motor City and Sports City
schoolClusters.note: The nearest ring of campuses to Production City and where much of its IGCSE cohort studies. Predominantly British curriculum at secondary with sixth-form routes, which makes Cambridge and Edexcel entry questions the most common ones we field from this area.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and the southern corridor
schoolClusters.note: Large established campuses serving Jebel Ali, Discovery Gardens, Al Furjan and Dubai South. A mix of British and Indian curriculum at secondary, so a single household sometimes has one child on IGCSE and one on CBSE in the same term.

modes.description: Two sessions a week for eight weeks, with a fixed end date. The first session each week repairs content; the second is a timed paper marked against the published mark scheme, with an error log carried forward. Sixteen sessions is enough to move technique reliably and not enough to drift, which is exactly why the end date is written in at the start.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar counted backwards, for a UAE candidate
paragraphs: Start with the series, then count. A Production City candidate sitting Cambridge IGCSE sits the June series; November is the resit route. There is no February or March series available to UAE candidates, that series being offered to India only. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE candidate sits May/June or November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

From the exam window, every other date moves backwards and is set by somebody other than the parent. The final entry deadline sits with the school's exams officer, months ahead. Coursework or practical assessment windows sit earlier still. Mocks are internal and usually land in the winter term for a June candidate, which is the first honest signal of where a student actually is rather than where their classwork suggests they are.

Results then set the next decision. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those two dates are why the resit conversation in this community happens twice a year, in late August and in late January, and why an eight-week block starting in September or February is the most commonly booked thing we do.

One operational warning worth repeating. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in, and read that timetable rather than a generic one.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of tutoring costs in Dubai, and what it buys
paragraphs: Price the block, not the hour. An eight-week block at two sessions a week is sixteen hours. At the Dubai market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, that is AED 2,400 to AED 4,800 for the whole intervention. At the in-home band of roughly AED 180-350, the same block is AED 2,880 to AED 5,600, and the difference is the car.

Seeing it as a block changes the decision in a useful way. A monthly package of AED 799 for eight online sessions, a figure seen on competitor package pages in October 2026, looks cheap per session until you ask what the eight sessions are for. Sixteen targeted hours with a defined outcome is a better purchase than forty unfocused ones, and it is also easier to stop.

The figures below are the Dubai market, drawn from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai rate table and read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram prices. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; EdFlik lists from AED 45-65 for budget online; TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED quotes AED 650 at the premium end. Three of the six main competitor pages in our research publish no price at all.

What the money does not buy is worth stating. It does not buy a grade, and we will not promise one. Sixteen hours of specialist teaching in the right eight weeks reliably improves technique, exam pacing and command-term reading, which is where most recoverable marks sit. It does not substitute for two years of content a student did not learn.

sections.heading: Why a home visit costs the exam block hours it cannot afford
paragraphs: In an eight-week block, hours are the scarce resource, and a home visit spends them in a place no mark scheme rewards. A tutor travelling to Production City from the Al Barsha or Motor City campuses faces twenty minutes off-peak and closer to forty between five and seven, which is exactly the window a Year 11 student is available. Over sixteen sessions that is a substantial amount of time priced into your invoice and none of it is teaching.

The second cost is reliability. A block only works if the sessions actually happen on schedule, because each one builds on the error log from the last. A cancelled session in week five of eight is not one lesson lost; it breaks the sequence. Road closures on the Expo corridor, a late school bus, a sandstorm afternoon: each becomes a cancellation when the lesson depends on somebody arriving.

The third is the pool. The narrower the requirement, the worse the local map performs. Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson modular units, Arabic as a first language: these have small cohorts, and a tutor who both knows the syllabus and will drive to IMPZ in the evening may simply not exist. Online, the requirement is subject knowledge and a shared hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is not a sales comparison between two things we sell. It is the reason we do not sell one of them here. Independent home tutors work in this area and for a younger child who needs physical supervision they can be the right answer. For a Year 11 exam block, the format that protects the hours is the one that does not require a journey.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can realistically achieve, subject by subject
paragraphs: The honest answer differs by subject, and any provider who gives you one number for all of them is selling rather than teaching. Technique-heavy components move fast. Content-heavy ones do not, because there is no way to compress two years of biology terminology into sixteen hours and no tutor should claim otherwise.

Mathematics responds quickly, because a large share of lost marks are method marks the student had already earned mentally and did not write down. Teaching a student to show bounds, to set out an algebraic rearrangement line by line, and to read whether a question wants an exact value or three significant figures is the work of a few sessions and it is worth marks across every paper.

English Language responds quickly for the opposite reason: the directed writing and summary tasks are governed by a structure. Once a student sees what the mark scheme is actually counting, their output changes within two or three sessions. Economics and Business Studies move on evaluation technique, which is the specific band most students never reach despite knowing the content.

The sciences are slower and more selective. Electricity in Physics, moles in Chemistry and genetics in Biology are each worth targeting individually, and a sensible eight-week plan picks two or three topics rather than attempting the syllabus. That is a decision made with a past paper and a highlighter in week one, not with a brochure. A student who tries to revise all of Cambridge 0620 in sixteen hours will cover everything shallowly and recover nothing.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: find out which one your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: A surprising number of Dubai parents do not know which board their child is entered under, and in a school running both it can differ by subject. It matters because the papers differ. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C; Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher and graded 9-1. A past paper from the wrong board is practice for an exam your child is not taking.

The sciences differ further. Cambridge 0625 Physics offers a practical paper and an alternative-to-practical route, and which one a school enters candidates for changes what needs practising. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are untiered. Pearson also offers some subjects in a modular pattern where units can be sat across sessions, and that single structural fact reshapes a revision plan more than any teaching method does.

Grading scales add confusion on a report card. A student with 9-1 grades in two subjects and A*-G in three is not inconsistent; they are entered with two boards. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, the sourced rule refers to five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, which covers both scales.

The practical step is a one-line email to the exams officer asking for the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject, in writing. Take that list to any tutoring conversation. We match tutors to the board as well as the subject, and the first thing we ask for is that list.
