sections.heading: Permits, KHDA and the questions to ask before you book anyone
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a rating from Outstanding to Very Weak. Those reports are free and public, and worth reading before a Year 10 transfer decision.

Individual tutors are a different matter. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time via the MoHRE app, website or e-services system.

u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fines is published anywhere official, so any specific figure quoted to you is unverified and should be treated as such. One further point relevant to Abu Dhabi families reading this: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises. We have no UAE office. Ask any provider which permit they mean when they describe themselves as approved, because the phrase is used loosely in this market.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than it once did, but practical assessment, controlled components and school-set projects still exist, and the honesty rules around them are the same as at Diploma level. A tutor teaches the skill and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not produce it.

On practicals specifically, a common question from Production City families is whether online tuition can prepare a student for a laboratory paper. It can, for the parts that are examined: experimental design, variable control, tabulating results, calculating gradients, identifying sources of error and evaluating a method. Those are paper skills and they are where the marks are. What online tuition cannot do is substitute for time holding a burette, which is the school's job and which schools do.

We also do not reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are copyright material. Our tutors reference the official source, link to it, and work with papers the student or school already holds legitimately.

One competitor in our research sells completed Internal Assessments. That market exists at IGCSE level too, under other names. Buying a piece of assessed work puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding, and the consequence falls on the child rather than the seller. We state this plainly on every page because the search results a worried parent sees in week six of eight do not, and because a parent under deadline pressure is exactly who those operators are written for.

sections.heading: Starting an eight-week block this week
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Send the subject, the board, the tier and the date of the next assessment. We match one specialist in that subject on that board. You take a free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on whatever the student is currently stuck on, and you decide afterwards. If the match is wrong, we rematch once at no charge.

Week one of the block is a diagnostic paper under timed conditions before any teaching happens, because a plan built on a report card is a plan built on an average. The paper shows which topics and which question types are costing marks, and the eight-week plan is written from that. Week four is a checkpoint and week eight is the end, with no quiet renewal.

On availability, we tell you the truth rather than filling the slot. Some combinations are thin in the exam term, particularly Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, and anything needing a 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time slot in the four weeks before a series. If the first specialist opening is a week away, we say so and we say the date. If your tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we tell you before you book.

During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar timing as a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, in Production City or anywhere else in the UAE, is send a tutor to your door. That service runs in India only, and an eight-week block is precisely the case where the journey would cost you the hours you are buying.

process.title: Send the board, not just the subject
process.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams. Tell us the subject, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier and the next assessment date, and the match becomes specific rather than approximate. Your school's exams officer can confirm all four in one email, and it is worth having in writing.

process.title: One matched specialist on that board
process.description: You get one named tutor who teaches that subject on that board at that tier, with their background and where they are based. Not a shortlist of five profiles to compare, because in the weeks before a series a week spent choosing is a week not spent on papers.

process.title: Diagnostic paper before the plan
process.description: The free trial is a teaching hour. The first paid session is a timed past paper under exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme. The eight-week plan is written from what that paper shows, which is routinely different from what the school report implied.

process.title: Two sessions a week, fixed slot, fixed end
process.description: One content session and one timed-paper session each week, at times that survive the Production City bus timetable, usually from 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time. The block has a written finish date so it concludes rather than drifts, and nothing renews unless you ask.

process.title: Week four checkpoint
process.description: Halfway through, we look at the error log and decide whether the plan still holds. If the diagnostic underestimated a gap, the remaining sessions change shape. If the student has moved faster than expected, the back half shifts to paper volume rather than content.

whyPoints.title: The calendar drives the plan
whyPoints.description: We ask for the series and the next assessment date before anything else, because eight weeks before a mock and eight weeks before a terminal paper call for different work. No competitor page in our research names a single exam series, deadline or results date, which is why their advice cannot be timed.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific teaching
whyPoints.description: A tutor matched to Cambridge 0625 is not interchangeable with one who teaches Pearson 4PH1. Tiering, grading scale, practical routes and modular options all differ. We match on board and tier as well as subject, and we ask for the syllabus code at the first conversation.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with an end date
whyPoints.description: An eight-week block is sixteen hours with a written finish. That is easier to judge, easier to budget and easier to stop than an open-ended monthly arrangement. Market monthly packages run from AED 799 for eight online sessions; a defined block is usually the better purchase.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the competitor or rate table it came from and the month it was read. Three of the six main competitor pages in our research publish no price at all and two quote USD, which is not a currency UAE families transact in.

whyPoints.title: Hours protected, not spent on the road
whyPoints.description: In a short block the scarce resource is time. Online delivery means every booked hour is a taught hour and the sequence survives a late bus or a closed slip road. We do not offer UAE home visits, and in an exam block that is a feature rather than a limitation.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises
whyPoints.description: We will not tell you sixteen hours produces a grade 7. Technique, pacing and command-term reading improve reliably in a short block, and those hold most of the recoverable marks. Content a student never learned across two years does not compress into eight weeks, and saying so is the only honest position.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough time to change my child's IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which subject and which marks are missing. Technique-led components move fast: Mathematics method marks, English directed writing structure, and the evaluation bands in Economics and Business Studies all respond within a few sessions because they are governed by a mark scheme a student can learn to read. Content gaps move slowly, and two years of unlearned biology terminology will not compress into sixteen hours. We find out which it is with a timed diagnostic paper in week one rather than guessing from a report card, and we tell you honestly what the block can and cannot reach.

faqs.question: Does my Production City child sit the June or the November series?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge IGCSE, the June series, with November available as the resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a UAE candidate. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, May/June or November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk, so ask your exams officer which zone your school sits in and read that specific timetable rather than a general one.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. Independent home tutors do work in this area, with Dubai market rates for in-home one-to-one running roughly AED 180-350 an hour. In an eight-week exam block, the arithmetic argues against the visit: a tutor travelling to IMPZ between five and seven faces thirty to forty minutes each way, that time is priced into your rate, and a late bus or a closed road turns a session into a cancellation that breaks the sequence.

faqs.question: What will an eight-week block cost us in total?
faqs.answer: Price it as sixteen hours rather than per session. At the Dubai market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, the block runs AED 2,400 to AED 4,800. A specialist at AED 200-450 takes it to AED 3,200 to AED 7,200. In-home equivalents sit higher because travel is in the rate. Those figures come from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than our price list. We begin with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the goal needs.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject, in writing. In a school running both, it genuinely differs by subject, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without any error. It matters because the papers differ: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is tiered Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C, while Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher on a 9-1 scale. Revising from the wrong board's past papers is practice for an exam nobody is sitting.

faqs.question: My child's results were disappointing in August. Should they resit in November?
faqs.answer: Only after a paper-level breakdown, not a grade-level one. Ask the school for the component marks, then identify which one or two papers actually moved the overall grade and whether the recoverable marks sit in technique or in content. Technique is worth a resit; two missing years of content usually is not. Entry deadlines sit months before the series and are handled by the exams officer, so confirm the deadline before planning anything. For Pearson candidates the January results date matters too: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Can online tuition prepare a student for the IGCSE practical papers?
faqs.answer: For the examined parts, yes. What a practical or alternative-to-practical paper assesses is experimental design, variable control, tabulating and processing results, calculating gradients, identifying error sources and evaluating a method. All of that is paper work and all of it is teachable over video, usually faster than in a lab because nothing has to be set up. What online tuition cannot replace is the hours a student spends physically handling apparatus, which remains the school's responsibility. Check with the exams officer which practical route your child is entered for, because that changes what to prioritise.

faqs.question: What time can sessions start for a Year 11 student living in IMPZ?
faqs.answer: Realistically from about 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time. There is no secondary campus inside Dubai Production City, so students bus to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Jebel Ali and are typically home between four and half past, needing food and a break before anything useful happens. Families in Dubai South and Emaar South often need 6pm or later. Because the session is online it starts at the booked minute rather than when a tutor arrives, which is what makes a tight evening workable twice a week for eight weeks.

faqs.question: For MoE equivalency, is it five or six accredited IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Five. Gulf Today reported in July 2026 that students on the British track must present five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor ranking for these queries states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before relying on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Does Pearson's modular option change how we should plan revision?
faqs.answer: Considerably. Where a subject is offered modularly, units can be sat across different sessions rather than in one terminal run, which means revision is sequenced unit by unit rather than built to a single peak. That is a genuine advantage for a student who struggles to hold a full syllabus in view, and a disadvantage for one who needs the pressure of a single deadline to work. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and revises them, so plan against the live official timetable PDF and confirm the entry pattern with your exams officer.

faqs.question: Are private tutors in Dubai required to hold a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Across the Jebel Ali corridor, which IGCSE papers cost the most marks?
faqs.answer: In our experience across the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor, the recurring four are Physics electricity, Chemistry moles and stoichiometry, Mathematics algebraic manipulation with bounds, and the evaluation bands in Business Studies. Three of those four are technique problems rather than knowledge problems, which is why they respond well to a short block. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a fifth, taken by a small cohort as a bridge to AS Level, and it is the subject where local specialist tutors are genuinely scarce because the number of students sitting it in any one community is small.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with school-set coursework or projects?
faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the skills the work assesses, explain what the criteria actually reward, question the approach before weeks are wasted on it, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor will not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The line is authorship, and it is not negotiable. Operators in this same search sell finished assessed work; buying it exposes the student to a malpractice finding and the consequence falls on the child. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, which are copyright material.

faqs.question: Can we pause the block during half-term or a family trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in an eight-week block it is better to shift a session than to skip it, because each lesson builds on the error log from the previous one. Because the sessions are online they also follow the laptop, so a week in another time zone usually means a different clock time rather than a cancellation. During Ramadan, moving to post-Iftar slots is a normal request and the tutor and slot are held. Tell us the dates when the block is planned and the schedule is built around them from the start.

faqs.question: What if you have no tutor free in my child's subject before the series?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date. In the four weeks before a series, 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time slots are the first to go, and some combinations are thin year-round: Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, and board-specific modular units. Rather than putting a generalist in front of your child we say when the specialist is actually available, which is sometimes more than a week away. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we tell you that before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting weekly tuition in Year 10 instead of waiting?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, and it is usually cheaper overall. One session a week through Year 10 and Year 11 tracks the school's own scheme of work, so topics are consolidated while they are still being taught rather than reconstructed eighteen months later. That pattern prevents the eight-week emergency rather than treating it. The eight-week block exists because families often arrive after the mock, and it works, but it costs more per mark recovered than two years of steady weekly work on a fixed slot would have.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.closingHeading: Start from the date, then decide
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-producti.closingBody: Find out the series, the board and the tier, and get them in writing from the exams officer. Then count backwards: entry deadline, practical window, mock, paper. Whatever number of weeks is left is the real brief, and it tells you whether this is a weekly arrangement through Year 10 or a sixteen-hour block with a diagnostic paper in week one. Either way, the hours are the thing to protect, which is why Production City lessons run online on Gulf Standard Time rather than behind a windscreen on Al Khail Road. Book a free trial lesson and start with one honest hour of teaching.

intro.heading: What this term actually has to achieve
paragraphs: Work backwards from the series rather than forwards from today. A Year 11 student entered for the June series has a fixed number of weeks left, and those weeks have different jobs. Autumn term is for diagnosis and for building whatever is structurally missing, because that is the only period with enough runway. The mock window is for evidence. Spring term is for technique and timed papers. The final six to eight weeks are for consolidation under exam conditions, and nothing structural can be started there.

The commonest error in Dubai Silicon Oasis households is not hiring too little. It is hiring at the wrong point and then asking the wrong thing of the hours. A family that books a tutor in March and expects algebraic fluency to be built from scratch by May is asking for something the calendar does not allow, however good the tutor and however high the rate. The same family booking in September would have got it comfortably.

The Dubai academic year gives you four natural blocks: autumn term to the half-term break, the stretch from half-term to the winter break, the spring term, and the run to the series. Between them sit the breaks, which are the only periods with no school-run constraint and no homework competing for the evening. Structural catching up belongs in the breaks. Term time is for maintenance and technique.

The series themselves are fixed and worth getting right, because a surprising number of pages give UAE parents the wrong ones. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai school sits it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City and the surrounding communities, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For calendar-driven work that format has a specific advantage: a session can be moved in a message when a mock week shifts or a deadline lands early, which a visiting arrangement cannot absorb nearly as easily.

The rest of this page is the calendar in detail. What each block is for. What eight weeks genuinely achieves. How entry deadlines sit relative to the papers. When November becomes the right answer rather than a failure. And how Ramadan and the breaks change the pattern, which is the part nobody writes down.

One framing worth holding before any of the detail. A calendar plan is not a longer plan; it is often a shorter one placed better. Families who read the year properly frequently buy fewer total hours than those who panic in March, because the autumn block does the structural work cheaply and the final weeks are then free to do what they are actually good at. The saving comes from the sequencing rather than from any rate negotiation.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.subjectsIntro: This grid is organised by how long each subject takes to move, because that is the calendar question. Some respond inside eight weeks and some do not, and buying the slow ones late is the commonest disappointment in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Procedural topics such as reverse percentages and similar shapes move in two or three sessions at any point in the year. Algebraic fluency does not: it is built by repetition over terms, which means a March start cannot deliver it before a June series.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit handling and working layout respond quickly and can be fixed in the final eight weeks. Six-mark written explanations take longer, because naming a mechanism rather than describing an effect is a habit, so that work belongs in autumn or earlier.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most calendar-friendly science. Moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are finite procedures that genuinely respond inside a short block, so a late start in chemistry is less damaging than a late start in physics or English.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content recall can be rebuilt relatively quickly with structured revision, but the precision of written answers takes longer. A student who loses marks for vague phrasing needs marked practice across a term rather than a sprint.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing technique responds inside six to eight weeks, because answering the specified audience and form is a readable rule. Reading-response depth takes longer, so a spring-only plan will usually lift one half of the paper and not the other.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: The slowest subject to move in the entire IGCSE set. Quotation selection and close analysis require repeated marked practice over months, so a Literature plan started in spring of Year 11 is the clearest example of asking the calendar for something it cannot give.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Among the fastest to respond, because data-response technique and stating an explicit judgement in evaluation questions are both teachable rules. A short block in the final term is a reasonable purchase in these subjects in a way it is not in Literature.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: The theory paper responds to structured revision inside eight weeks for most students, because the content is finite and the question styles repeat. Practical coding confidence takes longer and is better addressed in Year 10.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Hardest to plan late, because a gap may sit in any of three subjects and the content is compressed. A student behind in a combined entry needs the autumn term, not the spring, and a tutor comfortable across all three rather than a specialist in one.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Support works from the school's approved material, since different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission, which also limits how much an outside plan can compress.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year in four blocks
paragraphs: The year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a half-term break in autumn, a winter break around the turn of the year, a spring break and a long summer. That gives four working blocks separated by three pauses, and each has a different capacity. Treating the year as one continuous subscription wastes the blocks that could do most and overloads the ones that can do least.

Block one, September to the autumn half-term, is diagnosis and foundation. This is when a weakness can still be addressed at its root, because there is runway in front of it. Block two, half-term to the winter break, is consolidation plus the mock window at many schools. Block three, the spring term, is technique and timed practice. Block four, the final six to eight weeks, is consolidation under exam conditions only.

The pauses matter as much as the blocks. Breaks are the only periods with no school-run constraint and no homework competing for the evening, which makes them the natural home for anything that needs an uninterrupted stretch: a full past paper, a missed unit, a topic that needs three hours rather than one. A family that uses one week of the spring break well often reduces its term-time booking afterwards.

Written out like this the implication is obvious and almost nobody follows it. The money should be weighted towards the first block and the breaks, and lightest in the final block, where only technique is reachable. Most families do the reverse, because urgency arrives in block four and nothing feels urgent in block one. The table below is the version worth keeping in front of you.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, series and the UAE position
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only. That single fact invalidates a great deal of advice circulating about UAE entry deadlines, because a February exam window implies an entry deadline in the previous autumn that simply does not apply here.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth reading before trusting any date printed on a tutoring website, this one included. Your school's exams officer holds the zone and the correct timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series and revises them, which is why no page should be the source of truth for a date.

What a family can plan around is the shape rather than the dates. Entries close months before the papers, which means the subject list and the tier are fixed long before anyone feels urgent about them. Mocks sit a term earlier. Results arrive in August for a June series and in January for a November one. Those four facts are enough to build a calendar, and they do not change between years.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can and cannot repair
paragraphs: This is the question most families are really asking when they call in March, and it deserves a straight answer rather than encouragement. Eight weeks of focused weekly work with marked practice reliably moves exam technique: command-word reading, working layout, timing, question selection, and the specific procedural topics that are finite sets of steps. Those are real marks and they are often worth a grade boundary on their own.

What eight weeks does not do is build fluency. Algebraic manipulation in mathematics, precision of written explanation in biology and physics, and close analysis in English Literature are all habits accumulated through repetition. A student who cannot rearrange a formula without hesitation in March will still hesitate in May, because the only thing that fixes it is doing it several hundred times across months. Saying otherwise sells hours and disappoints families.

So an eight-week plan should be built on the honest list. Pick the procedural gaps that are closable, the technique faults that respond, and the topics the student has simply never revised properly. Leave the structural weaknesses out of the plan explicitly, and tell the student they are being left out, because a plan that quietly includes an impossible goal produces the sense of failure rather than the sense of progress.

The week-by-week shape below is the one that works most often. It alternates a technique focus with a content focus, puts a full timed paper at the midpoint and another near the end, and keeps the last week light because a student revising at full intensity in the final days arrives at the paper depleted. It is deliberately unambitious, which is why it tends to deliver.

sections.heading: Mock season is the cheapest diagnostic in the year
paragraphs: Mock papers are marked by the school at no cost to you and contain more usable information than any paid assessment. Most families read the grade, feel something about it, and file the paper. The grade is the least informative part. The useful part is the distribution of lost marks: which question types, which topics, and which of them were lost to not knowing versus not finishing versus misreading.

The exercise takes under an hour and needs no subject expertise. Go through the marked paper and sort every lost mark into four buckets: did not know it, knew it but ran out of time, misread what was asked, or knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks. Count the buckets. Almost every student produces a strongly skewed result, and the largest bucket tells you what the next block should be about.

A heavy did-not-know bucket means content revision, which is the cheapest kind of help and can often be supervised rather than taught. A heavy ran-out-of-time bucket means timing and question selection, which is pure technique and moves fast. A heavy misread bucket means command words, which is close to a single session. And a heavy knew-it-but-did-not-earn-it bucket means answer structure, which is the most teachable thing on the list.

This is also the point at which a plan should be cut rather than extended. A subject that has stabilised since autumn does not need the remaining term of weekly lessons, and a family that reviews at the mock window and cancels one booking saves more than any discount will ever provide. Nobody has an incentive to prompt that review except you, which is why it belongs in a page like this one.

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and the shape of the Dubai year
paragraphs: Ramadan changes the day rather than removing it. School hours shorten, which makes the afternoon easier for tuition than usual, while the late afternoon becomes the worst part of the day for a fasting student's concentration and the hour after Iftar among the best. Most Silicon Oasis families move the slot to a post-Iftar time and keep the same tutor, which is a message to arrange with an online booking and a renegotiation with a visiting one.

Arrange the change before the month begins rather than week by week. Evening slots fill quickly once everybody tries to move at once, and a family that waits until the first week finds the convenient hours gone across the whole platform. The same applies to the weeks immediately after Ramadan, when schools often compress assessments into a short window and demand for sessions rises sharply.

The breaks deserve a plan of their own. Half-term is one week, which is enough for one named topic rather than general revision. The winter break is long enough to recover a missed unit and attempt full papers. The spring break sits immediately before the final run and is the single best-placed week in the year for an intensive, because the student is close enough to the papers to take it seriously and far enough out for it to matter.

The summer is the one most families waste and the one that could do most. For a student entering Year 11, four or five sessions across the summer aimed at the structural weakness identified in Year 10 arrives at September already repaired, which changes what the autumn block can be used for. It is also the cheapest time to buy, because demand in the after-school window is at its lowest.

sections.heading: When November is the right answer, not a failure
paragraphs: A November entry is often described to families as a last resort, and that framing causes real harm. It is simply the other series, and for some students it is the better one. A student who was unwell during the June papers, or who arrived mid-year from another system, or who was entered at the wrong tier, is not failing by sitting in November. They are using a route the board provides.

The timing makes it workable. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. January results are early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations, which means a November grade can still open the door that the June grade closed. That is a materially different situation from waiting a full year.

Planning for it changes the budget. Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by a tutor, so the reserve has to exist before the whole budget goes into term-time lessons. Preparation is a focused block rather than a repeat of the year: the student has already met the content, so the work is technique, the specific topics that failed, and a different approach to timing. Eight to ten weeks is a realistic shape.

The decision point comes quickly after August results, and a remark has its own short deadline. So the honest advice is to decide in advance what threshold would trigger a November entry, and to hold both the reserve and the intention before results day. Families who make that decision in advance act calmly; families who make it in the third week of August act expensively.

sections.heading: The calendar differs by board, so confirm the code
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE in Dubai and their calendars are not identical. Cambridge uses four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry, splits many subjects into Core and Extended routes, and runs June and November series with centres allocated to zones. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1, sets Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics, and runs May and June plus November.

The differences that affect a plan are concrete. A modular structure on some Pearson qualifications changes when a paper can be sat and how a resit works. Cambridge's alternative-to-practical written paper on several science syllabuses changes what practical preparation should look like. And the Core or Extended entry on Cambridge subjects caps the grade available, with the review window falling in Year 10, which is a calendar fact as much as an academic one.

Finding out costs one message. Ask the school, in writing, for the board and the code for each subject, plus the tier where Cambridge applies. Many Dubai schools enter some subjects with one board and some with the other, so the reply must be subject by subject rather than general. Quote the codes when you ask for a tutor, because a plan built on the wrong paper structure will be a competent plan aimed at the wrong examination.

One more reason to get this right early. The autumn block is the only one with runway, and it is wasted if the first three weeks are spent discovering which board and tier the student is on. Families who establish the codes in the first week of September get a full structural block; families who establish them in October get a shorter one, and the difference lands in June.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: Send four things: the syllabus codes and tiers, which series your child is entered for, the school's mock dates, and the hour your child is realistically at a desk. Those four facts let us tell you what this term can achieve before anybody has paid for anything. We then match a tutor to the code and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note setting out the closable gaps, the structural ones, and which block of the year each belongs in. If you are calling in March and the main weakness is algebraic fluency, the note will say that eight weeks cannot deliver it and will propose what eight weeks can deliver instead. That is a less attractive message than the alternative and it is the one that produces a result.

The limits, stated plainly. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no board or regulator approval, so nobody here is KHDA approved or Cambridge accredited. We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; we reference them and link to the official source.

And we publish no dates as authority. Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page is attributed and backward-looking, and the forward-looking statements are deliberately month-only, because a series named by month stays true and a series named by month and year is wrong a year later with nobody having touched the page. Take your actual dates from the school's exams officer or the board's live timetable.

process.title: Establish the codes and the series in week one
process.description: Ask the school in writing for the board, the code and the tier for each subject, and which series your child is entered for. The autumn block is the only one with runway, and three weeks of it spent finding this out is three weeks that cannot be recovered in June.

process.title: Get the school's mock dates
process.description: Mocks are the free diagnostic that the whole calendar pivots on, and schools in this corridor run them at different points. Knowing the date means the autumn block can be aimed at arriving at the mock ready rather than at surviving the current unit.

process.title: Sort the mock paper into four buckets
process.description: Did not know it, ran out of time, misread the question, or knew it and did not earn the marks. Counting those four tells you what the next block is for and needs no subject knowledge. It is the single highest-value hour a parent can spend.

process.title: Weight the spend early and in the breaks
process.description: The autumn block and the spring break can do things the final eight weeks cannot. Most families spend the reverse way because urgency arrives late. Shifting even one booking from April to September changes what is achievable without changing the total.

process.title: Decide the November threshold in advance
process.description: Agree with the school what grade would trigger a November entry, and hold a reserve for entry fees from the start. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the route is genuinely useful, and deciding in advance makes August calm rather than expensive.

whyPoints.title: The year is planned in blocks, not sold as a subscription
whyPoints.description: Autumn has runway, the breaks have uninterrupted time, the spring term suits technique, and the final eight weeks can only consolidate. A plan that respects that distribution achieves more from the same number of hours than one that treats every week as equivalent.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer about eight weeks
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks moves command words, timing, working layout and finite procedural topics. It does not build algebraic fluency or close analysis in English Literature. Saying so loses us hours and is the only version of this advice that produces a result in June.

whyPoints.title: The UAE series stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge runs June and November here, and the February and March series is India-only, which invalidates a lot of circulating advice about entry deadlines. Every date on this page is attributed and backward-looking, and forward-looking series are named by month only.

faqs.question: When in the year should a Dubai Silicon Oasis family start IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: September, if the weakness is structural, because the autumn block is the only period in Year 11 with enough runway to build fluency. Procedural gaps and technique faults can be addressed later and still move marks. The distribution most families use is the reverse: nothing in the autumn, everything in the spring. Shifting even one booking from April to September changes what is achievable without changing the total amount spent.

faqs.question: Can eight weeks of tutoring fix my child's IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong. Eight weeks of focused weekly work with marked practice reliably moves command-word reading, working layout, timing, question selection and the finite procedural topics, and those are often worth a grade boundary. It does not build algebraic fluency, precision of written explanation or close analysis in English Literature, because those are habits accumulated over months. A good plan states which of your gaps are in which category.

faqs.question: Which series does a Dubai Silicon Oasis IGCSE candidate sit, and when?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series or the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai student sits it, and any advice built on a February entry deadline is imported from another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so take the actual timetable from your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: How should we use my child's mock results?
faqs.answer: Sort every lost mark into four buckets: did not know it, knew it but ran out of time, misread what was asked, or knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks. Count them. Almost every student produces a skewed result, and the largest bucket tells you what the next block should be for. It takes under an hour, needs no subject knowledge, and is more informative than any paid assessment.

faqs.question: Is a November IGCSE resit a bad outcome?
faqs.answer: No, it is simply the other series, and for some students it is the better one. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Preparation is a focused eight to ten week block rather than a repeat of the year, because the content has already been met and the gap is narrower.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Cedre Villas or Silicon Gardens?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For calendar-driven work the online format has a specific advantage: when a mock week moves or a coursework deadline lands earlier than expected, a session can be rescheduled in a message. A visiting arrangement cannot absorb that nearly as easily, and across a term the flexibility is worth more than the convenience of someone at the door.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change an IGCSE revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, which makes the afternoon easier than usual, while the late afternoon becomes the hardest part of the day for a fasting student's concentration and the hour after Iftar among the best. Most families move the slot to a post-Iftar time and keep the same tutor. Arrange the change before the month begins, because evening slots fill quickly once everybody tries to move at once, and demand stays high in the compressed assessment weeks afterwards.

faqs.question: Which break is the best one to buy an intensive in?
faqs.answer: The spring break, because it sits immediately before the final run: the student is close enough to the papers to take it seriously and far enough out for the work to matter. Half-term is one week and suits one named topic rather than general revision. The winter break is long enough to recover a missed unit and attempt full papers. The summer before Year 11 is the most under-used block of all and the cheapest to buy.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entry deadlines fall for a UAE candidate?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers rather than weeks, and they are administered by your school's exams officer rather than by the family directly. What matters practically is that the subject list and the tier are fixed long before anyone feels urgent about them, so a Core to Extended review has to happen in Year 10 or early Year 11. Ask the exams officer for the actual dates; boards revise provisional timetables, so no tutoring page should be your source.

faqs.question: Which subjects should not be left until the spring term?
faqs.answer: English Literature first, because quotation selection and close analysis need repeated marked practice over months. Then anything in mathematics that depends on algebraic fluency, and the precision of written explanation in biology and physics. By contrast, chemistry's moles calculations and qualitative analysis tables, economics data-response technique and computer science theory all respond reasonably to a short late block, so a spring start in those is defensible.

faqs.question: Should we keep paying for a subject that has improved since autumn?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and nobody has an incentive to tell you so. The mock window is the natural review point: if a subject has stabilised, cancelling that booking saves more than any discount a provider will offer, and the money can be redirected to whatever the mock has newly exposed. A plan that looks identical in the third term to the first means nobody has read the evidence, which is a failure of review rather than of teaching.

faqs.question: Do we need to know the syllabus code before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes one message to the school. Cambridge uses codes such as 0580, 0620 and 0625 with Core and Extended routes; Pearson uses forms like 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics. Many Dubai schools split boards across subjects, so ask subject by subject. A plan built on the wrong paper structure is a competent plan aimed at the wrong examination, and it looks fine until the mock.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic timetable reduce IGCSE study time?
faqs.answer: It occupies school timetable space, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. That reduces the hours available for IGCSE content within the school day, which is worth factoring in when judging how much a term can realistically cover.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Dubai Silicon Oasis need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Since it costs nothing, ask directly.

faqs.question: What will the first month of a calendar-based plan produce?
faqs.answer: A written statement of which gaps are closable in the time available and which are not, which is the most valuable thing you can hold in March and the thing nobody supplies. Plus one measurable technique change, usually in timing or working layout. No grade prediction, because nobody can honestly give one, and a provider that opens with a predicted grade has told you how it sells rather than how it plans.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.closingBody: The difference between a tuition budget that works and one that disappoints is usually not the tutor or the rate. It is whether the hours were bought in a block of the year that could do the job asked of them. So send the syllabus codes, the series, the school's mock dates and the hour your child is genuinely free. The free trial lesson costs nothing, runs as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, and the written note that follows will say plainly which gaps this term can close and which needed September.

Each is matched to a specific board and tier, because a 0580 Extended candidate and a 4MA1 Higher candidate are not sitting the same paper.

intro.heading: Does the answer change between Dubai South and the next community along?
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai South comparing tutoring options almost always ends up comparing neighbourhoods. The Al Furjan listings look busier. Dubai Investments Park has the schools. Jebel Ali has the older, more established provision. The implied question is whether a family on the wrong side of a junction gets a worse tutor. For in-home tuition the answer is yes, measurably, because the pool shrinks with every kilometre of evening traffic a tutor has to absorb. For online tuition the answer is no, and the comparison collapses entirely, which is the single most useful thing on this page.

The practical difference between these communities is the school run, not the tutor market. Green Community children can be home by 15:45 because the school is minutes away. Dubai South and Emaar South households are usually home between 16:00 and 16:30 after a run into Dubai Investments Park. Dubai Production City families driving to Motor City or Sports City are later again, closer to 17:00. Those thirty-minute differences decide when a session can start. They do not decide who can teach it, once the lesson is delivered over video.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and this page will not imply otherwise. What a Dubai South family gets instead is a specialist matched to the board, the tier and the paper, teaching live one-to-one with the student's own marked script on screen. For an IGCSE candidate that specificity matters more than most parents expect, because IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 International GCSE Mathematics are different syllabuses with different papers, different tiering and different formula sheets.

So the comparison on this page runs on four axes. First, the neighbourhoods themselves: which schools each feeds, what time the day ends, when a session realistically fits. Second, the two boards: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject, with the syllabus codes a parent can check against their child's timetable. Third, the tiers: Core against Extended for Cambridge, Foundation against Higher for Edexcel, and the grade ceiling each imposes. Fourth, the money: what Dubai providers publish, cheapest band first, with the source of every figure named.

One regulatory note to set expectations. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes annual school inspection ratings, which are worth reading before any admissions conversation in this cluster. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership, and runs no UAE centre. The credential that genuinely exists for an individual tutor is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and it is reasonable to ask any tutor you hire to show it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South sits between British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE at 16 and IB continuum schools that run the Middle Years Programme to the same age. Families here often have children in both, which is why all three stages below get asked about.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, and the stage where most of the damage that shows up in Year 11 is actually done. Algebraic fluency, scientific notation, structured written explanation and reading speed are the four things a Year 9 student either has or spends Year 10 acquiring under pressure. Nothing is externally examined, which is why weaknesses go unnoticed until the first IGCSE mock paper returns a grade nobody expected.
programmes.countryNote: In this corner of Dubai, Key Stage 3 is also when option choices start narrowing. Whether a school enters a student for Cambridge or Edexcel, and whether triple or double award science is on offer, is set at the school level and varies between the Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools. A Year 9 parent comparing communities should compare those two facts rather than the building.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, externally examined at the end. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel offers Foundation and Higher tiering in mathematics. Grading is 9 to 1 on Edexcel and on reformed Cambridge subjects, with A*-G still in use on some. The tier a student is entered for caps the grade available, which makes the entry decision as consequential as the revision.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE candidates in Dubai South sit the June series, with November available as a resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not a UAE option, which is worth knowing because at least one widely read page has told UAE parents otherwise. Entry deadlines are set by the school as the examination centre, and they fall months before the papers.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB alternative to IGCSE for the same age group, marked on four criteria per subject from A to D on a 0-8 scale and converted to a 1-7 grade. There are no public examinations in most schools, and the Personal Project in the final year carries the heaviest time load. Students strong on content and weak on process lose marks in the inquiry and reflection criteria rather than in knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Dubai South run the Middle Years Programme rather than IGCSE, which means two children in neighbouring villas can be in the same year group facing completely different assessment. A family moving between the two systems mid-secondary needs gap mapping rather than general tutoring, because the content overlaps while the assessment format does not.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Dubai South families request most, with the syllabus codes and the specific place marks are lost. Codes are worth checking against your child's own timetable, since the board varies by school in this cluster.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended carries the full 9-1 range; Core caps lower, which makes the entry tier a grade decision. Paper 2 and Paper 4 are the Extended papers and both permit a calculator. Marks go on algebraic manipulation, on bearings and vectors, and on failing to show method where a question says so. The formula list is given, and most candidates have never read it before the examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, both calculator-permitted, with Higher tiering required for the top grades. Pearson's style differs from Cambridge: more multi-step contextual questions and a heavier emphasis on ratio and proportional reasoning. Students moving school mid-course between boards most often stumble on question phrasing rather than on content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Paper 4 is the Extended theory paper and Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, which asks about apparatus, variables and sources of error rather than recall. Candidates lose marks on unit prefixes, on describing an experiment without naming the controlled variable, and on graph questions where the gradient has to be read and interpreted rather than calculated.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables account for most of the spread. The ionic equation questions are routinely attempted without balancing charge, which scores nothing. Organic chemistry at this level is nomenclature and reaction type rather than mechanism, which makes it one of the most recoverable topics in the syllabus in a short block of sessions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: High recall volume, so the marks come from structured note-making and from command-term discipline. Describe, explain and suggest demand different answers, and writing the longest possible response to a two-mark question wastes examination time. The genetics and transport topics reward diagram work; the ecology topics reward precise terminology.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry the weight, and both are marked on structure as much as on expression. The commonest loss is answering in the wrong register for the stated audience and purpose. Reading comprehension marks go on the summary question, where candidates copy phrasing from the passage instead of condensing it in their own words.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study based, with marks awarded for applying a concept to the specific business in the stimulus rather than defining it. Analysis and evaluation command words carry the highest tariff and are where most candidates stop short. Calculation questions on break-even, cash flow and ratios are reliably available marks and reliably under-practised.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, and an unlabelled axis costs the mark regardless of the prose. The data-response paper rewards reading the figures before writing, which candidates under time pressure routinely skip. Elasticity calculations and the distinction between a movement along a curve and a shift of it account for a large share of lost marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 is theory, including data representation and hardware, and Paper 2 is algorithms and programming expressed in pseudocode. Candidates who have only coded in one language lose marks on pseudocode conventions they never practised. Trace tables are a reliable source of marks and are almost never drilled.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai schools because Arabic is mandatory under KHDA rules. Assessment covers listening, reading, writing and speaking. The writing component rewards a small bank of accurately drilled structures over a wide but shaky vocabulary, which makes it one of the most improvable components in a short block.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Offered by some schools as a bridge towards A Level or the IB Diploma, covering calculus, trigonometry and vectors beyond 0580. Students take it alongside the main mathematics syllabus, and the overlap is smaller than they expect. It is a genuine advantage for a student heading into Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: The alternative to three separate sciences, with a reduced content load and a different paper structure. Students entered for a combined route sometimes assume the grade ceiling is lower; it is the content coverage that differs. Families should confirm which route the school has entered their child for before planning any science tutoring, because the papers are not interchangeable.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-south.regionsIntro: The communities compared on this page. Online delivery means the tutor pool is the same in all of them; what differs is when a session can start.

regions.name: Dubai South
regions.note: The district around Al Maktoum International and the Expo site, including Residential District and The Pulse. Most school runs end in Dubai Investments Park, putting the household home between 16:00 and 16:30 and the earliest workable weekday slot at about 16:30.

regions.name: Emaar South
regions.note: Villas and townhouses around the golf course inside Dubai South, with a younger age profile than the apartment communities north of it. Primary and lower-secondary demand dominates here, which concentrates bookings in the 16:30 to 18:00 window.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: North on the Sheikh Zayed side with its own metro station and its own school provision. Secondary students commonly travel to Discovery Gardens or Dubai Investments Park, arriving home between 15:45 and 16:30 depending on the route.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: The school cluster for this whole corner of the emirate, with British, IB continuum, Indian and SABIS provision close together. Families living here have the shortest run in the comparison and the widest choice of early slots.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: The established residential zone west of the cluster, with long-standing British and Indian-curriculum schools. IGCSE candidates in Years 10 and 11 are the bulk of the tutoring demand, followed by transition work into A Level or the Diploma.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Dense apartment living with a cost-conscious parent population and strong interest in what each AED band actually buys. Sessions here cluster after 18:00, because working parents prefer to be home while a lesson runs.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-rise housing inside Dubai Investments Park, minutes from the schools. One of the few communities in this comparison where a 16:00 weekday session is genuinely workable during term time.

modes.title: Weekly subject tuition across a term
modes.description: One session a week in one subject, with work set between sessions and marked at the start of the next. For an IGCSE candidate this is the format that moves a tier decision, because it produces enough evidence over a term for a school to reconsider a Core entry. Most families in this cluster begin here and add a second subject only when the first is stable.

modes.description: Common in Year 11, where a student is weak across two linked subjects and the underlying cause is shared — usually algebra, or data handling, or the inability to read a graph. Running both subjects with one specialist who can see the common thread works better than two separate tutors treating two symptoms.

sections.heading: Dubai South against the next community along: the comparison, settled
paragraphs: Here is the comparison a parent in this cluster is actually making, laid out rather than implied. The four communities below differ in which schools they feed, how long the run takes and therefore when a session can start. They do not differ in which tutors are available, because once the lesson is delivered over live video the tutor's address stops being a variable. That is the whole argument, and it is worth stating before the table rather than after it.

What the table does show is a scheduling reality. A Green Community family can run a 16:00 session during term; a Dubai Production City family cannot, because the car is still on the road. An Emaar South family with a primary and a secondary child can run both in one evening online, which is physically impossible with a visiting tutor who can only be in one house at a time. These are the operational facts that decide whether a plan survives a term, and no competitor page in this market publishes them.

The second thing the comparison exposes is school variation. The Al Furjan and Jebel Ali schools are predominantly British-curriculum and run IGCSE; the Dubai Investments Park cluster mixes IB continuum, British and SABIS. That means two children of the same age in neighbouring communities may be sitting completely different assessment at 16. A parent comparing tutoring between neighbourhoods is often, without realising it, comparing two qualifications. Checking the syllabus code on the child's own timetable resolves it in thirty seconds.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Schools in this cluster use both boards, sometimes within the same building for different subjects. A tutor who does not know which one a student is entered for will set the wrong past papers, and the student will spend a term practising question styles they will not meet. The syllabus code on the school timetable settles it: 0580 is Cambridge Mathematics, 4MA1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 0625 is Cambridge Physics, 4PH1 is Pearson.

The differences are real but narrow. Cambridge tends to ask shorter, more compartmentalised questions and runs a Core and Extended tier across many subjects. Pearson tends towards longer multi-step contextual questions and uses Foundation and Higher tiering in mathematics. Cambridge sciences include a separate alternative-to-practical paper that asks about apparatus and error; Pearson handles practical skills differently. None of this changes what a student needs to understand; all of it changes what a student needs to practise.

Session dates differ too, which matters for planning. Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Neither board's UAE candidates sit a February or March series — that one is offered to India only. Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Check the zone with the school.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and the grade your child can actually reach
paragraphs: The tier decision is the most consequential thing that happens to an IGCSE candidate, and it is usually made by the school with limited discussion. A Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics caps the grade available; an Extended entry opens the full range but presents harder papers. The same logic applies to Foundation and Higher on Pearson. A student entered at the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, which means an entry decision made in Year 10 on the basis of a weak term can close a university route two years later.

The honest position is that both over-entry and under-entry cost marks. A student placed on Extended who cannot handle the algebra will score badly on papers designed for somebody else and may end up below where a confident Core performance would have landed them. A student placed on Core who was always capable of Extended loses grades they could have had. The decision should rest on evidence from timed papers at both tiers, not on an impression formed in class.

That is a practical use for a term of weekly tutoring in Year 10. Sitting a timed Extended paper under conditions, marked against the official scheme, produces the evidence a school needs to revisit an entry. It is also why the tier has to be established before any tutoring plan is written: setting Extended practice for a Core candidate wastes the term, and setting Core practice for an Extended candidate guarantees an unpleasant surprise in the examination hall.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in Dubai, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work up, because that is how a household comparing options actually reads a price list. The cheapest published online tuition in Dubai starts around AED 33-52 an hour on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik, typically delivered by university students or non-specialist tutors. Next up, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visits sit apart from that ladder rather than above it. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. The gap between an online qualified tutor at AED 150-300 and an in-home one at AED 180-500 is largely the driving. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the clearest illustration of what travel costs.

Where the money gets wasted, in order. First, buying hours at the cheap end for a specialist problem: a non-specialist cannot diagnose why a 0625 Paper 6 script is losing marks, so the hours teach nothing. Second, buying hours without a diagnosis, which turns a tutor into a weekly homework supervisor. Third, paying the travel premium for a lesson whose working material is a script and a mark scheme, both of which are more legible on a shared screen. Every figure above is attributed to the provider that published it; these are market bands, not IB Gram's rates, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an examination session at all, which is remarkable given that the session is the only fixed point a tutoring plan has. For a Dubai South IGCSE candidate there are two: the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge IGCSE runs June and November, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates.

Counting backwards is the useful exercise. The entry deadline sits months before the papers and is handled by the school as the examination centre, not by the family. Mock papers typically land a term earlier. Coursework or practical deadlines, where a subject has them, land earlier still. Results reach centres before students: for Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the published, checkable reference points.

The practical reading of the table below is that an eight-week tutoring block has to be placed relative to a mock, not relative to the examination. A student whose mock is six weeks away has a different plan from one whose mock has already returned a grade. And because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used, the one thing worth doing today is confirming the zone and the final timetable with the school rather than trusting any restated date.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for an IGCSE candidate in this cluster
paragraphs: The comparison is narrower at IGCSE than at Diploma level, because IGCSE specialists are more plentiful than Higher Level Diploma specialists. A Dubai South family hiring in-home for Mathematics 0580 has a reasonable local pool. The same family hiring in-home for Computer Science 0478 or Arabic 0544 at short notice does not, and will end up with a generalist. That is the shape of the trade: common subjects, either format works; less common subjects, only one format reaches a specialist.

On cost, the in-home premium is the travel. Bestimate's band starts at AED 180 for in-home against far lower online entry points, and the monthly packages make it starker: AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. On scheduling, a visiting tutor fits one session an evening while an online tutor fits several, which matters to any household with two children in secondary school.

What in-home genuinely delivers is presence for a younger child who will not settle in front of a screen, and the option for a parent to observe from the next room. For a Year 10 or 11 candidate working through marked past papers, the balance moves the other way: the lesson material is a script and a mark scheme side by side, which reads better shared on screen than passed across a table. IB Gram delivers to Dubai South online and does not offer home visits in the UAE; the table sets out what that means rather than glossing it.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in the UAE, and how to check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the route as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services, with a two working-day completion time and no fee.

Two things follow for a Dubai South parent. First, a tutor who tells you no permit is needed is wrong, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you as unverified. Second, a permit is a legal licence to tutor, not a quality credential. It says nothing about whether the holder has taught Cambridge 0620 to Extended tier before.

A separate point worth knowing if you are considering a school teacher privately. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the ADEK detail as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. The underlying principle is consistent across the UAE: your child's own class teacher is not the right private tutor, however convenient it looks.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: MoE equivalency for IGCSE students
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a school-leaving certificate for use in the UAE, and IGCSE families meet it later than they should. The British-track requirement is published and specific: five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that matters most, and that at least one ranking competitor page gets wrong, is what counts towards the five. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. A competitor page currently tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, excluding those two. A family planning subject entries around the wrong number may pay examination fees for a subject that was never needed, which is an expensive way to be misinformed.

For the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics via at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB there is no points threshold in any source this page can verify, so none is published here. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority directly. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it — any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.
