process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Before anything else, check the syllabus code on the school timetable. 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. A tutor given the wrong board sets the wrong past papers for a whole term. Thirty seconds on a timetable prevents it, and it is the one thing most parents in this cluster have not yet done.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's marks on it tells a specialist in five minutes what a conversation takes an hour to approximate. Where marks were lost is visible on the page. If no script exists, the first session makes one by setting a short timed section from the correct board and marking it against the official scheme.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One full session at no charge, with no card required, taught by the tutor who would take the term. It returns a written diagnosis naming the topics and the techniques losing marks, and a proposal for the first four sessions. If the match is wrong, we rematch rather than asking you to persevere with it.

process.title: Place the block relative to the mock, not the examination
process.description: The useful fixed point is the mock paper, because it is the next piece of real evidence. A student six weeks from a mock needs coverage; a student holding a returned mock needs targeted repair. Both plans end in a pre-series intensive, but they start in different places.

process.title: Run the cycle and review it each half term
process.description: Work set at the end of every session, marked at the start of the next. Each half term, compare progress against the school's own deadlines for coursework, mocks and entry confirmation. That is where a tier conversation gets reopened with evidence, which is the single highest-value outcome available in Year 10.

whyPoints.title: The neighbourhood stops mattering
whyPoints.description: Dubai South, Emaar South, Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Green Community draw from the same tutor pool once delivery is online. The only thing that still differs is what time a session can start, and that is a thirty-minute question rather than a quality one. Families comparing communities for tutoring are comparing something that no longer varies.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different syllabuses. A tutor matched to the board and tier sets the right past papers from the first session; a tutor matched only to maths spends a term on question styles the student will never sit. This is the commonest avoidable waste in IGCSE tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Tier evidence a school will take seriously
whyPoints.description: A timed Extended paper sat under conditions and marked against the official scheme is evidence. Class impressions are not. For a student placed on Core who is capable of more, producing that evidence in Year 10 is worth more than any amount of revision later, because the entry decision caps the grade before revision begins.

whyPoints.title: AED figures that can be checked
whyPoints.description: Every rate here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it. Three of the most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which no Dubai household transacts in. A number a parent cannot check is not worth printing.

whyPoints.title: The right exam series, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only. That distinction has been published incorrectly to UAE parents elsewhere, and a family who plans around the wrong series loses the plan. We say which series applies and point to the school for the zone timetable.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no UAE centre
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Regulators are explained on this page because the explanation is useful to a parent, not because the names lend us anything.

faqs.question: Will I get a better IGCSE tutor in Al Furjan than in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Not through an online service, because the tutor pool is the same in both. The difference between these communities is the school run: Al Furjan households are often home by 16:00 while Dubai South households are closer to 16:30, so the earliest workable session differs by about fifteen minutes. For in-home tuition the comparison does change, since a tutor's willingness to drive varies with distance and traffic. That is precisely the constraint online delivery removes, and it is why the neighbourhood question stops being a quality question.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board does my child's school in Dubai South use?
faqs.answer: It varies by school and sometimes by subject within one school, so the reliable answer is on your child's own timetable rather than in any directory. Look for the syllabus code: 0580 is Cambridge Mathematics, 4MA1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 0625 is Cambridge Physics, 4PH1 is Pearson. The British-curriculum schools around Al Furjan and Jebel Ali commonly use Cambridge, but there is no safe generalisation. Confirming the code takes thirty seconds and determines which past papers a tutor should be setting from the first session.

faqs.question: Can my child be moved from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the lever is evidence rather than argument. Schools reconsider an entry tier when a student sits a timed Extended paper under examination conditions and the marked script supports the move. Class performance alone rarely shifts a decision. The practical route is a term of weekly tutoring in Year 10 ending in a full timed paper marked against the official scheme, then taking that script to the subject lead. The decision matters because a Core entry caps the grade available however well a candidate performs on the day.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE exam session in February or March for UAE students?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. This matters because a family that plans a revision block towards a session their child cannot sit has lost the term. Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Confirm the zone with the school.

faqs.question: How much does a home tutor cost in Dubai compared with online?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Published monthly packages make the gap clearest: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Most of that difference is the driving being paid for, not better teaching. These are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to homes in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. Dubai South families are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked script and the official mark scheme shared on screen. We state this plainly rather than leaving it to be discovered, because a page that implies a car will arrive is misleading the family paying for it. Independent in-home tutors do operate in this part of Dubai if presence is the priority for you.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE processes it through its app, website and e-services with a two working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

faqs.question: Is six IGCSE subjects the right number for a Dubai South family to plan around?
faqs.answer: No. The sourced rule is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. The British track also requires either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no lower than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. At least one widely read competitor page tells UAE parents six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: My child is sitting papers in six weeks. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change. Six weeks is not enough time to cover a syllabus, and attempting it produces panic without marks. What works is a pre-series intensive: two or three sessions a week built entirely on timed questions, with no new content taught. The first session diagnoses from a marked script, the rest attack the specific topics and techniques that script shows as weak. Students routinely gain marks in this window from timing discipline, command-word reading and mark-scheme vocabulary alone, none of which requires new knowledge.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both of my children in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Different children usually need different specialists, because a Year 8 and a Year 11 candidate are at different points of different syllabuses. What online delivery does allow is two sessions in one evening, back to back, which a visiting tutor physically cannot provide. If both children need the same subject at adjacent levels, one specialist can take both, and the practical saving is in scheduling rather than in price. Each child still gets a one-to-one session with their own set work and their own written note afterwards.

faqs.question: What is the alternative to practical paper in Cambridge sciences?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 in Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 is the alternative to practical, and it examines experimental skills on paper rather than in a laboratory. Questions ask candidates to identify variables, read instruments, spot sources of error, suggest improvements and complete results tables. It is heavily under-practised because it does not feel like content revision, yet it carries real marks and the question types repeat across series. A handful of sessions working through past Paper 6 questions is one of the most efficient mark gains available at IGCSE.

faqs.question: Is Arabic compulsory in Dubai private schools at IGCSE level?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, under KHDA's requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups. For an IGCSE candidate, Cambridge 0544 Arabic as a Second Language is the usual entry, and the writing component is where a small bank of accurately drilled structures pays off fastest.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results come out for UAE candidates?
faqs.answer: Results reach examination centres before students. For Pearson Edexcel, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The pattern holds: a June series produces results in August and a November series produces results in January. Those dates set the window for a remark request or a resit entry, both of which are handled through the school as the examination centre rather than directly by the family. Confirm the exact dates with the school each year.

faqs.question: Where does tutoring money get wasted in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three places, in order of cost. Buying cheap hours for a specialist problem, where a non-specialist cannot diagnose why a particular paper is losing marks and the hours teach nothing. Buying hours with no diagnosis, which turns a tutor into a weekly homework supervisor at a subject-specialist rate. And paying the in-home travel premium for a lesson whose entire working material is a marked script and a mark scheme, both of which read better shared on a screen than passed across a table. All three are avoidable by naming the component before booking.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor actually knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask for the syllabus code they have taught, not the subject. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry to Extended tier will say so and will know that the qualitative analysis tables are examined. A tutor who answers chemistry has told you nothing. Then ask what they would set in the first session; a specialist names a paper and a topic, a generalist describes an approach. The free trial lesson exists so that this test happens before any money changes hands rather than after a term of it.

The tutor pool is the same; only the start time moves. What still matters is the board, the tier and the component. Send us the syllabus code, the tier and a recent marked script, and the free trial lesson returns a written diagnosis. Lessons are one-to-one online on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service and are not offered in the UAE.

intro.heading: The two comparisons behind this search
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai Sports City typing this phrase is almost always running two comparisons in parallel. The first is geographic: is a tutor easier to arrange here than in Motor City across Hessa Street, or in Arabian Ranches down the road, and does living inside a master-planned sports community help or hinder? The second is about format: does a tutor need to be in the room at all?

The geographic comparison resolves more simply than most families expect. Sports City has schools inside its own boundary, Motor City has one minutes away, Victory Heights has a primary school on the doorstep, and Arabian Ranches has a long-established British and IB cluster. What differs between them is not the availability of tutors but the shape of the afternoon: bus routes, fixture timetables, and how late a Year 11 student gets home. Those differences change the hour a session is booked. They do not change which syllabus the student is sitting.

The format comparison is the one with money attached. Published market rates in Dubai put in-home one-to-one tuition between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is in the figure, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is a car journey. For a Year 10 student in Mudon or Remraam, the second journey of the day lands on the student rather than the tutor, which makes the arithmetic worse again.

IB Gram resolves the format question by stating it rather than negotiating it. Lessons for every UAE family are live, one-to-one and online over video. No tutor is sent to a Dubai address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. What the online model buys in exchange is the ability to match a student to the exact syllabus they sit — Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended or Combined Science 0653 — rather than to whoever teaches science within a twenty-minute drive.

That distinction is sharper at IGCSE than families realise, because two schools in neighbouring communities can enter the same subject with different boards, different paper structures and different tiering rules. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach good content against the wrong mark scheme. The section on boards below sets out what actually differs.

The rest of this page is built as the comparison the search is asking for: community against community, board against board, format against format, and cost against what the cost buys. Every AED figure is attributed to the provider who published it, and every examination date is either sourced from Cambridge and Pearson or left out. Read the tiering section before the rate tables if your child is in Year 10, because the Core or Extended entry has a longer effect on the final grade than the hourly rate ever will.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-c.programmesIntro: Three stages generate IGCSE tutoring requests from this part of Dubailand. The years before the course matter more than most families expect, because the gaps that surface in Year 10 were usually left behind in Year 9.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course per subject, examined by written papers at the end, with most students entering eight to ten subjects. Cambridge grades on A* to G or 9 to 1 depending on the syllabus; Pearson International GCSE uses 9 to 1. Some Cambridge syllabuses are tiered into Core and Extended, which caps the attainable grade, and that decision is made by the school long before the papers.
programmes.countryNote: The UK curriculum is the largest single curriculum by enrolment in Dubai's private schools, which is why almost every community around Sports City has an IGCSE cohort. UAE candidates sit the June and November series only; Cambridge offers the February/March series to India alone, so a Sports City family should never plan around it.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint years
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally and, in many schools, by Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Algebraic manipulation, scientific explanation and extended writing are built here. A student who leaves Year 9 unable to rearrange a formula will meet the same weakness in six IGCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Town Square, Mudon and Remraam most often enquire at this stage, because the communities are younger and the cohorts are heavier in Years 7 to 9. The useful intervention is short and specific rather than open-ended weekly support.

programmes.name: Post-16 progression from IGCSE
programmes.description: After IGCSE, students in this part of Dubai split between A Level and the IB Diploma, and the split often happens between schools rather than inside one. Subject choices at 16 close doors at 18, so the grade that matters is not the average but the one in the subject a student intends to continue. Entry requirements are set by the receiving school.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sports City families move a child from an IGCSE school to a Diploma school in the same year, which means meeting two sets of expectations at once. A bridging block over the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the common request, focused on the specific subjects being continued.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-c.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE courses Sports City and Motor City families ask for most, named with the syllabus codes that actually determine what a student sits. The code is the first thing worth checking on a school's subject information sheet.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers in both boards. Cambridge Extended reaches further into algebra, functions and trigonometry than Core, and Core caps the attainable grade. Marks go missing on method never written down, premature rounding, and a final answer given without units.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics. Cambridge includes a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option. The reliable losses are unit conversion before substitution, treating vectors as scalars, and explanation answers that recite a formula instead of giving a cause.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: States of matter, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, electrolysis, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Mole calculations and ionic equations produce the widest mark spread, and most of the recoverable marks are in setting out the calculation rather than in the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. Heavily assessed on data and diagram interpretation. Long answers reward precise terminology: osmosis described without mentioning a partially permeable membrane scores lower than the student expects.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: The two-award and double-award routes for students not taking three separate sciences. Content is lighter per subject but the papers mix disciplines, so revision has to be organised by paper rather than by science. Progression to a Higher Level or A Level science from this route needs checking with the receiving school.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, with marks for register, audience and structure as much as for accuracy. Students lose marks by summarising when asked to analyse, and by writing a correct text in the wrong form — a report when a letter was specified.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study based papers requiring application to the given business or economy. Definitions earn little; applied analysis and a supported judgement earn most. Diagram accuracy in Economics is the single largest avoidable loss, usually axes left unlabelled.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, security and algorithm design across two papers. Pseudocode questions are marked on logic rather than syntax, which students who have only written in one programming language often misread entirely.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level or Higher Level mathematics. Covers calculus, functions and trigonometry at a level closer to AS, and is the best single preparation for the step up at 16. Requests for it from Sports City cluster in the second half of Year 11.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Skills papers and case-study based extended writing. Both reward named, dated, located examples; a generic answer about urbanisation or revolution without a specific case earns a fraction of the available marks. Source questions in History are a technique rather than a knowledge test.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Dubai Sports City means here
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Dubai Sports City means private one-to-one tuition in a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel subject, arranged outside school, for a student living in or around the Sports City master plan. IB Gram supplies that teaching live online over video. It does not send a tutor to a Dubai address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is stated on every UAE page on this site.

The word 'home' in the search is describing a category of tuition rather than a delivery method, and it has survived because for twenty years in Dubai the two were the same thing. They stopped being the same thing when the binding constraint changed. A tutor no longer has to be within driving distance of Victory Heights to teach a Victory Heights student, but the cost of driving has not fallen.

What that frees up is the matching criterion. A request for Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended can be matched to a teacher who has taught 0620 Extended, instead of to the nearest available science graduate. For a Year 11 student eight weeks out from the papers, that is the difference between recovering marks and being taught content they already have.

The practical arrangement is plain enough to describe in a sentence: a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, one named tutor per syllabus, homework set from past papers and marked against the published scheme, and a written note after each session. Where no specialist is free for a syllabus, the honest answer is a stated wait rather than a substitution.

sections.heading: Sports City against Motor City, Victory Heights and the Ranches
paragraphs: Families comparing communities usually want to know whether one is better served than another. For tutoring delivered online, the honest answer is that the communities differ in timing and in cohort composition, not in access. The table below sets out what actually changes between them, which is the shape of the weekday afternoon and the mix of subjects requested.

Sports City itself has the earliest usable slot of any community in this belt, because its schools sit inside the master plan and students are often home before half past three. Motor City loses that advantage to sport: fixtures and swim training run into the early evening on weekdays, and a 4pm booking there gets cancelled more often than it gets kept. Victory Heights families send secondary students out of the community, which costs the end of the afternoon.

Arabian Ranches and DAMAC Hills behave differently again. Both have substantial school clusters, both sit further from the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed interchange, and both generate heavier Year 11 triple-science demand than Sports City does. Remraam and Dubailand Residence sit at the far end of the commute, and for those families the removal of a second journey is the whole value of the online format.

The cohort composition matters as much as the clock. A community with a primary school inside it and secondary commuting out produces a different enquiry pattern from one with a through-school: Victory Heights generates triple-science and Additional Mathematics requests from students taught elsewhere, while Town Square and Mudon generate Year 7 to Year 9 catch-up work. Knowing which pattern a community sits in is why the first question in any enquiry is the year group and the syllabus code rather than the postcode. The answer to 'which community is better served' is that none of them is underserved once the drive-time filter is removed, and the only community-level variable left is what time the session can realistically start.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what actually differs
paragraphs: Two schools in neighbouring Dubailand communities can enter the same subject with different boards, and the difference is not cosmetic. Papers differ in number and structure, tiering rules differ, and practical assessment is handled differently. A tutor teaching Cambridge content against a Pearson paper will cover the right chemistry and drill the wrong technique.

The first thing to find is the syllabus code, which appears on the school's subject information sheet and on every past paper. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610. Pearson International GCSE uses 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1. Once the code is known, everything else — paper structure, tiering, formula sheet, calculator rules — follows from the official specification rather than from guesswork.

The second thing to find is whether the school has entered a tiered or single-tier route, because Cambridge Core caps the grade a student can achieve. A Year 10 student placed in Core who intends to take an A Level or Higher Level science has a decision to make, and it is better made in Year 10 than discovered in Year 12. The table sets out the comparison by subject.

The third difference is how practical science is handled. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option, and the question style on that paper is distinctive: variable control, apparatus choice, tabulating results, spotting the flaw in a described method. Pearson handles the same skills differently within its own papers. A student drilled on one board's practical paper and then entered for the other will know the science and misread the questions, which is exactly the failure that looks like carelessness in a mock report and is actually a mismatch.

None of this is an argument that one board is harder. Both are respected, both feed the same post-16 routes, and the grade on the certificate does not record which paper structure produced it. The argument is only that tutoring has to be matched to the specification the student is actually entered for, and that a parent can establish which one that is in about two minutes by looking at a past paper header.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the grade ceiling nobody mentions in Year 10
paragraphs: Cambridge tiering is the decision with the longest shadow in the IGCSE years. Where a syllabus is split into Core and Extended, the papers differ and so does the range of grades available. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and the entry is made by the school, often quietly, on the basis of Year 9 and Year 10 attainment.

That is not an argument for pushing every student to Extended. A student placed on Extended who cannot handle the algebraic demand will lose more marks on harder papers than they would have gained from the higher ceiling, and the experience of sitting a paper they cannot attempt does real damage in the weeks before the series. The decision is a genuine judgement, and it should be made with the student's actual Year 10 mark profile on the table.

What a tutor can do is make the judgement informed. A diagnostic against the Extended content list shows which topics are absent rather than weak, and whether the gap is six weeks of work or two years of foundations. Where the gap is closable, the useful move is a targeted block in the first half of Year 11 and a conversation with the school. Where it is not, the honest advice is Core with a plan for the subject at 16.

Pearson's Foundation and Higher structure behaves similarly but not identically, so the same conversation has to be held against the specification the school actually entered. Either way the question to ask at the Year 10 parents' evening is specific: which tier has my child been entered for, what grade does that cap, and what would have to change for that to be revisited?

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs across this belt, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most searches start. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student end of the market. That tier is real and it has a use: homework supervision, content recap, keeping a Year 9 student moving. It is not the tier that recovers marks on a Year 11 Extended paper.

The next band up is qualified subject teaching delivered online, which Unitors publishes from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai table puts the mid band at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month for weekly one-hour sessions, and the budget band at AED 240 to 600. Specialist exam-year support sits at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month in the same table.

Above that, specialist rates run from AED 200 to 450 and beyond — TutorChase quotes AED 270 — and the premium named end reaches AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel is included. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

All of those are market figures published by the providers named, read in October 2026, and none of them is IB Gram's price list. They are printed because three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars. sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs you instead
paragraphs: Set the two bands side by side. In-home tuition in this part of Dubai is published at AED 180 to 500 an hour. Qualified online subject teaching is published at AED 150 to 300. The overlap is narrow and the top of the in-home range is well above the top of the online one, and the reason is not that the teaching is better. It is that somebody drove to Victory Heights and will drive back.

The cost of that journey is not only money. A tutor who spends eighty minutes travelling for a sixty-minute lesson can teach fewer students, so their availability is thinner and their cancellation rate is higher. A session that depends on the Hessa Street interchange at six in the evening starts when it starts. And the pool a family is choosing from shrinks to people who happen to be free in that corridor on that evening.

There are things a person in the room genuinely does better, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. A nine-year-old is easier to keep on task in person. Apparatus handled in real life is not the same as apparatus on a screen. For Year 10 and Year 11 students working through past papers, the balance runs the other way: annotating a mark scheme on a shared screen is better than annotating it upside down across a table, and the session can be rewatched before a mock.

IB Gram's position needs no hedging. There are no home visits in the UAE, India is the only country where that service runs, and the case for the online format is in the comparison rather than in a promise. What the saved travel premium buys is specialist selection, and at Extended tier in a science that is the variable that moves the grade.

sections.heading: June, November, and the date that actually binds
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate plans around June, with November as the resit route, and a Sports City family reading advice written for Indian candidates will be working to the wrong calendar.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth taking literally: the timetable a parent finds through a search is not necessarily the timetable the school's centre is working to.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. In the most recent completed cycles, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a school should always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The binding date, though, is not the examination. It is the final entry deadline, which sits months earlier and is the point at which the subject, the board and the tier are fixed. A tiering conversation held after entries have closed is a conversation about next year. That is the single most useful thing on this page for a Year 10 family in Sports City: find out when your school's entries close, and have the tier discussion before it.

sections.heading: Five subjects, equivalency, and what comes after the grades
paragraphs: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or no less, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the same guidance sets English proficiency at an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math. No verified IB points threshold is published here, because none could be read from a Ministry source, and publishing an unsourced one across thousands of pages would be worse than omitting it.

Equivalency is a Ministry process. IB Gram does not perform it, influence it or guarantee an outcome, and no tutoring is required for it. The reason it belongs on this page is that most Sports City families discover it in Year 12 or later, by which point the subject count and the grades are fixed. Knowing in Year 10 that five subjects at grade 3 or above must sit outside Arabic and Islamic Education occasionally changes a subject choice, which is the point of saying it early.
Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before acting on it. Rules change, and a tutoring page is not the authority on them.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the real Year 11 timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Across the other emirates the map is ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator does more than inspect.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools are required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

For a Year 11 student in Sports City, the consequence is arithmetic. The eight or nine IGCSE subjects on the entry sheet are not the whole timetable, and the mandatory subjects take real lesson time. Revision plans built on the assumption that school hours map onto examined subjects run short, and the shortfall usually shows up in the subject the student likes least.

The market context explains the rest. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 curricula; seven new private schools are being added for 2026-27, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against fees at that scale, a targeted eight-session tutoring block is a small line item, which is an argument for spending it precisely rather than spreading it across a year.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not just the subject
process.description: An enquiry that says 'Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended, Year 11, last mock a 5' can be answered properly. One that says 'science help needed' cannot. The code is on the school's subject information sheet and on every past paper, and it decides which tutors are a genuine match.

process.title: Trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: A full online session with the proposed specialist rather than a call with a coordinator. The tutor works through the student's own marked paper, sorts the lost marks by cause, and sends a written summary with the topics to rebuild. No card is required and there is no obligation to continue.

process.title: Fix a target and a block length
process.description: Work is booked against a named objective — mole calculations, Paper 2 timing, directed writing forms — in a block short enough to judge. A target makes the block reviewable; an open-ended weekly hour tends to continue on momentum regardless of whether marks have moved.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked past-paper work
process.description: Each session sets questions from past papers, marked against the published scheme before the next one. The topic checklist is updated and shared, and the note home says what was covered and what was set rather than reporting that the session went well.

process.title: Review at four sessions, change if needed
process.description: At four sessions the block is measured against its target. If the marks have not moved, the answer is a different diagnosis, a different tutor or a different frequency, and changing the match costs nothing. Families who never review a block are the ones who pay for a year of no movement.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus, not a subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers with different question styles. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach correct chemistry against the wrong mark scheme, and that is the most common way a Year 11 block produces no movement at all.

whyPoints.title: Rates printed with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Most pages competing for this search publish no price, and the two that do quote US dollars. A family in Sports City deserves to see the bands before the conversation about fees, not afterwards.

whyPoints.title: The tiering conversation, held early
whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation entries cap the grade a student can reach, and the entry is usually made in Year 10 without much discussion. A diagnostic against the Extended content list shows whether the gap is weeks of work or years of foundations, which is what makes that conversation useful.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's June and November series, the six administrative zones, and Pearson's May/June and November windows are stated from the boards' own pages. The February/March series is not mentioned as an option because Cambridge offers it to India only, and advice written for Indian candidates misleads UAE families.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated on the page
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are live, one-to-one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram sends no tutor to a home in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting runs only in India. That is on the page rather than discovered after a deposit has been paid.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval and claims none. The regulators and boards named here are described so parents know who does what. Any provider describing its tutors as regulator-approved is making a claim worth checking before paying.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a villa in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Independent tutors in this part of Dubai do visit homes, and published market rates for in-home one-to-one sessions run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is in the figure, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The difference pays for the journey. The online model is offered instead because it allows matching by syllabus code.

faqs.question: Where exactly do I look to see which IGCSE board my child's Sports City school entered?
faqs.answer: Look for the syllabus code rather than the board name. It appears on the school's subject information sheet, on the exam entry confirmation, and on the top of every past paper the student has been given. Cambridge codes look like 0580, 0620 or 0625; Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4CH1 or 4PH1. Schools in neighbouring communities around Sports City sometimes enter different boards for the same subject, so the answer cannot be inferred from where you live.

faqs.question: Is Sports City better served for tutors than Motor City or Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: For online tuition, access is the same across all three; what differs is the shape of the afternoon. Sports City students are often home before 3.30pm because their schools sit inside the master plan, so a 4pm slot holds. Motor City loses the early slot to sport and swim training. Victory Heights secondary students commute out towards Al Barsha, and DAMAC Hills and Remraam have longer bus journeys again. The practical answer is that the community sets the session time, not the tutor supply.

faqs.question: If my child is entered for Core, what is the highest IGCSE grade still available?
faqs.answer: Where a Cambridge syllabus is tiered, Core and Extended sit on different papers and Core caps the grade that can be achieved however well a student performs. Pearson's Foundation and Higher structure works similarly. The entry is made by the school, usually during Year 10, on the basis of attainment to that point. If your child intends to continue the subject at A Level or Higher Level, ask which tier they have been entered for and what would have to change for that to be revisited.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IGCSE tuition around Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Published rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the university-student end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, through AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching, which is where Unitors publishes its IGCSE rate from AED 150. Specialist rates reach AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do families in this part of Dubai struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at Extended tier, Chemistry, and English Language, in roughly that order of enquiry volume. In Mathematics the losses cluster in algebraic manipulation and in method never written down. In Chemistry they cluster in mole calculations and ionic equations, where most recoverable marks sit in how the calculation is set out. In English Language the common failure is writing a competent text in the wrong form, which no amount of content knowledge rescues.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 student in Sports City start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Early enough for the tiering decision to still be open, which in practice means the first half of Year 10. That is when a diagnostic against the Extended content list is most useful, because absent topics can still be rebuilt rather than patched. Waiting until the Year 11 mock results means working inside whatever tier was entered, with weeks rather than terms available. A short diagnostic block in Year 10 is cheaper than an intensive in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and two sciences for the same student?
faqs.answer: It is possible but rarely the better arrangement. Each syllabus has its own paper structure, command terms and mark scheme, and a tutor strong in one is usually average in another. The approach here is a specialist per syllabus, with sessions spaced across different evenings so the student is not carrying three sets of homework into one night. For a triple-science student in Year 11, two tutors on separate evenings produces more movement than one tutor across three subjects.

faqs.question: Are science practicals a problem if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Practical skills are assessed through written components, and Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route in several sciences, so the examinable skill is largely about experimental design, variable control, data handling and evaluating method. All of that can be taught on screen using real past-paper data. What online lessons cannot do is replace handling apparatus in a school laboratory, which is the school's job. The honest division of labour is that the school supplies the bench and the tutor supplies the technique.

faqs.question: Do tutors working in Dubai Sports City need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and is open to school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications are made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Dubai student need for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. A competitor page ranking for these searches states six; the sourced requirement is five. Confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring provider decides it.

faqs.question: What happens if we try a tutor and the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: You ask for a different one, and that is treated as normal rather than awkward. The trial lesson exists to make the mismatch visible before money is committed, and blocks are reviewed at four sessions so a quiet lack of progress gets caught. The failures worth avoiding are the silent ones: a pleasant weekly hour that nobody measures, continuing for a term because changing felt like a complaint. Reviewing a block against a stated target removes that problem entirely.

faqs.question: Can sessions be rescheduled around fixtures and swim training?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Motor City and Sports City that comes up most weeks. Because lessons are online, moving a slot needs no journey rearranged on either side, so a Tuesday session can become Wednesday within the same week without anybody losing travel time. The limit is the tutor's own timetable rather than geography. Families with a weekly fixture clash usually settle on a fixed weekend morning slot instead, which holds better through a season than a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Does a tutor help with coursework for IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the assessment criteria, questions the method, discusses whether evidence supports a conclusion and gives feedback on what the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of assessed work. That line is a board rule rather than a house preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student. Any provider offering finished coursework is selling a risk that lands on the candidate, not on them.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the plan has to change. Eight weeks is not enough to rebuild absent topics across a syllabus, so the work becomes triage: identify which marks are recoverable in the time available, drill those, and stop spending sessions on content the student will not reach. Full timed papers with immediate mark-scheme review is the format that works at this range. What does not work is starting at topic one and hoping to arrive at the end before the series.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-c.closingHeading: Send the code, the year and the last paper
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubai-sports-c.closingBody: If you want an IGCSE home tutor in Dubai Sports City, the useful first message names the syllabus code, the year group and the most recent marked paper. From that it is possible to say honestly whether a specialist in that exact syllabus is free, what the first block should try to move, and whether the tier your child has been entered for is the right one. The trial lesson is a full teaching session with the tutor who would do the work, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time, and it ends with a written list of topics to rebuild rather than a quote.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach International GCSE subjects to Dubailand families, and each profile names the board as well as the subject. That matters more than it looks: a Cambridge 0625 Physics specialist and a Pearson 4PH1 specialist are preparing students for differently structured papers.

intro.heading: Does anyone near Dubailand know which IGCSE your child is actually sitting?
paragraphs: Parents in the Dubailand belt type the phrase and get a list of names sorted by how far away they live. The list looks reassuring and answers the wrong question. International GCSE is not a single qualification. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award it, their syllabuses carry different codes, their papers are structured differently, Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended while Pearson generally does not, and Pearson offers a modular route in some subjects that Cambridge does not offer at all. A tutor who does not know which of those your child is entered for cannot usefully prepare them for any of it.

Add the geography. Dubailand is a development zone, not a street. It runs along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and absorbs Arabian Ranches and its two successors, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Two families both describing themselves as Dubailand residents can be twenty-five minutes apart in evening traffic. An in-home tutor who can reach Motor City at half past five is not the same person who can reach Town Square, and the person who claims both is building the journey into the fee.

The subject supply problem follows from that. Independent tutors concentrate where journeys are short, which in Dubai means the coastal corridor, Al Barsha and Business Bay rather than a villa belt forty minutes inland. The narrower a parent draws the radius, the more the available person becomes a generalist. For a Year 11 student who needs Extended tier chemistry taught against a specific syllabus code, a generalist is not a small compromise; it is the difference between practising the right paper and the wrong one.

There is a documented legal frame around this too. Private tuition in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any site quoting an amount with suspicion. A parent should be able to ask about the permit and get a straight answer.

So the straight answer from IB Gram is this: we do not send anybody to a Dubailand address. Home visits exist only in our India service. For UAE families the lesson runs one-to-one over live video, which takes the drive out of the equation and lets the match be decided by board, code and tier. What follows is the detail a parent needs to run that check themselves: how the two boards differ, what the tier does to the grade ceiling, what the belt pays, how the November route works, and where a tutor's role ends on coursework.

Cambridge tiers subjects into Core and Extended; the tier caps the achievable grade

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: Four routes cover nearly every Dubailand family asking about International GCSE. The differences below are practical rather than administrative: they change which papers a student sits and when.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely entered International GCSE in Dubai schools. Several subjects are tiered: Core papers lead to grades C to G, Extended papers to A* to E, and the tier is decided at entry. Syllabus codes identify the exact specification, for example 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics. Cambridge runs the qualification in a June series and a November series.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand schools entering Cambridge candidates make the Core or Extended decision in Year 10, often on the basis of a single internal assessment. That is the single most consequential academic decision a family in this belt makes before sixteen, because an Extended entry made late is harder to prepare for than one planned from the start of Year 10.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Awarded on a 9 to 1 scale in most subjects, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics and 4PH1 Physics. Pearson generally examines a single tier in sciences, with Higher and Foundation tiers in mathematics. A modular route is available in some subjects, so units can be sat across more than one series and the best result carried forward. Examinations run in May/June and November.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into the Dubailand belt from a UK state school meet Pearson most often, and the modular option is the part they tend not to know about. Splitting units across two series changes the revision plan completely and should be checked with the school's examinations officer rather than assumed from a specification page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before International GCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. These are diagnostic rather than certificating, and their real function is to indicate whether a student is on a Core or Extended trajectory. Weaknesses visible at Checkpoint in algebra, scientific explanation or extended writing are the ones that decide tier two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubailand belt has a heavy primary and lower-secondary population because of its newer communities, so a large share of enquiries from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon and Town Square are about Years 7 to 9 rather than Year 11. Work done here is cheaper and more effective than remediation in the examination year.

programmes.name: AS and International A Level progression
programmes.description: The route most Dubailand British-curriculum students take after International GCSE, alongside the IB Diploma. Subject choice at sixteen is constrained by International GCSE tier and grade, which is why the tier decision matters beyond the certificate itself. Cambridge International A Level also runs in June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, is required alongside the five International GCSE subjects. Families planning a UAE university application should check that before finalising the sixth-form option block.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: These are the International GCSE subjects Dubailand families ask about most. Each note names the board-specific detail that changes how the subject should be taught, because that is the information a distance-based search cannot supply.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended (0580) · Pearson Higher and Foundation (4MA1)
subjects.description: The tier decision is everything here. Extended and Higher papers carry algebraic manipulation, functions and trigonometry that Core and Foundation papers do not reach. Marks are lost on method presentation: an unsupported correct answer scores less than a shown-working answer that ends slightly wrong.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and mechanics dominate the mark distribution and are taught early, so gaps compound. Students who understand the physics still lose marks on units, significant figures and graph work. Practical skills are assessed through written questions about method rather than through a performed experiment in most routes.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry carry the difficulty. The recurring error is answering a describe command term when the question asks for an explanation, and writing equations that balance but omit state symbols the markscheme requires.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Vocabulary-dependent and content-heavy. A student can recall a process accurately and still score two of six because the answer is not structured the way the markscheme reads. Data and graph interpretation questions are where the strongest candidates leak marks.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: A single or double award covering all three sciences with reduced content in each. Students on this route need teaching that respects what has been removed, because revising from separate-science material wastes a large share of the available hours on topics they will never be examined on.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response, with marks dominated by structure and the ability to select evidence precisely. Students raised bilingually in Dubai often have strong vocabulary and weak paragraph discipline, which is the specific skill that moves the grade.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different specification with its own reading and listening components. Many Dubailand families are not clear which of the two English routes their child is entered for, and the revision material for one is of limited use for the other.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application and evaluation carry the top band marks, not definitions. Students who learned to define terms in Year 9 keep defining them in Year 11 and run short of time on the longer questions where most of the marks sit.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two very different subjects that parents routinely conflate. Computer Science carries algorithms and pseudocode; ICT is practical and application-based. Tutoring built for the wrong one is a term wasted, and it happens often enough to be worth checking at the first session.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. The productive skills carry the assessment weight, and the school's own material is the correct basis for support.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.regionsIntro: The communities inside and beside the Dubailand belt differ in school supply, commute and what time a session can realistically run. These are the operational notes that matter for an International GCSE timetable.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Established villa community with on-site primary provision; Year 10 and 11 students mostly travel out of the belt. The practical consequence is that a Year 11 revision slot before six in the evening rarely survives a full term.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Younger demographic, heavier Checkpoint and Year 9 enquiry volume. Al Qudra Road is the afternoon constraint, which is why parents here favour arrangements that do not depend on anyone driving.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Newest phase, with a high rate of mid-year transfers between British and IB settings. Board changes mid-Year-10 are the hardest version of this and need the syllabus code confirmed before any planning.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Apartment-dense with on-community schooling and a crowded evening sports calendar. Short fixed weekday sessions outperform long flexible ones here, particularly through the Year 11 mock period.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Academy training dominates weekday evenings for a large share of students. Weekend morning revision is the realistic pattern, which works online and is prohibitively expensive as a visit.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: Villa community with its own school and long outbound journeys for students attending coastal-corridor schools. Arrival time home, not school finish time, sets the earliest usable slot.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: Far end of Al Qudra Road and the clearest case where a distance-first search fails. An Extended-tier specialist willing to drive here twice weekly is rare at any rate.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Mixed stock with community schooling for younger years and longer travel from Year 7. Requests to cover two siblings on the same evening come from here more than anywhere else in the belt.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches and the Al Qudra corridor
schoolClusters.note: The older half of the belt, where British-curriculum secondary provision sits a short drive north of the villa communities. Families here often have one child on Cambridge and another on Pearson depending on when and where they joined.

schoolClusters.note: Newer and denser, with several schools inside the communities. International GCSE cohorts here are growing quickly, which is exactly when board and tier confusion is most common.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: find out before you buy a single hour
paragraphs: This is the first question to answer and most families cannot answer it on the spot. Ask the school's examinations officer which board each subject is entered with, and ask for the syllabus code. Not the subject name, the code. Mathematics could be Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1. Physics could be 0625 or 4PH1. Those are different specifications with different paper structures, and material built for one is partially useful for the other at best.

The differences are structural rather than cosmetic. Cambridge tiers several subjects, so a Core entry in mathematics caps the grade at C while an Extended entry reaches A*. Pearson uses a 9 to 1 scale in most subjects and tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Pearson offers a modular route in some subjects, meaning units can be sat in different series with the better result carried, which is a planning option Cambridge candidates simply do not have. English is a further trap: Cambridge 0500 First Language and 0510 Second Language are separate specifications, and students are routinely revising from the wrong one.

Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole area-page cluster of competing tutoring sites researched for this project. That is the measure of how little attention this gets, and it is the cheapest advantage available to a parent. A tutor who asks for the code in the first message is working from the specification; one who says the subject name is enough is working from memory.

The table below sets out where the two boards diverge for the subjects Dubailand families ask about most. Treat it as a checklist for the conversation with the school, not as a substitute for the school's own entry record.

sections.heading: What the tier does to the grade ceiling, and when it can still be changed
paragraphs: A Cambridge Core entry in a tiered subject cannot produce a grade above C. That single sentence decides more Dubailand outcomes than any revision technique, and plenty of parents learn it in Year 11 rather than Year 10. The tier is chosen at entry by the school, usually on internal evidence, and it is intended to give the student the paper where they can demonstrate what they know. It is a sound principle and it also quietly fixes a ceiling.

The consequence runs forward. If a student needs five International GCSE subjects at specific grades for a sixth-form option or for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a Core entry in a subject they need at a higher grade is a problem that cannot be solved by working harder in the examination room. It has to be solved before entries are submitted, which happens months ahead of the papers.

That is where a diagnostic earns its cost. A tutor working against the actual specification can tell you in three or four sessions whether the Extended paper is realistically reachable and what closing the gap would require in weeks. That evidence, written down, is more persuasive in a conversation with a head of department than a parent's conviction. Sometimes it says the opposite, and an honest Core entry with a strong grade is better than an Extended entry producing an E.

For Pearson candidates the modular route changes the arithmetic. Where a subject permits it, units can be sat across more than one series with the better result carried forward, which converts one high-stakes moment into two lower ones. Whether a subject offers it is a question for the examinations officer, because it varies by specification and by what the centre chooses to enter.

Use award-specific material only; separate-science revision over-prepares

sections.heading: Why the nearest International GCSE tutor is usually the wrong one here
paragraphs: Return to the original question, because the board and tier detail above is what makes it answerable. A parent wants somebody competent who can be in the villa by a given hour. In a dense neighbourhood those two requirements overlap comfortably. Across a belt that stretches fifteen kilometres inland from Sheikh Zayed Road, they usually do not, and the thing that gets sacrificed is specificity.

Think about the tutor's diary rather than the parent's. A specialist in Extended-tier Cambridge chemistry has a limited number of usable weekday evening slots, and every family wants the same two hours. If each visit costs forty minutes of driving at each end, the tutor serves perhaps three Dubailand families a week against six in Al Barsha. The rate must carry the fuel and the dead time, and the subject range must widen to keep the diary full. A tutor advertising maths, all three sciences and English across Years 7 to 11 is not necessarily weak; they are responding rationally to a dispersed market.

For a Year 9 homework-habit problem that generalist may be entirely sufficient, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. For a Year 11 student eight weeks out from an Extended paper, it is not, because the work at that point is board-specific technique and the generalist is reconstructing the specification from memory.

Removing distance from the match reverses the constraint. The question becomes which specialist has taught 0620 Extended recently, and that has a real answer. A Town Square family and an Arabian Ranches family can book the same specialist at different hours of the same evening, and neither pays for a car. That is the whole argument, and it is why IB Gram delivers to this belt online rather than claiming a coverage area it cannot honestly serve.

sections.heading: What International GCSE tuition costs across the Dubailand communities
paragraphs: Budget by the month, because that is how the decision actually gets made. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget provision at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward. Packages circulating in the market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those monthly figures are more useful than an hourly rate because they expose what a full Year 11 actually costs.

Translated to hours, the cheapest band runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching 500. The premium band tops out around AED 650 with BartyED.

Where does the money get wasted in this belt? Three places. Buying twenty cheap hours for a Year 11 Extended paper when six specialist hours would move more marks. Paying the in-home travel premium for a Year 10 student who works perfectly well on a screen. And paying for tuition in a subject where the real problem is that the tier is wrong, which no number of hours fixes after entries close.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, so the point of listing sourced bands is that a parent can sanity-check a quote. Our own answer to the cost question is a free trial lesson and a conversation, because the only figure that matters is whether this specialist moves this student.
