sections.heading: The November route, and the gap before results arrive
paragraphs: The November series is the part of the calendar that competing pages in this market do not mention at all. The word November returned no hits on every fetchable competitor page researched for this project. For a Dubailand family it is the most useful thing on the calendar, because it is the resit and the second chance.

Get the geography right first. Cambridge International runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a March window or a late-November entry deadline for a spring examination is handing parents a date they cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Backward-looking dates are worth citing because they can be checked. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So the real interval from the November papers to a result is roughly nine weeks, landing in January, and that gap is the thing to plan around: a student retaking in November will not know the outcome before sixth-form conversations begin. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the official timetable is always the document to check.

One Cambridge administrative detail catches families who have moved. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone the centre sits in before building a revision schedule from a timetable found online.

sections.heading: How science practicals work when the tuition is online
paragraphs: This is the objection that arrives in almost every first conversation with a Dubailand parent, and it rests on a misunderstanding of how the qualification is assessed. In the main International GCSE science routes, practical skills are examined through written questions about experimental method rather than through a performed experiment marked on the day. The student is asked to identify a variable, criticise a method, read a scale, process data, evaluate reliability and suggest an improvement.

Those are exactly the skills that can be taught on a screen, and in some respects taught better. A shared document with the student's own data table on it, annotated live, does more for graph technique than watching a demonstration. The tutor can put up a flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is precisely the question format the papers use. What a screen cannot do is build the muscle memory of handling a burette, and that part belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technician.

So the division of labour is clear and worth stating to a parent directly. The school runs the laboratory work. The tutor teaches the written practical paper: the vocabulary of controlled and dependent variables, the structure of an evaluation answer, the arithmetic of percentage error, the habit of quoting units and significant figures consistently. Those are the marks students lose, and they are lost on paper rather than at the bench.

There is a related point about resources. We do not reproduce or supply board material. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. A tutor points to the official source, works with what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style.

sections.heading: Building the option block with Ministry of Education equivalency in mind
paragraphs: Equivalency is where the subject choices made in Year 9 come back, and it is almost entirely absent from competing pages. Several of the query clusters researched for this project contain no mention of it at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count. For a Dubailand family who may want a UAE university place, that is the detail worth getting right early.

The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or International GCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A competitor page stating six subjects is simply wrong, and a family who planned an option block around the wrong number has made a real mistake.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no verified points threshold could be read on an official Ministry source for this project, so none is published here; check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority.

Two things IB Gram will not do. We will not describe equivalency as a process we perform, expedite or guarantee, because it belongs to the family and the Ministry. And we will not suggest that tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or school progression. It is not, and a page implying otherwise is inventing pressure around a regulatory procedure.

sections.heading: What an International GCSE tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: International GCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where coursework exists the boundary is the same, and it is worth stating because one page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work outright. The penalty for that falls on the student, not on the seller, so the line is not an abstraction.

A tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, test whether a proposed approach is workable, read what the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach citation and referencing properly. They may ask uncomfortable questions about whether a conclusion follows from the evidence. All of that is teaching.

A tutor must not produce the work. They do not draft a coursework submission, do not rewrite a student's text until the voice has gone, and do not supply a finished piece for submission. Where a school requires an authentication statement, the student signs it, and a tutor who has crossed the line has put that signature at risk. The same applies to the mandatory UAE subjects: for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so support works from the school's own material.

There is a UAE-specific rule worth knowing alongside this. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document, but the principle is sound: your child's own classroom teacher is not the person to pay privately.

process.title: Get the board, code and tier from the school
process.description: One email to the examinations officer asking which board each subject is entered with, the syllabus code, and the tier where one applies. That reply is worth more to a tutor than any description of the problem, and it takes a parent five minutes to obtain.

process.title: Describe the failure, not the feeling
process.description: "Loses marks on six-mark explain questions in 0620" is actionable. "Struggling with chemistry" is not. If you have a recent paper with a mark breakdown, that is the single most useful document you can share before a first session.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: A full session at no charge and no card. Judge it on one thing: can the tutor name the specific skill costing marks by the end? If not, the match is wrong and we will find another rather than asking you to persevere.

process.title: Fix the slot around the real arrival time
process.description: Not the school bell but the time the student is actually home, fed and able to concentrate. In Motor City and Sports City that often means after training, and in Town Square it means later than parents expect. Weekend mornings are a legitimate answer.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the diagnostic
process.description: Six sessions shows whether method is changing, even where the grade has not moved. Compare against the first paper rather than against an impression. Pause for mock weeks and travel; nothing needs to run unbroken to work.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code comes first
whyPoints.description: Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole competing area-page cluster researched for this project. We ask for it before matching, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers and a tutor who does not know which one is involved is guessing.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation happens early
whyPoints.description: A Core entry caps a Cambridge grade at C, and that cannot be undone in the examination room. A diagnostic against the real specification tells a family whether Extended is reachable and what it would cost in weeks, in writing, before entries close.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as the market, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or source that published it, in monthly as well as hourly form. Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The November series is part of the plan
whyPoints.description: Cambridge runs June and November in the UAE; the February and March series is India-only. Pearson runs May/June and November, and November results land in January, which changes what a resit can realistically achieve before sixth-form decisions.

whyPoints.title: No board or regulator approval claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no UAE office. We explain what each body does and link to it, because a platform claiming otherwise is telling you something about its other claims.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before payment
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free for a narrow subject or an awkward hour, we say so and give a date. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is why families keep finding out in week three.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to my house in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram runs home visits only in India; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Independent in-home tutors do operate across the Dubailand belt, and the market quotes them at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel built in. The comparison worth making is that the premium over an online specialist buys the drive, not better teaching, and across a belt reaching from Arabian Ranches to Town Square it also restricts you to whoever is willing to make that journey twice a week.

faqs.question: Our Dubailand school never told us the exam board. Where do we get it?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the board and the syllabus code for each subject, not just the subject name. You are looking for something like 0580 or 4MA1 for mathematics, 0625 or 4PH1 for physics. Ask about the tier at the same time, since Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended and Pearson tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. That one reply determines which papers the revision should target, and a tutor who does not ask for it is working from memory rather than the specification.

faqs.question: Does a Core entry really limit the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes, in Cambridge tiered subjects. Core papers lead to grades C to G and Extended papers to A* to E, and the tier is set at entry by the school rather than chosen in the examination room. It is a reasonable principle, because the paper should let the student show what they know, but it does fix a ceiling. If a higher grade is needed for a sixth-form option or for Ministry of Education equivalency, the conversation has to happen before entries close, supported by evidence from work against the real specification.

faqs.question: What does a good IGCSE tutor cost per month for a Year 11 student in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Market estimates rather than our prices. Bestimate's Dubai figures for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Packages of around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions circulate, and in-home blocks of four two-hour sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. For a Year 11 Extended-tier paper the specialist band is usually the honest answer, and a free trial lesson is the sensible way to test it first.

faqs.question: Can online lessons prepare my child for the science practical papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, because in the main International GCSE science routes practical skills are assessed through written questions about method rather than a performed experiment. Students are asked to identify variables, criticise a method, read scales, process data, evaluate reliability and suggest improvements. Those are screen-friendly skills, and annotating the student's own data table live does more for graph technique than watching a demonstration. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which has the equipment. The marks, though, are lost on paper, and that is where the tutoring belongs.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubailand families most often get wrong on the tutoring brief?
faqs.answer: Three recur. English, where Cambridge 0500 First Language and 0510 Second Language are separate specifications and students revise from the wrong one. Computer Science against ICT, which parents conflate although 0478 carries algorithms and pseudocode while 0417 is application-based. And the combined or coordinated science awards, where families revise from separate-science material and spend weeks on content that has been removed from their award. All three are fixed by asking the school for the code.

faqs.question: Why can't I just hire the closest tutor to Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: You can, and for a Year 9 homework-habit problem it may be the right call. The difficulty is that independent tutors cluster where journeys are short, so a villa belt forty minutes inland has a thin pool by subject. A tutor losing eighty minutes to driving per visit serves roughly half as many families as one working in Al Barsha, so rates rise and subject ranges widen to fill the diary. For a Year 11 Extended paper that generalisation costs you the board-specific technique that is where the marks actually are.

faqs.question: What is the November IGCSE series and should we use it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. The November route is mainly a resit and a second chance. The timing matters: Pearson's November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November candidate waits about nine weeks and learns the outcome in January. That lands after many sixth-form conversations begin, which is the practical argument for treating November as a backup rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a UAE licence to teach my child privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published. Since it costs nothing, there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for a UAE university place?
faqs.answer: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or International GCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae, and note that tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency in any form.

faqs.question: What may a Dubailand tutor legitimately touch on an IGCSE coursework piece?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the criteria reward, test whether a proposed approach is workable, read the student's own draft and show where marks are being lost, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach referencing properly. A tutor must never produce the submission or rewrite it until the student's voice has gone. Where a school requires an authentication statement, the student signs it, and a tutor who crossed that line has put the signature at risk. One page in this market sells finished work outright; the penalty falls on the student.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9 and nothing is wrong yet. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: Not premature, just different in purpose. Year 9 and the Checkpoint stage is where the Core or Extended trajectory is being set, and the weaknesses that decide it are specific: algebraic fluency, writing a scientific explanation rather than a description, and sustaining a structured paragraph. Work on those is cheaper and more effective now than remediation in Year 11, and it is the reason a large share of enquiries from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon and Town Square concern Years 7 to 9 rather than the examination year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two siblings on different IGCSE boards in the same evening?
faqs.answer: They can, but it is often better that they do not. A Cambridge 0580 Extended specialist and a Pearson 4MA1 Higher specialist prepare students for differently structured papers, and asking one person to hold both well is an unnecessary compromise. What works cleanly online is two consecutive slots with two specialists, which costs nothing extra because there is no travel to pay for. Families in Mudon and Remraam ask for this arrangement more than anyone else in the belt, and it is straightforward to schedule.

faqs.question: Will you send us past papers and mark schemes to work through?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers a download library. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are Cambridge and Pearson copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. What a tutor does instead is cite and link the official source, work from material the school has legitimately issued, and write equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. That produces the same preparation without inheriting somebody else's copyright problem.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Ask for the code before you book the hour
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Dubailand, the most valuable five minutes you will spend is an email to the school asking for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject. With that in hand, the match stops being a question about distance and becomes a question about who has taught that exact specification recently, which has a real answer. Book a free trial lesson with the relevant specialist, judge it on whether the tutor can name the skill costing marks, and go from there. Nothing is sent to your address and no card is needed to start.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects at Core and Extended, with a bias towards the Years 10 and 11 content Emaar Beachfront families ask for in an exam term: Maths, the three sciences, English and Economics.

intro.heading: Count the weeks first, then book the tutor
paragraphs: An IGCSE year has a shape, and almost every mistake families make with tutoring comes from ignoring it. The external papers are fixed months in advance. Entries close long before the first exam. The school's own mock window, coursework deadlines and practical assessments sit in front of that, and they are the signals that tell you whether the external result is on track. A tutor booked in response to a report card arrives at a different point in that shape than a tutor booked in response to a mock script, and the work they should do is not the same.

For UAE candidates the series are June and November with Cambridge. The February/March series exists, but Cambridge offers it to India only, so a Dubai family who plans around a February exam has planned around a date their centre will not sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each; the guidance is explicit that using the wrong zone version is the centre's risk and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam as a result. Ask your school which zone it sits in before you build any plan on a published date.

Emaar Beachfront adds a logistical layer to that calendar. The peninsula is reached by one road link off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, there is no school and no tuition centre inside it, and visitor access to tower basements needs a resident to clear it. Children here leave before 07:00 for schools in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and are back after 15:30. In an exam term, where two sessions a week is the pattern that moves a grade, a format that depends on a tutor crossing that causeway twice a week in the 16:00 to 19:00 window is the format most likely to lose sessions. IB Gram teaches one-to-one online over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows is the calendar in usable form. The milestones, counted backwards from the series, with who sets each one. The differences between Cambridge and Edexcel that change your dates rather than just your syllabus codes. An eight-week plan with the evidence you should be able to see at the end of each block. The AED rates this market charges, cheapest first, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. And the content boundary on coursework, which in an exam term is when families are most tempted to cross it.

One more thing before the detail. A tutoring plan is a claim about time, and the claim should be falsifiable. If a block is working you should be able to see it at the fortnight, in the form of a topic-level mark breakdown rather than a reassuring message. If you cannot see it, the plan is wrong and should change. Everything on this page is arranged so that you can tell the difference between progress and activity, which in an exam term is the only distinction that matters to a result.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.programmesIntro: An IGCSE plan depends on which of three stages your child is in, because the same subject needs different work in Year 9 than it does in the February before a June series. These are the stages Emaar Beachfront families schedule around.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external series, but this is where the IGCSE grade is largely decided. Algebraic manipulation, equation balancing, graph interpretation and written explanation either become automatic here or they do not. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October where a school uses them, which gives an early external reference point.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving this cluster teach the IB Middle Years Programme to Year 9 before switching to IGCSE, so a Beachfront family may be preparing for a transition rather than a continuation. Confirm the school's published pathway before you plan two years of support.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally at the end. Year 10 is content coverage; Year 11 is technique, timing and mark-scheme literacy. Core and Extended tiers cap the available grade differently, and the tier decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 on evidence it already holds.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are counted, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One ranking competitor publishes six as the requirement; the sourced figure is five.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after IGCSE
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is a gate rather than a destination. A Level and Diploma entry requirements are published by each school, and the subjects a student can continue are decided by the Year 11 results. Maths and the sciences are where the gap between an Extended grade B and a grade A shows up fastest in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency on the British track also requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, in addition to the five IGCSE subjects.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge and Edexcel subjects most requested from this cluster, with the syllabus codes that determine which papers your child actually sits. Check the code on the school's entry confirmation rather than assuming it from the subject name.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling of C; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A*. Edexcel 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher. Marks go missing in method lines rather than in final answers, and in rounding instructions that were given in the question.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits cause more lost marks than any other topic at this level, usually because a circuit diagram is redrawn wrongly before the physics starts. Cambridge offers a practical test or the Alternative to Practical paper; which one your child sits is a school decision.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables carry disproportionate marks. Students who memorise the test results without the reasoning cannot handle an unfamiliar salt, which is exactly what the Extended papers ask for.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. The commonest self-inflicted loss is answering a cheaper command term than the one printed: describing a graph when the question said explain, which scores nothing in the top band.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences (0653, 0654)
subjects.description: Single or double award routes covering all three sciences in reduced depth. Useful for a student who needs the science requirement without three separate subjects, but the content is not simply a third of each: the selection differs, and revising from a single-science resource leaves gaps.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510/0511)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition reward structure and register control more than vocabulary. Reading responses lose marks for retelling the passage rather than selecting from it. Which syllabus a student is entered for changes the paper entirely.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram-led. A correct demand and supply shift drawn without axis labels or a stated direction of movement scores far below what the student knew. Data response questions reward reading the figures before writing the theory.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Application marks dominate. A textbook definition applied to no named context collects the first mark and stops. Case study technique is teachable in a handful of sessions and is where most of the available improvement sits.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Maths or Maths AA HL. It front-loads calculus and trigonometry, and a student who is still insecure on 0580 algebra will struggle with both at once.

subjects.name: ICT (0417) and Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Both carry practical components with strict file and evidence requirements. Marks are lost in documentation discipline rather than in coding ability: screenshots missing, filenames wrong, evidence not matching the task order.

regions.name: Dubai Harbour
regions.note: The adjoining development around the cruise terminal and marina berths, sharing the same access corridor. Exam-term scheduling here behaves identically to the Beachfront, and cruise-call days add an unpredictable afternoon variable.

regions.note: Older and denser, with tram access and the most road capacity in the cluster. That capacity is fully used between 15:30 and 19:00, which is precisely when a twice-weekly exam-term plan needs to run.

regions.note: Walkable, long-settled, and home to much of the cluster's established freelance tutoring. Families here still hit the same shortage of Extended-tier science specialists in the eight weeks before a series.

modes.description: Two sessions a week across eight to twelve weeks, sequenced backwards from the series rather than forwards from the textbook. Past papers are worked under timed conditions from the first week, and mark-scheme language is taught explicitly, because a student who cannot predict what the examiner wants cannot self-correct between sessions.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Every date that matters sits in front of the exam, not on it. Final entries close months before the first paper. Coursework and practical assessment deadlines are set internally by the school and are often the earliest hard date in the year. The mock window comes before that for most centres, and the tier decision between Core and Extended is taken on evidence the school collects earlier still. A family who starts tutoring after the entry has been filed has lost the ability to change the tier, which is sometimes the single largest available improvement.

The windows themselves are published and should be read from the awarding body rather than restated from a tutoring site. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; the November 2025 series results landed with students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 Edexcel results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge publishes a separate timetable for each of its six administrative zones and warns that the wrong version is the centre's responsibility. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why this page links the live official timetable instead of reprinting dates that can be revised.

Use the table as a planning spine and fill in your own school's internal dates alongside it. The column that matters most is the last one: what a student should already have done by each milestone. A student who reaches the final-entry deadline without a completed timed paper under exam conditions is not ready for a tier decision, whatever the report card says. A student who reaches the mock window without having read a mark scheme is about to receive a grade that reflects technique rather than knowledge, and will be tutored for the wrong problem as a result.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the differences that change your dates
paragraphs: Parents are usually told the two boards are equivalent, which is true of the qualification and misleading about the planning. The syllabus codes differ, the paper structures differ, the practical assessment arrangements differ, and the resit timing differs. A student revising Cambridge Physics 0625 from an Edexcel 4PH1 resource will meet questions in the wrong format, and the formula support available in the exam is not the same either.

The resit route is where the practical difference bites hardest. A Cambridge candidate who underperforms in June looks to November. A Pearson candidate has the same November option, with results arriving in January rather than in August. For a Year 11 student whose post-16 place depends on a grade, the January result changes what can be negotiated with a sixth form and when. That is a conversation to have with the school before the June series, not after the result.

Ask the school three questions and write the answers down: which board and which syllabus code for each subject, which tier the child is entered at, and which practical component applies. Those three facts determine every past paper your child should be working from. Families in this cluster regularly discover in April that half a year of revision has been done from the wrong board's papers, which is a tutoring failure rather than a student failure. Keep the written answers somewhere the whole family can see them, because the person buying past papers online in February is rarely the same person who spoke to the exams officer in September. A single line on the fridge naming the board, the code and the tier for each subject prevents more wasted revision than any study technique.

sections.heading: An eight-week plan that actually changes a grade
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window families in this cluster most often arrive with, usually a fortnight after mock results. It is enough time to move a grade in one or two subjects and not enough to rescue five. The first decision is therefore which subjects to work on, and the honest answer is the ones where the mock script shows marks lost to technique rather than to absent content. A student who understood the topic and wrote a poor answer is a faster repair than a student who never secured the topic.

The structure that works is diagnostic, then narrow, then broad. Weeks one and two are spent on the marked scripts and on one timed paper per subject, with no teaching at all beyond what the errors demand. Weeks three to five take the two or three topics responsible for the largest mark loss and close them properly, with past-paper questions on each topic rather than textbook exercises. Weeks six to eight return to whole papers under timing, marked against the real mark scheme with the student doing the marking first and the tutor auditing it.

The evidence you should be able to see is specific. By the end of week two, a mark breakdown by topic rather than a percentage. By week five, the same topic questions answered correctly without prompting. By week eight, two full papers at or above the target grade boundary with the student able to predict their own mark within a few marks. If those checkpoints are not appearing, the plan is wrong and should be changed rather than extended, which is a conversation we would rather have in week three than in week seven.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Dubai, cheapest first
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market because that is where most families start looking. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that level you are usually buying a university student with good subject knowledge and limited exam-technique experience, which is adequate for homework support in Year 9 and thin for an Extended-tier paper in Year 11. Bestimate's monthly estimate for budget provision at one hour a week is AED 240 to 600.

The next band is qualified subject tutors delivering online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and the broader market sits between AED 150 and 300 an hour. Bestimate puts the monthly figure for this tier at AED 600 to 1,200. Above that are IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 for premium cover. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Two observations worth carrying into any conversation. First, the in-home premium is a travel charge, not a quality charge; the same person online costs less and loses no teaching time to the causeway. Second, three of the seven competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Every figure above was read in October 2026 and is attributed to the source that published it. They describe the market, not IB Gram's rates; ours are agreed after the free trial lesson, once the subject count and session frequency are known.

sections.heading: Why the exam term is the worst time to rely on a tutor crossing the causeway
paragraphs: An exam-term plan needs two sessions a week for eight to twelve weeks. That is sixteen to twenty-four appointments, each of which has to happen. The arithmetic of an in-home arrangement on this peninsula is unkind to that: a tutor travelling to a Beachfront address spends roughly two and a quarter hours to deliver one, needs a resident to clear basement access, and crosses a single road link in the window between 16:00 and 19:00 when the whole cluster is moving. Lose two sessions out of twenty and the plan has lost a week it does not have.

The second problem is the shortlist. Filtering for people who teach Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 or Physics 0625, who are free twice a week at a fixed hour, and who will drive onto the peninsula, leaves very few names in April. Families take whoever is available, which is how a Year 11 student in the eight weeks that matter most ends up with a generalist running through a textbook. The grade does not move and the conclusion drawn is that tutoring does not work.

Online one-to-one removes both constraints at once. The slot can shift by half an hour without anyone losing an evening, it survives a family trip, and the tutor is selected for the syllabus code and tier rather than for proximity. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so the comparison here is between our online sessions and what the local in-home market charges. If a tutor in the room is non-negotiable for your child, the rates in the table above tell you what that costs; for a Year 11 exam block it buys presence and costs reliability.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar puts real constraints on an exam-term plan and almost no competitor page acknowledges them. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the working day shifts, and families reorganise around iftar. For a student entered in a summer series, that often falls inside the most important revision block of the two years. A plan written in January that assumes a steady 17:00 session every week until June will break, and the break will be blamed on the student.

The workable approach is to decide the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than improvising it. Some families move sessions to the post-iftar evening and find concentration is better than it was at 17:00. Others shift to late mornings at the weekend and reduce midweek frequency. Both work; what does not work is cancelling for a month and resuming in the final fortnight. The content closure planned for those weeks has to land somewhere, and the only remaining space is the week before the paper.

The same forward planning applies to the school's own calendar. Mid-term breaks, sports fixtures, Model United Nations trips and the school's mock window all compete for the same hours. Ask for the school calendar in writing at the start of the block, mark the unavailable weeks, and build the plan on the weeks that remain. A ten-week plan on paper is often an eight-week plan in practice, and knowing which eight weeks they are changes what can be promised.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less internally assessed work than the Diploma, but what it does carry is tightly controlled and it falls in the same weeks as the heaviest revision. Practical skills components, ICT and Computer Science practical tasks and any coursework element are assessed under conditions the school sets within the board's rules. Pressure peaks exactly when a family is most likely to ask a tutor for something they should not.

The line is the same at IGCSE as at Diploma level. A tutor may teach the content and the practical technique, explain how a component is marked, review a method, point out that a results table has no units, and give feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor may not complete a task, supply work for submission, or do the write-up. Reproducing or supplying board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads is also off limits; those are referenced and linked to their official source, not handed over as files.

This is worth stating plainly because the market around these queries includes operations that do sell completed work. One page researched for this project sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. The equivalent at IGCSE is a completed practical write-up or coursework piece, and a student who submits one is exposed to a malpractice finding that can void the subject or the series. Our tutors work on the student's own material, use the school's deadlines as the schedule, and will say no to the other request directly.

sections.heading: Starting an exam-term plan from a Beachfront address
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject list with board and syllabus code, the tier for each subject, the mock results with the actual scripts if you have them, and the hours that are genuinely free once the school bus and dinner are accounted for. The scripts matter more than the grades. A grade tells us the student is at a 5; the script tells us whether that is three topics missing or twenty marks of technique, and those require different tutors and different session counts.

We then match a specialist per subject and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, used for diagnosis rather than for selling: by the end of it you should have a written view of where the marks are going and how many sessions the gap realistically needs. If the match is wrong after the trial or after week two, we change the tutor. Persisting with a poor match in an exam term is the most expensive thing a family can do with the weeks it has left.

Finally, the honest limits. Eight weeks will not rescue five subjects, and anyone who says otherwise is selling hours. A niche subject at a specific twice-weekly hour sometimes has no specialist free that week, and when that is the case we say so and offer the realistic alternatives rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. We also cannot promise a grade, and no tutor who has read a mark scheme would. What we can do is make the remaining weeks count and tell you each fortnight whether they are.

process.title: Confirm the board, code and tier
process.description: Ask the school for the syllabus code and tier for every subject and write them down. 0580 Extended and 4MA1 Higher need different past papers, and a term of revision from the wrong board's material is the commonest avoidable waste in an exam year.

process.title: Send the mock scripts, not just the grades
process.description: The marked paper shows whether marks went to missing content or to technique. Those need different work, different tutors and different session counts, and a reported percentage cannot distinguish between them. If the school will release the script, that is the single most useful document you can send us.

process.title: Fix the slots around the real afternoon
process.description: Two sessions a week at 17:00 or later, chosen against the school bus rather than against an ideal timetable. Mark the school's breaks, trips and mock window first so the plan is built on weeks that actually exist, and agree the Ramadan pattern before it arrives.

process.title: Free trial, then a written diagnosis
process.description: One trial lesson per student, no card required. It ends with a view of where the marks are going, which topics are unsecured, and how many sessions the gap needs. You keep that assessment whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Review at the fortnight, not at the end
process.description: Every two weeks the plan is checked against the evidence: topic-level mark breakdowns, then unprompted correct answers, then self-predicted marks on full papers. If the checkpoints are not appearing, the plan changes. Extending a plan that is not working is how eight weeks become four.

whyPoints.title: Sessions survive a Dubai afternoon

whyPoints.description: KHDA inspects Dubai private schools; MoHRE issues the private tuition permit. Neither endorses a tutoring platform, and IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation. Pages that imply otherwise are selling a credential that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor come to our apartment in Emaar Beachfront?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. Independent home tutors in Dubai do visit this peninsula, and market sources quote AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home one-to-one with travel included. In an exam term the trade-off is sharp: a visit buys a person in the room, and costs you the sessions lost to one access road and escorted basement parking across a sixteen-session block.

faqs.question: Which series is a Beachfront candidate entered for, June or November?
faqs.answer: With Cambridge, the June series or the November series. The February/March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so a UAE plan built around a February exam is built on a date the centre will not sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable, and using the wrong zone version is the centre's risk. Ask your exams officer which board, which series and which zone before fixing any revision plan.

faqs.question: If we take the November resit route, when would the result reach us?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November results reach students in January: the November 2025 series results landed with students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. June results come sooner, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge publishes its own release dates per series. Because provisional timetables are revised, check the awarding body's live timetable page rather than any tutoring site, including this one.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough time to change an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: In one or two subjects, often yes. In five, no. The deciding factor is what the mock script shows: marks lost to technique on content the student understood are recoverable in weeks, while three absent topics are not. A workable eight-week block spends two weeks diagnosing, three closing the highest-cost topics, and three on whole papers under timing. If the checkpoints at week two and week five do not appear, the plan should change rather than be extended into the final fortnight.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended, and can we change tier?
faqs.answer: Core and Extended are different paper sets with different grade ceilings: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3 and tops out at C, while Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches A*. Edexcel tiers as Foundation and Higher. The tier is chosen by the school on its own evidence, usually in Year 10, and once final entries are filed it is no longer a live decision. That is why a family who starts tutoring after the entry deadline has lost one of the largest available improvements.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSE passes be enough for Ministry equivalency later on?
faqs.answer: Five. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, is also required. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects as the requirement; the sourced figure is five. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before acting.

faqs.question: Can a tutor working over video prepare my child for the 0625 practical component?
faqs.answer: The practical assessment happens at school, under conditions the school sets within the board's rules. Cambridge sciences are assessed either through a practical test or through the Alternative to Practical paper, and which one applies is the school's decision. Online tutoring works on the examinable part: apparatus choice, sources of error, how to read a results table, why a repeat was needed, and the write-up conventions the mark scheme rewards. A tutor teaches that technique; the tutor does not produce results or write the method up.

faqs.question: What should I pay for IGCSE tutoring in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, from AED 150 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, and AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits with travel included. Monthly estimates for one session a week are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 for specialist exam-year work. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours; our number is set after the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should we revise from Cambridge or Edexcel past papers?
faqs.answer: From whichever board your child is entered with, and only after you have the syllabus code. Cambridge 0625 Physics and Edexcel 4PH1 Physics cover similar content in different paper formats with different formula support, so practising the wrong one trains the wrong technique. Ask the exams officer for the board, the code and the tier for every subject in writing. Families in this cluster regularly discover in April that months of revision used the wrong board's material, and that is a planning failure rather than a student failure.

faqs.question: How should we schedule the revision block once Ramadan starts?
faqs.answer: Decide the pattern before it starts rather than improvising. School hours shorten and the family day reorganises around iftar, so the useful options are a post-iftar evening session, which many students concentrate better in than a 17:00 slot, or late weekend mornings with reduced midweek frequency. What fails is cancelling for the month and resuming in the final fortnight, because the content closure planned for those weeks has nowhere else to go but the week before the paper.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest point to buy a grade. The content is still being taught, so a weekly session closes topics as they land rather than reconstructing them a year later, and the tier decision is still live and can be supported with real evidence. Prevention at one session a week through Year 10 costs less over two years than a twice-weekly rescue block in the spring of Year 11, and it removes the scenario where the tier was set low on thin evidence.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in this cluster struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Extended Maths 0580, Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620, in that order, with electricity, moles and ionic equations accounting for a disproportionate share of lost marks. English First Language causes a different problem: students read well and write answers that retell the passage rather than selecting from it, which is a technique gap rather than an ability gap. Additional Maths 0606 is the subject most often taken by students who are not yet secure on the 0580 algebra underneath it.

faqs.question: Do you keep to our school's deadlines or your own schedule?
faqs.answer: Your school's. The school sets the coursework and practical deadlines, the mock window and the internal reporting cycle, and those are the dates the plan is built around. Send the school calendar at the start of a block so the unavailable weeks are marked before the plan is fixed; a ten-week plan on paper is often eight usable weeks once trips, breaks and mocks are counted. Knowing which eight weeks they are changes what can honestly be promised in them.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not the right fit in week two?
faqs.answer: Say so and we change them. A poor match in an exam term is expensive in a way it is not in Year 9, because there are no spare weeks to absorb it. The signals are specific: the student cannot say what the session was about afterwards, the work between sessions is not being set or checked, or the fortnightly evidence checkpoints are not appearing. We would rather move a tutor in week two than defend a match in week seven when nothing can be rebuilt.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.closingHeading: Tell us the series, and we will work backwards from it

Send the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier, the mock scripts if the school will release them, and the hours that genuinely exist after the bus from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. intro.heading: The number three of six ranking pages refuse to print
paragraphs: Of the most visible providers competing for IGCSE tutoring searches in Dubai, three publish no price at all. One has a frequently asked question titled how much does tutoring cost and declines to answer it. Two more quote in US dollars, which is not a currency an Emaar South household transacts in. A parent trying to work out what this should cost is therefore guessing, and guessing in a market where the published range runs from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour is an expensive position to be in.

So this page prints the numbers. Every band below is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the format stated. None of them is an IB Gram price: our own commercial conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis, not a rate card. What the bands do is let a family in Emaar South see the shape of the market before they ring anybody, which is the position every other page in this cluster leaves them out of.

The second thing this page does is explain what each band buys, because the price ladder does not track quality in any measurable sense. It tracks two things: who is doing the teaching, and whether somebody is driving. An AED 50 hour and an AED 220 hour differ in the first. An AED 220 online hour and an AED 320 in-home hour differ mostly in the second. A parent should know which of those two differences they are paying for, and most rate cards are designed to obscure exactly that.

The third is where the money goes to waste, and this is the part that matters most in Emaar South specifically. Families here are buying tutoring for a Year 10 or Year 11 student with a long daily school journey, often for two or three subjects at once, from a community at the southern edge of the emirate. There are five reliable ways to waste that budget and all five are avoidable with information that costs nothing to obtain.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Emaar South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, which among other things means the travel premium in those published in-home bands is not part of what you pay. We say this plainly rather than leaving it to be discovered, because the honest version of a cost page has to include what is not on offer.

One factual note on the regulatory side. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually, publishes the ratings, and confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and runs no UAE centre. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.programmesIntro: Emaar South households are mostly buying support at one of three stages, and each costs differently because each needs a different amount of it.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: No external examination, so no urgency, and that is precisely why this is the cheapest stage at which to fix something. A gap in algebraic fluency or structured writing addressed in Year 8 costs a term of weekly sessions. The same gap addressed in Year 11 costs an intensive block at a specialist rate and still leaves the student behind on the content arriving at the same time.
programmes.countryNote: Emaar South's age profile skews young because the community is newer, which means a lot of households here are at exactly the stage where the cheap intervention is available. Very few take it, because nothing is visibly wrong yet. The honest observation is that Key Stage 3 money is the best-value tutoring spend in this market and almost nobody spends it.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, externally examined, with a tier decision that caps the achievable grade. This is where most of the money in this market is spent and where most of the waste happens, because families buy hours in several subjects at once without a diagnosis in any of them.
programmes.countryNote: An Emaar South IGCSE candidate is usually sitting the June series with a long daily commute, which limits how many weekly sessions a plan can realistically hold. That constraint is useful: it forces the question of which subjects actually repay tutoring rather than allowing three parallel arrangements that each get a third of the attention.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB alternative for the same age band, marked against four criteria per subject from A to D and converted to a 1-7 grade. It changes the spending logic completely, because the cheapest useful block is a short one teaching the criteria explicitly, which pays into every subject at once rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Emaar South families travel to run the Middle Years Programme rather than IGCSE, so two neighbouring households can be buying very different things. A family comparing what a neighbour pays should first check whether the neighbour's child is even in the same system, because the sensible spend differs substantially.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE route leads, and worth knowing about when budgeting, because tier and award decisions made at sixteen can close options that later cost more to reopen. A student who needs a November resit to satisfy a sixth-form requirement is paying twice for one grade.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 support costs more per hour in the published bands, with Bestimate putting specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month. For an Emaar South family budgeting across both stages, the implication is that money spent correctly at IGCSE reduces what has to be spent later rather than being a separate cost.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Emaar South families most often buy support in, with an honest note on how much tutoring each one repays.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The subject that repays tutoring most reliably, because the weaknesses are specific and diagnosable and the gains show on past papers quickly. Algebraic fluency, ratio and the diagram topics are all improvable in a term. The tier decision is what caps the return, so settle that first.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Same reasoning as Cambridge with one caveat: the question style is heavier on multi-step contextual problems, so a tutor working from Cambridge past papers is teaching correct mathematics towards a paper the student will not sit. Paying a specialist rate for the wrong board is the purest waste available.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Repays tutoring well, and most of the cheap gains are in Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which carries real marks and is almost never drilled. A short technique block is better value here than a term of content sessions for a student who already understands the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and qualitative analysis are procedural, which makes them cheap to fix in a compressed block. Ionic equations unbalanced for charge score nothing and the check takes seconds. Good value per hour provided the diagnosis comes first.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The recall volume means much of the work is note compression, which a student can do alone once shown how. That makes Biology one of the subjects where a short block teaching method, followed by independent work, beats a standing weekly session on value.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the summary question are marked on structure, which is teachable and improves quickly. Where money is wasted here is general reading practice, which feels productive and moves nothing. Target the components, not the subject.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study based with marks for applying a concept to the named business rather than defining it. Analysis and evaluation command words carry the highest tariff and are reliably where candidates stop short. A short block on those two verbs outperforms broad content coverage.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, and an unlabelled axis loses the mark whatever the prose says. Diagram drill and elasticity calculation are short, cheap and high-yield. Reading more of the textbook is neither.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are both procedural and both under-practised, which makes a short block excellent value. The specialist pool is thinner than for the sciences, so booking early matters more than price shopping does here.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: Worth checking before paying for anything, because past papers from the separate sciences are not usable for a combined candidate. A tutor given the wrong route sets content that is not on the syllabus, which is a full term of fees for no gain.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules, and frequently the grade a family is most worried about. The writing component responds fast to a small bank of drilled structures, making it unusually good value per session.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: An extra syllabus some schools offer, covering calculus and further trigonometry beyond 0580. It needs its own slot rather than being folded into a maths hour, which means it is an additional cost rather than a free extension of one, and worth budgeting for separately.

sections.heading: The published Dubai bands, by provider model
paragraphs: Here is the market, with sources. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online and typically delivered by university students or non-specialist tutors. In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors online. TutorChase, a UK agency serving the Gulf, quotes AED 270.

In-home provision sits apart from that ladder rather than above it. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate also places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200-450 or more, which overlaps the agency and premium bands.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 for budget provision, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours. That last pair is the single most informative comparison available: double the money for half the sessions.

The table collects all of it in one place. Read it as the market rather than as a recommendation, and note what it does not contain: an IB Gram price. We do not publish one on this page because our conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis, and because a rate quoted before anybody has looked at a marked script is a number without a question attached to it.

sections.heading: What each band actually buys
paragraphs: The ladder is not a quality scale and treating it as one leads families to overspend at the top and waste money at the bottom. It is two separate variables stacked on top of each other: who is doing the teaching, and whether somebody is driving. Separating them is the single most useful thing a parent can do before making any call.

At the budget end, AED 33-65 an hour buys supervised homework. A university student can keep a Year 10 student working, answer direct questions and check arithmetic. What they cannot usually do is look at a marked 0625 Paper 6 script and identify that the results table headings are losing marks, or that the suggested improvements are addressing the wrong error. That is a specialist diagnosis and it is not in this band, which does not make the band useless. It makes it the wrong purchase for a diagnostic problem.

At AED 150-300 online, a family is buying a trained subject teacher who knows the syllabus, the tier and the mark scheme. This is where the diagnostic capability sits. At AED 180-500 in-home, a family is buying roughly the same teaching plus a car journey, and the difference between the two bands is mostly that journey. At AED 500-650, a family is buying a named individual with a published profile, which is a reputational purchase rather than a measurably different lesson.

The practical consequence for an Emaar South household is to decide which problem is being solved before choosing a band. A student who will not sit down without supervision has a budget-band problem. A student who understands the content and keeps underscoring has a specialist-band problem, and buying budget hours for it is the most expensive thing in this market, because it costs money and a term and ends with the same script.

sections.heading: The five places this money gets wasted
paragraphs: First, and most expensively, buying hours without a diagnosis. A family worried about a grade books a standing weekly session, the tutor arrives with no marked script and starts at the beginning of the syllabus, and six weeks later something feels better and nothing has changed. The fix costs nothing: send a marked mock and ask what the first session will target. If the answer is a topic rather than a component, the diagnosis has not happened.

Second, paying a specialist rate for the wrong board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are separate syllabuses with different paper structures; so are 0625 and 4PH1. A tutor given the wrong one teaches correct material towards a paper the student will not sit. Checking the syllabus code on the timetable takes under a minute and prevents a full term of unusable past papers at full price. The same applies to the separate-sciences and combined-science routes.

Third, paying the travel premium for a lesson made of documents. The working material for a Year 11 candidate is a marked script and a mark scheme, both of which read better shared on a screen than passed across a table, and the in-home premium from an Emaar South address sits at the upper end of the published band because the journey is long. For a seven year old who will not sit at a screen, that premium buys something real. For a Year 11 candidate it buys a car.

Fourth, three parallel subjects at a third of the attention each. A household with a long school run cannot sustain three weekly sessions plus the independent practice that makes them work, and the plan collapses around half term having spent three subjects' worth of fees. Sequencing one subject at a time, preceded by a technique block that pays into all three, costs less and produces more. Fifth, continuing a standing arrangement past the point where the diagnosis says it is done, which is a quiet and very common way to spend several thousand dirhams on reassurance.

sections.heading: Tutoring in the context of the whole education bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest line in a Dubai family's education budget and it is often the only one treated as discretionary. Setting it next to the other costs makes the decisions clearer. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That freeze is the anchor: school fees are flat for the year, which means tutoring is the variable part of the bill.

The wider market context is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment, followed by Indian, US and International Baccalaureate provision, according to the Dubai Media Office summary of the sector published in January 2025. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

For a family in Emaar South the practical reading is that supply is growing and fees are held, which makes the question of how much tutoring to buy a genuine choice rather than a forced one. It also means a school with a weak KHDA inspection rating is not the only option in the way it might have been a few years ago, and a family currently buying heavy tutoring to compensate for a teaching problem has an alternative worth at least considering.

The table puts the pieces side by side. The intention is not to make tutoring look cheap; it is to make the comparison possible. A parent who knows that specialist examination-year support runs at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month on Bestimate's estimates, against a school fee that is held flat for the year, is in a position to decide how many months of it are actually needed rather than committing to two years by default.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects actually repay tutoring
paragraphs: Not every subject returns the same value per hour, and a family with a fixed budget should know which ones do. The reliable rule is that subjects whose losses are procedural repay tutoring quickly, and subjects whose losses are about reading volume or practice time repay it slowly, because the student can do most of that work alone once shown how.

Mathematics repays best. The weaknesses are specific, diagnosable from a script and improvable within a term, and the gains show on past papers fast enough to keep a student engaged. Physics repays well, and much of the cheap gain sits in Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which carries real marks and is essentially never drilled. Chemistry repays well on the procedural topics: mole calculations, qualitative analysis, balancing.

Biology repays more slowly, because the dominant task is compressing a large body of recall into usable notes, and that is work a student does alone. The high-value purchase here is a short block teaching the method, not a standing weekly session. English Language sits in between: the components are teachable and improve fast, while general reading practice feels productive and moves nothing. Target the directed writing and the summary question specifically.

Economics and Business Studies both repay a narrow block aimed at the high-tariff command words and the diagram or calculation work, and repay broad content coverage poorly. Computer Science repays a short procedural block on pseudocode and trace tables. Arabic as a Second Language repays unusually well at the writing component, because a small bank of accurately drilled structures moves the mark quickly. The table sets it out so a budget can be allocated rather than spread.

sections.heading: What to ask before any money changes hands
paragraphs: A short list of questions separates a provider who will help from one who will bill. None of them is awkward and all of them have definite answers, which is itself diagnostic: a provider who cannot answer them in a sentence each is not organised around the student's outcome.

Ask which syllabus code the tutor has taught and at which tier, not whether they teach the subject. Ask what the first session will target, and treat a topic as the wrong answer and a component as the right one. Ask whether the quoted rate includes VAT, because that should be stated clearly rather than discovered later. Ask what happens if the match is wrong in week two, and whether a replacement costs anything. Ask what you receive in writing after each session.

Then ask the practical ones. Is the price per hour or per lesson, and what is the lesson length. What is the cancellation window and what happens if a session is missed on either side. Is there a minimum commitment and, if so, how long. Does the rate change closer to examinations, which some providers do. Does a package expire. For an Emaar South household there is one more: what time slots are actually available, because a provider with nothing after 17:00 cannot serve a community with this school run.

On the regulatory side, ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need it under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor not to hold one. It is a legal licence rather than a quality credential, and anybody claiming to be a KHDA-approved tutor is misdescribing the regulator: KHDA oversees schools and issues Educational Services Permits to training institutes with premises.

sections.heading: Group tuition, siblings and the shared-cost options
paragraphs: Group tuition is cheaper per student and it is a genuinely different product rather than a discounted version of the same one. In a group of two to four, a tutor cannot run a diagnosis from each student's marked script and aim the hour at one person's specific faults. What a group does well is cover content, maintain pace and provide structured practice, which suits a student who is behind on coverage rather than one losing marks to technique.

The honest guidance is therefore to match the format to the problem. A student who has not covered half the syllabus benefits from a group that moves through it. A student who understands the content and keeps scoring below expectation does not, because their problem is individual and invisible in a group setting. Buying group hours for a diagnostic problem saves money per hour and wastes the whole spend.

Siblings are a different case. Two children in the same household rarely need the same tutor, because a Year 8 and a Year 11 candidate are at different points of different syllabuses. What helps is scheduling rather than sharing: two consecutive one-to-one sessions in one evening is ordinary online and impossible for a visiting tutor, who can be in one place at one time. For an Emaar South household with two different school arrival times, that is the difference between one committed evening and two.

One child with two subjects is the most common shared-cost question we get from this community, and the answer is usually to sequence rather than parallelise. Four to six weeks on the weaker subject, then four to six on the other, preceded by a technique block that pays into both, costs less than two standing weekly arrangements and produces a clearer diagnosis in each. That is a cheaper plan that works better, which is an unusual combination and worth taking when it appears.
