sections.heading: What the free trial lesson should produce
paragraphs: A trial lesson that is really a sales call is worse than no trial lesson, because it costs an hour of a student's evening and produces nothing to act on. The test of a genuine one is whether you receive something in writing afterwards that you could hand to a different tutor and have it be useful. If the output is enthusiasm, the trial was a pitch.

What ours produces is a written diagnosis: which component is losing marks, whether the losses are content or technique, what the first four sessions would target and in what order, and an honest view on how much support the student actually needs. Sometimes that answer is four sessions rather than a term, and saying so costs us money and is the correct answer. Sixteen of the published FAQ pages in this market do not mention what a trial produces at all.

The trial is taught by the tutor who would take the block, not by a coordinator, because a trial with somebody else tells you nothing about the match. It is free, it requires no card, and there is no condition attached to it: the word free is used here with nothing hidden behind it, which is worth stating because the alternative practice exists. If the match is wrong, we rematch rather than asking you to persist with it.

For an Emaar South family there is a scheduling point worth making. Book the trial into a slot you would actually use for the term, not an early one that happens to be free, because part of what the trial tests is whether that time of day works for your child after the journey. A trial at 16:15 that goes well and a term at 16:15 that does not is a bad test, and in this community it is the commonest one.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor cost in Emaar South?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. From a community at the southern edge of the emirate the premium sits at the upper end, because the journey is long. Qualified subject tutors online are AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are market figures from the providers named. IB Gram delivers online only and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Why can I not find an IGCSE tutoring price anywhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three of the six most visible providers competing for these searches publish no price at all, and one even includes a frequently asked question about cost and then declines to answer it. Two more quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. The commercial logic is that a number invites comparison and a conversation does not. The practical effect is that a parent trying to budget is guessing across a published range that runs from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, which is an expensive position to be in.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific problem. At AED 33-65 an hour, which is what Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, a family is buying supervised work: somebody who keeps a student at the desk, answers direct questions and checks arithmetic. For a student who will not sit down without company that is the correct purchase and the specialist bands are a waste. What that band generally cannot do is read a marked Paper 6 script and identify that the results table headings are losing marks, which is a different problem entirely.

faqs.question: What is the single most expensive mistake in this market?
faqs.answer: Buying budget hours for a diagnostic problem. A student who understands the content and keeps scoring below expectation is losing marks to something specific: command words, units, pacing, a results table convention. A non-specialist will re-explain the content, which the student already has, and the next script will look the same. The family has then spent a term and a few thousand dirhams and still does not know what the problem is. The cheap hour was the expensive one.

faqs.question: Does paying more for a named tutor get a better lesson?
faqs.answer: It buys a reputational guarantee rather than a measurably different hour. BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors and TutorChase quotes AED 270, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. What the premium reliably provides is a published profile and the confidence that comes with it. What it does not reliably provide is a better diagnosis than a board-experienced subject teacher at AED 200 would give, because the diagnostic work is reading a script against a mark scheme.

faqs.question: How many subjects should an Emaar South family pay for at once?
faqs.answer: One at a time, in most cases. A household with a twenty-five to forty-five minute school run each way cannot sustain three weekly sessions plus the independent practice that makes sessions work, and plans like that generally collapse around half term having spent three subjects' worth of fees. Sequencing works better and costs less: four to six weeks on the weakest subject, then the next, preceded by a technique block on command words and graph work that pays into all of them simultaneously.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether the quoted rate includes VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the answer should be a clear one rather than something to be discovered on an invoice. We are not going to state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general rule on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we are not publishing one. What is reasonable is to ask any provider whether the number they quoted is the number you will pay, and to treat vagueness on that point as information about how the rest of the arrangement will go.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson actually have to produce?
faqs.answer: Something in writing that you could hand to a different tutor and have it be useful: which component is losing marks, whether the losses are content or technique, what the first four sessions would target and in what order, and an honest view of how much support is needed. If the output is enthusiasm, the hour was a sales call. Ours is taught by the tutor who would take the block, requires no card, and sometimes concludes that four sessions will do rather than a term.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up alongside tutoring costs?
faqs.answer: Not for this academic year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That makes school fees the fixed part of an education budget and tutoring the variable part, which is useful framing when deciding how many months of specialist support to commit to rather than defaulting to two years of it.

faqs.question: Does group tuition save money for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: It costs less per hour and it is a different product rather than a discount on the same one. In a group of two to four, a tutor cannot aim the hour at one student's specific faults from their marked script. What a group does well is cover content and maintain pace, which suits a student who is behind on coverage. For a student losing marks to technique it is the wrong purchase, and buying it saves money per hour while wasting the entire spend.

faqs.question: Can my two children share one tutor to reduce the cost?
faqs.answer: Usually not usefully, because a Year 8 and a Year 11 candidate are at different points of different syllabuses and a shared hour serves neither well. What does help an Emaar South household is scheduling rather than sharing: two consecutive one-to-one sessions in one evening, each with its own set work and written note. That commits one evening instead of two. A visiting tutor cannot offer it, because they can be in one place at one time, which is where the in-home premium bites hardest here.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing an Emaar South family can buy first?
faqs.answer: Four diagnostic sessions built on marked scripts, ending in a written priority list. It has a defined end point, it produces something you can act on with or without us, and it frequently reveals that the problem is narrower than feared. The second cheapest is a technique block on command words, graph work and significant figures, because those faults appear across every science and maths subject at once and treating them once is cheaper than treating the symptoms three times.

faqs.question: When should an Emaar South family stop buying sessions?
faqs.answer: When the checkpoint evidence says the diagnosis is closed, which is why blocks should have end points. Compare the timed section at the end of each fortnight against the original written diagnosis: if the losses that were named are no longer appearing, the block has done its work. Continuing by default past that point is the quietest way several thousand dirhams get spent on reassurance rather than on marks, and it is extremely common because nobody involved has an incentive to raise it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Emaar South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. On a cost page that matters because the travel premium in the published in-home bands is not part of what you pay: Bestimate puts in-home at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is included. Independent in-home tutors do operate in Dubai if physical presence is your priority.

faqs.question: Is there a credential I can ask an Emaar South tutor to show?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free to hold so there is no reason a legitimate tutor would not have it. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It is a legal licence rather than a quality credential. Anybody describing themselves as a KHDA-approved tutor is misdescribing the regulator: KHDA oversees schools and issues Educational Services Permits to training institutes with premises.

faqs.question: What should I ask about cancellation and minimum commitments?
faqs.answer: Whether the price is per hour or per lesson and what the lesson length is. What the cancellation window is and what happens if a session is missed on either side. Whether there is a minimum commitment and how long it runs. Whether the rate changes closer to examinations, because some providers raise it. Whether a package expires. For an Emaar South household add one more: which weekday slots exist after 17:00, because a provider with nothing late cannot serve this school run.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingHeading: Send a script, get a diagnosis, then talk about money
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emaar-south.closingBody: If you are pricing an IGCSE home tutor in Emaar South, the published market runs from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour and the band you need depends entirely on what is actually wrong. Send the syllabus code, the tier, the entry route and a recent marked script. The free trial lesson is taught by the tutor who would take the block, requires no card, and returns a written diagnosis you could hand to anybody. Sometimes it says four sessions rather than a term. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects to families across Emirates Living over live video. Before anything else, ask each one which board and syllabus code they have taught to examination. The answer separates a tutor who can work with your child's paper from one who knows the subject in general.

intro.heading: The comparison Emirates Living families actually run, and where it lands
paragraphs: A family in Emirates Hills weighing up IGCSE support almost always runs a comparison first, and it is rarely the comparison the search results expect. It is not agency against marketplace. It is this community against the one next door. A neighbour in The Meadows found someone good. A colleague in The Springs pays less. Somebody in The Greens says the apartment makes it difficult. Somebody in Jumeirah Park drives to a centre in Al Barsha. The question underneath all of it is whether where you live changes the answer.

It does change some things, and this page sets out exactly which. Housing type changes where a child can actually work without interruption. Distance to the school cluster changes when an afternoon session can start. The mix of schools nearby changes which examination board your child is most likely sitting, and therefore which specification a tutor needs to know. Local tutor density changes how many informal offers appear in a community group chat. Those are real differences and they are worth mapping.

What it does not change is the thing that decides whether IGCSE tutoring works. IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a set of specifications published by different boards, each with its own code, its own paper structure and its own practical arrangements. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 are different courses that happen to share a name in conversation. A tutor who knows one and assumes the other wastes your money in exactly the same way whether they do it in a villa in Emirates Hills or over video to an apartment in The Views.

So the comparison keeps landing in the same place, and the reason is arithmetic rather than preference. The pool of tutors who have taught a specific syllabus code to examination is a national or international pool, not a neighbourhood one. Restrict it to people who can reach a gated community set around a golf course before six in the evening and the pool becomes very small. Restrict it to people who can also teach the exact specification and it can empty entirely. Removing the travel requirement is what makes the match possible, which is why IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

The phrase at the top of this page is the one parents type, and it is used honestly. What follows is the comparison in full: the six communities and what each does to the practicalities, the board-by-board differences that actually matter, the published dirham rates and why geography does not move them, how many subjects the UAE equivalency rule counts, how practical science works when lessons are online, and the permit question, whose answer is identical in every community on the list.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.programmesIntro: Before the comparison, it is worth being clear about what sits either side of IGCSE in this part of Dubai, because the next step shapes what the two years before sixteen should be building towards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses in individual subjects, each with its own specification and syllabus code, ending in terminal written examinations. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for candidates in the UAE, and the extra February sitting it also operates is offered to India only, so it is not a route from Dubai; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Several subjects are tiered, which sets a grade ceiling at entry.
programmes.countryNote: Around Emirates Living both boards are represented, sometimes within one school and occasionally within one department. Families comparing notes between communities often discover their children are sitting different specifications in the same subject, which is why a recommendation that worked for a neighbour may not transfer. Ask your school's examinations officer for the board and code in writing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Standard or Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment combines external examinations with internally assessed components, and subject choice at sixteen is constrained by what was studied and achieved at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools on the Emirates Living edge run the Diploma, which makes it the common next step for families in these communities. The IGCSE subjects that matter most for that route are mathematics and the sciences, where the step up in algebraic demand is the steepest. A student planning Higher Level sciences should be sitting Extended rather than Core.

programmes.name: A Level and International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth over two years, with AS and A2 structures depending on the board and school. Cambridge International A Levels and Pearson Edexcel International A Levels both run in the UAE, and entry requirements are usually expressed as specific IGCSE grades in the subject.
programmes.countryNote: The British-curriculum schools nearer The Springs and Jumeirah Park more often continue to A Level than to the Diploma. If that is the likely route, the IGCSE subject grades matter directly as entry conditions, so the comparison between Core and Extended entry in a subject your child wants to continue is worth having early.

programmes.name: The Middle Years Programme alternative
programmes.description: Some schools on this side of Dubai run the IB Middle Years Programme instead of IGCSE for the two years before sixteen, assessing against four criteria per subject rather than against a specification with terminal papers. A few run both, with IGCSE entries alongside the Middle Years framework.
programmes.countryNote: This is the sharpest difference between neighbouring communities in Emirates Living, because two children a few minutes apart can be assessed in completely different ways at fifteen. A tutor who is strong on criterion language is not automatically the right person for a syllabus code, and the reverse is equally true.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.subjectsIntro: The list below names the IGCSE subjects Emirates Living families ask about most, with the board detail that actually changes the teaching. Use it to give a tutor a code rather than a subject name, because the code is what determines which papers your child will sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Cambridge also offers International Mathematics 0607 and Additional Mathematics 0606. The tier decision sets a ceiling at entry, so the first question for any maths tutor is which tier your child is entered for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Both cover forces, energy, waves, electricity and nuclear physics, and they differ in emphasis and in how practical skills are assessed. Cambridge candidates typically sit an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test; Pearson assesses practical understanding within the written papers. Electricity is the topic most often named in requests from this part of Dubai.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, rates, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. The reliable losses are mole arithmetic under pressure and the qualitative analysis observations, which students revise last. Specification wording differs enough between the two boards that practising the wrong board's past papers wastes effort.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics, ecology and human physiology. Marks are lost to imprecision rather than ignorance: naming a process without naming the structure, or describing where the question says explain. Command-term work against the correct board's mark schemes moves marks faster than rereading content.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and double award sciences
subjects.description: Combined routes giving one or two grades across all three sciences rather than three separate ones. Content is reduced in breadth rather than in difficulty, and families frequently do not know which route their child is on. It matters, because the papers and the available grades differ from the separate sciences.

subjects.name: English as a First Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing, composition and, in literature, set texts with timed essays. Strong readers lose marks on structure and on answering the question asked rather than the one they prepared. This is one of the few subjects where tutoring transfers cleanly between boards, because the underlying skills are the same.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking components with a tightly specified task format. Students who speak fluent English still lose marks by not matching the register, audience and purpose named in the prompt. Format training is quick and produces a disproportionate improvement, which makes it good value in a short block.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study based papers where application to the named business or economy carries the marks. Generic answers that would fit any company score poorly however accurate the theory. Evaluation that reaches a judgement rather than listing both sides is the specific skill, and it is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 first language and 0544 foreign language
subjects.description: Two quite different qualifications, and the placement is the school's decision. Separately, Arabic is also a mandatory subject in Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, taught under KHDA requirements, so a child may be sitting an IGCSE Arabic paper and following a mandatory Arabic programme at once.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Algorithms, programming, data representation and systems, with practical components in some specifications. The two boards differ substantially here in both content and assessment, more than in most subjects, so the code genuinely determines what a tutor should be teaching.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case studies, source work and structured extended answers. In history the discriminating skill is source evaluation; in geography it is applying a named case study precisely rather than generally. Both reward a clear answer structure, and both punish students who write everything they know about the topic.

sections.heading: Six communities compared on what actually affects IGCSE support
paragraphs: Run the comparison on the four things that genuinely differ and it becomes short. Housing type, which decides whether a child has a door that closes. Distance and approach to the school cluster, which decides when an afternoon session can start. The board mix in the nearby schools, which decides which specification is most likely. And local tutor density, which decides how many informal offers circulate in a community group.

Emirates Hills scores well on space and poorly on access. A large villa usually has a room that can be a study room, which removes a problem that apartment families have to solve. The gated approach and the community road network mean a visiting tutor's door-to-door time is longer than the map suggests, and gate queues at the end of the school day are not predictable. The Meadows and The Lakes sit close to the same schools with slightly shorter approaches. The Springs has a different school mix, weighted more towards British-curriculum places.

The Greens and The Views invert the picture. Access is easier and the study space is harder: a shared bedroom, a sibling at home and an open-plan living area all affect whether an hour is usable. The single most valuable thing an apartment family can do before booking anything is establish where the session will happen and who else will be in the room, because a tutor cannot fix an interrupted hour. Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village have the widest board mix and the most local informal offers, which is a mixed blessing covered later on this page.

Put them side by side and the pattern is clear. The practicalities differ by community and all of them are solvable. The thing that is not solvable by moving house is whether a tutor knows the specification. That is why the comparison lands in the same place from every address in the table below.

sections.heading: Why the comparison keeps producing the same answer
paragraphs: Having mapped the differences, it is worth being explicit about why they do not change the conclusion. The reason is that the thing you are shopping for is not a person who lives nearby. It is a person who has taught your child's exact specification to examination and can therefore read a marked paper and say which mark scheme line was missed.

That pool is organised by syllabus code, not by geography. Think about how small it becomes when you add conditions. Start with tutors who have taught Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 to examination, which is already a specialist subset. Add those available at a workable evening hour in Gulf Standard Time. Add those willing and able to travel into a gated villa community and still teach a useful hour, which means leaving wherever they are at least forty minutes early and returning in the dark. The last condition is the one that empties the list.

Remove that condition and the first two are satisfiable in a normal week. This is not a clever argument for a format we happen to sell; it is the reason the format exists. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, because the honest version of a visiting service in this market would be a promise to send whoever is nearby rather than whoever knows the specification. Visiting tuition is a service we run only in India, where the density and the geography are different.

There is a second, smaller reason the answer is the same in every community, and it is about what IGCSE work actually looks like. Most of it is paper: a past question, a mark scheme, a marked script, a diagram. Photographed and annotated on a shared screen, that work is at least as effective as it is across a kitchen table, and it leaves a saved record the student can reuse. The exception is practical science, which belongs in the school laboratory and is addressed later on this page.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Here is the detail that makes the specification question concrete, and it is the single most useful thing on this page for a family in any of these communities. Two children can both be sitting IGCSE Physics and be sitting different courses, with different codes, different paper structures and different practical arrangements. A tutor who assumes the wrong one will set the wrong past papers for a year.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Its Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and those are Primary and Lower Secondary tests rather than an IGCSE sitting; the extra February window some sources mention is offered to India only, so a candidate in Emirates Hills has June and November and nothing else. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The practical science arrangements differ most and matter most to parents. Cambridge science candidates typically meet practical skills through an alternative-to-practical written paper or a practical test, depending on the school's entry. Pearson assesses practical understanding within the written papers. Either way, the examined skill is interpreting and evaluating experiments rather than performing them under examination conditions, which is why online tuition can prepare it properly.

Tiering is the other place the boards diverge in wording. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics splits into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Several science specifications offer Core and Extended routes, and the co-ordinated and double award options give one or two grades across all three sciences rather than three separate grades. Each of those decisions carries a grade ceiling, and each is made by the school, usually earlier than families expect. Ask the examinations officer for the board, the code and the tier in writing, and keep the reply.

sections.heading: The villa and the apartment: solving the study space before the first lesson
paragraphs: This is the one part of the comparison where the community genuinely decides the outcome, and it gets almost no attention in tutoring advice. An hour of IGCSE work needs a surface, a closing door, a charger and nobody else in the room. In an Emirates Hills or Meadows villa that is usually available and the family has already solved it without thinking about it. In an apartment in The Greens or The Views it has to be decided.

The specific failure is interruption rather than noise. A tutor can work through background sound. What cannot be worked through is a student who stops mid-explanation four times an hour, because the thread of a multi-step problem does not survive that. If the only workable space is a shared living area, the honest fix is to move the session to a time when the room is empty, which often means earlier than the family would prefer or at a weekend.

A second apartment-specific point concerns siblings. Two children in a two-bedroom apartment cannot both have a lesson at the same time, so the slots have to be staggered, and staggering is easier when both sessions are online and neither depends on a visitor's route between two addresses. Families with children on different boards, which is common across every community in this comparison, need two specialists anyway, so staggering is the only arrangement that works.

Villa households have a different problem, which is that space makes it easy to be casual. A session at the kitchen island with a phone face-up and a sibling passing through is not better than an apartment session behind a closed door. The checkable standard is the same in every community: a surface, a door, no phone, and nobody else in the room for the hour. Set that up before the free trial so that the trial tests the tutor rather than the room.

sections.heading: Published rates are the same in every community; only the format changes
paragraphs: Families comparing notes between communities often conclude that one neighbourhood pays more than another. The published figures do not support that. Dubai providers publish one rate card for the emirate, and what differs between The Greens and Emirates Hills is not the price of an hour but which formats are practical to buy. Here are the figures, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026.

Cheapest first, because that is where most comparisons start. Tutopiya publishes from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both buying a general tutor rather than a specification specialist. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's premium named tutors at AED 650. Visiting tuition is published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by home tutors generally, with travel inside the figure.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Packages seen in the market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visiting sessions. None of these is an IB Gram price list; our own rate depends on the subject, the level and what the brief needs, and the free trial is how you judge an hour before paying for one.

What does vary by community is which of those rows is realistically available. In a gated villa community the visiting option exists at the published premium but with a narrow choice of tutor. In an apartment community a tuition centre group class in Al Barsha is an easier drive, which lowers the per-student cost and adds a journey. Online is identical from every address on the list, at the same rate, with the same choice of specialist, which is the practical reason the comparison keeps collapsing to one answer.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects, and the equivalency count that decides it
paragraphs: Across every community in this comparison, the question of how many subjects a child should take comes up in Year 9 and is usually answered by the school. There is a published rule worth knowing before that conversation, because it sets a floor that has nothing to do with school advice.

For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause is the one families miss, because it means a child taking Arabic and Islamic education plus four others does not meet the count.

It is worth saying that at least one ranking competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. That is not what the published requirement says. The published rule is five accredited subjects at E or grade 3 excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and a parent who plans around six because a tutoring website said so is planning around an error. Verify it on the Ministry's own channel before making a subject decision.

The American track has separate thresholds: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points figure appears in the source we have read, so this page publishes none. Equivalency is a Ministry process that IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee, and no tutoring is required for it; we describe it and point you to the official channel.

sections.heading: Practical science when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the objection that comes up in every community on the list and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. If lessons are delivered over video, what happens to the practical side of IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics? The answer has two parts, and the first is about what the examination actually assesses.

Cambridge science candidates typically meet practical skills through an alternative-to-practical written paper or a practical test, depending on the school's entry, and Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. In both cases the examined skill is reading a method, identifying variables, spotting a flaw, reading a scale correctly, processing results and evaluating a procedure. None of that requires the student to hold apparatus during the paper. It requires them to have thought carefully about apparatus, which is a trainable analytical skill.

So an online session prepares the examined component well: a method on screen, the student annotating what is wrong with it, a results table processed in a spreadsheet, a graph drawn and criticised, a mark scheme checked line by line. What online tuition does not and should not replace is the hands-on laboratory work the school provides, which exists for the learning rather than for the paper. A tutor who implies otherwise is overselling, and a tutor who says the laboratory is the school's job is telling you the truth.

One related boundary. We do not supply past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables, because those are the boards' copyright material. A tutor should reference them and link to the official source, which also keeps you on the current version rather than a copy of uncertain date. Anyone offering to sell you a bundle of board material is selling something they do not have the right to distribute.

sections.heading: The permit question, whose answer is the same in every community
paragraphs: Informal local arrangements are more common in some of these communities than others, and the question that follows is identical everywhere. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible categories are broad, which is why most people offering tutoring can hold one: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the government's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so any page quoting you a figure is quoting something unverified. Ask the question before money changes hands, in every community, at every price point. There is a second rule worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school.

A separate matter is an operation with premises and staff, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We are an independent tutor-matching platform, and that is a more useful thing to know than a badge nobody can check.

sections.heading: Starting, from whichever side of the comparison you are on
paragraphs: The first step is the same from every address on this page and it is not about tutoring. Get three facts from the school in writing: the board, the syllabus code and the tier or route for each subject you are considering support in. Without those three, any tutor is guessing, and a guess in this market means a year of practice on the wrong board's past papers.

Then send a brief that a specialist can act on: the subject, the board and code, the year group, the school, the topic or paper where marks are going, and two windows that work in your week. Add photographs of the last two marked assessments with the teacher's annotations visible. A tutor who reads those before the trial can name the problem in the first ten minutes, which is the whole point of sending them.

The free trial lesson then runs in full, online, with no payment and no card details. Use it to test two things. Does the tutor work from your child's own marked script and the correct board's mark scheme, or from generic material? And does your child speak during the hour? Ask the tutor to state which paper or topic they would target first and why. A specification specialist answers that immediately; a general tutor talks about confidence.

Finally, the honest limit. If no specialist for your exact code is free in your window, we say so and offer an alternative time, a date, or a tutor from the other board who will state plainly what they will have to check. We will not put a general tutor into a specification brief, because that is the one thing this whole comparison was designed to avoid. Review the arrangement every four to six weeks against marked work rather than against how the sessions felt, and change it when the evidence says to.

faqs.question: Does living in Emirates Hills rather than The Greens change what IGCSE support we should buy?
faqs.answer: It changes the practicalities and not the conclusion. A villa usually solves the study space without anyone thinking about it, while an apartment family has to decide where the session happens and who else will be in the room. Access works the other way: the gated approach into Emirates Hills makes a visiting tutor's door-to-door time longer than the distance suggests. Neither difference touches the thing that decides whether tutoring works, which is whether the tutor knows your child's exact specification.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's school uses for each subject?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer or the subject teacher for three facts in writing, per subject: the board, the syllabus code and the tier or route. Schools provide this readily and it is the most valuable information you can gather before spending anything. Two children in neighbouring villas in these communities often sit different specifications in the same subject, and a tutor working from the wrong code will set the wrong past papers for a year without either of you noticing until a mock.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE interchangeable?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate specifications with separate codes, different paper structures and different practical arrangements. Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Pearson is 4PH1; chemistry is 0620 against 4CH1; mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers against 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. Content overlaps substantially, which is why the difference is easy to miss, but specification wording, emphasis and assessment differ enough that practising the wrong board's papers wastes effort. Confirm the current specification on the board's own site.

faqs.question: My neighbour's tutor was excellent. Why might that not transfer to us?
faqs.answer: Most often because the children are on different specifications or different frameworks entirely. Around Emirates Living some schools run Cambridge, some run Pearson, some run the IB Middle Years Programme and a few run combinations, so a tutor who was ideal for a neighbour may be learning your child's course from scratch. The recommendation is still worth having; just check the board and code match before assuming it carries over, and ask the tutor directly which specifications they have taught to examination.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Emirates Hills or The Meadows?
faqs.answer: IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. The market does offer visiting tutors at published rates of AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by home tutors generally, with travel inside the figure. The practical cost is not the premium but the narrowing of choice: only tutors who can complete the journey into a gated community and still teach a useful hour are available to you.

faqs.question: How do science practicals work if IGCSE lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The examined skill is analytical rather than manual. Cambridge candidates typically meet practical work through an alternative-to-practical written paper or a practical test depending on the school's entry, and Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Either way the paper asks the student to read a method, identify variables, spot flaws, process results and evaluate a procedure, all of which prepare well on a shared screen with a spreadsheet and a mark scheme. The hands-on laboratory work remains the school's job and should.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child actually need?
faqs.answer: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking competitor page states six subjects are required, which is not what the published requirement says. Verify it on the Ministry's own channel before deciding.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Al Barsha better value than online one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student and reasonable for content and pace, which is a real benefit. What it cannot do is diagnose your child's marked paper, because eight students cannot each have their script read inside an hour. Add the evening car journey in both directions from Emirates Living, which is easier from the apartment communities than from the villas. A common compromise is group classes for content plus a short private block on the one or two components actually losing marks.

faqs.question: Someone in our community offers IGCSE tutoring cheaply. What should I check?
faqs.answer: Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Because it is free and takes two working days through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one, and individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Also ask which board and code they have taught, because a low rate for the wrong specification is not a saving.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in our household?
faqs.answer: Only if the specifications genuinely match, which in these communities they often do not. Siblings here are frequently on different boards, or one is on a Cambridge specification while the other is assessed against Middle Years criteria. Separate specialists in staggered slots works better and also solves the single-quiet-room problem in an apartment. Where one tutor can honestly cover both, we will say so; where they cannot, combining the two is a saving that costs a grade.

faqs.question: What should an apartment family in The Views sort out before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: The room. An hour needs a surface, a closing door, a charger and nobody else present. The failure mode is interruption rather than noise: a tutor can work through background sound, but a multi-step problem does not survive a student stopping four times an hour. If the only workable space is a shared living area, move the session to a time when the room is empty, which often means earlier in the evening or a weekend morning. Sort this before the trial so the trial tests the tutor.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutoring rates differ between Emirates Hills and the cheaper communities nearby?
faqs.answer: The published rates do not. Dubai providers publish one rate card for the emirate: Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table placing specialist IGCSE and IB work at AED 200 to 450 and above, with visiting tuition at AED 180 to 500. Those were read in October 2026 and belong to those providers. What varies by community is which of those formats is practical to buy, not the hourly figure.

faqs.question: My child changed school mid-course and the board changed too. What now?
faqs.answer: A short bridging block, not a restart. The first job is a written list of what the new specification expects that the old one did not cover, which a tutor who knows both codes can produce in a session. Then the paper format differences, the command-term differences and the mark-scheme conventions, which are often the larger shock. This happens regularly across these communities and it is a bounded piece of work, usually a handful of sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: Will you supply past papers and mark schemes for our board?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring service should. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are the examination boards' copyright material, and distributing them is not something a tutor has the right to do. A tutor should reference them and link to the official page on the board's own site, which has the additional benefit of keeping you on the current version rather than a copy of unknown date. Anyone selling a bundle of board material is selling what they do not own.

faqs.question: When does the Core or Extended decision stop being reversible?
faqs.answer: That depends on your school rather than on the board, which is why it has to be asked locally. Tier entry is made by the school and submitted with the examination entry, and the practical deadline is therefore the entry deadline rather than the examination. Published board calendars show how early that sits: the Pearson International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry deadline for it had passed well before the autumn term's mock marks existed. Cambridge works the same way, with June entries closing in the spring, several months ahead of the first paper. Ask your examinations officer for your own entry date and the school's internal cut-off for tier changes.

faqs.question: How do we start if we are in The Springs rather than Emirates Hills?
faqs.answer: Identically, because the process is address-independent. Get the board, code and tier in writing from the school. Decide where the session will happen. Send the subject, code, year group, school, the paper or topic where marks are going, and two realistic windows, with photographs of the last two marked assessments attached. We match a specialist for that specification and the trial lesson runs in full online with no payment and no card details taken.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-hills.closingBody: If you have been comparing an IGCSE home tutor in Emirates Hills with what families in The Meadows, The Springs or The Greens are doing, the comparison is worth running and it lands in one place. The practicalities differ by community and all of them are fixable; what no address can fix is whether the tutor knows your child's specification. So get the board, the code and the tier from the school, send them with the marked work and two realistic windows, and we will match a specialist for that exact paper. The first lesson is free, and tuition is delivered one to one over live video.

intro.heading: Four systems on four adjacent streets, and only one set of exams
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community hold schools running UK, Indian, American, SABIS and IB routes within a short drive of each other. KHDA reported 17 different curricula across the emirate's 227 private schools in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. In this particular catchment, that diversity is not an abstraction: it is the street.

The practical consequence is that comparing notes with a neighbour here is often useless and occasionally harmful. A parent whose child sits IGCSE at 16 hears from a neighbour that their child has no external exams that year, and concludes the school is softer or harder than it is. A CBSE family and an IGCSE family discuss "the boards" and mean two different things. An American-curriculum family talks about GPA, which does not exist in the IGCSE world at all.

So this page starts by setting the four routes side by side at the 14 to 16 stage, because a parent who understands what their child's system actually assesses can then judge a tutor, a quote and a school report sensibly. It then moves to the IGCSE detail: the two boards, the grade scales, the tiering, the exam series, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rules that care about how many certificates a student ends up with.

There is a third reason this matters here specifically. Children in this catchment move between systems more often than the Dubai average, because the schools sit so close together that a change of school does not require a change of home. A student who spent Years 7 to 9 in the Middle Years Programme and then transfers into an IGCSE Year 10 has strong independent-work habits and almost no experience of writing against a clock. One arriving from a CBSE school has the opposite profile: well drilled on procedure, under-practised at the evaluation questions that carry the top marks. Those are different first months, and a tutor who does not ask where the student came from will spend both of them on the wrong thing.

The second comparison is geographic and shorter. Green Community sits inside Dubai Investments Park, low-rise and walkable, with schools close by. The streets around it - Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai South, Emaar South - share the school catchment and differ mainly in how far a tutor would have to drive. For in-home tutoring that difference is the whole of the price variation. For online tutoring it does not exist.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We say that near the top rather than at the bottom of a terms page, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

What follows: the four-route comparison, grade scales explained, the board differences, the AED bands with their sources and what you can actually verify, the calendar counted backwards, and the equivalency arithmetic. Read it with your child's exam entry statement to hand.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Separate subject qualifications with four-digit codes such as Mathematics 0580, Chemistry 0620 and English as a First Language 0500, each examined externally at the end of the course. programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1 and English Language A 4EA1, graded 9-1, with Foundation and Higher tiers in the tiered subjects. Examined in a May/June window and a November window, with provisional timetables published ahead of each series and then revised.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria out of eight, with no external papers for most students, and the Personal Project in MYP 5. The record of these years is a sequence of criterion judgements rather than examination grades, and some schools offer optional on-screen eAssessments.

An MYP student at 16 has no external subject certificates unless the school entered them for eAssessments, and that changes the Ministry of Education equivalency conversation entirely.

programmes.name: CBSE and American routes
programmes.description: CBSE assesses through school and board examinations with a Class 10 board result; American-curriculum schools typically report a grade point average across courses, with standardised tests such as the SAT taken later. Neither produces subject certificates of the IGCSE kind at 16.
programmes.countryNote: Indian-curriculum schools account for 26% of Dubai private enrolment and are well represented in this catchment. The Ministry of Education publishes different equivalency requirements by track - the American track requires specified SAT, IELTS or TOEFL evidence - so the route determines the paperwork later as well as the assessment now.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-green-communit.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Green Community families ask about most, with the part of each specification where marks are typically lost in this catchment.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3 and Extended sits Papers 2 and 4; Edexcel runs two equally weighted papers across tiers. Marks go on unwritten method lines and on rounding applied before the final step.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Reading passages and directed writing. The audience and form specified in the question carry marks, so a strong piece in the wrong register scores below a competent one in the right register.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an assessed speaking component, very common in a catchment with this many home languages. Writing marks rise fastest with paragraph planning rather than vocabulary lists.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry first, organic second. The practical component rewards precision about apparatus and about why a step controls a variable, which is examined more explicitly than it is taught.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits dominates the weakness list, followed by moments and pressure. Students who recognise a relationship but cannot transpose it quickly lose the back half of multi-part questions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. Six-mark answers written as unlinked lists cap the mark regardless of knowledge, because the question wanted a connected account.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy in Economics, case-study discipline in Business Studies. The highest-tariff questions want evaluation, and listing advantages against disadvantages without a judgement caps the answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation, networks and the practical ICT tasks. Confident coders still lose theory marks on binary and hexadecimal conversion, which is examined in prose rather than in code.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities dominate, and local tutor supply for these codes is the thinnest in the catchment.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA mandating separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. Identify the stream before the first lesson.

sections.heading: What each of the four routes is actually assessing at 16
paragraphs: IGCSE assesses subject knowledge and technique through external papers sat at the end of the course, producing one certificate per subject. That is the whole model: everything rests on performance in a sitting, with limited coursework, and the grade is a judgement on papers rather than on a year's classwork. Its strength is portability and its weakness is that a bad fortnight is expensive.

The IB Middle Years Programme assesses against four lettered criteria per subject, each out of eight, judged on work produced through the year rather than in an examination hall. Most MYP students sit no external papers at 16 at all. That is a genuine strength for independent and reflective work and a genuine gap in examination stamina, and it means an MYP student at 16 has no subject certificates unless the school entered them for optional eAssessments.

CBSE assesses through a combination of school assessment and board examinations with a Class 10 result, and it is content-dense with a strong emphasis on accurate procedural work. American-curriculum schools report a grade point average built from course grades across the year, with standardised testing coming later. Neither produces IGCSE-style subject certificates at 16.

Set against each other, the differences explain most of the confusion in this catchment. A parent whose MYP child has no exams is not in a softer school; they are in a different assessment model. A CBSE student arriving into IGCSE Year 11 is usually strong on procedure and under-practised at evaluation questions. And a tutor needs to know which system is in play before anything else is discussed.

sections.heading: Grade 9-1, A* to G, and why neither is a percentage
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects now report on a 9 to 1 scale, with some still using A* to G depending on the subject and the centre's choice. Parents who grew up with letters misread the numbers in both directions. A 7 sounds worse than an A and is broadly comparable. A 4 sounds like a comfortable pass and sits at the lower edge of what many sixth forms accept for a subject the student intends to continue.

Neither scale is a percentage, and this is the part that matters for tutoring decisions. Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked, so that standards remain comparable between sittings, which means the same raw mark can fall either side of a boundary in different years. Anyone converting a past-paper score into a confident grade prediction is guessing, and we do not publish or distribute boundary tables because they are the boards' copyright material.

The scale also does not translate into a grade point average. Families moving between an American-curriculum school and an IGCSE school in this catchment sometimes try to map one onto the other and reach conclusions that do not hold. The sensible approach is to read the sixth form's own stated entry requirement in the currency it uses, rather than converting.

What is actually useful from a marked paper is not a predicted grade but a classification of the losses. Marks lost to habits - unwritten method, early rounding, command terms answered too shallowly, questions abandoned after the first part - are recoverable in weeks. Marks lost to genuinely unmet content need a term. Those two have different prognoses and different costs, and an hour of external marking separates them.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: subject availability and tiering
paragraphs: Families in this catchment often discover their child's board only when asked. Both Cambridge and Pearson award International GCSEs, both are accepted by UAE and overseas universities, and schools sometimes enter different subjects with different boards within one timetable. The code on the exam entry statement is the only reliable answer.

The structural difference is how candidates are divided. Cambridge uses Core and Extended routes in most subjects, with Core candidates sitting one pair of papers and Extended candidates another, and Core capping the attainable grade. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in its tiered subjects, with Mathematics A 4MA1 running two papers of equal weight rather than a short-and-long pair.

Subject availability differs too, and that occasionally decides a school's choice rather than any pedagogical preference. Cambridge offers English as a Second Language under 0510 and 0511, which matters in a catchment with this range of home languages, while some Pearson subject offerings suit schools running a particular progression into A Level. For a tutor the consequence is simple: the past-paper diet and the topic emphasis differ, and preparing a student on the wrong specification wastes weeks.

The administrative differences are worth equal attention. Cambridge's six administrative zones determine which timetable applies, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Pearson revises provisional timetables before each series. In both cases the live official PDF is the only thing to plan from, including in preference to this page.

sections.heading: The in-home premium between Green Community and Dubai South
paragraphs: The geographic comparison is short because the answer is simple. Green Community has a reasonable in-home tutoring supply by the standards of this cluster, because it sits inside Dubai Investments Park where several schools and therefore several teachers already are. Al Furjan is similar or slightly better, helped by the metro. Dubai South and Emaar South are poorly served, and Jebel Ali Village sits in between with port-road traffic deterring evening bookings.

That variation shows up as price and as availability. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per hour with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and the drive sits inside those numbers. A tutor who will take a Green Community booking at 5pm may decline the same booking in Emaar South, or offer only a 6.30pm slot, or charge more for the same hour of teaching.

What that pattern does not vary with is the quality of teaching or the qualification being sat. The same Cambridge 0580 paper is marked by the same examiners to the same scheme regardless of which of these communities the candidate lives in. So the honest reading of a higher quote from a more distant community is that you are buying a journey, not better preparation.

Once delivery is online, every community in this catchment gets the same pool at the same hour. For a common subject like Mathematics the practical difference is modest, since local supply exists. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, a first-language Arabic stream or an assessed speaking component, it is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs here, and the five things you can verify
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent tutors to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages seen include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Price is the easiest thing to compare and the least informative, which is why it is worth listing what can actually be checked. First, the MoHRE private tuition work permit: ask whether the tutor holds it, since the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years and there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be without one. Second, the syllabus code: ask which they have taught and ask them to name the papers in it.

Third, the marking method: is work marked against the official scheme, or by impression? Fourth, the replacement policy: what happens if the match is wrong, which is the likeliest failure and usually a matter of pace rather than competence. Fifth, the written record: is there a note after each session, so a parent can see what was covered without relying on a teenager's summary.

None of the AED figures above are IB Gram prices and this page carries no rate card, because the fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands are published so a quote can be judged. Three of the pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and one carries an FAQ asking what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it.

sections.heading: The series calendar counted backwards, and the resit question
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is handing them another country's dates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

Counting backwards keeps a plan honest. Final entries close months before the papers, which is when route or tier is fixed. Mocks sit roughly a term ahead and exist to produce data rather than a verdict. A timed-paper cycle needs the final eight to ten weeks, which implies the syllabus has already been covered once. Most families enquire after the mocks, by which point the content window has closed and the honest plan is habit repair.

The resit question deserves its own note, because the timings are counter-intuitive. The checkable Pearson dates show that November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. A November resit therefore confirms in late January, which is tight against spring sixth-form deadlines and worth knowing before the resit is chosen rather than after.

Two rules follow. Plan from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, this one included. And ask your centre which Cambridge administrative zone it belongs to, in writing, because the zone determines which timetable version applies to your child.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the mandatory UAE subjects, and what they add to the week
paragraphs: Families here planning a UAE university application need Ministry of Education equivalency for the school-leaving certificate, and the British-track rule is published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five.

That last clause is the one most often misread, and in both directions. It does not mean Arabic is optional at school; it means Arabic and Islamic education do not count towards the five subjects the equivalency requires. For the American track the requirements are different again, with English evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we read, so we publish none.

Separately, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval.

For a Year 10 or 11 family the practical point is workload. These subjects occupy real timetable hours alongside nine IGCSE subjects, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a recommended minimum lesson length of 25 minutes. Equivalency itself is a Ministry process that IB Gram neither performs nor influences, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Online delivery, permits and how to start
paragraphs: IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time and offers no home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For code-matched IGCSE work the format suits the task, because most of it is a marked paper on a shared screen with both people annotating the same question. Sessions can start at 4pm rather than 5.30pm, and they do not cancel for traffic.

The honest limitations: a student who will not begin work without an adult present does better in person; a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says; and a shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines any lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If that is your household, hire locally and use the five checks set out above.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

To start: send the syllabus code, the subject, the year group and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. If you do not have the code, the paper carries it on the front cover. A specialist on that specification then teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online built on that paper, ending in a written note of what it showed and what the first month should target. The note is yours whether or not you continue, and if nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so and offer alternatives.
