faqs.question: Why does my neighbour's child in Green Community have no exams at 16?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because they are on the IB Middle Years Programme rather than IGCSE. The MYP assesses against four lettered criteria per subject, each out of eight, judged on work produced through the year, and most MYP students sit no external papers at 16 unless the school enters them for optional on-screen eAssessments. It is a different assessment model rather than an easier or harder school. In this catchment four or five systems sit within a short drive, which is why cross-street comparisons mislead so often.

faqs.question: Should pupils in Dubai study the IGCSE or the MYP?
faqs.answer: They assess different things and suit different students. IGCSE produces one certificate per subject through external papers, which is portable and transparent, and it rewards examination technique. The MYP produces criterion grades and builds inquiry, independent work and reflective writing, which pays later in the IB Diploma's internally assessed components. The MYP's gap is timed examination stamina; the IGCSE's is that a poor fortnight is costly. Within this catchment both are available locally, so it is a genuine choice rather than a constraint.

faqs.question: Is a 9-1 IGCSE grade the same as a percentage?
faqs.answer: No. Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked so that standards stay comparable between sittings, which means the same raw mark can fall either side of a boundary in different years. A grade tells you where a performance sat against that series' boundaries, not what proportion of questions were correct, and it does not translate into a grade point average either. The useful thing to take from a marked paper is not a predicted grade but whether the losses were habits, which move in weeks, or content, which takes a term.

faqs.question: My child is moving from CBSE into an IGCSE school. What changes?
faqs.answer: The format more than the content. CBSE is content-dense with a strong emphasis on accurate procedural work, and students arriving from it are often well drilled and under-practised at the evaluation and extended-response questions that carry the top marks in IGCSE. The command terms are also used more precisely than many transferring students expect. A first month spent on answer formats and command-term depth, rather than on content, is usually what moves the first set of IGCSE marks.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count towards the five subjects UAE equivalency requires?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the clause most often misread. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. That does not make Arabic optional at school: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. The two rules sit side by side, which is exactly why they get confused.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Green Community tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Five things, in this order. Do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years? Which syllabus code have they taught, and can they name the papers in it? Do they mark against the official scheme, and can they show a marked example? What happens if the match turns out to be wrong? And is there a written note after each session? Price is the easiest thing to compare and the least informative of the six.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home quote for Emaar South higher than one for Green Community?
faqs.answer: The drive. Green Community sits inside Dubai Investments Park where several schools and therefore several teachers already are, so local in-home supply is reasonable by this cluster's standards. Emaar South is a long way from most of the city, so tutors decline, surcharge, or offer only a late slot. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independents to AED 500, and the journey sits inside those figures. The same paper is marked identically regardless of which community the candidate lives in.

faqs.question: Do you cover English as a Second Language for this catchment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more requested subjects here, because home languages in Dubai Investments Park and Discovery Gardens are very mixed. Cambridge offers it under 0510 and 0511, which include an assessed speaking component, and the two codes are not interchangeable so the exam entry statement matters. In practice the fastest mark gains come from structured paragraph planning and from reading the question's audience and form accurately, rather than from vocabulary lists, which is the work most students expect.

faqs.question: When will my child's November IGCSE results arrive?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, which matters if a resit is being used to meet a sixth-form condition. The checkable Pearson dates show that November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. A November resit therefore confirms in late January, which is tight against spring deadlines. Plan from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a student in this catchment usually take?
faqs.answer: Commonly eight or nine, including the mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside them. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a recommended minimum lesson length of 25 minutes. Those hours are real and they are part of why a Year 11 timetable here feels full. It is also why we suggest starting with one tutored subject rather than three.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IGCSE subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the pairing. Mathematics with Physics works reasonably, because the shared difficulty is usually algebraic rearrangement. Chemistry with Biology works less well, since the mark schemes reward different things and most schools staff them separately for that reason. Economics with Business Studies is a sensible pair. Each subject still needs its own slot, since these are one-to-one lessons. Tell us both subjects and codes at the enquiry and we will say honestly whether one tutor is the better arrangement.

faqs.question: Is online tuition suitable for a Year 9 student in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and Year 9 is a good year to start, because the tier decision and the habits that carry marks are both still cheap to influence. The requirements are a reliable connection and a quiet hour, which in the villas here is usually straightforward and in a shared apartment needs planning around siblings. Where it works less well is with a student who will not begin work without an adult physically present; in that case hire locally, and use the five checks rather than a price comparison.

faqs.question: Do you provide IGCSE past papers, notes or mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We do not host or distribute them. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and specifications are copyright material, and circulating unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for the student. We reference and link the official sources and work from the copies your child's school is licensed to provide. Any service offering you a complete paper library, or material that has not been released, is worth declining on that basis alone rather than negotiating over.

faqs.question: How do lessons work around Ramadan here?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the plan usually does not. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. Where a series is close, families generally keep the frequency and change only the time, which is the arrangement that holds up best. Because no tutor is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute, and it moves back just as easily.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-green-communit.closingHeading: Name the system, then the code, then send a paper
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-green-communit.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Green Community, the three questions that make everything else quick are which system your child is actually in, which board and code they are entered for, and what their last marked paper shows. Send the code, the year group and a photograph of the paper. A specialist on that specification reads it, tells you whether the lost marks are habits or content, and teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online at a Gulf Standard Time hour that fits the short school run here. The written diagnosis is yours whether or not you continue.

intro.heading: IGCSE is nine or ten separate examinations, and families rarely need help with all of them
paragraphs: The useful thing to know about IGCSE is that it is not one qualification. It is a set of separate examinations, each with its own syllabus code, its own paper structure, its own calculator rules and its own way of losing marks. A parent in Hor Al Anz asking for an IGCSE tutor almost always needs one or two of them rather than all nine, and the quickest way to waste money in this market is to buy general support for a specific problem.

So this page is built by subject. For each one it names the Cambridge and Pearson codes, says what papers the student sits, and describes where the marks actually drain away. Maths loses marks to notation and rounding instructions. Physics loses them to algebra. Chemistry loses them to balanced equations and method selection. Biology loses them to imprecise terminology and to long answers containing fewer distinct points than the mark allocation required. These are different problems with different repair times.

Hor Al Anz sits in Deira, inland from Al Mamzar and next to Abu Hail, Al Muteena and Al Qusais, with the Green Line of the Metro running through the area. It is a dense, mid-rise, mid-income residential district, and the education market around it is unlike the one in New Dubai. Tuition centres are plentiful and cheap, the private home-tuition trade is active at the budget end, and a significant proportion of students are either in Indian-curriculum schools or have moved into a British-curriculum school from one.

That last point generates a specific kind of enquiry: a student who was comfortable in CBSE arithmetic and is now losing marks on worded, context-heavy IGCSE questions, or who has strong content knowledge and no practice at the structured long answers the mark scheme wants. That is not a weak student. It is a mismatch between two assessment cultures, and it is closed in weeks rather than years once somebody names it properly.

There is a budget question underneath most enquiries from this district, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a brochure. Tuition here is available at every price point, from group classes at a centre to informal home tuition to specialist one-to-one work, and the published Dubai bands span roughly AED 45 to 500 an hour depending on which of those you buy. A fixed budget spread across three subjects buys three arrangements that diagnose nothing. The same money spent on one subject, chosen from marked evidence rather than from a sense of which subject feels hardest, usually produces a better set of grades, because the weakest subject is frequently weak for a reason it shares with another.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We teach one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. In this part of Dubai the honest argument for that is partly the tutor pool, which stops being limited to those who will travel to Abu Hail on a weekday evening, and partly reliability, because sessions that depend on nobody's journey do not disappear in a bad week.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names the codes most used in Dubai schools and says where the marks actually go. Use it to decide which one or two subjects are worth paying for.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge sits one paper without a calculator, so exact form and notation matter; Pearson allows a calculator throughout, so rounding and interpretation matter more. Rounding instructions are the cheapest marks in either.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, unit prefixes and gradients read from a drawn line. Students who write only answers forfeit method marks they had already earned.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Method selection in calculations, balanced equations, state symbols and ionic charges. Notation here is marked as right or wrong rather than as presentation.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Terminology precision and point-counting on long answers. A six-mark question needs six distinct points, not a thorough paragraph containing three.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different papers. Confirm which appears on the entry, because preparation diverges sharply between them.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading responses. Marks are lost to register and to answering a different question from the one asked rather than to weak writing.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise definitions. The data-response paper rewards brevity, and able writers often over-explain and run short of time.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Break-even, ratio and cash-flow questions are examined arithmetic, and a numerate student can lift this grade quickly by treating them as free marks.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Format discipline carries the marks: the layout of a statement is assessed, not just the figures in it. Students lose marks for presentation that is actually content.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the theory paper. Confident programmers still lose marks on the written conventions the scheme expects.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Early calculus and trigonometric identities alongside the main grade. Valuable once the main grade is secure, and a liability while it is not.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: All three disciplines for two grades, with less content and identical technique demands. Revision has to be planned across disciplines rather than within one.

sections.heading: Maths: the code decides the revision, and the instructions decide the marks
paragraphs: Maths is the most requested IGCSE subject from this district and the one where the syllabus code matters most. Cambridge 0580 sits two papers, one of them without a calculator, which means non-calculator fluency, exact-form answers and notation carry real weight. Pearson 4MA1 sits two equally weighted papers with a calculator allowed throughout, which shifts the risk to rounding, accuracy and interpreting what the display actually means. Both are tiered, and the tier caps what is available.

The marks that go missing are mostly not topic knowledge. The largest recoverable category across marked papers is instruction-reading: an answer given to two decimal places when three significant figures were requested, a length given where an area was wanted, units omitted or wrong. These are fast to fix and a tutor who starts with circle theorems instead has chosen the harder route for no reason.

The second category is abandoned method. On the long structured questions, method marks are available even when the final answer is wrong, and a student who stops because the number looks unpleasant forfeits marks already earned. Training a student to write the next line even when they expect to be wrong takes about three sessions and is worth several marks a paper for the rest of their school career.

The third is genuine algebraic fluency: sign errors when expanding, dropped negatives, index laws, and rearranging a formula with the unknown on both sides. This is where a real content gap usually lives and it generally traces back to Years 7 to 9. It is repairable in six to eight weeks of short consistent practice and not in a fortnight, and a parent deserves to hear that in week one rather than week six.

sections.heading: The three sciences, and the three different reasons marks disappear
paragraphs: Physics, chemistry and biology fail in different ways, which is why a single revision instruction underperforms across them. In physics the losses are mathematical: rearranging a formula when the unknown sits in the denominator, standard form on very large or very small values, unit prefixes, and reading a gradient from a drawn line rather than from two plotted points. A student who is strong in biology and weak in physics usually has an algebra problem wearing a physics costume.

In chemistry the losses are method selection and notation. A student who can convert a mass to moles on request but does not recognise that a question requires it has a selection problem, and the repair is mixed practice where the method has to be chosen rather than applied. Alongside that, balanced equations, state symbols and ionic charges carry marks that students read as neatness. They are not neatness, and the fix is mechanical, which means it holds under pressure.

In biology the losses are terminology and point-counting. The precise term scores and an approximation of it often does not, and a six-mark question wants six distinct scoring points rather than a thorough paragraph containing three. Reading the mark allocation first and planning that many separate points in the margin is a two-session habit that pays out on every long-answer question in the paper.

Across all three sits the practical component, which at most international centres is examined as a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than as a laboratory test. That paper is trainable technique: reading an instrument to the right precision, identifying variables, finding the flaw in a described method, building a results table with units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting an improvement that addresses the specific weakness rather than a generic one. It is the most neglected component in the qualification and one of the most recoverable.

sections.heading: Coming from CBSE: what transfers, and what has to be learned
paragraphs: A large share of enquiries from Hor Al Anz involve a student who moved into a British-curriculum school from CBSE or ICSE, either at the start of Year 10 or part-way through. These students are frequently misdiagnosed, including by themselves. They are not behind on content. They are usually ahead on procedural arithmetic and systematic practice, and unpractised at the specific things IGCSE mark schemes reward.

Three differences account for most of it. The first is worded, context-led questions: IGCSE wraps the mathematics or the science in a scenario and expects the student to extract what is needed, where the previous system more often asked the question directly. The second is the expectation that method is shown and credited, so a student trained to produce answers efficiently loses marks they had earned. The third is the structured long answer, scored by distinct points against a mark scheme rather than by overall quality.

None of those is a deficiency and all three are learnable quickly, usually in a term of focused work. What they are not is fixable by covering the syllabus again, which is the standard offer a transferring family receives. The right first step is an audit: specification topic by topic, what was covered and to what depth, compared with the new school's teaching order. That produces a short list rather than a syllabus, and it prevents paying to re-teach material the student already holds.

The table sets out the transfer picture subject by subject. It is a starting hypothesis for the audit rather than a conclusion, because individual schools vary far more than curricula do, and a student should always be assessed on their own script rather than on their previous curriculum's reputation.

sections.heading: What tuition actually costs around Deira, and how to spend a fixed budget
paragraphs: This district has one of the most active tuition markets in Dubai and also the widest spread of prices, so published figures are genuinely useful here. Market rates from provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai table put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300, an IGCSE specialist at about AED 200 to 450 or more, and an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is inside the fee. Monthly figures run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject.

Those are the market and not our price list. The reason to publish them is that most pages competing for this search publish nothing: three of the six examined for this project quote no figure at all, and one asks the price in its own list of questions and then declines to answer it. A family with a fixed budget cannot allocate it sensibly without knowing what the bands are.

The allocation question matters more here than the rate question. A fixed budget spread across three subjects buys three thin arrangements, none of which diagnoses anything. The same budget spent on one subject properly, chosen by marked evidence, usually produces a better set of grades, because the weakest subject is often weak for a reason shared with a second. Maths is frequently the right single choice, since the same gaps damage physics and chemistry calculations.

Group tuition at a centre is cheaper per hour and genuinely useful for content coverage where a student is simply behind on material. Its weakness is diagnosis: nobody in a group reads one student's script closely enough to notice they are losing marks to command words rather than to content. The sensible combination for a budget-conscious family is content coverage in a group plus occasional one-to-one marking, rather than more group hours.

sections.heading: The practical shape of an evening in a Deira apartment
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz students mostly travel by school bus or on the Green Line, which produces a more predictable arrival time than a car in New Dubai traffic but not an early one. Students attending the Al Qusais or Al Nahda cluster are generally home between 15:30 and 16:30; students crossing the Creek to Al Garhoud, Festival City or Oud Metha arrive later. Add food and a change of clothes, and the slot that holds reliably across a term is 17:00 to 17:30 at the earliest.

Apartment study space is the second practical issue and it deserves five minutes of planning. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper and a ruler for graph work, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so that a busy household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page rather than at the face, because in every one of these subjects the diagnosis comes from watching the working appear.

Where siblings share a room, which is common here, staggered slots on different evenings work and a shared session does not. Two students at different levels in the same session means one of them is being supervised rather than taught. If the budget only covers one child's tuition, that is a decision worth making deliberately rather than by splitting the hour.

Ramadan reshapes the pattern for several weeks and Dubai schools adjust their hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them, agreed before the month begins. For a Year 11 student these weeks often sit close to a mock series, which is exactly why planning the shift is better than improvising through it.

sections.heading: The series, the entry and the resit route
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE runs in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are the windows available to a UAE candidate. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, which matters especially in a district where many families have direct experience of the Indian system and may reasonably assume otherwise. A date attached to that series should be disregarded by a Dubai family.

The entry carries the syllabus codes and the tier and is lodged months before the papers. One email to the examinations officer asking for codes and tiers per subject removes the largest single source of wasted revision time, because it determines which past papers are worth sitting. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the real calendar: its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the live official timetable rather than any summary is the document to work from.

The resit conversation should happen in the spring rather than in August. Summer results arrive late in the month and the November entry closes within weeks, which puts the decision under time pressure before anyone has seen a script. Ask the examinations officer when the November entry closes and how a script copy can be obtained, and agree in advance what evidence would justify a resit. Where a post-16 place or an equivalency application depends on a grade, the binding deadline is the receiving institution's, so ask them in writing.

sections.heading: Equivalency and what the grades have to add up to
paragraphs: Families in this district planning for UAE university entry meet the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements, and the IGCSE grades feed into them directly. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects.

That exclusion is worth noting carefully because one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the published rule. A family planning a subject combination on the wrong number may take a decision it cannot reverse, and the window in which the combination is changeable is Year 9 and early Year 10, the same window as the tier decision.

For the American track the published requirements differ in kind: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the source we rely on, so no IB figure should be published without a reading from the Ministry's own site, and we leave the gap rather than guessing.

Equivalency is a regulatory process that IB Gram does not perform, influence or guarantee. We describe it and point you at the official channel. Nothing on this page should be read as implying that tutoring is required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; it is not, and a provider suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Permits, honest limits and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit, which matters in a district where informal home tuition is widely available. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page: a figure circulating online could not be verified and publishing it would be guesswork dressed as fact. Asking a tutor about their permit is an ordinary question with an ordinary answer, and evasiveness in response is itself informative. We would also advise against any arrangement involving your child's own schoolteacher, which the permit's code of conduct and reported regulatory rules both point away from.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not enter candidates for examinations and we do not perform equivalency. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold none because we have no premises.

On materials and figures: we reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. Every number on this page carries a source, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

process.title: Name the one or two subjects that matter
process.description: Not school in general. A specific subject, with the syllabus code if you have it, and what is going wrong. That focus is what allows a fixed budget to buy something that works, and it also lets us tell you when the honest answer is one subject rather than the three you were considering.

process.title: Get the codes and tiers from the school
process.description: One email to the examinations officer, asking for the syllabus code and tier for each subject on the entry. Dubai schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects in the same year group, and a student revising the wrong board's papers is working hard in a dialect the examination does not speak.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a report
process.description: The marked script shows where the marks went: instruction-reading, abandoned method, a genuine content gap, or questions never reached. A report shows a grade. We categorise every lost mark rather than counting them, and the resulting tally decides what the first month contains.

process.title: Free trial lesson on real questions
process.description: The first session is free and runs on past-paper questions drawn from the script you sent. The tutor watches the working appear, which is where diagnosis happens. A short written note follows naming the two priority items and the order to fix them in, and the note is yours whether or not you book.

process.title: Agree a finite plan and review it
process.description: A named number of sessions with the school and public holidays already subtracted, two priority topics in writing, and a review against a second marked paper. If the problem is solved we say so and stop. If a marking clinic would now do the job more cheaply than teaching, we say that too.

whyPoints.title: One subject funded properly, not three funded thinly
whyPoints.description: A fixed budget spread across three subjects buys three arrangements that diagnose nothing. The same money on the subject the marked scripts identify, often maths, usually lifts two grades because the underlying gap was shared. That is the recommendation most families here get from us.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different calculator rules and different past papers. Tutors here are matched to the code and tier your child is entered for, which removes the most common avoidable waste of revision time in this qualification.

whyPoints.title: Transfers audited before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE usually have the content and not the answer technique. One audit session produces a short gap list and names the technique problem, instead of selling a syllabus re-run to a student who did not need one.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: This page names the Deira market bands in dirhams and says who published each figure. Three of six competitor pages publish no price at all, and one asks the question in its own FAQ then declines to answer it. A family with a fixed budget needs the bands to allocate it.

whyPoints.title: The cheapest workable option is named, including when it is not us
whyPoints.description: Group content coverage plus occasional one-to-one marking is often the right combination on a tight budget, and we will say so. A marking clinic is frequently the honest recommendation where a full term of teaching was being requested.

whyPoints.title: Plain about what we are not
whyPoints.description: A tutor-matching platform with no board or regulator approval, no UAE premises, and no home-visit service in the Emirates. We do not enter candidates or perform equivalency. Where this page names a regulator it explains what that body does and links its own pages.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send IGCSE tutors to homes in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. IGCSE support here is delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The practical advantages in this district are real: you select from everyone who has taught your child's syllabus code rather than from those willing to travel to Abu Hail on a weekday evening, you do not pay a travel premium, and no session disappears because somebody was stuck in traffic on Al Ittihad Road.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost around Hor Al Anz and Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300, an IGCSE specialist at about AED 200 to 450 or more, and an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee. Monthly estimates run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. Those figures come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table rather than from us; we quote after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: With one subject's budget to spend in Hor Al Anz, where does it go furthest?
faqs.answer: Usually the one where a marked paper shows the largest recoverable loss, which is not always the lowest grade. Maths is frequently the right single choice, because the rearrangement, standard form and proportional reasoning that cost marks there also damage physics and chemistry calculations, so fixing it lifts more than one grade. Biology is more often a terminology and point-counting problem that a disciplined student can work on with less supervision once the method has been taught. Send one marked paper per subject and we will name the order.

faqs.question: Our child moved from CBSE to IGCSE and the grades dropped. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost always a technique mismatch rather than a knowledge gap. IGCSE wraps the content in worded, context-led questions and expects the student to extract what is needed. It credits method shown even when the final answer is wrong, so a student trained to produce answers efficiently loses marks they had earned. And its long answers are scored by distinct points against a mark scheme rather than by overall quality. All three are learnable in a term. What does not help is covering the syllabus again, which is the usual offer a transferring family receives.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Deira as good as one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For different things. A centre is cheaper per hour and genuinely effective at content coverage where a student is simply behind on material. Its weakness is diagnosis: in a group nobody reads one student's script closely enough to notice that marks are going to command words or rounding instructions rather than to content, and that is the kind of finding that actually changes a grade. On a tight budget the sensible combination is group content coverage plus occasional one-to-one marking, rather than more group hours.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus is my child entered for, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the code, not the subject name. Cambridge 0580 sits two papers with one taken without a calculator, so non-calculator fluency, exact form and notation carry real weight. Pearson 4MA1 sits two equally weighted papers with a calculator throughout, which moves the risk to rounding and interpretation. Cambridge 0607 is the graphic-display-calculator syllabus and 4MB1 is Pearson's more compressed alternative. Each has its own past-paper library, and practising on the wrong one is the most common avoidable waste of revision time we see.

faqs.question: How are practical science skills examined if lessons are on a screen?
faqs.answer: Laboratory work for school purposes happens at school under the school's supervision, and no tutor takes part in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, which most international centres sit as an alternative-to-practical paper. Those questions are predictable: reading an instrument to the correct precision, identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, spotting the flaw in a described method, completing a results table with headings and units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting an improvement that addresses the specific weakness described.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in physics but not in biology?
faqs.answer: Because physics examines mathematics. Rearranging a formula when the unknown sits in the denominator, standard form on very large or very small values, converting between unit prefixes, and reading a gradient from a drawn line are all maths skills tested inside a physics paper. Biology rewards precise terminology and well-counted long answers, which is a different kind of diligence. A student strong in one and weak in the other usually has a specific algebra gap, and closing it improves the chemistry calculations at the same time.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and two sciences for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is often not the best arrangement. Most strong tutors teach two of those three well and are honest about the third, and the difference between a competent explanation and an expert one is largest exactly in the topics that are causing trouble. Two specialists on two evenings with one shared written plan generally beats one generalist across three subjects. If we do not have a good match for a subject we will say so rather than stretching somebody into it.

faqs.question: What time can sessions start for a student travelling back from Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Around 17:00 to 17:30 in practice. Students attending the Al Qusais, Al Nahda or Abu Hail cluster are usually home between 15:30 and 16:30 by bus or Metro, and after food and a change of clothes that is the earliest slot that holds through a term. Students crossing the Creek to Al Garhoud, Festival City or Oud Metha arrive later and need a correspondingly later slot. Because sessions are online nobody is travelling to the lesson, so the only thing the slot has to survive is the household's own evening.

faqs.question: Do you work with students at Indian-curriculum schools as well?
faqs.answer: This page is written for IGCSE, which is what the search asks about, and many families in this district have children in both systems. Where a student is sitting CBSE or ICSE examinations, the subject knowledge overlaps substantially and the assessment conventions do not, so tell us which board and which year when you enquire. Where a transfer into IGCSE is planned, the most useful work is the audit and technique bridge described on this page, ideally in the term before the move rather than after it.

faqs.question: Can two children share one session to keep the cost down?
faqs.answer: We would advise against it, and the reason is practical rather than commercial. Two students at different levels in one hour means one of them is being supervised while the other is taught, and neither gets the diagnostic value that comes from a tutor watching one student's working appear. If the budget covers one child's tuition, it is better to make that choice deliberately, fund the subject that gives the widest benefit, and use a marking clinic for the other child rather than splitting an hour two ways.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in Dubai sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Dubai centres normally enter the main Year 11 cohort for the summer window and use November as the resit route. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so any date attached to it should be disregarded here. Ask the school for the zone-correct Cambridge timetable, because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working in Deira need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount you read as unverified. Asking about the permit is a reasonable question in any arrangement.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingBody: IGCSE support works best when it is narrow. Tell us one or two subjects, the syllabus codes if you have them, and send a marked paper, and we will tell you where the marks are going, which single subject gives the widest benefit for a fixed budget, and whether a marking clinic would do what weekly teaching is being bought for. Everything is delivered one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, at a time that works once the bus or the Metro has got them home.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IGCSE mathematics, the sciences, English language, business studies and economics for students travelling out of International City to schools across eastern Dubai, on both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications.

intro.heading: What time does the school day actually end here?
paragraphs: The honest answer in International City is later than the timetable says. The district has no international school inside any of its clusters, so a Year 10 or Year 11 student travels out - most often to Al Warqa or Al Qusais, often to Silicon Oasis or Academic City, sometimes as far as Mirdif or Garhoud. The school day may finish at half past two, and the child may walk through the door of a flat in the England Cluster at a quarter past four.

That gap matters more than any other practical fact about tutoring here. It is the difference between a 4pm session that is theoretically possible and a 6pm session that actually happens every week. Families who book against the timetable rather than against the bus lose the first ten minutes of most lessons, and over a two-year IGCSE course that is a substantial amount of paid time spent waiting.

The second constraint is homework. A Year 11 student carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects has school work most evenings, and a tutoring session placed on top of it without thought simply displaces the work the school set. The sessions that produce results are the ones with agreed homework between them, which means the weekly timetable has to have room for both the session and the work after it.

The third is that a bus-dependent household has less flexibility than a car-dependent one. In several clusters the school bus rather than a family car sets the return time, and bus timings do not negotiate. This is why weekend mornings matter so much in this district: a Saturday morning slot is the only time in the week when a full timed paper can be sat properly, and a three-hour paper cannot be done at seven in the evening after a long day.

None of this has anything to do with whether a tutor lives nearby, which is the point. IB Gram delivers one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service. A session that starts when the laptop opens is worth considerably more to a household on this timetable than one that depends on a second person also crossing the city at half past five.

There is one more reason the timetable deserves this much attention. Tutoring arrangements in this district fail far more often from scheduling friction than from bad teaching: a slot that moves weekly, a session that starts fifteen minutes late every time, a plan that assumed two free weekday evenings the household never had. Getting the week right is unglamorous and it is the part that decides whether the arrangement still exists in February. What follows is the practical version: which schools each part of the district feeds and how long the run takes, a weekly timetable that fits a session and its homework around nine subjects, the syllabus codes to confirm before anybody teaches anything, and the June and November series counted backwards from a bus timetable rather than from an ideal.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.programmesIntro: Four positions families in these clusters write to us from, each with a different timetable problem as well as a different academic one.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the option choices
programmes.description: The year the tier and route decisions are made, usually by the school and often without a conversation. Mathematics is split into Core and Extended or Foundation and Higher; sciences into separate subjects, a double award or a single combined science. Both decisions cap what is achievable two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For a commuting family this is also the year to ask about the practical side: what time the bus returns, how much homework a Year 10 evening carries, and whether the school runs after-school support that would make private tutoring unnecessary. Several schools in Al Warqa and Al Qusais do, and nobody mentions it unless asked.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: Content is taught and nothing is urgent, which makes this the cheapest year to fix a problem and the right year to argue for a tier change with marked evidence. Past-paper work can begin at the intended tier rather than being saved for Year 11, which is the commonest planning error at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: The timetable is also kinder in Year 10 than in Year 11, which matters here. A single weekday session plus homework fits a Year 10 evening comfortably; the same arrangement in Year 11, with nine subjects setting work and mock examinations approaching, needs the weekend slot instead.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the June series
programmes.description: Content finishes and the useful work becomes technique: working shown, command terms answered as asked, timing per mark, final long questions attempted rather than abandoned. That reliably recovers marks and cannot replace a topic never taught, and an honest tutor says which you are buying.
programmes.countryNote: For a bus-dependent household in Year 11, the realistic shape is one weekday evening session and one weekend morning. The weekend slot carries the timed papers; the weekday slot carries the mark-scheme walkthrough and the error log. Two weekday evenings rarely works, because the second one lands on a tired student with homework still to do.

programmes.name: November resit
programmes.description: A subject retaken in the November series after a June result below a sixth-form requirement. Cambridge and Pearson both run November sessions, so the gap is roughly five months. Entry goes through the school or an approved centre and the deadline sits months ahead of the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Timing matters for a family planning a sixth-form move. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, after most courses had started, so ask the receiving school in writing whether a conditional place survives until a January result before entering. Also request the component breakdown, because that decides whether a resit is sensible at all.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.subjectsIntro: Each entry says what the subject costs in evening time as well as what it demands academically, because in this district those are the same question.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Two papers, with a non-calculator component in common variants. The quickest recoverable marks are working shown and rounding controlled. Fits a weekday evening well, because the practice sets are short and the feedback is immediate.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, calculator permitted throughout, so non-calculator drilling is wasted here. The recoverable marks sit in the long multi-step problems at the end of each paper, which students leave blank far more often than they attempt.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry the heaviest load. Cambridge offers a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical; Pearson 4PH1 has no practical examination. Confirm which before buying revision aimed at apparatus technique.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis repay targeted drilling more than anything else in the subject. Practical questions reward exact vocabulary for separation techniques and gas tests, which is memorisable in a fortnight of short evening sessions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, with command terms deciding the grade. Suits short, frequent work rather than long sessions, which fits a commuting household better than most subjects on this list.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in two subjects, with papers that move between biology, chemistry and physics. Students lose real time re-orienting, so revision should follow the paper section rather than the subject - a specific technique worth a weekend session to establish.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Form errors cost whole mark bands: a good essay written when a letter was specified scores badly. Needs the weekend slot for full timed writing, because a complete response cannot be produced properly after seven in the evening.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Accuracy beats ambition in the mark scheme. Note-taking and summary tasks are the most teachable components and the ones where short evening sessions produce the fastest visible movement.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward application to the case material in front of the student. Economics diagrams must be titled, labelled and referenced in the prose; Business Studies top bands need a justified judgement rather than a list. Both work well in short sessions.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Geography marks go on case-study specificity - named place, figure, date. History marks go on source evaluation that addresses provenance rather than content. Both are techniques rather than content and both move quickly.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Computer Science loses marks on trace tables and algorithms that ignore edge cases. ICT is practical-assessment heavy and the loss is procedural: steps omitted, evidence not captured, naming conventions ignored.

subjects.name: Bridging into A Level or the Diploma
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation and timed essay structure, all assumed from the first week of Year 12. Six to eight summer sessions, when the evening timetable is empty and nothing competes for the hours.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.regionsTitle: The clusters, the schools they feed, and the run
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.regionsIntro: International City is a set of named clusters rather than one neighbourhood, and the route out differs between them enough to change what time a session can start.

regions.name: China Cluster and Dragon Mart
regions.note: The commercial centre, with the heaviest local traffic exactly when the school run happens. Buses from here are the least predictable in the district, which is why 6pm is the sensible floor rather than 5.30pm.

regions.name: England Cluster
regions.note: Dense residential blocks feeding mainly the Al Warqa and Al Qusais schools. Around twenty minutes on a clear morning and longer in the afternoon, so a weekday session before six rarely survives contact with reality.

regions.name: France Cluster
regions.note: Similar profile to England Cluster, with a large share of working households and consequently strong demand for weekend-morning slots rather than weekday evenings.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-international-.modesIntro: Three arrangements that fit a commuting household's week, plus a straight answer on the in-home option.

modes.title: One fixed weekday evening session
modes.description: A single 60-minute session in the same slot every week, timed to the bus rather than to the school bell. A fixed slot matters more for a bus-dependent household than for any other kind, because a session that moves each week eventually stops happening. Content follows the school's scheme of work so nothing runs in parallel.

modes.description: The slot that makes real examination practice possible in this district. A full paper sat to time, marked properly against the published mark scheme, and walked through question by question. It cannot be done on a weekday evening after a long commute, and it is the single most useful thing a Year 11 student does.

sections.heading: Which schools the clusters feed, and how long the run takes
paragraphs: Because no international school sits inside International City, the first useful piece of planning is simply knowing where the children go and what the journey costs in time. The destinations fall into three groups. Al Warqa and Al Qusais are the near group, around twenty minutes on a clear morning. Silicon Oasis and Academic City are the middle group, reached on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. Mirdif, Garhoud and Nad Al Sheba are the far group, chosen deliberately for a particular school.

The afternoon journey is the one that matters for tutoring and it is not the morning journey in reverse. School buses make multiple stops, the Ras Al Khor and Dragon Mart junctions are slower in the afternoon, and a bus that leaves a school in Silicon Oasis at three can reach the Persia Cluster closer to four than to half past three. Families consistently underestimate this, and consistently book sessions that start before the student is home.

The table below gives working figures by destination group, with the realistic earliest session start for each. Treat them as planning numbers rather than promises; the point is the shape rather than the minutes. If your child is on a school bus, ask the school for the actual route timing rather than estimating, because bus routes vary and a ten-minute error repeated weekly is expensive.

One further operational point for this district specifically. Several clusters have limited parking and dense through-traffic around Dragon Mart, which is exactly the sort of friction that turns an in-home arrangement from convenient into unreliable. It is a small thing that matters, because a tutoring arrangement only works if it actually happens every week.

sections.heading: A week that fits nine subjects, a commute and a tutor
paragraphs: A Year 11 IGCSE student typically carries eight or nine subjects, each setting work. Adding tutoring to that week without removing anything produces a student who attends the session and stops doing the school's homework, which is a net loss however good the tutor is. So the week has to be designed rather than filled.

The arrangement that works in this district is one fixed weekday evening session plus one weekend morning, with agreed homework from the session fitted into a named evening rather than left to find its own space. Two weekday evenings rarely works: the second lands on a tired student who still has school work to do, and the quality of the second session is routinely half that of the first.

The weekend morning is where the heavy work goes. A full timed paper takes two to three hours including the walkthrough, and that is not available on a weekday evening at any price. Students who sit one complete paper a week through the final term arrive at the series having practised the actual activity rather than having revised for it, and the difference in performance is substantial.

The table below sets out a workable week. It is deliberately modest, because the commonest failure in this district is an ambitious schedule that collapses in week three. A plan the household can actually sustain for two terms beats a better plan abandoned in October. The test is whether it still works on a bad week rather than a good one.

sections.heading: Confirm the specification before anybody teaches anything
paragraphs: This is five minutes of work that prevents a term of waste, and it is particularly worth doing in this district because students here change schools within Dubai more often than in more settled neighbourhoods. A move in Year 10 can mean a change of specification mid-course, which leaves content covered under one syllabus and never under the other.

Ask the examinations officer for the entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option for every paper. It is common for a single Year 11 student to sit Cambridge in three subjects and Pearson Edexcel in two. The differences are operational rather than cosmetic. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical; Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 have no practical examination at all.

The tier is the other number to confirm. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5 and Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5, while Extended and Higher run the full range. Both lower tiers comfortably satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency, which asks for five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Neither satisfies a sixth form asking for grade 6 in mathematics.

With that list in hand, a tutor can say honestly whether they teach that exact specification routinely. A provider who quotes before asking for it is going to teach a generic course, and for a household already spending an hour a day on a commute, paying for content the child will never sit is the least affordable kind of waste.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted back from a bus timetable
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any advice to prepare for a February paper is advice for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

The sourced reference points are useful for planning: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any date you act on should come from the live official timetable.

One Cambridge detail that belongs in every plan: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. If your child travels to a school in another district, the zone is the centre's rather than yours, and it is worth confirming.

Counting backwards from the papers for a commuting household produces one specific recommendation: start the weekend-morning timed paper habit in the first term of Year 11, not after the mocks. By the second term the weekends fill with mock preparation and coursework deadlines, and the habit never establishes. Starting early costs nothing extra and is the difference between practising the examination and revising for it.

sections.heading: Mock results, and reading them properly from a distance
paragraphs: Mock results in Dubai schools typically arrive in the second term, and for a family that does not pass the school gate daily they often arrive as a number with no context. The grade is the least useful part. The marked script, with the question-level breakdown, is what makes a plan possible, and it is worth asking for explicitly rather than waiting for a parents' evening.

Read the script for pattern. Marks lost evenly across a paper usually mean timing or technique. Marks lost in clusters usually mean a topic. Marks lost heavily in the last third almost always mean pacing, which is the easiest of the three to fix and the one that responds fastest to timed practice. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is a question-style problem rather than a knowledge gap, and that is a fortnight of work rather than a term.

For a student sitting a double-award science or a combined science, look for something else as well: whether the marks cluster in one of the three sciences. The papers move between biology, chemistry and physics, and a student can lose most of their marks in one subject area while appearing uniformly weak. That distinction decides whether you need one tutor or none.

Bringing the marked script to the first session saves two sessions of exploratory questioning. At market rates for a qualified online subject tutor - roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across this market, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 - that is real money for a household already carrying a commute and school fees.

sections.heading: Practical science when nobody can get back to the laboratory
paragraphs: This district has a specific version of a common problem. A student at a school in Silicon Oasis who needs an extra set of readings cannot simply walk back in after dinner, because the school is a bus ride away and the bus has gone. So whatever practical work the course requires has to be completed in the timetabled laboratory sessions, and the preparation around it has to happen elsewhere.

Fortunately that preparation is where most of the assessed marks sit. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, depending on the school's choice. Pearson candidates sit neither: 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1 assess experimental skills inside the written papers as method-design and data-analysis questions.

Both routes test the same underlying skills, and all of them are teachable on a shared screen with a real dataset. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables. Choosing a sensible range and interval. Justifying a number of repeats. Reading a scale to appropriate precision. Recording to consistent significant figures. Plotting with a sensible scale. Drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Writing an evaluation that names one specific limitation and one realistic improvement.

What cannot be taught remotely is handling the apparatus, and that belongs in the school's own laboratory under any arrangement, including one with a tutor who travels. So the honest position for a family here is that online delivery costs nothing in practical science and saves the commute, provided the student makes full use of the laboratory time the school gives them.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the year
paragraphs: School days shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon and changes the tutoring question for a commuting household. The bus comes back earlier, so an afternoon session becomes physically possible for the first time in the year - and concentration in the late afternoon during the month is usually poor, so it is often money spent on an hour nobody benefits from.

The two slots that work are weekend mornings and after Iftar on weekdays. Because no tutor is travelling, moving to a post-Iftar slot is a scheduling decision rather than a logistical one, and it should be fixed before the month begins rather than renegotiated weekly. In most years the month also overlaps with revision for the June series, so the plan has to account for both rather than treating Ramadan as a pause.

School holidays are the other structural opportunity, and they are worth more in this district than in most. The commute disappears, the evening timetable empties, and a two-hour block becomes possible. For rebuilding a genuinely missing topic - as opposed to technique work - holiday weeks are the only time that can be done properly without displacing school work.

The practical recommendation is to plan the year in three parts: term time as one fixed evening session plus a weekend morning, holidays as concentrated topic blocks, and Ramadan as weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots with the afternoon deliberately left alone. A household that plans the year this way sustains the arrangement; one that improvises week to week usually stops by the second term.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

One arrangement to decline rather than pursue: the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own subject teacher, privately, is a problem for the teacher before it is a benefit to you.

What we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson; no guaranteed grades; no star ratings we cannot evidence with countable reviews; and no supplied board papers or mark schemes - we cite and link the official sources instead.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE home tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: You can get one-to-one IGCSE tutoring for a child living in International City, delivered live online rather than by a tutor coming to your flat. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers in India only. For a household in these clusters the online version has a practical advantage beyond the rate: no international school sits inside the district, so your child already spends an hour a day travelling, and an online session starts when the laptop opens rather than when a second person finishes crossing the city.

faqs.question: What time can tutoring realistically start from the clusters on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Around six. The school day may end at half past two, but the afternoon bus makes multiple stops and the Ras Al Khor and Dragon Mart junctions are slower in the afternoon, so a child travelling back from Silicon Oasis or Al Qusais often reaches home closer to four than half past three, and then needs to eat. Booking a four o'clock session against the timetable rather than the bus costs you the first ten minutes of most lessons for two years.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from International City usually attend?
faqs.answer: No international school sits inside the district, so they travel. The near group is Al Warqa and Al Qusais - GEMS Our Own English High School, Universal American School, The Millennium School Dubai, Apple International School, Dubai Scholars Private School. The middle group is Silicon Oasis and Academic City, including GEMS Wellington Academy and Dubai English Speaking College. The far group is Mirdif, Garhoud and Nad Al Sheba, chosen deliberately. Schools are named as context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: How do we fit tutoring around nine IGCSE subjects and a commute?
faqs.answer: By designing the week rather than filling it. One fixed weekday evening session from six, one named evening for the homework that session sets, two evenings protected for school work only, one weekend morning for a full timed paper, and a rest day. Two weekday evening sessions rarely work here, because the second lands on a tired student who still has school work to do and routinely delivers half the value of the first at the same price.

faqs.question: Why does the weekend morning matter so much in this district?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only time a full timed paper can be sat properly. A complete paper plus the mark-scheme walkthrough takes two to three hours, and that is not available on a weekday evening after a long commute at any price. Students who sit one complete paper a week from the first term of Year 11 arrive at the June series having practised the examination itself rather than having revised for it, which is a meaningfully different kind of preparation.

faqs.question: My child changed schools in Year 10. What should we check?
faqs.answer: Two things, and this happens more often in this district than in more settled neighbourhoods. First, the specification: a change of board mid-course leaves content covered under one syllabus and never under the other, which is invisible on a report and obvious in a marked paper. Second, the tier, because tier names and ceilings differ between boards. Ask both schools for the entry details and have one timed paper marked at the new specification to find the gap.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know the exact syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a provider who quotes before asking for it will teach a generic course. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, so hand-arithmetic drilling is essential for one and wasted for the other. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical; Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 have no practical examination at all. Ask the examinations officer for the entry list in writing.

faqs.question: How can my son prepare for practical science if he cannot get back to the lab?
faqs.answer: Apparatus handling has to happen in the timetabled laboratory sessions, which for a student travelling to Silicon Oasis or Al Qusais means making full use of the time the school gives. Everything else - identifying variables, choosing a range and interval, justifying repeats, reading scales precisely, recording to consistent significant figures, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, writing an evaluation that names a specific limitation - is taught on a screen with a real dataset, and that is where the written practical marks sit.

faqs.question: What should we ask for when mock results come out?
faqs.answer: The marked script and the question-level breakdown, not just the grade. Read it for pattern: marks lost evenly across a paper mean timing or technique, marks lost in clusters mean a topic, and marks lost heavily in the final third mean pacing. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is a question-style problem rather than a knowledge gap. For a double-award science, check whether the losses cluster in one of the three subject areas, because that decides how many tutors you need.

faqs.question: Do Ramadan timings change what we should book?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a way that surprises families here. The school day shortens so the bus comes back earlier, which makes an afternoon session physically possible for the first time all year - and late-afternoon concentration during the month is usually poor, so it is often an hour nobody benefits from. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Fix the pattern before the month starts rather than renegotiating weekly, and remember that revision for the June series usually overlaps.

faqs.question: Are school holidays a good time to buy tutoring?
faqs.answer: In this district, better than term time for certain work. The commute disappears, the evening timetable empties, and a two-hour block becomes possible, which is the only realistic way to rebuild a genuinely missing topic without displacing school work. Technique work suits term time; topic rebuilding suits holidays. Agree the session count before the block starts so the total is known, and keep the final fortnight before a series free of new content.

faqs.question: Is Core tier enough for a UAE university later?
faqs.answer: For Ministry of Education equivalency, yes. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Core tier reaches that comfortably. But equivalency is a floor, not an entry requirement: a sixth form asking for grade 6 in mathematics has excluded a Core candidate before the paper is sat.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE papers sat, and could we get the timetable wrong?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. On getting it wrong: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable for each, stating that using the correct version is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination otherwise. The zone belongs to the centre, not to your home address.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE tutoring cost for a family in these clusters?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers publishing them: budget and university-student online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. From this district that in-home premium buys a long journey against the same traffic your child just travelled.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed for a tutor teaching IGCSE privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students.
