intro.heading: The money question, answered with numbers rather than adjectives
paragraphs: Parents in Jumeirah Beach Residence researching an IGCSE home tutor run into the same wall. Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all. Two quote in US dollars, which is not what a Dubai household transacts in. One publishes an hourly rate in its page copy that contradicts the figure in its own structured data. A family trying to budget for Year 10 and Year 11 is left comparing adjectives, and adjectives are why people overpay.

So here are the bands, sourced and dated. In October 2026 the Dubai market runs at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutors and university students, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home one-to-one visit with travel priced in, AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards for an IGCSE or IB specialist, and AED 500 to AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages seen on the open market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. These come from published UAE agency rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

What the range does not tell you is where the money goes. Two quotes of AED 200 can buy completely different things. One buys sixty minutes of talking, with homework set and never read. The other buys sixty minutes of teaching plus a past paper marked against the published mark scheme between sessions, a written note to the parent, and a tutor who knows that your child's school enters 0580 rather than 4MA1. The second is cheaper per grade. The hourly figure cannot show you that, which is why this page spends more words on inclusions than on rates.

The delivery model matters to the arithmetic too, and it should be stated before any comparison is made. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Tuition for families in JBR is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. That is not a cost-saving dressed up as a feature: it removes travel from the price, removes the twenty minutes a tower block takes from the start of a visit, and removes distance from the list of filters applied when choosing who teaches your child.

The sections that follow take the cost question apart properly. What the market charges by provider model. The four places JBR families most often spend tutoring money without buying a grade. What a session should contain at each price point. How the Core and Extended decision changes both the bill and the grade ceiling. What examination entry costs if your child sits as a private candidate. And when the right financial decision is to stop paying, which no page in this market will tell you.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: Three qualification routes run through JBR households at ages 14 to 16, and each one carries a different cost profile because each one is examined differently. Knowing which your child's school enters is the first step in not paying for the wrong expertise.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a June series and a November series, with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0500 First Language English. Most subjects split into Core and Extended, which changes both the papers sat and the grade ceiling. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: The zone detail is a real cost risk rather than trivia. Cambridge states that using the wrong zone timetable means it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination. A tutor planning revision against the wrong version wastes paid hours on a schedule that does not apply to your child's centre.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Available in May/June and November each year, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. Tiering runs Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and several subjects allow a modular route where units are banked separately. Calculators are permitted in both Mathematics papers, which changes what revision time should be spent on.
programmes.countryNote: For a JBR family the modular option is the one with budget consequences. Banking a unit early can reduce the pressure, and the cost, of a single heavy final term. It also means an entry decision made in Year 10 affects what tutoring is worth buying in Year 11, so the conversation belongs early rather than in March.

programmes.name: What comes after: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai run IGCSE to 16 and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. The choice changes which IGCSE grades matter: a prospective Mathematics or Physics A Level student needs the Extended or Higher tier content secured, while a Diploma applicant is judged on breadth across six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: This is where tutoring money is best targeted in Year 11. Spending on the two subjects that gate the next stage usually returns more than spreading the same budget across five. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, so the post-16 choice in this area is widening.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: UAE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.
programmes.countryNote: The reason this belongs on a cost page is that one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, and families who believe it buy a sixth subject's worth of tutoring they did not need. The five-subject rule is what the published clarification states. Verify your own case with the Ministry rather than with a tutoring website, including this one.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects JBR families book most, with the syllabus codes and the specific place marks go missing. Each description says what a paid hour should be spent on, because that is the difference between tutoring that returns a grade and tutoring that returns a receipt.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge, 4MA1 Edexcel)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge now sets a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator paper, which exposes students whose fluency lives in the device. Edexcel permits calculators in both papers. Paid hours are best spent on algebraic manipulation and on reading the command word, not on topic revision a textbook already covers.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route, with investigation and modelling papers that reward exploration rather than recall. Students moving from 0580 find the paper style unfamiliar before they find the content hard. A tutor who has not taught 0607 specifically will spend your money teaching 0580 technique that scores less well here.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge, 4PH1 Edexcel)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where Extended candidates lose most marks, usually on circuit reasoning rather than on formulae. Practical assessment differs between boards and routes, so confirm which paper your child sits before buying practical-skills hours. Unit errors in multi-step calculations cost more marks than any single topic.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge, 4CH1 Edexcel)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. The questions requiring an explanation rather than a recall sentence are the ones that separate tiers. Worth paying for: structured practice on explanation-length answers, marked against the published mark scheme.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge, 4BI1 Edexcel)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Content-heavy and therefore the subject families most often over-tutor. The marks are in precision of terminology and in answering at the depth the command word asks. An hour spent on past-paper answer length usually beats an hour spent re-reading transport in plants.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two or one grade, which changes revision economics completely. Students often study it without realising which content is excluded from their award. Clarifying that first can remove whole topics from a revision plan, and that is tutoring money saved rather than spent.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500, 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task reward control of register and structure far more than vocabulary. Reading-response marks are lost by quoting rather than analysing. Progress here is measurable within four or five sessions if the work is marked, and invisible for a term if it is not.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: A distinct qualification from First Language English with different papers and expectations, and a common and expensive mix-up at enrolment. Listening and the summary task carry predictable mark patterns, which makes short, frequent sessions better value than long ones.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation language are the two gains available quickly. Case-study questions need application to the given business, not a general answer about businesses. Both subjects reward a repeatable answer structure, which is a short piece of work rather than a term of lessons.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Two very different subjects frequently confused when a tutor is hired. Computer Science examines pseudocode, trace tables and data representation under examination conditions. ICT examines practical application within software. Confirming which one your child sits prevents a term of well-taught irrelevance.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Arabic as a Second Language (0544)
subjects.description: Mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabic as a first language by group. Tutoring demand here outstrips supply, so booking early costs less than booking in the final term.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.regionsTitle: Where IGCSE families around JBR actually are
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: Rates do not vary much by community in this corner of Dubai, but what a family gets for the money does, because building type, bandwidth and the length of the school run differ street by street. These are the communities booking alongside JBR.

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: High-density towers on the beachfront, where an in-home visit pays a hidden tax in visitor parking and lift time. The same AED 250 buys noticeably less teaching here than in a villa community, which is the core of the cost argument on this page.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: One bridge in and out, and a tutor charging travel is charging for that bridge at the worst hour of the day. Households here book the same online slots as JBR and pay for teaching rather than for the crossing.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Tower living with the same parking arithmetic as JBR. Families comparing quotes between the two communities should compare inclusions, since the headline rate is effectively identical across the tram line.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Apartment study space is the variable that matters most here. A quiet corner and headphones improve an online session more than a higher hourly rate does, and both are free.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Shorter school runs and earlier arrivals home, which means a 16:15 start is realistic. More of the paid hour lands on teaching when nobody is still travelling at the start of it.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities where in-home visits lose less time, so the cost comparison is genuinely closer. The remaining difference is the tutor pool: distance still filters who is available at Extended tier in the sciences.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Closest to the senior school cluster, so families here often buy fewer hours overall simply because the student arrives home with energy left. Session length rather than session count is the lever worth pulling.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Households frequently running two or three children through IGCSE at once, where the question is how to split a fixed budget across siblings. Concentrating spend on the subjects that gate the next stage beats spreading it evenly.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools within reach of JBR
schoolClusters.note: The schools JBR Year 10 and 11 students most often attend. Which board each enters matters more to a tutoring budget than the school's reputation does, because a tutor fluent in 0580 is not automatically fluent in 4MA1.

schoolClusters.city: Schools running both IGCSE and the IB Diploma
schoolClusters.note: Several schools near JBR take students through IGCSE at 16 and then into the Diploma, which changes which Year 11 grades carry weight. Families here should buy tutoring for the subjects the Diploma will build on.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where a private-candidate route comes up
schoolClusters.note: Students who have moved mid-cycle, repeated a subject or taken an extra IGCSE outside school sometimes sit as private candidates through an examination centre rather than their school, which carries its own entry costs and deadlines.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: The lowest-cost format that reliably moves a grade: one hour a week in a single subject, with a past paper or exercise marked between sessions. Buying one subject properly outperforms buying three subjects thinly on the same budget, because a thin hour spread across three syllabuses becomes homework review rather than teaching.

This saves a slot in a crowded week and often a little on rate, but only works where the pairing is genuine. Paying one tutor for two unrelated subjects buys a specialist in one and a generalist in the other.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in JBR costs, by provider model
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in JBR, meaning somebody who drives to the tower, is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour in this market, with travel either included in that figure or added to it. The Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise between AED 200 and AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit lower, at AED 150 to AED 300. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and lessons for JBR families are delivered online.

Comparing those figures requires knowing what each model carries. An agency rate includes a margin for matching, replacement and administration, which is worth something if a tutor leaves mid-term and worthless if the agency has nobody to replace them with. A freelance rate is lower and carries no replacement at all. A tuition centre group class looks cheapest per hour at AED 90 to AED 200 per student, but the attention per student falls with group size, which is why a centre class and a one-to-one hour are not substitutes at any price.

The table below sets the models side by side on the questions that change value rather than on rate alone. Every band is attributed, and every band is a market figure rather than an IB Gram price. For what IB Gram charges, the trial lesson and the consultation give a real number for your child's subject and level; publishing one figure for every combination would be inaccurate rather than transparent.

sections.heading: The four places JBR families lose tutoring money
paragraphs: Overspending in this market is rarely a matter of paying too high a rate. It is a matter of buying the wrong thing at a fair rate, and the same four errors recur across this neighbourhood. The first is buying hours in the wrong board. A tutor who knows Cambridge 0580 inside out and is handed a child sitting Pearson 4MA1 will teach good mathematics against the wrong paper style, the wrong tier labels and the wrong calculator rules. The grade moves less than the invoice suggests it should.

The second is paying for travel in a tower block. An in-home visit in JBR spends real minutes on basement parking, the security desk and a lift at the hour the whole building comes home, and those minutes are billed. The third is buying unmarked hours. A session with no marked work between visits produces a student who feels tutored and a paper that nobody has diagnosed, and diagnosis is most of what a tutor is for at this level.

The fourth is over-buying breadth. A family with a fixed budget often splits it across four subjects at thirty minutes each, which produces four homework reviews rather than one piece of teaching. Concentrating the same spend on the one or two subjects that gate the next stage returns more. The audit table below puts numbers against each error so the comparison is concrete rather than rhetorical. Read the table as a shortlist of questions to ask before the first invoice rather than as a verdict on any one provider, because the same error costs a different amount at each tier.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and the whole bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is a marginal cost sitting on top of a large fixed one, and judging it in isolation leads families to both overspend and underspend. The useful context in Dubai right now is that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second phase of Dubai's economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A household whose largest education line has held flat is in a better position to judge a tutoring decision against a known total.

The rest of the bill is less visible. Examination entry for a private candidate is charged per subject by the examination centre, and the centre sets that fee rather than the board, so it varies across Dubai and has to be asked for directly. Resources are a smaller line than parents expect, because board syllabuses, specimen papers and past papers are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own websites. No tutor should be charging you for material the board gives away, and no tutor should be supplying board papers or mark schemes as downloads, which is the board's copyright.

The table below assembles the full picture for a JBR family running one child through Year 11. The tutoring rows use the market bands published above; the school fee row is left to the family's own invoice because fees vary by school and year group by a wide margin. The point of the table is the ratio: tutoring at one hour a week is a small fraction of a Dubai school fee, which is why the question worth asking is whether it is targeted, not whether it is affordable.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that changes both the bill and the ceiling
paragraphs: Tier choice is the single most consequential cost decision in IGCSE and the one families discuss least. Cambridge Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ranges: Core candidates cannot be awarded above a C, while Extended reaches A*. Pearson runs Foundation and Higher on the same logic. A student entered at Core who needed Extended has a ceiling placed on them by an administrative decision, and no amount of tutoring lifts it after entries close.

That cuts the other way too, and this is where money gets wasted most quietly. A student entered at Extended who is not secure on Core content will score poorly on papers aimed above their current level, and the family then buys more hours to chase marks on material the student is not ready for. The honest conversation is about which tier matches current attainment and what the next stage requires, and it needs to happen before the school's entry deadline rather than after a disappointing mock.

The tutoring implication is practical. Moving a student from secure Core to viable Extended is a defined piece of work with a defined number of weeks, usually concentrated in the topics Extended adds rather than spread across the whole syllabus. Framed that way it is a budgetable project. Framed as general improvement it becomes an open-ended monthly cost with no finish line, which is how tutoring bills in this city quietly run for two years. The way out is to write the finish line down before booking: a tier, a target grade and the series it will be sat in, all three agreed with the school.

sections.heading: Which board, and why the answer changes what a tutor is worth
paragraphs: Before any rate is agreed, find out which board your child's school enters. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are the two dominant routes in Dubai, with OxfordAQA present in some centres. They examine the same subject differently enough that a tutor fluent in one is doing guesswork in the other. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 now sets a non-calculator paper; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Tiering is Core and Extended at Cambridge and Foundation and Higher at Pearson. Pearson offers modular banking in some subjects; Cambridge does not work that way.

The practical test for a prospective tutor is short and costs nothing. Ask which syllabus code they are teaching to. A tutor who answers "IGCSE maths" is telling you they will find out later at your expense. A tutor who answers "0580 Extended, and I would want to see whether the school has entered her for Paper 2 and Paper 4" has already done the work. Series availability differs too: Cambridge runs June and November series, while Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November.

Entry deadlines are the detail that makes this urgent rather than academic. Cambridge sets the final entry deadline for each series per timetable zone, and for a June series it falls in the spring, months before the papers; Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 window ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with its deadline long past by the time it opened. That gap between the entry deadline and the paper is months wide, which means tier and board decisions are locked long before the revision term in which families usually start thinking about tutoring. Always check the live official timetable, since boards revise provisional dates.

sections.heading: What a session should contain at each price point
paragraphs: A rate on its own is not information. What makes AED 180 expensive or AED 320 cheap is the list of things that happen around the hour. At the bottom of the market, below roughly AED 150 online, expect live teaching and nothing else: no marking, no written note, no tracking of your child's school deadlines. That can be the right purchase for a confident student who needs a weekly question-and-answer session, and it is the wrong purchase for a student who does not know why they are losing marks.

In the AED 150 to AED 300 band, a qualified subject tutor teaching online should be naming the syllabus code, working from the student's own marked scripts, and sending something short in writing afterwards. Above AED 300, a specialist rate should be buying diagnosis: a paper marked against the published mark scheme with the mark allocation explained, a view on tier and entry, and a plan keyed to the school's deadline calendar rather than to a generic revision timetable.

Two things should be inside the rate at every level and frequently are not. The first is marked work between sessions, because the error pattern on a timed script is the only reliable diagnosis available. The second is honesty about progress, including the sentence nobody wants to deliver: this is not working, and here is what would. A tutor who cannot say that is charging you for optimism, and over a Dubai school year optimism is the most expensive item on the invoice.
bullets: Below AED 150 online: live teaching only, suited to a confident student
AED 150-300: syllabus code named, student's own scripts used, written note after
Above AED 300: marked papers, tier advice, plan built on school deadlines
At every level: marked work included, and a willingness to say it is not working

sections.heading: The permit question, and why the cheapest tutor can cost the most
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tutor work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone.

Because the permit is free, a tutor without one is not saving you money. They are carrying a risk you cannot see and offering no recourse if the arrangement goes wrong mid-term. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A tutor who cannot discuss their permit status when asked has told you something useful for free.

One further boundary belongs here because it is a cost question as well as an ethical one. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Paying a premium for your child's own class teacher is therefore buying an arrangement that may not survive scrutiny. That is reported policy rather than quoted regulation, so verify the current wording with the authority before relying on it.

sections.heading: When the right financial decision is to stop
paragraphs: No page selling tutoring tells you when to stop buying it, so this one will. There are three clear signals. The first is that marked papers have stopped improving across six to eight weeks of consistent work. That is not a reason to add hours; it is a reason to change the diagnosis, because more of an intervention that is not working costs more and returns the same. The second is that the student has stopped bringing anything to the session. A tutored hour with no work attached to it is a conversation, and conversations are cheaper elsewhere.

The third is the end of the series. Once the written papers are sat, tutoring in that subject should stop rather than taper indefinitely, and the enquiry-about-results window belongs to the school rather than to a tutor. Families who keep a weekly slot running through the summer out of habit spend several thousand dirhams on momentum they do not need, and the student would be better served by the break.

What should happen instead at each of those points is a review rather than a renewal. If a subject has stabilised, the hours move to the one that has not, or they stop. If nothing is moving, that is said plainly and the arrangement ends. A trial lesson exists so the match is tested before any commitment, and it takes no card details to book. The honest outcome of a bad fit is a different tutor or no tutor, not a term of billed sessions nobody believes in.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes, not the subject names
process.description: The most useful first message names the school, the exam board and the syllabus codes your child is entered for, plus the tier if it is already decided. That one detail prevents the most expensive error in this market, which is paying a competent tutor to teach against the wrong paper.

process.title: Get the band before you get the quote
process.description: You have the Dubai market bands on this page with their sources. Use them to sanity-check any quote you receive, from IB Gram or anywhere else. A figure well outside the band in either direction deserves a question about what is included rather than an assumption about quality.

process.title: Trial lesson on real marked work
process.description: The first session is a trial, booked without card details, and it should run on your child's own returned paper rather than on introductions. You get a short written note afterwards saying what the tutor found, which tier they think fits and what they would do in the first month.

process.title: Agree what sits inside the rate
process.description: Before the second session, settle three things in writing: whether marked papers are included, what the written follow-up looks like, and how the plan maps to your school's own deadlines. Those three inclusions are what separate two identical-looking hourly figures.

process.title: Review on marked evidence every six weeks
process.description: Every six weeks, look at the marked scripts rather than at the sessions attended. If the marks are moving, continue. If a subject has stabilised, move the hours. If nothing is moving, change the approach or stop, which is the review this page exists to make easy to ask for.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to a published rate card or a named survey and dated October 2026. Most pages in this search publish no figure at all, and two of those that do quote US dollars. A number you cannot trace is not useful for a budget decision.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons to JBR are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, so nothing in the rate pays for a drive across Dubai or for the twenty minutes a tower block takes from the start of a visit. The hour booked is the hour taught.

whyPoints.title: Marked work treated as standard, not an extra
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis that makes tutoring work comes from a timed script marked against the published mark scheme. That belongs inside the rate. A cheaper hour that omits it produces a student who feels supported and an error pattern nobody has examined.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus code matched before the first booking
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on tiering, calculator rules and paper structure. Tutors are matched to the code your child is actually entered for, which removes the most common and least visible way tutoring money gets wasted in Dubai.

whyPoints.title: Board material referenced, never resold
whyPoints.description: Syllabuses, specimen papers and past papers are published free by Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked rather than supplied as downloads, because reproducing board material is a copyright matter. Nobody should be charging you for it.

whyPoints.title: A stated point at which to stop
whyPoints.description: The page sets out three signals that mean tutoring should end or change rather than continue: flat marked papers over six to eight weeks, a student bringing no work, and the close of the examination series. A provider unwilling to name those is selling renewal rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE home tutor in JBR cost per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced in, per the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and advertised independent rates, reviewed October 2026. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to AED 300, and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so these are market figures rather than a price list. In a JBR tower an in-home hour also loses ten to twenty minutes to parking, the security desk and the lift.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition cheaper than a tutor visiting our tower?
faqs.answer: On the published bands, yes: AED 150 to AED 300 online against AED 180 to AED 500 in-home, because the second figure carries travel. The larger saving is not on the rate though. It is on the minutes. A visit to a JBR tower spends real time on basement parking, a visitor pass and a shared lift at the hour the building fills up, and that time is billed. An online session starts at the agreed minute, so a sixty-minute booking is sixty minutes of teaching rather than forty-five.

faqs.question: How do I know whether I am paying for the right exam board?
faqs.answer: Ask the school which board and which syllabus code your child is entered for, then ask the tutor the same question before agreeing a rate. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 differ on tiering labels, calculator rules and paper structure, so a tutor fluent in one is estimating in the other. A tutor who answers with a code and a tier has already done the preparation. A tutor who answers "IGCSE maths" will learn your child's paper at your expense over the first few weeks.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor actually cost more over a Year 11?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the mechanism is specific rather than general. Below roughly AED 150 an hour online, sessions usually carry no marked work, which removes the diagnosis that makes tutoring effective. A student gets taught around their misconceptions instead of through them, and three months later the same marks appear. The cheaper hour is only the better buy for a confident student who needs a weekly question-and-answer session. For a student losing marks without knowing why, unmarked hours are the most expensive thing on the invoice.

faqs.question: Should we spread the budget across all my child's weak subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A fixed budget split across four subjects at half an hour each produces four homework reviews and no teaching depth, which is why families doing it see little movement and conclude tutoring does not work. Concentrating the same spend on one subject until marked papers improve, then moving to the second, returns more per dirham. Choose the subject that gates the next stage: a prospective Mathematics or Physics A Level student needs those secured far more than a broad half-grade lift across five.

faqs.question: Does the Core and Extended choice affect what tutoring is worth buying?
faqs.answer: It decides it. Cambridge Core cannot be awarded above a C while Extended reaches A*, and the equivalent split at Pearson is Foundation and Higher. A student entered at the wrong tier has either a ceiling tutoring cannot lift or papers aimed above their current level. Moving from secure Core to viable Extended is a defined piece of work, usually eight to sixteen weeks on the extension topics, which makes it budgetable. Confirm the entry with the school before buying hours, because entries close months before the papers.

faqs.question: Are past papers and mark schemes an extra cost?
faqs.answer: They should not be. Cambridge and Pearson publish syllabuses, specimen papers and past papers on their own websites, and no tutor should charge you for material the board gives away. Nor should a tutor supply board papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, which is the board's copyright. What you are reasonably paying for is a paper sat under real timing, marked against the published mark scheme, and the explanation of what the error pattern shows. That is work. The document itself is free.

faqs.question: What does examination entry cost if my child sits as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: The examination centre sets that fee per subject rather than the board, so it varies across Dubai and has to be asked for directly from the centre you intend to use. Ask early, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers: a Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, well before the first paper, and the Pearson November 2026 entry had closed long before a window that ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A tutoring plan built without reference to the entry deadline can miss the series entirely, which is the costliest error available.

faqs.question: Is a permit-free tutor a cheaper option in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, because the permit itself is free. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A tutor working without one is not passing a saving to you; they are carrying a risk of fines and penalties under the applicable laws and offering you no recourse mid-term. No fine amount is published, so treat any figure you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a short block before the exams rather than a whole year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many students it is the better purchase. A six to ten week block before a June or November series, built on timed papers marked against the published mark schemes, is good value where the content is broadly there and the marks are not. It is poor value where content is genuinely missing, because ten weeks will not cover a syllabus. The honest test is a marked past paper now: if the errors are technique and timing, a block works, and if whole topics are blank, it does not.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre a cheaper substitute for one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour, at roughly AED 90 to AED 200 per student for groups of two to four on published Dubai centre price lists, but it is not the same product. Attention divides by group size and the pace is set by the group rather than by your child's error pattern. Groups work well for covering breadth and keeping a student moving. A specific, diagnosed weakness in Extended Chemistry needs one-to-one. Using the group rate as a substitute saves money on the invoice and not on the grade.

faqs.question: How many subjects does my child actually need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published clarification states five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, and families who believe it buy tutoring they do not need. Verify your own case with the Ministry, not with a tutoring website.

faqs.question: What should be included in the rate that often is not?
faqs.answer: Three things. Marked work between sessions, because a timed script is the only reliable diagnosis at this level. A short written note to the parent, so you know what was found rather than only that an hour happened. And a plan keyed to your school's own internal deadlines and mock window, which differ between Dubai schools by several weeks. Settle all three before the second session. They are what make two identical hourly figures worth completely different amounts.

faqs.question: At what point should a JBR family stop paying for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three signals. Marked papers have not improved across six to eight weeks of consistent work, which calls for a changed diagnosis rather than more hours. The student brings nothing to the session, which turns a paid hour into a conversation. Or the examination series has been sat, at which point the subject should close rather than taper through the summer. At each point the right action is a review on marked evidence, not an automatic renewal. A provider who will not name a stopping point is selling renewal.

faqs.question: Do rates in Dubai rise closer to the examination series?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards tend not to change, but availability does, and that has the same effect on your options. In the weeks before a June or November series the specialists with convenient slots are already committed, so what remains is either a less suitable match or a less convenient time. Families booking in October for a June series get both the tutor and the slot they want. Families booking in March usually get one of the two, and sometimes pay a premium band for the privilege.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.closingHeading: Budget the subject, not the hour
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jbr.closingBody: If you are pricing an IGCSE home tutor in JBR, the figure that matters is not the hourly rate. It is what the hour contains and whether it is pointed at the right syllabus code, the right tier and the subject that gates your child's next stage. Send us the school, the board, the codes and the tier, and you will get a tutor matched to exactly that, a trial lesson booked without card details, and a written note on what the marked work shows. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video to JBR in Gulf Standard Time, with marked papers inside the rate rather than beside it.

intro.heading: Four communities, one answer: why the Jebel Ali comparison keeps ending in the same place
paragraphs: Families in this part of Dubai do their tutoring research by comparison. A parent in Jebel Ali Village asks friends in Al Furjan what they pay. Someone in Green Community gets a quote and checks it against Discovery Gardens. A family that has just moved to Dubai South discovers that the agency which happily serves Al Furjan will not take a booking that far out, or will only take it at a higher rate.

The comparison is worth doing, because the quotes genuinely differ. What surprises most parents is where the difference comes from. It is not teaching quality and it is not the exam board. It is the drive. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western end of Dubai, wrapped around the port and the free zone, and the residential communities around it are spread out. A tutor living in Mirdif or Al Barsha and taking a 5pm booking in Emaar South is committing to a round trip that eats the evening.

That drive gets priced, and it gets priced in two ways. The visible way is the hourly rate: Dubai rate guides put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors as high as AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online. The invisible way is choice. A family in Jebel Ali choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from the people willing to drive there, which for Cambridge Chemistry 0620 or Edexcel Further Pure Maths is a very short list.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we say so near the top of the page rather than at the bottom of a terms link. For Jebel Ali and Dubai South families, lessons are live, one-to-one and over video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the tutor and student annotate the same past-paper question together.

The effect of that on the comparison is simple and it is the point of this page. Once the tutor is not driving, Jebel Ali Village, Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Green Community, Dubai Investments Park, Dubai South and Emaar South become the same place. The same Cambridge 0580 specialist is available to all of them, at the same time, at the same rate. The neighbourhood question stops being a constraint on who can teach your child.

What still differs between these communities is the school set, the exam board in use, and what time a session can realistically start given the school run. Those are covered below, with the board comparison, the AED table and the examination calendar counted backwards from the series your child is actually entered for. Read the board comparison first; it is the one that most often turns out to have been the real problem all along.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.programmesIntro: An IGCSE student in this catchment is on one of two boards, sometimes both at once across different subjects, and is heading for one of two sixth-form routes. The differences are concrete and they change how a tutor prepares.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-coded qualifications such as Mathematics 0580, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610, graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the subject and the school's choice. Most subjects offer a Core and an Extended route, and the Core route caps the attainable grade. Cambridge runs exams in a June series and a November series, with centres allocated to one of six administrative zones.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park set run Cambridge. The zone rule matters here: Cambridge states that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and that it is essential to use the correct timetable version, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Biology 4BI1, graded 9-1, with Foundation and Higher tiers in the tiered subjects. Exams run in a May/June window and a November window each year. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and revises them, so the live PDF is the only safe reference.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's recent UAE-relevant dates are checkable: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January gap is the detail that catches out families planning a sixth-form application.

programmes.name: What comes after: IB Diploma or A Level
programmes.description: The IGCSE year ends in a branch. The IB Diploma takes six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, graded out of 45. A Levels take three or four subjects in depth. The choice is made during Year 11, usually before the IGCSE results arrive, on predicted grades.
programmes.countryNote: Within this catchment both routes are available without leaving the area: Greenfield International School and Fairgreen International School run IB programmes, Sunmarke School offers the Diploma alongside a UK route, and The Winchester School Jebel Ali and Dove Green Private School run the A-Level path. The decision is therefore a curriculum decision rather than a relocation decision.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE, with optional Checkpoint tests Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Nothing here appears on a school-leaving certificate, which is exactly why gaps formed in Years 8 and 9 surface as unexplained IGCSE underperformance in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Furjan and Green Community often start tutoring in Year 9 for this reason, once they have seen a Checkpoint report. It is the cheapest point of intervention in the whole school career, because fixing algebraic fluency at 13 costs a term and fixing it at 16 costs a grade.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most requested across the Jebel Ali and Dubai South communities, with the syllabus code and the part of the specification where marks actually go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. Edexcel 4MA1 runs two papers of equal weight. Marks are lost on unwritten method lines and on rounding at an intermediate step rather than at the end.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits is the recurring weak topic, followed by moments and pressure. Students who can recite a formula but cannot rearrange it under time pressure lose the second half of every multi-part question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry carry the difficulty. The practical paper rewards precision about apparatus and about why a particular step controls a variable, which is rarely taught explicitly in class.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. The difference between "state", "describe" and "explain" decides whether a six-mark answer earns two marks or five, and the fix is drills rather than revision.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages paper. Marks go to candidates who write for the specified audience and form; a strong essay in the wrong register scores below a competent one in the right one.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an assessed speaking component. Very common in this catchment given the mix of home languages, and the writing mark rises fastest with structured paragraph planning.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy in Economics and case-study discipline in Business Studies. The highest-tariff questions ask for evaluation, and candidates who list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap themselves.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation and the practical ICT tasks. Students who code confidently in Python still lose theory marks on binary, hexadecimal and network concepts, which are examined in prose.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for Higher Level maths or A-Level Further Maths. Narrow tutor pool locally, which is precisely where online matching changes the available choice.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA mandating separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. A tutor must know which stream your child sits before the first lesson.

sections.heading: What the Jebel Ali quote and the Al Furjan quote are actually measuring
paragraphs: Put two in-home quotes side by side and the difference is almost always distance. Both tutors teach the same syllabus. One lives twelve minutes from Al Furjan and one is coming from across the city to Emaar South. The second quote is higher, offers fewer possible slots, and carries a higher chance of a cancelled lesson, and none of that reflects on either tutor.

This is why neighbourhood comparison shopping produces confusing results in this part of Dubai. A parent concludes that Dubai South is an expensive place to get tutoring, when what they have actually discovered is that Dubai South is a long way from where most tutors live. The qualification being bought is identical. The qualification your child sits does not change by postcode, and neither does the mark scheme that will be applied to their paper in August.

There is a second, quieter effect. In a community where only a handful of tutors will travel, the parent takes what is available. A Year 11 needing Cambridge Chemistry 0620 ends up with a general science tutor because that is who said yes. The specification difference between a general science background and 0620 mole calculations shows up in the mocks, not in the first month.

Once lessons are delivered live online, both effects disappear at once. There is no drive to price and no drive to limit the list. Every community in this cluster gets the same pool. That is the entire argument of this page, and the tables below put numbers against it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the differences that change a lesson plan
paragraphs: Parents in this cluster routinely discover halfway through Year 11 that the neighbour's child sits a different board. Both are International GCSEs, both are accepted by UAE and overseas universities, and they are not interchangeable in the classroom. The paper structures differ, the tiering differs, and some topics sit in one specification and not the other.

Cambridge divides most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core candidates sitting one pair of papers and Extended candidates another, and the Core route carries a lower grade ceiling. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in the tiered subjects, with Mathematics A 4MA1 running two equally weighted papers. For a tutor, that means a different past-paper diet and a different sequence of topics.

The administrative differences matter too. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable can cost a candidate their exam, stating that it cannot accept responsibility in that case. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then revises them, which is why any page restating dates rather than linking the live PDF is a hazard rather than a help.

The first question we ask a Jebel Ali or Al Furjan family is therefore not "which subject" but "which code". If you do not know, your child's exam entry statement does, and so does the subject page on the school's curriculum section. Getting this wrong costs a term of preparation aimed at the wrong paper.

sections.heading: The IGCSE market in AED, read from the monthly cost upward
paragraphs: Most families in this cluster do not budget by the hour. They budget by the month, because that is how the school fee arrives and that is what the household plan has room for. So read the market from the monthly end first, then check the hourly figure against it.

Dubai rate guidance published for 2026 puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Published packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those two numbers are the comparison in miniature: roughly double the monthly cost for half the number of visits.

The hourly bands behind those monthly figures, as published in October 2026: EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33-52 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online; Dubai rate guides put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors to AED 500; TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work and one premium provider, BartyED, publishes AED 650.

None of these are IB Gram prices and we do not publish a rate card on this page, because the fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. What the bands are for is judgement. A quote of AED 500 an hour for Cambridge 0580 in Al Furjan is at the top of the in-home band for a subject with the widest tutor supply in the market, and you are entitled to ask what the premium buys.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: This is the single most consequential academic decision in the IGCSE years and it is frequently made badly, usually in the wrong direction. A Year 10 student has a poor term, the school suggests the Core route to protect the grade, and the family agrees because it sounds like safety. The grade ceiling that comes with it only becomes visible when the sixth-form entry requirement arrives eighteen months later.

The honest framing is that Core and Foundation exist for students for whom the Extended or Higher paper would produce a very low grade, and for those students they are the right choice. They are not a revision strategy and they are not a stress-management tool. If a student is capable of the higher route with support, moving down to protect a term's confidence trades a short-term comfort for a long-term constraint.

The way to decide is with evidence rather than impression. Sit a timed paper at each route, have it marked against the official scheme, and look at what the marks say rather than how the hour felt. A student who scores low on the Extended paper because of unwritten method and rounding errors is not a Core candidate; they are an Extended candidate with two fixable habits. A student who cannot access the questions at all is a different case, and the marking makes the difference obvious.

Then check the destination. A sixth form offering the IB Diploma or A Level Mathematics will have a stated entry grade, and some of those grades are not reachable from the Core route at all. Make the tier decision after reading the entry requirement, not before.

sections.heading: The examination calendar, counted backwards from the series your child sits
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, and a page telling a Dubai parent otherwise has handed them a date they will act on and a deadline that does not apply. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

The useful way to read a calendar is backwards from the paper, because every milestone that matters sits months earlier. Final entries close well before the exams. Mocks land a term ahead. Coursework and practical components, where the subject has them, close earlier still. By the time a family starts worrying, two of those doors have usually closed.

Checkable Pearson dates give the shape of it. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - a four-week gap into the new year that catches families who assumed a November resit would be confirmed before the spring sixth-form deadlines.

Two practical rules follow. Work from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. And ask your centre which Cambridge administrative zone it sits in, because Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable.

sections.heading: What UAE Ministry of Education equivalency actually requires of an IGCSE student
paragraphs: Families in this catchment planning a UAE university application need equivalency for the school-leaving certificate, and the British-track rule is published and specific. It is also widely misstated: one ranking page in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published requirement says.

For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail families most often get wrong in the other direction.

The American track is different again: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we read, so we do not publish one, and you should treat any page that does with caution until you have read it on moe.gov.ae.

Two boundaries worth stating plainly. Equivalency is a Ministry process and IB Gram neither performs it nor influences it; we describe it and point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one from a Dubai South or Jebel Ali address, with the limitations named
paragraphs: The case for online delivery in this cluster is unusually strong, and it is strongest in exactly the communities where in-home service is weakest. A family in Emaar South comparing an online specialist against an in-home generalist is not making a close call. A family in Al Furjan, where in-home supply is decent, has a genuine choice to make.

What online gives you is the full specialist pool, a session that can start at 4pm rather than 5.30pm, and a shared screen on which tutor and student annotate the same past-paper question at the same time. For diagnostic work - reading a marked script, counting where the marks went, rebuilding a method line - the shared screen is better than a single paper copy passed across a table.

The limitations are real and we would rather you heard them from us. A student who will not sit at a desk without an adult in the room does better with a person there. Children under about ten lose attention faster on a screen than in company. A weak connection shortens a lesson in practice even when the clock says otherwise. And a household where the only quiet space is shared - common in Discovery Gardens apartments - needs the slot planned around siblings rather than around the tutor.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE, so if your child is in one of those cases you should hire locally and you should ask the tutor for their MoHRE private tuition permit before the first lesson. That is a better outcome than us taking a booking we are the wrong fit for.

sections.heading: Where the boundary sits on coursework, and how to start
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where a component exists - a practical investigation, a speaking assessment, a piece of directed writing submitted for assessment - the same rule applies as anywhere else. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write it, redraft it into their own prose, or complete it.

This market contains services selling finished coursework, with one advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting bought work is a malpractice matter that can cost a student the qualification, and no price makes that a reasonable risk. We also do not host or distribute board papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because they are copyright material; we link the official sources instead.

Starting is deliberately short. Send the subject, the syllabus code if you have it, the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. The code tells us which specification to prepare; the marked paper tells us where the marks went, which is almost never where the student thinks. A specialist in that subject then runs a free one-to-one trial lesson online and writes up what the script showed.

If no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you want, we will say so and offer the real alternatives: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot opens, or an honest recommendation to look elsewhere. Nobody in this market publishes what happens when they cannot help, which is reason enough to put it on the page.

whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, teach method and mark drafts. They do not write or complete assessed work. Services in this market selling finished coursework expose the student to a malpractice finding, and that is not a risk worth any saving.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Jebel Ali, and should we pay for that?
faqs.answer: Local agencies do serve Jebel Ali, and Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per hour, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. The travel sits inside that figure. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Whether the premium is worth paying depends on your child. For a student who needs an adult present to start work, it probably is. For a Year 11 needing Cambridge 0620 mole calculations, the specialist matters more than the presence.

faqs.question: Why is a tutoring quote for Dubai South higher than one for Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Distance, almost always. Al Furjan has reasonable in-home tutor supply because it is close to where many tutors live and has metro access. Dubai South and Emaar South are a long drive from most of the city, so tutors either decline bookings there or price the journey in, and they offer fewer possible slots. The teaching and the qualification are identical. Once lessons are delivered live online there is no journey to price, which is why the same specialist is available to both communities at the same rate and the same hour.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board does my child's school in this area use?
faqs.answer: It varies within a single street, and sometimes within a single child's timetable, because schools can enter different subjects with different boards. The answer is on your child's exam entry statement, which lists the syllabus code: 0580 and 0620 are Cambridge, 4MA1 and 4CH1 are Pearson Edexcel. The school's curriculum pages usually state it as well. Ask before booking a tutor, because the specifications differ topic by topic and a term spent on the wrong past papers is a term that cannot be recovered in Year 11.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child in Jebel Ali be entered for?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered in India only, so any page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is giving you a date from another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window. Always confirm against the live official timetable, and ask your centre which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in, because the zone determines which timetable version applies to your child.

faqs.question: Should my child take the Core or the Extended route?
faqs.answer: Decide it on a marked timed paper at each route rather than on how the term has felt. Core and Foundation set a lower grade ceiling, which is the right choice for a student who cannot access the higher paper at all and the wrong choice as a confidence measure. A student losing Extended marks to unwritten method lines and premature rounding is an Extended candidate with two fixable habits. Check the sixth-form entry grade before confirming, because some IB Diploma and A Level maths entry requirements are not reachable from the Core route.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the Ministry of Education count for a Jebel Ali IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One page ranking in this market tells UAE parents the figure is six, which is not what the published rule says. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry of Education before you rely on it for an application.

faqs.question: What does an online IGCSE lesson from Green Community look like in practice?
faqs.answer: A video call at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, one tutor and one student, with a shared screen carrying either the student's marked script or a past-paper question both can annotate. The tutor works through the question with the student writing, not watching. Sessions run 60 or 90 minutes, and a short written note afterwards records what was covered and what to do before the next one. For diagnostic work the shared screen is better than a paper copy, because both people are looking at the same mark line at the same moment.

faqs.question: Is online tuition really cheaper than a home tutor in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: On published figures, yes, and the gap is mostly travel. Qualified online subject tutors in Dubai are advertised from around AED 150-300 per hour, while in-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 with independent tutors to AED 500. Monthly packages tell the same story: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home visits. Those are market figures published in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. The saving is real, but the bigger difference for an exam-year student is usually the width of the specialist pool.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE practical or coursework component?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the method, explain what the assessment criteria reward, discuss why a step controls a variable, and give feedback on the student's own write-up. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it into their own words or complete it. Services in this market sell finished coursework, one of them advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and submitting bought work risks the qualification itself. Practical procedures happen in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision, as the specification requires.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit needed to tutor a Year 11 privately in Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. Ask any independent tutor directly before the first lesson; because it costs nothing to hold, a straight answer is a fair expectation.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with mocks in a few weeks. What is worth doing now?
faqs.answer: A timed-paper cycle rather than more content. Sit one full paper under real timing, have it marked against the official scheme by someone who is not the student, and turn the marking into a ranked list of repeated habits. Most students lose a consistent five to fifteen marks a paper to three or four habits: skipped method lines, rounding at intermediate steps, command terms answered too shallowly, and questions abandoned after the first part. Habits move in weeks. A year of missed content does not, and an honest tutor will tell you which you have.

faqs.question: Can we use one tutor for both of our children in different year groups?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the distance between them. One maths specialist can reasonably hold a Year 9 and a Year 11 on the same board, because the content is continuous. A Year 7 and a Year 11 are different jobs with different pacing, and a Core-route Year 10 and an Extended-route Year 11 need different past-paper diets even in the same subject. Each child gets their own slot in any case, since these are one-to-one lessons. Tell us both year groups at the enquiry stage and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits.

faqs.question: Do you offer lessons in Arabic for the Dubai mandatory subject requirement?
faqs.answer: We cover Arabic streams, and the first step is identifying which one your child sits. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and it mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires schools to ensure teachers of these subjects hold appropriate KHDA approval. Tell us the stream and the school's scheme of work.

faqs.question: What happens to our weekly slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves, and we plan the move rather than improvising it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and household evenings reorganise around iftar, so a 5pm weekday slot usually becomes either early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. Because no tutor is travelling to an address, shifting a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute, and it can shift back afterwards just as easily. Families with a live series approaching usually keep the frequency and change only the hour, which is the arrangement that holds up best.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we start with is the wrong fit for our Year 11?
faqs.answer: Say so after the first or second session rather than waiting a term. The usual cause is pace rather than competence: a tutor pitched for a confident Extended candidate working with a student who needs the method rebuilt from Year 9, or the reverse. We change the tutor rather than asking the student to adapt, and the written session notes make the mismatch easy to describe precisely. The free trial lesson exists for this reason, which is why it is a diagnostic lesson with a written outcome rather than an introductory call.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingHeading: Compare the communities, then stop letting geography pick the tutor
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingBody: If you have been comparing what an IGCSE home tutor in Jebel Ali costs against quotes from Al Furjan, Green Community or Dubai South, the pattern you have found is a travel premium rather than a quality difference. Send us the subject, the syllabus code and a photograph of your child's last marked paper. A specialist on that board reads the script, names where the marks went, and teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online at a Gulf Standard Time slot that suits the school run. You get the written diagnosis either way. After that it is a fixed weekly slot with the same tutor, reviewed against the mocks and the series your child is actually entered for.

Each works to a named syllabus code rather than to a generic Year 10 scheme, and session times are set around the commute home.

intro.heading: Working up from the cheapest IGCSE tutoring in JLT, not down from the dearest
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages start at the premium end and reason downwards, which makes every tier below look like a compromise. Start at the bottom instead. Tutopiya advertises online tutoring in this market from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At those rates you are generally buying a capable university student who knows the subject at their own level, has not taught the syllabus, and will not have seen a mark scheme for the code your child is entered against. For checking homework in Year 9, that is often enough, and paying more would be waste.

The next tier up is a qualified subject tutor working online, quoted at AED 150 to 300. Unitors publishes AED 150 upward for IGCSE and AED 200 upward for IB. What the extra buys is syllabus-specific: someone who knows that Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel ask different things of the same physics content, who can tell you which paper your child's marks are being lost on, and who marks to the published criteria rather than to a general impression. For Year 10 and Year 11 that difference is the whole value.

Above that, a visiting tutor in a JLT tower is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. The jump from the online qualified tier to the in-home tier is not a jump in teaching. It is the cost of a car crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00, visitor registration at the tower desk, and the tutor's inability to teach anyone else during the drive. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and the honest reason is that the premium buys logistics rather than better lessons.

The second decision costs more than the tier decision, and almost nobody discusses it. An IGCSE student typically sits eight to ten subjects. Funding a weekly hour in each at a mid-market AED 220 would reach five figures a term, and it would be mostly wasted, because a student struggling with 0580 Extended algebra is not simultaneously struggling in nine ways. The useful question is which two or three subjects sit furthest below the grade the next step requires, and what the cheapest intervention in each of those looks like.

The third thing to get right before spending is the code. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Physics is 0625; the Pearson Edexcel equivalents include 4MA1 and 4PH1. The papers, the tiering and the assessment structure differ between boards for the same subject name, which is why a tutor who asks 'Cambridge or Edexcel, and which code?' in the first minute is worth more than one who asks what grade you want. Find the code on your child's exam entry sheet or ask the school's examinations officer, then hire against it.
