dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits in the middle of a longer route, and a JLT family funding Year 10 support is usually funding readiness for whatever comes at 16. The four stages below are the ones that affect how much tutoring is worth buying and when.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10-11
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects, examined externally, with tiering in several of them. Cambridge offers Core and Extended routes in subjects such as Mathematics 0580, and Pearson Edexcel offers Foundation and Higher tiers in subjects such as 4MA1. The tier decision caps the grade available, so it is a bigger decision than most families realise and it is often taken by the school on the basis of Year 9 evidence. Support is most efficient in Year 10, when the tier is still open.
programmes.countryNote: JLT students sit IGCSE at schools across Al Barsha, Barsha South, Al Sufouh and the Marina, and the boards vary by campus rather than by area. Two children in the same tower can be entered for different codes in the same subject, which is why a shared tutor arranged between neighbours in a JLT cluster frequently works for one child and not the other.

programmes.name: Years 7-9, before the entries are set
programmes.description: The cheapest useful tutoring in the whole route sits here, because nothing is examined and nothing is capped yet. A student whose fractions, ratio and algebraic manipulation are secure at the end of Year 9 keeps the Extended or Higher tier open in Mathematics, and the same holds for reading stamina in English. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, a short block in Year 9 is the lowest-cost intervention available in this market.
programmes.countryNote: JLT families often start looking in Year 11, which is the most expensive possible moment. Year 9 support costs less per hour, needs fewer hours, and influences the tier decision the school will make. If your child is in Year 9 now and wobbling in maths, that is the term to act, not the term before the papers.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma at 16
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide which post-16 routes are open. A Level courses usually require a grade threshold in the subject; the IB Diploma requires six subjects across groups and a reasonable spread. A student entered on a lower tier may meet the grade but not the entry requirement for the Higher Level version of the subject, which is the specific trap worth paying to avoid in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the JLT catchment run both A Levels and the IB Diploma, and the entry requirements differ between them. Ask the school for the published thresholds before deciding how much IGCSE support to fund, because that number tells you exactly how far your child has to travel and in which subject.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.ageRange: At the end of the school route
programmes.description: Equivalency converts a school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can accept. For the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five.
programmes.countryNote: That rule changes subject planning in Year 9 for a JLT family, because a household counting Arabic towards the five would think the requirement met when it is not. IB Gram does not perform, arrange or guarantee equivalency; verify the current wording with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority before relying on it.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: The grid below is organised around where marks are actually lost rather than around content lists, because that is what decides how many sessions a subject needs. Codes are given where they are the common ones in Dubai schools; confirm your child's own code on the entry sheet.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers at each tier, one with a calculator and one without under the current syllabus structure. Marks go on algebraic manipulation, on method marks never shown, and on reading a question's command word. The tier decision caps the grade, so check it before buying anything.

subjects.name: Additional or Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for Higher Level or A Level mathematics. It is the single best predictor of a comfortable Year 12 and the subject most often dropped under pressure. Support here is technique-dense and responds well to short blocks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit handling, rearranging formulae under time, and the practical or alternative-to-practical component. Electricity is the topic JLT parents raise most often, and it is fixable, because the problem is almost always circuit reasoning rather than arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic naming carry disproportionate marks relative to teaching time. Students who can describe a reaction but not calculate a yield lose marks in a predictable place, which makes this one of the cheapest subjects to lift with a short targeted block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with command terms doing the discriminating. 'Describe' and 'explain' demand different answers and students who revise content without revising answer shape sit below their knowledge. Diagram labelling and data questions are the other two recurring losses.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise retrieval and inference; writing questions reward structure and register. Marks are rarely about vocabulary. A small number of sessions on paragraph architecture and on timing usually moves a grade more than months of reading practice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different paper set from first-language English, with listening and speaking components. Students placed in the wrong course lose marks for reasons that have nothing to do with ability, so confirm which code your child is entered for before buying support.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definitions and the evaluation sentence at the end of a long answer. Students lose the final marks on almost every extended question by stopping at explanation, which is a teachable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the practical component. The written paper rewards precision in a way code that merely works does not, and that gap catches confident programmers who have never written a trace table under time.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: As organised by the school under KHDA requirements
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs. These sit outside the five subjects the equivalency rule counts, and tutoring must follow the school's own material, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Lettered clusters around four lakes, with visitor registration at most towers and permit-controlled podium parking. Year 10 and 11 students are generally home between 16:00 and 16:50, so 17:00 is the dependable start on a school night.

regions.name: The Greens

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Adjacent to The Greens with lighter evening traffic on the golf-course side. Year 11 students here tend to prefer a single longer weekend session during the spring term.

regions.name: Barsha South
regions.note: The route that adds most time to a JLT commute. Students travelling from here are home latest, and a 17:30 start is often the earliest that works.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: A destination rather than a residential base for most JLT families; several of the schools their children attend sit here. The campus matters more for timing than the home cluster does.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Immediately south of JLT with a large resident population and a different school mix, skewing towards Indian and British curricula. Session demand here concentrates on maths and the sciences.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The main destination cluster for JLT secondary students and a mix of Cambridge and Pearson entry across campuses. Two children in the same tower can be sitting different codes in the same subject, so ask the school rather than a neighbour.

schoolClusters.city: Marina, Al Sufouh and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The second cluster for JLT families, with several campuses running IGCSE before splitting into A Levels or the IB Diploma at 16. The post-16 entry thresholds differ between those routes and are worth reading before funding Year 11 support.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jlt.modesIntro: Three ways to buy IGCSE support, ordered cheapest first. Each is the right answer in a different situation, and the commonest mistake is buying the third when the first would have done.

modes.title: A diagnostic block of four sessions
modes.description: Four one-to-one online sessions on one subject, aimed at finding out exactly which paper and which question type is costing marks. It produces a written answer you can act on, including the answer that no further tutoring is needed. At the lower end of the qualified band this is the cheapest way to replace a guess with a plan, and it has a hard stop.
bullets: Four sessions, one subject, a written diagnosis at the end
Known total cost before you start
Can conclude that nothing further is needed
Best first purchase if you have never used a tutor

modes.title: A targeted paper block
modes.description: Six to ten sessions on the specific paper or component where marks are going, worked through past material under timed conditions with marking against the published criteria. This is where most IGCSE value sits, because an IGCSE grade is decided by paper technique at least as much as by content knowledge, and technique moves quickly once it is taught explicitly.
bullets: Scoped to one paper or component, not a whole subject
Timed practice marked to the published criteria
Six to ten sessions with a defined finish
Repeatable for a second subject if it works

modes.title: Weekly across Year 10 and 11
modes.description: A standing slot across both IGCSE years for a subject where the gap is structural rather than technical. It is the most expensive format and sometimes the correct one, particularly where a student is on the Extended or Higher tier with Year 9 foundations that were never secure. Enter it deliberately, with a termly review, rather than by renewal.
bullets: Same tutor across both years, continuous records
Appropriate where foundations rather than technique are the issue
Termly review with an explicit continue-or-stop decision
Highest total cost of the three formats

sections.heading: What each price tier actually delivers for IGCSE
paragraphs: Here is the market read from the bottom. The figures are the providers' own published rates, quoted with their sources, and none of them is IB Gram's price list. What matters in the table is not the number but the final column: the situation in which that tier is the right purchase. A parent who buys the top tier for a Year 9 homework problem has wasted money, and a parent who buys the bottom tier for a Year 11 Extended paper has wasted a year.

The pattern across tiers is that you are not buying more enthusiasm as you go up, you are buying narrower knowledge. A capable undergraduate at AED 45 an hour knows physics. A qualified subject tutor at AED 200 knows Cambridge 0625 Physics, which paper the practical skills are examined on, and what the mark scheme accepts as a complete answer. Those are different products and only one of them is priced by the hour in a way that reflects the work.

Note where the in-home band sits in the table. At AED 180 to 500 it overlaps the specialist online band entirely, which means a family paying in-home rates is often paying specialist money for non-specialist teaching, with the difference going on the drive. That is the specific waste this page exists to name, and it is easy to test: ask a visiting tutor what the rate would be without travel, and ask which syllabus codes they have taught.

The step up the tiers buys narrower syllabus knowledge, not more effort

sections.heading: Eight to ten subjects, and the two or three worth funding
paragraphs: This is the decision that moves the total spend more than any rate negotiation. An IGCSE student in a Dubai school typically sits eight to ten subjects. Funding a weekly hour in each at a mid-market AED 220 is roughly AED 2,000 a week before anything else, which no sensible household does, and yet the instinct when results slip is to spread support thinly across everything.

The sharper method takes twenty minutes and costs nothing. Write down each subject, the most recent school assessment grade, and the grade the post-16 route your child wants actually requires. Most subjects will show no gap. One or two will show a gap of one grade, which is usually a paper-technique problem. One may show a gap of two or more, which is usually a content problem and the only subject that justifies a standing weekly slot.

Two refinements matter in this market. Mathematics is almost always worth funding first where there is any gap at all, because it gates the most post-16 routes and because its paper technique transfers to the sciences. And a subject your child dislikes but passes comfortably should be left alone; tutoring it buys a marginally better grade in a subject they will never use again, at the same hourly rate as the subject that is blocking their next step. One more refinement for a JLT household with two children at school: resist the symmetry instinct. Funding the younger sibling because the older one is being funded doubles the bill and halves the attention paid to the gap that actually mattered.
bullets: List every subject, the current grade and the grade the next step requires
Fund the one or two largest gaps, not the subjects that feel worrying

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel? Find the code before you hire
paragraphs: The single most common waste in this market is hiring a tutor for the wrong board. The subject name is identical, the content overlaps heavily, and the assessment does not. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0625 Physics for a decade will teach your Pearson 4PH1 candidate good physics and the wrong exam habits, and neither of them will notice until a mock paper comes back.

Finding the code takes one message. It is printed on the examination entry statement the school issues, and the examinations officer will confirm it. Ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, then keep that list, because it is the brief you give any tutor you speak to. A tutor who does not ask for it should not be hired, and that single screening question is worth more than a reference.

The structures differ in ways that matter to a plan. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. Pearson's modular structure in some subjects allows units to be sat across sessions, which changes when revision has to peak; Cambridge's linear structure concentrates it. Confirm which applies to your child's subjects before buying a revision block timed for the wrong month. None of this is exotic information. It is two lines on an entry statement, and the only reason it goes unasked is that tutoring pages in this market talk about grades rather than codes.

sections.heading: Tiering, and the grade ceiling families find out about too late
paragraphs: In several IGCSE subjects your child is entered on a tier, and the tier sets the highest grade available. Cambridge uses Core and Extended routes in subjects including Mathematics 0580; Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher tiers in subjects including 4MA1. The Core and Foundation routes carry a lower ceiling than the Extended and Higher routes, and the exact grade range is printed in the syllabus for the series your child sits, which is where it should be read rather than taken from a tutoring page.

The consequence is concrete. A student capped below the grade their chosen A Level or Higher Level course requires cannot reach it however well they perform, and no amount of tutoring in Year 11 changes that. Schools make tier decisions on evidence, usually during Year 10, and they can sometimes be revisited. The leverage point is Year 9 and early Year 10, which is also when tutoring is cheapest and shortest.

So the first question to ask the school is not 'how is he doing' but 'which tier is he entered for, and what is the ceiling'. If the answer is the lower tier and your child needs the higher one, you have a specific, time-limited, fundable problem, and a six to ten session block aimed at the evidence the school uses is a rational purchase. If the answer is the higher tier already, then the ceiling is not your issue and the money belongs elsewhere.

sections.heading: Choosing a series, and the economics of a resit
paragraphs: Series choice is a cost decision as much as an academic one, and it is barely discussed in this market. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. A November resit sits roughly five months after June results, which means a focused block of support in September and October rather than a year of it.

The entry deadlines sit much earlier than parents expect, and that is where plans fail. The Pearson November series is the clearest worked example, because its dates are published: the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the results for the November 2025 series before it reached students on 22 January 2026. The entry deadline sat months before that window opened. Cambridge behaves the same way, with June entries closing in the spring and November entries closing well ahead of the autumn papers, each set per series and per timetable zone. The deadline is far enough before the first paper that a decision to resit has to be taken while the previous grade still feels raw.

Timetable zones are the other trap. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A JLT family comparing dates with relatives abroad can easily be looking at a different zone's timetable. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the upcoming International GCSE November series, so the live official timetable on the board's site is the only version worth planning from.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go, paper by paper
paragraphs: Grades at this level are lost in a small number of repeatable places, and naming them is what converts an open tutoring budget into a short block. In mathematics it is unshown method, which forfeits marks the candidate had earned, and misread command words. In the sciences it is units, significant figures and the practical or alternative-to-practical component, where students who have done the experiments still lose marks on variables and uncertainty.

In English the losses are structural. Reading questions reward precise retrieval and inference, not general appreciation, and writing questions reward a plan. In economics and business the final evaluation marks on extended answers go unclaimed by students who explain thoroughly and then stop. In computer science it is pseudocode convention and trace tables, which catch confident programmers who have never written one against the clock.

The reason this matters commercially is that each of those is a short intervention. None needs a year. A student losing method marks in 0580 can be taught to show working in two sessions and will then need practice, not teaching. That is why the diagnostic block comes first in the formats above: four sessions that identify the loss honestly will usually save you six that would have been spent on content the student already had. There is a diagnostic shortcut a parent can run alone, without paying anyone. Take the last mock script, cover the grade, and read only the places where marks were not awarded. If the working is right and the marks are missing, it is technique. If the working stops early, it is content. The two answers point at completely different purchases.
bullets: Maths: unshown method and misread command words
Sciences: units, significant figures, variables and uncertainty
English: retrieval and inference in reading; planning in writing

sections.heading: What your school already provides, and the questions to ask before paying
paragraphs: Before any money changes hands, find out what you have already bought. Most Dubai secondary schools run after-school subject clinics, examination technique sessions, past-paper workshops in the spring term and a mock programme with feedback. Those are included in fees that, as KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026, are not rising for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year. A family paying AED 220 an hour for what the school runs free on a Tuesday has made an avoidable mistake.

The second question is for the subject teacher, and it is narrow: which paper and which question type is my child losing marks on, and what would you have them practise. Teachers answer this well when asked precisely and vaguely when asked how a child is doing. The answer is the brief for any tutor you then hire, and it also tells you whether the problem is content or technique, which decides the length of the block.

The third is about the tier and the code, covered above. With those three answers in hand a JLT parent can brief a tutor in four sentences and buy six sessions instead of a term. Without them, the first two sessions of any arrangement go on diagnosis that the school would have given you free, and at the specialist tier that is several hundred dirhams spent on information you already owned. Ask the questions in writing, by email, so the answers can be forwarded to a tutor verbatim. A paraphrase of a teacher's diagnosis loses exactly the detail that made it useful, and a forwarded message costs nothing to produce.
bullets: Ask what free clinics, workshops and mock feedback the school already runs
Ask the subject teacher which paper and question type is losing marks
Get the board, code and tier for every subject in writing

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the offer a cheap tutor may make you
paragraphs: At the bottom of this market a tutor will sometimes offer something they should not: a folder of scanned mark schemes, a bank of papers presented as unreleased, or coursework assistance that crosses into writing. Official Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are referenced and linked from the boards' own sites. They are not reproduced or supplied as downloads, and material that is not publicly released is not something any legitimate tutor has.

Where IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a controlled assessment, the boundary is the same one that applies at Diploma level. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what is being assessed, question an approach and give feedback on work the student has already produced. A tutor may not draft it, rewrite it to completion, or supply text that appears in a submission. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; the consequence of buying one falls on the student.

The practical screen for a parent is cheap and reliable. Ask a prospective tutor what they would do if your child sent a finished piece and asked them to fix it. A teacher describes feedback and a redraft by the student. A service describes a turnaround time. You will learn more from that one answer than from any list of qualifications, and it costs nothing to ask before the first paid session. The reason to run that screen at IGCSE rather than waiting for the Diploma is that the habits form here. A student who has had one piece of work quietly improved for them will ask again under pressure in Year 12, when the stakes are an Internal Assessment and a malpractice finding.
bullets: Board materials are cited and linked, never copied or redistributed
Unreleased papers are not something a legitimate tutor can supply
Coursework support is criteria teaching and feedback, never drafting
Ask what they would do with a finished draft; the answer sorts teacher from service

sections.heading: Starting from a JLT tower without overcommitting
paragraphs: The sequence that keeps the spend down is deliberately unglamorous. Collect the board, code and tier for each subject. Ask the school what it already runs and what the subject teacher recommends practising. Then send us the subject, the code and that recommendation, and we propose a tutor who has taught that code and a slot set after the commute home to JLT rather than during it.

You take one free trial lesson, at no cost and with no card details required, and only then decide. For most families we will propose the four-session diagnostic block rather than a weekly slot, because at the end of it you have a written answer about where the marks are going and a defensible decision about whether to continue. Matching usually takes two to four working days for mainstream IGCSE subjects.

Coverage is disclosed rather than assumed. Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Economics, Business and Computer Science are normally staffed in UAE evening hours. A less common language, a specialist art or design option, or an unusual code may not be, and when that is the case we say so instead of placing a general tutor against a specialist brief. The table below sets out how we handle it, including the fallback and what happens to the rate. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, and several providers route UAE families to a non-UAE number rather than admit one. Disclosing it costs us occasional enquiries and saves you a term spent discovering the gap yourself.

process.title: Collect the board, code and tier
process.description: From the examination entry statement or the examinations officer, for every subject. This list is the brief. It takes one message to obtain and it prevents the most expensive mistake in this market, which is paying a specialist rate for the wrong board's technique.

process.title: Ask the school two narrow questions
process.description: Which paper and question type is losing marks, and what should be practised. Then ask what free clinics and workshops already run. Between them these answers remove two paid sessions of diagnosis and often reduce the plan you need to buy.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session at no cost with no card details required, with a tutor who has taught your child's code. If the fit is wrong, say so and we propose someone else. A trial ending in an honest no has done its job and cost you nothing.

process.title: Buy the diagnostic block first
process.description: Four sessions, one subject, a written answer at the end about where the marks are going. The total is known before you start and the honest outcome is sometimes that no further support is needed. It is the cheapest way to replace a guess with a plan.

process.title: Extend only against evidence
process.description: If the diagnosis points to technique, a six to ten session paper block follows. If it points to foundations, a weekly slot may be justified and we will say so plainly. Either way the next marked school assessment is the review point, not the calendar.

whyPoints.title: Priced from the bottom of the market up
whyPoints.description: Every tier on this page is named with its published rate and its source, starting at the cheapest. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai household transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Hired against a syllabus code
whyPoints.description: We ask for the board, code and tier before proposing anybody, because Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are not the same examination. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the whole area cluster we researched, which tells you how rare that question is here.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks with an end point
whyPoints.description: The default proposal is four diagnostic sessions, then a paper block if the evidence supports one. A standing weekly slot is available where foundations are genuinely the issue, but it is the exception rather than the opening offer.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE and holds no UAE office. A page with 'home tutor' in the URL should say that in its first paragraph, not in small print.

whyPoints.title: Board materials cited, never copied
whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked from Cambridge and Pearson directly. Nobody will email you a folder of scans, and nobody will produce coursework. That boundary is also the fastest way to tell a teacher from a service.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If we cannot staff your child's subject or code this term, we say so at the enquiry stage rather than placing a general tutor and hoping. A declined enquiry costs us a booking and saves you a term of a plan built on the wrong brief.

faqs.question: What does the cheapest IGCSE tutoring in Dubai actually get you?
faqs.answer: At the AED 33 to 65 an hour advertised by Tutopiya and EdFlik, you are generally buying a capable university student who knows the subject at their own level. What is missing is syllabus-specific knowledge: which code your child is entered for, which paper the practical skills are assessed on, and what the mark scheme accepts as a complete answer. For Year 7 to 9 homework support that is usually enough and paying more would be waste. For a Year 11 Extended or Higher tier paper with a grade threshold to clear, it rarely is.

faqs.question: How many of my child's IGCSE subjects should we actually fund?
faqs.answer: Usually one or two, occasionally three. Write down every subject, the most recent school grade and the grade the post-16 route requires. Most subjects will show no gap at all. Fund the largest gap first, and fund mathematics first where any gap exists, because it gates the most routes and its paper technique transfers to the sciences. A weekly hour across eight subjects at a mid-market AED 220 would be roughly AED 2,000 a week, and most of it would be spent on subjects that were never the problem.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our school teaches Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the examination entry statement the school issues, and the examinations officer will confirm it in a single message. Ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, then keep that list, because it is the brief for any tutor you speak to. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 and Physics 0625; the Pearson Edexcel equivalents include 4MA1 and 4PH1. The content overlaps and the assessment does not, so a tutor who has never asked which code your child sits is guessing.

faqs.question: Does the tier my child is entered for limit the grade they can get?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the fact families discover latest. Cambridge uses Core and Extended routes in subjects including Mathematics 0580, and Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher tiers in subjects including 4MA1. The lower route carries a lower ceiling, and the exact grade range is printed in the syllabus for the series your child sits, which is where to read it. Schools set tiers on evidence, usually in Year 10, and the decision can sometimes be revisited. Ask which tier and what ceiling before funding anything else.

faqs.question: Is starting in Year 10 better value than starting in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Considerably, for three reasons. The tier decision is usually still open in Year 10, so support can affect the ceiling rather than only the grade beneath it. There are more assessed tasks and mocks left for the work to influence. And availability is better, so you are choosing from the full set of specialists rather than from whoever is still free in April, when the published band stops mattering and scarcity sets your price. Year 9 is cheaper again, and the foundations built there are what keep the higher tier open.

faqs.question: Should a resit go in the November series or wait for June?
faqs.answer: November is usually the cheaper and better option, because it sits roughly five months after June results and needs a focused block in September and October rather than a year of support. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. The constraint is the entry deadline, which the centre sets months ahead of the papers, so the decision has to be taken while the previous result is still fresh. Confirm the deadline with the examinations officer immediately.

faqs.question: Why does our exam timetable differ from a cousin's abroad?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A JLT family comparing dates with relatives in another country can easily be reading a different zone's paper. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables before each series, so plan only from the live official timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: Can one tutor sensibly cover two IGCSE sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Sometimes at the lower tiers, rarely well at Extended or Higher. The content is separable but the mark schemes are not interchangeable: chemistry rewards a particular style of working in calculations, physics rewards unit discipline and formula selection, and biology discriminates on command terms. A tutor strong in one is often adequate in the second and that adequacy shows up in a mock rather than in a session. Two short blocks with two specialists usually costs less in total than one generalist working across both for a year.

faqs.question: Is it a warning sign if a tutor offers us scanned mark schemes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Official Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced and linked from the boards' own sites, not reproduced or redistributed as downloads, and unreleased material is not something any legitimate tutor holds. A provider who emails a folder of scans has told you how it treats rules in general, which is worth knowing before coursework season. The same applies to any offer to produce assessed work: that is a malpractice risk and the consequence falls on your child, not the seller.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 look like as papers?
faqs.answer: Candidates sit two written papers at their tier, one with a calculator and one without under the current syllabus structure, with Core and Extended routes carrying different papers and different grade ceilings. Check the paper numbers and the exact structure in the syllabus for the series your child sits, since Cambridge has revised it. For tutoring purposes the practical consequence is that calculator technique and non-calculator fluency are separate skills, and a student comfortable in one can be losing most of their marks in the other.

faqs.question: Our child is on the lower tier in maths. Can that still be changed?
faqs.answer: Often, if you act in Year 10. Schools set tiers on internal evidence and will usually explain what evidence they would need to move a student up. That turns a vague worry into a fundable, time-limited brief: six to ten sessions aimed at the specific assessment the school uses to decide. Once entries are submitted the tier is fixed for that series, and no amount of tutoring lifts a grade above the ceiling. If the ceiling is already below what the post-16 course needs, replan the route rather than buying more hours.

faqs.question: How many sessions does one weak IGCSE paper usually need?
faqs.answer: Six to ten for a technique problem, longer if the foundations are missing. Technique moves quickly once taught explicitly: a student forfeiting method marks in mathematics can be taught to show working in about two sessions and then needs practice rather than teaching. A content gap stretching back to Year 8 is a different purchase and may justify a weekly slot across both years. The four-session diagnostic block exists to tell you which of those two you have before you commit to either.

faqs.question: Does a visiting tutor make sense for IGCSE if we live in a JLT tower?
faqs.answer: For most IGCSE work the case is weak. In-home rates are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and that band overlaps the specialist online band entirely. Add visitor registration at the tower desk, podium parking and the drive across Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; lessons run one-to-one over live video, which also means hiring by syllabus code rather than by driving distance.

faqs.question: What free IGCSE support does a Dubai school usually already run?
faqs.answer: Most secondary schools run after-school subject clinics, examination technique sessions, past-paper workshops in the spring term, and a mock programme with written feedback. Those are inside fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 will not increase for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year. Ask the form tutor what exists before paying for anything, because at AED 220 an hour the cost of duplicating a free Tuesday clinic across a term is substantial, and the clinic is run by the teacher who sets the tasks.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody covers our child's IGCSE subject or code?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the enquiry stage rather than placing a general tutor against a specialist brief. Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Economics, Business and Computer Science are normally staffed in UAE evening hours, with a match in two to five working days. A less common language, a specialist art or design option, or an unusual code sometimes is not, and in that case we say so and you should look elsewhere. For Arabic and Islamic Education, support has to follow the school's own material, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jlt.closingHeading: Buy the code, the tier and four sessions, in that order
dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jlt.closingBody: An IGCSE home tutor in JLT is worth buying once you know three things: the board and syllabus code, the tier and its ceiling, and which paper is losing the marks. With those in hand, four diagnostic sessions and then a short paper block will usually do what a year of weekly tutoring was going to be sold to you as. Market rates run from AED 33 an hour to AED 650, and the top of that range is mostly travel and reputation rather than teaching. Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details required.

intro.heading: A grade is not a diagnosis, and the paper is
paragraphs: Most tutoring in Dubai is bought on a grade. A report says 5 in Business Studies, a parent in Jumeirah 1 searches for a tutor, and a term of weekly lessons begins with somebody re-teaching the topic list. It often produces no movement at all, and the reason is that a grade describes an outcome rather than a cause. Two students with the same 5 can be losing marks in entirely unrelated places: one writes knowledge where the question asked for application, the other knows the content and never reaches the evaluation sentence that the top band requires.

The marked paper tells you which. Every Cambridge and Pearson mark scheme is explicit about what earns a mark, and the pattern of losses across a paper is readable in twenty minutes by somebody who knows the syllabus. That is the work a first session should do, and it is the difference between buying teaching and buying a repair. A tutor who starts at chapter one has decided not to look, and a term of that costs a family both the money and the window in which the problem was still cheap to fix.

This page is written from the subject outwards rather than from the location inwards, because the subject is what actually varies. It lists the syllabus codes Jumeirah 1 families ask about, names the highest-yield mark-scheme trap in each, works through the command words that decide marks, sets out the assessment structure behind each grade, and gives a past-paper protocol that teaches instead of simply measuring. The cost section leads with the question that actually determines value: whether the hour includes marking your child's written work.

On delivery, the position is stated plainly. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and nothing here will promise a tutor at a UAE address. Lessons for Jumeirah 1 families are one-to-one over live video, with the student's own marked paper on screen, the mark scheme beside it and written work annotated between sessions. For subject work specifically that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the document being discussed is the document both people are looking at.

Jumeirah 1 itself shapes only the timing. The district runs inland from Jumeirah Beach Road through Al Bada'a and Al Hudaiba, with Pearl Jumeira and La Mer on the water and City Walk behind, and most secondary students here commute to the Al Safa, Al Wasl or Umm Suqeim schools. Beach Road in the afternoon is slower than its distance suggests, which pushes a realistic weekday start past 16:45 for most of the district. Everything else on this page is about the syllabus.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits at the end of one sequence and the start of another, and the subject work that matters depends on which. These are the programmes Jumeirah 1 families ask about, with what each one demands in terms of written technique.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects, each with its own syllabus code, component structure and command-word list. The two-year course is taught topic by topic and examined by question type, which is why students who know the content can still underperform. Tiering applies in some subjects at Cambridge, where Core and Extended report different grade ranges, and at Pearson, where Foundation and Higher do the same.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the entry is made by the school as a Cambridge or Pearson centre, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the exams officer is the person to ask for the zone, the codes and the current tier.

programmes.name: A Level, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: The most common destination for Jumeirah 1 IGCSE students. A Level subjects assume specific IGCSE fluencies rather than general ability: algebraic manipulation for sciences and maths, source evaluation for History, evaluative writing for Business and Economics. Students who reached a good IGCSE grade through recall rather than technique meet the gap in the first term, not the first year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. A November entry is usually a retake or an early entry and compresses revision into the first half of the autumn term, which for a Year 12 student collides with new A Level content.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in this part of Dubai, and the one where IGCSE written technique transfers most directly. Diploma papers are built on precise command terms and criterion-marked internal assessments, so a student who learned to read a command word at 16 arrives with a real advantage. Students who learned to write everything they know arrive with a habit to unlearn.
programmes.countryNote: No IB Diploma points figure for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency is published that this page can cite, so none appears here. The British-track rule is sourced and specific: five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Some Jumeirah 1 students arrive at an IGCSE entry from MYP, having been assessed against criteria out of eight rather than against mark schemes. The transition is a technique change rather than a content gap: timed writing, command words and the habit of answering the question asked rather than the topic recognised all have to be learned deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from this district sits mainly in Al Safa, Umm Al Sheif and the Al Barsha campuses. Some of those schools enter MYP students for Cambridge papers alongside criterion assessment, most often Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607, so a student can be assessed two ways in the same year.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Each IGCSE subject fails in its own way. These are the courses Jumeirah 1 families ask for, with the content that carries the marks and the place the marks usually go.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500 and 0990
subjects.description: A reading paper with comprehension, summary and directed writing, and a writing paper with directed writing and composition. Summary marks are lost to lifted phrasing rather than to misunderstanding, and directed writing is lost to ignoring the stated audience and form. Both are technique, and both move quickly with marked practice.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language A 4EA1
subjects.description: A non-fiction and transactional writing component plus a poetry and prose component, with a coursework alternative at some centres. The transactional writing task is where structure earns marks: students who plan a shape score above students who write fluently without one, and that is the cheapest improvement in the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Two papers behind four assessment objectives: knowledge, application, analysis and evaluation. Nearly all avoidable loss sits in application and evaluation. Students describe a concept correctly and never attach it to the case-study business, or they analyse two options and never recommend one with a reason. Both are fixable in three marked pieces.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper and a structured paper carrying the larger share. Diagrams lose marks when axes are unlabelled or curves shift without explanation, and the extended evaluation questions lose marks when a student lists arguments without weighing them. Diagram discipline plus one evaluative sentence structure is most of the gap.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Information and Communication Technology 0417
subjects.description: A theory paper plus practical papers covering document production, data manipulation, presentations, spreadsheets and website authoring. The practical papers are marked against precise outputs, so a student loses marks for formatting that looks fine and does not match the brief. Screen-shared practice is exactly the right format for this.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460
subjects.description: A geographical themes paper, a skills paper, and either coursework or the alternative-to-coursework paper. The skills paper is the most recoverable component in the subject: map reading, cross-sections, graph interpretation and data response are all teachable procedures. Case-study answers lose marks when places are named without specific detail.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE History 0470
subjects.description: Structured questions, a source-based paper, and either coursework or an alternative depth-study paper. The source paper is where grades are made and lost. Students retell the source instead of using it as evidence, and never address provenance, purpose or the limits of what it can show. That is a learnable routine rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE French 0520 and modern languages
subjects.description: Four components covering listening, reading, writing and speaking, each carrying a quarter of the grade. Speaking is the component families most often leave to chance because it feels unteachable at a distance; it is in fact the most rehearsable, since the task types are stable and timed practice with feedback moves it fast.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: A theory paper covering data representation, networks, hardware and security, and a paper on algorithms, programming and logic. Pseudocode answers lose marks for undeclared variables and untraced loops. Trace tables are the single highest-yield routine in the subject and almost nobody practises them deliberately.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge now examines a non-calculator paper at both tiers, which put arithmetic fluency, surds and exact values back at the centre of revision. Pearson awards method marks generously, so working written out recovers marks that mental calculation throws away silently. The two boards reward different habits.

sections.heading: Reading a marked paper before buying a single hour
paragraphs: The cheapest hour in IGCSE tutoring is the one nobody charges for: sitting down with your child's most recent marked paper and sorting the lost marks into four piles. Content the student did not know. Content they knew and did not apply. Marks lost to the command word, where the answer was good and answered a different question. And marks lost to time, where the final questions are blank or rushed. Those four piles need four different interventions, and three of them are not more teaching.

Parents are often surprised by the result. A student with a 5 in Business Studies frequently has almost no content gap at all. The knowledge marks are there, and the losses sit in application, where a correct definition was never attached to the case-study business, and in evaluation, where two options were analysed and neither was recommended with a reason. That is a writing routine, learnable in three marked pieces, and no amount of revising the syllabus touches it.

The same exercise in a science produces a different answer. There the losses usually sit in calculation fluency and in practical reasoning: no working shown, rounding mid-calculation, units omitted, generic safety precautions, improvements suggested that do not address the error the student identified. In History the losses sit in the source paper, where a student retells the content of a source instead of using it as evidence. In Geography they sit in the skills paper, which is procedural and therefore the fastest to repair.

Do this before you contact anybody, and send what you find with the enquiry. It changes the conversation from a general one about a subject to a specific one about a question type, and it is the single best filter for a tutor. Somebody who responds to the detail is worth a trial lesson. Somebody who responds with a package and a promise about outcomes has not read it.
bullets: Sort lost marks into content, application, command word and time
Three of those four piles are not fixed by more teaching

sections.heading: The subject-by-subject trap, with syllabus codes
paragraphs: Every IGCSE subject has one or two places where most of the recoverable marks sit. Experienced teachers know them and name them immediately; a general tutor works through the textbook and arrives at them by accident in March. The table below is that list, written so a parent can check it against their own child's paper without any subject knowledge at all.

Read it as a shortlist of things to ask about rather than as a diagnosis. If your child takes Cambridge IGCSE History 0470 and the source paper mark is well below the structured-questions mark, the trap in the table is almost certainly the problem. If both marks are low, the issue is content and the plan is different. The point of naming the trap is to make the first two sessions targeted rather than exploratory.

Several entries are worth highlighting because they are so frequently missed. Trace tables in Computer Science 0478 are the highest-yield routine in that subject and are almost never practised deliberately. The Geography skills paper is entirely procedural and recoverable in weeks. ICT practical papers are marked against precise outputs, so work that looks correct and does not match the brief scores nothing. And in modern languages the speaking component is more rehearsable than any other part of the course, because the task types are stable.

What all of these have in common is that they are routines rather than knowledge. A routine can be taught, practised and made reliable inside a six-week block, which is why a targeted block so often outperforms a year of general support. It is also why the marked paper matters more than the report: the report tells you there is a problem, and the paper tells you which routine is missing.

sections.heading: Command words are the mark scheme, not a writing style
paragraphs: Cambridge publishes a command-word list in every syllabus and Pearson sets out assessment objectives for every paper. Students treat these as instructions about tone. They are instructions about structure, and getting one wrong costs the whole question however good the content is. A student who explains when the paper said describe has written something that cannot be credited, and the mark scheme is not being awkward: describe and explain ask for different things and are worth different marks.

The habit this produces is the most expensive one in IGCSE. Under pressure a student reads the topic rather than the instruction, recognises the territory, and writes everything they know about it. In a four-mark question that scores two. In an eight-mark evaluation it scores in the bottom band, because the band descriptor requires weighing and the answer only lists. Both students then conclude that they are bad at the subject, which is not what happened.

The fix is mechanical and fast. Highlight the command word before writing anything. Say out loud what that word requires. Then write to that shape. Three weeks of that, applied to real past-paper questions and marked against the real mark scheme, moves students who looked stuck. It is also the single most transferable thing in IGCSE, because the same discipline is worth marks in every written subject and again in the Diploma or at A Level.

The table below covers the command words that cost the most across the subjects in this district. The third column is what students actually write, taken from the patterns teachers report most often. Read it alongside your child's marked paper and you will usually recognise at least two rows immediately.

sections.heading: The assessment structure behind each grade
paragraphs: Revision plans fail when they are built around topics and the grade is built around components. A student who revises Business Studies content evenly across both papers has ignored the fact that the marks are distributed across four assessment objectives, and that two of those objectives are writing routines rather than content. A student revising Geography evenly has ignored that one whole paper is skills, which is procedural and recoverable, while another rests on case-study detail that takes longer to build.

The table sets out the component structure of the subjects this district asks about most. Where coursework and an alternative paper both exist, the school chooses, and that choice changes what a tutor may legitimately do: coursework is assessed work the student must produce themselves, while an alternative paper is examined and can be practised freely. Knowing which route your child's centre entered is a question for the exams officer.

Two structural facts deserve attention. First, several subjects place a large share of the grade in one component, so a weakness there has an outsized effect on the final grade. Second, coursework routes are usually completed well before the written papers, which means the time to help with them is a year earlier than most families start thinking about tutoring at all.

Entry deadlines sit behind all of it, and the series comes first. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and those two are the ones UAE centres sit; the February/March series is offered to India only, so dates found through a general search may belong to a series your child will never take. Final entries are agreed between Cambridge and the centre months before the first paper, and the tier is part of that entry rather than part of the revision. Pearson ran its November 2026 International GCSE timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, published June 2026 results to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026, and issues provisional timetables for later series that may be revised.

sections.heading: A past paper that teaches, instead of one that only measures
paragraphs: Past papers are the most used and least well used resource in IGCSE. The default pattern is to complete a paper, check the answers, note the score and move to the next one. That measures a student repeatedly and teaches them almost nothing, which is why a child can finish twelve past papers and sit at the same grade. The paper only becomes teaching when the marking is done properly and the corrections are worked, which takes longer than the paper itself.

The protocol below is what a working session should do with a paper. The part families skip is step four. Writing a corrected answer to the same question, after seeing the mark scheme, is where the learning happens, and it is the step a student will never do unsupervised because it feels like repeating work already finished. It is the opposite of repetition: the first attempt revealed the gap and the second closes it.

Marking deserves its own note. A student marking their own paper awards marks for intention, because they know what they meant. The mark scheme awards marks for what is on the page. That gap is where most of the self-assessment error in Year 11 lives, and it is the single strongest argument for having written work marked by somebody else. If a tutoring arrangement does not include marking between sessions, a large part of the method is missing.

One constraint worth stating. Official syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We work from them in sessions and point families to the boards' own pages, and we do not host or supply their documents. Any provider offering a downloadable archive of papers and mark schemes is doing something it should not, which is a reasonable signal about everything else it does.

sections.heading: Extended writing: the questions worth six marks and more
paragraphs: Every written IGCSE subject has a long question at the end, and it is where grades separate. Six marks in a science, eight in Economics, twelve in some Business and Geography papers. These are marked against band descriptors rather than point by point, which means a correct answer in the wrong shape sits in the bottom band while a thinner answer in the right shape sits in the top one. Students find that unfair until they see two answers side by side.

The band descriptors reward three things consistently. Linked reasoning, where each point follows from the last rather than sitting beside it. Specific support, where a named example, figure or case-study detail is attached to a claim. And, in evaluative questions, a judgement with a stated basis, which means saying which consideration matters most and why rather than concluding that it depends.

The structure that satisfies all three is simple enough to rehearse: a claim, a mechanism explaining how it works, specific support, then the counter-consideration, then a judgement that says which weighs more and on what criterion. Written out it is five sentences. A student who practises that shape on six real questions, marked each time, moves from the middle band to the top band in most subjects, and the gain transfers across every written subject they take.

Science extended responses work the same way with different furniture. A six-mark question in Biology wants linked scientific reasoning in sequence, not a list of true statements. In Chemistry it wants the mechanism stated in the correct order with the right terminology. Students who write everything they know on the topic land in the middle band because the marker cannot find a chain of reasoning. Writing fewer, better-linked sentences scores higher, which is counter-intuitive enough that it has to be taught explicitly.
bullets: Band-marked questions reward shape as much as content
Claim, mechanism, specific support, counter-consideration, judgement
A judgement needs a stated criterion, not the phrase it depends
Science extended answers want a chain of reasoning, not a list of facts

sections.heading: Tiering, and the content that moves with it
paragraphs: Tiering is a content decision disguised as an administrative one. At Cambridge, Core and Extended report different grade ranges and examine different amounts of material; at Pearson, Foundation and Higher do the same. In Mathematics, Cambridge Core reports C to G and Extended reports A* to E, while Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 and Higher reaches grade 9 while allowing a grade 3. In the sciences the tier changes both the content and the question difficulty.

The practical point is that the tier bounds the ceiling before any tutoring begins. A student on a Core entry cannot reach the top grades however well they are taught, so if a university or sixth-form requirement needs a higher grade, the tier is the first conversation and the tutor is the second. Schools tier provisionally in Year 10 from internal assessment, and the decision becomes binding at the centre's final entry deadline.

Moving up a tier is a real option and a real commitment. The additional content has to be taught, and the question difficulty increases, so a move made in February with a weak foundation can produce a worse outcome than a strong Core performance. A move made in Year 10, with a term of targeted work behind it, usually produces a better one. The deciding evidence should be a marked Extended or Higher paper rather than a conversation about potential.

Non-science subjects complicate the picture, because many are single tier. In Business Studies, Economics, History, Geography and Computer Science there is one entry and the differentiation sits inside the paper, in the extended questions. That is why the writing routines in the previous sections matter so much in those subjects: there is no tier to move, so the only route to a higher grade is the band descriptor on the long questions.

sections.heading: What subject tuition costs, and whether marking is in the hour
paragraphs: Before any rate band, ask one question: does the hour include marking my child's written work between sessions? It is the question that decides value in subject tutoring and the one almost nobody asks. An hour of live teaching with no marking leaves the student self-assessing, which is where most of the error in Year 11 sits. An hour that comes with written work annotated against the mark scheme is a different product, and the price difference between them is usually smaller than the difference in effect.

With that in mind, the published Dubai figures, read in October 2026. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour inside a band of roughly AED 45 to 150, and at that level marking is rarely included. A qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150 to 300; one Dubai agency's rate card listed IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with a UK agency operating in the Gulf at AED 270 and a named-tutor service at AED 650. In-home visits across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

For monthly budgeting, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 for budget support, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those figures is an IB Gram price and this page publishes none; ask on the consultation after the free trial lesson.

The subject-tutoring conclusion is about shape rather than tier. A six-week targeted block that includes marking, bought at the specialist end, usually costs less in total than two terms of unmarked weekly teaching at the budget end, and it produces a repaired routine instead of a record of attendance. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, so this is a clean decision about a block of sessions rather than one competing with a fee increase.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects in this district run coursework routes, and the distinction between coursework and an examined alternative decides what help is legitimate. Where Geography or History coursework is entered, the work is assessed and must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the skills it requires, explain what the criteria reward and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not plan it for them, write any part of it, or edit it to completion, and nobody at IB Gram will.

Where the alternative paper is entered instead, the same material is examined rather than submitted, so it can be practised without limit. That is why the exams officer's answer about which route the centre entered is worth having before any plan is made. Families sometimes buy coursework support for a child whose school entered the alternative paper, which is both unnecessary and the wrong preparation.

Science practicals sit in a similar place. Cambridge examines practical skills in a separate paper worth a fifth of the grade in each separate science, either a practical test with apparatus or the alternative to practical, which is written. Pearson embeds those skills in the written papers. The written reasoning around experiments, which is most of the mark scheme, can be taught entirely over video; apparatus handling stays with the school.

Two other boundaries, stated because competitors in this market cross them. Official syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' property, so we cite and link them rather than hosting them. And nobody here is described as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, because the claim is widely made and rarely checkable. If anybody offers it, ask which board, which component and which series.

sections.heading: Permits, the school week and when subject work happens
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit, and the specifics are checkable. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here.

The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. No individual is KHDA approved, because the KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no premises anywhere in the UAE.

On the week itself: Jumeirah 1 students mostly commute to the Al Safa, Al Wasl or Umm Suqeim schools, and Beach Road in the afternoon is slower than the distance implies. A realistic weekday start for most of the district is after 16:45, earlier for the Al Wasl and Al Hudaiba edges where the journey runs away from the coast. Timed whole papers belong in a weekend morning, because an hour and a half of examination conditions is not available at 17:30 on a Tuesday for anybody.

Ramadan moves the whole pattern. School days shorten, afternoons compress and the productive window shifts to the evening after Iftar. Families who move the slot two to three hours later and keep the frequency hold the marking cycle through the month; families who cancel usually lose six weeks rather than four, because restarting takes a fortnight. Plan the shift before the month begins and the subject work continues uninterrupted.
