process.title: Sort the lost marks before you enquire
process.description: Take the most recent marked paper and divide the lost marks into content, application, command word and time. It costs nothing, it takes twenty minutes, and it converts a vague worry about a subject into a specific question type. Send what you find with your enquiry.

process.title: Get the syllabus code and the tier
process.description: One email to the exams officer: which board, which syllabus code, which tier, and for Geography or History whether the centre entered coursework or the alternative paper. Those answers decide what is worth teaching, and three of the four cannot be guessed from the textbook.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the marked paper
process.description: One trial lesson, one subject, before any paid block is booked. The tutor reads the paper against the mark scheme with your child, names the routine that is missing and says what six weeks would target. You decide afterwards whether to continue and in which subject.

process.title: Run one six-week block, with marking
process.description: One subject, one routine, six weeks, with written work set every session and annotated between them. Make marking an explicit part of the arrangement rather than an assumed one, because an unmarked hour leaves the student self-assessing and that is where most Year 11 error lives.

process.title: Re-test the same question type
process.description: At the end of the block, a timed question of the identical type, marked to the published scheme. If the routine is reliable the mark moves and you can pick the next target. If it has not, the diagnosis was wrong and more of the same will not help. Open-ended tuition hides both results.

process.title: Count back from the entry, not the exam
process.description: Ask the exams officer which of the two UAE Cambridge series your child is entered for, June or November, and when final entries close, because tier decisions live at that deadline rather than in a parents' evening. Build the revision block back from the first paper in your centre's administrative zone and the plan fits inside a Dubai term.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0450 and Pearson's business specification are different animals, as are Cambridge 0500 and 4EA1. Our tutors teach named syllabuses to their published command words and assessment objectives, which is what makes the first two sessions targeted rather than exploratory.

whyPoints.title: Marking is part of the hour, not an extra
whyPoints.description: Written work is annotated against the mark scheme and returned before the next session, and the session starts from the corrections. A student marking their own work credits intention; the scheme credits what is on the page, and the gap between those is most of the lost marks.

whyPoints.title: Routines rather than revision
whyPoints.description: A source routine in History, an evaluation structure in Economics, trace tables in Computer Science, working written out in maths. These are learnable in weeks and they transfer to A Level and the Diploma, which general revision does not.

whyPoints.title: A past-paper method, not a past-paper pile
whyPoints.description: Sit it to time, have it marked strictly, classify every lost mark, rewrite the answer properly, then re-test the same question type a fortnight later. The step families skip is the rewrite, and it is the one where the learning happens.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is somebody else's published number, read in October 2026 and attributed, including what each tier usually includes. We do not present market rates as ours, and we do not hide a figure behind a form.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits, in writing
whyPoints.description: Coursework is the student's own work and we mark drafts rather than produce text. Papers and mark schemes belong to the boards and we link rather than host them. We run no in-home service anywhere in the UAE, and no page here promises a tutor at a Dubai address.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is costing my child the most marks?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily the one with the lowest grade. Take each marked paper and divide the lost marks into four groups: content the student did not know, content they knew and failed to apply, marks lost to the command word where a good answer addressed a different question, and marks lost to time where the last questions are rushed or blank. A subject with a middling grade and a large command-word loss is usually the fastest to repair, and a subject with a genuine content gap takes longer. The paper tells you; the report does not.

faqs.question: What does the command word explain actually require?
faqs.answer: A causal link, stated rather than implied. Describe asks what happens; explain asks why it happens, and the mark is for the connective reasoning between cause and effect. A student who writes an excellent description for an explain question has produced something the mark scheme cannot credit, which feels unfair and is simply how band descriptors work. The habit that fixes it is mechanical: highlight the command word before writing, say aloud what it demands, then write to that shape. Three weeks of that on real past-paper questions moves students who looked stuck.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on eight-mark evaluation questions in Economics?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer lists arguments without weighing them. Band descriptors for evaluative questions reward a judgement with a stated basis, which means saying which consideration matters most and on what criterion, not concluding that it depends. The structure that satisfies the band is five sentences: a claim, the mechanism that makes it work, specific support, the counter-consideration, then the judgement with its criterion. Diagram discipline is the other half in Economics, because an unlabelled axis or an unexplained curve shift loses marks before any writing is read.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge First Language English 0500 different from the 9 to 1 version?
faqs.answer: The syllabus content and assessment approach are closely aligned; the difference is the grading scale, with 0990 reporting on the 9 to 1 scale and 0500 on A* to G. What matters more for tutoring is that both are won and lost in the same two places: summary, where marks go to lifted phrasing rather than genuine condensing, and directed writing, where marks go to ignoring the stated audience, form and purpose. Check which code is on your child's entry, because the statement of results will carry it and university applications later may ask.

faqs.question: How should a Business Studies answer be structured to reach the top band?
faqs.answer: By attaching everything to the case-study business. Cambridge 0450 marks across four assessment objectives, and the losses sit overwhelmingly in application and evaluation rather than knowledge. A top-band answer defines the concept briefly, applies it explicitly to this business and its stated circumstances, analyses the consequence in a chain rather than a list, then recommends one course of action with a reason tied to the business's own situation. Students who write textbook-correct answers about no particular company sit in the middle band however much they know.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE ICT still have practical papers, and can they be taught online?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Cambridge 0417 pairs a theory paper with practical papers covering document production, data manipulation, presentations, spreadsheets and website authoring, and those papers are marked against precise outputs. That makes screen-shared tuition close to the ideal format, because the tutor watches the actual work being produced against the actual task wording. The commonest loss in ICT is output that looks perfectly reasonable and does not match the brief, which is only visible when somebody reads the task and the result side by side.

faqs.question: My child's History answers retell the source instead of using it. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: With a routine applied to every source without exception: who produced it, for what purpose, at what moment, and therefore what it can and cannot be taken to show. Cambridge 0470's source paper is where the grade is made, and retelling content is the default failure because it feels like answering. Five to eight weeks of marked source practice usually converts it, because the routine is short and the mark scheme rewards it consistently. Compare your child's source-paper mark with their structured-questions mark; a gap between them confirms the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do Geography and History coursework options change what a tutor can do?
faqs.answer: Substantially, so find out which route the centre entered. Where coursework is submitted, the work is assessed and must be the student's own: a tutor may teach the skills, explain what the criteria reward and give feedback on a draft the student has written, and may not plan it, write any part of it or edit it to completion. Where the alternative paper is entered instead, the same material is examined rather than submitted and can be practised without limit. Families sometimes buy coursework support for a child sitting the alternative paper, which is the wrong preparation entirely.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 student actually complete?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families think, worked much harder. A paper sat to time, marked strictly against the published scheme, with every lost mark classified and the weakest answers rewritten properly, is worth four papers completed and glanced at. Six to eight papers treated that way across the final two months is a substantial programme. Twelve papers completed and scored teaches almost nothing, which is why a student can finish a stack of them and sit at the same grade. The rewriting step is the one that moves marks.

faqs.question: Should my child mark their own past papers?
faqs.answer: Not alone, and this is the strongest practical argument for marking being part of a tutoring arrangement. A student marking their own work awards marks for intention, because they know what they meant to convey. The mark scheme awards marks only for what appears on the page. That gap is where most self-assessment error in Year 11 lives, and it produces confident students who are surprised in August. Self-marking has a place for multiple choice and short calculation answers; for anything band-marked, somebody else has to read it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in a non-science subject?
faqs.answer: In many non-science subjects there is no tier at all. Business Studies, Economics, History, Geography and Computer Science are single-entry at Cambridge, and the differentiation sits inside the paper rather than between tiers, concentrated in the extended band-marked questions. That matters because there is no tier to move up: the only route to a higher grade is the band descriptor on the long questions, which is exactly why evaluation structure and specific support carry so much weight in those subjects.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate include marking my child's written work?
faqs.answer: Ask explicitly, because it varies and it is the single biggest determinant of value. Budget platforms advertising from AED 33 to 65 an hour rarely include marking. Qualified subject tutors published at AED 150 to 300 often include some written feedback. Specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above usually mark between sessions as part of the arrangement. The price difference between an unmarked and a marked hour is typically smaller than the difference in effect, so this question is worth more than negotiating the rate down.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can we sensibly tutor at once from Jumeirah 1?
faqs.answer: One properly, or two alternating. A Year 11 student in this district is already carrying eight to ten subjects, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education, a commute along Beach Road and whatever else the week contains. Three tutored subjects consumes the independent practice time the tutoring is supposed to improve. One subject with one target routine for six weeks produces visible movement; two subjects alternating in a single weekly slot works when there are two borderline grades rather than one serious weakness.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE speaking and listening components?
faqs.answer: Yes, and modern language speaking is one of the most rehearsable components in the whole qualification. Cambridge 0520 French and its sister syllabuses use stable task types across series, so timed rehearsal with feedback on register, tense accuracy and fluency moves the mark reliably. Families often leave speaking alone because it feels unteachable at a distance, which is backwards: a video call is a conversation, and a conversation is exactly what the component assesses. Listening practice works the same way with recorded material and marked transcription work.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects benefit least from tutoring?
faqs.answer: Subjects where the student's content knowledge is already secure and the loss is purely timing, and subjects where the work is practical and the school's provision is already strong. A student who scores well on every question they reach and leaves the last two blank has a pacing problem that a few timed papers fix without a term of teaching. It is also worth being honest that a strong student in a well-taught subject often gains more from six marked past papers than from thirty hours of instruction, and we would rather say so.

faqs.question: What should a tutor be able to tell me about my child's syllabus in the first ten minutes?
faqs.answer: The code, the components and the trap. A tutor who knows Cambridge 0470 will name the source paper as where the grade is decided before you mention it. One who knows 0450 will ask whether your child's answers reach the case-study business. One who knows 0460 will ask whether the skills paper or the themes paper is weaker. If the conversation stays on topics, chapters and general revision, you are speaking to somebody who teaches the subject rather than the assessment, and the difference shows up in the marks.

Find the most recent marked paper in the subject that worries you, sort the lost marks into content, application, command word and time, and ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the tier and whether any coursework route was entered. That turns a grade into a diagnosis, and a diagnosis into a six-week target that can be tested at the end. intro.heading: Stop pricing the hour and start pricing the mark
paragraphs: A family in Jumeirah 2 comparing IGCSE tutors will be shown hourly rates spanning more than a factor of ten, from about AED 45 to over AED 650, and almost no information about what separates them. Comparing those numbers against each other is the wrong exercise, because the hour is not the thing being bought. What is being bought is a number of marks on a specific paper, and the same hour buys wildly different quantities of them depending on what the hour is spent doing.

That reframing has practical consequences immediately. A student sitting three marks below a grade boundary and a student sitting twenty-five marks below it have almost nothing in common as purchases, even in the same subject at the same school. The first needs accuracy discipline and two timed papers, which is two or three sessions. The second needs one or two topic areas rebuilt, which is a block. Spending the second plan on the first student wastes most of it, and spending the first plan on the second student achieves nothing at all.

The commonest expensive mistake in this market is the opposite of extravagance. It is thin spending spread wide: a weekly hour across nine subjects, which at the middle of the Dubai qualified-teacher band is a substantial monthly commitment and reliably secures nothing, because nine subjects of one hour a week produces nine subjects of light familiarity. Two subjects properly repaired beats nine lightly attended, and it usually costs less.

The second expensive mistake is paying for the wrong activity. Homework supervision, re-explanation of content the school already taught adequately, unmarked past-paper practice and encouragement are all things a family can buy at tutoring rates and none of them are tutoring in the sense that moves a grade. Each has a legitimate place; none of them should be billed as subject teaching, and a parent who knows the difference can ask for the right one.

Jumeirah 2 adds its own constraint, which is the household rather than the market. A villa district with no secondary school inside it means every teenager commutes, usually with a younger sibling on a different bus, so the evening has one reliable window rather than three. Money spent on a slot that collapses in week three is money spent on nothing, which makes scheduling a cost question and not an administrative one.

The delivery position, stated before any figures. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 2 address, or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Every AED figure on this page is a published market band or a competitor's own published rate, with the month it was read, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: An IGCSE spending plan depends on where a student sits in the longer route, because the cheapest interventions are available at the start of it and the most expensive at the end. The four stages below are described with what each one costs in practice for a Jumeirah 2 household.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, assessed internally and sometimes by Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge runs in March, May and October. The content that decides an IGCSE grade later is narrow: directed number, fractions as operators, index laws, equation solving with brackets, and the first graph work. Nothing here carries an external grade, which is exactly why it is cheap to fix.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest place in the whole route to spend money and the stage almost no Jumeirah 2 family spends it. A Year 8 gap in algebraic manipulation costs a handful of sessions to repair and reappears in Year 11 as a problem that costs a term. Families who have been through one IGCSE cycle routinely say they would spend earlier with the second child.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10, the first examined year
programmes.description: The course begins, often in the January of Year 9 at Dubai schools rather than the September of Year 10, and the tier decision starts to form on internal evidence. Nothing is entered yet, nothing is capped, and a single weak topic can be rebuilt without competing against eight other subjects' revision.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is where the tier conversation can still be won, because entries for a series are confirmed months before the papers. For a Jumeirah 2 family the practical move is a marked full paper in the summer of Year 10, which costs one session and either confirms the tier or produces the evidence needed to argue it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11, the examined year
programmes.description: Mocks, entries, forecast grades and the series itself, with eight or nine subjects competing for the same evenings. Everything is more expensive here: the tier is fixed, the time is short, and the money has to be aimed rather than spread. This is also the year in which most families start spending, which is the structural reason so much of it is wasted.
programmes.countryNote: A Year 11 budget in Dubai should be aimed at two subjects, chosen by how close the mock sits to a boundary rather than by which subject causes the most anxiety at home. That single discipline changes the return on a fixed budget more than any choice of provider does.

programmes.name: After the series: retakes, A Level or the Diploma
programmes.description: Results bring three decisions: a possible remark, a possible retake in a later series, and the sixth-form route. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, which are the two a UAE candidate sits; Pearson runs May/June and November. A retake is a fresh entry and a fresh fee, paid to the exam centre rather than to a tutor.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms set their own entry requirements, generally a grade 6 or B in the subject for A Level and an equivalent expectation for Diploma Higher Level. That makes a retake a route-preserving purchase rather than a vanity one, and it should be costed against the alternative route rather than in isolation.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the set a Jumeirah 2 household is usually choosing between, with the syllabus codes Dubai schools enter and a note on what makes each one cheap or expensive to support properly. Codes matter here because they change what an hour has to contain.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 and 0980
subjects.description: Two papers per tier, one without a calculator and one with. Cheap to support per mark, because accuracy discipline and two-pass paper technique recover marks across every topic rather than inside one.

subjects.name: Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers, calculator permitted in both, reported 9-1. Method marks are generous but conditional on written working, so layout habits are among the cheapest marks available in the whole qualification.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula rearrangement, standard form and graph gradients with units mean a large share of physics losses are actually maths losses. Supporting the maths is frequently cheaper per physics mark than supporting the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, percentage yield and titration arithmetic account for most calculation marks. Procedural, drillable and therefore inexpensive per mark compared with the descriptive topics.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Light on calculation, heavy on command-term precision and graph reading. Describe, explain and suggest earn different answers, which is a habit rather than content and costs very little to install.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into fewer papers. Cheaper to support than three separate sciences because one tutor can cover it, and the commonest place a family over-buys by hiring three specialists.

subjects.name: English Language 0500 and 0990
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing assessed against criteria rather than content. Expensive per mark early and cheap later, because the gains come from redrafting against a mark scheme rather than from teaching.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: A different qualification with a different mark scheme, frequently confused with 0500 when a tutor is hired. Checking which code is on the entry prevents an entire term of wrongly aimed practice.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455
subjects.description: Data response marks reward a student who can read a percentage change, an index and a simple calculation. The quantitative marks are the ones most often dropped by strong essay writers and the cheapest to recover.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, logic gates and pseudocode trace tables. Highly procedural and therefore good value per mark, and usually coverable by the same tutor who handles Extended maths.

subjects.name: Geography 0460 and History 0470
subjects.description: Source and case-study papers where structure earns the marks. A tutor's time is best spent on answer frameworks and marked practice rather than on content, which the school normally covers adequately.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, binomial expansion and radian trigonometry a year early. A thin subject in Dubai, taught in small groups or not at all, and the one most likely to need an external specialist rather than a general maths tutor.

regions.note: Nearest to the Umm Suqeim cluster and the shortest school run on the strip, so an earlier start is realistic. The same tutor pool and the same published bands as Jumeirah 2 in practice.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: Jumeirah College and Horizon English School sit here, both British-curriculum, so this is where much of the local IGCSE teaching capacity actually works. Pick-up congestion on Al Wasl Road is why a 16:00 session rarely begins on time.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Kings' School Dubai and Raffles World Academy draw from the whole corridor. Households here face the same published rates and a slightly shorter commute, and the IB continuum schools mean 0607 appears more often than 0580.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: The inland campuses, thirty minutes away at six in the evening in each direction. This journey is the one that sets the travel premium in every in-home quote a Jumeirah 2 family receives.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Coastal developments with no school inside them, so every pupil commutes twice daily. Removing a third evening journey is a real saving in time, which for a Year 11 in February is the scarcer currency.

regions.name: City Walk and Al Manara

schoolClusters.note: Jumeirah 2 has no secondary school of its own, so IGCSE candidates here are spread across campuses on either side. The practical consequence for a budget is that two neighbours can be sitting different boards, which changes what an hour of support has to contain.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.modesIntro: Four ways to spend the same budget, which differ mainly in how much of it reaches the marks. The honest framing is what each one removes from a parent's own workload and what it leaves behind.

modes.title: A short diagnostic purchase
modes.description: One or two sessions bought deliberately as an assessment rather than as teaching. A full past paper is sat, marked against the published scheme question by question, and the losses are sorted into content, method and clock. The output is a written judgement about where money should go, which is frequently the cheapest useful thing a family can buy.

sections.heading: The only unit that matters: dirhams per recovered mark
paragraphs: Hourly rates in this market are not comparable to each other, because the hours are not comparable. The unit that makes a decision possible is dirhams per mark a student is realistically able to recover, and while nobody can produce a published figure for that, the ranking of interventions is stable and knowable. Some repairs are cheap because one habit pays across every topic. Others are expensive because attention has to be divided.

The cheapest repairs are procedural and general. Accuracy discipline is the clearest case: a student who records the full calculator value and rounds only in the final line stops losing accuracy marks on questions they already understood, and those marks are attached to multi-step questions throughout both papers. One or two sessions installs it. Two-pass paper technique is the same shape: no new content, and it recovers the unattempted final questions that carry the highest mark values.

Rebuilding a single high-weight topic area sits in the middle. It requires real teaching over four to six sessions, so it costs more, but the marks recur in every series and across both papers, which makes it defensible. Rebuilding three or four topics simultaneously is where the return collapses, because the same hours are divided and nothing becomes reliable. Reliability is what converts understanding into marks under time pressure.

The table below sets this out with cost ranges computed from the published Dubai bands rather than from any outcome data. They are arithmetic, not predictions: an hour at the qualified-teacher band of AED 150 to 300 multiplied by the number of sessions an intervention typically takes. No figure here is a promise about a grade, and any provider offering one should be treated with scepticism.

sections.heading: How far the mock sits from a boundary changes where the money goes
paragraphs: Grade boundaries are set after each series, by the board, on the basis of that series' papers, and they are not published in advance. That means nobody can tell a Jumeirah 2 family in January exactly how many marks their child needs. What a marked mock does tell them, reliably, is the shape of the gap, and the shape is what should determine the spend.

A student a few marks short of their target in a marked mock has an accuracy and technique problem, not a content problem, and the correct purchase is small: one or two sessions on accuracy discipline and two full timed papers. Buying a term of content teaching for that student spends a large amount of money re-teaching material they already know, and the marks do not move because they were never lost to ignorance.

A student fifteen marks short has one or two genuine topic gaps plus technique. A block is the right purchase. A student thirty marks short has several, and the first thing to establish is whether the entry tier is appropriate at all, because Core caps the available grade at C and no amount of teaching lifts a ceiling. Spending at specialist rates before that question is settled is the single most avoidable waste in the IGCSE year.

There is also a case for moving the money to a different subject entirely. A family funding a subject the student is already comfortably above target in, while a second subject sits just below a boundary, is spending in the wrong place. Reading all the mock results together, rather than reacting to the one that caused an argument at home, is free and changes the allocation more than any negotiation on rate.

sections.heading: Four purchases that look like tutoring and are not
paragraphs: Four things are routinely sold at tutoring rates in Dubai and are not subject teaching. Each has a legitimate use, and a family that can name which one they are buying will not be surprised when the marks do not move. The problem is never that these services exist. It is that they are invoiced as the same thing.

The first is homework supervision. An adult sitting with a student while they work through what the school set is genuinely useful for a disorganised fourteen-year-old, and it is worth paying for on those terms. It is not teaching, it does not diagnose anything, and at AED 200 an hour it is an expensive way to buy structure. A quieter room and a fixed time often achieves the same thing.

The second is content re-explanation. If the school taught a topic competently and the student did not attend properly, hearing it again helps. If the school taught it competently and the student still cannot do it, hearing it again a third time will not help, and the actual problem is that nothing has been practised to the point of reliability. The difference is visible in a marked paper and invisible in a conversation.

The third is unmarked practice. Past papers attempted and then compared against answers produce familiarity and almost no diagnosis. The marking is the expensive part of the work and the part that carries the information, which is why a family should ask explicitly whether marking is inside the hour or billed beside it. The fourth is encouragement: valuable, often necessary, and not something to pay subject-specialist rates for.

Re-explanation: helps inattention, does not help unpractised material

sections.heading: What a session costs once the marking is counted
paragraphs: Marking a full IGCSE paper properly against the published scheme, question by question, with losses attributed to cause, takes a competent teacher between thirty and sixty minutes. That labour is the most informative thing in the whole arrangement and it happens outside the lesson. Whether it is inside the quoted rate is therefore the most consequential question a parent can ask about price, and it is almost never volunteered.

At the budget end of the Dubai market, roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, marking is rarely included and often not offered, which is reasonable at that price. What a family gets is an hour of presence and re-explanation. At the qualified-teacher band of AED 150 to 300, marking is usually included within reason, though reason should be defined before the first invoice. At specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above, a written diagnosis by cause rather than a total should be part of the arrangement.

Three other things belong in the same question. Planning: who decides what the next four sessions cover, and is that written down with dates. Reporting: what a parent receives at the end of a block, and whether it is a score or an explanation. And rescheduling: what notice period protects the fee, which in a two-school-run Jumeirah 2 household is not a technicality but a recurring monthly cost.

The table below is a checklist rather than a judgement on any provider. Taking it into a first conversation converts a rate into a comparable price, which is the only way the factor-of-ten spread in this market becomes navigable. Our own position: marking a full paper is inside the hour, the plan is written and dated, and a written outcome follows each block.

sections.heading: The Dubai bands read as a monthly bill
paragraphs: Households budget monthly, so the bands are more useful converted. One weekly hour at the budget online band of AED 45 to 150 is roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on published estimates. One weekly hour with a qualified subject teacher at AED 150 to 300 is about AED 600 to 1,200. Two weekly sessions with an exam-year specialist is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified teacher. The difference is the journey, and from a Jumeirah 2 villa the journey in question is usually the Al Barsha run at six in the evening: perhaps forty minutes each way that nobody can teach during. The premium buys presence and sight of the working environment. It does not buy syllabus knowledge, and it narrows the pool to tutors willing to drive.

Published monthly packages deserve one caution each. A package is a prepayment, and a prepayment converts a flexible arrangement into a fixed one at precisely the point where a family knows least about whether it is working. A sensible sequence is a diagnostic, then a short block, then a package if the block produced something. Paying for a term before the first marked paper is the normal way a Dubai family ends up funding the wrong subject.

Some context from the regulator, which matters when a household is weighing one bill against another. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. On VAT, the only honest statement any provider can make is whether its own quoted price includes it; the general treatment of tuition fees should be confirmed with the Federal Tax Authority.

sections.heading: The tier on the entry form is also a spending decision
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. Core caps the available grade at C; Extended runs to A*. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in the same way. The tier is chosen by the school on internal evidence and locked at the final entry deadline for the series, which both boards publish per series and the exam centre holds. UAE candidates sit the June or the November series, and in either case that deadline falls months before the papers. After it, the tier cannot move for that series.

That makes the tier a hard budget constraint, and one most families discover late. Spending at specialist rates to push a Core candidate towards a B is spending on something structurally unavailable. The money is not wasted in the sense that the teaching is bad; it is wasted in the sense that the ceiling is below the target. Establishing which tier a child is entered for, from the statement of entry rather than from assumption, costs one message to the school office.

Where a tier change is genuinely warranted, the spend that produces it is small and specific. A full Extended past paper, sat under timed conditions in the autumn of Year 11 and marked honestly, is one or two sessions. If it shows the student accessing Extended-only content, it is evidence a head of department can act on. If it comes back with those questions untouched, the tier is right and the family has saved itself a term of pointless argument, which is also a return.

The related trap is the reverse: a strong candidate on Extended whose family funds broad support when the actual gap is one topic. Extended adds functions, histograms with unequal class widths, vectors in column form and the sine and cosine rules, and in most cases two of those are secure and one is not. A marked paper identifies which, and the block that follows costs a fraction of the general arrangement it replaces.

sections.heading: Cancellation, rescheduling and the money a two-school-run household loses
paragraphs: A Jumeirah 2 villa with two children at different schools generates between two and five scheduling collisions a term: a late bus, a fixture, a parents' evening, a sibling's assembly, a visitor. Each one is a potential lost fee, and across a year the total is often larger than the difference between two providers' hourly rates. This belongs in a price conversation and almost never appears in one.

Three terms decide the exposure. The notice period: twenty-four hours is common and reasonable, two hours is unusual, and a week is punitive in a household with school fixtures. Whether a missed session is lost or credited. And whether a credit expires, because a credit that must be used within the same month in a household with four busy weeks is not really a credit. Those three answers, in writing, are worth more than a ten per cent reduction in rate.

Prepaid packages concentrate this risk. Eight sessions bought as a block are eight sessions that have to be consumed inside whatever window the provider sets, and a family travelling for a week of a Dubai break will lose some. A pay-as-you-go arrangement at a slightly higher rate is frequently cheaper in practice for a household with an unpredictable evening, which is the opposite of how packages are usually sold.

The structural defence is the slot itself. Choosing 18:30 instead of 17:00 at the start of a term, because 18:30 survives a late bus and a second pick-up, prevents most cancellations rather than managing them. Online delivery helps here in a way that is purely practical: there is no travel to abort, so a session delayed by fifteen minutes is a shorter session rather than a cancelled one.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the summer: months that get paid for and not used
paragraphs: Two periods in the UAE year reliably absorb tutoring money without producing much, and both are avoidable with a conversation in advance. The first is Ramadan, when school days shorten across Dubai and the productive study window moves later. Families who hold a 17:00 slot through the month usually find the sessions tired and thin. Families who move the slot to after Iftar and keep the frequency generally keep the value.

The second is the long summer. Dubai schools break for roughly two months, and a Year 10 student moving into Year 11 can use part of that productively: the ground covered in a quiet August is the ground that does not have to be recovered in a crowded February. What does not work is a notional arrangement across a summer the family spends abroad in three different time zones, paid for in advance and attended twice.

The honest planning move for both is to agree the working weeks before any money changes hands. Which weeks the family will be in Dubai or on a compatible time zone, which weeks are written off, and what happens to the slot afterwards. That conversation costs five minutes and routinely saves the equivalent of three or four sessions, which at the qualified-teacher band is AED 600 to 1,200.

The December and spring breaks are the opposite case: short, usually spent partly at home, and well placed ahead of a February or May series. Three or four sessions inside one week of a break, with no homework competing for the evening, is the best value available in the whole calendar for covering content. The one condition is that weekly sessions resume afterwards, because content covered in an intensive and never revisited decays at exactly the rate a parent would expect.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 2 family should and should not expect to be told
paragraphs: Since this page is about money, it should be explicit about the claims that money ought not to buy. Nobody can promise a grade, a specific improvement or a refund tied to a result, and a provider offering any of those is describing something outside their control. Grade boundaries are set per series after the papers are marked; a promise made in January about a grade in August is a sales line with no mechanism behind it.

Statistics deserve the same scepticism. A satisfaction percentage, a success rate or an average score quoted without the number of students, the date and the method is not evidence, and this market is full of them. What a family can legitimately expect instead is specific and checkable: a marked script, a named component, a dated plan, and a second marked script four weeks later showing whether the first two worked.

On regulation, the honest position is simple. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any quoted figure with caution. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA training-institute permit.

And on coursework, where the cheapest offers in this market are also the most dangerous. A tutor may teach the content a task needs, work a parallel example, explain what the criteria reward and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. A tutor may not supply the solution, rewrite a submission or produce any part of what is handed in. The research behind these pages found a site selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is not a cheaper form of tutoring but a route to a candidate losing a qualification.

process.title: Send all the mock results, not just the worst one
process.description: Photographs of the marked papers across every subject are what make the allocation decision possible. Reading them together shows which subject sits nearest a boundary, which is where the budget belongs. Reacting to the single result that caused an argument at home is how families fund the wrong subject.

process.title: Confirm the code and the tier from the entry
process.description: The statement of entry names the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Those three facts decide what an hour has to contain, and getting them wrong costs a whole term of wrongly aimed practice. It takes one message to the school office and nothing to the tutor.

process.title: Buy the diagnostic before the teaching
process.description: One session in which a full past paper is marked against the official scheme, with losses attributed to content, method or clock. It produces a spending decision rather than a lesson, and it is routinely the cheapest useful purchase in the whole arrangement.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, nothing payable, no card details, built around a question the student has already lost marks on. It shows whether the tutor knows the code rather than the subject. If the answer is no, a different tutor is proposed rather than the same one defended.

process.title: Agree the terms in writing before the block
process.description: The rate, whether paper marking is inside the hour, the notice period, what happens to a missed session, and what arrives at the end of four weeks. Five minutes of clarity here is worth more over a year than any negotiation on the hourly figure.

process.title: Review against a second marked paper at week four
process.description: The block closes or continues on evidence. If the targeted marks moved, the next priority is chosen. If they did not, the diagnosis was wrong and it changes, rather than the family being asked to buy more of the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Priced in marks, not in hours
whyPoints.description: The first conversation is about which marks are recoverable and what it costs to recover them, because that is the only comparison that makes a factor-of-ten spread in hourly rates navigable. Accuracy discipline and paper technique come before content, since they are cheaper per mark.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the hour
whyPoints.description: Marking a full paper against the published scheme takes a teacher thirty to sixty minutes and carries most of the information in the arrangement. It is part of what is paid for rather than an extra line, and the losses come back attributed to cause rather than as a score.

whyPoints.title: Two subjects, not nine
whyPoints.description: A weekly hour across nine subjects is the most expensive pattern per mark in this market, because nothing becomes reliable. The budget is aimed at the one or two subjects sitting nearest a boundary, chosen from the marked mocks rather than from which subject causes the most worry.

whyPoints.title: Every figure sourced and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here come from published market rate tables and providers' own published prices, read in October 2026, with the source named in each table. Cost ranges for interventions are arithmetic from those bands, not outcome data, and they are not presented as predictions.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no improvement guarantee, no refund tied to a result, no satisfaction percentage without the number of students, the date and the method. What a family gets instead is a marked script, a dated plan and a second marked script to check it against.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what IB Gram is not
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no accreditation from Cambridge, Pearson, the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, no UAE office, no school partnerships, and no in-home service anywhere in the UAE. Each of those is checkable, which is why it is stated.

faqs.question: How should I think about tutoring cost per mark rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Ask what an intervention costs and where on the paper the marks it targets actually sit. Accuracy discipline takes one or two sessions and recovers marks attached to multi-step questions throughout both papers, which makes it the cheapest thing available. Rebuilding one high-weight topic takes four to six sessions and the marks recur every series, which is reasonable value. Spreading the same hours across four topics costs the same and secures nothing, because nothing becomes reliable. At the Dubai qualified-teacher band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, that is the difference between AED 300 well spent and AED 3,000 poorly spent, and it is decided by the plan rather than by the provider.

faqs.question: My child is three marks below a grade boundary. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: Considerably. A gap of a few marks in a marked mock is almost always accuracy and technique rather than missing content, and the correct purchase is small: one or two sessions on recording full calculator values and rounding only in the final line, plus two full timed papers to install a two-pass approach to the paper. Buying a term of content teaching for that student spends a lot of money re-teaching material they already know, and the marks do not move because they were never lost to ignorance. Reading the marked script rather than the grade is what tells the two cases apart.

faqs.question: Are grade boundaries published before the exam?
faqs.answer: No. Boundaries are set by the board after each series, on the basis of that series' papers, so nobody can tell you in January how many marks your child needs in June. Anyone presenting a boundary table as a target for an upcoming series is presenting last series' figures as this one's. What a marked mock does tell you reliably is the shape of the gap, which is what a spending plan should be built on. We also do not reproduce board grade-boundary tables, past papers or mark schemes, because those belong to Cambridge and Pearson and should be referenced from the official source.

faqs.question: Is homework supervision the same thing as tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters because they are often sold at the same rate. An adult sitting with a student while they work through what the school set is genuinely useful for a disorganised fourteen-year-old, and worth paying for on those terms. It does not diagnose anything, it does not teach, and at AED 200 an hour it is an expensive way to buy structure that a quiet room and a fixed time might provide. If supervision is what a household needs, buy it deliberately and at an appropriate price, rather than buying subject teaching and receiving supervision.

faqs.question: Is marking included in a Dubai tutoring rate?
faqs.answer: It varies, and it is the most consequential question about price that parents rarely ask. At the budget band of AED 45 to 150 an hour, marking is rarely included and often not offered, which is reasonable at that price. At the qualified-teacher band of AED 150 to 300 it is usually included within agreed limits. At specialist rates a written diagnosis by cause, rather than a score, should form part of the arrangement. Ask directly whether marking a full past paper is inside the hour or billed beside it, because that single answer changes the real price of the hour substantially.

faqs.question: How much does marking a full paper actually take?
faqs.answer: Between thirty and sixty minutes for a competent teacher, marking question by question against the published mark scheme and attributing each lost mark to content, method or the clock. That labour happens outside the lesson and it carries most of the useful information in the whole arrangement, which is why it is worth knowing whether you are paying for it. Marking that produces only a total is quicker and worth very little: a score tells a student how they did, whereas a breakdown by cause tells them what to do next, and those are different products.

faqs.question: What does a Jumeirah 2 family typically pay a month for one IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: On published Dubai bands read in October 2026, one weekly hour with a qualified subject teacher online works out at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month. A budget online tutor is about AED 240 to 600. Two weekly sessions with an exam-year specialist is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Advertised monthly packages in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures from rate tables and providers' own published prices, not an IB Gram price list, and the sources are named in the tables on this page.

faqs.question: Does an in-home tutor charge more to reach a Jumeirah 2 villa?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in Dubai run at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher working online, and the gap is the journey rather than the teaching. From a Jumeirah 2 address the relevant journey is usually the Al Barsha or Al Sufouh run at around six in the evening, perhaps forty minutes in each direction that nobody can teach during. Minimum session lengths are common in this market for exactly that reason. The premium buys presence and sight of the working environment; it does not buy knowledge of the syllabus code.

faqs.question: Will a tutor arrive at our villa in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. IGCSE support for a Jumeirah 2 household is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked paper and a shared whiteboard on screen and the session available to rewatch before an exam. The Dubai in-home market does exist and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is a fair comparison to make, and this page sets out what that premium does and does not buy.

faqs.question: If my child is entered for Core, is there a point where more spending stops helping?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a hard ceiling rather than a soft one. Cambridge Core caps the available grade at C, and Pearson Foundation works the same way, so spending at specialist rates to push a Core candidate towards a B is spending on something structurally unavailable. Before committing a budget, establish the tier from the statement of entry rather than from assumption. If a change is warranted, the evidence that moves a head of department is a full Extended past paper sat under timed conditions and marked honestly, which costs one or two sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee when we cancel at short notice?
faqs.answer: That depends on terms that should be agreed in writing before any block starts, and three answers matter. The notice period, where twenty-four hours is the common and reasonable standard. Whether a missed session is lost or credited. And whether a credit expires, because a credit that must be used inside the same month is not much of a credit for a household with school fixtures. Across a year, a household with two school runs will generate several collisions, and the cost of those usually exceeds the difference between two providers' hourly rates.

faqs.question: We have two children on different school buses. Does one tutor make this cheaper?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking about specifically. Two children in the same subject and within a year of each other can occasionally share a session productively, and the per-student cost falls. Two children in different subjects or two years apart cannot, and attempting it produces two half-sessions rather than one good one. What reliably saves money in a two-school-run household is a single later slot, usually 18:30, held for one child at a time, because the collisions that waste fees happen in the earlier windows.

faqs.question: Should we keep paying through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Keep the frequency and move the slot. School days shorten across Dubai, meals are late, and the productive study window shifts, so a session held at 17:00 through the month tends to be tired and thin while the same session after Iftar is not. Because lessons are online there is no travel attached to a later start, which makes the shift practical. Pausing for the month and planning to catch up afterwards usually costs four weeks that the final block then has to absorb, generally at the expense of full timed papers, which are the part that matters most.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai summer break cost us momentum or money?
faqs.answer: Either, depending on how it is arranged. A Year 10 student moving into Year 11 can use part of a quiet August productively, because ground covered then does not have to be recovered in a crowded February. What wastes money is a notional arrangement across a summer the family spends abroad across several time zones, paid for in advance and attended twice. Agree before any money moves which weeks the family will be in Dubai or on a compatible time zone, which weeks are written off, and what happens to the slot in September.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE tutoring invoice in the UAE show?
faqs.answer: The sessions delivered with their dates and durations, the rate applied, what is included beyond the lesson itself, and whether the amount includes VAT. On the VAT point, the only statement any provider can honestly make is whether its own quoted price includes it; the general treatment of tuition fees in the UAE should be confirmed with the Federal Tax Authority rather than taken from a tutoring page, and a provider should publish a tax registration number only if it holds one. Alongside the invoice, a family should also be receiving something about the teaching: a marked script, a dated plan, or a short written outcome.

faqs.question: What should make me walk away from a tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Four things. A promised grade, an improvement pledged in advance, or a refund tied to a result, since nobody controls any of those. A statistic quoted without the number of students, the date and the method. A claim of KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval that cannot produce a permit or centre number. And an offer to supply completed coursework, or a library of mark schemes and past papers, which is either an academic-integrity breach or a distribution of material the provider has no right to distribute. Any one of those says more about the arrangement than the hourly rate does.

intro.heading: Why the Jumeirah 3 answer is also the Umm Suqeim answer
paragraphs: A parent in Jumeirah 3 and a parent in Umm Suqeim, four kilometres apart, run almost the same search and get almost the same list of providers. Both are inside ten minutes of several British-curriculum school gates. Both sit on the two roads that carry the afternoon load along this coast. Both have a Year 10 or Year 11 child who has just brought home a set of marks that do not match the target grade. The interesting part is that the comparison usually ends in the same place regardless of which villa the family lives in, and the reason has nothing to do with distance.

Start with what an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah 3 means in practice. Someone qualified drives to the house, teaches for an hour or ninety minutes, and leaves. The appeal is obvious: no technology to manage, a parent in the next room, a child who cannot wander off. The constraint is just as obvious once you look at it from the tutor's side. The person must be free between about 4pm and 7pm, must be able to reach Jumeirah 3 or Umm Suqeim inside that window, and must happen to teach the exact syllabus your child sits. Each condition cuts the pool. Together they usually cut it to whoever is available rather than whoever is right.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai. Our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses; that is a service we run only in India. What a family on this coast gets instead is one-to-one online IGCSE tutoring with a tutor matched to the board and tier your child is entered for, which is the variable that actually decides whether a session helps. A Cambridge 0580 Extended candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 Higher candidate are sitting different papers with different mark schemes, and a tutor who teaches one fluently and the other approximately will produce a good lesson and a disappointing result.

The cost comparison points the same way. Dubai providers publishing rates during 2026 put online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 once the drive is absorbed. Budget online options advertise from AED 45 to 65 an hour, and premium named tutors have been quoted at AED 650. Those are market figures from the providers themselves, not our price list. The pattern across all of them is consistent: the travel is never free, and it is paid either in the rate or in a session that starts late.

So this page is built as a set of comparisons. Jumeirah 3 against the communities either side. Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject. Core against Extended. Provider model against provider model, with sources and dates for every rate quoted. The Ministry of Education's equivalency rules are set out too, because the number of IGCSE subjects a UAE family needs is a question competitors answer wrongly more often than they answer it at all.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Along this part of the coast most children meet the International GCSE at 16 after a British primary and lower secondary route, then split between A Levels and the IB Diploma. The four stages below are the ones Jumeirah 3 families ask about, with what each actually assesses.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external qualification sits here, which is exactly why it gets neglected. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for schools that use them, and those results are the clearest early signal of whether a child will cope with Extended tier work later. Algebraic fluency and written explanation are the two skills that carry forward.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is when Jumeirah 3 schools begin setting IGCSE option blocks, and a child who is borderline in maths or science often gets placed on a safer tier simply because nobody intervened in Year 9. A term of work here changes which papers are available in Year 11.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: A two-year course per subject, examined at the end, with most students entering eight to ten subjects. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Several Cambridge subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and Pearson maths into Foundation and Higher.
programmes.countryNote: This is the qualification that feeds UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, where five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. Getting the subject spread right in Year 10 matters more than most families realise.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: The most common post-16 route in British-curriculum schools on this coast, usually three or four subjects with linear or modular assessment depending on the board. Subject choices here are constrained by IGCSE outcomes: a Core-tier maths grade rarely opens an A Level maths place, which is why tier decisions in Year 10 have consequences two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, sits alongside the five IGCSE subjects. Verify the current requirement with the attestation authority before relying on it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme as the alternative at 16
programmes.description: Six subjects with Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and CAS, scored out of 45. Students moving from IGCSE into the Diploma meet two specific jumps: mathematics, where the Analysis and Approaches route assumes Extended-tier fluency, and the volume of internally assessed work, which has no real IGCSE equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB World Schools within a short drive of Jumeirah 3 take students from British-curriculum schools at 16, so this transition is common here. Families planning it usually want Extended maths and two sciences at IGCSE rather than the minimum spread.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Requests from Jumeirah 3 cluster around maths, the three separate sciences and English, with Economics and Business Studies behind them. Each description names the board difference or the mark-scheme trap rather than restating the subject title.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers per candidate in both boards, with Cambridge Extended on Papers 2 and 4 and Pearson Higher on 1H and 2H. Marks disappear in rounding, in unshown method and in failing to read 'give your answer in terms of pi'. Tier placement is the single most consequential decision in the subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge assesses practical skills through a separate practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson examines practical understanding inside its two written papers. Electricity circuits and moments generate the most requests. Students lose marks writing qualitative answers where the question wants a calculation with units.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry are the predictable pressure points, and both boards reward precision in state symbols and balanced equations. Candidates who learn reactions as lists rather than as patterns stall around the middle grades, which is diagnosable from one past paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is high but recall alone caps a grade. The marks sit in command words: describe, explain, suggest and compare each want different structures, and data-response questions need a stated trend plus a figure quoted from the graph. Required practicals should be revised as procedures, not stories.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response dominate. The common failure is retelling the passage instead of analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and the fix is mechanical: quote short, name the technique, state the effect on the reader. Pearson's assessment includes a non-fiction anthology that has to be known in detail.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Closed-book or set-text conditions vary by board and route, which changes how quotations must be learned. Essays score on an argument about meaning, not on plot coverage, and the fastest improvement for most students comes from planning three ideas before writing rather than writing to find out what they think.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the middle marks and evaluation decides the top ones. Students who can draw a correctly labelled market diagram and then weigh two consequences against each other move up a band quickly. Definitions must be exact, because a vague definition loses the mark outright.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study material rewards application: the same theory point scores differently depending on whether it is tied to the business in the question. Calculation questions on break-even, cash flow and ratios are reliable marks that students often skip in revision because they feel like maths.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are examined more precisely than students expect, and binary, hexadecimal and data representation questions are short, frequent and heavily weighted relative to how little time they take to secure.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: A mandatory subject in Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and one that frequently arrives new to a child who has moved to the UAE recently. Support has to work inside the school's own scheme of work rather than a parallel syllabus, because the published KHDA guidance restricts additional content.

sections.heading: What the search means, and what we actually deliver
paragraphs: Taken literally, an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah 3 is a qualified person who comes to the house on a weekday evening. That market exists in Dubai, it is large, and the rates for it are published: Dubai providers quoting in 2026 place in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. If that is specifically what you want, those providers are easy to find and this page will still be useful to you, because the board and tier sections below apply whoever teaches your child.

What IB Gram provides is different and we would rather say so in the first screen than in a footnote. Lessons are one-to-one and online, taught over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and home visits in Dubai are not part of the service; the visiting-tutor model is one we run only in India. The trade is deliberate. Removing the drive means the tutor is selected on the only criteria that predict a better grade - the board, the tier, the papers they have taught to examination - rather than on whether they can reach this part of Dubai by 4:30pm.

For an IGCSE student that trade is unusually favourable, because International GCSE teaching is board-specific in a way parents are rarely told. The same subject at the same school down the road may be examined under Cambridge in one cohort and Pearson Edexcel in another, with different paper structures, different practical arrangements and different grading scales. A tutor who knows one and improvises the other wastes the first month of a block discovering it. Matching by board first is cheap to do and expensive to skip.

sections.heading: Jumeirah 3 against the communities either side
paragraphs: Families comparing neighbourhoods usually want to know whether the tutoring options genuinely differ a few kilometres away. For the most part they do not. The school gates change, the drive changes, the rate quotes do not, and the board question stays identical. The one real difference the map makes is proximity to the tuition centres clustered inland around Al Quoz, which is a shorter journey from Al Manara or Al Safa than from the beach road.

The table sets out what the afternoon actually looks like from each community, because that is the variable a provider will not discuss with you. A visiting tutor's day is a route, and your session's start time is a function of where you sit on it. Being first on the route means a reliable start and an early finish; being third means a reliable delay. None of that is visible when you book, and it is the most common reason a family that chose in-home in September is looking again in January.

Read the last column as the practical conclusion. In every one of these communities the same two things decide whether tutoring works: a slot that survives the week, and a tutor who teaches the right board. Jumeirah 3 is not a special case, and neither is Umm Suqeim - which is why this page says plainly that the answer travels across the whole coast rather than pretending each community needs a different solution.

The pattern in the numbers is worth stating directly. Rates rise with three things: the level being taught, the scarcity of the specialism, and the travel involved. An entry-level online tutor advertised from AED 45 an hour and a named examiner-level tutor quoted at AED 650 are both real market positions, and the useful band for a Year 11 IGCSE candidate sits between them. If a quote you receive sits well outside these bands in either direction, ask what explains it: an examiner-level specialist at the top end, or a university student at the bottom, are both legitimate answers, and both change what you should expect from the session.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out before you book anyone
paragraphs: The first question to ask your child's school is which board each subject is entered under, and the second is which tier. Parents are often surprised that the answer differs between subjects inside the same school, and occasionally between cohorts in the same subject. Until you know, any tutoring is partly guesswork, because the papers are not interchangeable. A Cambridge candidate sitting a separate practical test needs practical technique rehearsed; a Pearson candidate whose practical understanding is examined inside the written papers needs something different from the same hours.

The table compares the two boards for the subjects most often requested from this coast, using the syllabus codes that appear on your child's statement of entry. Those codes are the most useful thing on the document. They let you find the correct specification and the correct past papers on the board's own site, and they let a tutor confirm in one line that they teach the right course. Syllabus-code specificity is almost entirely absent from competing pages in this market, which is odd, because it is the detail that prevents a wasted term.

One practical note on materials. Neither we nor any provider should be sending you syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those are the boards' copyright. The right approach is to reference them and link to the board's own site, where the current specification and the published past papers live. A provider that supplies a folder of other people's documents is telling you something about its attitude to the rules it operates under.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: who decides and when
paragraphs: Tiering is the decision that quietly sets the ceiling on a result, and it is usually made by the school in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence available at that point. Cambridge splits several subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher. The lower tier is a shorter content list with a lower maximum grade; the upper tier is more content with the full range available. Neither is a judgement about a child's worth, and both are reversible up to the entry deadline, which is the detail families miss.

Where tutoring genuinely changes the picture is the window between a mock result and the final entry decision. If a student is sitting just under the threshold the school uses, a focused block on the specific topics that separate the tiers can move them over it. That requires knowing which topics those are, which is a board-and-syllabus question rather than a general maths question. It also requires starting early enough that the school still has time to change the entry, which is why the mock period is the moment to have the conversation rather than the end of Year 11.

The honest counterpoint: moving a student up a tier they are not ready for produces a worse outcome than a secure result on the lower tier. A candidate who finishes the Extended papers having attempted half the questions will not beat the same candidate on Core. We will give you a view based on marked past-paper evidence rather than optimism, and if the evidence says the lower tier is the better entry, we will say that even though it is the less flattering answer.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track
paragraphs: Families who intend to study or work in the UAE eventually meet certificate equivalency, and the British-track rules are published clearly enough to state. Reporting on the Ministry's clarification sets out that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject figure matters because a ranking competitor in this market publishes six, and a family planning around the wrong number may drop a subject it needed or carry one it did not. The subject spread is the part worth planning in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 12. Note also that equivalency rules are administered by the Ministry and the emirate attestation channels, not by any tutoring provider: we can explain the requirement and point you to the official channel, and we cannot process or guarantee any part of it.

For the American track the same reporting gives different requirements - English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. For the IB there is no points threshold in that source, so no IB equivalency figure appears anywhere on this page. Verify whichever track applies to your child directly with the Ministry before making a decision that depends on it.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in Dubai, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal, and a parent comparing providers is entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Two further points are worth knowing. First, no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting you a specific penalty amount is quoting something unverified. Second, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs an educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority for a training institute. That is a specific permit issued to specific premises, and it is the thing providers are describing when they call themselves approved by the authority. IB Gram does not hold it, does not claim it, and has no office in the UAE.

In Abu Dhabi a further rule applies that Dubai parents should still know about, because families move between emirates: press reporting on the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules describes school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. The practical reading for any family is simple - never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately, however convenient it looks.
