sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is deliberately short. Tell us the subject, the board if you know it, the tier if you know that, the year group and the evenings that suit a Jumeirah 3 schedule. We match a tutor who teaches that specification, and the first lesson is a free trial with that tutor, taught on real syllabus content so you can judge the teaching rather than the sales pitch. No schedule is agreed until afterwards, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than asking you to give it another fortnight.

Availability is where most providers go quiet, so here is the honest position. Mainstream IGCSE subjects can usually be covered within a few working days. A narrow combination, or a request in the fortnight before mocks or the weeks before a written series, can take longer. When the right specialist has no slot we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same tutor, a specialist outside the UAE teaching the same board on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start with the work resequenced around the deadline that matters. Putting a generalist in front of a Year 11 candidate to fill a gap serves nobody.

A last word on what to send. The single most useful document is your child's statement of entry or option sheet, because it carries the syllabus codes. The second most useful is the most recent marked assessment, ideally the paper itself rather than the grade. With those two things a tutor can plan the first three sessions before the first one starts, which is otherwise a fortnight of discovery that you paid for.

process.title: Send the subject, board and tier
process.description: A short message with the subject, the board if you know it, the tier if that is decided, the year group and the evenings that work. If you have the statement of entry or the option sheet, the syllabus codes on it answer most of our questions before we ask them.

process.title: We match on specification, not location
process.description: Tutors are matched to the exact syllabus - Cambridge 0580 Extended rather than maths in general - because the papers are not interchangeable. Distance from Jumeirah 3 plays no part in the match, which is what widens the pool of genuine board specialists.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: One lesson, taught on real syllabus content, with no schedule agreed beforehand. You and your child judge the explanation and the pace, then decide. If it is not right, we change the tutor; the risk of a poor match sits with us rather than with your term.

process.title: A block with a target written down
process.description: Sessions are booked as a block aimed at something nameable: a tier decision, a paper to finish in the time, a topic never secured. A target makes the block reviewable at the end, which an open-ended weekly arrangement never is.

process.title: Audit it after four weeks
process.description: Four weeks in, compare the marked work against the diagnostic paper from week one. If the gap has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does. We would rather have that conversation in November than in April, and so would you.

whyPoints.title: Board-first matching
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subject differently, from paper structure to how practical work is assessed. Matching on the specification rather than the subject name removes the first month of mutual discovery that a cross-board tutor otherwise needs.

whyPoints.title: The same answer across the coast
whyPoints.description: Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Jumeirah 1 share gates, traffic and rate quotes, so a provider claiming a bespoke neighbourhood solution is describing marketing rather than a difference. What changes between these communities is the drive, and an online slot removes it.

whyPoints.title: Rates with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to a published provider page or a dated Dubai cost table, quoted as a market band. We do not present market rates as our own prices, and we do not publish an invented price list to look competitive.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice from marked evidence
whyPoints.description: Whether a student should sit Extended or Core is answered from past papers marked against the published scheme, not from encouragement. Sometimes the useful answer is the less flattering one, and a provider that never gives it is not giving you information.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the permit position
whyPoints.description: We explain the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime and the separate training-institute permit for premises, and we state plainly that IB Gram holds no regulator approval and has no UAE office. Providers implying otherwise are making a claim that is checkable.

whyPoints.title: Boards' materials referenced, not redistributed
whyPoints.description: Specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and live on their sites. We point you to them and teach from them rather than handing out a folder of other people's documents, which is both a copyright question and a sign of how a provider works.

faqs.question: Would the answer be different if we lived in Umm Suqeim rather than Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all, and that is the useful finding. These two communities share the same coastal road network, draw on overlapping school gates, and get quoted the same rates by the same providers. The afternoon traffic profile is near identical, so a visiting tutor faces the same unpredictable drive from either address. What decides whether tutoring works in both places is the same pair of factors: a slot that survives a busy week, and a tutor matched to the correct examination board and tier. Only one real difference exists on this coast, which is that tuition centres inland around Al Quoz are a shorter trip from Al Manara and Al Safa.

faqs.question: How do I find out which International GCSE board my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, subject by subject, and ask for it in writing. The definitive document is your child's statement of entry, which lists the syllabus code for every entry: four digits such as 0580 or 0625 for Cambridge, and codes such as 4MA1 or 4PH1 for Pearson Edexcel. Those codes let you find the correct specification and past papers on the board's own website, and they let a tutor confirm in one line that they teach the right course. Boards can differ between subjects within one school, so a single answer for the whole timetable is usually incomplete.

faqs.question: What actually differs between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Paper structure, practical assessment and tier naming, mostly. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended and assesses science practical skills through a separate practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson Edexcel examines practical understanding inside its written papers and splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Question stems, diagram conventions and mark-scheme wording differ enough that revising with the wrong board's past papers is actively unhelpful. The content overlap is large, which is why a cross-board tutor sounds convincing in a first lesson and then costs a student marks in a real paper.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for the Core tier or the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: The school decides, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11, from the evidence it has. The lower tier covers less content and caps the maximum grade; the upper tier covers more and leaves the full range available. The decision can be changed up to the board's entry deadline, which is why the mock period is the moment to raise it. A focused block on the topics that separate the tiers can move a borderline student up. A student who would not finish the upper-tier papers is better served by a secure result on the lower tier.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE tutor cost for a family on the Jumeirah coast?
faqs.answer: Market figures published by Dubai providers in 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, a visiting tutor at the home at roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed, and specialist examination-year tutors at AED 200 to 450 or more. Budget online options advertise from AED 45 to 65, and one premium named tutor is quoted at AED 650. Those are the market's numbers with their sources, not our price list. If a quote sits outside those bands, ask what explains it before you accept or dismiss it.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor who travels to the villa charge more per hour?
faqs.answer: Because the hour you book is not the only hour the tutor spends. A journey across this part of Dubai in the afternoon peak can take forty to ninety minutes each way, and that time has to be paid for somewhere. In the published Dubai bands it shows up as a higher hourly rate for in-home work than for the same tutor teaching online. The other place it shows up is the start time: a session scheduled at 4:30pm on a route with three stops often begins later than booked. Removing the journey removes both costs at once.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count for British-track equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market publishes six, which is the sort of error that leads a family to carry a subject it did not need. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry and the emirate attestation channels, so verify the current rule with them before planning around it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards those five subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The reporting on the Ministry's requirements is explicit that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. They remain mandatory at school in Dubai under the published guidance from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which requires them regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so a child takes them and they occupy timetable periods. They simply do not count towards the equivalency total. That distinction is worth confirming with your school when option blocks are set, because it affects how many other accredited subjects your child needs to carry.

faqs.question: Does booking an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah 3 mean a tutor arrives at our villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We target the phrase because it is what parents in Dubai search, and we would rather answer it in the first screen than bury the answer. Our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and home visits in Dubai are not a service we offer; the visiting model is one we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The benefit is a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code your child sits, and an evening start that does not depend on the beach road clearing in time.

faqs.question: Can my child sit different subjects with different examination boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many Dubai schools do exactly that, entering maths with one board and the sciences with another. It is decided by the school rather than the family. The practical consequence for tutoring is that each subject needs its own board-specific preparation, including the right past papers, and that revision resources have to be checked individually rather than bought as a set. When you ask us for help in two subjects, we confirm the board for each separately, because assuming one answer covers the whole timetable is how the wrong papers end up in a revision folder.

faqs.question: When are International GCSE examinations actually held, and which series will my child sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also operates an extra February sitting, but it is offered to India only and a candidate in Jumeirah 3 cannot enter it; June and November are the two series available here, each on one of six zone timetables, with entry deadlines months before the papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. Which series your child sits is set by the school, so confirm it with them and use the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the choice is genuinely open. The content built in Year 10 is what Year 11 papers assume, and the tier decision is made on Year 10 and early Year 11 evidence, so support in that window influences which papers are available at the end. Starting in Year 11 is still worthwhile and is when most families actually begin, but the work becomes triage: choosing the components where effort converts into marks and accepting that some topics will not be rebuilt. The worst time to start is after the final entry deadline has fixed a tier nobody intended.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if lessons are taught online?
faqs.answer: Practical work itself happens at school, where the equipment and the supervision are. What a tutor can do online is prepare the examined element, and that differs by board: Cambridge candidates face either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards rehearsed technique, correct tabulation, graph plotting and uncertainty handling. Pearson Edexcel candidates meet practical understanding inside the written papers, which rewards knowing method and sources of error. Both are taught well through worked examples, past-paper practical questions and marking against the published scheme. Neither requires a tutor standing beside a bench.

faqs.question: What should I send so the first lesson is not spent on discovery?
faqs.answer: Two documents do most of the work. The statement of entry or option sheet, because it carries the syllabus codes and the tier, and the most recent marked assessment, ideally the script itself rather than the reported grade. With those, a tutor can plan the first three sessions before the first one begins. Add the school's next internal deadline and the mock window if you have them. Families who send nothing usually pay for a fortnight of the tutor working out what the school has already written down, which is the easiest waste to avoid.

intro.heading: The school run is the real constraint, not the tutor supply
paragraphs: Ask a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent when their child could sit down with a tutor and the first answer is usually optimistic. Four o'clock, they say. Then you walk through the actual afternoon. School finishes between 2.45pm and 3.30pm depending on the campus and the year group. The pick-up queue at the Jumeirah Park gate or on the Sports City side runs fifteen minutes before anyone moves. Al Khail Road at 3.30pm adds another twenty. A snack, a shower, a bag emptied onto the kitchen island. By the time a fifteen-year-old is capable of thinking about simultaneous equations it is closer to half past five, and if there is football or swimming in Sports City it is closer to seven.

This is why in-home tuition in communities like this one so often disappoints. The tutor is driving in through the same traffic, from Al Barsha or Motor City or further, and arrives at the hour when the student has already run out of attention. Forty of the sixty minutes get spent warming up. The family pays for the car as well as the lesson, because market in-home rates in Dubai include the travel whether the invoice itemises it or not.

IB Gram's answer is to remove the travel from the equation entirely. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, with a tutor chosen for the specific board and subject your child sits. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that is a service we run only in India. Saying so plainly matters more than it sounds, because it is the difference between a family planning around a 7.15pm video call and a family waiting for a car.

There is a second reason the school run belongs at the top of this page rather than in a footnote. Which school your child attends determines which awarding body they sit, and the campuses around this community are split. A Cambridge candidate and a Pearson Edexcel candidate living on the same street in Jumeirah Golf Estates need different past papers, different tier decisions and, in several subjects, different tutors. The first question we ask is therefore not what grade you want but which syllabus code appears on the last report, because everything after that depends on the answer.

What follows is built for the Jumeirah Golf Estates timetable. It names the schools this community feeds and which boards they use, maps the realistic window for a session against each school's finish, sets out where IGCSE marks are actually lost at Core and Extended, prices the market honestly, and counts the June and November series backwards so you can see which levers are still available. Nothing here promises a grade, and every dirham figure on this page belongs to the market rather than to us.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Golf Estates children on a British-curriculum path meet two IGCSE awarding bodies and then a fork at sixteen. Which board your child's school uses changes the paper structure, the tiering and in some subjects the content, so it is the first thing to establish before any tuition starts.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The more common route in Dubai. Subjects carry a four-digit syllabus code — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English — and most science and maths subjects split into Core and Extended. Core caps the available grade at 5; Extended runs the full 9 to 1. The tier decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10, and it is reversible more often than families assume.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone applies. UAE candidates sit the June and November series only; the February and March series is offered to India.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Used by a significant minority of Dubai schools and by most private candidates. Codes look different — 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A — and the tiering language differs too: Foundation covers grades 5 to 1 and Higher covers 9 to 4. Several subjects assess in two papers rather than three, which changes revision shape considerably.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. As a checkable example of lead times, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma after Year 11
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools around Jumeirah Golf Estates continue to A Level, while several campuses a short drive away switch to the IB Diploma. The choice is made in Year 11 and it reaches back into IGCSE subject selection: a student intending Diploma Higher Level sciences needs Extended tier, and a student intending A Level Mathematics is served by Additional Mathematics 0606 in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: This fork matters for Ministry of Education equivalency later. The published British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before relying on them.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of New Dubai concentrate on Mathematics and the separate sciences, with English as a Second Language and Economics appearing from Year 11. Below is what each subject assesses and where Jumeirah Golf Estates students most often lose marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, trigonometry, transformations and probability. The commonest lost marks are not conceptual: unrounded intermediate values carried through a multi-step answer, and method lines omitted on questions worth four or five marks where the final figure is wrong.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken in Year 11 by students heading to A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics. Introduces calculus, logarithms and vectors ahead of time, and it is the single best preparation for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. Students struggle with differentiation applied to problems rather than to expressions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. Electricity is where the grade is usually decided: series and parallel reasoning collapses under unfamiliar circuit diagrams, and candidates quote a formula without rearranging it correctly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, organic chemistry and qualitative analysis. Moles questions carry disproportionate weight and are rushed; the ion tests in the practical paper are memorisable marks that students routinely leave on the table.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics and ecology. The content is manageable and the marks are lost on precision of language: osmosis answers that omit the words partially permeable membrane, or enzyme answers that say the enzyme dies.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award for students not taking three separate sciences. Coordinated Science 0654 is worth two grades and covers all three disciplines at Extended depth; Combined 0653 is a single award. Students moved onto these routes mid-Year 10 need the gap identified rather than the whole syllabus retaught.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in 0511, a speaking endorsement. Writing marks hinge on text type and register — a student who produces an essay when a report was asked for loses marks nobody has ever explained to them.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. The reading paper rewards close selection of evidence and short precise comment; long paraphrase scores badly, and it is the habit most students arrive with.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Market systems, the price mechanism, government intervention and development. Diagrams must be labelled fully and then referred to in the prose. A correct diagram the answer never mentions earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Business activity, marketing, finance and people in business. The structured questions require application to the case organisation, and generic answers about customers and profit are the standard reason a confident student plateaus at grade 6.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode questions reward disciplined layout; students who code fluently often lose marks because trace tables are untidy rather than wrong.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must run Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, so this sits on the timetable whatever the IGCSE choices are. Because outside content needs Ministry of Education permission, support here follows the school's own material.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah Golf Estates afternoon actually looks like
paragraphs: A session time is a logistics decision dressed up as an educational one. Here is the afternoon in this community, accurately. Secondary finish times across the campuses Jumeirah Golf Estates families use range from about 2.45pm to 3.30pm. The pick-up queue costs ten to twenty minutes before a car moves. The drive home from the nearest cluster is eight to fifteen minutes; from the Al Barsha South ring it is twenty to twenty-five, and more if the Al Khail junction has stacked.

Add the human part. A teenager needs twenty minutes between arriving and being able to do anything useful. If there is a club in Dubai Sports City — and for this community there very often is — the child leaves again at 4.30pm and gets back after six. That single fact is why so many Jumeirah Golf Estates tuition slots that look sensible on paper collapse within three weeks.

The workable windows, therefore, are narrower than families expect and later. Weekday sessions land well between 6pm and 8.15pm. Friday afternoon works for some households and is impossible for others. Weekend mornings are the most underused slot in this community and the best one for anything requiring sustained concentration, which in Year 11 means past papers.

Online delivery is what makes those windows usable at all. There is no tutor in a car, so a 7.15pm start is simply a 7.15pm start, and a session can move to Saturday morning in a heavy week without anybody renegotiating a round trip.

sections.heading: Which board is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This question stops more tuition from working than any other, and most parents cannot answer it on the first call. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different papers, different tier structures and, in some subjects, genuinely different content. A tutor who teaches 0580 fluently and has never opened 4MA1 will waste your child's time on topics that are not examined and miss ones that are.

Find the answer on the last school report or on the examination entry confirmation, where the syllabus code appears. Cambridge codes are four digits: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0654 Coordinated Science, 0500 First Language English. Pearson codes start with a digit and letters: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. If neither appears anywhere, ask the head of year directly; it takes one email.

It is also entirely normal in Dubai for a child to sit different subjects with different boards, because schools pick per department. A Jumeirah Golf Estates student can be a Cambridge mathematician and a Pearson physicist in the same Year 11. That is fine, and it is another argument for subject-specific tutors rather than one person covering everything.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Of all the things a Year 10 parent should understand, tiering is the one most often missed until it cannot be changed. On Cambridge IGCSE, Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5. On Pearson, Foundation entry caps it at 5 as well. A student targeting a grade 7 for A Level or Diploma Higher Level entry cannot get there from the lower tier, no matter how well the paper goes.

Schools make the decision for sound reasons: a borderline student entered for Extended can score below the lowest Extended grade and come away with nothing, where Core would have produced a safe 4 or 5. That is a real risk, not administrative caution. But it is a decision made in Year 10 on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved. Nobody moves them if nobody asks.

This is where a diagnostic block earns its keep. Six sessions on Extended material produce a straightforward answer: either the student handles the additional topics or the gap is wider than one term can close. We have told Jumeirah Golf Estates families both things, and the second is more useful than an encouraging guess.

If your child is already on the lower tier and the post-16 plan requires a 7, the honest conversation is about whether the post-16 plan changes or whether a November resit on the higher tier is the route. Both are legitimate. Pretending the ceiling is not there is not.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Parents arrive describing a subject. Examiners see something narrower: a repeated technical habit costing four or five marks across a paper. Mathematics students lose marks by rounding an intermediate value and carrying it forward, so a correct method produces a wrong number, and by writing only an answer on a five-mark question where the method lines are the marks. Neither is a knowledge gap and both are fixable in three sessions.

In Physics, electricity decides the grade. Series and parallel reasoning holds up in the textbook circuit and collapses in an unfamiliar one, and candidates quote the right relationship then rearrange it wrongly under time pressure. In Chemistry, moles questions carry weight beyond their apparent size, and the qualitative analysis ion tests are pure recall marks that students repeatedly leave blank. In Biology, the loss is linguistic: an osmosis answer that never says partially permeable membrane, an enzyme answer that says the enzyme died.

In English, the reading paper rewards short precise comment anchored to a selected quotation, and the habit most students bring is extended paraphrase, which scores very little however well written. In Economics and Business Studies, the marks sit in application: a fully labelled diagram the prose never refers to, or a tool recited accurately and never applied to the organisation in the stimulus.

This is why the most valuable thing you can send before a trial lesson is a marked paper. A tutor reading your child's actual mistakes can name the pattern in twenty minutes. A tutor given only a subject name starts at the beginning of the syllabus, which is almost always the wrong place.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Take the cheapest option first, because it is the one most Jumeirah Golf Estates families price against. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student, is advertised in this market from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; one platform publishes rates from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65. At one weekly hour that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month on published monthly estimates. For a Year 9 student needing homework structure, that can be perfectly adequate.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits higher, at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour on rates published in October 2026; one agency lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Monthly, that is in the region of AED 600 to AED 1,200 for a weekly session. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel runs from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with one provider publishing monthly packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. Specialist IGCSE and IB tuition is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision as high as AED 650.

Two honest observations. The in-home premium buys travel, not teaching time, and in this community the travel is substantial. And the figures above are market rates attributed to the providers and surveys that published them, with the research date stated; they are not IB Gram's prices, which are quoted to you after the free trial lesson. Anyone quoting you a rate should be able to say what it includes and whether it is per hour or per lesson.

For context on the wider budget, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are therefore the fixed part of your planning and tuition is the variable.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Families consistently start too late because the calendar is described forwards. Counted backwards it is clear what is still available. The examination is fixed. Entry deadlines sit months in front of it. School mocks sit roughly a term ahead. By February of Year 11, several decisions — tier, board, subject count — are already behind you.

Get the series right first. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Jumeirah Golf Estates candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk, not theirs. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November, with provisional timetables published well ahead of each series.

The useful habit is to work from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page. As a check on how far ahead the machinery runs: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in the UAE
paragraphs: It is worth asking, and almost nobody does. Private tutoring in the UAE sits under a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is wider than families assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category explains part of the AED 45 to AED 150 band, and it is worth knowing when you are comparing a rate rather than a person. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted.

One boundary to respect. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. This has been reported in the regional press and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. Practically: do not ask for your child's own classroom teacher as a paid tutor.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity again and needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre or office, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule, stated correctly
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, the school-leaving certificate goes through a Ministry of Education equivalency process, and the British-track requirement is specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause matters in Dubai, where Arabic and Islamic Education are mandatory school subjects. A student can be sitting eight or nine subjects in total and still need to check which five are being counted. One provider currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule says five. Getting this right is not a detail when a family is choosing whether to drop a subject in Year 11.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process the Ministry performs, not something a tutoring provider performs or can guarantee, and tuition is not a requirement for it. And requirements change, so verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before acting. We describe it here because no competitor page in this market mentions equivalency at all, not because we administer it.

The practical use of the rule in Year 11 is defensive. If a Jumeirah Golf Estates family is weighing whether to drop a subject under pressure, the question is whether five countable subjects will still be in place afterwards, with Arabic and Islamic education set aside from the count. That is a five-minute check against the entry list, and it is far easier to do in November than to discover in August.

sections.heading: Booking a tutor that survives a Dubai term
paragraphs: Half the tuition arrangements that fail in this community fail on logistics rather than teaching. A slot agreed in September against an optimistic view of the afternoon collapses by October, the sessions become irregular, and the continuity that makes tuition work disappears. So we ask for the awkward information first: what time does your child actually get through the door, and which afternoons already have something in them.

Then we ask for the board and syllabus code, and for the last marked paper or report. With those three things a match is usually quick and accurate. The free trial lesson exists to test the only thing a profile cannot show you: whether this tutor can explain the specific confusion your child has. Give them a real lost question from the mock beforehand.

What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a student on the wrong board and let the term run. If no appropriate board-specific tutor is free in your windows, you are told the wait and, where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, told that too, before any payment. And we agree a stop date at the outset, usually study leave or the end of a specific block, so that tuition is reviewed rather than renewed by inertia.
Nothing on this page promises a grade. We publish no guaranteed outcomes, no satisfaction percentages, and no self-asserted ratings, and in this market that absence is information in itself.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor come to our home in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach Jumeirah Golf Estates students one-to-one over live video, at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai and published market rates for an in-home visit including travel run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Dropping the visit is what lets us match your child to a tutor who teaches their exact board rather than one who happens to live nearby.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start for a child in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first suggest. Secondary finish times across the campuses this community uses run from about 2.45pm to 3.30pm, the pick-up queue costs ten to twenty minutes, and the drive home is eight to twenty-five minutes depending on the cluster. Add the twenty minutes a teenager needs to become useful and the earliest sensible start is about 5.30pm. If there is a club in Dubai Sports City, which there often is, it moves to 7pm or 7.15pm. Weekend mornings are the most underused slot here and the best one for timed papers.

faqs.question: How do I check which board the Jumeirah Golf Estates school run ends at, Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Look for the syllabus code on the last school report or on the examination entry confirmation. Cambridge codes are four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Pearson codes combine a digit and letters — 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. If no code appears anywhere, email the head of year. It is entirely normal in Dubai for one student to sit different subjects with different boards, because schools choose per department.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series does a Jumeirah Golf Estates candidate sit, June or November?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, the June series, with November available as the resit route. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it should play no part in a UAE family's planning. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable, so confirm your zone with the exams officer.

faqs.question: Is my child on the Core or the Extended tier, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than almost anything else. Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and Pearson Foundation entry does the same, so a student needing a 7 for A Level or IB Diploma Higher Level cannot reach it from the lower tier. Schools decide tiering in Year 10 for defensible reasons, since a borderline student on the higher tier carries real risk. But the decision is reviewable early in Year 11 if the evidence changes, and nobody reviews it unless a parent asks. Check the entry, not the assumption.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost around Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Cheapest first: budget online tuition, usually a university-student tutor, is advertised in Dubai from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at one weekly session. A qualified subject tutor online sits at about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, or AED 600 to AED 1,200 monthly. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to AED 500. faqs.question: Where do IGCSE students most often lose marks?
faqs.answer: On habits rather than knowledge. In Mathematics, rounding an intermediate value and carrying it forward, and writing an answer without the method lines that carry most of the marks. In Physics, unfamiliar circuit diagrams and formula rearrangement under time pressure. In Chemistry, moles calculations and the recall marks in the ion tests. In Biology, imprecise language — osmosis answers missing partially permeable membrane. In English, extended paraphrase where short comment on selected evidence was wanted. Each of these is fixable in a few sessions once identified, which is why a marked paper is worth more than a description.

faqs.question: How many subjects should my child take tuition in at once?
faqs.answer: One, usually, and two at most. The constraint is not money but the student's week: a subject needs unaided practice between sessions, and that attempt is where the learning happens. Three weekly tuition slots on top of a full Dubai timetable and a club schedule produces attendance without progress. If three subjects genuinely look weak, start with the one that most affects the post-16 plan, run a short diagnostic block in it, and see whether the technique fixes transfer. They often do, because the error is frequently about reading questions.

faqs.question: Does my child need a permitted tutor, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold it and under which category. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Can my child resit an IGCSE if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in November as well as May/June, so a resit is roughly five months away rather than a year. Two practical points. First, the entry deadline for November falls well before the exam and often before results have settled in a family's mind, so find out the date in advance rather than after results day. Second, a resit is an opportunity to change tier where that is the real constraint. Private candidate entry is possible through approved centres in Dubai.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE equivalency rule actually count?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which matters in Dubai where both are mandatory school subjects. One provider ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six subjects are required; the published rule says five. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae, because the Ministry runs this process, not a tutor.

faqs.question: Which schools do IGCSE students in Jumeirah Golf Estates generally attend?
faqs.answer: The immediate cluster is British curriculum and sits in Jumeirah Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, with a second ring fifteen to twenty-five minutes away in Al Barsha South and JVT that includes campuses continuing to the IB Diploma. Finish times across these schools differ by up to forty-five minutes, which is why two neighbours in the same street can need very different session slots. faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around mock exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the clearest practical advantage of online delivery for a family here. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, move within the week when a coursework deadline or a tournament collides, and pause entirely during mock or final examination weeks. None of it requires a tutor's round trip to be rearranged, so it can usually be settled in the same week. We also agree a stop date at the start, normally study leave or the June series, so the arrangement has a defined end rather than drifting on.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the content, explains what the assessment criteria reward, interrogates a plan, points out where a method will not produce usable data, marks a draft against the criteria and explains what is losing marks, and teaches referencing properly. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of the work, supply a finished research question, or provide data the student has not collected. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. Keep the written session notes: a dated record that the help given was feedback on the student's own drafts protects the student.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for my child's subject and board?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a realistic wait, rather than offered somebody who teaches the other board. Availability is thinnest for Pearson science combinations, Computer Science and Additional Mathematics 0606, and tightest in the eight weeks before the June series. Where the only available specialist is based outside the UAE, we say so before you pay anything, including which time zone they teach from. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is precisely why we do: the bookings we take are the ones we can actually staff.

intro.heading: The evening is the constraint, not the subject
paragraphs: Jumeirah Islands is a gated community of villas built around lakes, with a pavilion at its centre and no school inside the gates. That single fact shapes tutoring here more than anything academic. Every child leaves the community for school, most travelling to Jumeirah Village, The Meadows, Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, and the return journey puts them home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50 depending on the school and the route order.

So the first useful question is not which tutor, but which hour. A session booked at 16:30 sounds reasonable on paper and in practice begins before a fifteen-year-old has eaten, changed or stopped thinking about the bus. Sessions booked at the wrong hour are the commonest reason a tutoring arrangement quietly stops in week five, and it has nothing to do with the tutor's ability.

The second question is which term. IGCSE support is usually bought in the spring of Year 11, which is the most expensive point in the cycle and the one with the least room to work. The same money spent across Years 10 and 11 as a single weekly hour does considerably more, keeps the higher tier reachable while that decision is still open, and secures a slot before the demand arrives.

The third is the entry itself. Ask your school's exams officer for the syllabus code and tier in each subject, because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are examined differently and their past papers are not interchangeable. That email is free and it prevents the most expensive mistake in Dubai IGCSE tutoring, which is a competent tutor working from the wrong board's material.

On delivery we are direct. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service, and there is no office or centre here either. What a Jumeirah Islands family gets is live online IGCSE tutoring: one tutor, one student, video, past papers shared on screen, scheduled around the arrival time that actually applies to your household.

It is worth saying what this page deliberately does not do. It does not describe our tutors as dedicated or passionate, because you cannot check either. It gives you the arrival times that decide your slot, the questions to put to your exams officer, the published rates in this market with the month we read them, and the two UAE rules that shape a Dubai timetable. If a section does not answer something, it should not be on the page.

That turns out to suit this community particularly well. Nobody has to add a second journey to an evening that already contains one, a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a negotiation, and the arrangement survives a family's travel and a change of school without the search starting again. The rest of this page is the practical detail: slots, terms, boards, subjects and what the market charges.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-islan.programmesIntro: The UK-curriculum sequence has four stages, and the amount of support each needs differs sharply. The cheapest intervention is the earliest one.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Fractions, negative indices, algebraic beginnings, the habit of showing working, and writing an explanation that answers the question asked. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October where a school uses them, and give an external reference point before any tiering decision is made.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools set IGCSE tiering on Year 9 evidence, sometimes before the family has discussed it. For a household here, an hour a week in Year 9 is the least expensive way to keep the higher tier available.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, externally examined by Cambridge or Pearson. Grades decide sixth-form subject access and count towards Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track. Tiering caps the grade and removes content, which matters more than most families realise.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge's June and November series, or Pearson's May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no plan here should be built around a February exam window.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects, with the real step up being independence rather than content volume. Students who built working habits during IGCSE need less support here; those who were carried through Year 11 by intensive tutoring frequently need more.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade, alongside five IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-IGCSE route, offered by several schools within reach of these gates. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Students arriving from Extended IGCSE mathematics are usually well placed for Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Diploma step widens rather than narrows the workload, which catches families out. If that route is likely, use the summer after Year 11 for algebraic fluency rather than discovering the gap in October.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-islan.subjectsIntro: The subjects Jumeirah Islands families ask about, with how many weekly hours each realistically needs and where the marks go. Use this to choose one subject rather than spreading an hour across three.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject with the strongest case for a full weekly hour across both years, because it compounds and because it gates sixth-form options. Extended work is method-led: multi-step questions where the setup is right and the middle is lost. Marked past papers under time do most of the work.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Needs more weeks than families budget for, because electricity and moments usually have to be rebuilt rather than revised. Three sessions on circuits alone is normal. The practical component rewards precise method description, which transfers to the other two sciences.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Good value per session, because the common weaknesses are procedural. Mole calculations need one reliable layout drilled; qualitative analysis and separation techniques carry marks that students drop only because the tests were never systematically learned.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Slower to shift than the other sciences because the problem is precision of language rather than content. Mark schemes want a named variable and a direction; students write that something improved. Budget weeks rather than money, and work against real mark schemes.

subjects.name: English Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading comprehension respond quickly; composition takes longer. Worth confirming which English qualification your child is entered for, because students entered for the wrong one lose marks for reasons nobody explains to them.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Level-of-response marking means an undeveloped correct point earns little, so the work is structure and evaluation rather than content. Technique transfers between the two subjects, which makes a short block unusually efficient if your child takes both.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: A thinner tutor pool, so slots are scarcer in the spring. Computer Science wants pseudocode, trace tables and algorithmic reasoning in a written paper; ICT is practical and applied. The two get confused at option time and the choice is hard to unwind in Year 11.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level Mathematics or the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Calculus arrives early and assumes complete algebraic fluency, so weaknesses from the main syllabus surface immediately.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. Excluded from the five subjects Ministry of Education equivalency counts, which affects where support money is best spent.

subjects.name: Exam conduct across all subjects
subjects.description: Showing working so method marks survive a wrong answer, managing time across a paper, avoiding early rounding, and answering the command term asked. The cheapest marks available in any IGCSE subject, and the ones most often left untaught because they feel too obvious.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah Islands means here
paragraphs: Used locally, the phrase means one-to-one, board-specific teaching arranged for a child who lives in this community, without the family adding another journey to the evening. Since Jumeirah Islands has no school and no tuition centre inside the gates, the day already contains a long drive in each direction, and the appeal is obvious.

IB Gram meets that need differently. Lessons are live online, one tutor to one student, with the past paper open on a shared screen for both. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our in-person service runs in India only, and there is no office or centre here either. That is stated on the page rather than in small print.

For a Year 10 or Year 11 student this works well. The age group can hold a focused hour on video, the work is written and shared rather than discussed, and the thing that actually moves an IGCSE grade is board-specific exam technique rather than physical presence. A tutor who knows what Pearson 4MA1's papers ask is worth more than one who lives nearby.

Where in-person provision genuinely wins is with a student who will not stay in the chair without an adult present, a household with nowhere quiet at six in the evening, or hands-on practical equipment work. In those cases hire locally and expect the premium: published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's survey, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500.

There is one further practical advantage for this community. Families here move house and change schools reasonably often, and an online arrangement survives both. A tutor who already knows a student's weak topics in September is worth considerably more than a new local tutor starting the diagnosis again from nothing.

sections.heading: Which slot actually survives the journey home
paragraphs: This is the operational detail that decides whether an arrangement lasts a term, and no competitor publishes it. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30. A Jumeirah Islands address is almost always on a bus route that serves two or three other communities first, so the return leg is longer than the distance suggests.

The result is arrivals home between about 15:40 and 16:50, depending on the school and where your community sits in the route order. Add time to eat and change, and 17:00 becomes the dependable weekday start, with 17:30 more comfortable for anyone travelling from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh.

Because bus routes are built around schools rather than around communities, two households inside the same gates can have genuinely different windows. Ask your school's transport office for your own route timings rather than copying a neighbour's slot, since twenty minutes is the difference between a session that works and one spent waking up.

The Red Line station on the edge of Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a short drive from here and worth mentioning because it looks relevant and is not. It is useful for an older teenager's independence and for after-school activities. It makes no difference to a tutoring timetable, because the session happens at home either way.

During Ramadan this changes again: school hours shorten, households run later, and a post-Iftar slot or a late-morning weekend session usually works better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, because the June series does not move to accommodate the calendar.

sections.heading: What each term of Years 10 and 11 should target
paragraphs: Most IGCSE tutoring is bought reactively, after a report or a mock, which means it arrives at the most expensive point in the cycle with the least room to act. A term-by-term plan costs the same per hour and does considerably more, because each stage of the two years has a different useful target.

In the autumn of Year 10 the target is foundations and tier security: the algebra, arithmetic and written-explanation habits the whole course rests on, plus keeping the higher tier available while that decision is still open. In the spring the target is keeping pace with the school's scheme of work and closing gaps as they appear rather than letting them compound.

The summer between Years 10 and 11 is the most under-used opportunity in the whole cycle. With nothing else in the diary, a block of four to eight sessions can rebuild a topic properly, which term-time weekly work struggles to do. It also secures a weekly slot before Year 11 demand fills the early evenings across the city.

In the autumn of Year 11 the work shifts from content to timed past papers for the exact syllabus code, marked together. By the mock window the marked paper becomes the plan: which question types fail and whether the cause is content, method or misreading. In the final weeks it is papers and exam conduct, nothing else.
The table sets this out stage by stage. It is written so you can decide in September what you are buying in February, rather than discovering in February that you should have decided in September.

sections.heading: Get the board and the tier before you spend anything
paragraphs: This is free and it prevents the most expensive mistake available. Email your school's exams officer and ask for the syllabus code and tier for each subject. You should get back something like 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher. Departments within one school sometimes use different boards for different subjects, so ask per subject rather than assuming one answer.

The reason it matters is that Cambridge and Pearson examine the same content differently. Cambridge IGCSE tiers many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses Foundation and Higher in some subjects and offers modular entry in others. Calculator rules, paper counts and the way practical skills are assessed all differ between them.

A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers will teach competently, your child will work hard, and the grade will not move. Parents typically discover it after a term. One email prevents it, and a tutor who can quote the paper structure for your child's code back to you without looking it up is demonstrating that they are a specialist in it.

The tier is the second fact and the more consequential one. Core and Foundation cap the grades available and remove content that post-16 courses assume. If your child is near the boundary and needs the subject for sixth form, that is a Year 10 conversation with the head of department, held with marked evidence rather than with an opinion.

Specifications are revised, so the current version is the authority and the school holds the copy your child is actually sitting. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one.

sections.heading: Choosing one subject rather than three
paragraphs: In a household where the child gets home at half past four, the week is the scarce resource rather than the money. Eight to ten IGCSE subjects already generate homework every evening, and adding three tutoring sessions to that produces a schedule that collapses by about week six, usually with the homework stopping first.

The arrangement that works is one tutored subject on one weekday evening, a second weekday deliberately left clear, and a Saturday morning paper in the examination year. That is three fewer hours than an anxious parent wants to buy and it produces more improvement, because each hour finishes a piece of work.

Choosing which subject is the real decision, and it should be made from marked papers rather than from a feeling. Pick the subject that most affects sixth-form options, usually mathematics, or the one with the clearest fixable problem. In many households the second subject then needs no tutoring at all, because exam technique transfers.

Parents defend splitting an hour between two subjects on grounds of fairness, which is understandable and is not a teaching principle. Twenty-five minutes on chemistry and twenty-five on physics completes nothing in either, marks no paper, and leaves nobody able to say whether it worked.

If two subjects genuinely need support, use two separate evenings rather than one split hour, and accept that this is a bigger commitment than it looks in a community where the journey home already takes an hour out of the afternoon.

sections.heading: What this costs, and what the money should be doing
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IGCSE and IB work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65.

The planning figure matters more than the hourly one. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 a month for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support in one subject. Published packages run from about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Set against that, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. One line in the household budget is therefore stable while you plan this one.

Where the money leaks is predictable: paying an in-home travel premium for a generalist, buying a twenty-session package before testing the match, starting in February for a June series, and splitting one hour across three subjects. None of those is about choosing an expensive tutor over a cheap one.

Every figure above is the provider's or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on subject, tier and weeks remaining. sections.heading: Equivalency, mandatory subjects and the fuller week
paragraphs: Two UAE-specific facts shape an IGCSE timetable and neither appears on most tutoring pages. The first is the mandatory-subject requirement: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current guidance to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. It also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited.

The practical consequence for a Year 10 or 11 household is a fuller week than the option list implies, which strengthens the case for one tutored subject rather than three. For the mandatory subjects themselves, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so support there means helping with the school's own material.

The second fact is equivalency. On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

That exclusion changes the arithmetic. A student taking ten subjects including Arabic and Islamic Education has eight that count, not ten. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency and no tutoring is required for it; verify the current requirements with the Ministry of Education before acting, since they are revised.

sections.heading: What we will not do
paragraphs: Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework or a controlled component, a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on work your child has written. A tutor does not write, part-write, rewrite or supply any of it. Submitting work that is not the student's own puts the qualification at risk and the risk falls on the student rather than on anyone selling the service.

We do not sell grade guarantees, promised score improvements or money-back schemes, because nobody can honestly deliver one. Be wary of any provider who offers one: the promise tells you more about the operator than about their teaching, and it is the fastest way to identify who to avoid in this market.

We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage. Any statistic on this page would need its sample size, date and method attached, and we would rather publish nothing than publish a number you cannot check. Several providers in this market show two conflicting ratings on a single page.

We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs. A folder of exam material offered by a tutor is a copyright problem rather than an advantage.

And we claim no approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute with premises.

faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no office or centre here either. IGCSE tuition for Jumeirah Islands families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers shared on screen. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's survey and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors if presence in the room is essential for your child.

faqs.question: Which term of Year 10 or 11 should we actually start in?
faqs.answer: The autumn of Year 10 if you have the choice. That is when foundations can be built and when the tier decision is still open, and a single weekly hour spread across two years costs less in total than an intensive programme in the spring of Year 11. If you are already in Year 11, the next best points are immediately and the week after the mock, because the marked mock paper turns a vague worry into a specific six-week plan.

faqs.question: Is the summer between Year 10 and Year 11 worth using?
faqs.answer: It is the most under-used opportunity in the whole cycle. With no homework and no journey competing for the time, four to eight sessions can rebuild a topic properly in a way term-time weekly work struggles to manage: electricity in physics, a reliable mole layout in chemistry, algebraic fractions in maths. It also secures a weekly slot before Year 11 demand fills the early evenings across Dubai, which matters in the scarcer subjects.

faqs.question: How do we find out which exam board each subject uses?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the syllabus code and tier per subject. You should get back something like 0620 Extended or 4PH1 Higher. Ask per subject rather than per school, because departments inside one school sometimes use different boards. Cambridge and Pearson examine the same content differently, including calculator rules and how practical skills are assessed, so a tutor working from the wrong past papers will teach competently and change nothing.

faqs.question: Can we tutor three subjects at once if the sessions are short?
faqs.answer: You can buy it and we will advise against it. In a household where the child reaches home at half past four, the week is scarcer than the money: eight to ten subjects already generate homework every evening. Three tutoring sessions on top of that collapses by about week six, usually with the homework stopping first. One subject on one evening, a second weekday left clear, and a Saturday paper in the exam year is the arrangement that survives.

faqs.question: Does the metro at Jumeirah Lakes Towers make any difference to lessons?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth saying because it looks as though it should. The Red Line station on the edge of Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a short drive from these gates and is genuinely useful for after-school activities and for an older teenager travelling independently. It changes nothing about tutoring: an online session happens at home, and an in-home tutor arrives by car in the same evening traffic as everybody else.

faqs.question: Which single subject should we spend the hour on?
faqs.answer: Usually mathematics, because it compounds across two years and because it gates the most sixth-form options, including A Level sciences and the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches. The exception is where a marked paper shows a sharper, more fixable problem elsewhere: electricity in physics, or a mole layout in chemistry. Decide from marked papers rather than from a feeling, and expect that the second subject may need nothing once exam technique transfers.

faqs.question: What should we do with the mock paper when it comes back?
faqs.answer: Read the paper, not the grade. The grade tells you roughly where your child stands and nothing about what to do; the marked paper shows which question types lost marks and whether the cause was content, method or misreading the question. Those three need different responses over different numbers of weeks. Marking it with a tutor who then builds a six-week plan from the actual errors is the single most productive session in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan and the school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families change them. During Ramadan school hours shorten and households run later, so a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot usually works better than anything at five. In the holidays many families pause and others switch to an intensive block, which is the better use of the time if an exam year is coming. Because nobody travels, a change is a slot swap rather than a renegotiation, and the weekly slot is held.

faqs.question: Our child is on Core tier but wants a science at A Level. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: It is worth contesting in Year 10, with marked evidence. The tier removes content as well as capping the grade, and post-16 courses assume the Extended or Higher material. A term of weekly work aimed specifically at the content that separates the tiers, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments, is what changes a head of department's view. If the cap stands, ask the receiving sixth form directly what bridging work they expect rather than assuming the subject is closed.

faqs.question: How many months of tutoring do most families here end up buying?
faqs.answer: The arrangements that work tend to be long and light rather than short and heavy: one hour a week through two academic years, with a holiday block and a rise in frequency in the final six weeks. On Bestimate's monthly bands that sits at roughly AED 600-1,200 a month mid-market for one subject. The arrangements that fail are usually three sessions a week bought in February, which cost more per month and finish before the papers.

faqs.question: Which schools do IGCSE students from this community attend?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside the gates, so families travel. The schools named most often by households here include Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, GEMS Wellington International School, Regent International School, Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle, Dubai Heights Academy and Safa Community School. We have no affiliation with any of them and name them as context for the local market; confirm current curricula and programmes on KHDA's own school listing before enrolling.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about the Arabic and Islamic Education lessons too?
faqs.answer: Know how they affect the week, and know what support can legitimately look like. They are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, KHDA calculates their time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. They are also excluded from the five subjects equivalency counts, which affects where support money is best spent.

faqs.question: What is the first thing you would ask us before matching a tutor?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order: which school and therefore what time your child genuinely gets home, the syllabus code and tier for the subject, and what the last marked paper actually said. The first decides the slot, the second decides which past papers the tutor uses, and the third decides what the first six weeks target. A provider who asks only for the year group and the subject is not going to be specific enough to help.

Then email the exams officer for the syllabus code and tier so the tutor works from the right past papers. After that, one subject on one fixed evening beats three split sessions every time. Our lessons run live online, one to one, with a free trial first.
