intro.heading: The two questions that decide which IGCSE tutor you need
paragraphs: Most parents in Jumeirah Park begin with the subject and the grade. The more useful starting point is the entry. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are different qualifications with different paper structures, and a tutor who prepares a child for the wrong one will produce confident work that scores badly. Your child's school has made that choice already; the exams officer can tell you in a sentence.

The second question is tier. Cambridge offers many subjects at Core and Extended. Core caps the available grades and covers less content; Extended goes further and carries the higher grades. Schools make the decision on the basis of Year 9 and Year 10 performance, sometimes earlier than the parent realises, and sometimes it can still be changed. If your child is capped at Core in a subject they need for sixth form, that is the conversation to have before you book any tutoring at all.

Only once those two are settled does the tutoring question make sense. An IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah Park is, in practice, someone who can work through past papers for one specific syllabus code at one specific tier, mark to the published scheme, and tell your child what the examiner wanted rather than what the textbook says. That skill is subject-specific and board-specific, and it has nothing to do with where anyone lives.

On delivery, we are direct. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service. What we provide to Jumeirah Park families is live online IGCSE tutoring: one tutor, one student, video, a shared whiteboard with a past paper open on it, scheduled around when your child actually gets home. We target the home-tutor phrase because it is the phrase parents use, and then we tell you what the service is.

It is worth saying what this page is not. It is not a list of adjectives about dedicated tutors. It is the information a Jumeirah Park parent needs in order to hire well: the entry questions, the tier decision, what the local market charges and who published those figures, the two series a UAE candidate can actually sit, and the equivalency rule that decides how many of your child's subjects count. If a section does not answer something, it should not be here.

The trade in doing it this way is a bigger pool of tutors against the absence of someone in the room. For IGCSE that trade is favourable, because the Year 10 and Year 11 student is old enough to work on video and the thing that moves the grade is exam technique. Dubai is a large market -- 387,441 private pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, 37 per cent of them on the UK curriculum -- but a tutor who knows Pearson's modular structure and Cambridge's zone timetabling is still a specialist, not a commodity.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Park's UK-curriculum families pass through four stages, and each one needs a different kind of tutoring. The IGCSE years are the first where a public examination result follows the student permanently.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally and optionally through Cambridge Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. This is where the gaps that later look like IGCSE weakness are actually formed: fractions and negative indices in maths, and the inability to write a structured explanation in science.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 decides tiering in several Dubai schools, which means a quiet term in Year 9 can cap a child at Core before anyone discusses it with the family. If your child is borderline, this is the cheapest year in which to intervene.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally. Cambridge grades on a 9-1 scale and offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses 9-1 and offers some subjects in a modular structure. Grades matter for sixth-form entry and for Ministry of Education equivalency.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Park students sit these papers at their own school as a centre. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a zone-specific timetable, and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong version, so the school's copy is the one that counts.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The route most Jumeirah Park IGCSE students take next, typically three or four subjects. The step up is in independence rather than content volume: A Level questions reward a sustained argument or a multi-step derivation where IGCSE rewarded recall and a clean method.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-IGCSE route, offered by several schools within a short drive of Jumeirah Park. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Students coming from Extended IGCSE maths are usually well placed for Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Diploma step is sharper than the IGCSE-to-A-Level step, because breadth increases rather than narrows. Jumeirah Park families considering it should test the HL load in the summer before Year 12 rather than discovering it in October.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Jumeirah Park families ask about most, with the syllabus codes where they are stable and the place marks are usually lost. Tutors are matched to the code and tier, not to the subject in general.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Extended carries the higher grades and includes functions, transformations, more demanding algebra and trigonometry beyond the right angle. Marks go missing on method rather than answers: unshown working on a multi-step question scores nothing when the final figure is wrong. Past papers under time, marked together, is most of the work here.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics / Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths course by students heading for A Level Maths or Further Maths. Calculus arrives early and the pace assumes complete fluency with algebraic manipulation. Students who are comfortable in the main course can still find this one exposes gaps in indices and surds.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, energy, magnetism and radioactivity. The practical paper rewards students who can describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it. Electricity circuits and moments are the two topics that most often need rebuilding from the start rather than revising.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, the periodic table, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Mole calculations are where the Extended grades are won and lost, and they are entirely trainable. Separation techniques and qualitative analysis carry easy marks that students routinely drop.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A long specification where the problem is precision of language rather than understanding. Examiner reports repeat the same point every series: answers that say 'the plant grows better' where the mark scheme wants a named variable and a direction. Tutoring is mostly answer construction against real schemes.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, double or single award
subjects.description: The route for students taking science as one or two subjects rather than three separates. Content is reduced but the paper still asks for the same quality of explanation, and students often arrive with three half-learned sciences instead of one coherent one. Worth clarifying which award your child is entered for.

subjects.name: English Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: First Language English assesses reading comprehension, directed writing and composition; ESL is a different qualification with a different mark scheme and different expectations. Students entered for the wrong one lose marks for reasons nobody explains to them. Directed writing responds well to tutoring; composition takes longer.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and both are marked with level-of-response schemes, which means a correct point with no development earns little. Case-study questions need a plan before any writing. Numerical sections -- break-even, ratios, elasticity -- catch out students who chose the subject to avoid maths.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Computer Science covers data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms and programming, with a written paper that asks for pseudocode and trace tables. ICT is practical and assessed on applied tasks. The two are regularly confused at option time, and the wrong choice is hard to reverse in Year 11.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. These sit alongside the IGCSE load and are excluded from the five subjects Ministry of Education equivalency counts.

paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Jumeirah Park means one-to-one exam-board-specific teaching for a child living in this community, arranged so nobody has to drive to a centre after school. The reason this works well specifically for IGCSE is the age group. A Year 10 or Year 11 student can hold a focused hour on video, can type and write at the same time, and benefits more from a tutor who knows Pearson 4MA1's paper split than from a tutor who is physically present. The constraint on a home visit here is travel; the constraint on a grade is board-specific technique.

Where in-person genuinely wins, we will say so. A student who needs an adult to keep them in the chair, a household with no quiet room at six o'clock, or hands-on practical equipment work are all better served face to face. sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out before you hire anyone
paragraphs: This is the question that saves the most wasted money in Dubai IGCSE tutoring, and almost no parent asks it first. Two children on the same street, both taking IGCSE Maths, can be sitting entirely different papers with different numbers of components and different styles of question. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers will look competent and will not move the grade.

The differences are concrete rather than philosophical. Cambridge runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in June and November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and offers some subjects in a modular structure where units can be sat separately. The paper counts, the balance between short and extended answers, and the way practical skills are assessed all differ.

Your school's exams officer will tell you the code in one email. Ask for the exact syllabus code for each subject -- 0580, 0625, 4MA1, 4PH1 and so on -- and the tier where the subject is tiered. Then make sure the tutor you hire can quote the paper structure for that code back to you without looking it up. If they cannot, they are not a specialist in it.

One further caution worth knowing: Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. You will see UAE-facing tutoring content referring to February and March exam windows, and it is simply wrong for your country. Act on the live official timetable your school holds, not on a date from a marketing page.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential thing in an IGCSE career and the least discussed at home. In a tiered Cambridge subject, Core covers less content and caps the grades available; Extended covers more and carries the top grades. Pearson's equivalent language is Foundation and Higher. A child capped at Core in maths has a ceiling that will affect sixth-form options two years later.

Dubai schools generally decide on the basis of Year 9 and early Year 10 performance, and the decision is often communicated as settled when it is in fact still movable. If your child is near the boundary, the useful intervention is a term of weekly work in Year 10 aimed specifically at the content that separates the tiers, followed by a conversation with the head of department.

The converse case matters too. A student placed on Extended who is genuinely struggling may be better served by a secure Core grade than a poor Extended one, depending on what they need the subject for. That is a judgement about the child, not about ambition, and it should be made with the school's marked evidence in front of everyone rather than on a feeling.

For tutoring, the practical point is that Core and Extended are different courses and need different preparation. A tutor teaching Extended content to a Core candidate wastes the hour and knocks the student's confidence. Confirm the tier before the first session, and confirm it again if the school reviews entries in Year 11.

sections.heading: The Jumeirah Park evening: fitting revision around the bus
paragraphs: Year 11 revision fails on logistics far more often than on motivation. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30; a Jumeirah Park address on a bus route that also serves Al Barsha and Jumeirah Village gets children home between 15:20 and 16:40 depending on the district and the route. Jumeirah Park has no metro station inside it, so none of this is avoidable by changing transport.

That leaves a usable evening of roughly four hours in which homework, a tutoring session, dinner and sleep all have to happen. Families who try to run two tutoring subjects plus homework on the same evening discover by week four that it does not work. One session per evening, two evenings a week, is the pattern that holds through to the June series.

The second scheduling reality is the week shape. With Friday as a short day for many schools and the weekend on Saturday and Sunday, a Saturday morning session is often the best slot in the week for a long past paper: the student is rested, there is no school the next morning, and ninety minutes is realistic rather than optimistic.

During Ramadan this changes again. School hours shorten, households run later, and a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot usually works better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, because the series does not move.

There is one more constraint specific to villa communities like this one. Siblings share walls and study spaces, and a Year 11 working at the kitchen table with a nine-year-old nearby is not working. Before the first session, decide which room the lessons happen in and make it the same room every week. A pair of headphones and a closed door do more for session quality than any change of tutor.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Jumeirah Park, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families start and where most of the disappointment happens. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. At that rate you are usually buying homework supervision from a university student. For a Year 9 who needs company while they work, that can be perfectly adequate and good value.

The next band up is where IGCSE grades actually move. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, which is roughly where a qualified subject teacher who marks to the scheme sits. Above that, TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work and Bestimate's Dubai survey puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200-450 or more, with BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650.

In-home visits carry a travel premium: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. Monthly packages seen across the market run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Every figure here is the provider's or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

Where the money gets wasted is predictable. Paying the in-home premium for a tutor who does not know your board. Buying a twenty-session package in September and using eleven. Starting a maths rescue in April when the paper is in June. One hour a week from the start of Year 10 costs less across two years than a panic block in Year 11 and works considerably better.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: If your child may study in the UAE, or needs a UAE-recognised secondary certificate, equivalency is the process that matters and almost no tutoring page mentions it. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. So a student taking ten IGCSEs including Arabic and Islamic Education has eight that count, not ten, and if several of those are weak the five-subject threshold is less comfortable than it looks. A ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

This shapes option choices in Year 9 more than it shapes tutoring in Year 11. A student who needs the equivalency route should be entered for five subjects they can realistically pass at the threshold, excluding the mandatory UAE subjects from that count. That is a conversation with the school's university guidance office, held early.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and nobody needs tutoring in order to obtain it. We describe the requirement because parents ask and because the published requirement is checkable. Verify the current rules with the Ministry of Education or the relevant attestation authority before acting, since requirements are revised.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody fails an IGCSE on exam day; they fail it in the eight weeks nobody planned. Counting backwards from the series makes that visible. For a UAE candidate the two Cambridge options are June and November, and for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE they are May/June and November. Entry decisions sit months before the papers and are made by the school.

The November series is the resit route, and it is worth understanding before results day rather than after. The Pearson precedent is instructive: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and results reached students in January, with November 2025 results arriving on 22 January 2026. A November resit therefore means a sixth-form application season spent with a provisional grade.

The mock window in January or February is the most useful data point in the year, and most families waste it by reading only the grade. The marked paper tells you which question types failed and why. That is what a tutor should work from in the spring, rather than starting again at chapter one.

Coursework and practical deadlines are the other thing to count backwards from, because they are set internally and arrive without warning. Where a subject carries a practical assessment or a controlled component, the school fixes the date and it typically sits well before the written papers. Ask for the department's internal calendar in September of Year 11 rather than discovering it in February.
Dates are revised, and Cambridge timetables are zone-specific. Use the live official timetable from your school's exams officer rather than any date written on a tutoring page, this one included.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every school listed on this page sits inside that system. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, and does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises.

The mandatory-subject requirement is the part that affects an IGCSE timetable directly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA required its current guidance to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, which is why we describe those courses rather than offering our own version of them.

On the tutoring side there is a separate regulatory point. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is free of charge and valid for two years. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

process.title: Send us the subject, the code and the tier
process.description: Email or ask your school's exams officer for the syllabus code and tier for each subject, then tell us. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher need different past papers and a different tutor brief. Getting this right before the first session is the single cheapest thing you can do.

process.title: Tell us when your child is genuinely home
process.description: Not when school ends, but when the bus reaches your district and the bag is down. For most Jumeirah Park families that is 16:00 to 16:40, which makes 17:00 the dependable weekday start. We fix the slot around that rather than around a timetable.

process.title: Take the free trial session
process.description: A full lesson with the matched tutor on your child's current material, with no payment and no card details. You get a written read afterwards: where the student actually is against the tier they are entered for, and what the first six weeks should target.

process.title: Run weekly to the school's scheme of work
process.description: Sessions follow what the school is teaching and when it assesses, not a generic specification order. You receive a short note after each one. In the autumn of Year 11 the balance shifts from content to timed past papers, and frequency rises before the series.

process.title: Use the mock as the review point
process.description: The mock paper is the best evidence anyone will get before the real series. We mark it with the student, rebuild the topic list from the actual errors, and decide whether to continue, change subject focus or stop. Stopping deliberately is a legitimate outcome.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor is briefed on Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 specifically, with the right past papers and the right mark schemes. Board-blind tutoring is the commonest way IGCSE money gets wasted in this market, and it is entirely avoidable with one email to the exams officer.

whyPoints.title: Tier treated as a decision, not a label
whyPoints.description: We will tell you if your child looks capped below where they need to be, and what a term of Year 10 work would have to achieve to change it. We will also tell you when a secure Core grade is the better outcome than a weak Extended one.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the school run
whyPoints.description: The session slot is built from when your child reaches Jumeirah Park, not from when the school bell rings. This page publishes the arrival pattern because a session booked at the wrong hour fails for reasons unrelated to teaching, and that is how most arrangements quietly end.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the month we read it. Three of the strongest competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars at families who transact in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval and claims none. There is no self-asserted star rating on this page and no statistic without its source, because an unsourced number is a liability rather than a selling point.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help with a stated limit
whyPoints.description: Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework, a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write it. We publish that limit so you can compare it against what else you are being offered in this market.

faqs.question: Which exam board is my Jumeirah Park school entering my child with?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer, by email, for the syllabus code and tier for each subject. You will get back something like 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher. That is the single most useful piece of information in IGCSE tutoring, because Cambridge and Pearson past papers are not interchangeable and a tutor working from the wrong set will look competent while making no difference. Departments within one school sometimes use different boards for different subjects, so ask per subject rather than assuming the school has one answer.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit villas in Jumeirah Park for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our in-person service runs in India only. IGCSE tuition for Jumeirah Park families is delivered live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers shared on screen. We target the home-tutor search phrase because that is what parents type, and then tell you what the service actually is. If presence in the room is essential for your child, the Dubai market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour for in-home visits including travel.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child moved from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot move them; the school decides tiering. What tutoring can do is produce the evidence. If your child is near the boundary, a term of weekly work in Year 10 aimed at the content that separates the tiers, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments, is what changes a head of department's mind. Start that conversation at the end of Year 10 with marked work in hand rather than an opinion. If the cap is genuinely right for the child, a secure Core grade beats a poor Extended one.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to support a Year 10 in this area?
faqs.answer: One hour a week with a qualified subject tutor, starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Market rates for that band run from about AED 150 an hour on published figures, which is more per hour than a student tutor at AED 33-65 but far less in total than an emergency programme in the spring of Year 11. Pick the one subject that most affects sixth-form options, usually maths, and do it properly rather than spreading an hour across three subjects.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE students in the UAE actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not available here, despite appearing in UAE-facing tutoring content. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Dates are revised each year and Cambridge timetables are zone-specific, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, so the version your school's exams officer holds is the one to plan around rather than any date on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count all ten of my child's IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is not what the sourced rule says. Verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education before acting, and note that no tutoring is required to obtain equivalency.

faqs.question: Is a Saturday morning session better than a weekday one?
faqs.answer: For a full past paper, yes. A ninety-minute slot on Saturday morning gives a rested student the only genuinely uninterrupted block in the week, with no school the next morning and no bus to recover from. Weekday evenings are better for shorter, targeted work on one topic. The pattern that holds through Year 11 for most Jumeirah Park families is two weekday sessions of an hour plus a Saturday paper, with the Sunday session spent marking that paper together.

faqs.question: My child's mock grades dropped. Is it too late to fix it?
faqs.answer: If the mock was in January or February and the series is in June, no, and the mock is the most useful thing you have. The marked paper shows which question types lost marks and whether the cause was content, method or misreading. Those three need different responses. What does not work is starting again at the beginning of the specification; what does work is a six-week programme attacking the specific failures, with a timed paper at the end to test whether it worked.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a licence, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor you hire directly whether they hold one; no fine amounts are published, so distrust quoted figures.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both maths and physics at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and at IGCSE level it works better than it does at A Level or Higher Level. The two subjects share algebraic method, graph work and rearrangement, and a tutor covering both sees whether a physics problem is actually a maths problem. It also halves the number of evening slots you have to protect, which matters in a household where the bus arrives at 16:30. Check that the tutor is comfortable with the practical paper as well as the theory before combining them.

faqs.question: What should we do about Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Treat them as a separate workload rather than part of the IGCSE programme. They are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. They are also excluded from the five subjects Ministry of Education equivalency counts. Because KHDA prohibits different or additional content without prior Ministry permission, support here means helping with the school's own material, not substituting a different course.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects most often need outside help in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Extended maths, chemistry and physics, in that order, and English as a Second Language where a student has been entered for the wrong English qualification. The common factor is multi-step method: a question that needs four correct decisions in sequence, where the student knows the content but loses the marks in the middle. That is a trainable failure and it responds quickly to marked past papers. Biology tends to need language precision rather than content, which takes longer but is just as fixable.

faqs.question: Does a November entry hurt a sixth-form application?
faqs.answer: It complicates the timing rather than the outcome. The Pearson precedent shows why: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. So a November resit means applying to sixth form with a provisional grade in that subject. Schools are used to it, but tell them early. Where the June result is genuinely borderline, that conversation is better had in August than in January.

faqs.question: How long before we can tell whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Six sessions, judged on marked timed work rather than on how the sessions felt. We expect to see specific question types that previously lost marks now scoring, and the student able to explain the method without prompting. If that has not happened by session six, the problem is either the match, the frequency or a diagnosis we got wrong, and we would rather change one of those than ask you to persist. No honest provider can promise a grade or a number of marks.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue over the summer or if we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many Jumeirah Park families pause through July and August, and others use a short intensive block before Year 11 starts, which is the single best-value timing available if your child is moving into the examination year. If you travel, sessions follow the time zone you are in provided we know the week before. Because nobody has to drive anywhere, a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a renegotiation, and that flexibility is one of the practical advantages of online delivery.

intro.heading: Two years with four doors in it, and most families arrive after the second
paragraphs: IGCSE looks like a two-year run at a single examination, and it is really a sequence of four decisions, each of which closes behind you. The first is the board and subject set, chosen on Year 9 option forms. The second is the tier — Core or Extended with Cambridge, Foundation or Higher with Pearson — usually set by the school during Year 10. The third is the final entry, confirmed by the school's examinations officer months before the papers. The fourth is the mocks, which are the last reliable diagnostic before the real thing.

A Jumeirah Village Circle family ringing in October of Year 10 can influence all four. A family ringing in March of Year 11 can influence none of them and is left with the papers themselves, which is still a worthwhile job but a different one. The single most useful thing you can establish before buying anything is which of those doors are still open, and that takes one email to the head of year.

What makes the Dubai version of this harder is the series question. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it should play no part in a UAE family's planning, and a tutor who suggests otherwise does not know the market. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable.

The other half of this page answers the phrase you typed. Jumeirah Village Circle is dense and central, so in-home tuition is genuinely practical here, and it is worth knowing what it costs and what the premium buys. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. We say so before you book, because a family waiting for a car that was never coming is nobody's idea of service.

One habit is worth adopting whatever the date. Treat the marked mock set as the most useful document of the two years rather than as a prediction to worry about. It arrives roughly a term before the series, which is still early enough to act on, and it answers the only question that determines what you should buy: are the marks being lost to missing content or to technique. Families who skip that step end up buying a term of general support aimed at a problem nobody ever diagnosed.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.programmesIntro: Three things govern the calendar for a Jumeirah Village Circle IGCSE student: which board, which tier, and whether the plan includes a November entry. Each one is a date-bound decision rather than a preference.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English. Most mathematics and science subjects split into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade at 5. The tier is set during Year 10 and reviewable early in Year 11 if the evidence changes, which is the most time-sensitive decision in the whole qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone applies.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A, with Foundation covering grades 5 to 1 and Higher covering 9 to 4. Used by a significant minority of Dubai schools and by most private candidates. Tutor supply for Pearson codes is thinner in this market, which affects how early you need to book rather than what you pay.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. As a checkable illustration of lead times, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official document.

programmes.name: The November series as a planned route
programmes.description: Both boards run a November series, so a second attempt sits roughly five months after June rather than a year, and entry as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre is possible. It is also the only realistic route past a tier ceiling: a student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which turns an unmovable grade 5 into a possibility.
programmes.countryNote: The practical trap is the deadline. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination and often before a family has finished absorbing August results, so find the date in March rather than in September. Entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre, not to a tutor, and belong in any honest budget comparison.

dubai/igcse-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.subjectsIntro: Subjects sit on different calendars, because coursework components and practical routes take different amounts of lead time. These are the ones Jumeirah Village Circle families ask about, with a note on when the pressure actually arrives.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: No coursework, so the calendar is purely about papers and the tier decision. That makes it the subject where a late start is least damaging and a tier error is most damaging, because nothing but the entry limits the outcome.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken in Year 11 and genuinely new content — calculus, logarithms, vectors — taught at pace in a single year. A late start here is the hardest to recover from, because there is no earlier material to consolidate instead.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The practical route is a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, decided by the school's entry. That matters to the calendar because practical-paper technique can be drilled at any point, and almost always is not until it is too late to matter.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The qualitative analysis ion tests are pure recall and can be secured in one session in any week of either year. Students leave them blank on the paper with striking regularity, which makes this the clearest example of marks lost to timing rather than ability.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content is manageable and the marks turn on precision of language. Because the fix is linguistic, it works equally well in Year 10 or in the final eight weeks, which makes biology the most forgiving science for a late start.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: One timetabled subject across three disciplines, so a weak discipline pulls two grades at once on the double award. The calendar implication is that identifying the weak discipline early matters more here than in any separate science.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The 0511 route carries a speaking endorsement, which is a scheduled assessment with a fixed school date. That is a real calendar item families miss, because it does not feel like an examination.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Habit work on selecting evidence rather than paraphrasing, which takes time to embed, so this is a subject where Year 10 intervention is worth considerably more than Year 11 intervention.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline and application, learned by practice over months rather than weeks. A student who starts in the final term can secure diagram labelling but rarely the application marks that separate a 6 from an 8.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case organisation is the ceiling, and it responds to repeated practice on past-paper stimulus material. Available at any point, but the number of papers worked through is what determines the outcome.

sections.heading: Years 10 and 11, in order, with the doors marked
paragraphs: Laid out as a sequence rather than as a vague two-year stretch, the qualification becomes much easier to plan against. Year 9 options set the board and the subject set. The first two terms of Year 10 produce the evidence the school uses for the tier decision, which is the most consequential moment in the whole qualification and the one families almost never know is happening. The third term of Year 10 and the first of Year 11 are the content window, when gaps can still genuinely close.

Then the entry deadline, handled by the school's examinations officer months before the papers, which locks the tier and the subject count. Then the mocks, roughly a term ahead, which are the last reliable diagnostic. Then the final eight weeks, which belong to technique rather than content. Then results, and then the November entry decision, which has its own deadline falling much earlier than families expect.

A Jumeirah Village Circle parent can establish exactly where they are with two questions to the school: which tier is my child currently entered for, and when is the final entry deadline. The answers take a day to obtain and they determine whether you are buying a tier-evidence block, a content block or a technique block — three different purchases at three different prices.

The table below is the version worth keeping. It is deliberately written as positions rather than dates, because dates move and because the board's published timetables are the only authority on them. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and Cambridge allocates zone-specific versions, so the live official document is always the thing to work from.

sections.heading: The tier decision is the one with a deadline nobody announces
paragraphs: A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. If the post-16 plan requires a 6 or a 7 — and A Level sciences and IB Diploma Higher Level routinely do — a student on the lower tier cannot get there however well the paper goes and however much tuition is bought.

Schools make the decision for sound reasons. A borderline candidate entered for the higher tier can score below its lowest available grade and come away with nothing, where the lower tier would have produced a secure 4 or 5. That is a genuine risk and heads of year are right to weigh it. But the decision is taken on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes materially in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved — if somebody asks before the entry deadline.

This is where a short block has real leverage. Five or six sessions on the higher tier's additional material produces a clear answer: either the student handles it or the gap is wider than the remaining time can close. Both answers are useful, and the second saves more money than the first. What it also produces is written evidence a head of year can act on, which is more persuasive than a parent's confidence.

If the tier cannot change, the honest options are to revise the post-16 plan or to enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Both are legitimate. What is not is buying thirty weekly sessions against a ceiling, and we will say so before taking the booking rather than after.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question in a dense community
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle is one of the easier Dubai communities for an in-home tutor to serve. It is central, it is dense, and the drive from Al Barsha or Motor City is short. So the honest version of this is not that home tutoring is impractical here. It is that it costs more and narrows the tutor pool, and that the second effect is the one that matters.

On cost: in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with a rate survey putting the band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500. One provider publishes monthly packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Market figures from the providers named, researched October 2026.

On the pool: the set of tutors willing to come to a specific address at a specific hour is smaller than the set who teach a specific syllabus code, and for Pearson codes it is smaller again, because Pearson supply in this market is already thin. For a Core-tier biology student that may not matter. For an Extended-tier 4PH1 candidate eight weeks from a series, it is the whole question.

IB Gram removes the travel. Lessons are one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. The calendar benefit is concrete: when a mock week lands or a school deadline shifts, a video session moves inside the same week without a round trip being renegotiated.

sections.heading: The eight weeks before a series, and what they can fix
paragraphs: This is the window most families actually buy, so it is worth being precise about what it holds. Eight weeks is enough to sit each paper under timed conditions more than once, mark it properly against the scheme, and remove the three or four recurring technique errors that cost most candidates a grade boundary.

In mathematics those errors are missing method lines on multi-mark questions, rounding an intermediate value and carrying it forward, and — for Cambridge candidates — non-calculator fluency that has quietly decayed across two years of homework done with a device on the desk. In the sciences they are command terms answered loosely, experiments described without naming the controlled variable, and recallable marks left blank: the chemistry ion tests, half-life calculations, genetics question shapes.

Eight weeks is not enough to teach two missing topics and polish technique at the same time. A provider promising both is selling optimism, and the cost of believing them is that neither gets done. The honest plan secures what is reachable, names the topics being abandoned, and treats the November series as the second attempt if the target grade needs one.

Four weeks narrows it to technique plus recallable marks. Two weeks is triage: paper-sitting with marking so the student stops losing marks to process, and a decision about what not to revise. Telling a student what to leave out is one of the more valuable things a specialist does at that point and almost never what a family expects to be paying for.

sections.heading: The November series, planned rather than panicked into
paragraphs: Almost nobody prices the November series in before June, and it changes the whole calculation. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in November as well as May/June. That puts a second attempt roughly five months after the summer rather than a year, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible.

The arithmetic is worth doing in March rather than in August. Thirty weeks of general weekly support before June, at a mid-band market rate, is in the region of AED 6,000. A focused block of eight to ten sessions after results, aimed at one paper and one tier, is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. If the realistic view in the spring is that one subject will land a band short, the second plan is both cheaper and better targeted.

Two cautions. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination, frequently before a family has finished digesting August results, so the date needs finding in advance rather than discovering afterwards. And entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre, not to a tutor, which belongs in the comparison.

The November window is also the only realistic route past a tier ceiling. A student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which converts a fixed grade 5 into a genuine possibility. That conversation belongs in the spring term with the school, not in September with a tutor.

sections.heading: Mocks are the most underused diagnostic in the qualification
paragraphs: Mock examinations sit roughly a term before the real series and they are treated, in most households, as a source of anxiety and a grade prediction. They are considerably more useful than that: a full set of marked mock papers is the clearest diagnostic information a family will get in two years, and it arrives at exactly the point where there is still time to act on it.

The practical move is to spend one session per subject going through the marked mock with a specialist, before any decision is made about what tuition to buy. That session identifies whether the losses are content or technique, which determines everything downstream. Families who skip it buy a term of general support aimed at a problem nobody diagnosed.

Mock timetables also differ across the schools Jumeirah Village Circle families use by up to a fortnight, which matters if you are trying to book a specialist in the window immediately afterwards. That window is busy for the same reason everywhere: every family in Dubai has just received marked papers.

One more use for them. If a tier change is being considered, the mock is the evidence. A student who performs above the Core ceiling on an Extended-style paper has a case that a head of year can act on, and that case is far stronger coming from a marked paper than from a conversation about potential.

Keep the papers themselves, too. A student who re-sits the same mock under timed conditions four weeks later has a direct measure of whether the block worked, which is a far better review mechanism than a conversation about how the sessions have been going.

sections.heading: Where a session fits in a Jumeirah Village Circle week
paragraphs: The afternoon here is shaped by two things: a short school run and a dense academy schedule. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, or eight to fifteen to Motor City, so they are often home by 3.45pm — earlier than families in the outlying villa communities. That sounds like it should open an early slot, and it rarely does, because Dubai Sports City is next door and academies there take students out between four and six.

So the usable windows are 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for the many who have one. Students travelling in from Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square are later again, home after 4.30pm, which pushes them to the back of that range.

Sessions work best after a first attempt at the school's problem set rather than before it. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, and a specific sticking point is what a specialist resolves in forty minutes. Scheduled before homework, the session becomes supervised homework, which is a low-value use of a subject teacher and builds dependence rather than technique.

Weekend mornings are the most underused slot in this community and the right one for whole timed papers, which need an uninterrupted ninety minutes that a weekday evening here cannot reliably provide. Online delivery keeps all of it flexible: sessions move within the week when a mock or a fixture collides, shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and stop cleanly at study leave.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, and what nobody holds
paragraphs: Engaging a home tutor means a stranger entering a Jumeirah Village Circle flat on a weekly basis, so the permit question belongs before the first session rather than after the fourth. The document is the private tuition work permit, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It costs the tutor nothing to hold: MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee, a two-working-day completion time, and an application made through the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system, with the permit then standing free of charge for two years. A tutor who tells you the paperwork is slow or expensive is describing some other process than the one MoHRE publishes.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category explains a good deal about the AED 45 to AED 150 band: a very low rate usually signals tutor category rather than illegality. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted.

One boundary becomes tempting exactly when the calendar tightens. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. Either way, do not approach your child's own teacher privately in the weeks after mocks.

The symmetry here is worth stating plainly for anyone searching for a home tutor. A tuition business operating from premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, issued by KHDA. IB Gram has no premises in the Emirates, no office and no centre, in Jumeirah Village Circle or anywhere else, and therefore holds no such permit. Nor is it accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and no page here will imply otherwise. The same restraint applies to documents: syllabus material, past papers and mark schemes are not reproduced or distributed from here. A tutor references the official source and links to it, and the school your child attends already holds licensed access to it.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor come to our home in Jumeirah Village Circle?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do serve this community easily, since it is central and dense, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. Dropping the visit widens the pool from those willing to drive here to everyone who teaches your child's syllabus code.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child in Dubai sit?
faqs.answer: June, with November available as a second attempt. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so it should play no part in a UAE family's planning. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk, so confirm yours with the exams officer.

faqs.question: When is the tier decision made, and can we influence it?
faqs.answer: Usually during Year 10, by the school, on Year 10 evidence, and most families do not know it is happening. It matters enormously: a Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation entry caps the available grade at 5, which rules out most A Level science and IB Diploma Higher Level routes. It is reviewable early in Year 11 if the evidence changes, but only if somebody asks before the entry deadline. A five or six session block on higher-tier material produces written evidence a head of year can act on.

faqs.question: What are the four decisions that close behind us?
faqs.answer: Board and subject set, chosen on Year 9 option forms. Tier, set by the school during Year 10. Final entry, confirmed by the examinations officer months before the papers, which locks the tier and the subject count for that series. And mocks, roughly a term ahead, which are the last reliable diagnostic. A family can influence all four in October of Year 10 and none of them in March of Year 11, which is why the first question worth asking is where you currently are.

faqs.question: How much can eight weeks before the June series actually change?
faqs.answer: A meaningful amount, provided it is spent on technique rather than content. Eight weeks allows each paper to be sat timed more than once, marked against the scheme, and the recurring errors removed: missing method lines, rounding carried forward, non-calculator decay for Cambridge candidates, command terms answered loosely, experiments described without the controlled variable, and recallable marks left blank. It is not enough to teach two missing topics and polish technique simultaneously, and a provider promising both is selling optimism rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Should we plan a November entry before we even see June results?
faqs.answer: If the spring-term view is that a subject will land a band short, yes, and the arithmetic supports it. Thirty weeks of general support before June runs to around AED 6,000 at a mid-band market rate, whereas a focused eight to ten session block after results, aimed at one paper, is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. The catch is the deadline: the November entry date falls well before the examination and often before results have settled, so it needs finding in the spring.

faqs.question: What should we do with the marked IGCSE mock papers a Jumeirah Village Circle school sends home?
faqs.answer: Treat them as the best diagnostic you will get in two years, not as a prediction. Spend one session per subject going through the marked paper with a specialist before deciding what tuition to buy, because that session establishes whether the losses are content or technique and therefore what the whole plan should be. It also produces the evidence for a tier-change conversation: a student performing above the Core ceiling on an Extended-style paper has a case a head of year can act on.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in Year 11 term two?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but the aim narrows. By then the tier and the subject count are locked for that series, so what remains is technique on the papers and securing recallable marks. That is genuinely worth doing: technique is the most improvable thing in the qualification and the fastest to move. What has gone is the ability to change the ceiling, which is why the honest conversation at that point sometimes includes planning a November entry on a higher tier instead.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a student living in the Circle?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in the outlying villa communities and later than you would hope. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, so they are often home by 3.45pm. The complication is Dubai Sports City next door, where academies take students out between four and six. In practice, 5.30pm works for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one. Students travelling in from Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square are later again.

faqs.question: Should tuition come before or after my child's homework?
faqs.answer: After, almost always. A student who has already attempted the school's problem set arrives with a specific sticking point, and a specific sticking point is what a subject specialist resolves quickly. A session scheduled before homework tends to become supervised homework, which is a low-value use of a specialist rate and builds dependence rather than technique. The exception is the week before a mock, when working straight through a past paper under timed conditions is more useful than anything the school has set.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect IGCSE revision in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and household energy patterns change, including for students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls close to the run-up to the June series. What works is shifting sessions to post-Iftar, keeping them shorter, and moving whole timed papers to weekend mornings for that month. Online delivery makes the rearrangement administratively trivial, since there is no travel to renegotiate on either side.

faqs.question: Which subjects are most damaged by starting late?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, because it is genuinely new content — calculus, logarithms, vectors — taught at pace in one year, with no earlier material to consolidate instead. First Language English is next, because the fix is a habit of selecting evidence rather than paraphrasing, and habits take months to embed. The most forgiving are biology, where the losses are linguistic and respond quickly, and mathematics, where there is no coursework and the only real constraint is the tier you are entered for.

faqs.question: What does it cost, and does booking late cost more?
faqs.answer: Not in rate, but it costs you in choice. Published Dubai rates run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialist provision, and AED 45 to AED 150 in the budget band, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500. Those do not move seasonally. Supply does: in the eight weeks before a series, every family wants the same specialists at the same two evening hours. Market rates researched October 2026.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for my child's code in the window we need?
faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait rather than somebody who teaches the other board. Availability is tightest in the eight weeks before the June series, which is when most families ring, and thinnest for Pearson science codes, Computer Science and Additional Mathematics 0606. In the meantime we can often run a useful adjacent block, such as a marking session on the mock or practical-paper technique, with a different specialist. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so before any payment.
